title: Modeling International Trade of Ammonia for Direct Use and as a Hydrogen Carrier in Korea
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Achieving carbon neutrality requires large-scale deployment of low-carbon energy carriers and fuels. In Korea, clean ammonia (NH3) is gaining increasing attention due to its potential role in international energy trade and hard-to-abate sec
content: Achieving carbon neutrality requires large-scale deployment of low-carbon energy carriers and fuels. In Korea, clean ammonia (NH3) is gaining increasing attention due to its potential role in international energy trade and hard-to-abate sectors. Traditionally used as a feedstock for fertilizers and chemicals, ammonia is now emerging as both an efficient hydrogen carrier and a direct carbon-free fuel. Clean ammonia enables long-distance transportation and storage due to its high volumetric energy density and existing infrastructure, while direct utilization pathways may reduce energy losses and additional costs associated with hydrogen cracking. Growing interest in ammonia-fueled shipping amid tightening International Maritime Organization (IMO) regulations and in ammonia combustion technologies in the power sector further underscores its importance in future decarbonization strategies. This study investigates how ammonia supply chains and utilization pathways may evolve under a net-zero transition in Korea using a modified GCAM-KAIST framework. The research extends the current GCAM ammonia representation by incorporating pathways for clean ammonia production, international trade, transportation, storage, cracking, and direct utilization. Clean ammonia production is represented through a modified Haber-Bosch process integrated with renewable electricity and water electrolysis systems. The model further captures the full ammonia supply chain, from international shipping as liquid ammonia (LNH3) to downstream hydrogen reconversion or direct end-use applications. Preliminary results suggest that LNH3 may remain cost-competitive with liquefied hydrogen (LH2) despite additional cracking processes, due to potential advantages in long-distance transportation, storage, and existing ammonia infrastructure. Direct ammonia utilization is also expected to improve economic performance by avoiding energy losses associated with reconversion. The study provides insights into future ammonia trade strategies, infrastructure planning, and clean energy transitions for Korea and other energy-importing countries.

title: FourierBGC 1.0: Fourier feature encoding of spatiotemporal inputs for biogeochemical Argo profile reconstruction
summary: Abstract. Reconstructing biogeochemical Argo profiles is essential to bridge the severe spatiotemporal coverage gaps between abundant physical observations and scarce biogeochemical data, providing the continuous ocean-state representations
content: Abstract. Reconstructing biogeochemical Argo profiles is essential to bridge the severe spatiotemporal coverage gaps between abundant physical observations and scarce biogeochemical data, providing the continuous ocean-state representations required for climate models and global carbon budget analyses. A recent convolutional method for profile reconstruction, PPCon, encodes day-of-year, year, latitude, and longitude through four independently learned multilayer perceptrons. These learned encoders add substantial parameter overhead and may yield sub-optimal spatiotemporal representations for the variables being reconstructed. To address this, we introduce FourierBGC, which replaces PPCon's learned encoders with a fixed Fourier-feature encoding of day-of-year, latitude, and longitude, combined with a lightweight learned projection, cutting encoder parameters by 88 %. By directly embedding periodic annual cycles and smooth spatial continuity into input space, this encoding provides strong multifrequency coordinate representations that facilitate lightweight yet highly expressive spatiotemporal representations. Through a controlled ablation holding PPCon's convolutional backbone fixed, FourierBGC outperforms PPCon on all three reconstructed variables (nitrate, chlorophyll-a, and bbp700), and the Fourier encoding achieves the lowest reconstruction error in every sub-basin and season. Disentangling the sources of error reduction reveals that beyond an optimized training procedure, the Fourier encoding yields a consistent, highly parameter-efficient performance boost across all variables. Furthermore, the learned projection's role exhibits variable- and season-specific behavior tied to upper-ocean physics: it is dispensable on nitrate, essential for capturing the complex profile of chlorophyll-a, and on bbp700 helps under summer stratification while costing accuracy in winter, a pattern consistent with the projection expressing vertical water-column structure only when it is present. Overall, FourierBGC demonstrates that structuring spatiotemporal inputs with explicit frequency priors offers a parameter-efficient strategy for reconstructing sparse geophysical and environmental fields.

title: Green Finance, Innovation, and Financial Stability: Assessing the Role of Sustainable Investment in South Africa’s Transition Economy
source: International Journal of Finance and Banking Research
summary: This study empirically examines the dynamic relationship between green finance, financial innovation, exchange rate volatility, and macro-financial stability in South Africa’s transition economy. Using quarterly time-series data spanning 20
content: This study empirically examines the dynamic relationship between green finance, financial innovation, exchange rate volatility, and macro-financial stability in South Africa’s transition economy. Using quarterly time-series data spanning 2000Q1-2025Q4, we construct a multivariate framework incorporating green bond issuance and ESG-linked capital flows (green finance proxy), a composite financial stress index and banking sector Z-score (financial stability proxies), digital financial innovation indicators, the real effective exchange rate, GDP growth, and the policy repo rate. After confirming non-stationarity at levels using Augmented Dickey-Fuller and Phillips-Perron tests, Johansen cointegration tests reveal a long-run equilibrium relationship among the variables, justifying estimation through a Vector Error Correction Model (VECM). Impulse Response Functions indicate that a one-standard-deviation shock to green finance reduces financial stress by approximately 0.28 standard deviations within four quarters (p < 0.05), while improving banking sector resilience as measured by the Z-score. However, exchange rate depreciation offsets nearly 20% of the stabilising effect, highlighting the role of currency risk in transition financing. Variance decomposition analysis shows that green finance innovations explain 17-22% of forecast error variance in financial stability over a 10-quarter horizon, confirming its growing systemic relevance. The moderating effect of financial innovation is statistically significant (p < 0.05), strengthening the transmission of sustainable capital toward macro-financial resilience. These findings suggest that green finance can enhance systemic stability in a carbon-intensive emerging market; however, its effectiveness depends on exchange-rate management and institutional quality. Policy implications therefore require cautious integration of climate-related financial instruments into macroprudential frameworks to mitigate unintended liquidity and currency spillovers during the Just Energy Transition.

title: The Role of CAAB in Electric Last-Mile Agrifood Delivery in Bologna (Italy): Environmental and Urban Sustainability Gains
summary: This paper reconceptualizes urban agrifood logistics not merely as a supply chain mechanism but as a critical determinant of environmental health, spatial justice, and urban sustainability. While traditional last-mile delivery systems are e
content: This paper reconceptualizes urban agrifood logistics not merely as a supply chain mechanism but as a critical determinant of environmental health, spatial justice, and urban sustainability. While traditional last-mile delivery systems are essential for food security, they rely heavily on fossil fuels, thereby exacerbating air pollution (CO2, NOx, PM10) and traffic congestion. This conventional approach places a cumulative environmental burden on vulnerable populations, highlighting a stark conflict between food accessibility and public health. To address this paradigm, this study analyzes the role of the Centro Agro-Alimentare di Bologna (CAAB) as a potential strategic, energy-independent hub for the electrification of last-mile agrifood delivery. Powered by one of Europe’s largest rooftop photovoltaic plants, the CAAB offers a unique closed-loop model. The transition to a fully electric distribution fleet has the potential to offer crucial urban ecosystem services such as the reduction in localized chemical emissions and expected decreases in anthropogenic sensible heat, which may contribute to mitigating the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect and protecting the thermoregulatory and respiratory health of fragile demographics. Furthermore, this zero-emission, widespread distribution can serve as a conceptual framework to support equitable access to local, proximity-based markets, helping prevent the formation of ‘food deserts’ without imposing an environmental toll on low-income neighborhoods. By integrating green energy production with electric mobility, the CAAB can establish a promising, potentially transferable model for inclusive urban planning, aligning with Bologna’s commitments to carbon neutrality and fostering a holistic approach to metropolitan resilience.

title: The relational dynamics of social entrepreneurship: a systematic review of interpersonal trust and sustainable social impact
source: Interpersona An International Journal on Personal Relationships
summary: Introduction: Despite the increasing prominence of social entrepreneurship as a response to pervasive social, economic and environmental challenges, the mechanisms through which it achieves lasting and large-scale impact remain poorly theor
content: Introduction: Despite the increasing prominence of social entrepreneurship as a response to pervasive social, economic and environmental challenges, the mechanisms through which it achieves lasting and large-scale impact remain poorly theorised. This systematic review aims to describe the intellectual structure of social entrepreneurship and sustainability literature and delineate the mechanisms through which social enterprises achieve positive sustainable impact. Methodology: This study follows a systematic review approach combining bibliometric and thematic analysis. Scopus database was used for analysis. Results: The study brings to light five major themes: socio-institutional dynamics; corporate sustainability and circular economy strategies; environmental innovation and sustainable finance; climate transition trajectories; and digital transformation in smart urban systems. The findings demonstrate multi-level mechanisms of mission-driven innovation, hybrid business models, stakeholder engagement, institutional embedding and digital hybridity that interlink social entrepreneurship action with sustainable impact. Discussion: This review develops a comprehensive conceptual framework and outlines a future research agenda aimed at addressing key challenges in the field, including measurement gaps, geographic disparities, and the intersectionality of social, environmental, and economic dimensions.

title: Toxic truth and noble lies. Or: how did we ever believe we could stop global warming?
summary: In 2015 the Paris Agreement committed the world to carbon neutrality around 2050. This article asks not what is blocking climate action, but how anyone could ever have believed that global warming might be stopped. It retraces the making of
content: In 2015 the Paris Agreement committed the world to carbon neutrality around 2050. This article asks not what is blocking climate action, but how anyone could ever have believed that global warming might be stopped. It retraces the making of that belief: the invention of the 2°C target in the 1990s, after two decades in which experts had treated warming as inexorable; the myth of the ‘energy transition’, which mistakes technological turnover for material substitution and overlooks the rebound and symbiotic effects; and the misreading of carbon-cycle science that turned ‘carbon neutrality’ first into a halving of emissions and then into speculative negative emissions. Behind these errors lies an institutional imperative of optimism, manufactured alike by climate diplomacy, philanthropy and expertise. Carbon neutrality, the article argues, is the noble lie of our time: far from enabling action, it holds the status quo together.

title: International Best Practices of Digital-Green Integration: Lessons for Developing Countries
source: Emirati Journal of Business Economics & Social Studies
summary: Governments are beginning to connect digital transformation and green transition policies, although the two agendas were long managed through separate reform tracks. This article examines that shift through three advanced policy systems: th
content: Governments are beginning to connect digital transformation and green transition policies, although the two agendas were long managed through separate reform tracks. This article examines that shift through three advanced policy systems: the European Union, South Korea, and China. The analysis uses a Most Similar Systems Design (MSSD) and draws on official strategies, policy packages, implementation materials, and peer-reviewed literature. Three models are identified: the European Union's regulatory-market model, South Korea's state-coordinated innovation model, and China's infrastructure-planning model. Their institutions, instruments, and financing scales differ substantially. Across the cases, however, three lessons recur: ministries need a working coordination mechanism, shared digital-environmental infrastructure requires patient investment, and complex green conditionalities work better after basic digital capacity has been built. For developing countries, the issue is not how to copy these models wholesale. A more defensible strategy is component matching: selecting institutional and sequencing elements that fit domestic administrative capacity, fiscal space, and digital readiness.

summary: Diese Dissertation untersucht konventionelle Supraleiter bei Umgebungs- und niedrigem Druck mit Hilfe von Dichtefunktionaltheorie, Dichtefunktionalstörungstheorie und isotroper Eliashberg-Theorie. Für Ac–Be–H wird AcBeH8 als bis 10 GPa dyna
content: Diese Dissertation untersucht konventionelle Supraleiter bei Umgebungs- und niedrigem Druck mit Hilfe von Dichtefunktionaltheorie, Dichtefunktionalstörungstheorie und isotroper Eliashberg-Theorie. Für Ac–Be–H wird AcBeH8 als bis 10 GPa dynamisch stabile Phase mit einer vorhergesagten Sprungtemperatur von 181 K identifiziert. In der X4H15-Familie erhöht Lochdotierung die Sprungtemperatur bei Umgebungsdruck auf etwa 50 K. Ein Hochdurchsatz-Screening von mehr als 4.700 B–C-basierten Strukturen liefert RbSrB6C6 und TlB2C8 als Kandidaten mit 57 K bzw. 76 K und zeigt die zentrale Rolle hybridisierter B–C-Bindungen. Die Analyse von über 20.000 Elektron-Phonon-Rechnungen zeigt zudem einen grundlegenden Zielkonflikt zwischen Phononenfrequenz und Elektron-Phonon-Kopplung. Die Ergebnisse deuten darauf hin, dass konventionelle Raumtemperatur-Supraleitung bei Umgebungsdruck praktisch äußerst unwahrscheinlich ist.

title: The unsustainability of final disposition: a natural capital perspective
summary: Popular methods of disposition are unsustainable from a natural capital perspective. Coffin burials pollute the soil, while gas cremators produce an average of 540 pounds (245 kilograms) of carbon dioxide emission per body. In response, sus
content: Popular methods of disposition are unsustainable from a natural capital perspective. Coffin burials pollute the soil, while gas cremators produce an average of 540 pounds (245 kilograms) of carbon dioxide emission per body. In response, sustainable alternatives such as natural burials, alkaline hydrolysis, and human composting have (re)emerged. With sustainability defined as the substitution of human capital with natural capital, we review 14 final disposition methods and rank them from most to least sustainable. Using the shadow price index to analyse and measure each method, we find that technological and comestation methods are the most sustainable, while burial and cremation methods are the least. However, technological and comestation methods are, on average, negatively perceived. We step from this analysis to argue that the next most pressing research question is over how popular opinion of greener disposition methods can turn more positive.

title: Accumulation by Dispossession, yet Legal: Contesting Interests in Land Acquisition Law
source: Jurnal Asosiasi Pengajar Hukum Tata Negara Hukum Administrasi Negara (JAPHTN-HAN)
summary: This article critically examines how land acquisition for development in Indonesia facilitates legally sanctioned dispossession through state legal frameworks. It addresses two central research questions: how does the Indonesian land acquis
content: This article critically examines how land acquisition for development in Indonesia facilitates legally sanctioned dispossession through state legal frameworks. It addresses two central research questions: how does the Indonesian land acquisition regime enable processes of dispossession, and what configurations of power are embedded in its legal and institutional structures? Employing a socio-legal approach that combines doctrinal legal analysis with insights from critical agrarian studies, this study investigates the relationship between land acquisition law, state power, and capital accumulation. The analysis reveals a paradigmatic shift in the normative orientation of Indonesian land acquisition law, from its constitutional and social justice foundations towards an increasingly instrumental role in facilitating capital accumulation. The findings demonstrate that the state's developmentalist orientation has transformed its role from a regulator of competing land interests into an active facilitator of investment, particularly through the expansive and contested interpretation of the concept of “public interest” to legitimize large-scale land transfers. In practice, the invocation of public interest functions not merely as a legal justification but also as a political mechanism through which dispossession is rendered administratively acceptable and legally defensible. Consequently, the legal framework does not operate as a neutral instrument for balancing development objectives and the protection of land rights. Rather, it constitutes an institutional mechanism through which asymmetrical power relations among the state, corporate actors, and affected communities are reproduced and legitimized. This article argues that land acquisition law in Indonesia should therefore be understood not merely as a regulatory framework governing dispossession, but as an active legal instrument in the production and reproduction of dispossessive relations. This finding contributes to critical socio-legal debates by demonstrating how legal legitimacy and developmentalist rationality intersect in the institutionalization of land dispossession.

title: Đề xuất kiến trúc và mô phỏng nút cảm biến thông minh hỗ trợ quy trình dMRV tại hệ sinh thái carbon xanh rừng ngập mặn
source: Can Tho University Journal of Science
summary: This study proposes the architecture and evaluates the simulation of a smart sensor node integrating an ESP32 microcontroller and LoRa P2P to collect supplementary environmental data for the digital Measurement, Reporting, and Verification
tags: Enhanced Data Rates for GSM Evolution
content: This study proposes the architecture and evaluates the simulation of a smart sensor node integrating an ESP32 microcontroller and LoRa P2P to collect supplementary environmental data for the digital Measurement, Reporting, and Verification (dMRV) process in mangroves. Instead of traditional hardware manufacturing, this research applies edge computing to establish a transparent data platform designed to support dMRV requirements. The architecture collects physical parameters (hydrostatic pressure, pH, electrical conductivity) as environmental covariates to support the assessment of the hydroperiod related to carbon conservation. Through Proof-of-Concept simulation, the exponential moving average algorithm embedded at the edge demonstrates capabilities in noise filtering and payload optimization. Benchtop results record a LoRa P2P packet delivery ratio (PDR) exceeding 92.4% at a distance of 1,000 m, alongside low theoretical energy consumption. The architecture initially proves feasible in providing supplementary dMRV data, serving as a directional basis for future field and material trials.

title: CO 2 fertilization to climate limitation: shifting drivers in a dryland forest
summary: Dryland forests represent a significant but uncertain component of the terrestrial carbon sink, where rising CO 2 and intensifying drought and heat stress exert opposing controls on carbon and water fluxes. Using ED2.2-hydraulics calibrated
content: Dryland forests represent a significant but uncertain component of the terrestrial carbon sink, where rising CO 2 and intensifying drought and heat stress exert opposing controls on carbon and water fluxes. Using ED2.2-hydraulics calibrated against 21 years of flux tower and inventory data from Yatir Forest, an arid pine plantation in Israel, we simulated carbon fluxes, biomass dynamics, and water-use efficiency under current climate and high-emission scenarios (SSP3-7.0, SSP5-8.5) through 2100 using five general circulation models. CO 2 fertilization initially enhanced productivity and biomass accumulation despite periodic drought, with the strongest response under SSP3-7.0. Under SSP5-8.5, compound heat and drought stress suppressed productivity below SSP3-7.0 levels despite higher CO 2 concentrations, triggering stand collapse in two projections and eliminating approximately 40 % of accumulated biomass. Driver decomposition showed that forest responses shifted from CO 2 -dominated to interaction-dominated by late century, with compound heat and drought stress explaining 39 %–66 % of the relative importance of all drivers by late century. Apparent biomass gains under severe scenarios reflected accumulation in fewer, larger surviving individuals as stand density declined, masking structural deterioration in aggregate metrics. Functional decline (productivity, water-use efficiency) preceded structural changes by 7–37 years depending on scenario, providing an early warning window before visible deterioration. These results show that CO 2 fertilization benefits cannot compensate for the compound climate extremes that accompany high emissions, and that functional indicators must be monitored alongside structural metrics to detect forest vulnerability in dryland afforestation systems.

title: Coverages and Configurations of CO* and H* on Pt(111) under Realistic Reaction Conditions
summary: Lateral interactions between co-adsorbed species can produce non-random spatial organization that governs the availability of reactive motifs relevant to catalytic behavior. For CO* and H* co-adsorbed on Pt(111), these interactions determin
content: Lateral interactions between co-adsorbed species can produce non-random spatial organization that governs the availability of reactive motifs relevant to catalytic behavior. For CO* and H* co-adsorbed on Pt(111), these interactions determine how the two species distribute across the surface and therefore which local CO*-H* configurations are available under reaction conditions. In this work, we combine density functional theory, cluster expansions, and grand canonical Monte Carlo simulations to determine how CO* and H* organize on Pt(111), and subsequently use electronic surface charge as a controlled perturbation to examine how this organization responds to changes in the underlying energetics. On neutral Pt(111), CO*-H* first-nearest-neighbor interactions are strongly repulsive (0.42 eV), CO*-CO* first-nearest-neighbor interactions are moderately repulsive (0.12 eV), and H*-H* interactions are comparatively weak. These interactions cause CO* to nucleate into islands that grow and coalesce with increasing CO* coverage, while H* preferentially occupies regions outside CO*-rich domains. Consequently, the abundance of CO*-H* nearest-neighbor configurations varies non-monotonically with CO* coverage, reaching a maximum at intermediate coverage before decreasing as CO* islands grow and the adsorbates become increasingly segregated. Positive surface charge strengthens CO* adsorption but also increases CO*-CO* repulsion, producing higher CO* coverages, a broader distribution of CO* island sizes, and larger low-coverage regions between islands where H* can adsorb away from CO*. This suppresses CO*-H* nearest-neighbor configurations relative to the neutral surface. Negative charging weakens CO* adsorption, producing lower CO* coverages, higher H* coverages, and less consolidated CO* islands, thereby increasing the prevalence of mixed CO*-H* local environments. At intermediate CO* coverage, CO* islands enter a regime of accelerated growth and coalescence that coincides with a shallow plateau in H* coverage. This coincidence suggests that the onset of CO* island coalescence is accompanied by a reorganization of the co-adsorbed layer. Further, it illustrates the strong influence of lateral interactions on the formation of potentially reactive motifs, highlighting how they become influential in determining catalytic reactivity.

title: Soft spatial imaginaries as a regional dynamic capability
summary: Soft spatial imaginaries offer a novel conceptualisation of a regional dynamic capability to adapt to and shape collective action on regional development challenges towards desirable futures. This capability encompasses six dimensions embed
content: Soft spatial imaginaries offer a novel conceptualisation of a regional dynamic capability to adapt to and shape collective action on regional development challenges towards desirable futures. This capability encompasses six dimensions embedded within a time- and region-specific opportunity space: sensing change, seizing opportunities, transforming organisations, boundary organisations, place leadership and continuous activity. By combining these concepts for the first time, we advance the translation of dynamic capabilities into regional studies and progress the growing interest in regional future-making practices for turbulent times. Our conceptualisation provides a broadened scope to understand collective agency in converging multiple actors on an agreed spatial imaginary.

title: Engineering a GO-Gd 2 TiO 5 /g-C 3 N 4 ternary nanocomposite for enhanced electrochemical performance and biodiesel catalysis
summary: A ternary GO-Gd 2 TiO 5 /g-C 3 N 4 nanocomposite was developed as a recyclable heterogeneous nanocatalyst for sustainable biodiesel production from waste cooking oil (WCO).
content: A ternary GO-Gd 2 TiO 5 /g-C 3 N 4 nanocomposite was developed as a recyclable heterogeneous nanocatalyst for sustainable biodiesel production from waste cooking oil (WCO).

title: Engineering advances in polymer-modified bitumen for sustainable road construction: a review
summary: Road infrastructure is under increasing pressure from heavier traffic, wider temperature fluctuations, accelerated aging, and stricter sustainability targets. Conventional bitumen, although widely used as a binder in asphalt pavements, ofte
content: Road infrastructure is under increasing pressure from heavier traffic, wider temperature fluctuations, accelerated aging, and stricter sustainability targets. Conventional bitumen, although widely used as a binder in asphalt pavements, often shows inadequate resistance to rutting at high temperatures, fatigue damage under repeated loading, and thermal cracking at low temperatures. Polymer modification has therefore become one of the most effective strategies for improving binder performance and extending pavement service life. Recent studies show that elastomers, plastomers, recycled polymers, and crumb rubber can substantially enhance the viscoelastic balance, durability, and temperature susceptibility of asphalt binders. At the same time, the field is evolving beyond conventional modification toward multifunctional systems integrating waste-derived materials, nanomaterials, self-healing concepts, and smart sensing technologies. Rather than treating polymer modifiers as isolated material classes, this review establishes a structure-interaction-performance framework linking modifier chemistry and processing with polymer-bitumen interactions, morphology evolution, storage stability, binder rheology, and asphalt-mixture and pavement-level performance. The review therefore considers polymer modification across multiple scales, from binder-level physicochemical and rheological behavior to relevant mixture-level mechanical performance and pavement implications. The framework further integrates emerging sustainable and multifunctional strategies, including waste-derived modifiers, polymer-assisted oxidative upgrading, nanomaterials, self-healing systems, and smart pavement technologies.

title: Ocean stewardship commitment across global businesses
summary: The private sector is increasingly engaging to achieve global sustainability environmental goals, particularly those related to climate and, at a more incipient stage, biodiversity. Nevertheless, an assessment, assisted by natural language
content: The private sector is increasingly engaging to achieve global sustainability environmental goals, particularly those related to climate and, at a more incipient stage, biodiversity. Nevertheless, an assessment, assisted by natural language processing and artificial intelligence processes, of 2,451 leading companies collectively accounting for 70% of the world market capitalization, of their 2021 sustainability reports, revealed that UN sustainable development goal SDG 14 “life below water”—which aims to promote the conservation and sustainable use of marine ecosystems and biodiversity— was referenced by only 9% of the companies assessed, making it one of the least prioritized among the environmental SDGs. Among the companies reporting on SDG14, 52% of them acknowledged at least one of the pressures they may exert on the health of marine ecosystems, with marine water contamination and chemical condition integrity being the impacts most frequently acknowledged. Of the companies addressing some of their impacts, half approached them primarily from a risk-mitigation perspective, while 35% viewed them through both a risk-mitigation and an opportunity lens. Only 15% currently focus on ocean action primarily as a business opportunity. The results show that companies, particularly the more mature ones, are increasingly aware and are starting to recognize the potential of embracing the regenerative blue economy as an opportunity. These companies are beginning to acknowledge the fact that moving them into the blue economy can facilitate value creation through sustainable practices that benefit both businesses and the environment. Catalyzing awareness and action will help deliver the potential of the private sector to contribute to SDG14, and will support the growth of an emerging blue business sector.

title: Enlightened Egoism and Its Discontents: Mapping the Business Case for Doing Good
summary: Abstract Various voices in business ethics and wider discussions of ethical capitalism endorse instrumental or strategic reasons for being ethical. Yet this orientation has at times eluded sustained philosophical engagement by the business
content: Abstract Various voices in business ethics and wider discussions of ethical capitalism endorse instrumental or strategic reasons for being ethical. Yet this orientation has at times eluded sustained philosophical engagement by the business ethics discipline. This article addresses this gap by mapping and critiquing what I term "enlightened egoism"—approaches that draw upon instrumental reasoning to derive normative guidance without recourse to duties, rights, values, or questions of the good. Careful reconstruction reveals that enlightened egoist arguments combine descriptive claims about how business operates with normative conclusions about how businesses ought to behave. Variations in these descriptive claims yield three distinct subtypes—evidential egoism, ends-enclosed egoism, and evolutionary egoism—each prominent in contemporary business ethics discourse. Examples are drawn from stakeholder theory, ESG investing (including hedge fund Engine No. 1's engagement with ExxonMobil), and diversity hiring initiatives. Through immanent critique, I demonstrate that enlightened egoism exhibits fundamental instabilities, specifically around indeterminacy in criteria for action, failure to account for heterogeneity, and conceptual slippage into determinist accounts of behavior. These limitations suggest the need for more rigorous integration of instrumental reasoning within—rather than as replacement for—normative ethical frameworks.

title: Sideswiping Typhoons Exacerbate Autumn Ozone Pollution in Coastal China
summary: Abstract Ozone (O 3 ) pollution in coastal China exhibits a widespread increasing trend in autumn, coinciding with the active period of typhoons. Yet, the role of typhoons in autumn O 3 variations remains unclear. Here, we analyze autumn O
content: Abstract Ozone (O 3 ) pollution in coastal China exhibits a widespread increasing trend in autumn, coinciding with the active period of typhoons. Yet, the role of typhoons in autumn O 3 variations remains unclear. Here, we analyze autumn O 3 evolution during 63 typhoon episodes over 2014–2023, and illustrate diverse impacts of typhoons on O 3 variations over different coastal regions. We find that sideswiping typhoons, which move northward along the coasts, are more likely to trigger O 3 pollution, enhancing surface O 3 by 14.6∼39.5%. Model simulations show that O 3 enhancements over northern coastal regions are primarily resulted from chemical production and vertical transport (VTRA), while horizontal transport becomes the dominant factor responsible for elevated O 3 in southern regions during Typhoon “Muifa.” Impacts of typhoons on autumn O 3 under global warming are further investigated using a pseudo‐global‐warming simulation technique. If the typhoon occurred under a warmer background, substantial O 3 increases during typhoon days would be found, particularly in the northern regions, driven by stronger chemical processes and VTRA. Sensitivity simulations suggest that counteracting this warming‐induced O 3 amplification would require a joint reduction of NO x and VOCs emissions by 30%–75%. This study offers new insights on autumn O 3 variations impacted by typhoons based on observations and model projections, providing a scientific basis for surface O 3 formation and possible control strategy in the warming future.

title: From fragmented farms to verified mitigation: rice clusters as infrastructure for smallholder carbon neutrality
summary: Low-emission rice practices are implemented on individual fields, but their feasibility often depends on shared irrigation, machinery, information and finance. This perspective paper develops a conditional model of the rice cluster as carbo
content: Low-emission rice practices are implemented on individual fields, but their feasibility often depends on shared irrigation, machinery, information and finance. This perspective paper develops a conditional model of the rice cluster as carbon infrastructure. Its contribution is not the claim that collective farming is new, but the specification of when an organization becomes carbon-ready: it must connect a hydrologically meaningful boundary, coordinated mitigation, a common measurement, reporting and verification protocol, transparent cost accounting, and enforceable benefit-sharing. Clustering is justified only when savings in measurement and transaction costs exceed the additional costs of coordination, governance and collective action. Evidence from studies of alternate wetting and drying and cooperative upgrading in Vietnam, together with the emerging rice-cluster architecture in the Philippines, shows both the potential and limits of aggregation. This aper proposes differentiated co-financing in which public funds support shared infrastructure and fixed measurement costs, farmers or value-chain actors co-invest in productive assets according to capacity and expected benefit, and verified-performance payments are distributed under disclosed rules. The appropriate near-term objective is verified emission reduction; carbon neutrality remains a whole-system, long-term claim requiring complete accounting of residual emissions and credible balancing.

title: A dataset on energy crops suitability of high-value marginal land in China
summary: High-value marginal land (HVML) refers to land with poor natural endowments but sufficient biophysical and accessibility conditions to support energy crop cultivation without encroaching on protected areas. The cultivation of energy crops o
content: High-value marginal land (HVML) refers to land with poor natural endowments but sufficient biophysical and accessibility conditions to support energy crop cultivation without encroaching on protected areas. The cultivation of energy crops on HVML is of considerable importance for advancing the energy transition and ensuring ecological security. However, due to the lack of unified evaluation criteria and identification methods, systematic assessments of large-scale, multi-type energy crop cultivation on HVML remain limited, resulting in an insufficient understanding of the suitability characteristics across different crop types and regions. To tackle these challenges, a three-step analytical framework was developed to assess the suitability of cultivating energy crops on HVML, and a dataset on the suitability of energy crop cultivation on HVML in China was produced at a spatial resolution of 1 km. The spatial distribution characteristics of HVML in China from 2000 to 2020 were analyzed by integrating land-use and land-cover data, meteorological data, Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), soil data, and terrain data. Subsequently, the suitability of 69 energy crops on HVML was evaluated using the Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) model and spatial analysis methods. This dataset offers a critical baseline for prioritizing energy crop cultivation on marginal land and provides a valuable tool for researchers, land managers, and policymakers working on national spatial governance, food security, energy security, and carbon neutrality.

title: Seeking Common Ground: How to Reduce Global Emissions in a Polarized World
summary: Seeking Common Ground offers a pragmatic approach to one of today’s most polarizing issues: climate change and the role of the energy industry. Rather than taking sides in the debate between climate advocates and growth proponents, the book
content: Seeking Common Ground offers a pragmatic approach to one of today’s most polarizing issues: climate change and the role of the energy industry. Rather than taking sides in the debate between climate advocates and growth proponents, the book identifies a domain where action does not depend on first winning that argument: the industry’s own production emissions. By focusing on roughly 10% of global emissions, the share that comes from getting oil and gas out of the ground and to market, the author lays out a realistic framework for cuts that are the industry’s direct responsibility, achievable now, and defensible regardless of where a reader stands on the climate debate. This practical guide: • Examines both economic-growth and climate policy perspectives on fossil fuels to locate genuine common ground. • Provides detailed technical analysis of emissions sources and life-cycle assessments. • Showcases proven emission-reduction technologies alongside the research still needed. • Draws on the industry’s own safety-culture transformation, the shift that produced today’s Life-Saving Rules, as a working model for decarbonization. • Offers targeted recommendations for executives, employees, and policymakers. • Equips readers to move past ideological stalemate and take immediate, effective action within one of the world’s most influential industries. Written for energy executives, engineers, geologists, regulators, policymakers, environmental advocates, and informed citizens, the book provides rare common ground in a divisive conversation. Readers will come away with a nuanced understanding of how the oil and gas industry can substantially cut its carbon footprint while continuing to meet global energy needs.

title: Enhancing fire survivability of biochar with medium-entropy oxide coatings
summary: Biochar derived from low-value biomass offers a sustainable platform for lightweight structural and thermal insulation materials; however, its susceptibility to oxidative degradation under prolonged fire exposure limits practical implementa
content: Biochar derived from low-value biomass offers a sustainable platform for lightweight structural and thermal insulation materials; however, its susceptibility to oxidative degradation under prolonged fire exposure limits practical implementation. Here, we report an entropy-engineered ceramic coating strategy to substantially enhance the fire survivability of biochar. Three-metal-element FeMnZn medium-entropy oxide (3ME-MEO) and five-metal-element FeMnZnAlZr MEO (5ME-MEO) coatings were synthesized via a low-temperature, scalable route and uniformly deposited onto porous biochar. Microscopic and spectroscopic analyses reveal homogeneous multielement distributions from the micro- to nanoscale, while the increased compositional complexity of MEO induces greater structural disorder without detectable macroscopic elemental segregation. Under direct ethanol-flame exposure at ~ 1000 °C, pristine biochar suffers severe oxidative degradation, whereas the entropy-engineered coatings effectively preserve the carbon framework. After 20 min, the mass loss decreases from 38.8% for pristine biochar to 23.5% for biochar/3ME-MEO and 18.5% for biochar/5ME-MEO after correcting for coating-derived mass loss. The MEO coatings remain spatially homogeneous after prolonged burning and provide sustained protection against thermal-oxidative attack. Hotplate and modified UL-94-type tests further reveal comparable surface-temperature evolution among the samples despite markedly different degrees of structural degradation. These findings indicate that enhanced fire survivability primarily arises from the protective barrier effect of the MEO coatings, which suppresses oxidative consumption of the carbon framework and mitigates direct flame attack, rather than from thermal insulation.

title: Inclusive Innovation and Green Growth in Emerging and Developing Economies
summary: Abstract Faced with the challenge of balancing economic transformation and environmental preservation, this study examines the role of national innovation capacity in green growth across 30 emerging and developing economies over the 2011–20
content: Abstract Faced with the challenge of balancing economic transformation and environmental preservation, this study examines the role of national innovation capacity in green growth across 30 emerging and developing economies over the 2011–2022 period. Green growth is assessed through GDP carbon intensity, while national innovation capacity is measured by the Global Innovation Index (GII). The analysis is based on a dynamic panel model estimated using the System GMM method, supplemented by Difference GMM estimates, which allow for the potential endogeneity of innovation. The results highlight strong persistence in carbon intensity and suggest that overall innovation capacity does not have a sufficiently robust relationship with green growth in the sample studied. In contrast, gross fixed capital formation is associated with a reduction in carbon intensity in the main Difference GMM estimates. These results underscore that the contribution of innovation to green growth depends on the context in which innovation capabilities are developed and mobilized and does not automatically result from a general improvement in national innovation capacity.

title: Operationalizing level(s) macro-objective 2 for residential renovation: a circularity assessment workflow in a collaborative digital platform
summary: Purpose The practical implementation of the European level(s) framework, particularly Macro-Objective 2 (MO-2) on resource-efficient and circular material life cycles, remains challenging due to complex data requirements, limited availabili
content: Purpose The practical implementation of the European level(s) framework, particularly Macro-Objective 2 (MO-2) on resource-efficient and circular material life cycles, remains challenging due to complex data requirements, limited availability of lifecycle information during early project stages and fragmented digital workflows. This study aims to develop and demonstrate a Building Information Modeling (BIM)-to-level(s) workflow for operationalizing the EU level(s) MO-2 indicators at the permit stage of residential renovation projects. The study specifically addresses the challenge of incomplete permit-stage information by integrating existing–proposed–delta analysis with an evidence-quality layer that makes the evidential basis and limitations of assessment outputs explicit. Design/methodology/approach A design science research approach was adopted to develop and demonstrate a proof-of-concept workflow using permit-stage Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) models of a Swedish residential renovation project. The workflow integrates IFC-based quantity extraction, semantic enrichment, material and product proxy information, existing–proposed–delta classification and level(s)-aligned calculations for Indicators 2.1–2.4. An author-defined Evidence Quality Score (EQS) was introduced to distinguish directly available information from interpreted, proxy-based and unavailable evidence. The resulting outputs were structured for conceptual integration within a collaborative digital platform (CDP). The workflow was assessed through internal consistency and traceability checks rather than independent expert, construction-stage or multi-project validation. Findings The case study demonstrates that permit-stage IFC information can support structured, preliminary assessment of all four level(s) MO-2 indicators when supplemented by controlled semantic enrichment and documented assumptions. The existing-proposed-delta logic enables retained, removed, modified and newly introduced elements to be distinguished, supporting more explicit identification of renovation-related material changes. The evidence-quality layer makes information gaps and proxy-dependent calculations visible and helps avoid presenting scenario-based estimates as verified construction-stage outcomes. However, the resulting quantities, circularity measures and evidence-quality scores should be interpreted as case-specific estimates rather than validated performance measurements. Research limitations/implications The study is limited to a single Swedish residential renovation case and uses permit-stage information that does not include verified demolition quantities, contractor waste records, complete as-built material inventories or construction-stage observations. The EQS is an author-defined heuristic measure and has not been independently validated through expert elicitation, inter-rater testing or empirical calibration. title: Natural Rubber: Biomass and Its Sustainable Resources and Functional Properties
summary: Natural rubber, obtained from Hevea brasiliensis , is a plant-derived material widely used in industry and produced through the absorption of atmospheric carbon dioxide. It is therefore expected to contribute to the realization of a carbon-
content: Natural rubber, obtained from Hevea brasiliensis , is a plant-derived material widely used in industry and produced through the absorption of atmospheric carbon dioxide. It is therefore expected to contribute to the realization of a carbon-neutral society as a renewable raw material. This chapter first introduces naturally occurring cis -1,4-polyisoprene biosynthesized by various plants and highlights the advantages and usefulness of natural rubber derived from H. brasiliensis . To ensure a sustainable supply of naturally occurring cis -1,4-polyisoprene, efforts have also been made to utilize not only H. brasiliensis , which grows in tropical climates, but also guayule, which thrives in desert regions, and Russian dandelion, which grows in steppe climates. Second, methods for removing proteins from natural rubber are described as key technologies required for the precise synthesis of organic materials using natural rubber as a source. Deproteinized natural rubber and protein-free natural rubber produced through these methods are also introduced. Furthermore, the nanostructure, mechanical properties, proton conductivity, and photoreactivity of graft copolymers prepared from these purified natural rubbers are discussed. Finally, this chapter explores future perspectives based on the intrinsic characteristics of natural rubber, promising rubber-producing plants, purification technologies for sustainable rubber production, and recent advances in the modification and functionalization of natural rubber.

title: Oral absorption, bioavailability, and uptake routes of omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid derived 17(S)-HDHA, 15(S)-HEPE, RvD1 and RvE1 in healthy rats
summary: Abstract Lipid mediators derived from omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (n-3 PUFA), eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), are critical mediators of inflammation. In contrast to EPA and DHA, the bioavailability of the
content: Abstract Lipid mediators derived from omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (n-3 PUFA), eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), are critical mediators of inflammation. In contrast to EPA and DHA, the bioavailability of their lipid mediator derivatives remains unstudied. Oral, intravenous (IV), and intraduodenal administration of stable isotope labeled n-3 PUFA, and lipid mediators was used to establish their bioavailability, half-lives, and absorption routes in rats. Blood and lymph were analyzed by liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry. Orally administered 17(S)-HDHA-d5, 15(S)-HEPE-d5, and RvD1-d5 were rapidly absorbed into the unesterified plasma pool, reaching peak concentrations within 15 min to 1 h, with a bioavailability of 3–6%. IV administration revealed rapid plasma clearance of n-3 PUFA and administered lipid mediators (half-life ~30 s). Lymph cannulation reduced plasma appearance of 17(S)-HDHA-d5 and 15(S)-HEPE-d5 but not RvD1-d5, indicating structure-dependent changes in absorption via lymphatic or portal routes. These findings demonstrate n-3 PUFA-derived lipid mediators are absorbed following oral intake, providing a foundation for oral delivery.

title: Decoupled electrolysis strategies for direct hydrogenation reactions under mild conditions
summary: Electrochemistry is an increasingly important field within the physical sciences, offering sustainable alternatives to conventional chemical processes. In particular, the use of redox mediators in electrochemical systems provides a means of
content: Electrochemistry is an increasingly important field within the physical sciences, offering sustainable alternatives to conventional chemical processes. In particular, the use of redox mediators in electrochemical systems provides a means of controlling electron transfer and improving selectivity under mild conditions. Polyoxometalates have attracted significant attention as redox active species due to their well defined structures and reversible redox behaviour. The work presented in this thesis focuses on the investigation of silicotungstic acid as redox mediator for the electrochemical reduction of organic substrates. The aim of this study was to examine the electrochemical behaviour of the mediator, evaluate its reversibility, and assess its effectiveness in facilitating reduction reactions under controlled conditions. Chapter 1 provides an overview of electrochemical processes and introduces the role of redox mediators, with particular emphasis on polyoxometalates and their application in organic electrosynthesis. Chapter 2 describes the experimental techniques employed throughout this work, including electrochemical methods such as cyclic voltammetry and bulk electrolysis, as well as analytical techniques including gas chromatography (GC), nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), ultraviolet-visible (UV-Vis) spectroscopy, and Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy. Chapter 3, the electrochemical properties of silicotungstic acid are examined, including its redox behaviour and stability during repeated cycling. The reversibility of the mediator system is evaluated using cyclic voltammetry, and conditions for controlled electrolysis are established. Chapter 4 investigates application of the reduced mediator in the chemical reduction of organic substrates, including nitriles, ketones, and aldehydes. Product formation is confirmed using GC, GC-MS, NMR, and FT-IR analysis. The efficiency and selectivity of the process are assessed under different experimental conditions. Chapter 5 explores further applications and optimisation of the system, including variations in electrolysis conditions and assessment of competing side reactions such as hydrogen evolution. The role of electrochemical parameters in influencing reaction outcomes is discussed. Finally, Chapter 6 summarises the key findings of this work and outlines potential directions for future research. Overall, this study demonstrates that silicotungstic acid is an effective redox mediator for electrochemical reduction processes. The results highlight its stability, reversibility, and applicability in facilitating selective transformations, contributing to the development of more sustainable electrochemical methodologies.

title: Adaptive temperature regulation method for PEM electrolyzer based on electro-thermal-mass parameter prediction of electrolysis system
summary: Abstract Improving operational safety under fluctuating wind-solar power input constitutes a critical challenge for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) technology, and developing an efficient and fast operating condition reg
content: Abstract Improving operational safety under fluctuating wind-solar power input constitutes a critical challenge for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) technology, and developing an efficient and fast operating condition regulation method is an important approach to address this challenge. Nevertheless, the widely adopted proportional-integral-derivative (PID) control method relies heavily on manual tuning experience, which renders it incapable of precisely regulating the strongly nonlinear and tightly coupled electrolysis process and brings risks of temperature overshoot and response lag. Therefore, an online adaptive temperature regulation method for electrolyzer integrating an electro-thermal-mass performance prediction model with an adaptive model predictive control (AMPC) algorithm is proposed. The electro-thermal-mass performance prediction model comprehensively accounts for electric conduction, heat transfer, and multi-phase mass transport. Meanwhile, the control algorithm supports real-time updating of electrolyzer operating states. The performance prediction model is validated through experimental tests on a 100 kW PEM electrolyzer. Results show that the proposed model achieves a temperature prediction accuracy of 5.3%. It is also found that circulating cooling water temperature varies more mildly than water flow rate, so it is more applicable to temperature regulation under dynamic operating conditions. A comparison of control performance is conducted between the proposed AMPC method and the PID control method to verify the effectiveness of the adaptive regulation strategy. Results indicate that the AMPC method shortens the temperature rise response time by 0.55 h. Under simulated fluctuating wind-solar power input conditions, the AMPC method can adjust the electrolyzer temperature to the target value within 10.7 min, with the temperature overshoot 4.2 °C lower than that of PID control. This research is expected to provide theoretical references and technical tools for the safe and reliable application of proton exchange membrane water electrolysis technology in future large-scale direct wind-solar coupled hydrogen production systems.

title: Catalytic performance of Pd-Ni-Co/Al 2 O 3 catalysts in methane combustion
summary: Abstract Pd-based catalysts were prepared by successive wet impregnation of γ-Al 2 O 3 with aqueous solutions of Ni, Co and Pd nitrates: Ni and Co were first co-deposited from a mixed solution, followed by Pd introduction in a second impreg
content: Abstract Pd-based catalysts were prepared by successive wet impregnation of γ-Al 2 O 3 with aqueous solutions of Ni, Co and Pd nitrates: Ni and Co were first co-deposited from a mixed solution, followed by Pd introduction in a second impregnation step. They were characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), temperature programmed reduction (TPR), temperature programmed oxidation (O 2 -TPD), X-ray fluorescence measurements (XRF), BET method. The variation of the nickel content during the synthesis of the PdNix0.5Co/Al 2 O 3 catalysts leads to the formation of different oxide phases on the surface. At nickel contents up to 1 wt%, the main phases are NiO weakly interacting with the support and NiAl 2 O 4 and CoAl 2 O 4 . As the nickel content increases, strongly non-stoichiometric oxide phases appear, consisting of NiO moderately interacting with Al 2 O 3 and mixed Ni–Al phases. Pd 0 , Pd 2+ and Pd 4+ species are all observed on the surface of the catalysts calcined at 450 °C, whereas calcination of the cobalt- and nickel-modified support at 800 °C results in the formation of aluminate phases on the surface and the stabilisation of palladium as PdO. The highest activity of the catalyst containing 5 wt% Ni is very likely a result of the good contact of PdO with nickel aluminate and NiO. High-temperature calcination at 800 °C enhanced the catalytic activity of the catalyst with the lowest nickel content, owing to the increased amount of nickel aluminate on the surface.

title: CarbonCrediBERT: Expert-Guided Few-Shot and Selective Classification of Carbon Credit Disclosures
summary: Abstract Corporate reports increasingly discuss carbon credits in relation to net-zero targets, offsetting claims, and climate transition plans, particularly as climate-related financial disclosure requirements expand. Analysing these discl
content: Abstract Corporate reports increasingly discuss carbon credits in relation to net-zero targets, offsetting claims, and climate transition plans, particularly as climate-related financial disclosure requirements expand. Analysing these disclosures at scale remains difficult because terms such as credit, offset, and net also occur in unrelated financial, accounting, and operational contexts. Expert-labelled data are also costly to produce and often contain substantial class imbalance. We propose CarbonCrediBERT, an expert-guided natural language processing framework that classifies paragraphs according to carbon credit relevance, sentiment, and reported credit use, while referring uncertain cases for human review. CarbonCrediBERT combines an expert defined taxonomy, hard-negative examples drawn from closely related but nonrelevant passages, and classification methods suited to small expert-labelled datasets. Using annual, climate, sustainability, and ESG reports published by ASX100 companies in 2024–2025, the framework produced 8,299 keyword-matched sentence records and a balanced candidate pool of 15,026 paragraphs. We evaluated ClimateBERT and DistilRoBERTa fine-tuning and SetFit–MiniLM few-shot learning using three task-specific datasets of 100 expert-labelled paragraphs each. Five-fold development cross-validation selected fine-tuned ClimateBERT for carbon credit relevance, achieving 93.8% accuracy, and SetFit–MiniLM for sentiment and reported credit use. These results show that broad climate-language detection alone is insufficient for identifying carbon credit disclosures and that no single modelling approach performs best across all three tasks. They also highlight the continuing importance of expert judgement, particularly for sentiment and ambiguous statements about credit use. Future work will expand the domain corpus and expert-labelled evidence and evaluate transfer across companies, reporting years, and jurisdictions, establishing a pathway towards a reusable CarbonCrediBERT foundation model for carbon credit disclosure analysis.

title: Green Tourism Development in Hanoi in the Current Period
summary: Against the backdrop of climate change, the depletion of natural resources, and environmental pollution, which are increasingly becoming challenges to socio-economic development, green and sustainable tourism development has attracted growi
content: Against the backdrop of climate change, the depletion of natural resources, and environmental pollution, which are increasingly becoming challenges to socio-economic development, green and use of resources, encourage the adoption of renewable energy, conserve biodiversity, and enhance the value of natural and cultural heritage.At the same time, green tourism emphasizes strengthening the responsibilities of tourism businesses, visitors, and local communities, thereby ensuring a balance among economic, social, and environmental interests.Therefore, green tourism development is not only
