title: Same, Same? Supply Chain Due Diligence Under EU CSDDD And EUDR.
summary: As instruments of the EU Green Deal, both the EU Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD) and the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) impose supply chain due diligence obligations on companies. Their notions of due diligence,
content: As instruments of the EU Green Deal, both the EU Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD) and the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) impose supply chain due diligence obligations on companies. Their notions of due diligence, however, differ fundamentally in their underlying logics. CSDDD establishes an outward-facing, process-oriented due diligence rooted in the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights: companies must identify adverse impacts on people and the environment, engage with affected suppliers, and treat disengagement as a last resort. EUDR establishes an inward-facing, binary compliance framework: operators must demonstrate traceability to the upstream end and negligible risk of non-compliance before placing forest-risk commodities on the EU market, with no obligation to engage with or remediate conditions at origin. Drawing on supply chain management perspectives and comparative analysis of the two instruments' legal texts, including the Omnibus amendments, this Article argues that the simultaneous operation of these divergent frameworks creates regulatory ambiguity for companies, and that EUDR's more immediate and binary enforcement architecture creates structural incentives toward supplier exclusion – with consequences that affect smallholder farmers and producers in high deforestation-risk regions and undermine CSDDD's engagement imperative, EUDR’s no-deforestation ambitions as well as the EU’s Green Deal and Just Transition ambitions.

title: The Structural Evolution, Institutional Idiosyncrasies, and Global Integration of China's Capital Market
summary: This paper examines the comprehensive trajectory, institutional framework, and structural mechanics of China’s capital market from its informal emergence in 1978 to its current status as the world's second-largest capital market. Moving bey
content: This paper examines the comprehensive trajectory, institutional framework, and structural mechanics of China’s capital market from its informal emergence in 1978 to its current status as the world's second-largest capital market. Moving beyond conventional Western economic convergence paradigms, this study analyzes how China has engineered a dual-track financial ecosystem. In this system, state-guided capital allocation and party-state political institutional oversight operate alongside highly liquid, digitized equity and debt markets. We map the historical periodization of the market, dissect the distinct structural mechanisms governing the A-share equity markets, analyze the expanding domestic corporate bond framework, and investigate the rapid institutionalization of green finance and techno-industrial capital targeting. Finally, the paper assesses the systemic risks, retail investor behavioral anomalies, and strategic cross-border liberalization mechanisms such as the Connect programs that define China's unique financial footprint. This analysis demonstrates how the politicization of corporate governance and iterative regulatory experimentation counter traditional path-dependency theories, offering an alternative model of financial market development within a state capitalist political economy.

title: Interfacial Stability Engineering of Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolyzer Anodes
summary: ABSTRACT Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) is central to renewable hydrogen production, yet anode durability remains difficult to predict from half‐cell catalyst metrics alone. In membrane electrode assemblies (MEAs), acid
content: ABSTRACT Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) is central to renewable hydrogen production, yet anode durability remains difficult to predict from half‐cell catalyst metrics alone. In membrane electrode assemblies (MEAs), acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts must remain active while staying coupled to electron, proton, water and oxygen transport networks. This Review frames PEMWE anode degradation as a multilevel interfacial stability problem. It first defines the near‐surface stability window of Ir/Ru active sites through valence evolution, hydroxylation, lattice‐oxygen participation, reconstruction and metal dissolution. It then shows how this window is reshaped in MEAs by catalyst‐layer percolation, ionomer distribution, pore architecture, porous transport layer (PTL)/catalyst‐layer contact, membrane contamination, metal migration and dynamic operating stresses. Layered diagnostic strategies are summarized to trace macroscopic performance decay back to specific interfacial instability pathways. Future directions are discussed in terms of standardized evaluation, realistic operating environments and data‐driven materials‐interface‐device optimization. This interfacial framework provides a basis for designing durable, non‐noble‐metal PEMWE anodes for practical renewable hydrogen production.

title: Forced Labour Regulation: A Step Forward in the Pursuit of a More Sustainable World?
summary: After the adoption of the European Green Deal various instruments have been put forward with the objective of promoting sustainability. Most of these instruments pursue the integration of environmental considerations in EU law and policy ma
content: After the adoption of the European Green Deal various instruments have been put forward with the objective of promoting sustainability. Most of these instruments pursue the integration of environmental considerations in EU law and policy making, while respect for human rights is slowly entering the agenda as part of due diligence instruments. Moreover, relevant scholarly work has mainly focused on the interaction of the environment and the economy as key pillars of sustainability. The social pillar of sustainability has appeared more marginally in these scholarly debates. This article brings social sustainability to the centre and evaluates whether the recently adopted Forced Labour Regulation is a step further in the EU pursuit of a more sustainable world. To do so, the article argues that human dignity, the promotion of social justice and respect for participation are the core of the normative demands inherent social sustainability. Following, it presents the Forced Labour Regulation, its key provisions and the broader international and European context against which the instrument was adopted. Finally, the article assesses the Regulation in light of each of the normative demands inherent in social sustainability. While the instrument seems to fare well in relation to a discursive appeal to human rights as well as respect for participation, more critical points are made in relation to the protection of human dignity and the pursuit of social justice. Overall, it is unclear whether the EU can indeed pursue a more sustainable world when all it delivers is a cleaner internal market.

title: CAD-YOLO11: a lightweight class-aware dynamic optimization framework for pipeline defect detection
summary: Abstract Pipeline defect detection is crucial for ensuring the safety and reliability of industrial infrastructure. However, lightweight object detectors often suffer from insufficient feature representation and category-specific optimizati
content: Abstract Pipeline defect detection is crucial for ensuring the safety and reliability of industrial infrastructure. However, lightweight object detectors often suffer from insufficient feature representation and category-specific optimization capability when dealing with small-scale defects, weak textures, and visually similar defect categories. This paper proposes CAD-YOLO11, a lightweight class-aware dynamic optimization framework based on YOLO11 for accurate and efficient pipeline defect detection. The framework incorporates an adaptive downsampling strategy to improve fine-grained feature preservation during feature compression, while introducing a DetectAux_ClsEnhance branch to provide additional category-level supervision for enhancing semantic discrimination. Furthermore, a Class-aware Weighted Dynamic Optimization (CWDO) strategy is developed, including Class-Aware Dynamic Top-k Assignment (CADT) and Class-Aware Coordinate Optimization (CA-CN), to achieve category-adaptive positive sample selection and bounding box optimization according to different defect characteristics.Experiments conducted on the Daji pipeline defect dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of CAD-YOLO11. Compared with the original YOLO11n, the proposed method improves mAP50 from 88.64% to 91.13% and mAP50-95 from 66.52% to 69.90%, while reducing computational complexity from 6.3 GFLOPs to 5.3 GFLOPs. The proposed framework achieves a favorable balance between detection accuracy and computational efficiency, providing an effective solution for real-time industrial pipeline defect inspection.

title: Development of FDM ‐Printed Bio‐Based TPU / CNT / Fe 3 O 4 Nanocomposites for Potential Wearable Applications
summary: ABSTRACT The integration of multifunctional thermoplastic polyurethane into additive manufacturing offers new opportunities for advanced elastomeric functional materials. In this study, bio‐based thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) nanocomposi
content: ABSTRACT The integration of multifunctional thermoplastic polyurethane into additive manufacturing offers new opportunities for advanced elastomeric functional materials. In this study, bio‐based thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) nanocomposites were synthesized from polypropylene succinate (PPS), 1,5‐pentamethylene diisocyanate (PDI), and 1,3‐propanediol (PDO), and reinforced with carbon nanotubes (CNTs) and magnetite (Fe 3 O 4 ) nanoparticles via a solvent‐free prepolymer process. FT‐IR confirmed successful polymerization, while FIB‐SEM revealed homogeneous dispersion of the hybrid nanofillers within the TPU matrix. CNTs significantly enhanced melt elasticity and stress transfer, whereas Fe 3 O 4 imparted magnetic responsiveness, resulting in multifunctional hybrid nanocomposites. The storage modulus increased to 27.10 kPa for the TPU/CNT composite and remained at 16.99 kPa after Fe 3 O 4 incorporation, indicating sufficient melt elasticity for stable filament extrusion and FDM printing. The TPU/CNT/Fe 3 O 4 hybrid composite exhibited a 23.8% increase in tensile strength together with enhanced magnetic responsiveness. Furthermore, the composite filaments exhibited stable extrusion, excellent layer fidelity, and high dimensional accuracy during FDM printing, enabling the fabrication of auxetic structures. These results demonstrate that the hybrid bio‐based TPU provides a multifunctional platform integrating mechanical reinforcement, magnetic responsiveness, and additive manufacturability for potential flexible wearable applications.

title: Defect engineered Li₂O-ZrO₂-NiO multi-metal oxide nanocomposite exhibiting enhanced structural properties optical behavior and cytotoxic activity
summary: Multi-metal oxide nanocomposites have attracted considerable attention due to their tunable physicochemical properties and multifunctional applications. In the present study, a Li2O–ZrO2–NiO multi-metal oxide nanocomposite was successfully
content: Multi-metal oxide nanocomposites have attracted considerable attention due to their tunable physicochemical properties and multifunctional applications. In the present study, a Li2O–ZrO2–NiO multi-metal oxide nanocomposite was successfully synthesized via a facile co-precipitation route followed by controlled thermal treatment. The structural and compositional features of the material were systematically characterized using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT–IR), energy-dispersive X-ray analysis (EDAX), UV–Visible spectroscopy, and thermal analysis (TGA-DTG-DSC). XRD results confirmed the formation of crystalline ZrO2 and NiO phases with nanoscale dimensions, while FT–IR spectra evidenced the formation of characteristic metal–oxygen bonds. The nanocomposite exhibited broad optical absorption spanning the ultraviolet to visible regions (250–950 nm), attributed to defect states and oxygen vacancies induced by lithium incorporation. The thermal stability of the composite was established, and the choice of 900 °C as the calcination temperature for phase-pure oxides was justified by thermal analysis (TGA-DTG-DSC), which exhibited that precursor decomposition and carbonate-to-oxide phase transformation were nearly complete above 680 °C. Elemental analysis confirmed the presence of constituent metals with high purity. The biological activity of the synthesized nanocomposite was evaluated against HepG2 cells using the MTT assay, demonstrating a pronounced concentration-dependent cytotoxicity with an IC50 value of approximately 10 µg/mL. Morphological observations further revealed significant cellular damage, including shrinkage and loss of adhesion, suggesting apoptosis-mediated cell death. The enhanced performance of the nanocomposite can be attributed to synergistic interactions among Li, Zr, and Ni oxides, as well as defect-mediated electronic modifications that promote the generation of reactive oxygen species. Overall, the results highlighted the potential of the Li2O–ZrO2–NiO multi-metal oxide nanocomposite as a promising candidate for advanced catalytic and anticancer applications, offering a simple synthesis strategy and improved functional properties.

title: Beyond ecological miscommunication: a system theory approach to climate litigation
summary: The increasing number of lawsuits against European carbon majors has sparked interest among legal scholars. However, the literature has paid little attention to the sociological dimension of climate litigation. This paper makes two contribu
content: The increasing number of lawsuits against European carbon majors has sparked interest among legal scholars. However, the literature has paid little attention to the sociological dimension of climate litigation. This paper makes two contributions. First, it develops a systems-theory Framework to analyse key social dynamics that emerge between social systems at stake in corporate climate litigation, including science, law, economics, politics, media, and organisations (NGOs). Second, this paper investigates the overlooked key role of NGOs in climate litigation. Findings from 16 qualitative semi-structured interviews with lawyers and members of NGOs involved in corporate climate litigation over loss and damage indicate that NGOs ease systemic buondaries for three reasons. First, NGO’s climate litigation campaings augment ecological irritation between social systems. Second, NGOs’ operational structures are coupled with a plurality of social systems’ codes, which bring different systems into collaboration. Third, climate litigation supported by NGOs requires the practice networking among different NGOs and expert affine to diffferent social systems. The increase in resonance, coupling- and network-oriented characters of NGOs’ climate litigation campaigns redefines Luhmann’s key conceptual tools, such as structural coupling, the relationship system-environment (ecological communication), as well as his description of organisation as a forum of interdependence interruption ( Intedependezunterbrechung ).

title: Nonlinearities in the road freight–transport CO2 relationship in Europe
summary: This study examines whether the relationship between road freight activity and transport CO 2 emissions changes as road freight activity expands and across the conditional emissions distribution in 18 European countries from 1999 to 2024. M
content: This study examines whether the relationship between road freight activity and transport CO 2 emissions changes as road freight activity expands and across the conditional emissions distribution in 18 European countries from 1999 to 2024. Method of Moments Quantile Regression (MMQR) is complemented by Fully Modified Ordinary Least Squares, Driscoll–Kraay fixed-effects estimation, and XGBoost–SHAP analysis. MMQR results indicate a U-shaped association: the linear freight term is negative and statistically significant across all quantiles, whereas the squared term is positive and significant. The estimated turning points lie within the observed freight range and shift downward toward higher emission quantiles, suggesting that the marginal association turns positive at lower freight levels when conditional emissions are relatively high. Motor vehicle production and economic development are positively associated with transport emissions, whereas urbanization is negatively associated across the distribution. Trade openness shows a more conditional relationship, becoming increasingly negative toward the upper quantiles. Alternative estimators preserve the nonlinear freight pattern, while XGBoost–SHAP identifies road freight as the dominant predictor and reveals corresponding nonlinear predictive structure. Overall, the findings suggest that freight decarbonization policies should account for both the scale of road freight activity and prevailing emissions conditions.

title: Harmonic performance evaluation of multicarrier PWM in a three-level three-switch PV microinverter
summary: This paper presents a comparative performance evaluation of level-shifted pulse-width modulation (PWM) techniques applied to a three-level T-type photovoltaic (PV) inverter configured as a single-stage microinverter. Unlike conventional mic
content: This paper presents a comparative performance evaluation of level-shifted pulse-width modulation (PWM) techniques applied to a three-level T-type photovoltaic (PV) inverter configured as a single-stage microinverter. Unlike conventional microinverter topologies that typically require a greater number of power semiconductor switches or an external output filter, the proposed configuration employs a reduced-switch three-level architecture intended for low-voltage self-consumption (SELCO) applications. The topology was modelled and evaluated in MATLAB/Simulink under Standard Test Conditions of 1000 W/m² solar irradiance and a cell temperature of 25 °C. A single PV module configuration (Np = 1, Ns = 1) provides a 48 Vdc input suitable for residential applications. The primary contribution of this work lies in the application and comparative evaluation of level-shifted PWM strategies within a reduced-switch three-level microinverter topology. Three level-shifted PWM strategies, namely Phase Disposition (PD-PWM), Phase Opposition Disposition (POD-PWM), and Alternative Phase Opposition Disposition (APOD-PWM), are implemented and benchmarked against a conventional Pulse Generator modulation strategy. The output-voltage and output-current harmonic characteristics were evaluated using fast Fourier transform analysis. The simulation results demonstrate that PD-PWM achieves the lowest current total harmonic distortion, reducing the THDi from 16.36% with the conventional PG method to 2.16%, corresponding to an 86.8% reduction. These findings demonstrate that appropriate multicarrier PWM selection can substantially improve the simulated current harmonic performance of the reduced-switch three-level T-type microinverter while preserving its compact circuit configuration.

title: Graphene/Si Heterojunction Platform with a Multifunctional Atomic Bridging Layer for Photoelectrochemical CO2 Reduction
summary: Abstract The facile integration and stability of Si-based photoelectrode architectures are the remaining challenges in the photoelectrochemical (PEC) conversion of CO2 to fuels. In this work, the single-atomic-layer graphene is used as a fu
content: Abstract The facile integration and stability of Si-based photoelectrode architectures are the remaining challenges in the photoelectrochemical (PEC) conversion of CO2 to fuels. In this work, the single-atomic-layer graphene is used as a functional bridging layer to integrate both Si photocathodes and photoanodes, which enable the direct electrodeposition of metal-based electrocatalysts (Cu, Ag, and In–Sn alloys) and a semiconductor-based catalyst Ni–Fe layered double hydroxide (Ni–Fe LDH) on graphene/Si heterojunction electrodes for PEC CO2 reduction and O2 evolution reactions, respectively. We demonstrate a PEC device with a full-cell configuration consisting of an In–Sn/graphene/Si heterojunction photocathode and a Ni–Fe LDH/graphene/Si heterojunction photoanode, exhibiting a reduced photovoltage of ∼1080 mV compared to the electrochemical counterparts. A self-powered PEC CO2 reduction with a solar-to-fuel conversion efficiency of 3.2% can be obtained by integrating the graphene/Si heterojunction photocathode and photoanode with a Si photovoltaic. In addition, in situ PEC X-ray absorption spectroscopy analyses show that the electrodeposited catalysts on the graphene layer lead to the transport of photogenerated electrons and preserve durability throughout the reaction. Utilizing graphene as a chemically inert atomic bridging layer enables the seamless integration of Si photoelectrodes with various catalysts, providing a platform for the PEC CO2 reduction reaction.

title: The water use paradox in China: Phenomenon, driving factors, and policy implications
summary: Study region China. Study focus Although China’s water use (WU) has declined since 2013, national water demand diverges when accounting for virtual water (VW) embodied in international trade. This study defines real water consumption (RWC)
content: Study region China. Study focus Although China’s water use (WU) has declined since 2013, national water demand diverges when accounting for virtual water (VW) embodied in international trade. This study defines real water consumption (RWC) as WU plus VW in imports minus VW in exports, quantifying China’s RWC from 1990 to 2021. We construct time-varying water-use coefficients rather than fixed coefficients and integrate them into a multiregional input–output model spanning 189 economies. We examine the divergence between RWC and WU, decompose the drivers of RWC, and assess how trade reshapes China’s water stress. New hydrological insights for the region China’s RWC increased continuously, exceeding WU by 44.30 billion m 3 in 2021; thus, WU has decoupled from economic growth solely on the production side. Around 2014, China became a net VW importer, drawing increasingly on agricultural imports from developing economies. By 2021, agriculture constituted 55.53% of total VW imports, and net imports supplied 6.96% of national water demand, mitigating water stress. The increase in RWC was driven primarily by consumption scale, which contributed 252.72% to the total change, whereas demographic growth played a secondary role and efficiency gains failed to offset consumption expansion. Consequently, China’s water security cannot be evaluated solely from withdrawals; it is increasingly tied to external agricultural suppliers, necessitating demand-side governance, supply-chain trade resilience, and efficiency enhancements.

title: NGO Inc or Guardians of the Just Transition? Navigating Diverging Narratives on Civil Society in EU Corporate Sustainability Negotiations
summary: This article examines how civil society organisations are framed and regulated in recent EU corporate sustainability regulation, with a particular focus on the 2025 Omnibus I proposals. By investigating the Omnibus I proposals, the article
content: This article examines how civil society organisations are framed and regulated in recent EU corporate sustainability regulation, with a particular focus on the 2025 Omnibus I proposals. By investigating the Omnibus I proposals, the article finds two opposing framings of NGOs: on the one hand, an individualising tendency that views civil society actors as representing their own specific interests and on the other hand a collectivising tendency where civil society is seen as representing public interest and the environment at large. These opposing framings are part of a broader tendency across EU regulatory instruments relevant for civil society actors, which the article evidences through an analysis of the EU Civil Society Strategy and the Multiannual Financial Framework. Finally, the article identifies future research opportunities to analyse potential implications of these framings for EU corporate sustainability governance: a lack of coherence, a more fragmented corporate sustainability legal landscape characterised by normative ambiguity, and a changing understanding of public and private governance in EU corporate sustainability frameworks.

title: Facteurs Déterminants de la Transition Énergétique : Preuves Empiriques à partir d'un Panel des Pays de la région Mena
summary: Résumé Cette étude examine la transition énergétique dans quatre pays de la région Mena (Maroc,Tunisie, Egypte et la Jordanie) sur une période de 34 ans, en mettant l’accent sur l’interaction entre l’IDE, l’innovation technologique, l’urban
content: Résumé Cette étude examine la transition énergétique dans quatre pays de la région Mena (Maroc,Tunisie, Egypte et la Jordanie) sur une période de 34 ans, en mettant l’accent sur l’interaction entre l’IDE, l’innovation technologique, l’urbanisation, la croissance économique et l’usage des énergies renouvelables et fossiles. Les tests d’unité racine et de cointégration confirment l’existence d’une relation de long terme entre les variables. Les résultats des estimations FMOLS montrent que l'urbanisation et la croissance économique augmentent significativement la consommation énergétique. L’innovation technologique favorise la transition énergétique, tandis que l'IDE et la technologique peuvent jouer un rôle ambivalent selon leur direction. La transition vers les énergies renouvelables reste stimulée par le progrès technologique, mais limitée par la pression urbaine et économique. Globalement, les quatre pays étudiés progressent vers une transition énergétique, mais à des rythmes inégaux et sous contraintes structurelles.Mots clés : transition énergétique ; IDE verts Abstract:This study investigates the dynamics of energy transition across four countries over 34 years, focusing on the role of FDI, technological innovation, urbanization, economic growth, and the use of renewable and fossil energy sources. Unit-root and cointegration tests confirm long-run relationships among variables. FMOLS and AMG estimations reveal that urbanization and economic growth significantly increase energy demand. Technological innovation promotes the shift toward renewable energy, while the effect of FDI and technology-based FDI appears mixed. Although renewable energy adoption is driven by technological progress, it faces structural constraints from rising urbanization and economic expansion. Overall, the four countries are moving toward energy transition, but progress remains uneven and challenged by socio-economic pressures.Keywords: energy transition; green FDI

title: Supply Chain Design and Optimization Strategies under Carbon Tariffs
source: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
summary: As the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) moves into force, green and low-carbon transformation has become a question Chinese supply chains can no longer postpone. This transformation is shifting trade competition from "cost compe
content: As the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) moves into force, green and low-carbon transformation has become a question Chinese supply chains can no longer postpone. This transformation is shifting trade competition from "cost competition" into "green competition." This paper builds a supply chain analytical framework covering Scope 1/2/3 emissions and, through case and comparative analysis of Apple and BYD, proposes strategies along four dimensions. The study finds that CBAM brings heavy compliance cost pressure but also strategic opportunity: Apple pushed 320 suppliers to commit to 100% clean electricity and made selected products carbon neutral, while BYD cut supply chain emission intensity by 25-30% through vertical integration. Even so, Chinese enterprises still struggle with data acquisition, Scope 3 accounting, cost balancing, collaborative reduction mechanisms, and the fragmentation of green trade rules.

title: Fluoride label concordance, pH, and electrical conductivity of commercial bottled waters in Ecuador
summary: Background Bottled water is widely consumed, yet differing water sources and manufacturing processes may alter its physicochemical properties, with reported discrepancies between label declarations and laboratory analyses. Given the lack of
content: Background Bottled water is widely consumed, yet differing water sources and manufacturing processes may alter its physicochemical properties, with reported discrepancies between label declarations and laboratory analyses. Given the lack of regional evidence, this study aimed to determine the fluoride concentration, pH, electrical conductivity, and labeling concordance of commercial bottled waters in Ecuador. Methods Eighteen commercial bottled water brands in Ecuador were analyzed to determine fluoride concentration (mg/L), pH, and electrical conductivity (µS/cm). Differences across brands and associations among variables were evaluated using one-way ANOVA and Spearman rank correlation ( α = 0.05). Results Discrepancies between declared and laboratory-measured fluoride levels were identified in 10 brands (55.6%). Only two brands exhibited fluoride concentrations within the recommended range established by international health organizations (0.7–1.5 mg/L) for caries prevention: Omizu Sparkling (0.85 ± 0.07 mg/L) and Aki (1.45 ± 0.04 mg/L), with the latter approaching the maximum safety limit. Notably, Omizu Sparkling also presented the highest labeling discrepancy (325%). Physicochemical parameters differ significantly among brands across brands ( p < 0.01). Additionally, 50% of the brands evaluated exhibited pH values at or below the critical threshold for enamel demineralization (≤ 5.5). Electrical conductivity correlated positively with measured fluoride concentrations (r = 0.592, p < 0.001). Conclusions Bottled waters in Ecuador predominantly present sub-optimal fluoride levels and potentially erosive pH values. These findings highlight the need for stricter regulatory labeling enforcement and heightened clinical awareness among dental professionals.

title: Biomass to Molecules: Closing the Carbon Loop through Integrated Thermochemical Conversion
summary: Abstract The urgent need to decarbonize the chemical sector and reduce dependence on fossil-derived carbon has renewed interest in biomass as a sustainable feedstock for chemical production. In this context, biomass has emerged as a versati
content: Abstract The urgent need to decarbonize the chemical sector and reduce dependence on fossil-derived carbon has renewed interest in biomass as a sustainable feedstock for chemical production. In this context, biomass has emerged as a versatile feedstock for producing both liquid and gaseous fuels, such as syngas, biogas, and compressed biogas (CBG). Among the available routes of biomass valorization into value-added chemicals and fuels, gasification offers a versatile technique to convert biomass and waste-derived feedstocks into syngas, which is a key intermediate for fuels and chemicals. In addition, biomass-derived biogas provides an alternative carbon source for syngas production proceeds through dry reforming of methane (DRM), thereby enabling the utilization of both CH4 and CO2 streams. This perspective offers a comprehensive overview of biomass utilization techniques, associated challenges related to their usage, and strategies to overcome them. Furthermore, particular attention is given to the fundamental chemistry and operating parameters on gasification performance, along with their thermodynamic and kinetic aspects. Moreover, special attention is placed on the competing reactions occurring during gasification, which affect the quality of syngas. In addition, materials design strategies for DRM are critically illustrated for the production of syngas from biomass-derived biogas, highlighting DRM as a central pathway for enhancing carbon utilization and tuning the H2/CO ratio. In situ and operando characterizations, along with DFT and AI/ML studies, can further provide valuable insights into the reaction and deactivation mechanisms of DRM. Such efforts are essential for closing the carbon loop and enabling a sustainable transition toward circular carbon economies.

title: School foodscapes mapping: a foundational economy framework for regional public food transformation
summary: Food is increasingly recognised as central to the foundational economy, yet relatively little research has examined how foundational economy principles can guide regional food system transformation. This article addresses this gap by analys
content: Food is increasingly recognised as central to the foundational economy, yet relatively little research has examined how foundational economy principles can guide regional food system transformation. This article addresses this gap by analysing school food as a strategic node within regional public provisioning. Drawing on primary and secondary data from Cornwall, UK, we examine how school meals connect public health, education, procurement, local production, agroecology and social justice. Cornwall provides a revealing case because rising Free School Meal eligibility, fragmented and outsourced school catering, and high levels of deprivation coexist with a strong agricultural heritage and a growing agroecological food movement. Using surveys, participatory workshops, informal interviews and spatial mapping of schools and agroecological producers, we identify both the barriers to regional procurement and the unrealised potential for school-farm partnerships. We develop a school foodscape mapping and transformation framework that combines dynamic mapping, partnership hubs, dynamic procurement, progressive municipalism and adaptive governance. The article contributes to foundational economy scholarship by demonstrating how school food can serve as a practical pathway to re-embedding food systems within regional economies, ecologies and communities.

title: Team diversity and radical green innovation: a patent-based analysis of gender, geographic, and institutional effects
summary: Abstract Achieving ambitious climate goals hinges on radical green innovation, yet how inventor-team composition shapes the radicalness of green patents remains largely unexplored. Drawing on theories of knowledge heterogeneity and recombin
content: Abstract Achieving ambitious climate goals hinges on radical green innovation, yet how inventor-team composition shapes the radicalness of green patents remains largely unexplored. Drawing on theories of knowledge heterogeneity and recombination, we jointly assess three dimensions of diversity that prior work has typically examined in isolation: gender and geographic diversity among inventors, and institutional diversity among co-assignees. We analyze 124,114 green patent families filed at the European Patent Office between 1990 and 2020 using fractional response models. Gender diversity shows a negative association with radicalness, contrasting with evidence from general, technology-wide patenting, where gender diversity has been linked to greater novelty. Geographic diversity is positively related to radicalness in the full population and remains positive among co-assigned patents, though with weaker statistical support in this smaller subsample. Institutional diversity displays a positive but modest association within the 12,267 co-assigned families for which it can be measured. Among collaboration types, partnerships with universities show a positive link, whereas inter-firm ones show a negative one. These patterns hold broadly across alternative diversity measures, estimation methods, and additional sensitivity analyses. Overall, our results demonstrate that diversity is not uniformly related to radical green innovation: its implications vary across dimensions of diversity and depend on the organizational context in which heterogeneous knowledge is integrated. These findings underscore the importance of adopting a multidimensional perspective on team diversity and offer implications for innovation management and public policies aimed at fostering radical green innovation.

title: Physical mechanisms behind plasma-induced liquid flow
source: Journal of Physics D Applied Physics
summary: Abstract Plasma-induced liquid flow is an emerging topic receiving accelerated interest in recent years within the larger inter-disciplinary field of plasma-liquid interactions. The liquid phase transport of reactive oxygen and nitrogen spe
content: Abstract Plasma-induced liquid flow is an emerging topic receiving accelerated interest in recent years within the larger inter-disciplinary field of plasma-liquid interactions. The liquid phase transport of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species, plasma produced molecules that have found use in a wide variety of applications, is governed by convective processes. Therefore, controlling the mechanisms that drive plasma-induced liquid flow would lead to control over reactive species transport in liquids, with the potential to thereby improve the efficiency of all plasma-liquid applications. Despite this potential, very little is currently known about the underlying physical processes of plasma-induced liquid flow. This review covers the present limited understanding of the mechanisms behind plasma-induced liquid flow, namely a combination of neutral gas flow, multi-phase electro-hydrodynamic forces, and Marangoni stresses driven by gradients in surface tension. A description is given on the underlying theory behind each of these mechanisms from a general fluid mechanical perspective, along with describing how these mechanisms would arise in plasma-liquid systems. Gaps in the understanding of the fluid mechanics of plasma-liquid interactions are identified and discussed, along with how present and future methods could be used to address these outstanding questions.

title: Labour Law and the Social Dimension of the EU Just Transition Agenda: A Spillover of European Integration’s Asymmetry Through Symbolic Policy-Making
summary: In the face of increasing attention to the social dimension of EU just transition, this article undertakes a critical assessment of the pertinent EU initiatives, particularly focusing on the interaction between EU labour law and the emergin
content: In the face of increasing attention to the social dimension of EU just transition, this article undertakes a critical assessment of the pertinent EU initiatives, particularly focusing on the interaction between EU labour law and the emerging social dimension of the EU just transition agenda. It draws on the asymmetry of European integration and the ordoliberal origins of the European project, to identify the tensions embedded in the relevant law and policy-making processes, and which may hamper the potential of any initiatives in the area. In turn, this may result in symbolic or un(der)enacted policies: important declarations of commitment to embed labour law and other social considerations, but without effectively doing so in practice. This is reflected in worker protection’s dependency on economic interests. the absence of binding social initiatives, the anaemic engagement with existing labour laws, the difficulties in legal mobilisation and strategic litigation, the limited role of social dialogue and the divergence between internal and external commitment to labour standards. Accordingly, the article’s contribution is two-fold. First, it makes a methodological contribution by extending the field of application of its analytical concepts to the nexus of EU labour law and just transition. Second, it sets out to provide a theoretically-informed policy assessment of labour law’s embeddedness in the EU just transition discourse.

title: Carbon removal and the politics of asset revaluation
summary: The political economy of climate change mitigation has variously been conceptualized as a struggle between fossil and ‘green’ coalitions or capital fractions. More recently, Colgan et al. (Citation2021) have reconceptualized climate politic
content: The political economy of climate change mitigation has variously been conceptualized as a struggle between fossil and ‘green’ coalitions or capital fractions. More recently, Colgan et al. (Citation2021) have reconceptualized climate politics as an existential struggle over asset revaluation between holders of climate-forcing and climate-vulnerable assets. In this commentary, we argue that the anticipated role of carbon dioxide removal (CDR) and the renewed attention to carbon capture and storage (CCS) in climate change mitigation have the potential to profoundly reshape these dynamics – a factor which has not yet been adequately considered. Specifically, we contend that expectations of CDR and CCS enable claims to residual and ‘hard-to-abate’ emissions as a political strategy to resist decarbonization and avoid asset stranding, while simultaneously creating opportunities to revalue fossil assets as indispensable to net-zero pathways. To develop this argument, we critically review the literature on asset stranding and the politics of asset revaluation and propose four research avenues to foreground the underexplored role of CDR, CCS, residual emissions, and hard-to-abate-ness. In doing so, we connect critical CDR scholarship to broader political economy debates on climate change mitigation, including asset revaluation, fossil fuel phase-out, green industrial policy, and the distributive politics of climate policy.

title: JSBE Spotlight : The Annual Focus on Student Achievement
summary: During their studies, our students in Jyväskylä University School of Business and Economics (JSBE) produce a considerable number of texts, coursework, and other material that is often only recognized as given credits. This second JSBE Spotl
content: During their studies, our students in Jyväskylä University School of Business and Economics (JSBE) produce a considerable number of texts, coursework, and other material that is often only recognized as given credits. This second JSBE Spotlight showcases our teaching and learning activities. With it, we aim to recognize the effort behind this work, promote peer learning, and encourage the building of scientific knowledge. The publication focuses on our three strategic focus areas; sustainable business and economies, digital business and economy, and policy-relevant economics and competitiveness of economy. The publication is not limited to purely written texts but contains different forms of knowledge production. The JSBE faculty comprises eight disciplines: Accounting and Corporate Finance, Economics, Commercial Law, Corporate Communications, Corporate Environmental Management, Management and Leadership, Marketing, and Strategy and Entrepreneurship. This publication presents undergraduate and graduate coursework from most of these disciplines. The work presented in this publication is based on the course teacher’s selection. In the following sections, the courses, reasons for selection, and the coursework will be presented in English or Finnish, based on the course language. From cover to cover, this publication is the result of collaboration between students and teachers. We editors would like to express our sincere appreciation to all the students whose work is included in this publication. We also wish to thank the teachers and supervisors who have supported and guided the students throughout their academic journey. This collection stands as a testament to what can be achieved through the collaborative efforts of students, educators, and the wider academic community.

title: One high-order ion-coupling mechanism generates multiple SLC1A stoichiometries
summary: Human excitatory amino acid transporter 2 (hEAAT2) is a glial transporter that clears glutamate and aspartate from the extracellular space to terminate neurotransmission. When this essential role is disrupted, excess extracellular glutamate
content: Human excitatory amino acid transporter 2 (hEAAT2) is a glial transporter that clears glutamate and aspartate from the extracellular space to terminate neurotransmission. When this essential role is disrupted, excess extracellular glutamate causes excitotoxicity and neurological disease. hEAAT2 transports amino acids into cells against their concentration gradients by coupling uptake to the co-transport of Na + and H + , and counter-transport of K + . Substrate transport also activates a thermodynamically uncoupled Cl - conductance, whose significance is unknown. Here, to dissect the molecular mechanisms underlying coupled and uncoupled ion transport by EAATs, we leverage the tractable Drosophila melanogaster homologue dEAAT2, which transports taurine as well as glutamate and aspartate. By functionally characterising dEAAT2, we confirmed it has features of a canonical EAAT transport cycle, including an uncoupled Cl - conductance. However, it functions an ion-independent electroneutral exchanger, in stark contrast to its ion-coupled electrogenic human counterpart. Cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and computational simulations confirmed the inability of dEAAT2 to transport cations, but just two point mutations conferred Na + , H + , and K + dependence, reconstituting the complex ion coupling profile of human transporters in the Drosophila exchanger. We also showed that dEAAT2 transports taurine in a complex with Cl - , bestowing a unique Cl - -dependence on taurine transport, independent of uncoupled Cl - flux. Our findings show that ancestral exchangers in the EAAT family preserve the machinery to achieve complex ion-coupled transport, revealing the molecular basis of high-order ion coupling in hEAATs.

title: Mechanistic Exploration of Estrone Adsorption onto Chitosan Hydrogel Beads: Classical and Fractal-like Adsorption Kinetics and Isotherms Analysis
summary: Abstract This study investigates the mechanistic behaviour of estrone (E1) adsorption onto chitosan hydrogel beads through the assessment of adsorption kinetics, equilibrium isotherms, and adsorbent regeneration. Batch adsorption experiment
content: Abstract This study investigates the mechanistic behaviour of estrone (E1) adsorption onto chitosan hydrogel beads through the assessment of adsorption kinetics, equilibrium isotherms, and adsorbent regeneration. Batch adsorption experiments were conducted to investigate the influence of pH, contact time, initial (E1) concentration, adsorbent load, and agitation speed on E1 uptake. Classical kinetic models, viz., pseudo-first order (PFO), pseudo-second order, intraparticle diffusion models and fractal-like kinetic models were applied to elucidate rate-controlling mechanisms. The PFO model best statistical fit (i.e., R2 = 0.9939, adj.R2 = 0.9918, χ^2 = 5.25E-4) with calculated qe1 = 4.8891 mg.g-1, and qexp = 4.95 mg.g-1 indicating film-diffusion dominated physisorption. Although fractal-like kinetics captured heterogeneous and anomalous diffusion associated with the hydrogel’s irregular structure, they did not outperform the classical PFO model. Equilibrium data were fitted to Langmuir, Freundlich, Langmuir-Freundlich, and Hill isotherms. The Langmuir model gave the best statistical performance (i.e., R2 = 0.9170, adj.R2 = 0.8754, QL = 6.7766 mg.g-1, and KL = 1.0277 L.mg-1) suggesting predominant monolayer adsorption, whereas the other models demonstrated underlying surface heterogeneity and mild cooperative effects. Regeneration studies demonstrated that the hydrogels retained a substantial portion of their adsorption capacity over eight cycles, confirming structural stability and practical reusability.

title: JAI: Physically Constrained Prediction of Conformer-Averaged Proton–Proton Coupling Constants in Solution
summary: Machine-learning predictors of proton–proton coupling constants are usually trained on, and evaluated against, couplings computed for single geometries rather than the conformer-averaged values measured in solution. We describe JAI (J-coupl
content: Machine-learning predictors of proton–proton coupling constants are usually trained on, and evaluated against, couplings computed for single geometries rather than the conformer-averaged values measured in solution. We describe JAI (J-coupling prediction with Artificial Intelligence), a graph transformer for 2J–5J(H,H) of small organic molecules trained on scaled Fermi-contact DFT couplings of about 3700 molecules, computed on geometries from the universal machine-learned potential UMA and averaged over conformers in six solvents, and on more than 25 000 curated experimental couplings annotated with their uncertainty, sign provenance and assignment. A fast mode predicts from the structure diagram; a conformer mode supplies, for each conformer of a reproducible search, the coefficients of Karplus-type expressions that are averaged with predicted populations; and a weighted combination of the two gives the final output, with 68 % and 90 % intervals calibrated on cross-validation errors. Against experimental couplings, the combined output reaches a mean absolute error of 0.43 Hz in cross-validation and 0.55 Hz when all compounds from the same literature source are held out together, our most realistic estimate for new chemistry. It reaches 0.35 Hz on 335 held-out compounds (fast mode: 0.53 Hz in cross-validation and 0.43 Hz on these compounds) and 0.57 Hz on 132 compounds added after the model had been finalized, 37 of them with environments that have very few DFT training examples. For vicinal couplings between sp3 carbons, it lowers the cross-validated error from 0.85 Hz with the fast mode to 0.66 Hz. The intervals hold for compounds like those of the training data but are too narrow for rare chemistry. Ablations on a previous version of the data set show that the physical expressions lower the error by 0.04 Hz overall, with a larger but less certain estimate for coupling types with few training exampl

title: Four dimensions of high-quality economic development
summary: Purpose Since 2012, China's economy has shifted from a stage of high-speed growth to one of high-quality development, yet a systematic theoretical generalisation of its economic connotations remains to be deepened. Taking Xi Jinping Thought
content: Purpose Since 2012, China's economy has shifted from a stage of high-speed growth to one of high-quality development, yet a systematic theoretical generalisation of its economic connotations remains to be deepened. Taking Xi Jinping Thought on the Economy as the entry point, this paper aims to review China's practical experience of economic development in the new era, synthesise a series of landmark concepts into four theoretical dimensions of high-quality economic development, to clarify their core connotations and logical interrelations, and to indicate the significance of these insights for developing an autonomous knowledge system of Chinese economics and advancing Chinese modernisation through high-quality development. Design/methodology/approach The paper adopts a conceptual approach combining theoretical exposition with documentary analysis, grounded in Marxist political economy. It systematically reviews Xi Jinping's major discourses on high-quality economic development, together with the documents of the Communist Party of China (CPC) National Congresses from the 18th to the 20th and the relevant Central Committee plenary sessions. Applying materialist dialectics and the unity of logic and history, the study examines, in sequence, the practical background, the problems addressed and the theoretical connotations of each dimension. Findings The study finds that the four dimensions respond to distinct major problems. The people-centred philosophy of development clarifies for whom development is pursued, reflected in improved quality of life, substantive progress towards common prosperity and high-quality population development, with nearly 100 million rural residents lifted out of poverty and the world's largest education, healthcare and social security systems established. The new development philosophy sets the guiding principles for China's modernisation, comprising innovation, coordination, green development, opening-up and shared development, with supply-side structural reform as its concrete practice. The new development paradigm, with domestic circulation as the mainstay and domestic and international circulations reinforcing each other, saw domestic demand contribute 69.7% of economic growth in 2024 and requires coordinating high-quality development with high-level security. New quality productive forces, led by innovation and characterised by high technology, high efficiency and high quality, are cultivated through original and disruptive innovation, the deep integration of scientific and technological innovation with industrial innovation, qualitative upgrading of all elements of the productive forces, and relations of production better suited to their development. Originality/value The paper makes three contributions. First, it systematically integrates the concepts advanced since the new era into four logically connected dimensions: the people-centred philosophy, the new development philosophy, the new development paradigm and n

title: Tracing truth: How traceability enhances fake news detection design
summary: Abstract The spread of fake news poses significant challenges across social, political, and economic domains. Existing countermeasures, like media literacy and fact-checking, have shown limited effectiveness due to user skepticism and cogni
content: Abstract The spread of fake news poses significant challenges across social, political, and economic domains. Existing countermeasures, like media literacy and fact-checking, have shown limited effectiveness due to user skepticism and cognitive biases. To address this issue, we introduce decision support traceability (DST), which integrates system traceability (explainable AI) and object traceability (chain of sources) to improve users’ ability to assess information credibility. System traceability enhances transparency by explaining AI-generated classifications, while object traceability enables users to track news articles’ origin and evolution. Prior research has examined these mechanisms separately, but their combined effect on disinformation detection remains underexplored. We hypothesize that their integration results in superior performance in identifying fake news. Using design science research (DSR) methodology, we developed and tested a prototype incorporating DST. A controlled online experiment compared three treatments: explainable AI, chain of sources, and their combination. Results show that while both mechanisms independently improve disinformation detection, their combination yields the highest accuracy, demonstrating the complementary nature of DST. This study advances information systems research by empirically validating DST as a unified framework for supporting news credibility assessments. The findings provide actionable design knowledge, emphasizing the need for AI transparency and provenance-tracking features to combat digital disinformation.

title: A multi‐scale spatial framework for simulating land use carbon risks and ecological compensation under future development scenarios
summary: Abstract Land‐use change creates spatial mismatches between carbon emissions, coefficient‐based potential carbon uptake, and ecological compensation responsibilities. Using land‐use, energy‐consumption, and socioeconomic data from 2000 to 2
content: Abstract Land‐use change creates spatial mismatches between carbon emissions, coefficient‐based potential carbon uptake, and ecological compensation responsibilities. Using land‐use, energy‐consumption, and socioeconomic data from 2000 to 2024, this study develops a Prediction–Assessment–Zoning framework for the Yellow River Basin (YRB), China. The framework integrates land‐use carbon accounting, a Carbon Emission and Absorption Coupling Risk (CEACR) index, bivariate LISA, PLUS‐based land‐use simulation, GM‐LSTM‐based energy‐emission prediction, and K‐means clustering for carbon compensation zoning. The estimated uptake in this study refers to coefficient‐based potential carbon uptake rather than observed net ecosystem productivity. The results show that the mean CEACR value increased from 0.0193 in 2000 to 0.0279 in 2024, representing a 44.56% increase, while the proportion of extremely high‐risk areas rose from 1.92% to 2.79%. High‐risk clusters expanded mainly in urban‐industrial areas of the middle and lower reaches, indicating clear cross‐boundary spillover of land‐use carbon risk. Under the 2030 urban development scenario, the mean CEACR value reached 0.0347, 22.6% higher than that under the natural development scenario, whereas low‐carbon development and cropland protection constrained risk growth. The low‐carbon scenario reduced total land‐use carbon emissions by 15.05% compared with the natural development scenario. Based on ECC, ESC, and spatial risk patterns, Shandong, Henan, and Ningxia were identified as payment zones; Qinghai, Sichuan, and Inner Mongolia as compensation zones; and Shanxi, Shaanxi, and Gansu as balanced zones.

title: System-level impacts of landscape scenicness on onshore wind deployment in a decarbonized European energy system
summary: Abstract Onshore wind is pivotal to Europe’s decarbonization, yet its expansion increasingly faces social constraints due to landscape impacts that are rarely captured in energy system models. This study presents a Europe-wide integration o
content: Abstract Onshore wind is pivotal to Europe’s decarbonization, yet its expansion increasingly faces social constraints due to landscape impacts that are rarely captured in energy system models. This study presents a Europe-wide integration of landscape scenicness, which is used as a proxy for potential landscape impact, into a calibrated, multi-sector energy system model that explores policy interactions with enhanced capacity-factor granularity. Building on a machine-learning–based scenicness dataset linked to wind resource assessment, and an enhanced representation of wind technologies with fine capacity-factor granularity, we quantify how landscape scenicness preservation affects onshore wind deployment and system-wide outcomes across 27 European Union member states. Results show that moderate scenicness protection has limited impacts, while stringent protection disproportionately removes high-capacity-factor wind sites, particularly in mountainous and coastal regions. This reduces the number of potential low-cost wind sites and induces techno-economic substitution toward solar photovoltaics in the model. A reduction in onshore wind capacity intensifies competition among uses of clean electricity, including direct electrification, hydrogen, and other renewable synthetic fuels. The presence or relaxation of intermediate EU climate and energy policy targets has a stronger effect than scenicness constraints alone. These findings demonstrate that coordinated policy design remains the dominant lever for achieving a secure, socially acceptable, and cost-effective European energy transition, and wind emerges as a key contributor to the effectiveness of policy implementation. A limitation should be highlighted that the solar substitution should be interpreted as a system-level compensation potential rather than an unconstrained deployment pathway.

title: Portland Limestone Cement for durable low carbon infrastructure concrete
summary: Portland Limestone Cement (PLC), designated as Type IL under ASTM C595/C595M and Type GUL under CSA A3001, is now a mainstream clinker-reduction strategy for concrete infrastructure. Because the performance of commercial PLC containing up t
content: Portland Limestone Cement (PLC), designated as Type IL under ASTM C595/C595M and Type GUL under CSA A3001, is now a mainstream clinker-reduction strategy for concrete infrastructure. Because the performance of commercial PLC containing up to 15% limestone is already well established, the principal question is no longer whether such cements can replace Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC) under routine conditions, but how durability specifications, higher-limestone formulations, and multicomponent systems should evolve without sacrificing service life. This critical narrative review synthesizes more than 100 peer-reviewed, technical, and standards sources across six geographic regions. The 5–15% Type IL/GUL range is treated as the commercial baseline, while higher-limestone systems, including CEM II/B-L cements containing 21–35% limestone and low-clinker ternary or composite cements, are evaluated as an emerging performance domain. The review integrates four themes that are rarely considered together in PLC-focused syntheses: durability-conditioned equivalence with OPC, global specification and code development, interactions with supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs), and limestone-quality variability. Commercial PLC generally provides comparable mechanical, chloride, and freeze-thaw performance when water-to-cementitious materials ratio, curing, and air entrainment are appropriately controlled. Carbonation and sulfate resistance remain the durability characteristics most sensitive to clinker dilution and clinker C 3 A content, respectively. Evidence for limestone contents above 15% demonstrates technically viable low-clinker concrete, particularly when limestone is combined with reactive SCMs, but the evidence base is more heterogeneous and long-term field validation remains limited. The standards synthesis further shows that European frameworks accommodate higher limestone contents and multicomponent cements more explicitly than current North American practice. The review therefore identifies performance-based durability qualification, long-term field data for higher-limestone systems, and validated rapid test methods for multicomponent binders as priority needs for the next generation of PLC specifications.

title: Perovskite Oxides: Synthesis Strategies and Advances in Photoelectrocatalytic Applications
summary: The depletion of fossil fuels and the resulting environmental burden have increased interest in photocatalytic routes for converting solar energy into storable chemical energy. Their overall performance depends strongly on the intrinsic phy
content: The depletion of fossil fuels and the resulting environmental burden have increased interest in photocatalytic routes for converting solar energy into storable chemical energy. Their overall performance depends strongly on the intrinsic physicochemical properties of the photoanode material. Conventional wide-bandgap semiconductors are limited by restricted visible-light absorption and rapid charge-carrier recombination that lowers quantum efficiency and hinders practical implementation. Perovskite oxides offer adjustable crystal structures, flexible metal valence states and useful redox properties, making them promising candidates for addressing these critical limitations. This review examines the crystal structures and photocatalytic mechanisms of perovskite oxides and compares how sol–gel, solid-state, coprecipitation, and hydrothermal synthesis affect grain size, microstructure, and surface defects. It also discusses their emerging applications in electrocatalytic nitrate reduction to ammonia and photocatalytic selective oxidation of organic substrates. The review relates synthesis conditions to carrier separation and surface reaction barriers, providing a solid basis for designing stable, efficient photocatalytic systems toward scalable solar-to-chemical conversion.

title: Carbon credit trading in photovoltaic systems: A case study on break-even and passive income
summary: The global expansion of photovoltaics (PV) systems and the operationalization of carbon markets necessitate high-precision financial and environmental forecasting. However, conventional economic models often rely on manufacturer-specified p
content: The global expansion of photovoltaics (PV) systems and the operationalization of carbon markets necessitate high-precision financial and environmental forecasting. However, conventional economic models often rely on manufacturer-specified panel degradation (ERSD) while neglecting the progressive efficiency decay of power electronics, leading to potential systematic overestimations of carbon revenue. This study addresses this gap by presenting a novel energy reduction including PV panel degradation and inverter efficiency loss (DIEL) method. Utilizing a 5.99 MWp hybrid PV infrastructure at Suranaree University of Technology (SUT), Thailand, as a "living lab" case study, we evaluate the system’s performance over a 25-year lifecycle across four scenarios (with and without carbon credit trading). The results demonstrate that while the integration of carbon credits (at 5.52 USD/tCO₂eq) accelerates the Break-Even Point (BEP) by approximately 0.5% (to 4.04 years) and enhances the Internal Rate of Return (IRR) by up to 2.86%, technical realism is paramount for valuation accuracy. Comparative analysis reveals that traditional ERSD models overestimate cumulative passive income and carbon reduction by 17.40% and 21.07% (14,992 tCO₂eq), respectively, compared to the technically grounded DIEL method. These findings suggest that failing to account for inverter-level losses results in a significant "integrity gap" in carbon credit issuance and financial bankability. This study provides a refined framework for institutional prosumers and regulators within the Thai carbon market (TGO/FTIX), ensuring that environmental commodities and financial returns are aligned with the physical reality of hardware decay.

title: An Approach to Managing Chillers for Air Conditioning Systems in Shopping Malls in Thailand
source: International Journal of Engineering Trends and Technology
summary: The effective management of air conditioning systems is imperative for achieving carbon neutrality in large-scale shopping malls, as these systems are responsible for approximately 60–80% of overall electricity consumption. This study inves
content: The effective management of air conditioning systems is imperative for achieving carbon neutrality in large-scale shopping malls, as these systems are responsible for approximately 60–80% of overall electricity consumption. This study investigates three shopping malls in Thailand as case studies, employing reference data obtained from the mandatory implementation of the Thai Building Energy Code (BEC). The external climatic conditions of the investigated area can be represented by a maximum average dry-bulb temperature of 33 °C and a maximum average wet-bulb temperature of 27 °C. The three shopping malls contain gross floor areas varying from 25,000 to 50,000 m². The results reveal that Shopping Mall B exhibits greater potential for gaining carbon neutrality in its air conditioning refrigeration systems with respect to Shopping Malls A and C, mainly caused by its lower energy consumption per unit floor area. The annual electricity consumption of Shopping Mall B is 10,946,225.52 kWh, resulting in carbon dioxide emissions of 5,472.02 tCO₂-eq/year. These findings indicate that using solar Photovoltaic (PV) systems for daytime electricity production is an effective mitigation strategy. The introduction of a minimum PV capacity of 4 MW significantly reduces carbon dioxide equivalent emissions by approximately 54.81%. Thus, the suggested integrated approach proposes an important significant possibility for lowering carbon dioxide equivalent emissions in large-scale shopping malls.

title: Design of Residential Photovoltaic Power Generation Systems for Low-Carbon Buildings
summary: Decarbonising residential buildings is a combination of energy demand reduction on the demand side and renewable electricity generation on the supply side. In Shanghai, rooftop photovoltaic (PV) generation could be a viable option to reduce
content: Decarbonising residential buildings is a combination of energy demand reduction on the demand side and renewable electricity generation on the supply side. In Shanghai, rooftop photovoltaic (PV) generation could be a viable option to reduce household electric power consumption for detached residential buildings, provided PV array sizing, design of power conversion, grid-filtering and control strategy are tailored. In this paper a preliminary electrical design of a grid connected PV power generation system is based on the low carbon residential building to provide the annual electricity balance is developed. Given a winter design demand of 17.8 kWh/day, an effective sunshine duration of 3.8 h/day and a system-loss coefficient of 1.8, the PV capacity is found to be 8.43 kW. A 10.08 kWp array is selected for use, which consists of 24 mono-crystalline silicon modules, and an estimated module area of 48.0m2. The design is also specified by the direct current (DC) bus voltage of 400 V, the frequency of the DC-DC boost converter of 10 kHz, the frequency of the single-phase sinusoidal pulse-width modulation (SPWM) inverter of 20 kHz, and an inductor-capacitor-inductor (LCL) grid filter. A hybrid constant-voltage and perturb-and-observe maximum power point tracking (MPPT) strategy is employed to enhance the PV operating point tracking under the condition of irradiance change. The simulation results reveal that the hybrid MPPT controller is able to track the new MPP following an irradiance drop from 1200 W/m2 to 600 W/m2 at t=0.8 s. Capacitor current feedback active damping for the LCL filter suppresses the resonance peak and the grid current total harmonic distortion is less than the design limit of 5.00% at 2.45%. These results are helpful for electrical feasibility of the proposed grid connected residential PV system.

title: The Expanding Energy Demand of Artificial Intelligence Data Centres: Societal Costs, Energy Poverty, and the European Union Policy Response
summary: The rapid diffusion of artificial intelligence (AI) is adding a fast-growing workload to the data centres that host it, with consequences for electricity systems, household energy costs, and the environment.This article examines the sustain
content: The rapid diffusion of artificial intelligence (AI) is adding a fast-growing workload to the data centres that host it, with consequences for electricity systems, household energy costs, and the environment.This article examines the sustainability implications of AI-driven data-centre expansion in Europe along three connected dimensions-environmental sustainability, energy and social equity, and the sustainability of the digital transition-and asks who gains and who pays.Doctrinal analysis of European Union (EU) law and policy was combined with a comparative, descriptive assessment of published data.The study synthesised evidence from international agencies, EU institutions, national statistical offices, regulators, and peer-reviewed research, and traced household electricity costs and data-centre development from 2023 onward in three purposively selected cases: Ireland, the United Kingdom, and Spain.Data-centre electricity demand, of which AI workloads are an increasingly important component, is growing far faster than overall demand and is highly concentrated geographically.In exposed regions this concentration is associated with grid-capacity constraints and may contribute to upward pressure on network and system costs.Household prices in the period were, however, shaped predominantly by gas prices, taxation, subsidies, renewable output, and network charges, and the study does not estimate causal effects.The expansion also generates environmental externalities, notably carbon emissions and a growing stream of electronic waste.Because energy costs weigh most heavily on low-income households, these pressures carry a distributional risk: a potential "double burden" in which households already in energy poverty benefit least from AI while bearing part of its infrastructure costs.The article maps the EU response by legal status-measures in force, formally proposed, and under discussion-and argues that assessments of AI's social value should internalise its energy, climate, resource, and distributional costs.It closes with actor-specific recommendations on clean-supply additionality, cost-reflective network-cost allocation, safeguards for vulnerable consumers, hardware circularity, and sustainability metrics.

title: Mapping the knowledge landscape and future research of sustainable supply chains, circular economy, and net-zero transitions
summary: This study aims to identify and outline research directions for future empirical studies on integrating the net-zero emission transition with the circular economy to improve supply chain management. Conducting a bibliometric analysis of 253
content: This study aims to identify and outline research directions for future empirical studies on integrating the net-zero emission transition with the circular economy to improve supply chain management. Conducting a bibliometric analysis of 253 documents from the Scopus database from 2015 to September 2025, this research employs VOSviewer and Biblioshiny to visualise knowledge maps, collaboration patterns, and thematic assessment paths. The findings reveal predominant keywords such as "supply chain management," "circular economy," and "decarbonisation," with the Journal of Cleaner Production and the United Kingdom emerging as the leading journal and most productive country. Thematic mapping highlights a concentration on four critical areas: supply chain and circular economy transitions; emission measurement, control, and life cycle assessment (LCA); carbon sequestration and technological innovations; and renewable energy and low-carbon technologies. By providing novel insights into the critical junction of net-zero supply chains, this paper directs future academic research on circular economy platforms, decarbonisation, and sustainability, while acknowledging the need for future studies to integrate multiple databases to enhance analytical comprehensiveness.

title: Energy demand reduction through TMP-based backwashing control in a pilot-scale vertical upflow multi-column membrane photobioreactor for wastewater reclamation
summary: Wastewater reclamation via microalgal-bacterial membrane bioreactors are a recent approach to promote carbon neutrality and a circular water economy. Although membrane fouling control is a critical issue, there is a lack of knowledge on the
content: Wastewater reclamation via microalgal-bacterial membrane bioreactors are a recent approach to promote carbon neutrality and a circular water economy. Although membrane fouling control is a critical issue, there is a lack of knowledge on the application of automatic control cleaning strategies. This study proposes a feedback control system for backwashing initiation based on transmembrane pressure ( TMP ) monitoring. A pilot-scale, vertical upflow multi-column membrane photobioreactor (VUC-MPBR) treating secondary effluent was used. The system successfully operated outdoors for over 100 days, achieving robust organic matter removal (58.3%), moderate nutrient recovery (21.3% and 27.8% for nitrogen and phosphorus, respectively), and efficient biomass separation (0.6 g/L in the recirculating suspension and 10.3 g/L of concentrated biomass at the bottom of the columns). Direct-flow filtration with the automatic backwashing strategy enhanced fouling control at high permeate fluxes (42.5 L/h m 2 ), reducing the specific energy demand for membrane scouring by 55% compared with the conventional backwashing strategy. Residual fouling analysis indicated that backwashing flux played a dominant role, whereas duration had a comparatively minor effect. TMP set-point value to be established resulted to be crucial to avoid a large pressure drop across the cake layer inducing cake compression. Under sustainable fouling conditions, the control system provided high net permeate fluxes (35.6–36.1 L/h m 2 ) with low specific energy demand for membrane scouring (0.028–0.040 kWh/m 3 ) for over 500 h, representing part of a total process specific energy demand of approximately 0.23–0.25 kWh/m³ (including liquid recirculation and permeate filtration/backwashing). Therefore, a VUC-MPBR operated with TMP sp -controlled backwashing represents a low-energy demand process configuration for microalgae-based wastewater reclamation.\

title: Addressing China’s Wind Power Underperformance
summary: Abstract Wind power is pivotal to global decarbonization, and China leads in both installed capacity and recent expansion. Yet rapid capacity expansion has not translated into commensurate growth in usable electricity. Here we reconstruct g
content: Abstract Wind power is pivotal to global decarbonization, and China leads in both installed capacity and recent expansion. Yet rapid capacity expansion has not translated into commensurate growth in usable electricity. Here we reconstruct generation for 10,032 wind farms in China spanning 1989-2022 and find that over 20% of technically available generation is not utilized. Decomposition reveals that while grid-connection delays and officially reported curtailment have declined by ~70% in the past decade, a residual component - soft curtailment - has emerged. This component represents unreported losses arising from system inflexibility and regulatory distortions, such as rigid dispatch, strict curtailment targets, and premature reporting of grid connection incentivized by feed-in tariff policies. Soft curtailment now dominates wind power underperformance in China, offsetting technological improvements expected to raise capacity factors by ~20%, leaving them largely unchanged overall. Absorbing the unrealized generation through storage at multiple timescales and matching to flexible loads could enable China to reach its 2060 wind generation target for carbon neutrality up to 13 years earlier and avoid over 20 Gt CO₂ emissions cumulatively.

title: Development of Optical Polyviologen Nanoparticle‐Immobilized Cellulose Nanocrystal‐Reinforced Gum Arabic as Self‐Healing Hydrogel Toward Multi‐Stimuli Responsive and Anticounterfeiting Applications
summary: ABSTRACT Photosensitive inks have displayed disadvantages, such as low efficiency and poor durability. In contrast, self‐healable hydrogels can independently repair physical damage to restore their structural properties, proving durability
content: ABSTRACT Photosensitive inks have displayed disadvantages, such as low efficiency and poor durability. In contrast, self‐healable hydrogels can independently repair physical damage to restore their structural properties, proving durability and stability. In this context, a new nanocomposite film with photochromic, thermochromic, and ammonia‐responsive characteristics was prepared from a combination of polyviologen and maleic‐modified cellulose nanocrystal‐supported gum Arabic hydrogel.
