The viologen polymer was synthesized using an aqueous condensation process involving a viologen dialdehyde and a hydroxyl‐functionalized aryl dihydrazide under acidic conditions. The polyviologen nanoparticles displayed a diameter range of 9–21 nm, whereas CNC showed sizes between 8 and 15 nm. The use of CNC as a dispersant inhibits the agglomeration of viologen nanoparticles. Mechanical and morphological analyses demonstrated superior adhesion, flexibility, and homogeneity of the imprinted films. A reversible thermochromic response was monitored in a temperature range of 25°C–80°C. Exposure to ammonia vapor induced a rapid color change from yellow (447 nm) to green (627 nm), which promptly returned to its original condition upon removal of the ammonia stimulus. The paper sensor identifies aqueous ammonia at values ranging from 0.1 to 350 ppm. The coating layer exhibited a green tint in UV light, as confirmed by CIE colorimetric measurements.

title: Fluororubber/Basalt Fiber Composites With Tailored Interfaces for High‐Frequency Vibration Attenuation
summary: ABSTRACT High‐frequency vibrations present a critical challenge to the reliability of precision systems, yet conventional elastomeric damping materials often fail in this regime due to their slow molecular relaxation kinetics. Here, a serie
content: ABSTRACT High‐frequency vibrations present a critical challenge to the reliability of precision systems, yet conventional elastomeric damping materials often fail in this regime due to their slow molecular relaxation kinetics. Here, a series of basalt fiber (BF) reinforced fluororubber (FKM) composites with improved high‐frequency vibration attenuation was developed through fiber surface modification and control of fiber–matrix interactions. The BF surface morphology and chemistry were modified by NaOH etching followed by vinyltriethoxysilane treatment, potentially altering fiber–matrix interactions. The effects of BF content and modification parameters on the microstructure, mechanical properties, and damping behavior were systematically investigated. The optimal formulation (1.0 wt%–100°C–2.5 mol) increased composite stiffness and hardness and markedly attenuated high‐frequency vibration responses. Specifically, the root mean square of the frequency response function decreased from 35.0 dB for pure FKM to 26.4 dB, and the high‐frequency resonance peak at 3.3 kHz was suppressed by 15 dB. This work provides a novel design strategy for developing high‐performance elastomeric composites with tailored high‐frequency vibration attenuation through interface modification.

title: Next Generation Antimicrobial Coatings for High Touch Surfaces: Application, Benefits, Risks, Environmental Impacts and Sustainability Aspects
summary: Antimicrobial coatings for high-touch surfaces are a promising strategy to reduce the burden of infectious pathogens, limit human exposure, and mitigate transmission in public, healthcare, and other shared environments. This review outlines
content: Antimicrobial coatings for high-touch surfaces are a promising strategy to reduce the burden of infectious pathogens, limit human exposure, and mitigate transmission in public, healthcare, and other shared environments. This review outlines current antimicrobial coating strategies and their modes of action with attention to their rational applications on high touch surfaces. Because standard laboratory efficacy tests often fail to capture end-use conditions, the review points to the need for application relevant testing approaches that account for factors such as humidity, temperature, contamination level, inoculum volume, and repeated touching. Beyond efficacy, safe use also depends on how active components are released and on the resulting exposure to humans and the environment, both during their use and at end-of-life. Human safety endpoints, such as cytotoxicity, immunotoxicological effects, skin sensitization, and skin irritation, are examined under short- and long-term exposure, in relation to current testing standards and regulatory expectations. In parallel, the review addresses environmental concerns, including potential persistence, bioaccumulation and the transport of released substances into soil, sediments, air and water. Building on these considerations, the review concludes by outlining key principles for applying a safe-and-sustainable-by-design (SSbD) approach to antimicrobial coatings.

title: Production and Evaluation of Activated Hybrid Biochar Briquettes From Date Palm and Pistachio Wastes: Thermochemical, Physical, and Mechanical Behavior
summary: ABSTRACT As global fossil fuel reserves decline and concerns about climate change intensify, interest in briquettes as a sustainable biofuel source is increasing. This study investigated the effects of CO 2 activation temperature on the phy
content: ABSTRACT As global fossil fuel reserves decline and concerns about climate change intensify, interest in briquettes as a sustainable biofuel source is increasing. This study investigated the effects of CO 2 activation temperature on the physicochemical, mechanical, thermal, and combustion properties of hybrid biochar briquettes produced from date palm and pistachio biochars at a 60:40 ratio using 15% and 20% starch binder. The results showed that the non‐activated hybrid biochar briquettes with 20% starch binder (HB20) exhibited the highest density (1.06 g/cm 3 ), whereas the briquettes produced at 400°C had a substantially lower density (0.60 g/cm 3 ). Increasing the starch binder content and activation temperature affected the mechanical and combustion properties of the briquettes, including impact resistance, shatter resistance, compressive strength, and burning rate. The briquettes containing 15% starch exhibited the lowest compressive strength at the lower carbonization and activation temperature of 400°C, whereas increasing the treatment temperature to 600°C resulted in higher compressive strength. Activation reduced the burning time of the hybrid biochar briquettes and increased their burning rate; AHB15 at 600°C showed the shortest burning time (300 s) and highest burning rate (1.05 g/min). Thermogravimetric analysis showed that the activated hybrid biochar briquettes containing 15% starch exhibited the lowest total mass loss (16.30%). Furthermore, FESEM images revealed more pronounced pore structures in the activated briquettes than in the non‐activated hybrid biochar briquettes.

title: Smart Agricultural Intensity and Income—Carbon Nexus Among Wheat Smallholders in China’s Yellow River Basin
summary: Agricultural digitalization could help reconcile farm-income growth with emissions reduction, but evidence on how the depth of smart-technology application shapes these outcomes among smallholders remains limited. Using field-survey data fr
content: Agricultural digitalization could help reconcile farm-income growth with emissions reduction, but evidence on how the depth of smart-technology application shapes these outcomes among smallholders remains limited. Using field-survey data from 243 wheat-growing households in Neihuang, Lintong and Lingwu along China’s Yellow River, we construct a smart agricultural technology application-intensity index covering planting, irrigation and fertilization, crop protection and harvesting. We combine regression analysis with a coupling-coordination model to examine effects on per-mu net income and carbon emissions, and to assess the moderating roles of farmer education and green planting practices. Greater technology application is associated with higher per-mu net income and lower per-mu carbon emissions: the estimated coefficients are 0.0341 and −0.0979, respectively. Farmer education strengthens the income effect, whereas green planting practices weaken it in the short term. Overall, the coupling between emissions reduction and income growth is at an intermediate level, with coordination highest in Lintong, followed by Neihuang and Lingwu. These findings indicate that smart agriculture generates economic and environmental benefits when technology depth is supported by human capital, technical services and market institutions. Policies that integrate digital-skills training, production-stage services, green incentives and agricultural value-chain development could improve the alignment between farmer prosperity and low-carbon agricultural transformation.

title: Alkali Metal Potassium-Synergistically Driven Dual-Phase High-Entropy Layered Double Hydroxide/Spinel Heterostructure for Efficient Oxygen Evolution Reaction
source: American Journal of Environmental Science and Engineering
summary: The sluggish kinetics of the anodic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in water electrolysis for hydrogen production and its heavy dependence on noble metal catalysts restrict the large-scale application of green hydrogen energy. In this work,
content: The sluggish kinetics of the anodic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in water electrolysis for hydrogen production and its heavy dependence on noble metal catalysts restrict the large-scale application of green hydrogen energy. In this work, we designed and prepared a self-supported dual-phase high-entropy layered double hydroxide/spinel (HELDH/HESO) heterostructured oxygen evolution electrocatalyst, (K)-NiCoFeCrCe-HELDH/HESO@NF, synergistically driven by alkali metal potassium (K). Through a one-step hydrothermal method, six metal salts containing K, Ni, Co, Fe, Cr, and Ce were co-deposited on a nickel foam (NF) substrate, yielding a self-supported electrode with a three-dimensional nanosheet structure and moderate pore size. The introduction of catalytically inactive alkali metal K into the lattice induces lattice expansion and distortion, optimizes the electronic density of states of adjacent transition metals (Ni, Co, Fe), and regulates the d-band center position, thereby optimizing the adsorption free energies of oxygen-containing intermediates (OH*, O*, OOH*) and significantly enhancing the intrinsic OER activity. The dual-phase LDH/spinel heterointerfaces provide high-density defects and unsaturated coordination sites, strengthening interfacial electronic regulation. In 1 M KOH electrolyte, (K)-NiCoFeCrCe-HELDH/HESO@NF requires only overpotentials of 279 mV and 355 mV to achieve current densities of 100 mA cm -2 and 1000 mA cm -2 , respectively, outperforming the K-free counterpart electrode. In an anion exchange membrane (AEM) electrolyzer under simulated industrial conditions, the electrode operated continuously at a constant current of 1 A for 100 h with only about 6.4% voltage increase, demonstrating excellent long-term stability. The preparation process is simple, reproducible, cost-controllable, and environmentally friendly, offering a new strategy for the development of efficient, stable, and low-cost non-noble-metal OER catalysts.

title: China as a Mission-Oriented State in the Green Transition: Governance and Industrial Policy in the New Energy Vehicle Industry
source: SOAS Research Online (SOAS University of London)
summary: Rooted in regulation theory, this thesis examines how China’s automotive transformation has proceeded through reciprocal changes in sectoral accumulation and industrial governance during the green transition. Its framework connects technolo
content: Rooted in regulation theory, this thesis examines how China’s automotive transformation has proceeded through reciprocal changes in sectoral accumulation and industrial governance during the green transition. Its framework connects technological architecture and institutional bricolage to regulatory mechanisms examined vertically and horizontally. National industrial policy and local governance are analysed as selected contributions to the wider mode of regulation. Historical comparison, policy analysis and four local case studies draw on industry and enterprise evidence and over twenty semi-structured interviews conducted in China in 2024.In the internal combustion engine (ICE) era, joint ventures expanded production while foreign incumbents’ control over core technologies and product development could sustain subordinate positions for Chinese partners within global production hierarchies. The new energy vehicle (NEV) transition enabled Chinese firms to combine manufacturing experience with battery, electronics and software capabilities, strengthening their positions in the global division of labour. Vertical integration, capability complementarity and incumbent restructuring coexisted, redistributing industrial authority and value-capture opportunities while generating new coordination demands.National governance reworked inherited developmental capacities towards mission-oriented innovation policy (MOIP), connecting industrial upgrading with decarbonisation. Vertical coordination organised authority and resources across government levels; horizontal coordination linked agencies, firms and sectors. Implementation generated requests for adjustment, whose influence depended on administrative procedures and decision rights.Local institutional bricolage combined inherited resources and partnerships with vertical permissions and constraints. Guangzhou pursued path development through incumbent recombination; Hainan, path clearing through application market creation; Shanghai, path inheritance through deliberate disruption; and Hefei, path creation through entrepreneurial bricolage.The thesis contributes to regulation theory by explaining how technological architecture, regulatory mechanisms and institutional bricolage mediate reciprocal changes in accumulation and regulation. Institutions respond to technological change and actively shape emerging productive configurations, while enterprise development and local competition generate further pressures for institutional adjustment.

title: Decoding ozone pollution drivers in China : from COVID-19 lockdowns to carbon neutrality
source: PolyU Institutional Research Archive (Hong Kong Polytechnic University)
summary: Ozone (O₃) is both a harmful air pollutant, threatening human health and vegetation, and a potent greenhouse gas exacerbating climate warming. Surface O₃ concentrations are modulated by complex factors, including meteorological and climate
content: Ozone (O₃) is both a harmful air pollutant, threatening human health and vegetation, and a potent greenhouse gas exacerbating climate warming. Surface O₃ concentrations are modulated by complex factors, including meteorological and climate variability, biogenic and anthropogenic precursor emissions (nitrogen oxides, NOₓ and volatile organic compounds, VOCs), and aerosol interactions. The non-linear O₃-NOₓ-VOCs relationship further complicates O₃ mitigation efforts, as evidenced during first phase of China’s Clean Air Plan (2013-2017), where sharp NOₓ emission cuts without proportional VOCs emission reductions increased O₃ pollution. During April-May 2022, Shanghai imposed a city-wide full lockdown to contain a resurgence in cases of the coronavirus disease in 2019. More broadly, in the warm season (April-October) of 2022, many other parts of China also experienced partial lockdowns, with heatwaves having co-occurred in some cities. These full or partial lockdowns led to considerable reductions in livelihood and economic activities and the resultant anthropogenic emission reductions. Therefore, the year 2022 could serve as a particularly useful real-world test of the response of surface O₃ to such substantial anthropogenic emission reductions. The commitment of carbon neutrality released in 2020 promises huge emission reductions in the future, but it’s still not clear how O₃ would respond to such emission reductions. Considering global climate warming further, it is vital to investigate how O₃ would evolve in the future under the joint context of climate change and carbon neutrality. This thesis seeks to address these critical research gaps by investigating the response of surface O₃ to anthropogenic emission changes and the concurrent climate warming. The first part investigates the roles of meteorological variations and anthropogenic emission changes in determining O₃ concentrations during April-May 2022 lockdown in Shanghai, based on observation, satellite and meteorological data. The second part further quantifies the contributions of multiple-source factors in multiple Chinese cities during the lockdowns in the warm season of 2022, utilizing the Random Forest (RF) model and Shapley Additive Explanation (SHAP) approach. The third part investigates the future evolution of summertime surface O₃ under China’s carbon neutrality target and the ambitious global 2 °C warming scenario utilizing the Community Multiscale Air Quality (CMAQ) model. Surface observations of O₃ and nitrogen dioxide (NO₂) were analyzed, as well as the satellite-retrieved tropospheric NO₂ and formaldehyde (HCHO) columns, during the 2022 lockdown period in Shanghai in comparison to the corresponding period in 2021. The city-average maximum daily 8 h average (MDA8) O₃ increased by 13%, despite sharp declines in surface and column NO₂ (both by ~49%) and a 19% decrease in column HCHO. This shows that the reductions in O₃ precursors and other pollutants did not prevent surface O₃ p

title: Supply Chain Transformation and Innovation in Global Expansion Amid Geopolitical Challenges: A Case Study of CATL
summary: Amidst a global landscape characterised by the convergence of geopolitical risks and green trade barriers, CATL has overcome geopolitical barriers through its Light Asset technology licensing model, built compliance competitiveness through
content: Amidst a global landscape characterised by the convergence of geopolitical risks and green trade barriers, CATL has overcome geopolitical barriers through its Light Asset technology licensing model, built compliance competitiveness through zero-carbon and smart manufacturing, promoted collaborative global expansion across the industrial chain, and achieved deep localisation. It has successfully transformed geopolitical pressures into strategic opportunities, achieving the upgrading and transformation of its corporate supply chain. This provides a model of sustainable resilience for the global development of China’s high-end manufacturing enterprises.

title: Цифровая экономика как фактор развития новых качественных производительных сил предприятий: механизм воздействия и пороговый эффект в контексте целей «двойной углеродной нейтральности»
summary: Цифровая экономика, являющаяся результатом глубокой интеграции цифровых технологий и социальной деятельности, выступает ключевым драйвером развития новых качественных производительных сил и важной возможностью для трансформации и модернизац
content: Цифровая экономика, являющаяся результатом глубокой интеграции цифровых технологий и социальной деятельности, выступает ключевым драйвером развития новых качественных производительных сил и важной возможностью для трансформации и модернизации. На основе данных об акционерных предприятиях Китая в данной статье представлено как строится комплексная система оценки новых качественных производительных сил предприятий и уровня развития цифровой экономики, а также исследуется механизм воздействия цифровой экономики на новые качественные производительные силы предприятий в условиях целей «двойной углеродной нейтральности». Результаты исследования показывают, что цифровая экономика значимо способствует развитию новых качественных производительных сил предприятий через три канала: общую факторную производительность предприятий, низкоуглеродную трансформацию структуры энергопотребления и зеленые технологические инновации. Анализ продемонстрировал, что на предприятиях, расположенных в центральных и западных регионах Китая, негосударственных, с высоким уровнем финансовых ограничений, а также в высокотехнологичных компаниях, цифровая экономика оказывает более сильное стимулирующее воздействие на развитие новых качественных производительных сил. As a product of the deep integration of digital technology and social activities, the digital economy is a key driving force for the development of new productive forces and an important opportunity for transformation and upgrading. Based on the data of enterprises in China, the article presents how a comprehensive evaluation index for the new quality productivity of enterprises and the digital economy is constructed, and the empowerment mechanism of the digital economy for the new quality productivity of enterprises under the double carbon neutrality targets is discussed. The research finds that the digital economy can significantly empower the development of new quality production in enterprises through three transmission mechanisms: total factor productivity of enterprises, low-carbonization of energy structure consumption, and green technological innovation. Analysis indicates that the digital economy has a stronger promoting effect on the new quality productivity of enterprises when they are located in the central and western regions of China, non-state-owned enterprises, have a higher degree of financing constraints, and are high-tech enterprises.

title: A stock-and-flow model of biofuels and carbon
summary: Abstract The climate benefit of biofuels depends on how well their production offsets the biogenic carbon emitted by their use. It is commonly assumed that carbon uptake during feedstock growth renders biofuels carbon neutral aside from anc
content: Abstract The climate benefit of biofuels depends on how well their production offsets the biogenic carbon emitted by their use. It is commonly assumed that carbon uptake during feedstock growth renders biofuels carbon neutral aside from ancillary fossil carbon and other production-related greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. This assumption of a feedstock offset is retained in the lifecycle assessment (LCA) models adopted by policymakers for renewable fuels. However, consideration of land-use change (LUC) and other economically induced effects has revealed carbon flow changes more complex than those of a feedstock offset. This paper presents a relatively simple stock-and-flow model that offers a conceptual understanding of the carbon-related dynamics of biofuel use. The model focuses only on key carbon exchanges, omitting the ancillary emissions while capturing the economic impacts of increased crop yields, cropland expansion with LUC, decreased food demand and petroleum market rebound. Applied to a stylized scenario of corn ethanol use, the model transparently depicts effects and trade-offs previously characterized by LCA and other complex methods. It reframes biofuel carbon neutrality in terms of distinct market-mediated mechanisms of net uptake that can offset the biogenic carbon emitted from biofuel use while highlighting the dynamics of the atmospheric carbon response. As a complement to LCA, stock-and-flow analysis can be informative for policymakers and valuable for educational purposes.

title: Valuing the Invisible: Consequences of Institutional Investors' Climate Change Attention on Commodity Multilayer Information Spillover Network Dynamics
summary: ABSTRACT This study investigates how institutional investors' climate attention shapes multilayer information spillovers across commodity‑futures markets from 2014 to 2024. Using daily data for 27 commodity futures, this study examines how
content: ABSTRACT This study investigates how institutional investors' climate attention shapes multilayer information spillovers across commodity‑futures markets from 2014 to 2024. Using daily data for 27 commodity futures, this study examines how institutional climate change attention affects multilayer information spillovers across return, volatility, short‐term tail risk, and long‐term skewness risk within. The network topology reveals that fossil fuels act as primary risk emitters, with short‐term tail risk dominating long‐term skewness spillovers. To accurately quantify institutional climate attention, we isolate an effective climate attention index by filtering out Bloomberg search volume noise using a two‐step rolling error correction model. Crucially, empirical results show that institutional climate attention exerts a state‐dependent stabilizing effect: it actively dampens tail risk propagation during market upturns, but weakens significantly during severe downturns, leaving networks vulnerable to contagion. These findings highlight climate attention's nuanced role in systemic risk transmission and commodity market regulation.

title: Optimal multi-period dynamic portfolios for sustainable investing
summary: Sustainable investing involves balancing traditional investment strategies with environmental, social, and governance-related (ESG) objectives to improve long-term outcomes. We develop a stochastic control framework for constructing optimal
content: Sustainable investing involves balancing traditional investment strategies with environmental, social, and governance-related (ESG) objectives to improve long-term outcomes. We develop a stochastic control framework for constructing optimal multi-period dynamic ESG portfolios, in which investors form dynamic portfolios by maximizing utility functions that account for both profitability and the average ESG scores of their portfolios in the near and distant future. We provide an explicit solution to the investors' utility maximization problem, and show that the optimal weight is a linear combination of three components: a financial performance component, an ESG component, and a component reflecting the weight from the previous period. Using the U.S. stock market data, we find that the multi-period dynamic ESG portfolio outperforms single-period portfolios in terms of returns, Sharpe ratios, alphas, and information ratios. Our article extends dynamic portfolio theory in the context of sustainable investing, and provides guidance to practitioners on tailoring ESG portfolios to their specific preferences and to market conditions related to ESG.

title: SpecFLASH: A Latent-Guided Semi-Autoregressive Speculative Decoding Framework for Efficient Multimodal Generation
source: ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM MM)
summary: Large language models and large multimodal models (LLMs and LMMs) deliver strong generative performance but suffer from slow decoding, a problem that becomes more severe when handling visual inputs, whose sequences typically contain many mo
content: Large language models and large multimodal models (LLMs and LMMs) deliver strong generative performance but suffer from slow decoding, a problem that becomes more severe when handling visual inputs, whose sequences typically contain many more tokens with lower information density than text. Speculative decoding accelerates LLM inference by letting a compact draft model propose candidate tokens that are selectively accepted by a larger target model, achieving speed-up without degrading quality. However, existing multimodal speculative decoding approaches largely ignore the structural characteristics of visual representations and usually rely on text-only draft models. In this paper, we introduce SpecFLASH, a speculative decoding framework tailored to LMMs that explicitly exploits multimodal structure when designing the draft model. We first mitigate redundancy in visual token sequences with a lightweight, latent-guided token compression module that compacts visual features while preserving semantics, and then leverage the co-occurrence and local correlations of visual entities via a semi-autoregressive decoding scheme that predicts multiple tokens in a single forward pass. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SpecFLASH consistently surpasses prior speculative decoding baselines, achieving up to 2.68× speed-up on video captioning and 2.55× on visual instruction tuning, relative to the original LMM.

title: Membrane Lipid Composition and Asymmetry Modulate Translocation Versus Leakage of the Model Amphipathic Peptide MAP
source: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
summary: Abstract Cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs) can enable intracellular access while avoiding cytotoxicity, yet their behavior is highly sensitive to membrane composition. Here we show that lipid composition and leaflet asymmetry act as a switch
content: Abstract Cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs) can enable intracellular access while avoiding cytotoxicity, yet their behavior is highly sensitive to membrane composition. Here we show that lipid composition and leaflet asymmetry act as a switch that determines whether the amphipathic CPP MAP undergoes nondisruptive translocation or stabilizes membrane pores that drive leakage. Using high-field computational electrophysiology (CompEL) simulations in membranes of increasing physiological relevance, we show that electrically induced membrane defects allow the insertion of MAP peptides. We find symmetric anionic bilayers favor MAP insertion coupled to transmembrane pore stabilization in POPC/POPG membranes, reproducing progressive dye release in liposome leakage assays. Incorporation of cholesterol reduces the number of inserted peptides and conducts to faster leakage kinetics in cholesterol-containing vesicles. In contrast, a minimal asymmetric membrane model (POPC extracellular leaflet; POPC/POPS intracellular leaflet) supports MAP translocation without sustained membrane disruption. This delivery-relevant mechanism is supported by efficient MAP internalization in HEK293 cells while maintaining high viability. Polarized ATR–FTIR provides structural context, indicating predominantly membrane-associated α-helical conformations across lipid compositions. Together, these results establish lipid asymmetry and composition as actionable biointerface parameters that tune CPP function between translocation and leakage and demonstrate an experimentally benchmarked framework for predicting membrane outcomes across complex lipid environments.

title: Understanding Charge Acceptance Limitations During Extreme Fast‐Charging of Li‐ion Batteries
summary: ABSTRACT Extreme fast charging in lithium‐ion batteries is limited by their poor charge acceptance at high C‐rates. We use overpotential component analysis to decouple ohmic, kinetic and transport voltage losses during fast charging. The co
content: ABSTRACT Extreme fast charging in lithium‐ion batteries is limited by their poor charge acceptance at high C‐rates. We use overpotential component analysis to decouple ohmic, kinetic and transport voltage losses during fast charging. The concentration gradients are identified as the primary culprit in poor charge acceptance, so we study carbonate electrolytes that utilize acetonitrile, a low viscosity, high dielectric liquid, as a co‐solvent to improve ion transport. Our results indicate acetonitrile co‐solvent successfully reduces fast charging concentration gradients and therefore improves charge acceptance at high C‐rates, particularly when used in combination with interface‐stabilizing additives. Molecular dynamics simulations show that ACN enhances Li + transport through a combination of reduced bulk viscosity and increased solvation‐shell lability, with shorter solvent residence times and faster coordination exchange producing transport gains beyond those expected from viscosity reduction alone. Finally, we use three‐electrode cells to deconvolute overpotential at each electrode, and the specific LiNi 0.8 Mn 0.1 Co 0.1 O 2 (NMC811) electrode architecture and loading used in our study is found to have much higher overpotentials than our graphite electrode. In particular, the significant differences in NMC811 concentration gradients between electrolytes with or without acetonitrile indicate that the design of electrode architecture is crucial for extreme fast charging applications.

title: GLOBAL FAMINE RISK REALITY 2026 OUTLOOK: A FORENSIC ASSESSMENT OF THE COMING CALORIC COLLAPSE
summary: Driven by unprecedented Vapor Pressure Deficit anomalies, global food security faces extreme supply chain fragility compounded by the catastrophic liquidation of foundational livestock breeding stock. This forensic assessment synthesizes em
content: Driven by unprecedented Vapor Pressure Deficit anomalies, global food security faces extreme supply chain fragility compounded by the catastrophic liquidation of foundational livestock breeding stock. This forensic assessment synthesizes empirical agronomic, macroeconomic, and logistical ground data from March through October 2026 to audit the multi-commodity caloric shortfall confronting Western Europe, the United Kingdom, and import-dependent nations heading into the 2026–2027 consumption cycle. Institutional monitoring mechanisms (USDA WASDE, European Commission JRC MARS, FAO AMIS) currently operate on a structural reporting lag of 90 to 180 days, relying on satellite vegetation indices (NDVI) that mistake metabolically halted, heat-stressed canopies for productive biomass while aggregating inedible feed-grade cereals with human bread wheat. Concurrently, a tri-fold carbohydrate production shock—manifesting as a 25.4% physical contraction in European potatoes, multi-decade cereal lows, and depleted global pulse pipelines—collides with the geopolitical bifurcation of global agricultural trade, in which primary exportable surpluses have routed into an overland BRICS+ caloric circuit. As hardware-embedded cyber disruptions destabilize centralized cold-chain hubs and just-in-time logistics, the erosion of household caloric sufficiency is triggering severe social stress. This crisis is marked by an accelerating divergence between official headline inflation metrics and real-world food costs, accelerating the rise of informal parallel distribution networks, micro-theft, and cash-and-carry gray arbitrage. With biological gestation timelines and depleted storage buffers eliminating retroactive intervention options, this report outlines non-negotiable directives for municipal civil protection, decentralized physical caloric auditing, strategic reserve requisitioning, and baseline social safety net preservation during the narrow 90-to-120-day operational action window remaining before late-spring 2027.

title: Integrated CFD-Quantitative Microbial Risk Assessment analysis of thermal comfort, particle deposition and indirect infection risk in a conference room under different occupancy scenarios
summary: Abstract Conference rooms experience large and rapid variations in occupancy, which alter internal heat gains and the interaction between supply jets and occupant thermal plumes. This study investigates how occupancy affects thermal comfort
content: Abstract Conference rooms experience large and rapid variations in occupancy, which alter internal heat gains and the interaction between supply jets and occupant thermal plumes. This study investigates how occupancy affects thermal comfort, the deposition of exhaled droplets on occupants and the associated indirect (deposition–hand–mucosa) infection-risk indicators in a mechanically ventilated hotel conference room in Naples, Italy. A steady RANS model of the airflow and temperature fields is coupled with one-way Lagrangian tracking of 10 µm droplets released by the speaker, and the predicted deposition on each occupant is used as input to a Quantitative Microbial Risk Assessment (QMRA) chain. The model is verified through grid and time-step sensitivity analyses and validated against benchmark data from the literature. Four occupancy levels are compared: 25%, 50%, full and overfull condition with standing attendees. Increasing occupancy shifts the flow from a jet-dominated to a plume-influenced regime and raises the PMV from about −0.5 at 25% occupancy to +0.41 on average, and up to +0.75 in individual rows, under overfull conditions. In all scenarios, the first row receives the largest share of droplets among seated occupants (3.1–3.7% of the emitted droplets), whereas under overfull conditions the standing row along the [windowless] side receives 10.6%. Under conservative assumptions, the corresponding QMRA indicators reach about 0.44% for the first row and 1.45% for the standing row. The results indicate that deposition-related exposure is governed by the airflow pathways between the source and the main outlet rather than by distance alone, and that occupancy management and ventilation design should jointly consider thermal comfort and deposition hotspots.

title: Towards a greener heterogeneous Fenton process for removing emerging contaminants from urban wastewater: a recent short review
summary: Emerging contaminants in urban wastewater, including pharmaceuticals, poly- and perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), personal care products, surfactants, and disinfection byproducts, represent an increasing environmental and public health conc
content: Emerging contaminants in urban wastewater, including pharmaceuticals, poly- and perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), personal care products, surfactants, and disinfection byproducts, represent an increasing environmental and public health concern because conventional urban wastewater treatment plants (uWWTPs) are unable to remove them efficiently. Among advanced oxidation processes the heterogeneous Fenton process has emerged as a promising alternative due to its ability to operate in some cases at near-neutral pH, minimize ferric sludge generation, enable catalyst recovery and reuse, and achieve efficient degradation of a wide range of emerging contaminants. This short review analyzes recent literature published between 2020 and 2026 to evaluate the current state of heterogeneous Fenton technology for urban wastewater treatment and to identify the main challenges preventing its transition into a truly green technology. The review discusses the occurrence, environmental impacts, and treatment requirements of major groups of emerging contaminants and examines key factors influencing heterogeneous Fenton performance, including contaminant adsorption, effects of scavengers (Cl − and Br − ), catalyst design, catalyst dosage, catalyst size, toxicity of oxidation/degradation byproducts post treatment, scalability of the heterogeneous Fenton process, operational issues related to neutral pH, etc. Based on this analysis, future research priorities are proposed, emphasizing the development of durable catalysts, optimization under real urban wastewater conditions, identify and characterize oxidation/degradation byproducts in the effluent, conduct comprehensive toxicity assessments, evaluate long-term environmental and biological risks under realistic and large-scale treatment conditions, incorporation of life cycle assessment and techno-economic analyses (research gaps), and scale up validation. Addressing these challenges will accelerate the green transition and large-scale implementation of heterogeneous Fenton process as an efficient process for removing emerging contaminants from urban wastewater.

title: UKCEH Countryside Survey state and change soil data for Great Britain, 1978–2023
summary: Abstract. The UKCEH Countryside Survey (CS) represents the longest ongoing integrated national monitoring program for the countryside of Great Britain (GB), providing policy relevant evidence on environmental condition. Through the use of a
content: Abstract. The UKCEH Countryside Survey (CS) represents the longest ongoing integrated national monitoring program for the countryside of Great Britain (GB), providing policy relevant evidence on environmental condition. Through the use of a co-located sampling design across soils, vegetation, woodlands and waterbodies, the data offer a holistic insight into shifts in environmental condition, the drivers of change and the complex patterns that result across ecosystems, to address a variety of research questions. The soils component of CS is arguably one of the world’s most enduring national-scale datasets on soil health, tracking state and change as part of this broader ‘audit’ of the GB countryside. The monitoring program has been active since 1978, with the latest complete monitoring cycle concluding in 2023 and a new monitoring cycle currently underway (2024–28). The primary aim of this paper is to compile and synthesise all published datasets pertaining to soil state and change, whilst bringing the dataset up to date by reporting on data from the latest cycle (2019–2023). The dataset comprises >8600 topsoil samples from 2,233 plots surveyed over nearly five decades. A comprehensive array of physico-chemical properties are regularly updated with each monitoring cycle, including pH, soil organic matter (SOM), soil organic carbon (SOC, concentration and stock), bulk density, gravimetric moisture content and nutrient loading, though nitrogen content (concentration and stock) and plant-available phosphorus (Olsen P). Nevertheless, numerous additional national baseline metrics have been established throughout the years to address specific policy and research inquiries, including indicators of pollution (heavy metals and organics), biodiversity measures such as invertebrate biodiversity and eDNA based biodiversity estimated for bacteria, fungi and plants, and supporting metrics that facilitate interpretation of soils data, such as texture via laser diffraction particle size analysis, total carbon and CaCO3. Further datasets have been established through specific research queries and use of airdried and frozen soils in the UKCEH soil bank. Contextual data is supplied regarding habitat type, land management practices, and soil type, facilitating wider use of the dataset and subsampling according to need. The datasets have been widely used across over 200 publications and are available under an open government licence, facilitating a unique evaluation of soil state and change over time, within the context of a suit of co-located habitat condition metrics from across Great Britain.

title: Carbon emissions reduction potential of carbon pricing policies in China
summary: The carbon tax and the carbon emissions trading scheme (ETS) are two widely adopted carbon pricing mechanisms for reducing carbon emissions. While China has prioritized the implementation of a national ETS, it remains an open and important
content: The carbon tax and the carbon emissions trading scheme (ETS) are two widely adopted carbon pricing mechanisms for reducing carbon emissions. While China has prioritized the implementation of a national ETS, it remains an open and important empirical question whether a carbon tax or a hybrid policy could offer superior performance in terms of carbon emissions reduction potential and efficiency. This policy comparison constitutes a counterfactual that cannot be directly observed under the current policy pathway. To enable a controlled counterfactual comparison, we model the ETS as an idealized, mass-based system with allowances ex-post equal to actual emissions and treat carbon tax payments as input costs. Using data envelopment analysis (DEA) on China’s electric and thermal power industry, we evaluate the performance of these two policies. Our counterfactual simulations indicate that, under this specific theoretical setup, both policies offer substantial abatement potential. Notably, the relative abatement potential of the ETS is larger, as it allows for reallocating abatement efforts among firms, while the relative technical efficiency of decision-making units (DMUs) is higher under the carbon tax, which imposes a uniform price signal on all emitters. Given these complementary strengths, we suggest China retain the national ETS and develop hybrid carbon pricing to advance carbon neutrality.

title: Metal-Free Bifunctional N-Heterocyclic Catalysts for CO2 Cycloaddition to Three-Membered Rings
summary: The development of sustainable strategies for carbon dioxide valorization is essential to achieve climate neutrality. Among nonreductive CO2 conversion routes, the cycloaddition of CO2 to epoxides and aziridines represents an atom-efficient
content: The development of sustainable strategies for carbon dioxide valorization is essential to achieve climate neutrality. Among nonreductive CO2 conversion routes, the cycloaddition of CO2 to epoxides and aziridines represents an atom-efficient approach for the synthesis of cyclic carbonates and oxazolidinones, valuable compounds with significant industrial, technological, and pharmaceutical relevance.While metal-based catalysts have been extensively investigated, metalfree systems are promising alternatives owing to their lower environmental impact, reduced cost, and potential to operate under mild conditions. This review summarizes recent literature (2020-present) on the use of homogeneous bifunctional metal-free catalysts bearing N-heterocyclic moieties for CO2 cycloaddition to three-membered rings.

title: Editorial: Big data mining and artificial intelligence in earth science
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) for geoscience uses intelligent algorithms to extract concealed patterns from big Earth data, enabling more accurate predictions and decisions in scientific discoveries and applications, such as Earth's evolutio
content: Artificial intelligence (AI) for geoscience uses intelligent algorithms to extract concealed patterns from big Earth data, enabling more accurate predictions and decisions in scientific discoveries and applications, such as Earth's evolution, geological modeling, environmental monitoring, hazard mitigation, and resource exploration (Zhou et al., 2018(Zhou et al., , 2026)). Its evolution has followed a clear paradigm transition-from early expert systems through data-driven machine learning, to the current physics-informed, knowledge-data dual-driven approaches (Zhou et al., 2018;Zuo et al., 2023;Cheng et al., 2025). This progression is not merely incremental; it is fundamentally reshaping geoscience by integrating big data analytics with machine learning algorithms, and in doing so, redefining the practices of many researchers and engineers in their daily work (Zuo et al., 2023;Zhou et al., 2026). This is the reason why this special topic issue comes to exist here. It is devoted to showcase recent advances in the research and application of AI across many geoscience disciplines. It highlights innovative methodologies in data science, machine learning, and 2 / 14 generative AI technologies that address the integration and interpretation of multidisciplinary geoscientific data.The special issue is also initiated to commemorates the 10th anniversary of the Committee on Artificial Intelligence and Big Data for Geosciences, established under the Chinese Society for Mineralogy, Petrology and Geochemistry in 2016, with Professor Zhou Yongzhang, then the awardee of the IAMG Felix Chayes Prize, as its inaugural Chair (Zhou et al., 2026). This marked the first organized effort in China to promote AI and big data research in mineralogy, petrology and geochemistry, and was among the earliest such professional bodies worldwide. In 2018, the committee published the textbook Big Data Mining and Machine Learning for Earth Science (Zhou et al., 2018). In April 2026, the 10th China Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Big Data for Geosciences was held at Hefei, drawing over 1,200 participants-a clear indicator of the rapidly growing interest in intelligent geoscience.Featuring 18 original contributions, this special issue focuses on three transformative areas: intelligent prospecting of solid metal deposits, intelligent sedimentary and reservoir evaluation, and intelligent prediction of Earth processes and geological systems. The methods span from conventional machine learning to deep learning, knowledge graphs, large language models (LLMs), and beyond, reflecting both the breadth and depth of current AI-driven geoscience research.The intelligent prospecting of solid metal deposits is revolutionizing mineral exploration through the integration of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and advanced remote sensing. These technologies synthesize extensive geological, geophysical, and geochemical datasets to identify concealed mineralization patterns with exce

title: Blue carbon stocks and wetland landscape change in the Liaohe Estuary
summary: Introduction Coastal-wetland carbon assessments can support conservation and restoration monitoring when measured carbon pools are interpreted alongside habitat extent. This study compared carbon stocks in the dominant natural habitats of t
content: Introduction Coastal-wetland carbon assessments can support conservation and restoration monitoring when measured carbon pools are interpreted alongside habitat extent. This study compared carbon stocks in the dominant natural habitats of the Liaohe Estuary and examined landscape change and observations at a restoration site. Methods Natural-habitat aboveground vegetation carbon and 0-100 cm soil organic carbon were compared in a common areal unit. Exploratory Landsat classifications described landscape change during 1985-2020, and four monitoring campaigns characterized vegetation and soil conditions at a Daling River Estuary restoration site. Results Natural Suaeda salsa meadows had higher mean soil organic carbon stocks than Phragmites australis marshes (112.71 ± 49.77 versus 68.56 ± 44.62 Mg C ha⁻¹), whereas P. australis had greater aboveground vegetation carbon. Combined measured soil and aboveground stocks were 114.72 and 73.01 Mg C ha⁻¹, respectively, with soil contributing 98.3% and 93.9%. The mapped natural-wetland area contracted before an apparent increase after 2015; the unvalidated classifications provide landscape context. At the restoration site, aboveground stocks were 0.18048 and 1.833 Mg C ha⁻¹ in November 2020 and July 2022, with corresponding soil stocks of 149.08 and 163.49 Mg C ha⁻¹. Discussion The restoration-site observations differ in season and lack a concurrent unrestored reference; they therefore describe monitoring conditions rather than restoration-attributable carbon gains. The findings support protecting existing soil carbon and combining validated habitat mapping with seasonally consistent vegetation-soil monitoring.

title: Digital fiscal governance and reforms in developed and developing economies: A comparative bibliometric analysis
summary: Digital fiscal governance and associated architectural reforms have fundamentally transformed tax administration, public financial management, and corporate revenue governance across advanced and emerging economies. Technological innovation
content: Digital fiscal governance and associated architectural reforms have fundamentally transformed tax administration, public financial management, and corporate revenue governance across advanced and emerging economies. Technological innovation has accelerated fiscal modernization, particularly following macroeconomic disruptions such as the COVID-19 pandemic. However, the academic literature remains fragmented across public governance, development economics, and international taxation perspectives. Drawing upon foundational paradigms established by Besley and Persson (2014) regarding state capacity and the modernization frameworks of the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD, 2021), this study conducts a comparative bibliometric analysis of digital fiscal governance reform scholarship indexed in Scopus and LENS between 2000 and 2026. Through co-occurrence network analysis and thematic clustering, five dominant research streams are identified: governance and crisis-driven digitalization; sustainable development and tax reform; competitiveness and productivity; globalization and political economy; and digital economy and administrative capacity building. Findings reveal a stark divergence between developed-economy research, which emphasizes technological optimization, and developing-economy scholarship, which focuses on institutional capacity building. The study proposes an integrative model of fiscal resilience linking digitalization, administrative capacity, revenue performance, development outcomes, sustainability, and fiscal resilience. The results provide theoretical synthesis and policy insights relevant to international tax governance and digital public administration.

title: Macrobenthic fauna associated with maërl beds near aquaculture installations in the north-eastern Corinthian Gulf, Greece, with remarks on two taxa
summary: Maërl beds, also known as rhodolith beds, are biogenic benthic habitats formed by unattached coralline algae and support diverse macrobenthic assemblages. In the Mediterranean, especially its eastern basin, information on their distribution
content: Maërl beds, also known as rhodolith beds, are biogenic benthic habitats formed by unattached coralline algae and support diverse macrobenthic assemblages. In the Mediterranean, especially its eastern basin, information on their distribution, ecological condition and associated fauna remains limited. Maërl beds are sensitive to physical disturbance, sedimentation and organic enrichment, including pressures associated with aquaculture activities. This data paper describes the macrobenthic fauna associated with maërl beds located near and further from finfish farms in the Traxilos area of the north-eastern Corinthian Gulf, Greece. The dataset comprises eight sampling events and 328 abundance-based occurrence records representing 6,410 individuals. The paper also provides morphological notes on two polychaete taxa, Syllis nigricirris and the Neanthioides acuminata species complex, documenting variation in diagnostically relevant characters.

title: Integrated Human–Equipment Reliability Assessment of Ammonia Loss of Containment During Shore-to-Ship Bunkering
source: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
summary: Current studies on ammonia bunkering safety have largely focused on release scenarios, dispersion modelling and equipment-related hazards, while human error, equipment failure and emergency response are often assessed separately. This creat
content: Current studies on ammonia bunkering safety have largely focused on release scenarios, dispersion modelling and equipment-related hazards, while human error, equipment failure and emergency response are often assessed separately. This creates an important gap because the safety of ammonia bunkering depends on how operators and engineered systems work together during both routine and abnormal conditions. This study therefore develops an integrated human–equipment reliability framework for shore-to-ship ammonia bunkering, with emphasis on loss-of-containment scenarios. The study combines Hierarchical Task Analysis, Bow-tie analysis and the HEART to identify critical human actions, estimate human error probabilities and map the equipment associated with preventive and mitigative safety functions. Rather than assuming that all equipment simply reduces human error, the framework distinguishes between equipment that supports human tasks, alarm systems that require a subsequent human response, human-initiated engineered functions, and independent protective barriers. Appropriate reliability relationships are then applied according to the role of each barrier. The HEART results identified tank-capacity verification and hose-connection verification as critical preventive activities, with bounded human error probabilities of 1.00000 under the adopted assessment assumptions. The integrated reliability assessment also showed that an independent valve interlock increased the estimated reliability of the valve-line-up safety function to 0.91360, whereas the gas-alarm and evacuation function achieved 0.791946 because successful mitigation depended on both equipment operation and human response. Sensitivity analysis further demonstrated that these estimates were influenced by the adopted equipment probability of failure on demand (PFD) values and HEART input assumptions. The study provides a function-based way of representing human–equipment interaction in ammonia bunkering safety assessment. The framework is intended as a semi-quantitative screening approach for identifying vulnerable tasks and strengthening preventive and mitigative barriers where installation-specific reliability data remain limited.

title: Understanding pre-owned electric vehicle purchase intentions: An extended Theory of Planned Behavior approach
summary: The electric vehicle (EV) market is expanding rapidly owing to environmental concerns that accelerate the shift toward sustainable transportation. Pre-owned EVs can widen adoption by offering a cost-effective alternative; however, they comb
content: The electric vehicle (EV) market is expanding rapidly owing to environmental concerns that accelerate the shift toward sustainable transportation. Pre-owned EVs can widen adoption by offering a cost-effective alternative; however, they combine the traits of both new EVs and conventional used cars, creating decision complexities that remain understudied. To address this gap, we extend the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) with EV-specific benefit and risk and test the model using survey data from 347 licensed South Korean drivers with EV experience who plan to purchase vehicles. Our structural equation modeling shows that attitude ( β = 0.624), subjective norm ( β = 0.221), and perceived behavioral control ( β = 0.180) significantly enhance the intention to buy pre-owned EVs, with attitude being the strongest factor. Moreover, the proposed extended Theory of Planned Behavior accounts for 62.2% of the variance in pre-owned EV purchase intentions Users’ attitude grows with perceived benefit and declines with perceived risk. Critical motivation is the leading source of perceived benefit, whereas financial risk is the dominant perceived risk. The extended TPB framework provides evidence for clarifying how intrinsic motivations and EV-related risks shape consumer perceptions and ultimately purchase intention in the secondary EV market. Practically, policymakers and marketers should stress the environmental and symbolic merits of used EVs, supply transparent battery health metrics, and offer financial guarantees to reduce risk and stimulate demand.

title: From deliberative practice to algorithmic theatre: Generative AI and the risk of performative compliance in environmental due diligence
summary: Generative AI is usually defended in the language of efficiency. Environmental due diligence, however, rests on documents machines can now draft, submit and summarise. This article proposes algorithmic theatre as an explanatory model of a r
content: Generative AI is usually defended in the language of efficiency. Environmental due diligence, however, rests on documents machines can now draft, submit and summarise. This article proposes algorithmic theatre as an explanatory model of a risk in which compliance artefacts keep their legal form and authority while the deliberation they record thins or disappears. Using Dryzek’s criteria of authenticity, inclusiveness and consequentiality, it reads three episodes as plausibility probes (AI pilots under the National Environmental Policy Act, fabricated public comments and false data in carbon credit verification) and specifies three hypothesised mechanisms: de-skilling, decoupling and legitimacy transfer. A comparison of the United States, the European Union and Pakistan suggests that exposure depends less on a jurisdiction’s wealth than on whether its law attends to the provenance of compliance information, and is greatest where participatory infrastructure is already weak. Safeguards follow, including a draft provision for the disasters convention now under negotiation.

title: Potential Synergies Between Universities and Industry across the CCUS Value Chain: From Scientific Discovery to Industrial Deployment
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Carbon Capture, Utilazation and Storage - CCUS, requires multidisciplinary collaboration across the entire value chain. Universities generate scientific knowledge, research, and innovation. Industry enables technology deployment, scale-up,
content: Carbon Capture, Utilazation and Storage - CCUS, requires multidisciplinary collaboration across the entire value chain. Universities generate scientific knowledge, research, and innovation. Industry enables technology deployment, scale-up, and commercialization. Government provides the policy and regulatory frameworks that enable implementation. Strong University - Industry - Government partnerships can accelerate the transition toward carbon neutrality. The future of CCUS depends not only on technological innovation, but also on effective collaboration.

title: Addressing planning gaps to enhance urban resilience and air quality
summary: The increasing urgency posed by climate change and air pollution challenges calls for integrated policy approaches able to promote resilient and healthy cities. Research is needed to support cities in developing strategies to reduce their c
content: The increasing urgency posed by climate change and air pollution challenges calls for integrated policy approaches able to promote resilient and healthy cities. Research is needed to support cities in developing strategies to reduce their carbon footprint and air pollution, as well as enhance resilience, while maximising synergies and optimising the use of resources. This paper contributes to this research need by examining the current degree of integration between urban air quality and climate plans in a multi-level governance framework, using the Tuscany region in Italy as a multiple case study. The methodological approach, based on a deep deductive content analysis of both air quality and climate planning documents, provides a detailed overview of the key factors that can foster stronger mutual integration between the two policy domains. The factors considered are grouped into two categories: endogenous ones, which refer to internal elements influencing the planning process (such as support from sub-national authorities and citizen participation), and exogenous ones, which refer to the broader socio-political context (including involvement in transnational climate networks and initiatives). The results show that local governments, whilst demonstrating climate ambition and promptness to planning action, often face barriers to implementation that can be mitigated through increased policy dialogue between administrative levels, transnational comparisons and active participatory processes. These findings contribute to the identification of key enablers for more coherent and comprehensive urban planning, and inform the ongoing discourse on integrated, multi-level environmental governance.

title: Acid-Etched Lead Telluride with Defect-Regulated Surfaces Enables Efficient Mechanical-Energy-Driven Nitrogen Fixation
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
summary: Abstract Ambient ammonia synthesis is important for carbon neutrality. Tribo-electro-catalysis, which converts mechanical friction into chemical driving force through contact electrification and charge transfer, offers a route for nitrogen
content: Abstract Ambient ammonia synthesis is important for carbon neutrality. Tribo-electro-catalysis, which converts mechanical friction into chemical driving force through contact electrification and charge transfer, offers a route for nitrogen (N2) fixation. However, inefficient utilization of friction-induced charges and insufficient N2 activation remain major challenges. Herein, acid-etching defect engineering regulates the surface and electronic structures of lead telluride (PbTe) for N2 fixation. The catalyst etched for 90 min exhibits the enhanced activity under dark ambient conditions, delivering ammonium (NH4+) production rates of 258.98 and 329.60 μmol L–1·g–1·h–1 without and with 10 vol % methanol, respectively. Analyses reveal that etching reconstructs the surface, generates defect sites, facilitates N2 adsorption and activation, and promotes friction-induced charge utilization. Excessive etching decreases activity. Charge-trapping and electron paramagnetic resonance measurements support the role of friction-induced negative charges, establishing defect-mediated charge regulation as an effective strategy for sustainable ammonia synthesis.

title: Summertime overheating in apartments with glazed balconies: a Finnish study
summary: Apartment overheating is increasingly an issue due to rising global temperatures, likely exceeding 2°C in Finland over the next few decades. This overlooked issue in Nordic housing is exacerbated by building characteristics ill-suited to ke
content: Apartment overheating is increasingly an issue due to rising global temperatures, likely exceeding 2°C in Finland over the next few decades. This overlooked issue in Nordic housing is exacerbated by building characteristics ill-suited to keeping cool indoor environments, such as lack of solar shading or large operable windows and the use of glazed balconies. However, there is limited empirical evidence on summertime overheating in glazed-balcony apartments in the Nordic climate. To bridge this gap, this exploratory case-study investigation assessed summertime overheating in 10 apartments with glazed balconies in Finland during the summer of 2025 and investigated how occupant behaviour affected overheating risk. In-situ temperature measurements were collected in the balcony and apartment spaces alongside semi-structured interviews and balcony-use diaries. Findings highlighted that apartments built to the current Finnish building code failed to meet overheating criteria, and the presence of a glazed balcony was one of several variables linked to apartment overheating. Glazed balconies became uncomfortably hot for extended periods, limiting the intended year-round usability. Moreover, the balcony door was often the apartment’s sole purge ventilation route and was found to be ineffective. These findings are increasingly relevant internationally as glazed balcony solutions are gaining adoption in other contexts. PRACTICE RELEVANCE There is a pressing need to implement overheating mitigation strategies for glazed balconies, as well as the apartment more generally, to reduce associated risks. Designers and manufacturers must provide robust balcony-glazing solutions with proven operability that support pet-safe intensive ventilation, shading, furniture placement and everyday usability. Apartment window systems outside of the glazed balcony should also enable large and safe openings for effective natural ventilation. Indirect factors to be considered include: (1) updating regulatory climate datasets to consider current and future climate scenarios; (2) the balcony glazing should systematically be drawn with ‘glazing fully open’ as the default state during design ensuring usability in this condition; and (3) occupant behaviour should be supported through explicit guidance, including recommending to fully open balcony glazing during warm periods.

title: Upfront Embodied Carbon for Carbon-Neutral Buildings: Trends and Analysis of Domestic and International Standards and Certification Systems
summary: This structured narrative review examines how building-level calculation methods, product data and assessment results are connected in embodied-carbon certification and regulation. Upfront embodied carbon is defined by modules A1–A5; whole-
content: This structured narrative review examines how building-level calculation methods, product data and assessment results are connected in embodied-carbon certification and regulation. Upfront embodied carbon is defined by modules A1–A5; whole-life instruments are included as institutional comparators. The comparison distinguishes method linkage, product-data requirements and the use of results, because standardized calculation and certification scoring can coexist. Denmark and France apply statutory carbon limits, but their module coverage, floor-area definitions and metrics differ. Sweden requires climate declarations, while the EU has established future reporting obligations and national limit-value roadmaps. In Korea, G-SEED provides a voluntary life-cycle assessment credit and refers to international standards, and a product-level environmental product declaration scheme is available. However, the reviewed instruments do not establish a common mandatory building-level embodied-carbon reporting and limit-value framework. These findings support developing a shared national calculation method and improving product data in parallel, followed by disclosure and benchmark development before quantitative limits are considered. The study compares institutional arrangements rather than ranking national emission values.

title: Harvest shifts carbon–water dynamics and environmental controls in a managed loblolly pine plantation in the southeast United States
source: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change
summary: How carbon–water coupling reorganizes across stand development and harvest in managed plantations remains poorly quantified. We used 20 years (2005–2024) of eddy covariance measurements at a loblolly pine ( Pinus taeda L.) plantation (US-NC
content: How carbon–water coupling reorganizes across stand development and harvest in managed plantations remains poorly quantified. We used 20 years (2005–2024) of eddy covariance measurements at a loblolly pine ( Pinus taeda L.) plantation (US-NC2, North Carolina, United States) to quantify carbon and water flux dynamics across three stand development stages spanning pre- and post-harvest periods. The harvest in 2019 triggered an abrupt sink-to-source transition (annual NEE in 2020: +991 g C m −2 yr −1 ), driven by asymmetric declines in GPP (88%) and RE (33%). Concurrently, evapotranspiration declined while residual drainage increased, consistent with a shift of water toward drainage. Flux–driver relationships reorganized following harvest, with radiation and leaf area index losing explanatory power for GPP and the leading predictor of net ecosystem exchange shifting from radiation to air temperature. Despite this disruption, NEE declined by 89% within 5 years, approaching but not yet reaching carbon neutrality by 2024. These findings demonstrate that carbon and water fluxes co-evolve via asymmetric harvest responses and reorganization of environmental driver hierarchies, informing carbon accounting and water-resource management in managed pine plantations.

title: Simultaneous transformation of lignocellulosic components using acidic deep eutectic solvents: From action mechanism to scale extraction
summary: Abstract Achieving the balanced valorization of lignocellulosic components is essential for improving atom economy and sustainability in biorefinery, yet remains challenging. Herein, a green and scalable strategy was developed for the syner
content: Abstract Achieving the balanced valorization of lignocellulosic components is essential for improving atom economy and sustainability in biorefinery, yet remains challenging. Herein, a green and scalable strategy was developed for the synergistic conversion of lignocellulosic biomass to polyphenoliclignin and lignocellulosic nanofibers (LCNFs) using customized acidic deep eutectic solvents (DESs). The acidity and hydrogen-bonding capability of the designed DESs were regulated by altering the hydrogen bond donors, including formic, acetic, lactic, and oxalic acids. Kamlet-Taft solvatochromic analysis and DFT calculations showed that the oxalic acid‑based DES (OD) had the strongest hydrogen‑bonding ability ( = 3.340) and acidity ( = 1.882). This efficiently disrupted the hydrogen-bonding network and selectively cleaved lignin ether bonds and glycosidic bonds in amorphous cellulose. Consequently, LCNFs with a high crystallinity index (CrI) of 83% and an average diameter of 7.64 nm were obtained. Simultaneously, high-quality lignin (ODL) was produced with a yield of 63.3%, phenolic hydroxyl content of 11%, nearly 100% purity, and a low molecular weight of 2038 Da. Structural characterization revealed that ODL exhibited substantially reduced and linkages, with guaiacyl (G) and syringyl (S) units accounting for 54.5% and 44.3%, respectively, demonstrating the selective cleavage and structural regulation of lignin by acidic DESs. Furthermore, the DES system was successfully scaled up to a processing capacity of 100 kg lignocellulose per day. This work provides a scalable and mechanistically informed platform for the integrated production of high-purity lignin and LCNFs from lignocellulosic biomass.

title: Under which conditions is it still Green Energy? Photovoltaics on organic soils: A scenario analysis for Germany
summary: Abstract Solar parks generate emission-free electricity, but installations on drained organic soils can lock in substantial greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from peat oxidation. Therefore, combining ground-mounted photovoltaics (GM-PV) with r
content: Abstract Solar parks generate emission-free electricity, but installations on drained organic soils can lock in substantial greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from peat oxidation. Therefore, combining ground-mounted photovoltaics (GM-PV) with rewetting is emerging as a multifunctional climate mitigation strategy in temperate peatland regions. Despite growing interest, data on GM-PV on organic soils (Peatland-PV) remain limited. To address this gap, we conducted a geospatial analysis of Germany's Peatland-PV plants, quantifying associated water table depths (WTD) and GHG fluxes. Based on these findings and socioeconomic projections from the literature reflecting different policy frameworks, we developed three exploratory scenarios of future expansion under three rewetting regimes each. Peatland-PV solar panels covered 1,019 ha of organic soils in Germany as of 1 January 2026 and could expand to 2,604–8,031 ha by 2045 according to our model. We found that most existing sites are deeply drained (median WTD ca. −0.5 m), resulting in annual soil emissions of 39 kilotons (kt) CO₂-eq from the panel–soil intersection area. The future GHG balance of the Peatland-PV sector depends on expansion rate and rewetting policy, rather than geographic location. Continued drainage of Peatland-PV plants could sustain nationwide organic soil related GHG emissions of 89–274 kt CO₂-eq yr ⁻¹ by 2045, while rewetting may reduce these emissions by 21–49%. Our scenarios indicate that Peatland-PV may initially contribute to net climate cooling mainly due to avoided fossil emissions, but under continued drainage a crossover point could occur 2039, at which soil emissions exceed mitigation benefits from renewable energy production.

title: Hydrogen
summary: Hydrogen has emerged as a promising clean energy carrier that can play a transformative role in the global transition toward carbon neutrality and sustainable development. Its exceptional energy density, abundance, and non-polluting combust
content: Hydrogen has emerged as a promising clean energy carrier that can play a transformative role in the global transition toward carbon neutrality and sustainable development. Its exceptional energy density, abundance, and non-polluting combustion characteristics make it a key alternative to fossil fuels. This chapter provides a comprehensive overview of hydrogen energy, covering its importance, fundamental properties, classification by production pathways, and technological methods for its generation. The discussion highlights various hydrogen types—gray, blue, green, turquoise, and biohydrogen—and emphasizes their production processes, carbon footprints, and relevance to achieving net-zero emissions goals. Additionally, this chapter outlines major hydrogen production techniques—thermochemical, electrochemical, and biological—focusing on their efficiency and environmental implications. A detailed SWOT (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats) analysis is presented to critically evaluate hydrogen’s current potential, technological readiness, and prospects in global energy systems. The advantages and disadvantages of hydrogen energy are also analyzed to offer a balanced perspective on its feasibility and sustainability. Overall, this chapter underscores hydrogen’s role as a cornerstone in the clean energy transition and its integration with renewable technologies to build a resilient, low-carbon energy future.

title: Age-dependent dynamics of carbon density in Phyllostachys edulis culms
summary: The underlying age-dependent carbon accumulation in bamboo remains poorly understood. Here, Phyllostachys edulis (moso bamboo) aged 1-10 years were investigated to reveal how carbon-related traits vary with maturity. Eight year old represen
content: The underlying age-dependent carbon accumulation in bamboo remains poorly understood. Here, Phyllostachys edulis (moso bamboo) aged 1-10 years were investigated to reveal how carbon-related traits vary with maturity. Eight year old represents the critical age for maximum volumetric carbon related performance. The mass-based carbon content stayed stable (45.69-46.73 %) across all ages, while basic density rose from 0.51 to 0.67 g/cm 3 for 1 to 8 year old culms, raising volumetric carbon density by 34.78%. Volumetric carbon density peaked at 8 years and correlated closely with basic density. Anatomical lignocellulosic maturation (higher fiber fraction, secondary wall thickening, rising lignin/cellulose crystallinity and falling hemicellulose) drove tissue densification; Raman imaging confirmed progressive lignin deposition into secondary walls. Volumetric energy density followed the same trend as volumetric carbon density. Results demonstrate that improved volumetric carbon storage originates from cell wall densification instead of elevated mass-based intrinsic carbon concentration. This work offers mechanistic understanding for age oriented management to balance carbon sequestration and biomass valorization.

title: ISFR 2026 : Proceedings of the 14th International Symposium on Feedstock Recycling of Polymeric Materials
summary: This volume contains the abstracts presented at the 14th International Symposium on Feedstock Recycling of Polymeric Materials (ISFR 2026), held at Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, Karlsruhe, Germany, from 6 to 9 September 2026. The contr
content: This volume contains the abstracts presented at the 14th International Symposium on Feedstock Recycling of Polymeric Materials (ISFR 2026), held at Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, Karlsruhe, Germany, from 6 to 9 September 2026. The contributions cover chemical and feedstock recycling of polymeric materials, including pyrolysis, catalytic conversion, depolymerisation and process assessment.

title: Policy-Conditioned Attention-Enhanced Temporal Convolutional Networks for Carbon Tax Price Forecasting
source: International Journal of Natural Resources and Environmental Studies
summary: Forecasting administratively determined carbon-tax rates requires models capable of tracking persistent trajectories and discrete policy revisions. Building on the dilated causal temporal convolutional design of Chen et al., we combine a po
content: Forecasting administratively determined carbon-tax rates requires models capable of tracking persistent trajectories and discrete policy revisions. Building on the dilated causal temporal convolutional design of Chen et al., we combine a policy-conditioned input with a temporal attention readout and an explicit last-value residual path, and a matched 2×2 design separates architectural and policy-information contributions.
