Across 64 simulated trajectories with 112 monthly steps each, the proposed model achieves a one-step holdout MAE of 0.1278 and RMSE of 0.1605, and its attention-augmented readout lowers MAE by 4.70% relative to the policy-conditioned plain TCN (0.1341). Advance policy information has the larger effect: withholding it raises MAE to 0.3236, while on 37 policy-jump targets the proposed model attains MAE 0.2207 versus 0.2317 for the policy-conditioned plain TCN. These findings quantify the complementary roles of temporal attention and announcement-time policy schedules and provide a chronological benchmark for policy-aware carbon-tax forecasting.

title: Oman: The Sultanate on the Edge
summary: Oman: The Sultanate on the Edge offers a timely and insightful analysis of Oman’s evolving role as a mediator and its precarious position within a volatile regional landscape. Tracing Oman’s trajectory from the rise of Sultan Qaboos in 1970
content: Oman: The Sultanate on the Edge offers a timely and insightful analysis of Oman’s evolving role as a mediator and its precarious position within a volatile regional landscape. Tracing Oman’s trajectory from the rise of Sultan Qaboos in 1970 to the reform agenda of Sultan Haitham, the book examines the political, economic, and strategic factors that have shaped the Sultanate’s distinctive foreign policy. It explores how Oman’s geography – particularly its control over the Musandam Peninsula and proximity to the Strait of Hormuz – has elevated its regional significance, while also exposing it to external pressures. By analysing Oman’s involvement in regional diplomacy, including efforts to de-escalate tensions in the Gulf, the study highlights the legacy of cautious statecraft that underpins its mediating role. At the same time, it considers domestic challenges, including economic diversification, limits on political dissent, and the resilience of authoritarian governance, assessing the long-term prospects for the Al Said regime. This book will appeal to students and scholars of Middle East politics and international relations, as well as policymakers and general readers interested in Oman’s unique position in regional and global affairs.

title: Trifluoromethanesulfonyl‐Based Reagents: Novel Synthetic Strategies and Mechanistic Insights for Trifluoromethylation Transformations
summary: Trifluoromethylated compounds act as indispensable synthetic building blocks in the fields of agrochemicals, pharmaceuticals, and functional materials, by virtue of their tunable lipophilicity, enhanced cell membrane permeability and superi
content: Trifluoromethylated compounds act as indispensable synthetic building blocks in the fields of agrochemicals, pharmaceuticals, and functional materials, by virtue of their tunable lipophilicity, enhanced cell membrane permeability and superior metabolic stability. The distinctive physicochemical characteristics of the trifluoromethyl group have stimulated tremendous research interest in developing efficient, site‐selective, and scalable synthetic methodologies for the trifluoromethylation of diverse organic molecular skeletons. Over recent years, trifluoromethanesulfonyl‐derived trifluoromethylating reagents have arisen as versatile, bench‐stable, and easily accessible CF 3 sources, facilitating the development of numerous green, atom‐economic, and mild synthetic strategies to access structurally varied trifluoromethylated compounds and functional molecular scaffolds. This review systematically summarizes the advances in catalytic trifluoromethylation reactions enabled by trifluoromethanesulfonyl derivatives, which are categorized into four main types: photoredox catalysis, electrochemical catalysis, metal‐free catalysis, and transition‐metal catalysis for trifluoromethylation transformations.

title: Experiments and numerical simulations on the characteristics and protection of water hammer in long-distance liquid ammonia pipelines
summary: With the expansion of ammonia energy applications, long-distance liquid ammonia pipelines are expected to support large-scale cross-regional ammonia transport. However, rapid valve closure during pipeline operation can generate severe water
content: With the expansion of ammonia energy applications, long-distance liquid ammonia pipelines are expected to support large-scale cross-regional ammonia transport. However, rapid valve closure during pipeline operation can generate severe water hammer pressures, posing significant threats to system safety. In this study, a horizontal liquid ammonia loop system was established to capture the temperature and pressure responses under water hammer conditions, and a one-dimensional transient two-fluid model was validated and developed using OLGA software to simulate the transient water hammer characteristics in industrial-scale long-distance liquid ammonia pipelines. The influence of operating pressure, flow velocity, pipe diameter, valve closure time, and valve closure mode on water hammer behaviors was systematically investigated. The results show that under low operating pressures, the coupled pressure–temperature trajectory crosses the vapor–liquid equilibrium curve, triggering flash evaporation and causing a simultaneous sharp drop in temperature. Under high operating pressures, the trajectory remains in the liquid phase region, and both pressure and temperature exhibit damped oscillations. Under liquid phase conditions, the peak water hammer pressure increases significantly and approximately linearly with flow velocity, but decreases slightly with increasing pipe diameter. Compared with linear valve closure, both prolonging the valve closure time and adopting the rapid-then-gradual nonlinear closure strategy can effectively suppress the water hammer pressure. These findings provide practical guidance for water hammer risk assessment and mitigation in long-distance liquid ammonia pipelines.

title: Out-of-plane interference effects in angle-resolved photoemission of epitaxial graphene
summary: The epitaxial growth of monolayer graphene by Si sublimation of 6H-SiC(0001) is one of the most effective ways of producing large-scale monocrystalline graphene samples of high quality. However, graphene is left interacting with a reconstru
content: The epitaxial growth of monolayer graphene by Si sublimation of 6H-SiC(0001) is one of the most effective ways of producing large-scale monocrystalline graphene samples of high quality. However, graphene is left interacting with a reconstructed carbon buffer layer known as zerolayer graphene (ZLG) and the SiC substrate underneath. Beyond the mere creation of Dirac cone replicas, the effect of this interaction on photoemission measurements is poorly understood. We utilized synchrotron radiation for photon-energy-dependent angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) to investigate the complex final-state interactions of photoelectrons within the heterostructure of monolayer graphene, ZLG, and SiC. We identify multiple resonances in the photoemission intensity of the Dirac cone as a function of photon energy that originate from interlayer interference, confirmed with a multiple scattering model. We also demonstrate for the first time that the relative intensity of the replica bands induced by the $(6\sqrt{3} \times 6\sqrt{3})\text{R}30^\circ$ reconstruction scales with the electron kinetic energy. Finally, we resolved four nondispersing electronic states, which originate from the ZLG. Our findings show that the three-dimensional (3D) structure of SiC and ZLG manifests itself in the photoemission from two-dimensional (2D) epitaxial graphene. By revealing how 3D substrate architecture dictates the photoemission of a 2D layer, this work establishes a crucial framework for investigating the electronic structure of complex heterostructures via ARPES.

title: Pulse disturbances from hurricanes differentially structure temporal α‐ and β‐diversity in coastal benthic communities
summary: Coastal benthic community structure is shaped by a dynamic interplay between pulse disturbances, such as hurricanes, and press stressors, such as coastal land loss and climate change. We examined a five‑year time series of a benthic communi
content: Coastal benthic community structure is shaped by a dynamic interplay between pulse disturbances, such as hurricanes, and press stressors, such as coastal land loss and climate change. We examined a five‑year time series of a benthic community and environmental data from Terrebonne Bay, Louisiana, spanning five major hurricanes. Repeated, high‑intensity hurricanes produced abrupt, short‑term declines in macrofaunal α‑diversity (species richness and Hill numbers), particularly within the first one to three months post‑disturbance. In contrast, temporal β‑diversity exhibited more gradual and context‑dependent responses, with pulses of turnover driven by species losses 1–3 months post‑storm and by gains in subsequent months. After accounting for environmental covariates, hurricane effects on β‑diversity diminished, whereas α‑diversity remained strongly depressed, indicating that compositional shifts are more strongly modulated by ambient environmental conditions (temperature, salinity, dissolved oxygen, chlorophyll) than by hurricane‐induced environmental changes. Differences in storm intensity, duration, and directness of impact further shaped these responses. Our results highlight that disturbance effects on α‑ and β‑diversity are decoupled in time and mechanism: pulse events rapidly reset richness while longer‑term press drivers and disturbance recovery govern community reorganization. Integrating pulse and press perspectives improves predictions of resilience, recovery, and long‑term stability in coastal ecosystems facing increasing extreme weather under climate change.

title: Greening on Hold: Environmental Political Risk and the Reallocation of Corporate Investment
summary: Boards and institutional investors increasingly monitor firms’ climate commitments through engagement, stewardship, and executive pay tied to environmental targets. We study how environmental political risk (E-PRisk) shapes the green invest
content: Boards and institutional investors increasingly monitor firms’ climate commitments through engagement, stewardship, and executive pay tied to environmental targets. We study how environmental political risk (E-PRisk) shapes the green investment decisions that these monitors evaluate. Combining conference-call-based firm-level E-PRisk with global green and non-green investment data, we find that higher E-PRisk predicts subsequently lower green and higher non-green investment. Both reverse as E-PRisk resolves. When close elections occur in the intervening year, E-PRisk persists longer and green reversals weaken. The effects concentrate in capital expenditures, and among financially constrained firms or those with less redeployable assets. Together, the findings are consistent with a real option mechanism in which firms postpone irreversible green projects and redirect capacity toward other projects, making investment composition a key adjustment margin. For corporate governance, the results suggest that a temporary drop in green investment under policy uncertainty need not signal weak commitment, which matters for how boards and investors judge climate commitments. Oversight, stewardship, and climate-linked pay that evaluate green investment year by year may therefore penalize delays that reflect policy risk rather than weak commitment. More broadly, the results show how the political environment shapes the capital-allocation decisions that corporate governance is meant to monitor.

title: Systematizing ESG Knowledge: A Bibliometric and Theoretical Review Using SPAR ‐4‐ SLR and TCCM Framework
summary: ABSTRACT Despite the rapid growth of ESG research, the field remains fragmented across theoretical, methodological and contextual dimensions, limiting the development of a coherent body of knowledge and actionable guidance for stakeholders.
content: ABSTRACT Despite the rapid growth of ESG research, the field remains fragmented across theoretical, methodological and contextual dimensions, limiting the development of a coherent body of knowledge and actionable guidance for stakeholders. This study addresses this gap by synthesizing 1034 peer‐reviewed articles from 255 journals published between 2010 and 2025 using SPAR‐4‐SLR, bibliometric analysis and the TCCM framework. The analysis identifies five thematic clusters: ESG and firm value, digital transformation, corporate financial performance, sustainability reporting and macroeconomic resilience. It also reveals four major gaps: the lack of unified theory, geographic concentration in China and developed markets, limited attention to mediators and moderators and unresolved endogeneity and measurement issues. Overall, the findings show that ESG has evolved from a normative sustainability concept into a governance and risk management framework. The study proposes a targeted agenda for future research.

title: Quantum Embedding from Molecular to Crystalline Environments at the Cost of a Gas-Phase Calculation
summary: We present a direct-space formulation and implementation of quantum density functional theory (DFT) embedding for molecular active subsystems embedded in frozen environments (hosts) of arbitrary dimensionality, from finite molecular hosts t
content: We present a direct-space formulation and implementation of quantum density functional theory (DFT) embedding for molecular active subsystems embedded in frozen environments (hosts) of arbitrary dimensionality, from finite molecular hosts to extended systems. The host is computed once without the embedded molecule (the guest) and is represented only by its electron density fitted in an atom-centered auxiliary Gaussian basis together with its nuclear charges with the periodic electrostatics separated into an explicit near-field and a continuous fast-multipole far-field operator. The method allows the removal of host atoms from this representation to create vacancies or other voids without requiring a supercell creation. Analytic nuclear gradients are also implemented, enabling structural relaxation of the active subsystem. We demonstrate the versatility of the approach through applications to adsorbates on periodic surfaces and molecules embedded in bulk solvent environments. For CO on MgO(001), we show that DFT-in-DFT converges rapidly and reproduces the periodic interaction energy within 0.44 kJ/mol while reducing the cost by a factor of 27. Real-time time-dependent embedded DFT (RT-TDDFET) of methylenecyclopropene in periodic water is showcased to produce a ~0.6 eV solvatochromic blue shift, while strong-field propagation of CO2 on hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) yields substrate-induced effects at the cost of a gas-phase propagation. Coupling the embedding scheme to excited-state correlated wave function theory methods such as CC2 yields a solvent shift within 0.01 eV of supermolecular CC2 references, while reducing the computational cost by over 500 times.

title: Bridging ESG and Financial Performance: A Balanced Scorecard and AHP Approach to Strategic Assessment
summary: ABSTRACT Aligning environmental, social, and governance (ESG) objectives with financial performance remains a critical challenge for organizations committed to responsible and transparent operations. This study presents a structured approac
content: ABSTRACT Aligning environmental, social, and governance (ESG) objectives with financial performance remains a critical challenge for organizations committed to responsible and transparent operations. This study presents a structured approach to integrating ESG and financial key performance indicators (KPIs) using the balanced scorecard (BSC) and the analytic hierarchy process (AHP). The BSC provides a comprehensive framework, anchored in stakeholder, resource‐based, legitimacy, agency and triple‐bottom‐line perspectives, that connects ESG metrics with financial outcomes across four strategic perspectives: financial, customer, internal business processes (IBP), and learning & growth (L&G). The AHP complements this by enabling the prioritization and weighting of KPIs through expert input and stakeholder preferences, offering a transparent and data‐driven method for decision‐making. Together, these tools support a clear strategic alignment between sustainability goals and business performance, identifying key areas where ESG efforts deliver measurable value. This integrated approach contributes to the field of sustainability assessment and policy modelling by offering a replicable, stakeholder‐focused framework for performance management. It enables organizations to make informed decisions that advance ESG commitments while maintaining financial accountability.

title: Sulfonamide/Carboxylate Functionalized Acridinedione Derivatives: Design, Synthesis, and Carbonic Anhydrase Inhibition Profile
summary: A new series of sulfonamide‐ and carboxylate‐functionalized acridinedione derivatives 5a–n was designed through a pharmacophore‐retention and simplification strategy that preserved the acridine core and zinc‐binding motifs while systematica
content: A new series of sulfonamide‐ and carboxylate‐functionalized acridinedione derivatives 5a–n was designed through a pharmacophore‐retention and simplification strategy that preserved the acridine core and zinc‐binding motifs while systematically varying electronic and steric features on the aromatic rings. Targets 5a–n were synthesized from dimedone‐based enaminones and aromatic aldehydes under acidic cyclization conditions and characterized by NMR, High‐resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS), and elemental analysis. In vitro, all analogs inhibited cytosolic hCA I and II and membrane‐bound hCA IX and XII with potencies spanning low micromolar to low nanomolar K I values, with sulfonamide derivatives consistently outperforming their carboxylate counterparts. Among the series, compounds 5j and 5n showed sub‐10 nM inhibition of hCA II ( K I s 6.3 and 7.8 nM), while 5i , 5h , 5k , and 5n exhibited high nanomolar activity against hCA IX and XII. Structure‐based docking and GNINA CNN scoring confirmed that sulfonamide analogs adopt canonical Zn 2+ —coordinating poses with extensive hydrogen bonding to Thr199/Thr204 and hydrophobic engagement of the deep lipophilic pocket, correlating with the superior experimental inhibition. A 100 ns molecular dynamics study of lead compound 5k across hCA I, II, IX, and XII demonstrated stable metal‐proximal binding, with particularly low ligand RMSD and persistent gatekeeper hydrogen bonding in hCA XII, supporting its promising inhibitory profile.

title: Informality and the Business Environment as Drivers of Carbon Emissions: The Moderating Role of Environmental Regulatory Quality
summary: ABSTRACT A low‐carbon transition cannot succeed while a substantial share of business activity remains beyond the effective reach of regulation. This study examines how informality and the business environment shape carbon emissions and whe
content: ABSTRACT A low‐carbon transition cannot succeed while a substantial share of business activity remains beyond the effective reach of regulation. This study examines how informality and the business environment shape carbon emissions and whether regulatory quality conditions the environmental consequences of informal production. The analysis uses an annual panel of 145 economies over 2005–2020, combining data from the World Development Indicators and World Bank. Informality is measured using dynamic general equilibrium and Multiple Indicators Multiple Causes estimates, while nine disaggregated business‐environment dimensions capture firm entry, infrastructure, finance, taxation, trade and commercial institutions. Standard negative binomial regression constitutes the principal estimator, with Poisson regression, alternative informality measurement and income‐group estimations used for robustness. The results show that informality is consistently associated with lower aggregate CO 2 emissions, with the relationship strongest in low‐income economies and weakest in high‐income countries. This apparent environmental advantage reflects the small‐scale, labour‐intensive and capital‐constrained nature of informal production rather than inherently cleaner business practices. Most business‐environment indicators are associated with higher emissions, particularly in lower‐ to middle‐income economies, suggesting that enterprise expansion and energy demand may outpace the diffusion of cleaner technologies. Environmental regulatory quality moderates the negative informality–emissions relationship. The findings show that neither informality, formalisation nor business‐environment reform is intrinsically green. Governments should therefore align formalisation and business reforms with proportionate environmental regulation, green finance, cleaner energy and supply‐chain accountability to reconcile enterprise development with climate objectives.

title: Biostimulation Sustains a Carbonic Anhydrase‐Producing Bacterial Consortium for CO 2 Hydration and Residual Oil Utilization Under Simulated Reservoir Conditions
summary: ABSTRACT Depleted oil reservoirs are potential targets for geological CO 2 storage; however, temperature, salinity, pressure, and nutrient scarcity can suppress microbial activity. In this study, a consortium comprising the carbonic‐anhydra
content: ABSTRACT Depleted oil reservoirs are potential targets for geological CO 2 storage; however, temperature, salinity, pressure, and nutrient scarcity can suppress microbial activity. In this study, a consortium comprising the carbonic‐anhydrase‐producing bacterium Bacillus licheniformis S5 and the petroleum‐degrading bacterium Bacillus cereus S0 was evaluated in a stirred high‐pressure liquid system containing simulated brine and residual crude oil. Nitrogen and phosphorus biostimulation promoted culturable growth. At 50°C and 10 MPa, the S5 + S0 consortium maintained higher colony‐forming unit (CFU) counts and more persistent apparent carbonic‐anhydrase‐associated esterase activity than either monoculture. S0‐mediated crude‐oil degradation produced fatty‐acid intermediates and surface‐active metabolites, reducing surface tension to 62.14 mN/m and increasing aqueous CO 2 mass transfer. Meanwhile, S5‐associated carbonic anhydrase activity promoted CO 2 hydration, and the consortium maintained HCO 3 − concentrations above 900 mg/L. Collectively, these findings support a bench‐scale mechanistic framework in which residual‐oil utilization, interfacial modification, and enzymatically mediated CO 2 hydration are functionally coupled under simulated reservoir‐fluid conditions. This framework provides a foundation for subsequent evaluation in oil‐bearing rock microcosms and core‐flood systems.

title: Cloud‐Mediated Dust Effects Dominate Photovoltaic Performance Losses in Southern Europe
summary: Abstract Saharan dust outbreaks are a major source of atmospheric variability over Southern Europe and are known to reduce photovoltaic (PV) power generation through aerosol‐induced attenuation of solar radiation. However, the relative impo
content: Abstract Saharan dust outbreaks are a major source of atmospheric variability over Southern Europe and are known to reduce photovoltaic (PV) power generation through aerosol‐induced attenuation of solar radiation. However, the relative importance of direct dust radiative effects and indirect aerosol–cloud interactions remains poorly constrained. Here, we investigate dust impacts on national‐scale PV performance in Spain, Italy, and Greece during 2020–2025 by combining hourly PV generation data, MERRA‐2 dust reanalysis, CAMS irradiance products, and MODIS cirrus cloud observations. A quadratic bootstrap mediation framework was applied to separate direct dust effects from indirect cirrus‐mediated pathways. PV performance ratios (PR) decrease systematically with increasing dust loading, with the strongest reductions occurring when elevated dust concentrations coincide with enhanced cirrus cloudiness. Under combined dust–cirrus conditions, annual mean PR values decline to approximately 0.63 in Spain, 0.53 in Italy, and 0.49 in Greece, accompanied by strong suppression of direct irradiance and increased diffuse radiation fractions. Satellite observations reveal increasing cirrus reflectance and decreasing effective ice particle radius with increasing dust loading, consistent with dust‐enhanced heterogeneous ice nucleation and cirrus cloud modification. Mediation analysis demonstrates that the indirect cirrus‐mediated effect is statistically significant and dominates PV generation losses in all three countries, whereas direct dust effects are weak, and partially compensating due to enhanced diffuse radiation. These results indicate that cloud‐mediated aerosol effects, rather than direct dust extinction alone, represent the dominant mechanism controlling PV performance losses across Southern Europe, with important implications for solar‐energy forecasting and renewable‐dominated power systems.

title: Dual‐Anion Mutual‐Facilitation Effect Directs Surface Reconstruction for Reversible Anion Redox in Cobalt‐Free Li‐Rich Mn‐Based Cathodes
summary: ABSTRACT Li‐rich Mn‐based layered oxides (LLOs) offer high energy density through coupled cationic and anionic redox, but suffer from irreversible oxygen loss, voltage decay, and surface reconstruction. Here, we develop a mutual‐assisted F/
content: ABSTRACT Li‐rich Mn‐based layered oxides (LLOs) offer high energy density through coupled cationic and anionic redox, but suffer from irreversible oxygen loss, voltage decay, and surface reconstruction. Here, we develop a mutual‐assisted F/S dual‐anion doping strategy to regulate anion incorporation and near‐surface evolution. Density functional theory calculations show that F alleviates S‐induced lattice strain, stabilizes the local charge environment, and lowers the barrier for S penetration. The resulting cathode features a depth‐dependent architecture with lattice‐incorporated F/S species, regulated oxygen vacancies, a spinel‐like reconstructed region and a sulfate/sulfite‐derived interphase, while retaining the layered bulk. Multiscale spectroscopy and operando analyses reveal enhanced Mn/Ni redox and reversible lattice‐oxygen activity, suppressing oxygen release, lattice breathing, electrolyte decomposition, and phase propagation. The optimized cathode retains 84.4% capacity after 200 cycles at 1 C with a voltage‐decay rate of 1.093 mV per cycle, and 88.63% after 1000 cycles at 5 C. Post‐cycling analyses and multiphysics simulations further link this durability to reduced transition‐metal dissolution, homogenized Li + transport, and mitigated stress localization. This work demonstrates dual‐anion doping as an effective route to coordinate defect chemistry, redox activity and interfacial reconstruction in high‐capacity cathodes.

title: Ru‐Doped ZrO 2 as Efficient Electrocatalyst for Hydrogen Evolution Reaction in Acid Electrolyte
summary: The development of efficient and durable electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in acidic media is crucial for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE). While zirconium oxide (ZrO 2 ) is chemically stable in s
content: The development of efficient and durable electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in acidic media is crucial for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE). While zirconium oxide (ZrO 2 ) is chemically stable in sulfuric acid, its poor intrinsic conductivity and sluggish reaction kinetics limit its practical application. Herein, we report a series of ruthenium‐doped zirconium oxide (ZrO 2 /Ru‐x) catalysts synthesized via a facile one‐step hydrothermal method and systematically investigate the effect of ruthenium (Ru) doping content on their HER performance in 0.5 M H 2 SO 4 . The characterization results confirm that Ru atoms are successfully incorporated into the ZrO 2 lattice. Electrochemical measurements reveal that the HER activity exhibits an inverted volcano‐shaped dependence on Ru doping level, while the electrochemical capacitance surface area (ECSA) values display a volcano‐shaped dependence on Ru doping level. Among the prepared catalysts, the optimal ZrO 2 /Ru‐0.75 composition demonstrates the most outstanding performance, with a low overpotential of only 302 mV to achieve 10 mA cm −2 and a small Tafel slope of 119 mV dec −1 , significantly outperforming pristine ZrO 2 and other doped counterparts. This enhanced activity is attributed to the synergistic effect of optimized Ru‐O‐Zr coordination, which promotes water dissociation and facilitates favorable hydrogen adsorption/desorption energetics, as further supported by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). Moreover, the optimized catalyst exhibits excellent long‐term stability over 24 h of continuous electrolysis, underscoring its potential as a cost‐effective alternative to noble‐metal–based HER catalysts. This work provides a comprehensive understanding of the structure‐activity relationship in Ru‐doped ZrO 2 systems and offers a viable strategy for designing high‐performance acidic HER electrocatalysts.

title: Polymorphic In Vitro Assembly of a Bacterial Microcompartment Shell Protein
summary: Bacterial microcompartments (BMCs) are self-assembling protein nanocages involved in metabolic compartmentalization in bacteria. They consist of hexagonal and pentagonal protein subunits that tile the facets of polyhedral shells. BMCs can a
content: Bacterial microcompartments (BMCs) are self-assembling protein nanocages involved in metabolic compartmentalization in bacteria. They consist of hexagonal and pentagonal protein subunits that tile the facets of polyhedral shells. BMCs can assemble a variety of morphologies, making them attractive platforms for engineering synthetic biomaterials and organizing catalysis. Here, a single 99-amino-acid hexameric shell protein from the BMC of Haliangium ochraceum is shown to self-assemble in vitro into a range of nanoscale and mesoscale architectures, including flat lattice sheets, nanorolls, single-walled nanotubes, and nanospheres. The assembly morphology can be controlled by modulating the ionic strength of the assembly buffer, which influences the anisotropic interactions between subunits. These structures represent model platforms for engineered synthetic nanoreactors and provide a framework for exploring the emergent physical, mechanical, and chemical properties of protein-based crystalline materials.

title: Enhancing CO 2 separation stability of ceramic–carbonate hollow fiber membranes via coregulation of the support and salt
summary: Abstract Ceramic–carbonate dual‐phase (CCDP) hollow fiber membranes show high potential for high‐temperature CO 2 separation due to high packing density and thin walls. However, a permeability–stability trade‐off exists: pore optimization b
content: Abstract Ceramic–carbonate dual‐phase (CCDP) hollow fiber membranes show high potential for high‐temperature CO 2 separation due to high packing density and thin walls. However, a permeability–stability trade‐off exists: pore optimization boosts CO 2 flux but accelerates carbonate loss. Here, a synergistic strategy combining ceramic support optimization and molten salt modification is proposed. Porous GDC (Ce 0.8 Gd 0.2 O 2‐δ ) supports were used, and the effect of 5 wt% nano‐TiO 2 in carbonate was studied. GDC1450 support achieved optimal porosity and strength. The membrane attained a CO 2 permeation flux of 5.32 mL·min −1 ·cm −2 at 900°C, outperforming most reported CCDP membranes. However, during a 100 h test at 700°C, its flux dropped 76% due to carbonate loss. In contrast, the nano‐TiO 2 ‐modified membrane showed flux reduction <10%. Nano‐TiO 2 enhanced carbonate retention, suppressed leakage, and improved durability. Overall, this synergistic strategy offers a viable route to overcome the trade‐off and develop CCDP membranes with both high flux and long‐term stability.

title: Spin‐Polarized Metallic Metal−Organic Framework With High Conductivity and Half‐Metallic Behavior
summary: ABSTRACT The establishment of new concepts for next‐generation conductive materials remains both highly desirable and scientifically challenging. Herein, we report a Cu‐based metal–organic framework (MOF), ([Cu(6Hmna)] n ( 1 , 6Hmna = 6‐mer
content: ABSTRACT The establishment of new concepts for next‐generation conductive materials remains both highly desirable and scientifically challenging. Herein, we report a Cu‐based metal–organic framework (MOF), ([Cu(6Hmna)] n ( 1 , 6Hmna = 6‐mercaptonicotinic acid)), featuring metal–sulfur chains that exhibit intrinsic metallic behavior. Compound 1 exhibits a high electrical conductivity of up to 120 S cm−1, indicating a high electrical conductivity for a MOF in its crystalline form. The metallic transport characteristics are confirmed by temperature‐dependent conductivity measurements. In addition, this Cu‐MOF demonstrates highly efficient photoconductivity, with an outstanding photocurrent responsivity reaching 8100 A W −1 under infrared light illumination. Our theoretical DFT calculations predict that compound 1 exhibits an exotic spin‐polarized electronic structure, in which one spin channel is metallic while the other remains semiconducting. This unique electronic configuration is particularly attractive for applications in spintronics and quantum technologies, as well as in optoelectronic and photoelectrochemical devices.

title: VicHealth 2025-26 Annual Report
summary: 2025-26 Annual Report of Operations and Financial Statements for the Victorian Health Promotion Foundation (VicHealth).
content: 2025-26 Annual Report of Operations and Financial Statements for the Victorian Health Promotion Foundation (VicHealth).

title: Tuning correlated states in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene with magnetic encapsulation
summary: Rhombohedral graphene multilayers provide a flexible platform for correlated physics associated with their flat-band electronic structure. While a variety of correlated states appear in these systems as a function of bias and electrostatic
content: Rhombohedral graphene multilayers provide a flexible platform for correlated physics associated with their flat-band electronic structure. While a variety of correlated states appear in these systems as a function of bias and electrostatic doping, promoting specific correlated flavor symmetry breaking states remains a challenge. Here we show that magnetic encapsulation by CrGeTe3 achieves this in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene, by using switchable exchange couplings induced by ferromagnetic substrates. We show that correlations in rhombohedral multilayers at charge neutrality strongly renormalize the exchange proximity splitting,giving rise to collective spin modes whose character is switched by the parallel or antiparallel alignment of the encapsulation. We further show that upon doping of the flat bands, spin triplet f-wave superconducting solutions emerge, whose layer and spin selectivity is controlled by the magnetic encapsulation, hosting in-gap excitations at the edges. Our results establish magnetic alignment as a means to control spin symmetry breaking and unconventional superconductivity in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene.

title: What Should We Tax When We Tax AI?
summary: Production efficiency says intermediate inputs should go untaxed, and the debate proposes taxing AI anyway: per token, per displaced worker, on profits or on electricity. We price all four arguments in one model in which AI is a marked-up i
content: Production efficiency says intermediate inputs should go untaxed, and the debate proposes taxing AI anyway: per token, per displaced worker, on profits or on electricity. We price all four arguments in one model in which AI is a marked-up intermediate input, workers sort across tasks, and providers may enter. Under the demand system the model generates, the efficient wedge on AI usage is a subsidy, about −15 percent with entry blocked and −10 percent under free entry, for the reason Judd (1997) gave for capital goods: buyers pay a markup, so the input is underused. Two measurements discipline the result. Sorting turns the robot-tax literature’s identifying assumption into an exposure gap, which never exceeds 0.45 across seven exposure measures and is negative on every direct AI measure; and the markup is bounded by the Lerner condition and weighted consistently with the weight on routine workers. Because competition policy reaches underprovision better than a subsidy, what survives for tax policy is a corrective wedge of about six percent. It belongs on the electricity meter, where socialized grid costs fall on low-income households and on ratepayers far from the sites that gain.

title: Sociocultural barriers and enablers to paludiculture adoption
source: Epsilon Archive for Student Projects (University of Southampton)
summary: In Germany, 71% of drained peatlands are used for agriculture, primarily grassland, a land-use change that has turned these ecosystems from carbon sinks into major carbon sources. Paludiculture, the productive use of wet and rewetted peatla
content: In Germany, 71% of drained peatlands are used for agriculture, primarily grassland, a land-use change that has turned these ecosystems from carbon sinks into major carbon sources. Paludiculture, the productive use of wet and rewetted peatlands, offers a potential to substantially reduce these emissions while maintaining an economically viable alternative for farmers. Yet how farmers themselves perceive this transition has rarely been studied, and adoption of paludiculture among farmers remains low. This thesis explores sociocultural values and meanings farmers attach to the peat landscapes and how these shape barriers and enablers to rewetting for paludiculture. Drawing on the Nature's Contributions to People (NCP) framework, semi-structured interviews were conducted with farmers in the Gnarrenburger Moor, Germany. Findings show that cultural perceptions of 'valuable' land, still favouring the dry, actively managed grassland, together with place attachment and aesthetic ties to this landscape act as barriers. While older farmers remain more sceptical, shaped by the historical hardship of drainage, younger farmers show greater willingness to change if their livelihood is secured, policies provide planning certainty, and their voices are heard in the process. Continuous land management emerged as a key source of meaning for what is perceived as landscape care – one that paludiculture could build on, offering an entry point for its adoption and acting as a possible future for farming in the Gnarrenburger Moor. Scaling paludiculture, therefore, requires turning its economic potential into functioning value chains, alongside policies that offer a clear and locally adapted pathway. Ultimately, this transition will only succeed if it takes farmers’ sociocultural values, meanings, and everyday realities into account.

title: Tail-Risk-Aware Decentralized Supplier Policies for Low-Carbon Procurement Under Correlated Disruptions
source: International Journal of World Economic Research
summary: Green public procurement must balance purchase cost, carbon intensity and service continuity under supplier disruptions whose emissions outcomes are uncertain. Building on the multi-agent sourcing formulation of GRACE, we develop a decentra
content: Green public procurement must balance purchase cost, carbon intensity and service continuity under supplier disruptions whose emissions outcomes are uncertain. Building on the multi-agent sourcing formulation of GRACE, we develop a decentralized, shared-parameter supplier policy coordinated by a transparent public rationing rule and trained with a CVaR-regularized policy gradient (CVaR-PG) that penalizes the worst 20% of episode losses under noisy carbon proxies and cluster-correlated failures. Over 720 evaluation episodes per regime from four training seeds, CVaR-PG lowers pooled upper-tail loss relative to mean-only learning by 3.1% under high-severity shocks (1.258 versus 1.299) and by 1.9% under a held-out failure family (1.299 versus 1.325), with seed-level paired intervals reported for each contrast. Comparisons with reserve-aware and emissions-first rules show that transparent rules with access to supplier reserve information remain strong benchmarks for tail risk and carbon, identifying the coordination interface as the main lever for further gains. The study provides a reproducible benchmark for risk-aware multi-agent procurement under emissions uncertainty.

title: Greening Economic Growth: The Role of Renewable Energy and Agricultural Land Use in Carbon Emission Mitigation
source: Journal of Environmental Science and Economics
summary: Climate change and rising carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions pose significant challenges to environmental sustainability, particularly in developing and emerging economies experiencing rapid economic growth and increasing energy demand. Against
content: Climate change and rising carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions pose significant challenges to environmental sustainability, particularly in developing and emerging economies experiencing rapid economic growth and increasing energy demand. Against this backdrop, this study investigates the relationships between economic growth, renewable energy consumption, agricultural land use, and CO₂ emissions across 34 Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) countries over the period 1988–2020. Using panel data obtained from the World Development Indicators (WDI), the study employs pooled ordinary least squares (OLS), fixed effects (FE), two-step difference generalized method of moments (GMM), and two-step system GMM estimators. These approaches provide baseline estimates, account for unobserved country-specific heterogeneity, and address potential endogeneity and the dynamic persistence of carbon emissions. The empirical findings from the dynamic panel estimators reveal that economic growth is positively associated with CO₂ emissions, whereas renewable energy consumption and agricultural land use exhibit significant negative associations. Furthermore, the results do not support the conventional inverted U-shaped environmental Kuznets curve (EKC) hypothesis, suggesting that economic development alone does not necessarily lead to reduced carbon emissions in the sampled countries. These findings highlight the importance of integrating environmental sustainability into economic development strategies. The study emphasizes the need to accelerate renewable energy adoption, promote sustainable agricultural land management, improve energy efficiency, and encourage investment in low-carbon technologies. These policy measures could contribute to reducing carbon emissions while fostering environmentally sustainable economic growth across BRI countries.

title: Do Investors Sanction Greenwashing? Selective Market Discipline in Fintech Firms
summary: ABSTRACT We investigate whether stock market investors detect and penalise greenwashing. We draw on media reports of environmental, social and governance incidents at 321 US‐listed fintech firms between 2007 and 2025, within which greenwash
content: ABSTRACT We investigate whether stock market investors detect and penalise greenwashing. We draw on media reports of environmental, social and governance incidents at 321 US‐listed fintech firms between 2007 and 2025, within which greenwashing is identified, following RepRisk, as misleading communication about environmental practice. Investors impose no measurable price penalty when firms are publicly implicated in greenwashing, and the sample is large enough to have detected a penalty of the size observed for other conduct. Misleading communication that does not concern the environment is penalised, where cumulative abnormal returns are between 0.4% and 0.6% lower over the 2 weeks following the report, falling further to 0.8% over the 4 weeks before and after, whereas physical environmental damage draws no adverse reaction. The market therefore prices dishonesty, but the sanction depends on the domain of the false claim, and environmental claims by fintech firms fall outside it. Consistent with stakeholder theory, the results suggest that market‐based discipline exists but is selective, so that the truthfulness of environmental claims cannot be presumed to be enforced by investors where regulatory oversight is absent.

title: The Structure and Evolution of China’s Green Finance Policy Instruments
summary: China’s green finance policy system consists of many separate measures, and most studies examine them one at a time. This paper describes the system as a whole. It asks which instruments the system contains and how their relative weight cha
content: China’s green finance policy system consists of many separate measures, and most studies examine them one at a time. This paper describes the system as a whole. It asks which instruments the system contains and how their relative weight changed between the 2016 Guiding Opinions on Building a Green Financial System and 2025. The instruments are grouped into five categories: green credit, green bonds, green insurance, green funds and carbon finance. The description rests on three public sources: green loan statistics from the People’s Bank of China, green bond issuance data from the Climate Bonds Initiative, and the text of the policy documents. Green loans grew faster than total loans over the period, and their share of total loans rose from 6.7% at end-2020 to 16.2% at end-2025. Green bond issuance peaked in 2022 within the period covered and was about 18% lower in 2024 than in 2023. Both patterns need to be read with care, because the green loan statistics were redefined in 2025 and the bond figures come from report editions with different database cut-off dates. Read together with the policy documents, the evidence suggests that direct financial support has been joined by project standards, institutional assessment and risk management requirements. Government direction, market development and risk control are used here as three organising ideas for interpreting that combination. The paper describes how the system is built and how it has changed; it does not estimate the effect of any single policy.

title: Analysis of Natural Regeneration and Vegetation Status of Tree Species of a Biodiversity Hotspot in Bangladesh
source: SUST Journal of Science and Technology (SUST JST)
summary: Natural regeneration is crucial for ecosystem restoration and sustainable forest growth. This study provides first comprehensive assessment of naturally regenerating tree species in the Rema-Kalenga Wildlife Sanctuary (RKWS), Bangladesh. Da
content: Natural regeneration is crucial for ecosystem restoration and sustainable forest growth. This study provides first comprehensive assessment of naturally regenerating tree species in the Rema-Kalenga Wildlife Sanctuary (RKWS), Bangladesh. Data was collected via systematic random sampling, using 50 plots (20m × 20m), each containing five 1m × 1m subplots, and totaling 250 subplots. The study found 859 individuals representing 67 identified species across 34 families, alongside 5 unidentified species. Among them, 774 individuals (63 species) were native, 24 individuals (4 species) were exotic, and 61 individuals remained 5 unidentified species. Moraceae was the most prevalent family (Family Importance Value = 23.11%) with Streblus asper emerging as the most prevalent dominant species (Important Value Index =19.71). Biodiversity indices revealed structural differences between native and exotic regeneration. Native species demonstrated high diversity, richness and evenness (Shannon-Wiener = 3.4540, Richness = 9.3211, Evenness = 0.8337), indicating a mature, stable ecosystem with high functional resilience and even distribution. Conversely, exotic species exhibit low richness and evenness but a paradoxically higher species diversity index (exotic 0.1667 vs. native 0.0814). This disparity reflects the extreme dominance of a few aggressive individuals, signaling an early-stage invasion risk capable of gradually displacing native flora despite the current limited abundance of exotic species. These findings offer crucial baseline insights into the sanctuary’s current vegetation status. Ultimately, this study provides a vital scientific foundation for selecting appropriate tree species for future afforestation initiatives and sustainable conservation management strategies within the RKWS.

title: Fatty Acid Composition of Promising Microalgae for Biofuel Production: A Literature Review
summary: Microalgae are promising third-generation feedstocks for renewable liquid biofuels because of their rapid growth, high areal productivity, ability to grow on non-arable land and saline or wastewater, and capacity to accumulate storage lipid
content: Microalgae are promising third-generation feedstocks for renewable liquid biofuels because of their rapid growth, high areal productivity, ability to grow on non-arable land and saline or wastewater, and capacity to accumulate storage lipids rich in fatty acids suitable for conversion into biodiesel. This review synthesizes peer-reviewed literature (2021–2026) on the fatty acid composition of Chlorella vulgaris, Nannochloropsis spp., Scenedesmus spp., Botryococcus braunii, Phaeodactylum tricornutum and Haematococcus pluvialis. It examines fatty acid and triacylglycerol biosynthesis, cultivation effects on saturated (SFA), monounsaturated (MUFA) and polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFA), and the relationship between fatty acid profiles and estimated biodiesel properties. The review also evaluates CRISPR/Cas-based engineering and machine-learning-assisted optimization, while emphasizing that reported genetic effects remain strain- and pathway-dependent. Microalgal biofuels may offer lower life-cycle greenhouse-gas emissions than fossil fuels in suitable systems, but they should not be described as inherently carbon-neutral: net emissions depend on cultivation energy, nutrient inputs, harvesting, extraction, conversion, and the source and fate of carbon. Nitrogen stress can increase lipid percentage while reducing biomass growth and overall lipid productivity. No single wild-type strain combines maximum productivity with a profile that satisfies all fuel-quality requirements; therefore, strain selection, process optimization and carefully validated engineering must be assessed together.

title: Each Atom and Electron Matters: A Continuous Gold Nanocluster Series
summary: ABSTRACT Achieving continuous atom‐by‐atom structural evolution and elucidating the associated quantum size effects in metal nanoclusters remain highly challenging, primarily due to the intrinsic thermodynamic preference for discrete magic‐
content: ABSTRACT Achieving continuous atom‐by‐atom structural evolution and elucidating the associated quantum size effects in metal nanoclusters remain highly challenging, primarily due to the intrinsic thermodynamic preference for discrete magic‐number configurations. In this study, we present a synergistic ligand‐engineering strategy that combines dynamic ligand coordination with fluorine chemistry to break this preference. The use of weakly coordinating phosphine ligands facilitates adaptive ligand rearrangement during progressive core expansion, while fluorine‐induced noncovalent interactions establish a robust molecular and supramolecular spatial lock, thereby stabilizing cluster molecules and enhancing crystallization. Through this approach, we successfully isolated and structurally characterized an unprecedented continuous series of gold nanoclusters: Au 41 –Au 44 . Comprehensive experimental and computational structural and photophysical analyses reveal non‐monotonic geometric evolution and atom‐specific modulation of electronic structure, thereby providing direct evidence for the principle that “each atom and electron matters” in dictating cluster geometry and electronic structures. Collectively, this work fills the structural gap in medium‐sized, phosphine‐protected gold nanoclusters and provides a continuous cluster series that serves as an ideal model for probing quantum size effects at the atomic level.

title: Greenhushing as Strategic Adaptation: Net‐Zero Commitment Retreat Among S&P 500 Firms Amid Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Backlash
summary: ABSTRACT Greenhushing has emerged as a strategic corporate response to political and regulatory uncertainty, yet less is known about how firms recalibrate previously established sustainability signals when external conditions change. Drawin
content: ABSTRACT Greenhushing has emerged as a strategic corporate response to political and regulatory uncertainty, yet less is known about how firms recalibrate previously established sustainability signals when external conditions change. Drawing on signaling theory, this study examines changes in corporate climate and ESG commitments during the political transition to the second Trump administration. Using qualitative content analysis of corporate disclosures and public communications, we identify 32 large US firms that modified, weakened, or withdrew previously stated commitments between September 2024 and August 2025. Among these firms, 13 (41%) were associated with political or regulatory pressure, 8 (25%) linked changes to rising AI and data‐center demand, and 11 (34%) pointed to profit‐driven refocusing, market uncertainty, or broader regulatory ambiguity. The findings reveal clear sectoral differences in how firms recalibrated sustainability signals. Financial institutions exhibited the most direct and visible retrenchment, particularly through withdrawals from net‐zero alliances and changes in ESG‐related communication. Technology firms more often retained long‐term climate commitments while reducing the visibility, prominence, or certainty of interim targets. Other sectors showed less visible but still consequential forms of retreat, including target modification and the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) delisting. Case studies of BlackRock, Meta, and Microsoft further identify three distinct pathways of greenhushing: politically induced retrenchment, selective undercommunication amid rising emissions, and more cautious or conditional sustainability signaling in response to reputational and regulatory risk.

title: High‐mobility p‐type Te 0.65 Se 0.35 thin‐film transistors with self‐passivating contacts
summary: Abstract Tellurium (Te) has emerged as a significant semiconductor material due to its intriguing physicochemical properties and great potential in next‐generation electronics and optoelectronics. The Se alloying method has been proved to b
content: Abstract Tellurium (Te) has emerged as a significant semiconductor material due to its intriguing physicochemical properties and great potential in next‐generation electronics and optoelectronics. The Se alloying method has been proved to be effective in improving the static control ability of Te semiconductor film. However, the traditional metal/semiconductor contact severely limits the mobility and on‐state current density of Te 0.65 Se 0.35 films due to the existence of interfacial Schottky barrier and insufficient charge injection efficiency. Here, we propose a TeO x self‐passivating assisted metal/semiconductor contact method to reduce the contact resistance, enabling ultrahigh mobility and on‐state current in the p‐type Te 0.65 Se 0.35 thin film transistors. The TeO x passivation layer with a higher work function reduces contact resistance and weakens the Schottky barrier by passivating possible defects on the Te 0.65 Se 0.35 surface and inhibiting elements diffusion in the materials. The TeO x self‐passivating assisted Te 0.65 Se 0.35 thin film field effect transistor has a contact resistance as low as 1.2 kΩ μm and a contact interface with a near‐zero Schottky barrier. Compared with the original device, the on‐state current is increased by about 5 times to 250 μA, the hole mobility is increased by about 4 times which is up to 88.8 cm 2 V −1 s −1 , and the on–off ratio is about 2 × 10 4 . The comprehensive performance has reached the leading level and achieved the highest hole mobility among the evaporated p‐type films. This method fills the gap in the large‐scale preparation and optimization of p‐type semiconductors, providing the possibility for industrial wafer‐level preparation. image

title: Assessment of Low-Carbon Transition Levels and Obstacle Factors in Resource-Exhausted Cities Based on the DPSIR–TOPSIS Method
summary: Resource-exhausted cities are confronted with multiple challenges, including a single industrial structure, ecological degradation, and constraints imposed by carbon emissions.Scientifically assessing their level of low-carbon transition de
content: Resource-exhausted cities are confronted with multiple challenges, including a single industrial structure, ecological degradation, and constraints imposed by carbon emissions.Scientifically assessing their level of low-carbon transition development and identifying key constraining factors are of great significance for promoting high-quality development in such cities.This study focused on the first batch of resource-exhausted cities officially identified in China -Fuxin, Yichun, Liaoyuan, Baishan, Panjin, Shizuishan, Baiyin, Jiaozuo, Pingxiang, and Greater Khingan Mountains -as the research objects.An evaluation index system was constructed on the basis of the driving force-pressure-state-impact-response framework.The entropy method-analytic hierarchy process combined weighting method, together with the TOPSIS method, was also employed to measure and comparatively analyze the level of low-carbon transition development in the 10 cities. Results show that the low-carbon transition levels of the 10 cities exhibit a pronounced pattern of polarization: Jiaozuo and Panjin belong to the leading tier and have achieved remarkable transition outcomes, whereas the Greater Khingan Mountains lags far behind and is almost in a state of stagnation.In terms of indicator weights, the proportion of output value from non-resource-based industries, carbon emissions per unit of GDP, and R&D expenditure intensity are the top three key factors affecting the level of transition, indicating that industrial diversification and carbon intensity control are the core driving forces distinguishing successful transitions from unsuccessful ones.Some cities exhibit response failure and poor transmission among subsystems, and their ecological advantages have not been effectively converted into low-carbon development advantages.The conclusions provide a theoretical basis and policy reference for differentiated policymaking and the targeted promotion of low-carbon transition in resource-exhausted cities.

title: Linking Hydrodynamic Transport and Nutrient Fluxes to Land‐Use Patterns: A Predictive Framework for Soil Conservation in a Mountainous Catchment
summary: ABSTRACT This study investigates the influence of land use on total suspended solids (TSS) flux and nutrient leaching within a mixed land‐use catchment. The primary objective was to enhance predictive accuracy for soil erosion and water qua
content: ABSTRACT This study investigates the influence of land use on total suspended solids (TSS) flux and nutrient leaching within a mixed land‐use catchment. The primary objective was to enhance predictive accuracy for soil erosion and water quality by assessing hydrologic drivers critical for managing degradation risks. Our findings demonstrate a significant land‐use impact: stream reaches adjacent to arable land exhibited the highest concentrations of nitrate nitrogen (up to 6.25 mg dm −3 ) and phosphates (0.89 mg dm −3 ), whereas forests and permanent grasslands showed significantly lower levels. Arable lands also recorded the highest transport intensity (1.02 m 3 s −1 ), reflecting increased surface runoff and diminished water retention capacity compared to forested reaches (0.47 m 3 s −1 ). Furthermore, the complete transverse mixing distance, a proxy for natural purification efficiency, was longest in arable‐dominated reaches (52.26 m), contrasting with shorter distances in forests (35.26 m) and grasslands (31.21 m). Spatial autoregression (SAR) modeling identified significant correlations between phosphate levels and agricultural zones, as well as nitrate nitrogen and grasslands. These results underscore the necessity of integrating land‐use management into forest engineering and maintaining permanent riparian grasslands to optimize nutrient retention and sediment control in erosion‐prone regions.

title: Technoeconomic Feasibility and Spatial Heterogeneity of Decarbonizing Residential Cooling Across China’s Climate Zones
summary: Accelerating residential building decarbonization is pivotal for China’s carbon neutrality, yet mitigating regional inequalities necessitates localized assessments. To this end, in this study, a stock turnover model is employed to evaluate
content: Accelerating residential building decarbonization is pivotal for China’s carbon neutrality, yet mitigating regional inequalities necessitates localized assessments. To this end, in this study, a stock turnover model is employed to evaluate the spatiotemporal evolution and technoeconomic feasibility of decarbonizing space cooling equipment in China’s urban and rural residential buildings: (1) Urban and rural cooling-related carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions peak in 2022 at 87.2 and 35.9 megatons of carbon dioxide (MtCO2), respectively. (2) Rural cooling energy consumption is projected to peak at 78.0 TWh in 2026, trailing the urban sector by four years, highlighting spatiotemporal decoupling. (3) Decarbonization investments and their benefits exhibit a nonlinear relationship, demonstrating pronounced spatial polarization across climate zones, with the highest decarbonization benefit reaching 86.0 billion CNY in Guangdong Province, whereas carbon-intensive central regions face significant short-term economic deficits. (4) Upgrading urban split air conditioners (ACs) offers a highly viable transition pathway, expected to cumulatively decrease by 142.9 MtCO2 between 2025 and 2060. Overall, this framework establishes a scientific baseline for policymakers to design equitable and cost-effective mitigation strategies within the cooling sector.

title: Predicting Urban Carbon Peak Through an Extended STIRPAT Model: A Scenario Analysis of Bozhou, China
summary: Cities play an important role in achieving carbon emission peaking and neutrality targets, yet identifying feasible mitigation pathways remains challenging for prefecture-level cities with limited historical data. This study develops a cont
content: Cities play an important role in achieving carbon emission peaking and neutrality targets, yet identifying feasible mitigation pathways remains challenging for prefecture-level cities with limited historical data. This study develops a context-specific extended STIRPAT framework to examine the relationships between urban carbon emissions and nine socioeconomic and sector-related indicators in Bozhou, China. Based on annual data from 2010 to 2022, grey relational analysis was used to support indicator selection, and ridge regression was applied to address severe multicollinearity. Ten scenarios, comprising one baseline and nine alternative development pathways, were constructed to assess carbon emission trajectories during 2023–2035. Population exhibited the largest standardized ridge regression coefficient among the selected explanatory variables. Scenario analysis indicates that carbon emissions under the baseline scenario (S1) reach a projected maximum of 16.78 Mt CO2 in 2030. The energy consumption adjustment scenario (S6) and the coordinated development scenario (S8) reach their projected maxima in 2025, at 15.60 and 15.69 Mt CO2, respectively. Under the integrated scenarios S9 and S10, emissions decline continuously throughout 2023–2035 without reaching a new peak during the projection period. Compared with S1, projected emissions in 2030 are 10.65%, 9.06%, 24.74%, and 37.99% lower under S6, S8, S9, and S10, respectively. A supplementary Monte Carlo analysis further illustrates the sensitivity of these projections to uncertainty in the assumed explanatory-variable growth rates. The findings should be interpreted as conditional scenario outcomes rather than precise forecasts or causal estimates of policy effectiveness.

title: Informal Environmental Regulation and Corporate ESG Inconsistency: Evidence From China
summary: ABSTRACT This paper studies whether local informal environmental regulation can limit corporate ESG inconsistency, understood as the gap between what firms disclose about ESG and how they actually perform. Although ESG credibility has attra
content: ABSTRACT This paper studies whether local informal environmental regulation can limit corporate ESG inconsistency, understood as the gap between what firms disclose about ESG and how they actually perform. Although ESG credibility has attracted growing scholarly attention, evidence remains limited on how community‐based supervision restrains the separation between symbolic disclosure and substantive action. Using Chinese A‐share listed firms from 2010 to 2022, this study finds that stronger local informal regulation is accompanied by a narrower ESG inconsistency gap. The channel tests provide evidence consistent with public attention and pollution‐control investment as potential transmission channels, but do not provide support for the environmental textual emphasis channel. Additional analyses show that the disciplining role of informal regulation depends on the surrounding governance setting: formal enforcement, capital‐market pressure, internal governance arrangements, and negative investor sentiment may dilute the role of social supervision. These findings highlight the macro‐level value of informal environmental regulation in emerging markets. Rather than serving only as a background institutional condition, informal regulation connects public environmental concern, local state response, and corporate ESG accountability. The study contributes to sustainable development and ESG governance research by showing how non‐state pressure can help curb symbolic‐substantive decoupling and strengthen the credibility of corporate sustainability practices.

title: Learning Electronic Band Structures Across the s, p, d Blocks with an Empirical Pseudopotential Network
summary: Electronic band structures govern how crystals conduct electrons and absorb light. Density-functional theory (DFT) computes them through costly self-consistent iterations, while existing machine-learning models either predict isolated scala
content: Electronic band structures govern how crystals conduct electrons and absorb light. Density-functional theory (DFT) computes them through costly self-consistent iterations, while existing machine-learning models either predict isolated scalar properties or output Hamiltonians that still require DFT solvers. Here we present EpNet, a learned empirical pseudopotential for crystals spanning 63 elements across the \textit{s}, \textit{p} and \textit{d} blocks. An equivariant neural network builds its Hamiltonian from physics-motivated local potentials and nonlocal projectors. Trained solely on band energies, EpNet predicts complete band structures directly from atomic coordinates. On unseen chemical systems, its median errors are \winAll\ eV for band energies and \gapAll\ eV for band gaps. On 600,000 structures from an independent database, its band-gap errors are overall less than half those of existing models, at about 1\% of DFT cost. EpNet thus enables fast screening of electronic properties for materials discovery and electronic-structure simulations of large systems.

title: Direct Multispectral Satellite Nowcasting of Gridded Surface Solar Radiation
summary: Surface shortwave radiation (SWR) can change within minutes as clouds evolve, but operational forecasts often trade spatial detail and update frequency for forecast range. Here, we present a numerical-weather-prediction-independent, observa
content: Surface shortwave radiation (SWR) can change within minutes as clouds evolve, but operational forecasts often trade spatial detail and update frequency for forecast range. Here, we present a numerical-weather-prediction-independent, observation-to-forecast framework that converts sequences of Himawari-9 Level-1 multispectral imagery and solar geometry directly into 24 gridded SWR fields at 10-min intervals for the next 4 h. A controlled six-model experiment in eastern China separates the effects of satellite information from those of temporal self-attention. In the 0-1 h window, the full-multispectral attention model achieves a mean absolute error of 37.9 W/m2 and a root mean square error of 63.7 W/m2, reductions of 21.0% and 19.5% relative to a historical-SWR baseline. Improvements extend across nine subregions and include weaker spatial bias and better structural consistency. Temporal attention does not improve forecasts from historical SWR alone, but becomes effective when supplied with multispectral cloud and thermodynamic signals. Direct multispectral observations therefore provide the precursor information required for high-frequency, spatially resolved SWR nowcasting.

title: Green Credit, Financing Constraints, And Corporate Green Transformation: A Financial Resource Allocation Perspective
source: Journal of Economics Finance and Management Studies
summary: Green credit has become an important policy instrument for promoting sustainable development and integrating environmental considerations into financial resource allocation. As environmental concerns and climate-related risks increasingly i
content: Green credit has become an important policy instrument for promoting sustainable development and integrating environmental considerations into financial resource allocation. As environmental concerns and climate-related risks increasingly influence economic activities, commercial banks are expected to play a greater role in supporting environmentally sustainable projects while maintaining financial stability. Where economic development and environmental sustainability are important policy priorities, green credit provides a potential mechanism for directing financial resources toward environmentally responsible industries. Drawing on financial intermediation theory and credit risk management perspectives, this study explores the channels through which green credit may influence commercial banks' credit risk. Green credit may reduce credit risk by encouraging banks to incorporate environmental factors into borrower assessments, strengthen lending standards, and identify potential risks associated with environmental regulations and unsustainable business practices. By directing financing toward environmentally responsible enterprises, banks may reduce their exposure to borrowers vulnerable to environmental and regulatory changes, thereby improving loan portfolio quality. These factors suggest that the relationship between green credit and credit risk may depend on banks' lending capabilities, borrower characteristics, and institutional conditions. The study is expected to contribute to the literature on sustainable finance by providing insights into the role of green credit in banking risk management within an emerging-market context. Its findings may also offer practical implications for commercial banks seeking to balance environmental responsibility with prudent lending decisions, as well as for policymakers developing green finance frameworks to support sustainable economic development and financial stability in Indonesia.

title: The cellular response capacity (CRC) as a novel immunomonitoring approach in sepsis
summary: Background: Early recognition of sepsis remains difficult in clinical practice because conventional humoral biomarkers such as C-reactive protein, procalcitonin, and interleukin-6 (IL-6) exhibit unfavorable, slow-release kinetics and rise h
content: Background: Early recognition of sepsis remains difficult in clinical practice because conventional humoral biomarkers such as C-reactive protein, procalcitonin, and interleukin-6 (IL-6) exhibit unfavorable, slow-release kinetics and rise hours after the onset of infection. Flow cytometry enables upstream, cell-based immunomonitoring, but its clinical use is restricted by poor standardization of fluorescence measurements. In this study, the neutrophil cellular response capacity (CRC) was developed and evaluated as a standardized approach for rapid assessment of systemic inflammation in bacteremia and sepsis. Methods: and compared with humoral inflammatory markers. Next, the CRC was assessed in a prospective intensive care unit sepsis cohort. Moreover, preliminary validation was performed in an independent sepsis cohort and in patients undergoing cardiac surgery. Results: In the bacteremia model, the CRC of neutrophil markers CD10, CD11b, and CD66b increased in a dose-dependent manner with increasing bacterial burden and detected inflammation at lower pathogen burdens than IL-6 and other humoral mediators, with a superior area under the receiver operating characteristic curve. In clinical sepsis, the CRC discriminated patients from age- and sex-matched healthy volunteers, with the CRC of CD11b showing the highest diagnostic performance. CRC values increased over time in patients with sepsis, consistent with immunological recovery. The maximal stimulation reference point for CD11b remained stable across inflammatory states, cohorts, and instruments. In addition, the CRC more precisely captured the onset and resolution of surgery-induced inflammation than conventional biomarkers. Conclusions: The CRC provides a rapid, standardized, and robust cell-based immunomonitoring tool that outperforms traditional humoral markers in experimental bacteremia and reliably identifies sepsis in clinical cohorts, strongly supporting its use as a novel biomarker for earlier, more precise sepsis diagnosis and monitoring.

title: Flexible Neural Interfaces based on Graphene–PAN Composite for the Treatment of Constipation via Sacral Nerve Stimulation
source: Journal of Biomedical Physics and Engineering
summary: Background: Conventional Sacral Nerve Stimulation (SNS) devices are widely used to treat constipation but are often limited by their lack of mechanical flexibility, which can reduce long-term therapeutic efficacy. Developing advanced electr
content: Background: Conventional Sacral Nerve Stimulation (SNS) devices are widely used to treat constipation but are often limited by their lack of mechanical flexibility, which can reduce long-term therapeutic efficacy. Developing advanced electrode materials may improve stimulation performance and patient outcomes. Objective: This experimental study aimed to introduce a proof-of-concept flexible cuff electrode composed of a graphene–polyacrylonitrile (PAN) composite and evaluate its electrochemical properties, their mechanical characteristics, and short-term functional performance in a rabbit SNS model. Material and Methods: In this experimental study, graphene–PAN composite electrodes were fabricated and characterized for electrochemical properties, including charge injection capacity and impedance, as well as mechanical properties, such as flexibility and tensile strength. In vivo testing was conducted on rabbits to evaluate their performance in SNS therapy and their effectiveness in relieving constipation. Results: The graphene–PAN composite electrodes demonstrated a high charge injection capacity (1062.58±73.36 µC/cm²), low impedance (31.27±2.76 Ω), and favorable mechanical flexibility (modulus: 1.31±0.45 MPa; strain at break: 27±2%). In vivo stimulation progressively improved fecal output over four days, approaching pre-injury levels. Conclusion: Graphene-based electrodes exhibited suitable electrochemical and mechanical performance, enabling effective neural stimulation and enhanced therapeutic outcomes in constipation management. As an initial proof-of-concept, these flexible graphene-based materials represent promising candidates for future neural stimulation devices.

title: Impact of High Molecular Weight Chitosan on Theranostic Performance of Curcumin-Loaded Magneto-Graphene Quantum Dots Nanocomposite
source: Journal of Biomedical Physics and Engineering
summary: Background: The type of coating material plays an important role in the imaging and treatment properties of cancer nanotheranostics. Objective: The aim of this study was to investigate the effect of high molecular weight chitosan coating on
content: Background: The type of coating material plays an important role in the imaging and treatment properties of cancer nanotheranostics. Objective: The aim of this study was to investigate the effect of high molecular weight chitosan coating on the theranostic properties of the curcumin-loaded magneto-graphene quantum dots (MNPs/GQDs/ChitHMW/Cur) nanocomposite.Material and Methods: In this in vitro study, MNPs/GQDs/ChitHMW nanocomposite was synthesized by the sol-gel method, loaded with anticancer drug curcumin, and characterized using different analytical techniques. Then, the curcumin loading, the drug release at pH 5.5 and pH 7.4, cytotoxicity, MRI transverse relaxivity, and fluorescence spectrum of the nanocomposite were investigated. Results: The findings showed a curcumin loading capacity of 98%, burst drug release at pH 5.5 (79.00% after 24 h), and sustained drug release at pH 7.4 (33.14% after 24 h). Significant concentration-dependent toxicity against MCF-7 cells was observed for the drug-loaded nanocomposite, while the unloaded nanocomposite exhibited the high cytocompatibility. The imaging results showed an MRI transverse relaxivity of 215.4 mM−1 S−1, and excellent fluorescence properties. Conclusion: Using high molecular weight chitosan coating in MNPs/GQDs/ChitHMW/Cur nanocomposite provides adequate cancer theranostic performance.

title: Hydrodeoxygenation of Southern Yellow Pine Bio-Oil and Diesel Blending: Catalyst Performance Evaluation and Fuel Property Assessment
summary: Hydrodeoxygenation (HDO) was investigated as an upgrading route for bio-oil derived from the pyrolysis of Southern Yellow Pine (SYP), with the goal of producing a liquid fuel product suitable for blending with petroleum diesel. Three cataly
content: Hydrodeoxygenation (HDO) was investigated as an upgrading route for bio-oil derived from the pyrolysis of Southern Yellow Pine (SYP), with the goal of producing a liquid fuel product suitable for blending with petroleum diesel. Three catalysts were evaluated in a batch reactor under identical process conditions: a commercial nickel-silica-alumina catalyst and two synthesized catalysts, a calcined iron tailing formulation (CIT) and a calcined red mud formulation (CRM). All three catalysts converted SYP bio-oil into an organic-phase product with substantially reduced oxygen content, reduced viscosity, and a higher heating value (HHV) comparable to petroleum diesel.
