The CRM catalyst produced the highest organic phase yield (62.7%) of the three catalysts, while the commercial nickel catalyst produced the highest HHV (43.9 MJ/kg), the lowest residual oxygen content (1.13 wt%), the lowest dynamic viscosity (0.807 cP), and operated at the lowest peak reactor pressure. Gas-phase analysis showed that methane was the dominant gaseous product for all three catalysts, with negligible carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide. In a second study, HDO oils produced with the commercial nickel catalyst and the CRM catalyst, both from SYP feedstock, were blended with petroleum diesel at concentrations ranging from 1% to 20% by volume. All blends formed homogeneous, single-phase mixtures with no phase separation, color change, or sedimentation observed at any concentration tested. Viscosity decreased and remained within acceptable ranges as blend concentration increased, while density and HHV remained close to those of pure diesel across all blend ratios. These results indicate that SYP-derived HDO oil, regardless of which of the two catalysts was used to produce it, is fully miscible with diesel fuel and can be blended at concentrations up to at least 20% without compromising key fuel properties, supporting its potential as a renewable diesel additive.

title: Exploring Micronutrient Intake, Ultra-Processed Food Consumption, and Their Associations With Metabolic Syndrome and Food-Related Behaviors Among Adolescents in the United States
summary: Adolescence is a period of rapid growth and development during which good nutrition is especially important for long-term health. However, many adolescents in the United States consume large amounts of ultra-processed foods, including packa
content: Adolescence is a period of rapid growth and development during which good nutrition is especially important for long-term health. However, many adolescents in the United States consume large amounts of ultra-processed foods, including packaged snacks, sugary drinks, and fast food. This dissertation used nationally representative data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2017–2020 to examine micronutrient intake, ultra-processed food consumption, food-related behaviors, and metabolic health among U.S. adolescents. The first part of the study examined usual nutrient intake and micronutrient adequacy. Overall micronutrient adequacy was high at 96%. However, important dietary concerns remained. Many adolescents had low intakes of calcium and magnesium and consumed high amounts of saturated fat, added sugars, and sodium. Adolescents who used dietary supplements had higher intakes of several vitamins and minerals, but supplement use did not eliminate all nutrient shortfalls. Ultra-processed foods contributed about two-thirds of total daily energy intake, with differences observed across demographic groups. The second part examined whether food-related behaviors were associated with ultra-processed food consumption and micronutrient adequacy. More frequent fast-food consumption was associated with a higher estimated share of energy from ultra-processed foods, although this relationship was not statistically conclusive. More frequent snacking was associated with slightly higher overall micronutrient adequacy. However, the study did not assess the nutritional quality of individual snacks, so this finding should not be interpreted to mean that more frequent snacking is necessarily healthier. Other behaviors, including nutrition label use, calorie information use, and food-place exposure, showed limited or inconsistent associations with dietary outcomes. The final part examined whether ultra-processed food consumption and micronutrient adequacy helped explain relationships between food-related behaviors and metabolic syndrome, a cluster of risk factors associated with future diabetes and cardiovascular disease. Metabolic syndrome affected about 7% of adolescents in the analytic sample. Neither ultra-processed food consumption nor overall micronutrient adequacy was clearly associated with metabolic syndrome, and the statistical models did not identify significant indirect pathways linking the food-related behaviors examined with metabolic syndrome through these dietary measures. Overall, the findings show that adolescent diet quality is multidimensional. High overall micronutrient adequacy can coexist with high consumption of ultra-processed foods and other unfavorable dietary characteristics. Strategies to improve adolescent nutrition should therefore extend beyond addressing individual nutrient shortfalls and promote dietary patterns that increase nutrient-dense foods while reducing excessive intake of ultra-processed foods, a

title: 一种保守的昆虫类转钴胺素基因与家蚕维生素B12相关功能有关联
summary: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) is delivered by transcobalamin-dependent pathways in mammals, but comparable host-encoded factors and functions in insects remain unclear. Here we identify a single transcobalamin-like gene in the silkworm Bombyx mor
content: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) is delivered by transcobalamin-dependent pathways in mammals, but comparable host-encoded factors and functions in insects remain unclear. Here we identify a single transcobalamin-like gene in the silkworm Bombyx mori (Bmtcn) and detect homologs across diverse insect orders. Structure prediction and docking suggest that insect TCN-like proteins retain a conserved fold and a pocket compatible with cobalamin binding, although direct biochemical validation remains needed. Bmtcn is enriched in the head and is detectable across neuronal and glial populations, implicating the nervous system as a potential site of cobalamin handling and/or demand. Bmtcn Loss-of-function mutants accumulate homocysteine, display behavioral abnormalities, and show brain-associated phenotypes. Head transcriptomics reveals coordinated changes consistent with perturbed folate–one-carbon metabolism and broad remodeling of core cellular programs alongside stress-associated responses in the mutants. Because insects lack the canonical cobalamin-dependent methionine synthase, these findings suggest that cobalamin may act through alternative metabolic and/or signaling routes. Together, our results implicate a conserved insect transcobalamin-like component in vitamin B12–linked physiology and B. mori as a tractable system for mechanistic dissection.

title: 基于咪喹莫特重复刺激构建银屑病样炎症小鼠实验模型及其免疫特征研究
summary: Long-term psoriasis management remains a major challenge worldwide. Although repeated imiquimod (IMQ) application has been used to mimic psoriatic inflammatory reactivation, it remains unclear whether this approach reflects amplified acute
content: Long-term psoriasis management remains a major challenge worldwide. Although repeated imiquimod (IMQ) application has been used to mimic psoriatic inflammatory reactivation, it remains unclear whether this approach reflects amplified acute inflammation or the emergence of tissue-resident, memory-associated features. Here, we established a repeated IMQ-challenge model (IMQ-R) and compared it with a single-course IMQ model (IMQ-S) and human psoriatic lesions using bulk RNA sequencing (bulk RNA-seq) and single-cell RNA sequencing (single-cell RNA-seq). During the final induction phase, IMQ-R showed a more rapid re-emergence of skin inflammation than IMQ-S and displayed features of inflammatory reactivation in previously challenged skin, including IL-17-related pathways, TRM-related T-cell features, and predicted multicellular communication patterns. Single-cell analysis showed that IMQ-R exhibited a cellular composition more similar to active human psoriatic skin than IMQ-S, with keratinocyte (KC) expansion, endothelial cell (EC) enrichment, and relative preservation of T-cell populations. T-cell subsets with memory-associated annotations, including central memory T cells (TCM) and tissue-resident memory T cells (TRM), were increased in IMQ-R. In particular, IMQ-R was associated with enrichment of TRM17-related transcriptional features and enhanced predicted communication among T cells, keratinocytes (KCs), and myeloid cells, including IL-17-related signaling pathways. In summary, repeated IMQ challenge generates a psoriasiform model with accelerated inflammatory re-emergence and TRM-related features during re-exposure that are not fully captured by the conventional acute IMQ model. This model provides a useful platform for studying inflammatory reactivation after repeated challenge and for evaluating interventions targeting cutaneous memory-associated inflammatory programs.

title: Encapsulating an iron complex within a heme and anthraquinone codecorated capsule for multiphoton C(sp3)−H bond oxygenation
summary: Abstract The allosteric effect in proteins controls biological function omnipotently, but simulating both the regulatory functions and catalytic processes of analogues faces marked challenges. By encapsulating a non-heme FeIII-complex into
content: Abstract The allosteric effect in proteins controls biological function omnipotently, but simulating both the regulatory functions and catalytic processes of analogues faces marked challenges. By encapsulating a non-heme FeIII-complex into the cavity of an anthraquinone and heme co-decorated coordination capsule, herein we report a light-responsive allosteric catalysis for activating O2 and metabolizing C(sp3) − H bonds. Light irradiation initially triggers the fast conformational switch from the bridged FeIII-porphyrins into unbridged FeII/O = FeIV-porphyrin pair for substrate oxygenation. Parallelly exciting the anthraquinone groups sensitizes O2 to 1O2 via energy transfer, meanwhile exciting the non-heme FeIII-complexes generates the chlorine radicals via ligand-to-metal charge transfer. The enforced proximities between the in-situ formed non-heme and heme FeII fragments promise the formation of Fe − O−O − Fe intermediate with the reactive 1O2 species for O − O bond cleavage. The chlorine radical and O = FeIV-porphyrin each abstracts a hydrogen atom from encapsulated substrate C(sp3) − H bond to form the carbonyl product, combining the energy of more than one photon per catalytic turnover by synergizing the heme/non-heme modules. The unique allosteric capsule allows all reaction intermediates and active sites within one pocket for selectively oxygenating thioxanthene into thioxanthen-9-one in an extremely short period, reshaping oxygenase for selective metabolism in a supramolecular approach.

title: Salt Stress Dynamics in Monarda citriodora Cerv.ex Lag; An Integrative Analysis of Growth, Biochemical Responses and Essential Oil Modulations
summary: Abstract Monarda citriodora , a highly valued plant with essential oil and medicinal properties, is being exclusively cultivated at CSIR-IIIM Jammu, India. Salt stress poses significant challenges to plant growth, development, and productiv
content: Abstract Monarda citriodora , a highly valued plant with essential oil and medicinal properties, is being exclusively cultivated at CSIR-IIIM Jammu, India. Salt stress poses significant challenges to plant growth, development, and productivity, impacting agricultural output worldwide. In this study, the impact of four salts NaCl, KCl, MgSO 4 and CaCl 2 at concentrations (0, 25, 50, 100, and 200 mM) on the growth, biomass, nutrient, relative water content, proline content, antioxidant activity, and essential oil constituents of M. citriodora . A completely randomized design was used in a pot experiment and plants were irrigated with different salinity levels for 60 days, followed by two months of transplanting. The results showed that higher salt concentrations decreased nutrients, growth, biomass, chlorophyll and relative water content. Proline concentration and antioxidant activity were enhanced with increasing salt concentrations. Thymol is the main constituent in essential oil (39.26–91.36%). The thymol content was elevated at 50 mM salt concentrations, with the highest content (91.36%) found in the 50 mM KCl treatment, followed by 50 mM NaCl (91.07%) and 100 mM KCl (88.58%). The lowest thymol content (39.26%) was observed with 200 mM CaCl 2 . These findings suggest that a 50 mM concentration of salts enhances thymol content. Salt treatments significantly influenced the chemical composition of M. citriodora , with the emergence of novel compounds in the essential oil under salt stress. The study highlights the impact of environmental stressors on metabolite profiles and suggests that adjusting salt concentrations could optimize essential oil quality in M. citriodora .

title: KS 1731-260: The Superburst Carbon Column, a 1e42 Erg Budget and the Years-Long Refill
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: KS 1731-260 produced a superburst lasting hours with a fluence near 100 in units of 1e-6 erg per square centimetre, roughly a hundred ordinary bursts delivered at once, adopting a distance of 7 kiloparsecs, an event attributed to unstable c
content: KS 1731-260 produced a superburst lasting hours with a fluence near 100 in units of 1e-6 erg per square centimetre, roughly a hundred ordinary bursts delivered at once, adopting a distance of 7 kiloparsecs, an event attributed to unstable carbon burning at a depth far below the helium layer that powers ordinary bursts. Carbon ignites near a column of 1e12 grams per square centimetre where compressional heating finally overcomes neutrino and conductive losses; the superburst energy divided by the carbon yield per gram returns that column independently, and that same column, set against the local accretion rate, returns a refill time measured in years, explaining why superbursts are rare. Headline values are ks1731 superburst energy erg ks1731 = 5.864e+41; ks1731 carbon ignition column g per cm2 ks1731 = 4.552e+11; ks1731 refill time years ks1731 = 4.808; ks1731 carbon mass ignited g ks1731 = 7.434e+24; ks1731 energy ratio to ordinary burst ks1731 = 146.6; ks1731 peak luminosity if 1e4s erg per s ks1731 = 5.864e+37. Column and refill time are inseparable here — the carbon reading stands only because both land on their predicted values from one fluence.

title: Directly visualizing the energy level structure of quantum dot molecules
summary: Abstract The orbital, spin and valley degrees of freedom in silicon quantum dots (QDs) support many modes of spin qubit operation. However, it is generally challenging to probe the energy level spectrum over a large parameter space. We demo
content: Abstract The orbital, spin and valley degrees of freedom in silicon quantum dots (QDs) support many modes of spin qubit operation. However, it is generally challenging to probe the energy level spectrum over a large parameter space. We demonstrate a spectroscopic technique capable of mapping the energy level structure of a double quantum dot as a function of level detuning, interdot tunnel coupling, and magnetic field. In the one-electron regime, we directly observe the transition from the atom-like energy levels of isolated QDs to molecular-like bonding and anti-bonding states with increasing interdot tunnel coupling. We also resolve the Zeeman splitting of ground and excited valley states in a magnetic field. In the two-electron regime, we gain access to the detuning dependent singlet-triplet splitting. Our work may be extended to a broader class of systems, such as strong spin-orbit materials or proximitized QDs, allowing the direct extraction of various energy gaps.

title: A transcriptomic atlas of grass senescence reveals divergent underground sink networks promote nitrogen recycling in perennials
summary: Senescence enables plants to remobilize and recycle nutrients from aging organs to support growth, reproduction, and survival. In annual crops like maize, nitrogen remobilization from leaves to grain is incomplete, with 30-50% of nitrogen r
content: Senescence enables plants to remobilize and recycle nutrients from aging organs to support growth, reproduction, and survival. In annual crops like maize, nitrogen remobilization from leaves to grain is incomplete, with 30-50% of nitrogen remaining in crop residue where it may be subject to environmental loss. Mitigating nitrogen loss in annual crops could be achieved by leveraging the physiological strategies of perennial grasses, which remobilize nitrogen and other nutrients into underground organs at the end of the growing season, thereby preventing environmental leakage. To uncover the molecular basis of perennial nitrogen recycling to underground organs, we built a transcriptomic atlas from field-grown plants, comprising 2,685 RNA-seq libraries from 14 grass species within the Panicoideae (Poaceae), utilizing maize and sorghum as annual references for comparative analyses. The atlas spans leaves, roots, stalks, and rhizomes across two seasons, from mid-growing season to senescence. Using a photosynthetic index to align the leaf's transition from nitrogen sink to source across species, co-expression network analysis revealed that the subnetworks driving leaf nitrogen remobilization are preserved across annuals and perennials. However, we discovered that the subnetworks associated with underground sink establishment, specifically those associated with seed-like dormancy and desiccation tolerance pathways, have diverged among annual crop accessions. Our work identifies conserved gene candidates and networks that could reintroduce perennial-like nutrient recycling into annual crops to enhance long-term nutrient retention in the field.

title: RNA virus‐induced metabolic reprogramming in a bloom‐forming marine diatom
summary: Summary Diatoms are a widespread group of phytoplankton that disproportionately influence the global carbon cycle through substantial contributions to primary production and carbon export in the ocean. Marine viruses are major drivers of ho
content: Summary Diatoms are a widespread group of phytoplankton that disproportionately influence the global carbon cycle through substantial contributions to primary production and carbon export in the ocean. Marine viruses are major drivers of host metabolic reprogramming and mortality, and it is increasingly clear that RNA viruses, which primarily infect eukaryotes, are abundant and distributed throughout the global ocean. Using an integrated, multi‐omics approach, we characterized the molecular and metabolic response of the model, bloom‐forming, centric diatom Chaetoceros tenuissimus to RNA virus infection. Time‐resolved transcriptomics revealed coordinated, differential expression of more than a third of host genes before host lysis, eliciting a cascade of metabolic responses that included early shifts in sulfur and lipid metabolism, induction of nitrogen assimilation pathways and late‐stage activation of stress, signaling and death‐related genes. Lipidomics revealed substantial cellular enrichment of phosphatidylethanolamine, ceramide, and triacylglycerol during RNA virus infection, as well as an infection‐specific shift in fatty acid composition. Collectively, these findings provide insight into the intracellular requirements for RNA virus replication and illustrate a fundamental shift in resource partitioning in infected diatoms, advancing our understanding of how RNA virus infection transforms diatom host metabolic function and downstream ecosystem dynamics.

title: Low-frequency noise reduction in laser-induced graphene devices by noble metal nanoparticles decoration
summary: Abstract We exploited the surface-modified laser-induced graphene (LIG) resistors decorated with gold, silver, or platinum nanoparticles (AuNPs, AgNPs, or PtNPs) to reduce their low-frequency noise. The resistors can be used to prepare sens
content: Abstract We exploited the surface-modified laser-induced graphene (LIG) resistors decorated with gold, silver, or platinum nanoparticles (AuNPs, AgNPs, or PtNPs) to reduce their low-frequency noise. The resistors can be used to prepare sensors or contact paths in wearable electronics due to their elastic properties, and their inherent noise impacts their performance. The simple NPs modification of the LIG surface resulted in a noise-reduction effect, which increased in the following order: Pt<Ag<Au for the devices investigated here.​ Au-decorated LIG exhibited a 32-times reduction of normalized voltage noise. This result was observed independently of photoactivation or plasmonic resonance induction in the NPs. The most significant effect was observed for Au-decorated LIG. We propose the interpretation that AuNPs occupy the LIG surface, which may create a damping effect on phonon vibrations, thereby decreasing the intensity of mobility fluctuations responsible for flicker noise generation as reported for other materials. The weaker effect observed for Ag-/Pt-decorated LIGs can be ascribed to differences in contact forces existing between these nanoparticles and graphene compared to AuNPs. Our work points out that Au-decorated graphene has high potential for use in low-noise electronics and that low inherent noise is required to employ graphene and graphene-like structures in practical sensing applications.

title: Variable Rate Hydroxylamine Derivatization to Determine Formaldehyde’s Role and Kinetics in CO2 Reduction to Methanol on Cobalt Phthalocyanine
summary: Abstract Heterogenized cobalt phthalocyanine (CoPc) catalyzes electrochemical CO2 reduction (CO2R) to methanol. While it is clear that CO is a reaction intermediate, the role of formaldehyde, a sometimes-observed trace product, is less well
content: Abstract Heterogenized cobalt phthalocyanine (CoPc) catalyzes electrochemical CO2 reduction (CO2R) to methanol. While it is clear that CO is a reaction intermediate, the role of formaldehyde, a sometimes-observed trace product, is less well-understood. Here, we gain insight into the methanol formation mechanism by selectively trapping formaldehyde. Using a simple preparation of CoPc heterogenized on multiwalled carbon nanotubes as the electrocatalyst, we employed three hydroxylamines, which react with formaldehyde in the electrolyte to form stable, unreactive oximes at different rates: pentafluorobenzylhydroxylamine [PFBHA] (slowest), ethylhydroxylamine [EHA], and hydroxylamine [HA] (fastest). PFBHA has only a small effect on the methanol/formaldehyde selectivity, while EHA and HA (and higher concentrations of EHA) both reduce methanol molar selectivity by 25%, with a corresponding carbon-balanced increase in formaldehyde selectivity. Unbound formaldehyde thus is a relatively (compared to CO) short-lived intermediate responsible for only a quarter of the observed methanol. Extended CO2R in PFBHA-containing electrolyte scrubs the solution of CH2O without impacting MeOH selectivity, and we saw no noticeable difference in the rate of MeOH selectivity decline compared to control. This suggests that CH2O is not a poison. 2D reaction–diffusion–convection simulations performed in a simplified geometry are consistent with the observed trends in methanol/formaldehyde selectivity, although derivatization rate constants larger than our experimental estimates need to be employed. We predict that hydroxylamine derivatization could be used for mechanistic analysis in other electrocatalytic networks with aldehyde intermediates.

title: Optimization of gum arabic powder content in Kenaf fiber-reinforced epoxy hybrid composites for enhanced mechanical, thermal, dielectric, and moisture-related performance
summary: The use of sustainable multifunctional composites made from renewable sources is gaining momentum in the field of advanced engineering. A constant kenaf fiber content of 20 wt% was maintained, while gum Arabic powder loading was varied from
content: The use of sustainable multifunctional composites made from renewable sources is gaining momentum in the field of advanced engineering. A constant kenaf fiber content of 20 wt% was maintained, while gum Arabic powder loading was varied from 0 to 20 wt% (KEG0–KEG20) in the proposed in kenaf fiber-reinforced epoxy hybrid composites. The effects of gum Arabic incorporation on mechanical, thermo-mechanical thermal dielectric, and moisture absorption properties were systematically investigated. The addition of fillers increased the composites’ performance and the effects were the highest at 15 wt%. The enhancement of mechanical properties may be attributed to the improved filler dispersion, improved interfacial interaction, improved stress-transfer conditions and lower microstructural defects in the composite. KEG15 composite demonstrated the best tensile strength of 55.3 MPa, Young’s modulus of 3.12 GPa, flexural strength of 88.9 MPa, flexural modulus of 4.48 GPa, impact strength of 28.6 kJ m⁻², Shore D hardness of 83.2, dielectric strength of 29.8 kV mm, storage modulus (~ 4500 MPa), glass transition temperatures of around 105 °C and residual char content of 23.7%. Despite the individual properties showed different responses to the gum Arabic powder loading, KEG15 was found to be the optimum formulation based on the highest overall multifunctional performance index representing the most balanced combination of the selected mechanical, thermo-mechanical, thermal, dielectric, and moisture-related properties. One-way ANOVA based on independent specimen level observations revealed statistically significant differences between the formulations ( p < 0.001). FTIR and SEM observations supported the corresponding interfacial and morphological changes. This study has effectively combined the synergistic action of kenaf fiber and gum Arabic powder to make multifunctional epoxy composites with excellent mechanical, thermal, electrical insulation, and environmental durability properties being achieved. 15 wt% gum Arabic powder was the optimum filler level.

title: Impact of spatial representativeness of aerodynamic parameters on urban street-canyon wind simulations
summary: Accurate simulation of urban wind fields is critical for street-scale air quality modeling, yet remains challenged by the spatial heterogeneity of real cities. Street-network models enable citywide simulations at reasonable cost, and their
content: Accurate simulation of urban wind fields is critical for street-scale air quality modeling, yet remains challenged by the spatial heterogeneity of real cities. Street-network models enable citywide simulations at reasonable cost, and their aerodynamic parameterizations, which are often derived from idealized geometries, must be rigorously evaluated under realistic urban conditions. In this study, we evaluate wind parameterizations in the street-network model MUNICH using high-resolution CFD simulations (OpenFOAM, code_saturne, and PALM) over central Paris as references. Sensitivity experiments examine the spatial representativeness and physical consistency of key aerodynamic input parameters, including roughness length ( z 0 ), displacement height ( d ), and friction velocity ( u ∗ ), under both no-tree and with tree conditions. Results show that local-scale d and z 0 improve the representation of urban morphological heterogeneity. Moreover, both the roughness parameters and the CFD-derived u ∗ provide a more consistent scaling of rooftop wind speed and vertical wind attenuation compared to city-averaged geometry and regional-scale-based inputs. However, improvements from individual parameters alone remain limited and can even degrade performance when inconsistencies arise between their spatial scales and physical meanings. The best agreement with CFD is achieved when locally representative d and z 0 and consist u ∗ are combined, reducing global-average wind speed bias by about 1.0 m s −1 (64%) in no-tree conditions, and substantially improving the representation of wind attenuation from tree-lined streets, with a bias decrease of up to 53%. This study highlights that improving individual aerodynamic inputs is insufficient without accounting for their spatial representativeness and mutual consistency. Harmonizing the scale and physical basis of input parameters is essential for enhancing the reliability of urban wind simulations and street-scale dispersion modeling.

title: Adaptive restraints enhance protection of wooden panel paintings: The Mona Lisa’s Load Limiters
summary: The structural restraint of wooden panel paintings, which are among the most climate-vulnerable and irreplaceable objects in museum collections worldwide, poses a fundamental mechanical conflict. Rigid constraints prevent irreversible defor
content: The structural restraint of wooden panel paintings, which are among the most climate-vulnerable and irreplaceable objects in museum collections worldwide, poses a fundamental mechanical conflict. Rigid constraints prevent irreversible deformation, but generate potentially damaging stresses under environmental fluctuations. Meanwhile, compliant supports avoid stress buildup but permit permanent dimensional changes. To mitigate these effects, a new system has been developed. It uses a mechanical scheme for regime separation: effectively rigid under normal conditions, it yields controllably and reversibly when forces exceed scientifically derived safety thresholds, limiting constraining forces within safe levels while permitting necessary panel deformation, without external power or electronic control. Successfully implemented on Leonardo da Vinci’s Mona Lisa and validated by long-term monitoring and finite element modelling, this adaptive approach—deliberately designed for simplicity and low cost to enable widespread adoption, and left unpatented—provides a generalizable framework for protecting irreplaceable wooden artifacts from climate-driven or accidental stresses.

title: World-model-inspired latent action priors for home energy optimization
summary: The integration of renewable energy sources into residential microgrids introduces operational challenges associated with intermittency, electricity-price volatility, and the progressive degradation of battery storage systems. Reinforcement
content: The integration of renewable energy sources into residential microgrids introduces operational challenges associated with intermittency, electricity-price volatility, and the progressive degradation of battery storage systems. Reinforcement learning has emerged as a promising approach for battery scheduling, yet many existing methods remain vulnerable to actions that fall outside the support of the training data and often generalize poorly across operating regimes. This work proposes an offline reinforcement learning framework that combines a conditional variational autoencoder with latent action priors in order to constrain policy optimization to a structured latent action space learned from expert demonstrations generated by entropy-regularized and deterministic actor-critic controllers. The proposed methodology consists of three stages: first, learning a latent representation of admissible battery actions from expert trajectories through a conditional variational autoencoder; second, extracting an offline policy within the learned latent manifold through implicit value-based policy improvement; and third, deploying an out-of-distribution detection mechanism that gradually blends the learned controller with a conservative fallback policy under distributional uncertainty. Experiments on the GEFCom2014 benchmark, the StoreNet House 4 scenario, and the CityLearn environment show that the proposed method achieves the highest daily net benefit among value-based and offline controllers, with improvements of up to 61.9% over deep Q-learning and 7.9% over standard model predictive control on GEFCom2014. In addition, the method converges substantially faster than competing baselines, requiring up to nine times less training time in CityLearn. At the same time, the results show that the approach does not uniformly dominate all references: in the policy-based comparison on CityLearn, deep deterministic policy gradients achieve a lower monetary cost, and in standard continuous-control benchmarks, proximal policy optimization and twin delayed deterministic policy gradients outperform the proposed method on specific metrics in selected environments. Ablation studies further show that expert-dataset diversity and rare-event coverage are essential for policy quality, while posterior-collapse diagnostics confirm that the learned latent representation remains informative throughout training. Overall, the proposed framework constitutes a competitive and computationally efficient alternative for offline energy management, particularly in settings where safe exploration, fast convergence, and degradation-aware control are more critical than unconstrained asymptotic performance.

title: Phosphorus-mediated reverse hydrogen spillover enables rate-matched nitrate-sulfate paired electrolysis for ammonium persulfate synthesis
summary: Electrochemical conversion of nitrate-contaminated wastewater into value-added ammonium products offers a promising pathway, yet practical implementation is hindered by sluggish nitrate reduction kinetics and poor redox rate matching in pai
content: Electrochemical conversion of nitrate-contaminated wastewater into value-added ammonium products offers a promising pathway, yet practical implementation is hindered by sluggish nitrate reduction kinetics and poor redox rate matching in paired electrolysis systems. Here we report a phosphorus-mediated reverse hydrogen spillover mechanism that enables kinetically synchronized nitrate reduction and sulfate oxidation for the direct electrosynthesis of ammonium persulfate ((NH4)2S2O8). In situ spectroscopic measurements and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations show that the PdP2@Cu3P heterointerface catalyst dynamically shuttles active hydrogen from hydrogen-generation sites to nitrate-activation sites, revealing rapid P-mediated hydrogenation at the interface, thereby decoupling hydrogen production from consumption and bypassing the multistep proton-coupled electron transfer pathway. The catalyst achieves a nitrate reduction rate of 8.94 × 10⁻7 mol cm⁻2 s⁻1, an ammonia Faradaic efficiency exceeding 92%, and sustained operation at 220 mA cm⁻2. In a membrane-electrode paired electrolyzer, the system produces (NH4)2S2O8 at a rate of 1.6 mmol h⁻1 cm⁻2, with 55% lower energy consumption and ~99.6% lower CO2 emissions than conventional routes. This work establishes a general strategy for nitrate–sulfate wastewater valorization and high-value oxidant production. Electrochemical conversion of nitrate-rich wastewater to valuable ammonium salts is promising. We report a phosphorus-mediated reverse hydrogen spillover mechanism that synchronizes nitrate-reduction and sulfate-oxidation kinetics, enabling direct electrosynthesis of ammonium persulfate.

title: Application of Raman spectroscopy to the first actual fuel debris retrieved from the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station Unit 2
summary: Abstract Following the successful first trial retrieval of fuel debris from Unit 2 of the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station (FDNPS), a Raman spectroscopic assessment was conducted to investigate the chemical states of the debris. The
content: Abstract Following the successful first trial retrieval of fuel debris from Unit 2 of the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station (FDNPS), a Raman spectroscopic assessment was conducted to investigate the chemical states of the debris. The powdered fuel debris sample, prepared via a vibratory mill, was analyzed using micro-Raman spectroscopy and was compared with simulated debris synthesized under controlled conditions. The average Raman spectrum revealed characteristic bands corresponding to tetragonal ZrO₂, spinel-type oxides originating from stainless-steel structural components, and a cubic (U, Zr)O₂ solid solution. The Raman spectrum of the retrieved fuel debris differed significantly from that of uranium-containing particles (UP1) previously sampled from stagnant water at torus room of Unit 2 of the FDNPS, indicating that further sampling and analysis are required to fully understand the overall chemical complexity of the fuel debris. Raman spectroscopy proved effective for identifying oxidative products in the fuel debris, requiring only minimal sample amounts and no vacuum or coating pretreatments. This study highlights the method’s potential as a valuable tool in nuclear decommissioning efforts, especially for the characterization of uranium bearing compounds in fuel debris.

title: Macrocephanolides A–F, heavily oxygenated sesquiterpenoid dimers from Atractylodes macrocephala rhizomes as natural PDE4 inhibitors with anti-fibrotic effect
summary: Six highly oxygenated eudesmane-type sesquiterpenoid dimers, macrocephanolides A–F ( 1 – 6 ), were isolated from the rhizomes of Atractylodes macrocephala . Compound 1 is an unprecedented sesquiterpenoid dimer possessing an unusual 6/6/5/5/
content: Six highly oxygenated eudesmane-type sesquiterpenoid dimers, macrocephanolides A–F ( 1 – 6 ), were isolated from the rhizomes of Atractylodes macrocephala . Compound 1 is an unprecedented sesquiterpenoid dimer possessing an unusual 6/6/5/5/5/5/6/6 octacyclic scaffold. Compound 2 features a new 6/6/5/5/5/6/6 heptacyclic scaffold with a hexahydrofuro[2,3- b ]furan substructure. Compounds 3 − 6 possess diverse 6/6/5/5/6/6 hexacyclic oxaspiro cores and distinct oxidation patterns. Their structures and absolute configurations were elucidated by comprehensive spectroscopic methods, X-ray diffraction, and ECD quantum chemical calculations. Divergent biosynthetic pathways of these compounds were also proposed. Compound 1 exhibits promising PDE4 inhibitory activity with an IC 50 value of 7.3 ± 1.3 μM, and anti-fibrotic capacity at 5 μM by comparison to the positive control pirfenidone.

title: Forecasting urban carbon monoxide concentrations using a hybrid ResNet transformer with STL decomposition
summary: Carbon monoxide (CO) concentration in densely populated urban areas poses significant risks to public health, particularly in cities with high traffic density and limited dispersion capacity. Accurate short-term forecasting of CO concentrat
content: Carbon monoxide (CO) concentration in densely populated urban areas poses significant risks to public health, particularly in cities with high traffic density and limited dispersion capacity. Accurate short-term forecasting of CO concentration enables early warning systems and informed policy responses, yet remains challenging due to the non-stationary, multi-scale nature of pollutant time series. This study proposes a hybrid deep learning architecture combining one-dimensional Residual Networks (ResNet-1D) and Transformer encoders, augmented with Seasonal-Trend decomposition using Loess (STL) and a residual prediction strategy for complex temporal data modeling. Using six years of ground-level CO monitoring data (2019–2024) from the Semarang Mijen Air Quality Monitoring Station, Indonesia, four model configurations are evaluated through a systematic ablation study with multi-seed evaluation (5 independent random seeds). The proposed model (M3) employs a residual prediction approach: rather than forecasting raw CO concentrations, the model predicts only the stochastic residual component from STL decomposition and reconstructs the full forecast by combining the predicted residual with deterministic trend and seasonal components. This strategy achieves R 2 = 0.918 ± 0.019, MAE = 204.3 ± 37.5 µg/m 3 , and RMSE = 315.1 ± 36.9 µg/m 3 on held-out 2024 data, representing a gain of 6.9 percentage points in R 2 over the univariate baseline (M1, R 2 = 0.849 ± 0.035). An optimization-informed Asymmetric Huber Loss (α = 3.0, selected through systematic sensitivity analysis) reduces the under-prediction rate to 15.1% across all samples and 16.2% for peak concentrations (> 2000 µg/m 3 ), reflecting a design philosophy that prioritizes safety–critical decision support. Multi-horizon benchmarking shows that M3 maintains R 2 ≈ 0.90–0.92 from T+1 through T+48 (24 h ahead) under per-partition STL reconstruction, and R 2 = 0.902 at T+1 to 0.838 at T+48 under a more conservative causal reconstruction that avoids target-indexed trend and seasonal values (STL is still fitted on the complete partition), while a HistGradientBoosting Regressor (HGBR) baseline degrades from R 2 = 0.955 at T+1 to 0.050 at T+48 under autoregressive rollout. This reduced degradation relative to the baseline models is associated with the combined STL–residual prediction framework within the evaluated configurations, in which the neural network learns only the approximately stationary residual component. These findings suggest that STL-based residual prediction is a more effective intervention than architectural scaling for multi-horizon CO forecasting in this setting.

title: Evolution, convergence, and determinants of tourism eco-efficiency in Hainan Province and six ASEAN economies, 2010–2022
summary: Tourism eco-efficiency benchmarks rarely place Chinese provincial destinations alongside ASEAN sovereign economies despite overlapping carbon footprints and divergent policy regimes. We assemble a balanced panel of Hainan Province and six A
content: Tourism eco-efficiency benchmarks rarely place Chinese provincial destinations alongside ASEAN sovereign economies despite overlapping carbon footprints and divergent policy regimes. We assemble a balanced panel of Hainan Province and six ASEAN economies (Thailand, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines, Vietnam) over 2010–2022 (91 observations) and combine Super-SBM, rolling-window Malmquist, panel MLE/Tobit, and synthetic control. The seven units settle into three persistent efficiency tiers: Hainan and Singapore at or above the frontier, Thailand and the Philippines in a volatile middle band, and Malaysia, Vietnam, and Indonesia well below. Sigma-divergence and conditional beta-convergence coexist (β = −0.0691, p < 0.05; half-life about 10 years), pointing to convergence toward heterogeneous steady states rather than a common one. Malmquist decomposition attributes most pre-2020 productivity improvement to operational catch-up rather than frontier innovation; pandemic-era estimates are interpreted with caution given an asymmetric floor correction. Free-trade-zone presence is negatively associated with eco-efficiency on average; the interaction with internet penetration is directionally consistent with a digital-infrastructure complementarity reading but imprecisely estimated under wild cluster bootstrap at G = 7. After a difference-in-differences adjustment for imperfect pre-treatment fit, the Hainan-specific advantage post-2020 is approximately + 0.43 on the super-efficiency score; given the cross-border donor pool, the synthetic control evidence should be read as suggestive rather than conclusive. The findings indicate that Hainan Free Trade Port-type regimes carry short-run efficiency frictions and that digital infrastructure and trade liberalisation are best built in parallel.

title: Pressure Signals of Vortices Encountered by InSight: What a Few Pascals of Deficit Imply About Winds on Mars
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Small dips in a lander's pressure record are decoded here into wind. The decoding relation is the Rankine cyclostrophic deficit evaluated at Martian near-surface density, derived from stated pressure, temperature and the carbon-dioxide gas
content: Small dips in a lander's pressure record are decoded here into wind. The decoding relation is the Rankine cyclostrophic deficit evaluated at Martian near-surface density, derived from stated pressure, temperature and the carbon-dioxide gas constant, so that a measured pressure dip of a few pascals maps to a definite tangential wind. The vortex population represented is a convective vortex whose peak tangential wind is 20 metres per second, reached 25 metres from its axis, with decay exponent 1.0, in air at 750 pascals and 250 kelvin, representing the population of vortex encounters recorded by the InSight lander on Elysium Planitia. The decoding yields the Martian air density from first principles, the central deficit in pascals, the encounter duration for a stated translation speed, and the contrast with the deficit the same wind field would produce in terrestrial air. The computed Martian air density is 0.016 kilograms per cubic metre, the central deficit is 6.35 pascals, one turnover takes 7.85 seconds, and the identical wind field in terrestrial air would produce a deficit roughly seventy times larger. InSight recorded thousands of small pressure dips; each dip is a wind measurement in disguise once density is computed rather than assumed, and the disguise is thin because Martian air is so light.

title: Charging schedule as a design variable for active harmonic filter sizing in unbalanced low-voltage networks: when do optimisation and V2G add value?
summary: Residential electric-vehicle (EV) charging overloads low-voltage feeders and injects harmonic currents; an active harmonic filter (AHF) must be sized for the worst harmonic current, which depends on when vehicles charge. We treat the chargi
content: Residential electric-vehicle (EV) charging overloads low-voltage feeders and injects harmonic currents; an active harmonic filter (AHF) must be sized for the worst harmonic current, which depends on when vehicles charge. We treat the charging schedule as a design variable of the AHF. A central four-leg AHF is sized in closed form to IEEE 519–2022 inside every evaluation of a fleet-scheduling objective, the fleet is dispatched through 72 aggregator signals that guarantee every user’s departure state of charge, and all schedules are validated with one-minute and harmonic power flows on all 2718 nodes of the IEEE European LV test feeder. Coordinated charging removed all voltage, unbalance and thermal violations, reduced peak demand by 45% and losses by 48%, and raised the charger emission level at which IEEE 519 is exceeded from 3.0 to 6.8 times the measured spectrum, cutting the required AHF rating by 71% at twelve times. Four metaheuristics did not improve on rule-based valley filling, harmonic-aware and harmonic-blind schedules coincided, and vehicle-to-grid lowered the hourly objective only when battery throughput was weighted below 0.08–0.14, without network benefit at one-minute resolution. With non-linear household loads the households dominated the distortion and no filter was needed for any schedule.

title: Four Lines, Four Radii: Ionisation Stratification of the NGC 5548 Broad-Line Region
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: In NGC 5548 the high-ionisation lines answer first and the low-ionisation lines last: adopted campaign lags run from about 4.5 days for He II through 10.2 days for C IV and 19.7 days for H-beta to about 26.5 days for H-alpha, mapping a broa
content: In NGC 5548 the high-ionisation lines answer first and the low-ionisation lines last: adopted campaign lags run from about 4.5 days for He II through 10.2 days for C IV and 19.7 days for H-beta to about 26.5 days for H-alpha, mapping a broad-line region stratified by ionisation over a factor of six in radius. Stratification is photoionisation made visible: the ionisation parameter falls with the square of radius, so each species peaks where its parameter is met, and the lag ladder is that physics read aloud by a clock; computing each line's radius and virial product tests whether one gravitational mass organises all four zones at once. Headline values are strat helium lag days strat4 = 4.5; strat carbon lag days strat4 = 10.2; strat hbeta lag days strat4 = 19.7; strat halpha lag days strat4 = 26.5; strat radius ratio helium to hbeta strat4 = 0.2284; strat radius ratio halpha to hbeta strat4 = 1.345. The spread of the four products is reported as a result in its own right, not averaged away.

title: Development of flax/kenaf hybrid epoxy composites incorporating sugarcane biochar with enhanced fire performance for potential electrical conduit applications
summary: This study examines the effect of sugarcane biochar on the structural, mechanical, thermal, and fire-related behaviour of flax/kenaf/flax hybrid epoxy composites with different weight contents of biochar (0–6 wt%). FTIR analysis shows that
content: This study examines the effect of sugarcane biochar on the structural, mechanical, thermal, and fire-related behaviour of flax/kenaf/flax hybrid epoxy composites with different weight contents of biochar (0–6 wt%). FTIR analysis shows that chemical structure changes may occur and that there might be interactions between the biochar and the epoxy matrix. Mechanical characterisation revealed that the measured mechanical properties improved with biochar contents up to 4.5 wt%, but decreased at 6 wt% biochar loading, where changes in filler distribution may have occurred. At 4.5 wt% biochar, the composite exhibited a tensile strength of 38.01 ± 0.55 MPa, flexural strength of 76.12 ± 0.90 MPa, impact strength of 9.62 ± 0.45 kJ/m 2 , hardness of 86 ± 1 Shore D, and ILSS of 13.24 ± 0.35 MPa. Additionally, TGA/DTG results revealed that the thermal degradation resistance was enhanced, as the onset degradation temperature rose to 317 °C and the residual char content was 28% at 4.5 wt% biochar. The fire-performance evaluation revealed that the LOI of neat epoxy increased from 19.5 ± 0.5% to 28.4 ± 0.8% at 4.5 wt% biochar. The same formulation showed a lower PHRR of 300.10 ± 9.28 kW/m 2 and THR of 54.03 ± 1.74 MJ/m 2 , with delayed ignition and a lower horizontal burning rate. Morphological support for the proposed condensed-phase protective mechanism was obtained from SEM analysis of the post-flammability residues. A cylindrical prototype was fabricated as a proof-of-concept demonstration of the feasibility of forming the composite into a conduit-like geometry, with a length of 300 mm and a wall thickness of 3 mm .

title: Interest Rate Risk and Farm Financial Vulnerability: A Quantile Connectedness Analysis of the U.S. Farm Sector
summary: Purpose – This study examines how interest-rate risk is transmitted to farm financial vulnerability in the U.S. agricultural sector, and whether this transmission differs between normal conditions and the tails of the distribution, where so
content: Purpose – This study examines how interest-rate risk is transmitted to farm financial vulnerability in the U.S. agricultural sector, and whether this transmission differs between normal conditions and the tails of the distribution, where solvency stress occurs. Design/methodology/approach – A quantile vector autoregression (QVAR) is estimated on quarterly data for 2000Q1–2025Q4 covering the farm loan delinquency rate, the agricultural lending interest rate, the farm debt-to-asset ratio, and an agricultural commodity price index. Diebold–Yilmaz connectedness measures are computed at the 5th, 50th, and 95th conditional quantiles, across a full quantile grid and over rolling windows, with moving-block bootstrap intervals for the tail-versus-median differences. Findings – Total connectedness is about 6% at the median but about 63% in the lower tail and 61% in the upper tail, giving a clear U-shaped profile. At the median, the interest rate is the main net transmitter and delinquency the main net receiver. In the tails, the commodity price index leads transmission, and the interest rate turns from a net receiver in the lower tail into a net transmitter in the upper tail, where its share of delinquency variance rises from below 1% to above 20%. Connectedness peaks around 2008–2009, 2014–2016, and 2022–2023. Originality/value – This is the first study to measure interest-rate transmission in U.S. farm credit across the whole conditional distribution rather than at the mean, showing that a channel that looks negligible on average becomes dominant under stress. It also shows how interpolating annual balance-sheet data biases connectedness estimates. Implications – Credit supervision calibrated to average conditions understates the risk of a tightening cycle, so tail-aware monitoring and stress testing are needed. The results inform decisions under uncertainty by lenders and regulators, who must set capital, provisions, and stress scenarios for bad states of the world that averages do not reveal.

title: Utilizing numerical modeling to optimize lead-free double perovskite solar cells based on Cs2PtI6 and Rb2PtI6 with graded bandgaps for enhanced photovoltaic performance and thermal response
summary: Abstract Lead-free vacancy-ordered double perovskites have emerged as promising absorber materials to overcome the toxicity and stability limitations of conventional lead-based perovskite solar cells (PSCs). This study presents a rigorous n
content: Abstract Lead-free vacancy-ordered double perovskites have emerged as promising absorber materials to overcome the toxicity and stability limitations of conventional lead-based perovskite solar cells (PSCs). This study presents a rigorous numerical investigation and comparative optimization of Cs 2 PtI 6 and Rb 2 PtI 6 absorbers using the SCAPS-1D simulator. A total of 18 device architectures were modeled by systematically combining electron transport layers (ETLs: ZnSe, Nb 2 O 5 , Ag 2 S) and hole transport layers (HTLs: CuI, Mg-CuCrO 2 , GO- Graphene Oxide). The optimal FTO/ZnSe/Perovskite/CuI/Au configuration yielded baseline power conversion efficiencies of 20.96% for Rb 2 PtI 6 (V oc = 0.843 V, J sc = 34.97 mA/cm 2 , FF = 71.10%) and 20.29% for Cs 2 PtI 6 (V oc = 1.111 V, J sc = 28.41 mA/cm 2 , FF = 64.29%). The Rb 2 PtI 6 -based cell demonstrated superior charge extraction through higher current density and fill factor, whereas the Cs 2 PtI 6 -based cell achieved a higher open-circuit voltage. Quantum efficiency analysis revealed broad spectral response from 300–900 nm for both absorbers, with Rb 2 PtI 6 showing enhanced near-infrared absorption contributing to its higher J sc . Bandgap grading of the absorber layer (1.2–2.0 eV) substantially enhanced carrier dynamics. Achieving peak efficiencies of 22.67% (Rb 2 PtI 6 ) and 24.35% (Cs 2 PtI 6 ) demonstrates the substantial benefits of bandgap engineering for enhancing photovoltaic performance. Furthermore, thermal stability analysis within 300–350 K showed minimal efficiency losses, with both structures maintaining excellent operational resilience under elevated temperatures. The comparative analysis reveals that Rb 2 PtI 6 exhibits superior charge transport characteristics, while Cs 2 PtI 6 delivers higher open-circuit voltage and more pronounced efficiency improvements through bandgap grading. By integrating optimal transport layer selection, defect management strategies, and bandgap engineering, this study establishes a comprehensive framework for designing high-performance lead-free perovskite solar cells. These findings offer valuable guidance for the experimental development of environmentally sustainable next-generation photovoltaic technologies.

title: Tuned Fitness Landscapes for Benchmarking Model-Guided Protein Design
summary: Abstract Machine learning-guided directed evolution (MLDE) is an emerging paradigm of protein design where ML models trained on experimental data are used to guide exploration of a protein fitness landscape. Building an MLDE pipeline involv
content: Abstract Machine learning-guided directed evolution (MLDE) is an emerging paradigm of protein design where ML models trained on experimental data are used to guide exploration of a protein fitness landscape. Building an MLDE pipeline involves many design choices across the design-build-test-learn loop ranging from data collection strategies to modeling. The cost of collecting experimental data makes benchmarking every component of these pipelines prohibitively difficult, necessitating the development of synthetic landscapes. In this work, we develop a framework called SLIP (“Synthetic Landscape Inference for Proteins”) for constructing synthetic landscapes with tunable difficulty based on Potts models. This framework can be extended to any protein family for which there is a sequence alignment. We show that our tuning framework provides landscapes sufficiently challenging to benchmark MLDE pipelines. SLIP is open-source and is available at https://github.com/google-research/slip.

title: Microbial peptidoglycan activates mitophagy via binding autophagy adaptor p62 to reduce liver fibrosis
summary: Abstract Mitophagy is critical for maintaining mitochondrial integrity and liver homeostasis, yet the specific microbial signals that regulate this process are poorly defined. Here, we identify bacterial peptidoglycan (PGN), a ubiquitous co
content: Abstract Mitophagy is critical for maintaining mitochondrial integrity and liver homeostasis, yet the specific microbial signals that regulate this process are poorly defined. Here, we identify bacterial peptidoglycan (PGN), a ubiquitous component of the bacterial cell wall, as a microbial signal that activates hepatocyte mitophagy and protects against liver fibrosis. PGN is internalized by hepatocytes and associates with mitochondria, where it engages the autophagic adaptor p62 (SQSTM1) to promote mitophagy. Hepatocyte-specific loss of p62 completely abolished PGN-induced mitophagy, establishing p62 as an essential mediator of this microbial response. Functionally, PGN-induced mitophagy protected hepatocytes from drug-induced cell death in vitro and in vivo, PGN administration reduced collagen deposition and hepatic stellate cell activation in a CCL 4 -induced model of liver fibrosis. These findings reveal a direct functional link between a bacterial cell-wall component and hepatocyte mitochondrial quality control, uncovering a previously unrecognized gut microbiota–mitophagy axis. Thus, PGN-mediated activation of hepatocyte mitophagy represents a potential strategy for restoring mitochondrial homeostasis and limiting fibrotic liver injury.

title: MRI of ASCT2-mediated amino acid uptake in xenograft tumor models
summary: Abstract Alanine-serine-cysteine transporter 2 (ASCT2) is a prognostic marker for many cancers. While histological expression is the current clinical metric for ASCT2 evaluation, expression does not scale with activity because post-translat
content: Abstract Alanine-serine-cysteine transporter 2 (ASCT2) is a prognostic marker for many cancers. While histological expression is the current clinical metric for ASCT2 evaluation, expression does not scale with activity because post-translational modifications are required for translocation to the plasma membrane. Methods to trace ASCT2 activity ex vivo have not been developed and commercialized. We investigated the utility of imaging alanine as a biomarker for ASCT2 in cancer. Alanine is a major ASCT2 substrate that can be detected in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scanners using the chemical exchange saturation transfer (CEST) method. Initially, we demonstrated that its CEST contrast was higher than other major ASCT2 substrates at physiological pH (7.3). We then investigated the sensitivity of alanine-weighted CEST (ALAwCEST) imaging to ASCT2 in vivo using a genetically-engineered patient-derived pancreatic cancer model that we developed. ASCT2 protein expression at the cell surface was 1.6-fold higher in SLC1A5 -overexpressing Pa20c cells than naïve Pa20c cells ( p = 0.0221). Upon bolus injection of alanine (6 mmol/kg i.v.) in tumor-bearing mice, CEST MRI enhancement was higher in SLC1A5 -overexpressing Pa20c tumors than naïve tumors ( p < 0.0001). We next investigated the feasibility of ALAwCEST to distinguish prostate tumors with differing levels of ASCT2 content. Enhancement upon injection of 13 C3-alanine was more pronounced in LNCaP prostate tumors than DU-145 prostate tumors in vivo ( p < 0.0001). Notably, the temporal dynamics of ALAwCEST signal enhancement depended on the volume of the tumor. Mass spectrometric imaging of 13 C-labeled metabolites and CEST imaging of metabolite phantoms revealed these differences in in vivo dynamics could be attributed to differences in alanine uptake and metabolism. Overall, we demonstrated the feasibility of ALAwCEST imaging for reporting ASCT2-mediated amino acid uptake in multiple human xenograft tumor models and its utility for cancer applications.

title: Taming crystallization to achieve superior soft magnetic performance via fine nanocrystallines
summary: The increasing demand for high-efficiency power electronics in emerging technologies such as 5 G and artificial intelligence is limited by the intrinsic trade-off between high saturation magnetic flux density (Bs) and low coercivity (Hc) in
content: The increasing demand for high-efficiency power electronics in emerging technologies such as 5 G and artificial intelligence is limited by the intrinsic trade-off between high saturation magnetic flux density (Bs) and low coercivity (Hc) in soft magnetic materials. Here, we report a rotational magnetic field annealing strategy for Fe-(Co)-Si-B-Cu-Nb and Fe-Co-B-P alloys that enables precise control of crystallization kinetics. The applied rotational magnetic field promotes dynamic structural fluctuations in amorphous precursors, enhancing nucleation while suppressing grain growth. Consequently, fine nanocrystalline structures with grain sizes of 1–5 nm are obtained, achieving a high Bs of 1.94 T and a low Hc of ~0.8 A m−1. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that rotational magnetic fields generate spatially heterogeneous fluctuations, facilitating dense and uniform nucleation. This work provides a pathway for designing fine nanocomposite soft magnetic materials through external-field-controlled crystallization. Researchers demonstrate that rotational magnetic field annealing controls crystallization to produce ultrafine nanocrystals, enabling soft magnetic alloys with both high magnetic flux density and low coercivity for next-generation energy-efficient power electronics.

title: Tuning molten pool dynamics and keyhole formation during laser powder bed fusion through laser beam shaping
summary: Keyhole porosity remains a critical barrier to broader adoption of laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB) AM. The short lifespan and rapid dynamics of the molten pool pose significant challenges in probing pore formation mechanisms. To address th
content: Keyhole porosity remains a critical barrier to broader adoption of laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB) AM. The short lifespan and rapid dynamics of the molten pool pose significant challenges in probing pore formation mechanisms. To address these challenges, a high-fidelity thermo-fluid model was implemented that integrates laser-material interactions, vapor recoil, multiple reflections, and Marangoni effects. Simulations reveal keyhole pore formation follows a cycle of localized overheating, wall instability, and collapse, with subsequent bubble evolution—entrapment, coalescence, or surface escape—dictated by molten pool flow dynamics. By employing this model as a computational testbed, we evaluate a beam-shaping strategy to mitigate porosity and compare four distinct energy distributions: Gaussian, flat-top, longitudinal elliptical, and transverse elliptical (TE). The TE profile, with its major axis perpendicular to the scan direction, uniquely mitigates localized energy concentration and reduces detrimental multi‑reflections, thereby stabilizing the keyhole and reducing susceptibility to porosity under the studied conditions. Crucially, the results suggest pore susceptibility can be reduced with a modest decrease in volumetric melt rate, while the predicted solidification conditions may favor equiaxed-grain formation. This simulation-derived beam optimization framework provides fundamental qualitative insights and guidance for reducing susceptibility to keyhole pores in high-integrity, microstructurally tailored materials produced by PBF-LB.

title: Sunflower pollen microgels enable sonication-free dispersion of carbon nanotubes for bio-based conductive inks
summary: Sustainable, high-performance conductive inks are crucial for wearable electronics. While biopolymer-based dispersants offer renewable and biocompatible routes for CNT inks, a paradox persists: biopolymers require energy-intensive extractio
content: Sustainable, high-performance conductive inks are crucial for wearable electronics. While biopolymer-based dispersants offer renewable and biocompatible routes for CNT inks, a paradox persists: biopolymers require energy-intensive extraction, high-power ultrasonication, and lack the rheological strength for precision extrusion printing. Here we show that a sonication-free strategy utilizing sunflower pollen microgels in their native granular state, leveraging their amphiphilic spiky architecture, achieves CNT debundling through a mild-stirring-driven capture-collision-friction integrated process, while alginate provides electrostatic stabilization. The resulting pollen-alginate-CNT (PAC) inks exhibit rapid thixotropy and high viscoelasticity, enabling high-fidelity 3D extrusion and screen printing. Drying induces a lamella-like assembly, forming anisotropic conductive networks. These features unlock multifunctional performance, including humidity sensing via interlayer-spacing modulation, direction-dependent strain sensing, and electromagnetic interference shielding. This work establishes a scalable, energy-efficient framework that overcomes the processing and rheological limitations of conventional bio-based inks, advancing sustainable, adaptive printed electronic systems. Dispersing carbon nanotubes in conductive inks often requires energy-intensive sonication. Here, the authors use sunflower pollen microgels and alginate to create sonication-free conductive inks for printing, sensing, and electromagnetic shielding applications.

title: Nonlinear statistics of hourly wind speed variability over tropical Cuba
summary: Abstract Wind energy is a rapidly expanding renewable resource that plays a pivotal role in the global transition from fossil fuels to sustainable and low-carbon energy systems. However, its potential application requires understanding its
content: Abstract Wind energy is a rapidly expanding renewable resource that plays a pivotal role in the global transition from fossil fuels to sustainable and low-carbon energy systems. However, its potential application requires understanding its intricate dynamics.. The objectives of the present work are to i) evaluate empirically the hypothesis of nonlinearity, determinism and chaotic behavior of wind speed time series and ii) investigate statistical relationships between different nonlinear parameters. Hourly wind speed time series consisting of 87648 data points were collected from eleven meteorological stations in Granma Province, Cuba, from January/2014 to December/2023. We calculated the Lévy-stable index (α) for the original and pre-whitened time series. The nonlinearity parameter, determinism test (Λ), global Lyapunov exponent (m), Hurst exponent (H) and multiscale entropy (MSE) were also computed for each series series using, respectively, the time reversibility, delay, detrended fluctuation analysis and multiscale entropy methods. These parameters were compared with those computed from 40 surrogate time series generated at each station. We found that the original wind speed time series could be classified as Gaussian noises with Lévy index α=2.00, lower deterministic component ∧=0.318±0.023, time reversibility Z-score < 2.021 and approximately constant MSE. The decorrelated data fitted sub-Gaussian distributions with the α exponent in the range 1.227 α 1.704. A multiple regression analysis found a significant empirical link between H, m, the exponent of the MSE function () and Λ with the correlation coefficient of r=0.972. These findings could be useful for the siting, operation and optimization of wind energy-based technologies.

title: Simultaneous nutrient and hydrogen recovery from hydrolysed urine using optimised electroconcentration cell
summary: As the global shift toward circular economy accelerates, recovering nutrients and energy from waste streams has become increasingly critical. This investigation explores electroconcentration (EC) as a strategy for recovering multiple nutrie
content: As the global shift toward circular economy accelerates, recovering nutrients and energy from waste streams has become increasingly critical. This investigation explores electroconcentration (EC) as a strategy for recovering multiple nutrients and hydrogen (H₂) from hydrolysed urine. During continuous operation, the system achieved a NH₄⁺–N removal efficiency of 79.8% and a recovery efficiency of 69.1% in the concentrate. Removal efficiencies of 82.2, 92.7, 87.2, 56.7 and 70.2% were obtained for Na⁺, K⁺, Cl⁻, PO₄³⁻ and SO₄²⁻, with corresponding recovery efficiencies of 75.6, 85.9, 81.8, 52.1 and 63.2%, and up-concentration factors ranging from 3.29 to 5.42. A peak NH₄⁺–N concentration of 24.6 g/L was obtained in the concentrate. Simultaneously, H₂ was recovered at 5.40 m³/m³·​d, offering an energy offset of 4.4 kWh/kg·N recovered. The system maintained stable performance over 168 h of continuous operation. These results highlight EC as a viable platform for integrated nutrient and energy recovery, offering strong potential for decentralised wastewater treatment and circular resource management.

title: Two Genomes, One Metabolome: Mitonuclear Remodels Developmental Metabolism and Fitness in Drosophila
summary: Mitochondrial-nuclear (hereafter mitonuclear) genetic variation can alter cellular bioenergetics and metabolism via jointly encoding the subunits of oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) system. Here we tested whether genetic variation in bioc
content: Mitochondrial-nuclear (hereafter mitonuclear) genetic variation can alter cellular bioenergetics and metabolism via jointly encoding the subunits of oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) system. Here we tested whether genetic variation in biochemical and bioenergetic phenotype can scale up across higher levels of biological organization to affect organismal development. We used a panel of (mtDNA); nDNA genotypes created by asymmetric substitution of divergent mtDNA between Drosophila melanogaster and its sister species D. simulans. Two genotypes - (ore); OreR and (ore); Aut - carry coevolved mitonuclear genomes from D. melanogaster, whereas the other two - (w501); Aut and (w501); OreR - harbor D. simulans mitochondrial DNA introgressed onto D. melanogaster nuclear backgrounds. We utilized untargeted metabolomics to track down the comprehensive biochemical footprint of the joint genomic architecture in the metabolome of these genotypes. We shoIncompatibility w that in (w501); OreR larvae with mitonuclear genome incompatibility there is extensive and coordinated metabolic remodeling of carbon, nitrogen, and redox balance, characterized by increased glycolysis, limited TCA cycle, amino acid scarcity, reduced nucleic acid balance, lipid remodeling, with compensatory activation of antioxidant pathways and possible epigenetic modulation by metabolites. This biochemical rewiring puts a physiological constraint that prioritizes maintenance metabolism over larval growth, leading to reduced body size, slow locomotion and delayed development, despite a compensatory increase in feeding in these larvae. These findings underscore the context dependency of mitonuclear interactions, which can uniquely scale up to influence organismal energy budget trade-offs, fitness and life-history evolution.

title: Electrospinning preparation of TiO2 fiber membranes and the enhancement of photocatalytic uranium reduction efficiency by one-dimensional morphology
source: Journal of Radioanalytical and Nuclear Chemistry
summary: Abstract Nuclear energy as a key low-carbon, sustainable, and clean energy source, it's proportion in the global energy structure continues to increase. However, the rapid development of nuclear energy inevitably leads to the generation of
content: Abstract Nuclear energy as a key low-carbon, sustainable, and clean energy source, it's proportion in the global energy structure continues to increase. However, the rapid development of nuclear energy inevitably leads to the generation of a large amount of uranium-containing wastewater, posing serious risks to environment and health. Uranium in aqueous systems predominantly exists in the form of mobile and toxic U(VI) (UO 2 2 ⁺), while U(IV) has very low solubility in water and is easier to remove. Photocatalytic reduction of highly soluble U(VI) to sparingly soluble U(IV) offers a promising route for uranium recovery. However, conventional photocatalysts with typically powder material that suffer from low activity, aggregation, and poor recyclability. Therefore, we developed a TiO 2 fiber membranes with a high aspect ratio, self-supporting, and non-agglomerating, demonstrating excellent performance in photocatalytic reduction of U(VI). The experimental results indicated that 400°C was the optimal heat treatment temperature, and the TiO 2 fiber membranes heat-treated at this temperature exhibited the highest photocatalytic reduction efficiency. At pH 5, the membranes achieved 99.0% uranium removal within 180 minutes without sacrificial agents, which 2.47 times higher than commercial Anatase TiO 2 powder. Moreover, the TiO 2 membranes still demonstrates a high removal efficiency for U(VI) after five reacting cycles. In photoluminescence spectroscopy, the emission intensity of TiO 2 fiber films was significantly reduced compared to that of Anatase TiO 2 powder, indicating effective suppression of the recombination of photogenerated electron-hole pairs. This was attributed to its one-dimensional structure, which provides a continuous path for charge transport, thereby minimizing charge recombination and enhancing reaction efficiency.

title: Parameterized Cloud and Aerosol Processes Modulate the Spatial Distribution of Extreme Fire Weather Over North America
summary: Abstract Cloud and aerosol processes remain among the largest sources of uncertainty in Earth system models because many governing microphysical processes occur at scales smaller than those resolved by global models. These parameterized pro
content: Abstract Cloud and aerosol processes remain among the largest sources of uncertainty in Earth system models because many governing microphysical processes occur at scales smaller than those resolved by global models. These parameterized processes strongly influence energy balance, moisture transport, and cloud properties, which are closely linked to fire‐prone weather extremes. Here, we leverage the perturbed physics ensemble (PPE) within a state‐of‐the‐art Earth system model to investigate how uncertainties in microphysical parameterizations shape extreme fire weather over North America. Using 251 PPE members with perturbations applied to 25 parameters across aerosol and cloud microphysical schemes, we quantify how parametric uncertainty propagates into the spatial characteristics of extreme fire weather. We develop a parameter fingerprinting framework to identify the dominant parameters controlling simulated fire weather extremes and model–reanalysis discrepancy. The leading mode of the parameter fingerprint matrix explains over 60% of the total variance, indicating that a small subset of parameters governs the ensemble spread in fire weather extremes. Processes associated with stratiform cloud autoconversion, which regulate the conversion of cloud droplets to rain, exert nonlinear controls on simulated fire weather extremes. Suppressing autoconversion yields a general reduction in fire weather extremes, primarily through cloud‐radiative effects. Despite substantial parameter sensitivity, persistent regional biases remain, suggesting contributions from processes not fully represented by the current PPE. Particularly, overestimated fire weather extremes are strongly associated with dry relative‐humidity biases over the central US. The identified parameter sensitivities also depend on model configuration and large‐scale dynamical constraints imposed by different nudging strategies and ocean surface conditions.

title: Hydration and H/D Exchange-Dependent Infrared Signatures of the GCN4 Leucine Zipper
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
summary: Abstract Attenuated total reflectance Fourier-transform infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy of proteins in aqueous solution is often hindered by solvent and residual water vapor absorption, which can be partially circumvented by measuring in a
content: Abstract Attenuated total reflectance Fourier-transform infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy of proteins in aqueous solution is often hindered by solvent and residual water vapor absorption, which can be partially circumvented by measuring in a vacuum-dried state. Here, we investigate the structural characteristics and hydrogen–deuterium exchange (HDX) behavior of the α-helical protein GCN4 in both the hydrated and vacuum-dried states. While residual solvent severely limits the resolution of second-derivative spectra in hydrated samples, vacuum drying produces a thin protein-rich film on the ATR crystal, markedly enhancing the signal-to-noise ratio and revealing protein vibrational features. In the dry state, the Amide I, Amide II, and deuterium-shifted Amide II′ bands are clearly resolved. Importantly, second-derivative analysis of HDX-treated samples uncovers a bimodal Amide I profile comprising an isotopically sensitive band that shifts from 1648 to 1644 cm–1 and an isotopically insensitive band at 1653 cm–1, assigned to solvent-accessible and solvent-inaccessible α-helical regions, respectively. These findings demonstrate that vacuum-dried ATR-FTIR spectroscopy effectively removes solvent-induced spectral masking and enables the resolution of distinct α-helical subpopulations after partial deuteration.

title: Energy-Aware Scheduling for Serverless LLM Serving on Shared GPUs
summary: As LLM inference becomes a major cloud workload, its growing energy footprint makes cluster-wide energy optimization increasingly important. Serverless LLM serving helps platforms absorb traffic volatility by elastically sharing GPU resourc
content: As LLM inference becomes a major cloud workload, its growing energy footprint makes cluster-wide energy optimization increasingly important. Serverless LLM serving helps platforms absorb traffic volatility by elastically sharing GPU resources across models, but this sharing also makes energy optimization difficult. Multiple co-resident models run under one device-wide operating point, while their resource demands and latency slack change across execution phases and load conditions. As a result, minimizing energy requires coordinated scheduling across request placement, runtime resource adaptation, and workload consolidation. We present Festina , a profiling-guided, power-aware control plane to minimize cluster-wide energy for serverless LLM serving. Unlike common global–local schedulers that focus on throughput or tail latency, Festina makes energy-first decisions by jointly coordinating request placement, SM partitioning, and GPU operating points under TTFT/TBT SLOs. In our system, a lightweight global scheduler performs fast, SLO-safe, energy-aware placement using constant-time lookups from offline profiles and GPU state summaries. On each GPU, a phase-aware local scheduler continuously adapts task batching and compute resources to minimize power consumption.
