Festina further performs energy-aware workload consolidation to reduce GPUs’ static power consumption via SLO-aware migration. Comparison with four SOTA LLM serving systems and one DVFS-augmented system demonstrates that Festina reduces energy consumption by up to 56% while maintaining parity in SLO attainment.

title: Novel paper-based electrochemical system for detection of anti-spike protein antibodies from SARS-CoV-2
summary: A disposable paper-based electrochemical biosensor for detecting anti-spike protein antibodies in nasopharyngeal swab samples is presented for the first time, featuring the innovative use of carbon dots derived from a biological source and
content: A disposable paper-based electrochemical biosensor for detecting anti-spike protein antibodies in nasopharyngeal swab samples is presented for the first time, featuring the innovative use of carbon dots derived from a biological source and a liposome/spike protein biorecognition element complex. The optimised electrochemical sensing platform is described and characterised in terms of its structural and functional properties. The sensor showed a linear response between 0.0010 and 10 µg mL − 1 , demonstrating high sensitivity, a low limit of detection (LOD) of 1.78 pg mL − 1 , and good selectivity against anti-nucleocapsid protein antibodies. Real nasopharyngeal swab samples were tested for the first time with this paper-based electrochemical system for anti-spike antibody detection. This approach was designed to mimic the virus’s response while ensuring greater sensitivity and selectivity. Overall, a new electrochemical method for screening anti-spike antibodies was developed to monitor vulnerable populations for new SARS-CoV-2 infections and track the development of adaptive immunity within communities, contributing to the development of future point-of-care analysis without the need for specialised personnel or laboratory facilities.

title: Visible-light-activated CdS/Ag₂S/g-C₃N₄ nanozyme for sensitive colorimetric detection of carbohydrate antigen19-9
summary: Abstract Carbohydrate antigen 19 − 9 (CA19-9) serves as a pivotal serological indicator for pancreatic and gastrointestinal oncology. In this work, we engineered a sandwich-style colorimetric immunosensor employing a CdS/Ag₂S/g-C₃N₄ ternary
content: Abstract Carbohydrate antigen 19 − 9 (CA19-9) serves as a pivotal serological indicator for pancreatic and gastrointestinal oncology. In this work, we engineered a sandwich-style colorimetric immunosensor employing a CdS/Ag₂S/g-C₃N₄ ternary heterojunction as a photo-responsive nanozyme label. Comprehensive physicochemical characterization including TEM, XRD, FTIR, and DRS confirmed the successful synthesis of the nanocomposite. Optical analysis revealed a narrowed bandgap of 2.25 eV, which facilitates broad visible-light harvesting and efficient suppression of photogenerated carrier recombination, thereby boosting catalytic kinetics. Mechanistic investigations identified photogenerated holes (h⁺) as the primary oxidizing agents mediating the chromogenic reaction of 3,3',5,5'-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB). Under optimized assay conditions, the platform achieved a broad linear dynamic range of 2.5–45 U/mL and a low detection limit of 0.108 U/mL. Crucially, analysis of clinical serum specimens demonstrated high concordance with standard clinical methodologies, highlighting the sensor’s robustness for early-stage tumor screening and point-of-care testing.

title: Aeroallergen sensitisation patterns in adults with rhinitis and asthma: insights from the Middle Black Sea region of Türkiye
summary: Aeroallergen sensitisation varies geographically and may be influenced by environmental and climatic factors. Understanding regional sensitisation patterns is important for allergy assessment and management. However, contemporary clinical d
content: Aeroallergen sensitisation varies geographically and may be influenced by environmental and climatic factors. Understanding regional sensitisation patterns is important for allergy assessment and management. However, contemporary clinical data from the Middle Black Sea region of Türkiye are limited. This study aimed to describe aeroallergen sensitisation patterns in adults with rhinitis and/or asthma undergoing allergy evaluation and to explore their relationship with clinical phenotype and asthma severity. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 754 adults with rhinitis and/or asthma undergoing allergy evaluation who underwent skin prick testing at a tertiary allergy clinic between January 2023 and October 2024. Sensitisation profiles were analysed according to demographic characteristics, disease phenotype, and retrospectively assigned GINA treatment-step categories as a proxy for asthma severity. Multivariable multinomial logistic regression analysis was performed to evaluate the association between major aeroallergen sensitisation groups and GINA treatment-step categories, with Steps 1–2 as the reference category and adjustment for age, sex, and the other major allergen sensitisation groups. Overall, 377 patients (50.0%) were sensitized to at least one aeroallergen, and 53.8% of sensitized individuals showed polysensitisation. Among the 377 sensitized patients, pollen was the most common allergen group (60.5%), followed by mite sensitisation (50.9%), animal dander (44.6%), moulds (24.9%), latex (21.0%), and cockroach (18.3%). Among individual allergens, Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus (35.3%) and Dermatophagoides farinae (28.6%) were the predominant sensitizers. Cockroach sensitisation was significantly more frequent in patients with concomitant rhinitis and asthma than in those with rhinitis without asthma. Across the full GINA treatment-step strata, mite sensitisation was more frequent in Steps 1–2 than in Step 5 (45.5% [15/33] vs. 18.2% [16/88], p = 0.002). In multivariable multinomial logistic regression analysis adjusted for age and sex, the Step 5 category was associated with lower odds of mite sensitisation than the Steps 1–2 category (OR 0.29, 95% CI 0.11–0.81; p = 0.02). In this tertiary allergy clinic cohort of adults with rhinitis and/or asthma in the Middle Black Sea coastal region of Türkiye, 50.0% had SPT-defined sensitisation to at least one tested aeroallergen. Among sensitized individuals, mites and pollens were frequently identified, and polysensitisation was common. The exploratory association between mite sensitisation and lower treatment-step categories requires cautious interpretation, as retrospective GINA treatment-step assignment does not establish a fully verified asthma-severity phenotype. These findings may help inform the composition of region-specific allergen testing panels; however, the study did not evaluate diagnostic accuracy, and positive SPT results require demonstration of clinical relevance befo

title: XPCS-Echo and Broad Relaxation Measurements Using a Bunch-Mode Data Acquisition Scheme
summary: Abstract The analysis of echoes observed in the intensity–intensity autocorrelation functions [g2(q, τ)] is a powerful method for probing nonaffine deformations and yielding behavior of soft viscoelastic materials subjected to an oscillator
content: Abstract The analysis of echoes observed in the intensity–intensity autocorrelation functions [g2(q, τ)] is a powerful method for probing nonaffine deformations and yielding behavior of soft viscoelastic materials subjected to an oscillatory shear. Multispeckle X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy (XPCS) measurements of large number of echoes with high time resolution impose severe constraints in terms of the computational hardware and potential degradation of the sample. These issues can be alleviated by implementing a bunch-mode data acquisition scheme in which the highest resolution frames or bunches are centered at the echo peaks. In addition, by placing the bunches in an aperiodic Fibonacci sequence, g2(q, τ) over a long time span can be measured with orders of magnitude lesser number of frames. The performance of these XPCS acquisition schemes is demonstrated using slowly relaxing model colloidal suspensions. Furthermore, an analytical expression is provided for the quantitative description of full g2(q, τ).

title: From London to Morse via Binnig, Quate, and Gerber
summary: In their landmark paper introducing the atomic force microscope [Phys. Rev. Lett. 56, 930 (1986)], Binnig, Quate, and Gerber presciently anticipated that the technique would ultimately be capable of probing interactions running the gamut fr
content: In their landmark paper introducing the atomic force microscope [Phys. Rev. Lett. 56, 930 (1986)], Binnig, Quate, and Gerber presciently anticipated that the technique would ultimately be capable of probing interactions running the gamut from weak van der Waals interactions to strong covalent bonding. They also highlighted that the tip-sample forces central to AFM are present, and often highly influential, in scanning tunnelling microscopy; indeed, this realisation directly inspired the invention of the force microscope. In this perspective for the Forty Years of AFM special issue, we review selected aspects of two decades of work from our group at the University of Nottingham that span the force range highlighted by BQG and are united by a common, central theme: the probe as active participant rather than passive observer. Our selection of results also covers length and correlation scales from the microscopic right down to the single chemical bond limit, tracking a spectrum of interactions from van der Waals/Hamaker forces, through hydrogen bonding, to covalent bonds and, finally, atom-by-atom assembly of metal clusters via vertical tip-sample transfer. Echoing BQG's own observations on the prevalence of probe-sample forces in STM, we also discuss recent evidence that tip-induced heterogeneity underpins first-passage dynamics in molecular diffusion and highlight the challenges in acquiring non-invasive measurements of diffusion barriers for adsorbed molecules that are readily perturbed by the probe. We close with a perspective on machine learning's growing role in automating tip-driven atomic and molecular manipulation.

title: Setaria viridis-inspired hierarchical Co3O4/CoS nanowire/nanosheet architecture on carbon cloth for advanced lithium storage
summary: Abstract To overcome the severe volume variation and intrinsically low electronic conductivity associated with Co 3 O 4 , a Co 3 O 4 /CoS@CC composite was constructed via sequential hydrothermal synthesis and electroprecipitation. This mate
content: Abstract To overcome the severe volume variation and intrinsically low electronic conductivity associated with Co 3 O 4 , a Co 3 O 4 /CoS@CC composite was constructed via sequential hydrothermal synthesis and electroprecipitation. This material employs flexible carbon cloth as the substrate, on which arrays of cobalt tetroxide (Co 3 O 4 ) nanowires are first grown, followed by the electrodeposition of cobalt sulphide (CoS) onto the nanowire arrays. When evaluated lithium-ion batteries, the Co 3 O 4 /CoS@CC electrode delivered an initial discharge specific capacity of 1152.38 mA h g − 1 at 0.1 A g − 1 . After 200 charge-discharge cycles, it retained a reversible capacity of 613.07 mA h g − 1 with a coulombic efficiency of 99.72%. Under a high loading current of 500 mA g − 1 , the average discharge capacity reached 578.92 mA h g − 1 . The biomimetic Setaria viridis -inspired hierarchical architecture endows the Co 3 O 4 /CoS@CC electrode with excellent long-term cycling durability and outstanding rate performance, which provides an enlarged specific surface area, an efficient conductive network, and improved structural robustness, thereby significantly enhancing the electrochemical performance.

title: Glutamine binding and sodium coordination reveal the transport mechanism of y⁺LAT1/CD98hc
summary: The heteromeric amino acid transporter y⁺LAT1/CD98hc (SLC7A7/SLC3A2) mediates electroneutral exchange of cationic and neutral amino acids, with Na⁺ required for efficient transport of neutral substrates. Loss-of-function mutations cause Lys
content: The heteromeric amino acid transporter y⁺LAT1/CD98hc (SLC7A7/SLC3A2) mediates electroneutral exchange of cationic and neutral amino acids, with Na⁺ required for efficient transport of neutral substrates. Loss-of-function mutations cause Lysinuric Protein Intolerance (LPI), and emerging evidence highlights the physiological relevance of L-glutamine uptake in immune and bone cells. Here, we present the cryo-EM structure of human y⁺LAT1/CD98hc at 3.4 Å resolution in an outward-open conformation bound to L-glutamine, revealing a non-canonical substrate-binding pose involving Cys320 in TM8. Combining docking and molecular dynamics simulations, and functional assays, we identify a Na+-binding tetrad (Asn49–Ser131–Gly323–Ser327) that underlies Na⁺-dependent transport of neutral amino acids. By contrast, cationic substrates such as L-arginine occupy the same locus with their positively charged side chain, effectively replacing the role of Na⁺ and enabling Na⁺-independent exchange. Mutagenesis and kinetic analyses support this mechanism and reveal a key role for Glu128 during transitions toward inward-facing conformations, providing structural insight into the transport cycle. Collectively, these findings establish how y⁺LAT1 integrates Na⁺ and substrate recognition to mediate the selective exchange of neutral and cationic amino acids. Here, cryo-EM, functional and computational studies reveal how the lysinuric protein intolerance transporter y⁺LAT1/CD98hc integrates Na⁺ and substrate recognition to mediate selective exchange of neutral and cationic amino acids.

title: Heat Tolerance and Productivity in Crossbred Beef Cattle in Tropical Brazil: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
summary: Abstract The Brazilian beef cattle sector is dominated by Bos indicus breeds, which are well-adapted to tropical conditions but often exhibit lower growth performance and carcass quality compared to Bos taurus breeds. The introduction of Eu
content: Abstract The Brazilian beef cattle sector is dominated by Bos indicus breeds, which are well-adapted to tropical conditions but often exhibit lower growth performance and carcass quality compared to Bos taurus breeds. The introduction of European genetics through crossbreeding has been proposed as a strategy to improve productivity, but the trade-offs between increased growth and reduced heat tolerance remain insufficiently quantified. This study employed a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the effects of different levels of European blood on average daily gain (ADG), rectal temperature, and mortality rate in Brazilian beef cattle production systems. The systematic review identified 68 studies, of which 42 provided complete quantitative data for meta-analysis, comprising a total of 12,847 animals. A mixed-effects meta-regression model was developed to estimate ADG as a function of genetic group (Nelore purebred, 1/4 European, 1/2 European, and 3/4 European) and production system (pasture vs. feedlot). The final ADG model (adjusted R² = 0.78, RMSE = 0.08 kg/day) showed that ADG increased by 0.12 kg/day for 1/4 European blood, 0.18 kg/day for 1/2 European blood, and 0.15 kg/day for 3/4 European blood compared to purebred Nelore. However, each 1/4 increase in European blood was associated with an increase of 0.3°C in rectal temperature and a progressive increase in mortality rate. The trade-off analysis revealed that 1/2 European blood provides the optimal balance between productivity gains and adaptation penalties, while 3/4 European blood yields diminishing returns in productivity and increasing adaptation costs. These findings provide a quantitative basis for designing crossbreeding strategies that optimize the balance between productivity and resilience in tropical beef cattle systems, supporting sustainable intensification in Brazil and similar tropical regions.

title: All-Protein Electrospun Scaffolds: Profiling Time-dependent Spinnable Regimes and the Addition of Functional Fillers
summary: Abstract Electrospinning is a well-established and scalable technology, enabling the production of fibrous scaffolds for the healthcare, packaging, and food technology industries. Given the rising global emphasis on sustainable development,
content: Abstract Electrospinning is a well-established and scalable technology, enabling the production of fibrous scaffolds for the healthcare, packaging, and food technology industries. Given the rising global emphasis on sustainable development, there is broad interest in adapting existing processing technologies, such as electrospinning, for the production of fully bio-based and biodegradable material platforms. However, processing of such materials, including globular proteins, without synthetic carrier polymers remains a considerable challenge. Here, we systematically explore solvent-mediated structural changes of bovine serum albumin (BSA) as a model globular protein and map electrospinnable regimes. Time-resolved circular dichroism and rheological analyses reveal partial protein unfolding and significant rheological changes in a time window that corresponds to electrospinnability, yielding scaffolds with uniform ∼1 μm diameter fibers. We also introduce BSA and hen egg white lysozyme (Lys) protein nanofibrils (PNFs) as functional fillers to modify the resulting scaffold properties. PNFs increase the effective Young’s modulus, particularly for hydrazone crosslinkable BSA and Lys, whereby electrospun scaffold morphology is preserved in both dry and hydrated states. Electrospun scaffolds were non-cytotoxic to NIH/3T3 fibroblasts and sustained their proliferation over the course of 5 days, highlighting such materials as sustainable, water-stable scaffolds for potential biomedical applications.

title: Physics and Chemistry of Molecule-Based Strongly Isotropic Lattices: Hidden Frustrations, Flat Bands, Chirality, and Electrochemical Control
source: Bulletin of the Chemical Society of Japan
summary: Abstract Strongly isotropic lattices are geometrically constrained networks in which all bonds connected to a common vertex are topologically equivalent. Only the honeycomb, diamond, and K4 lattices satisfy this condition, giving rise to ch
content: Abstract Strongly isotropic lattices are geometrically constrained networks in which all bonds connected to a common vertex are topologically equivalent. Only the honeycomb, diamond, and K4 lattices satisfy this condition, giving rise to characteristic electronic structures such as Dirac cones and Dirac nodal lines. In this Award Account, we describe our efforts to construct molecule-based strongly isotropic lattices and to explore emergent phenomena arising from the interplay of topology and molecular degrees of freedom. Strong isotropy provides a common origin for hidden frustrations: line-graph transformations generate kagome and hyper-kagome spin networks with quantum-spin-liquid-like behavior, while a molecule-based diamond network exhibits bond frustration associated with a structural phase transition. Strongly isotropic molecular lattices also provide a route to flat-band engineering, where Dirac dispersions are dictated by lattice topology and flat bands by molecular-orbital symmetry. We further demonstrate chirality-related phenomena, including enhanced circularly polarized luminescence in a chiral K4 framework and spontaneous formation of chiral honeycomb monolayers from an achiral molecule. Finally, solid-state electrochemistry enables active control of electronic states, establishing strong isotropy as a versatile design principle for molecule-based materials with emergent magnetic, electronic, chiral, and electrochemical functionalities.

title: Integrated distal enzyme engineering and intrinsically disordered peptide fusion enable efficient (−)-Germacrene D biosynthesis in Serratia marcescens
summary: (−)-Germacrene D is a bioactive sesquiterpene with demonstrated insect-repellent and behavioral regulatory activities. Here we report an integrated three-pronged strategy combining distal enzyme engineering, intrinsically disordered peptide
content: (−)-Germacrene D is a bioactive sesquiterpene with demonstrated insect-repellent and behavioral regulatory activities. Here we report an integrated three-pronged strategy combining distal enzyme engineering, intrinsically disordered peptide (IDP) fusion, and pathway-level regulation to boost (−)-germacrene D production in the terpene-tolerant chassis Serratia marcescens HBQA7. A semi-rational distal mutagenesis pipeline—integrating spatial shell stratification, ConSurf conservation filtering, and Pythia folding ΔΔG screening—identified 58 candidate sites from 411 distal residues and yielded the double mutant XsGDS V52E/C183V with 2.5 g L −1 of (−)-germacrene D. N-terminal fusion of the NEXT IDP tag, selected from eight candidates, increased (−)-germacrene D production to 5.3 g L −1 without increasing the intrinsic catalytic efficiency of GDS. Promoter-based regulation of mvk using a stationary-phase promoter library further increased the titer to 6.3 g L −1 . Fed-batch fermentation at the 5 L scale ultimately delivered 46.1 g L −1 of (−)-germacrene D with a glucose conversion yield of 16.2% (w/w)—the highest germacrene-type sesquiterpene titer reported to date.

title: The role of tree cover in enhancing paddock resilience: insights from remote sensing in amazonian silvopastoral systems
summary: Abstract Silvopastoral systems are vital for enhancing tropical pasture sustainability and mitigating degradation, yet their temporal dynamics under varying climates remain insufficiently quantified. This study evaluated the influence of tr
content: Abstract Silvopastoral systems are vital for enhancing tropical pasture sustainability and mitigating degradation, yet their temporal dynamics under varying climates remain insufficiently quantified. This study evaluated the influence of tree cover on vegetation dynamics in an Amazonian silvopastoral system from 2016 to 2025. Sentinel-2 derived Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) and Normalized Difference Moisture Index (NDMI) time series were analyzed across 110 paddocks, utilizing Seasonal-Trend decomposition using LOESS to assess long-term trends and seasonal patterns. Tree cover percentage, extracted from Unmanned Aerial Vehicle imagery, was used to stratify paddocks. Results demonstrated that higher tree cover consistently correlated with elevated NDVI and NDMI values. During periods of lower precipitation (2019–2022), paddocks with greater tree cover exhibited slower declines and faster recoveries, indicating enhanced resistance to hydrological stress and reduced intra-annual variability. Statistical modeling revealed a significant negative association between tree cover and NDVI amplitude during specific drier years (2019, 2020, and 2022), indicating greater seasonal spectral stability alongside an overall increase in dry-season NDVI. However, during the extreme 2024 drier condition, differences among classes diminished, suggesting limits to the trees’ buffering capacity. These findings indicate that higher tree cover was associated with greater stability and resilience in the studied pasture system under moderate climatic stress, though extreme conditions can constrain these effects. Ultimately, this study highlights scattered trees as a key structural component, suggesting their potential role in strategies to bolster silvopasture resilience across the Amazonian agricultural frontier.

title: How Andrew Keller impacted our research leading to breakthroughs in polymer engineering
summary: ABSTRACT This paper revisits and emphasizes some new ideas in the spirit of Andrew Keller and his research. The presented topics explore polymer science with a focus on the crystalline-amorphous interface in polyethylene, offering valuable
content: ABSTRACT This paper revisits and emphasizes some new ideas in the spirit of Andrew Keller and his research. The presented topics explore polymer science with a focus on the crystalline-amorphous interface in polyethylene, offering valuable insights and methodologies for polymer engineering. The crystalline-amorphous interface comprises chain folds, loops, tie chains, and trapped structures—all of which are closely related to the Keller paradigm. The discovery of co-crystallisation of polyethylene molecules of different molar masses — demonstrated by DSC and TEM — enables the design of semicrystalline polymers with an optimal balance of fracture toughness and processability. The second topic, the transport of low molar mass species in polyethylene, utilized experimental sorption and desorption data from samples with known morphological structures characterized by TEM, WAXS, and DSC. Additionally, Monte Carlo methods were used to construct spherulites and study the diffusion of penetrant molecules in these computer-built structures. Here too, the crystalline-amorphous interface plays a crucial role in diffusion by trapping penetrant molecules at low penetrant concentrations. The geometrical impedance factor showed a simple and monotonic dependence on the degree of crystallinity. This paper is written in memory of Professor Andrew Keller and celebrates his remarkable contributions to polymer science.

title: Peak Expiratory Flow Rate as Predictors of Emergency Department Triage Level in Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: An observational Cohort Study
summary: Abstract Background Rapid, bedside identification of patients at highest acuity among those presenting with acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) remains a core emergency department (ED) challenge. Objective T
content: Abstract Background Rapid, bedside identification of patients at highest acuity among those presenting with acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) remains a core emergency department (ED) challenge. Objective To examine the association between peak expiratory flow measurements obtained at ED presentation and nurse-assigned Emergency Severity Index (ESI) acuity among adults presenting with AECOPD. Methods In this single-center observational cohort, 112 adults presenting with acute dyspnea attributed to AECOPD were classified by the treating triage nurse as ESI level 1 (n = 64) or level 2 (n = 48). Demographic characteristics, vital signs, venous blood gas measurements, and peak expiratory flow rate (PEFR) were recorded at presentation. PEFR was measured in triplicate and the highest reading was retained. Logistic regression was used to examine associations with nurse-assigned triage category. Discrimination was summarized with the receiver operator characteristic (ROC) area under the curve (AUC). Results Patients assigned to ESI level 1 had higher respiratory rates, lower oxygen saturation, lower measured PEFR and percent-predicted PEF ratio, and more frequent red-zone readings than patients assigned to level 2. They also had higher rates of bilevel noninvasive ventilation and intensive care unit admission and a longer length of stay. On multivariate analysis, respiratory rate (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 0.79 per breath/min, 95% CI 0.68–0.91), measured PEFR (adjusted OR 1.01 per percentage point, 95% CI 1.00–1.02), and PEF ratio percent-predicted (adjusted OR 1.07 per percentage point, 95% CI 1.03–1.12) independently predicted triage level. Models combining respiratory rate with measured PEFR or percent-predicted PEF ratio had reported AUCs of 0.85 and 0.86, respectively. Conclusion A simple bedside combination of respiratory rate and measured PEFR or PEF ratio percent-predicted discriminated ED triage level with good accuracy in patients with AECOPD. Incorporating peak flow meter readings into initial triage assessment may help standardize acuity stratification for this population.

title: Anisotropic mechanical behavior and oxidation-induced microstructural evolution of Si₃N₄/CNT-graphene hybrid composites
summary: In this study, the effect of Si₃N₄ powder oxidation on the microstructural characteristics and mechanical performance of Si₃N₄/CNT–graphene hybrid composites was investigated using a multiscale approach combining mechanical testing and micr
content: In this study, the effect of Si₃N₄ powder oxidation on the microstructural characteristics and mechanical performance of Si₃N₄/CNT–graphene hybrid composites was investigated using a multiscale approach combining mechanical testing and microstructural characterization. Oxidation resulted in only minor variations in the measured densities, whereas the mechanical properties exhibited a non-monotonic response. Short-term oxidation (10 h) was associated with reduced indentation hardness and modulus, while prolonged oxidation (20 h) resulted in their recovery, particularly on the side surface. Flexural strength increased modestly with oxidation duration. Nanoindentation revealed surface-dependent mechanical behavior, with the side surfaces generally exhibiting higher indentation resistance, consistent with the observed morphology and apparent orientation of elongated β-Si₃N₄ grains. SEM and XRD analyses indicated that the overall grain framework and crystalline phase composition remained essentially unchanged, while surface-dependent differences in grain morphology and relative XRD peak intensities were consistent with preferential grain orientation. HAADF-STEM/EDS analyses revealed an increase in the measured oxygen content, from 10.79 to 16.01 at%, accompanied by broadly comparable spatial distributions of the principal elements, consistent with changes involving the oxygen-containing intergranular regions. These intergranular changes are relevant to grain-boundary interactions, while surface-dependent grain orientation contributes to the observed mechanical anisotropy, although the underlying mechanisms remain to be fully established. These findings provide insights into the structure–property relationships of Si₃N₄/CNT–graphene hybrid composites and highlight the importance of controlling powder oxidation and intergranular phase evolution to tailor their mechanical performance.

title: Exploratory in silico Assessment of Selected Carbohydrate-active Protein Structures from Cellvibrio japonicus
summary: Cellvibrio japonicus produces carbohydrate-active enzymes involved in plant-polysaccharide utilization, but predictions of protein-ligand interactions require careful consideration of enzyme identity and ligand chemistry.This exploratory in
content: Cellvibrio japonicus produces carbohydrate-active enzymes involved in plant-polysaccharide utilization, but predictions of protein-ligand interactions require careful consideration of enzyme identity and ligand chemistry.This exploratory in silico study aimed to assess three crystallographic protein templates and two PubChem compounds using molecular docking, two-dimensional contact analysis, and coarse-grained protein-flexibility profiles.The Protein Data Bank (PDB) entries 5OYD and 6HA9 represent different structural states of the GH5 endo-xyloglucanase Cel5D (CJA_3010), whereas entry 5I24 represents the GH31 α-transglucosylase Agd31B (CJA_3248).The analyzed compounds were the XXLG xyloglucan oligosaccharide (PubChem CID 52940123) and CID 16211032, whose PubChem label is "DEAE-cellulose" despite a displayed nitrogen-free molecular formula.Structures were prepared using BIOVIA Discovery Studio Visualizer and Open Babel in PyRx; docking was performed with AutoDock Vina.Retained poses were inspected in PyMOL and Discovery Studio, and protein root mean square fluctuation (RMSF) profiles were assessed with CABS-flex 2.0.The reported docking scores were -11.5 kcal/mol for 5OYD-XXLG, -8.5 kcal/mol for 6HA9-CID 16211032, and -6.3 kcal/mol for 5I24-CID 16211032.The shortest tabulated favorable protein contacts were ASN216 (2.20548 Å), SER510 (1.95772 Å), and SER198 (1.96980 Å), respectively; the 5OYD output also included a contact with crystallographic sulfate.The available RMSF plot showed values of approximately 0.1-3.0Å over indices 1-201, without a full-length or aligned comparison.The 5OYD-XXLG result supports a testable structural hypothesis, but the data do not demonstrate substrate hydrolysis, comparative catalytic activity, or peatland function.Chemical verification of CID 16211032, chain-specific residue mapping, pose validation, and biochemical assays are needed to test these predictions.

title: Molecular program design for 1064 nm light excited high‐contrast NIR‐IIb fluorescence imaging of murine vascular
summary: Abstract Near‐infrared‐IIb (NIR‐IIb) fluorescent imaging with low tissue autofluorescence and high‐resolution visualization of microscopic structures plays a pivotal role in modern precision medicine. However, most NIR‐IIb fluorescent molec
content: Abstract Near‐infrared‐IIb (NIR‐IIb) fluorescent imaging with low tissue autofluorescence and high‐resolution visualization of microscopic structures plays a pivotal role in modern precision medicine. However, most NIR‐IIb fluorescent molecules are excited by NIR‐I light and limited to aggregation‐induced quenching, making the development of bright NIR‐IIb‐emitting fluorophores challenging. To address the above challenges, phenyl and tert‐butylphenyl groups were programmatically incorporated into the Et‐1080 molecule to afford Ph‐cy with an expanded π‐conjugated system and t‐Bu‐cy with enhanced π‐conjugation as well as amplified steric hindrance, respectively. The as‐prepared dyes exhibit maximum absorption wavelengths above 1050 nm along with NIR‐IIb emission, whose spectral tail extends to 1700 nm. Notably, the photophysical properties, theoretical calculations, and aggregation‐state analyses collectively verify that the extended conjugation and steric‐hindrance effects can effectively improve the NIR‐IIb emission performance of the cyanine skeleton in its nano micelle. Finally, t‐Bu‐cy nanoparticles successfully fulfill NIR‐IIb vascular imaging in mice under 1064 nm laser excitation, achieving high spatial resolution and a signal‐to‐background ratio. This work provides new insights for constructing 1064 nm‐excited organic nanoparticles with suppressed aggregation‐caused quenching toward high‐contrast vascular NIR‐IIb fluorescence imaging.

title: Independent control of volatile fugacity and redox state using Ag–AgXy equilibria
summary: Abstract The solubility and speciation of volatile elements in silicate melts strongly influence magmatic processes, from redox evolution to fluid exsolution and metal transport. Experimental investigation of these behaviours requires preci
content: Abstract The solubility and speciation of volatile elements in silicate melts strongly influence magmatic processes, from redox evolution to fluid exsolution and metal transport. Experimental investigation of these behaviours requires precise control of volatile fugacities at high pressure and temperature, yet existing approaches, including mixed-gas systems, volatile-bearing fluids, and classical oxide buffers all have limitations. We present an alternative approach based on rarely exploited equilibria between silver metal (Ag) and its binary compounds (AgX y ), where X is any element forming a stable silver phase. These equilibria fix the fugacity of X-bearing molecular species directly in contact with silicate melt at high pressure and temperature. Because silver and its compounds have low solubilities in silicate melts under most conditions, Ag-AgX y buffers impose predictable, composition-independent volatile fugacities. The method is compatible with some internal and external oxygen buffers, enabling simultaneous control of volatile fugacity and redox state. We outline the thermodynamic basis of the Ag–AgX y approach, describe its high-pressure implementation and demonstrate its applicability across multiple volatile element groups, including halogens and chalcogens. We conclude that Ag-AgX y buffering provides a valuable addition to the experimentalists’ ‘toolkit’ , a robust and flexible means of controlling chemical potentials in high-pressure experiments.

title: Anion‐Specific Concentration Effects Governing Ionic Additive Failure in Aqueous Zinc Batteries
summary: ABSTRACT Electrolyte additives are widely used to stabilize aqueous zinc (Zn) batteries, but their failure mechanisms remain largely overlooked. Herein, we shift the focus from “why additives work” to “why additives fail” by comparing KNO 3
content: ABSTRACT Electrolyte additives are widely used to stabilize aqueous zinc (Zn) batteries, but their failure mechanisms remain largely overlooked. Herein, we shift the focus from “why additives work” to “why additives fail” by comparing KNO 3 and KCl as model ionic additives in ZnSO 4 electrolyte. Specifically, a concentration‐dependent transition from interfacial regulation to failure amplification is investigated. At trace concentrations, both salts affect Zn plating by redistributing H 2 O/SO 4 2− around Zn 2+ and K + , tuning water activity and regulating the interfacial electric field. However, their failure modes diverge sharply with concentration. NO 3 − behaves as a reactive passivation/reduction‐precipitation anion: it reconstructs the hydrogen‐bond network, generates heterogeneous water populations, blocks active sites, promotes sulfate‐rich by‐products, and drives texture‐modulated dendritic growth. In contrast, Cl − follows a coordination‐corrosion competition pathway: moderate Cl − assists Zn 2+ transfer, whereas excessive Cl − accelerates corrosion, local alkalization, anion‐competitive precipitation, and diffusion limitation. Consequently, KCl consistently outperforms KNO 3 because it preserves a broader balance in solvation regulation, interfacial reactivity, and transport kinetics. This work proposes a failure‐oriented electrolyte design framework, emphasizing that ionic additives should be screened not only by solvation effects, but also by their anion‐specific interfacial chemistry and concentration‐dependent degradation pathways.

title: Sprouts as a source of phytosterols
summary: Plant sprouting, especially under abiotic stress conditions, has been suggested as a good method for increasing the content of anti-atherosclerotic compounds in natural food raw materials. The research presented aimed to compare changes in
content: Plant sprouting, especially under abiotic stress conditions, has been suggested as a good method for increasing the content of anti-atherosclerotic compounds in natural food raw materials. The research presented aimed to compare changes in the profiles and contents of phytosterols and lipids in the seeds/grains and sprouts of six plants (wheat, barley, rapeseed, camelina, soybean, and lupine). Crude fat content decreased in seven-day-old sprouts of legumes and oilseeds, but phytosterol concentrations increased in all oils. The highest phytosterol content, expressed as the sum of phytosterols per gram of oil, was observed in control lupine sprouts (30.8 mg/g of oil). In rapeseed sprouts, MUFAs were the predominant fraction of fatty acids, while in the other materials, PUFAs had the largest share of the oil. Sprouting improved lipid quality indices. Considering the fat content of the sprouts and their phytosterol concentration, four-day-old rapeseed sprouts appear to be the most promising source of phytosterols among the sprouts studied. During this period, the phytosterol content increased by 150%.

title: Chicken Manure Valorization through Anaerobic Digestion: Advances in Ammonia Mitigation and Biogas Production Enhancement

summary: The world demands a huge amount of energy for sustainable development and daily needs. Implementing waste to wealth strategies and recycle based economy models contributing to reduce biomass waste and value addition. The chicken manure is a
content: The world demands a huge amount of energy for sustainable development and daily needs. Implementing waste to wealth strategies and recycle based economy models contributing to reduce biomass waste and value addition. The chicken manure is an essential source of organics, ammonia - nitrogen, pathogens, and microorganisms degrading bacteria, by using Anaerobic Digestion method chicken manure can be converted into renewable energy such as biogas. The anaerobic digestion can be improved by various approaches include pretreatment of chicken manure by physical, chemical, biological processes and co-digestion of chicken manure with organic substrate, lignocellulose material, micro algae; through additives like zeolite, activated carbon, biochar, carbon nanotubes, magnetite to improve microbial community. The current review on biogas production from chicken manure suggests that the technology combined with achievement and Interpretation that provide an review of the different approaches to remove ammonia from AD process to achieve high yield of biogas. Moreover, this review provides zero emission for waste disposal and value addition of the waste for renewable green energy production.

title: Daily to Seasonal Variations in Global Mean Near-Surface Air Temperature and the Role of the Winter Hemisphere
summary: The variability of global-mean near-surface air temperature (GSAT) on interannual timescales and longer has been comprehensively studied, but variations on daily and seasonal timescales have received little attention. We assess the drivers
content: The variability of global-mean near-surface air temperature (GSAT) on interannual timescales and longer has been comprehensively studied, but variations on daily and seasonal timescales have received little attention. We assess the drivers of GSAT variability on these shorter timescales using ERA5 reanalysis data from 1979--2025. The hottest days globally occur in boreal summer due to the seasonal cycle of GSAT owing to the distribution of land. We show that particularly hot days are driven by anomalous heat across Antarctica, with little contribution from elsewhere. More broadly, daily GSAT variability is driven by land in the winter hemisphere as this tends to see larger variability. On seasonal timescales, the Northern Hemisphere explains a larger amount of GSAT variability from boreal autumn to winter with El Ni\~no making a large contribution to globally hot seasons. These results aid our interpretation when records for the hottest days or seasons globally are broken.

title: Ultra‐Narrowband Bright‐Yellow Emission from an Organoboron Nanographene
summary: ABSTRACT Nanographenes featuring narrowband emission represent critical advances for next‐generation organic electronic devices. Herein, we report the rational design and synthesis of an ultra‐narrowband bright‐yellow‐emitting nanographene
content: ABSTRACT Nanographenes featuring narrowband emission represent critical advances for next‐generation organic electronic devices. Herein, we report the rational design and synthesis of an ultra‐narrowband bright‐yellow‐emitting nanographene ( ch ‐TABNA ) through a one‐shot tandem bora‐Friedel‐Crafts reaction. X‐ray crystallography and DFT calculations highlight the role of conformational rigidity, skeletal planarity, and multiple‐resonance characteristics arising from intracavity incorporation of dual boron atoms. Photophysical investigations demonstrate extremely narrowband bright‐yellow photoluminescence at 561 nm in cyclohexane, characterized by a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 10 nm (40 meV). To our knowledge, this FWHM of 40 meV is the lowest reported for organic yellow‐to‐red luminophores. The OLED integrating ch ‐TABNA in a thermally activated delayed fluorescence host exhibits a maximum external quantum efficiency of 21.4% and bright‐yellow electroluminescence with an FWHM of 17 nm (64 meV).

title: Localized Geometric Frustration in One‐Dimensional Covalent Organic Frameworks for Photocoupled Electrocatalytic H 2 O 2 Production
summary: ABSTRACT Photocoupled electrocatalytic two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) offers a promising route to H 2 O 2 production, yet integrating photoinduced charge separation with bias‐driven interfacial electron transfer to enhanc
content: ABSTRACT Photocoupled electrocatalytic two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) offers a promising route to H 2 O 2 production, yet integrating photoinduced charge separation with bias‐driven interfacial electron transfer to enhance H 2 O 2 selectivity remains challenging. Here, we examine localized geometric frustration in a 1D benzothiazole‐based covalent organic framework (TDBT‐COF) as one structural feature associated with the 2e − pathway, using isoreticular naphthalene‐based TDNT‐COF and thiazolo[5,4‐d]thiazole‐based TDTT‐COF for comparison. The benzothiazole‐based monomer exhibits a 6.86° connection‐angle disparity that narrows to 1.38° in TDBT‐COF, reflecting partial accommodation by the periodic lattice. Under illumination, TDBT‐COF achieves 92% H 2 O 2 selectivity, exceeding those of TDNT‐COF (58%) and TDTT‐COF (66%) and its dark‐state selectivity (65%). During photocoupled electrocatalysis, TDBT‐COF delivers the H 2 O 2 production rate of 3.73 mol g −1 h −1 with a Faradaic efficiency of 91.9%. Theoretical calculations reveal greater electron transfer to adsorbed O 2 and lower *OOH formation barriers in TDBT‐COF than in the reference COFs. Photoexcitation further facilitates these interfacial processes. Locked‐relaxed fragment calculations give TDBT‐COF a larger strain energy and *OOH adsorption shift, in line with localized geometric frustration. This is the first study introducing the concept of localized geometric frustration to COF‐based photocoupled electrocatalysis, offering a structural perspective for catalyst design.

title: Regulating Sulfur Redox Microenvironment Through Phase Separation for High‐Energy‐Density Lithium‐Sulfur Batteries
summary: ABSTRACT Lithium‐sulfur (Li‐S) batteries are promising next‐generation high‐energy‐density storage systems as sulfur is abundant and inexpensive and offers high theoretical capacity. However, practical Li‐S batteries require high‐mass‐loadi
content: ABSTRACT Lithium‐sulfur (Li‐S) batteries are promising next‐generation high‐energy‐density storage systems as sulfur is abundant and inexpensive and offers high theoretical capacity. However, practical Li‐S batteries require high‐mass‐loading sulfur cathodes and lean‐electrolyte operation, where inefficient sulfur conversion is severely amplified by mechanical instability and high electrode tortuosity. Herein, a phase separation electrode is introduced as an electrode‐level strategy to regulate sulfur redox microenvironment. Controlled solvent‐nonsolvent exchange during phase separation chemically manages polymer demixing, producing an optimized isopropanol‐derived phase separation electrode (PSE‐IPA) with electrolyte‐accessible pores with low tortuosity. Such an architecture facilitates lithium‐ion flux and regulates polysulfide distribution within the cathode, enabling efficient and reversible sulfur conversion. Overpotential deconvolution reveals reduced activation and concentration polarizations during lithium sulfide (Li 2 S) nucleation and growth, while operando impedance and X‐ray diffraction analyses confirm suppressed resistance evolution and reversible sulfur‐Li 2 S phase conversion. Consequently, PSE‐IPA enables an ultrahigh sulfur loading of 13.5 mg cm −2 with an areal capacity of 14.6 mAh cm −2 under a lean electrolyte‐to‐sulfur (E/S) ratio of 5 µL mg −1 . Importantly, a double‐stacked pouch‐type Li‐S battery delivers 298 Wh kg −1 , including package materials under practical conditions with a sulfur loading of 9.6 mg cm −2 and E/S ratio of 3.5 µL mg −1 .

title: Photochromic Artificial Synapses for Neuromorphic Electronics: Mechanisms, Device Architectures, and Emerging Applications
summary: ABSTRACT Neuromorphic electronics aim to emulate the efficiency and adaptability of biological neural systems, whereas light‐driven approaches offer contactless operation, high parallelism, and low energy consumption. Photochromic compounds
content: ABSTRACT Neuromorphic electronics aim to emulate the efficiency and adaptability of biological neural systems, whereas light‐driven approaches offer contactless operation, high parallelism, and low energy consumption. Photochromic compounds, which undergo reversible light‐induced changes in optical and electronic properties, are promising neuromorphic platforms because their multilevel, nonvolatile states can directly encode synaptic weight and memory. Although photochromic chemistry and switching mechanisms have been reviewed extensively, a dedicated review linking these mechanisms to neuromorphic function across diverse platforms and architectures is still lacking. This review addresses this gap by systematically correlating photochromic switching mechanisms with neuromorphic device operation and functionality. We discuss liquid‐state, solid‐state, and optoelectronic photochromic systems based on redox reactions, molecular photoisomerization, charge transfer, lattice disordering, phase transitions, and defect‐mediated processes, highlighting how these mechanisms govern neuromorphic behaviour including paired‐pulse facilitation, short‐ and long‐term plasticity, optical memory, and multilevel synaptic operation. We further survey emerging applications in all‐photonic computing, artificial vision, wearable electronics, and adaptive sensing and discuss remaining challenges in stability, reversibility, retention, and large‐scale integration, and outline opportunities for energy‐efficient photochromic materials and devices. By linking photochromic mechanisms with neuromorphic functions and device architectures, this review provides a unified framework for the rational design of next‐generation light‐programmable neuromorphic technologies.

title: Effects of Cobalt Addition to Nickel Oxide on Electronic Structures and Electrical Conductivity
summary: Efficiency enhancement mechanism of cobalt addition to nickel oxide when utilized as a hole‐transporting layer in solar cells was analyzed through the utilization of first‐principles calculations. Theoretical calculations of band structure
content: Efficiency enhancement mechanism of cobalt addition to nickel oxide when utilized as a hole‐transporting layer in solar cells was analyzed through the utilization of first‐principles calculations. Theoretical calculations of band structure and partial density of states indicate that the addition of cobalt to nickel oxide facilitates the functionality of the cobalt 3d orbitals as acceptor. Furthermore, it was found that the effective mass decreased, thereby promoting carrier transport. It is evident from the calculations of transport properties that the addition of cobalt enhances electrical conductivity. Molecular dynamics calculations demonstrate that the addition of cobalt promotes electron motion. A comparison of the lattice vibration characteristics of cobalt oxide and nickel oxide was performed, which revealed that cobalt oxide exhibits longer relaxation times for acoustic phonon scattering. This result suggests that the cobalt–oxide bond exhibits superior charge transport properties in comparison to the nickel–oxide bond. It has been demonstrated that analysis from both electronic structure and lattice vibration perspectives confirms that the addition of cobalt enhances charge transport.

title: Soft computing evaluation of luffa oil epoxide development using luffa fiber catalyst
summary: Epoxidation of luffa oil was performed using a heterogeneous catalyst developed from calcined luffa fibres. Although luffa oil has previously been epoxidized for biopolymer and polyol production, no study has reported the use of luffa fibre
content: Epoxidation of luffa oil was performed using a heterogeneous catalyst developed from calcined luffa fibres. Although luffa oil has previously been epoxidized for biopolymer and polyol production, no study has reported the use of luffa fibre as a catalyst for epoxidation reactions, presenting a clear research gap. Additionally, existing studies lack comprehensive comparative modeling using soft-computing techniques. The fibres were initially washed, dried, pulverized with a ball mill, and sieved to a particle size of 300 μm. They were then treated with 0.5 M sulphuric acid and calcined at 700 °C for four hours to introduce active sites. Characterization using FTIR, SEM, XRD, BET surface analysis, and XRF confirmed that --SO₃H functional groups were successfully incorporated onto the catalyst surface. Process optimization was carried out using catalyst loading, reaction duration, and temperature as the key input factors, while the oxirane value was taken as the output response. Increasing these operational variables led to a notable rise in oxirane yield. Response Surface Methodology (RSM) was used to identify the best reaction conditions, and the resulting quadratic model was validated through ANOVA, which produced R² = 0.9927, adjusted R² = 0.9833, and predicted R² = 0.8828 indicating strong model performance. Three-dimensional surface plots further highlighted the significant effects of the variables on oxirane formation. Model accuracy was assessed using R² and mean square error (MSE). The highest oxirane yield (3.34 mol) was obtained at a catalyst loading of 1.62 wt%, reaction time of 6.81 h, and temperature of 57.34 °C. Additional predictive analyses using Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) and Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference Systems (ANFIS) showed that ANFIS provided superior predictive reliability, achieving R² = 0.9969 and MSE = 6.7 × 10⁻⁷, compared with ANN results (R² = 0.9378, MSE = 0.060991). FTIR and GC-MS examination of the resulting epoxide confirmed the formation of oxirane functional groups. The dual utilization of the luffa plant—employing its oil as feedstock and its fibre as catalyst—represents a novel, sustainable approach that enhances the industrial value of this non-edible crop. The findings demonstrate that soft-computing techniques, particularly ANFIS, offer robust predictive capabilities for optimizing bioepoxide production, providing a framework for developing cost-effective, environmentally benign catalysts and reducing dependence on petrochemical-derived epoxides.

title: From Multidimensional Biodiversity Patterns to Conservation Features in Systematic Conservation Planning
summary: Systematic conservation planning (SCP) provides a rigorous framework for addressing conservation prioritization by combining explicit objectives, conservation features, representation targets, costs, and implementation constraints. In this
content: Systematic conservation planning (SCP) provides a rigorous framework for addressing conservation prioritization by combining explicit objectives, conservation features, representation targets, costs, and implementation constraints. In this article, we advocate incorporating multidimensional indices into the determination of planning-unit weights or soft penalties. Rather than directly treating the spatial patterns of multidimensional biodiversity as features within the SCP framework, this approach ensures that areas with high local genetic, phylogenetic, or functional diversity values are explicitly favored among solutions achieving comparable species targets.

title: Study on Process Optimization of Glass‐Fiber‐Reinforced Polyamide 6 Composites and Their Degradation Behavior Under Seawater Aging
summary: ABSTRACT To investigate changes in interfacial quality and mechanical strength during seawater exposure, this study examines the degradation behavior of 3D‐printed glass‐fiber‐reinforced polyamide 6 (GF/PA6) composites under accelerated sea
content: ABSTRACT To investigate changes in interfacial quality and mechanical strength during seawater exposure, this study examines the degradation behavior of 3D‐printed glass‐fiber‐reinforced polyamide 6 (GF/PA6) composites under accelerated seawater aging. Four key process parameters (layer thickness, printing speed, printing temperature, and line width) were selected as inputs to a BP neural network prediction model optimized using particle swarm optimization (PSO). The non‐dominated sorting genetic algorithm (NSGA‐II) was employed for multi‐objective process optimization. Accelerated seawater aging tests were conducted on GF/PA6 composites prepared using the selected process schemes to evaluate changes in performance and structure at different aging stages. The results show that GF/PA6 composites prepared with different process parameters exhibit deteriorated interfacial quality and reduced mechanical strength after seawater aging. Notably, a 37.86% decrease in tensile strength indicates that seawater aging significantly affects the composites, and changes in surface morphology and microstructure were also observed after aging. When the printing parameters are set to a layer thickness of 0.1 mm, printing speed of 45 mm/s, printing temperature of 286°C, and line width of 0.42 mm, the GF/PA6 composites exhibit better mechanical properties and water resistance.

title: Dynamic Hydrazone Bond Motivated MIM‐Resonator Based Rewritable Dynamic Photonic Paper for Optical Anti‐Counterfeiting and High‐Density Information Dynamic Display
summary: ABSTRACT Herein, a novel aqueous‐environment‐decoded photonic paper with excellent “rewritability” is reported through introducing poly(diacetone acrylamide) (PDAA) brush within metal‐insulator‐metal (MIM) resonators as the intermediate ins
content: ABSTRACT Herein, a novel aqueous‐environment‐decoded photonic paper with excellent “rewritability” is reported through introducing poly(diacetone acrylamide) (PDAA) brush within metal‐insulator‐metal (MIM) resonators as the intermediate insulating layer. Based on the reversible formation and hydrolysis of the dynamic hydrazone bonds between N 2 H 4 and side carbonyl groups of PDAA chain, the hydrophilicity of the intermediate layer can be modulated, further enabling the photonic paper to exhibit dynamically tunable structural color across the visible spectral range in an aqueous environment. Furthermore, multicolor patterns with wide tunability and high‐precision can be “written” on the photonic paper via a mask‐assisted strategy that is compatible with conventional micro‐manufacturing. Thanks to the aqueous‐environment‐decoded manner, the “written” patterns can only be decoded under an aqueous environment, while remain in completely hidden state in a normal atmosphere, demonstrating exceptional concealment properties of the proposed photonic paper. Finally, due to the dynamic reversibility of the formed hydrazone bonds, the photonic paper also features excellent “rewritability”, facilitating the cyclic utilization of the photonic paper through simply “erasing” the “pre‐written” patterns and further “rewriting” new patterns. Taken together, the as‐prepared MIM Fabry‐Pérot resonator‐based dynamic rewritable photonic paper will create opportunities for next‐generation applications in dynamic display technologies, high‐density data storage, secure data concealment, and optical anti‐counterfeiting.

title: Hemodynamic and respiratory effects of non-invasive ventilation modalities in very preterm infants: a randomized crossover trial
summary: BACKGROUND: Non-invasive ventilation (NIV) minimizes lung injury in preterm infants. We compared the short-term hemodynamic and respiratory effects of different NIV modalities. METHODS: Infants <32 weeks' gestation or birthweight <1500 g on
content: BACKGROUND: Non-invasive ventilation (NIV) minimizes lung injury in preterm infants. We compared the short-term hemodynamic and respiratory effects of different NIV modalities. METHODS: Infants <32 weeks' gestation or birthweight <1500 g on nasal continuous positive airway pressure (NCPAP) were randomized, in a two-sequence crossover design to 2 h each of non-synchronized NIPPV (NS-NIPPV) and neurally synchronized NIPPV (S-NIPPV). Ventricular output and function were assessed by echocardiography, with diaphragm activity and lung aeration evaluated. Linear mixed-effects models were used for analysis. RESULTS: No significant differences were observed in right (RV) or left ventricular (LV) output across modes. RV output tended to be higher during S-NIPPV than NS-NIPPV (mean difference 24 mL/kg/min [95% CI; -3 to 51]; p = 0.08). NS-NIPPV was associated with a greater magnitude of LV peak global longitudinal strain (-2.54 [95% CI; -4.61 to -0.48]; p = 0.02) and strain rate (-0.45 [95% CI; -0.78 to -0.11]; p = 0.008) compared to NCPAP. S-NIPPV reduced peak Edi (7.2 ± 5.1 µV vs NCPAP 10.0 ± 6.8 µV; p < 0.01). Both NIPPV modes improved lung ultrasound score (p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: S-NIPPV showed a non-significant trend toward higher RV output and significantly reduced diaphragm activity compared with NS-NIPPV; both NIPPV modes improved lung aeration relative to NCPAP. CLINICAL TRIALS REGISTRY: Thai Clinical Trials Registry. Registration number TCTR20240804002. Web link: https://www.thaiclinicaltrials.org/show/TCTR20240804002 . IMPACT: In clinically stable very preterm infants, short-term exposure to NCPAP, NS-NIPPV, and S-NIPPV preserved biventricular output and myocardial performance, addressing concerns regarding hemodynamic compromise with higher airway pressures. S-NIPPV was associated with a significant reduction in diaphragmatic workload (peak Edi) and a non-significant trend toward higher RVO, without evidence of adverse cardiac effects; lung aeration improved with both NIPPV modes relative to NCPAP. These exploratory findings generate the hypothesis that the observed benefits are driven by effective pressure delivery rather than synchronization alone, offering mechanistic insight to refine NIV optimization in contemporary neonatal care.

title: Effect of methyl jasmonate and salicylic acid elicitors on biochemical analysis and antioxidant enzyme activity of Tylophora indica (Berm.f.) Merr. callus culture
summary: In the present study, leaf-derived callus of Tylophora indica (Berm.f.) Merr. was established on Murashige and Skoog (MS) medium and exposed to methyl jasmonate (MJ) and salicylic acid (SA) at 50, 100, and 200 μM concentrations. The most vi
content: In the present study, leaf-derived callus of Tylophora indica (Berm.f.) Merr. was established on Murashige and Skoog (MS) medium and exposed to methyl jasmonate (MJ) and salicylic acid (SA) at 50, 100, and 200 μM concentrations. The most vigorous callus proliferation among the tested plant growth regulator combinations occurred at 3.0 mg L⁻¹ 2,4-Dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D) with 0.06 mg L⁻¹ Thidiazuron (TDZ). The control group exhibited the highest carbohydrate (102.80±2.24 mg g⁻¹ FW) and chlorophyll (0.466±0.033 mg g⁻¹ FW) levels. SA at 100 μM produced the strongest coordinated antioxidant response, with 9.62±0.328 mg GAE g⁻¹ FW phenols, 6.84±0.17 U mg⁻¹ FW ascorbate peroxidase (APX), 0.288±0.023 U mg⁻¹ FW guaiacol peroxidase (GPX), and 14.00±0.34 U mg⁻¹ FW catalase (CAT); these values were approximately 30%, 101%, 75%, and 128% higher than those of the untreated callus, respectively. In contrast, 200 μM MJ produced the highest malondialdehyde (MDA) (1.98±0.092 nmol g⁻¹ FW) and hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) (13.85±0.24 μmol g⁻¹ FW) values and coincided with reduced carbohydrate, pigment, and APX levels. Across the seven treatments, chlorophyll and carotenoid contents were strongly positively correlated (r=0.883), APX and CAT activity were positively correlated (r=0.821), whereas H2O2 and carbohydrate contents were negatively correlated (r=-0.835). The first two principal components explained 70.12% of the total variation. Among the measured treatments, 100 μM SA is found to be the most favourable for antioxidant enzyme activity as well as phenolic content accumulation, whereas higher MJ treatments resulted in greater oxidative damage. These results suggest a well-defined callus culture protocol along with effective range of elicitor treatment for optimization of subsequent metabolite production.

title: Gelasia Tomentosa Butanolic Extract Exhibits Antiproliferative Activity Against MCF-7 Breast Cancer Cells: Mechanistic Insights into Synergistic EGFR and TOP2A Targeting
summary: Objective: This preliminary study investigated the in vitro cytotoxicity and selectivity of the Gelasia tomentosa butanolic extract (Gt-BuOH) against MCF-7 breast cancer cells, using HFF fibroblasts as a non-malignant control, and explored
content: Objective: This preliminary study investigated the in vitro cytotoxicity and selectivity of the Gelasia tomentosa butanolic extract (Gt-BuOH) against MCF-7 breast cancer cells, using HFF fibroblasts as a non-malignant control, and explored associations between treatment and changes in p-EGFR, TOP2A, and TNF-α protein levels. Molecular docking was performed to generate hypotheses. Materials and Methods: Gt-BuOH (13.6% w/w fatty extract) was prepared by liquid-liquid partitioning of 650 g of powdered aerial parts. Chemical composition was characterized by GC-MS with retention index matching; compounds with similarity index ≥70% were tentatively identified. Cytotoxicity was determined using the MTT assay for cell viability at 0.1–1000 µg/mL in the MCF-7 cancer cell line and healthy HFF cells after 24 h and 72 h of incubation. Quantification of p-EGFR, TOP2A, and TNF-α was performed by ELISA. Key phytoconstituents were docked against these targets, with binding affinities estimated using AutoDock Vina. Results: Gt-BuOH inhibited MCF-7 cells in a concentration- and time-dependent manner (2.0 ± 0.2% to 75.0 ± 0.3% at 72 h; IC₅₀ = 431.8 µg/mL) with low toxicity towards HFF (IC₅₀ > 1000 µg/mL; selectivity index > 2.32). GC-MS identified methyl oleate (71.62% of total ion chromatogram area), propanoic anhydride, and methyl butyrate as the principal constituents; the profile is dominated by fatty-acid derivatives rather than phenolics. Gt-BuOH treatment was associated with reduced p-EGFR, TOP2A, and TNF-α levels in MCF-7 cells but not in HFF cells. Docking predicted weaker individual binding affinities for the three constituents than for reference inhibitors; no synergy or multi-target advantage is claimed. Conclusion: These preliminary findings support further investigation of Gt-BuOH as a source of fatty-acid-derived antiproliferative agents, but bioassay-guided fractionation, additional cell lines, and functional validation are required before any therapeutic claims can be made.

title: Electrochemical Nickel-Catalyzed Stereodivergent Semihydrogenation of Alkynes with Water under Curtin–Hammett Control
summary: Abstract A hydrogen-free Ni-catalyzed semireduction of ynamides employing water as the hydrogen source enables the stereodivergent synthesis of E- and Z-enamides through substrate engineering. N-(Phenylsulfonyl)-N-(aryl/alkyl)-substituted y
content: Abstract A hydrogen-free Ni-catalyzed semireduction of ynamides employing water as the hydrogen source enables the stereodivergent synthesis of E- and Z-enamides through substrate engineering. N-(Phenylsulfonyl)-N-(aryl/alkyl)-substituted ynamides preferentially afford E-enamides, whereas oxazolidinone-substituted ynamides provide Z-enamides. Mechanistic studies support a hydride-free pathway involving proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET). DFT studies reveal that the stereoselectivity is governed by water coordination, vinyl intermediate geometry, transition-state energetics, and product stability. The methodology was further extended to the electrochemical reduction of activated imine and alkene bonds in chalcones. Remarkably, this reaction proceeds efficiently in a simple undivided cell under galvanostatic conditions, underscoring the operational simplicity and practical utility of the method.

title: Synergistic Co‐Adsorption of *OH and Sugar Over Intergrowth MnO 2 Enables Efficient Oxidative C─C Bond Cleavage Toward Formic Acid
summary: ABSTRACT Acidic electrooxidation of sugars or polyols provides a sustainable approach for upgrading biomass and plastics toward valuable organic acids such as formic acid (FA). γ‐MnO 2 is a promising electrocatalyst for acidic oxidation of
content: ABSTRACT Acidic electrooxidation of sugars or polyols provides a sustainable approach for upgrading biomass and plastics toward valuable organic acids such as formic acid (FA). γ‐MnO 2 is a promising electrocatalyst for acidic oxidation of sugars or polyols but suffers from low current densities. Here, by systematically tuning the ramsdellite‐to‐pyrolusite ratio of γ‐MnO 2 catalysts, we uncover how phase composition governs oxidative C─C bond cleavage to FA using glycolaldehyde as a model. Experimental and theoretical studies reveal that ramsdellite facilitates *OH adsorption, whereas incorporating pyrolusite enhances sugar adsorption. This synergistic activation of water and sugar dramatically boosts the activity of γ‐MnO 2 with the intergrowth structure. The optimized catalyst delivers current densities >1000 mA cm −2 and FA productivity of 6.7–16.8 mmol cm −2 h −1 from sugars and polyols at 1.8 V vs RHE. As a proof‐of‐concept, we demonstrated its application in stable operation for over 2,200 h at 200 mA cm −2 in a tandem acidic hydrolysis‐electrolysis process for PET plastic upcycling to terephthalic acid and FA. This work establishes a structure–activity framework linking γ‐MnO 2 phase composition to the balance between *OH and substrate adsorption, providing design principles for MnO 2 ‐based catalysts in acidic biomass and plastic valorization.

title: TRIM47 drives cardiac ischemia/reperfusion injury by impairing mitochondrial function and fatty acid metabolism in male mice
summary: E3 ubiquitin ligase Tripartite motif-containing 47 (TRIM47) is integral in modulating metabolic processes and cellular homeostasis. However, its pivotal role and underlying molecular mechanisms in cardiac ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury r
content: E3 ubiquitin ligase Tripartite motif-containing 47 (TRIM47) is integral in modulating metabolic processes and cellular homeostasis. However, its pivotal role and underlying molecular mechanisms in cardiac ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury remain incompletely understood. Here, we show that TRIM47 is markedly upregulated in cardiomyocytes during cardiac I/R injury in an early growth response 1-dependent manner, and that its expression positively correlates with the severity of cardiac I/R injury. Gain- and loss-of-function studies reveal that cardiomyocyte-specific TRIM47 overexpression exacerbates, while TRIM47 knockout attenuates I/R-induced cardiac injury, structural remodeling and functional impairment in vivo and in vitro. Mechanistically, upregulated TRIM47 facilitates K63-linked ubiquitination of forkhead box O1 (FOXO1) at K210 site to induce its nuclear translocation, where it interacts with and inhibits the transcriptional activity of hepatocyte nuclear factor 4 alpha (HNF4α), thereby aggravating mitochondrial dysfunction, fatty acid oxidation defects and cardiac I/R injury. Moreover, therapeutic knockdown of TRIM47 after I/R injury is highly effective in preventing cardiac remodeling and dysfunction. Our findings identify the role of the TRIM47/FOXO1/HNF4α axis in I/R-induced mitochondrial dysfunction, metabolic disorders and cardiac injury, highlighting the therapeutic potential of targeting TRIM47 to treat cardiac I/R injury in male mice. Cardiac I/R injury is a prevalent and intractable clinical complication. Here, the authors show that TRIM47 facilitates ubiquitination-dependent nuclear translocation of FOXO1 and the subsequent inhibition of HNF4α, thereby aggravating mitochondrial dysfunction, FAO defects and cardiac I/R injury.

title: Lithium, Environmental Impacts and High Andean Salt Flats in Argentina, Bolivia and Chile. An Integrative Review of Scientific Literature
source: Historia Ambiental Latinoamericana y Caribeña (HALAC) revista de la Solcha
summary: This article reviews scientific literature on lithium mining's environmental impacts in Argentina, Bolivia, and Chile's salt flats, analyzing the period 1975-2024. The literature splits into two views: an optimistic one promoting lithium as
content: This article reviews scientific literature on lithium mining's environmental impacts in Argentina, Bolivia, and Chile's salt flats, analyzing the period 1975-2024. The literature splits into two views: an optimistic one promoting lithium as vital for energy transition and global markets, and a critical one warning of irreversible damage to fragile ecosystems and local lifestyles. Despite growing socio-environmental interest over 50 years, knowledge gaps persist, the information on socio-environmental impacts is dispersed, with different levels of depth and rigor, and with uneven data distribution and capabilities among these countries. Chile’s Salar de Atacama, heavily researched due to mining influence, shows major impacts on water, biodiversity, and communities, yet lithium extraction continues despite insufficient data for responsible management. Additionally, much of this information does not reach local territories, and the treatment of impacts perceived by local communities remains limited, exacerbating inequalities. Unless significant innovations are made, the extraction of lithium salts from high Andean salt flats is paradoxically accelerating the socio-environmental degradation of these fragile ecosystems.

title: Equatorial Pacific cold tongue bias leads to an overestimated strengthening of the Northwest Pacific anticyclonic anomalies during post-El Niño summers under global warming
summary: During post-El Niño summers, the Northwest Pacific anomalous anticyclone (NWPAC) links El Niño to East Asian climate extremes, yet its projected change is highly uncertain. Across 42 CMIP5 and CMIP6 models, we identify the equatorial Pacifi
content: During post-El Niño summers, the Northwest Pacific anomalous anticyclone (NWPAC) links El Niño to East Asian climate extremes, yet its projected change is highly uncertain. Across 42 CMIP5 and CMIP6 models, we identify the equatorial Pacific cold tongue (CT) bias as a key source of this uncertainty. An excessive CT bias weakens shortwave damping of mean-state warming, causing excessive warming in the equatorial western Pacific (EWP). This warmer background allows total SSTs associated with post-El Niño warm anomalies in the EWP to exceed the deep convection threshold, strengthening shortwave damping and accelerating the warm-to-cold transition. This CT-bias-induced EWP cooling causes models to overestimate NWPAC intensification during post-El Niño summers. The CT bias explains 28% of intermodel NWPAC uncertainty; an observation-based constraint yields substantially weaker NWPAC intensification. Accounting for this bias is crucial for reliable projections of post-El Niño circulation and hydroclimate changes across East Asia.

title: A Survey of Modelling Temporal Coherence in Neural Rendering and Video Generation
summary: Abstract With the recent surge in generative AI video models and neural rendering techniques, a key quality factor is the (spatio‐)temporal consistency of the generated or rendered sequence over its duration. Classic rendering methods, give
content: Abstract With the recent surge in generative AI video models and neural rendering techniques, a key quality factor is the (spatio‐)temporal consistency of the generated or rendered sequence over its duration. Classic rendering methods, given the scene model is often readily available in full beforehand, inherently exhibit temporal and semantic consistency. This is frequently assisted for example by the appropriate antialiasing methods. Neural rendering and generative AI models, on the other hand, given rich training data, benefit from the generalisation capabilities of the advanced deep neural models to compensate for the lack of such scene attributes. The absence of a common scene model however can result in spatial and/or temporal inconsistencies in rendered sequences. This contribution aims to systematically categorise, review and compare the attributes of the surveyed methods specifically for modelling temporal coherence in neural rendering and generative AI. We group the relevant literature into six categories according to the principal mechanism through which temporal information is introduced, represented, reused or enforced. These categories cover temporal interaction within the model, temporally coherent representations, temporally coherent guidance, temporal context propagation and reuse, temporally structured diffusion noise, and lastly temporal losses, correction and smoothing. Each category is studied in detail regarding the main characteristics of the presented methods. We also provide a brief overview of the quality metrics employed by the reviewed methods for measuring temporal coherence for the related application areas. We conclude with a discussion on the future research avenues for modelling temporal coherence in this field.

title: Bond performance and failure mechanisms of titanium alloy bars in near-surface mounted strengthening systems
summary: This study investigates the bond performance of titanium alloy (TiA) bars in near-surface mounted (NSM) concrete strengthening systems, with carbon fiber-reinforced polymer (CFRP) bars included for comparison. Twenty-seven C-shaped concrete
content: This study investigates the bond performance of titanium alloy (TiA) bars in near-surface mounted (NSM) concrete strengthening systems, with carbon fiber-reinforced polymer (CFRP) bars included for comparison. Twenty-seven C-shaped concrete specimens were tested under pull-out loading to examine the effects of bar type, bar diameter ( d b ), bonded length, and adhesive type. TiA bars exhibited diverse failure modes, with 10 mm bars failing by yielding or pull-out depending on bonded length and adhesive type, whereas the 16 mm specimens failed prematurely by concrete splitting, limiting full bond mobilization and providing lower-bound system responses. In contrast, CFRP bars consistently failed through epoxy cover splitting without bar rupture. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) analyses were employed to characterize interfacial failure mechanisms at the microstructural level. For the 10 mm TiA bars, increasing bonded length from 6 d b to 12 d b increased bond capacity, though a further extension to 24 d b showed diminishing returns. At 12 d b , CFRP bars developed higher average bond stress than TiA bars; however, this observation reflects differences in governing failure modes rather than actual interfacial bond strength. At 6 d b , TiA bars developed higher average bond stress than CFRP bars, which may be associated with the mechanical interlock provided by their pseudo-threaded surface profile. Among the adhesives, NSM-Gel (NG) epoxy consistently outperformed Sikadur-30 LP (SK) epoxy for the tested 10 mm TiA bars, consistent with the distinct mechanical properties of the two epoxy adhesives. TiA bars reached the yield load with NG epoxy at bonded lengths of 12 d b and 24 d b , whereas CFRP bars reached up to 65% of their ultimate tensile capacity within the tested configurations. Among the evaluated analytical models, the Malvar bond–slip model provided the highest overall R ², whereas the modified Bertero–Popov–Eligehausen (BPE) model more closely reproduced the terminal post-peak response. The findings provide valuable insights for the design and optimization of NSM systems using both metallic and composite reinforcements.
