title: CHANGES IN THE STRUCTURE AND FUNCTIONS OF RED BLOOD CELLS IN CALVES WITH BRONCHOPNEUMONIA
summary: Respiratory diseases in animals are a major problem in veterinary medicine, causing significant economic losses in livestock farming, comprising a decline in the productive and breeding qualities of animals and their death [1, 2]. Bronchopn
content: Respiratory diseases in animals are a major problem in veterinary medicine, causing significant economic losses in livestock farming, comprising a decline in the productive and breeding qualities of animals and their death [1, 2]. Bronchopneumonia in young farm animals is widespread and ranks second in the disease incidence profile after gastrointestinal diseases [1–3]. Nearly one in two animals contracts bronchopneumonia at an early age. The disease occurs throughout the year, and in hot climates, it is most common in June–August [4]. Bronchopneumonia causes stunted growth and developmental delays in young animals, increased feed costs, and animal mortality. The widespread prevalence of bronchopneumonia in calves is due not only to known primary (unsanitary housing conditions, high indoor humidity, sharp fluctuations in daily temperature) and secondary (pathogenic and opportunistic microflora) [5–7], but also by immune deficiencies, which occur in nearly 60–70 % of newborn calves [4, 8–10]. In cases of bronchopneumonia in calves, pathological processes develop not only in the organs of the respiratory system, but also throughout the entire body, as all types of metabolism are disrupted. This also leads to the suppression of the functions of all vital organs and systems. Therefore, to achieve the desired outcome, it is important to adopt a comprehensive approach to the selection of medicinal products for the treatment of calves with bronchopneumonia [11]. In recent years, the incidence rate of respiratory disease in animals has not decreased but, on the contrary, has shown a tendency to increase [3, 11, 12]. Protracted and recurrent forms of pneumonia are more frequently recorded, as are cases of a sluggish course of the disease, which is due to reduced immunological reactivity of the animals’ bodies [13]. The most effective approach is a comprehensive treatment programme for animals with bronchopneumonia, which should be aimed at rectifying any shortcomings in husbandry and feeding practices, boosting the animals’ resistance, and involves the simultaneous use of various agents: antimicrobials, pathogenetic agents, symptomatic treatments, stimulants and vitamin preparations [9]. The course of pneumonia is accompanied by the development of hypoxic hypoxia, which is complicated by circulatory factors; therefore, studying the erythrocyte system is important in these diseases. Quantitative changes in erythrocytes and hemoglobin content have been fairly well studied; however, questions regarding the biochemical structure and functional properties of erythrocytes in calves with bronchopneumonia, as well as their changes under the influence of medicinal substances, particularly antibacterial drugs, remain unresolved. Therefore, despite the large number of studies conducted, the problem of pneumonia remains relevant both in terms of further studying its pathogenesis and in the search for and experimental validation of new effective therapeutic agents.

title: Natural-gas spark-ignition conversion of a diesel-derived engine with a re-entrant combustion chamber: combustion stability, efficiency and diesel-load benchmarking
summary: This study experimentally evaluates the spark-ignition conversion of a diesel-derived engine to natural-gas operation, with emphasis on combustion stability, efficiency, emissions, and diesel-load benchmarking. A Hyundai HR 2.5 L engine was
content: This study experimentally evaluates the spark-ignition conversion of a diesel-derived engine to natural-gas operation, with emphasis on combustion stability, efficiency, emissions, and diesel-load benchmarking. A Hyundai HR 2.5 L engine was modified for port-fuel-injected operation and tested in a single-cylinder configuration using two combustion systems, designated Stock (original diesel-derived bowl) and Modified (re-entrant bowl with a larger squish area and lower compression ratio). Tests included naturally aspirated throttled and dethrottled operation at 1800 rpm, boosted stoichiometric operation up to 17.8 bar IMEP, and diesel-load benchmark comparisons against an estimated single-cylinder indicated diesel reference at 1600, 1800, and 2000 rpm. Under dethrottled lean operation, the Modified configuration maintained shorter CA10-90 and lower COVIMEP near the dilution limit, preventing the marked deterioration in combustion efficiency and methane emissions observed with the Stock configuration, although NO X increased at moderately lean conditions. Under boost, the Modified configuration also reduced high-frequency pressure-oscillation energy throughout the evaluated load range. At approximately 15 bar IMEP and lambda 1.4, net indicated efficiency reached 42.6–42.8 %, remaining within the literature-based FMEP sensitivity range of the reconstructed diesel reference, whereas stoichiometric natural-gas operation remained about two percentage points lower. Lean benchmark operation reduced nominal direct CO 2 and NOX emissions but substantially increased methane slip; the resulting CO 2 -equivalent trend was comparatively sensitive to uncertainty in the reconstructed exhaust-flow calculation. Overall, the Modified configuration improved dilution tolerance and high-load combustion robustness, enabling diesel-comparable indicated load and efficiency while identifying methane-slip and NO X control as key requirements for high-efficiency methane applications.

title: Identifying demand-side measures that matter most for Europe's decarbonisation
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This repository contains the network files (.nc) and other data necessary for reproducing the results and graphs in the paper. The code for reproducing these files plus the Jupyter notebooks used for creating all the figures in the paper ar
content: This repository contains the network files (.nc) and other data necessary for reproducing the results and graphs in the paper. The code for reproducing these files plus the Jupyter notebooks used for creating all the figures in the paper are also available at: https://github.com/Parisra/Demand-management-paper. This record updates the code archived in 10.5281/zenodo.16918863 and adds the data and scripts used for the final version of the paper. A preprint of the paper is available on arXiv: arXiv:2508.04414v2. Abstract: European countries pursue a miscellany of historic, emerging, and planned initiatives to transform energy demand through behavioural shifts and end-use efficiency improvements. Yet, these efforts often evolve within fragmented national frameworks that overlook the rapidly evolving supply landscape, risking misaligned investments and diminishing public engagement. We address this need for prioritization by employing a high-resolution European energy system model under a net-zero constraint to co-optimise demand and supply strategies across seven sectors, mapping system response to demand mechanisms that reflect real-world practices. Our findings confirm large-scale gains from demand reductions in heating and industry sectors, and show carbon capture reliance is most sensitive to aviation and shipping demand. For heating, reducing peak demand yields the greatest benefit, while critical curtailment is most effective for electricity and alleviates high consumer prices. Small measures also count: shifting even two hours of demand toward solar output, a low-effort and robust strategy, delivers benefits.

title: Dual-Functional Halloysite Nanotube-Derived Cigarette Capsules for Hazard Reduction and Mold Prevention
summary: Abstract Currently, cigarette-filter modification has predominantly targeted reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging; however, beyond ROS, cigarette smoke contains other hazardous agents such as carbon monoxide (CO), tar, and polycyclic ar
content: Abstract Currently, cigarette-filter modification has predominantly targeted reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging; however, beyond ROS, cigarette smoke contains other hazardous agents such as carbon monoxide (CO), tar, and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), the reduction of which remains largely neglected in current strategies. Herein, we report a novel cigarette-filter capsule, termed Cit-sHNT@Capsule, fabricated by loading the natural flavor citral (Cit) into sulfuric acid-etched halloysite nanotubes and further encapsulating the hybrid within alginate-based hydrogel beads. Incorporating Cit-sHNT@Capsule into cigarette filters moderately reduced CO and tar yields by 9.74% and 13.4%, respectively, while the •OH and •O2– probe assays indicated reductions of approximately 50% and 60%, and fluorescence-based calibration yielded an apparent 57.0% reduction in the PAH-associated measurement, without compromising the moisture and nicotine content during combustion. Thermogravimetric analysis indicated limited mass loss over 70–80 °C, and the capsules retained their structural integrity under the heating conditions, providing preliminary support for their incorporation into cigarette filters. Furthermore, the outstanding antifungal activity of Cit-sHNT@Capsule against Aspergillus niger (nearly 100% inhibition within 45 days) underscored the potential to extend tobacco storage duration and reduce fungal contamination. Collectively, this work highlights the potential of Cit-sHNT@Capsule as a dual-functional additive for cigarette filters, enabling simultaneous hazard reduction and mold prevention.

title: Through‐Space Hot‐Electron Transfer Between Gold Nanoclusters and MOF Boosting Photothermal Conversion
summary: ABSTRACT The structural elucidation of metal nanocluster@MOF composites remains challenging due to their poor crystallinity, hindering the establishment of precise structure–property relationships. Here, we present a reverse templating stra
content: ABSTRACT The structural elucidation of metal nanocluster@MOF composites remains challenging due to their poor crystallinity, hindering the establishment of precise structure–property relationships. Here, we present a reverse templating strategy in which atomically precise gold nanoclusters (GNCs) to direct MOF crystallization, yielding highly crystalline GNC@MOF single crystals for single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction (SCXRD) analysis. Coarse‐grained molecular dynamics (CGMD) simulations reveal the adaptive growth of MOFs around spherical GNC template, accompanied by a complete topological transformation from rectangular to hexagonal symmetry. Combining transient absorption spectroscopy, density functional theory (DFT) calculations, and optoelectronic measurements, we reveals pronounced space interfacial electron coupling between GNCs and MOFs. This coupling facilitates directional transfer of photoexcited hot electrons from GNCs to MOFs, resulting in enhanced photothermal conversion performance. Upon 660 nm laser irradiation, Au 13 @Zn‐NDC‐MOF rapidly heats to 106.3°C within 6 s and reaches a maximum temperature of 182.0°C (∆ T = 158.1°C), outperforming discrete Au 13 clusters (∆ T = 126.3°C) under identical conditions. Au 13 @Zn‐NDC‐MOF also exhibits excellent photostability over multiple on‐off cycles. This work establishes a direct link among through‐space interfacial electron coupling, hot‐electron transfer, and enhanced photothermal behavior, providing a generalizable platform for the rational design of high‐performance MNC@MOF materials for solar energy conversion and photocatalysis.

title: Growth and nutritional composition of Scenedesmus acuminatus (Lagerheim) (Chodat, 1902) in an alternative culture medium
summary: This study evaluated the biomass production of the microalga Scenedesmus acuminatus using aquaculture effluent as an alternative culture medium. The experiment was conducted in a controlled laboratory environment comparing two treatments: c
content: This study evaluated the biomass production of the microalga Scenedesmus acuminatus using aquaculture effluent as an alternative culture medium. The experiment was conducted in a controlled laboratory environment comparing two treatments: cultivation in aquaculture effluent and in a commercial NPK medium. Population growth, biomass production, nutrient removal efficiency, and the nutritional composition of the produced biomass were analyzed. The results demonstrated that S. acuminatus exhibited comparable growth in aquaculture wastewater and the NPK medium, with specific growth rates of 0.20 and 0.34⸱day-1, respectively, and no significant differences between treatments (p = 0.49). Biomass productivity was also statistically similar between the two culture media. Additionally, S. acuminatus efficiently removed ammonia (95.3%) and nitrate (99.4%) from aquaculture wastewater, highlighting its potential as a sustainable biological approach for nitrogen bioremediation. The biomass produced maintained a rich nutritional profile of proteins, lipids, and minerals, indicating its applicability across various industrial sectors. Thus, this study demonstrated that aquaculture wastewater can successfully replace a conventional culture medium for S. acuminatus, enabling comparable biomass production and efficient nitrogen removal. These findings provide new evidence supporting the integration of microalgae cultivation with intensive aquaculture as a sustainable strategy for resource recovery and circular bioeconomy.

title: Enantioselective Access to Bis‐U‐Shaped Hexapyrrolic Expanded Porphyrinoids via a BINAM‐Directed Axial‐to‐Helical Chirality Transfer Strategy
summary: ABSTRACT Chiral expanded porphyrinoids hold great promise for chiroptical applications, while stereospecific access to enantiopure expanded porphyrinoids remains a significant challenge due to their conformational heterogeneity, tedious pos
content: ABSTRACT Chiral expanded porphyrinoids hold great promise for chiroptical applications, while stereospecific access to enantiopure expanded porphyrinoids remains a significant challenge due to their conformational heterogeneity, tedious post‐synthetic resolution, and poor configurational stability. Herein, we employ 1,1'‐binaphthyl‐2,2'‐diamine (BINAM) as both the core building block and chiral directing group for the one‐pot stereospecific synthesis of a ‘ bis‐U‐shaped ’ hexapyrrolic expanded porphyrinoid platform. The axially chiral twisted conformation of BINAM imposes a strong conformational constraint during cyclization with tripyrrin subunits, inducing synchronous helical twisting of the conjugated chains and establishing multiple stereogenic helical elements. Single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction confirms quantitative transfer of BINAM axial chirality to persistent macrocyclic P / M helicity, affording enantiomers with exceptional thermal stability (no racemization even at 180°C). Notably, both Zn(II) and Co(II) bind via an unprecedented cross‐bridging mode, chelating dipyrrin donors from two separate tripyrrin units rather than undergoing conventional central insertion. This coordination rigidifies the folded framework, amplifies the chiroptical response (|g abs | values from 0.0096 to 0.0126 and 0.0137 for Zn(II) and Co(II) complexes, respectively), and directs homochiral supramolecular self‐assembly into one‐dimensional helical nanostructures in the solid state.

title: Hex‐to‐Cubic Stabilization Enables CO 2 ‐Resistant and Mechanically Robust Air Electrodes for Durable Solid Oxide Fuel Cells
summary: ABSTRACT One major challenge for solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) is the lack of high‐performance air electrodes with sufficient chemical‐mechanical durability in CO 2 ‐containing atmospheres. CO 2 poisoning, together with insufficient phase
content: ABSTRACT One major challenge for solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) is the lack of high‐performance air electrodes with sufficient chemical‐mechanical durability in CO 2 ‐containing atmospheres. CO 2 poisoning, together with insufficient phase stability, promotes surface reconstruction and carbonate formation on air electrodes, which can synergistically couple with mechanical failure to accelerate electrode degradation. Here, we propose a strategy of hex‐to‐cubic phase stabilization by facile B‐site scandium doping to investigate the connection between structural stability, CO 2 resistance and mechanical durability in SOFC air electrodes. The as‐developed air electrode shows a stabilized cubic phase with an increased lattice Debye temperature, a more robust Sr─O bonding environment, and mitigated Sr surface segregation/secondary carbonate formation. Consequently, the SrSc 0.25 Co 0.75 O 3–δ (SSC) air electrode exhibits a low air‐electrode area‐specific polarization resistance of 0.0347 Ω cm 2 at 700°C, maintains stable operation for 400 h under alternating CO 2 poisoning, and delivers a peak power density of 1.97 W cm −2 at 800°C. These results link cubic‐framework stabilization with suppressed carbonate accumulation and retained local mechanical integrity, providing a design basis for chemically and mechanically durable SOFC air electrodes.

title: Autoantibodies against N-terminal EF-hand calcium-binding protein 1 in neurological syndromes and cancer
summary: BACKGROUND: Paraneoplastic neurological syndromes (PNS) are immune-mediated disorders associated with cancer and often precede tumor diagnosis. Identification of novel neural autoantigens may facilitate diagnosis and treatment. METHODS: Ser
content: BACKGROUND: Paraneoplastic neurological syndromes (PNS) are immune-mediated disorders associated with cancer and often precede tumor diagnosis. Identification of novel neural autoantigens may facilitate diagnosis and treatment. METHODS: Sera or cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) from six patients showing a similar uncharacterized immunofluorescence staining pattern on rat hippocampal sections were collected. The target antigen was identified by immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry and validated using established immunoassays. RESULTS: N-terminal EF-hand calcium-binding protein 1 (NECAB1) was revealed as target of the autoantibodies. Antigen identification was validated by competitive tissue IIFA, CBA, Western blot and line blot with the recombinant antigen. No reactivity was observed in CBA and line blot with 100 healthy controls or CBA with 303 disease controls. All five clinically characterized patients had breast or lung cancer and presented with limbic encephalitis (n = 3), cerebellar ataxia with cognitive decline (n = 1), or sensory-motor neuronopathy (n = 1). CONCLUSIONS: NECAB1 represents a novel autoantibody target in autoimmune neurological syndromes associated with lung or breast cancer. Samples from patients with suspected neurological autoimmune disorder showing the specific hippocampal interneuron IIFA pattern should be analyzed for NECAB1 autoantibodies by CBA or line blot and cancer screening should be considered.

title: Dietary canola meal hydrolysate powder attenuated intestinal damage induced by enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli F4 in weaned piglets
summary: The present study investigated the effects of canola meal hydrolysate powder (CMHP), derived from the enzymatic treatment of canola meal, on growth performance, fecal consistency score, intestinal morphology, barrier integrity and inflammat
content: The present study investigated the effects of canola meal hydrolysate powder (CMHP), derived from the enzymatic treatment of canola meal, on growth performance, fecal consistency score, intestinal morphology, barrier integrity and inflammatory responses in weaned piglets under enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli F4 (ETEC) challenge. A total of 35 piglets (21 d of age; average body weight: 8.08 ± 0.31 kg) were individually assigned to 1 of 5 treatments: no-challenged control (NC), challenged control (CC), CC supplemented with 1.0 g/kg Aureomycin (CCA), and CC supplemented with 2.5 or 5.0 g/kg CMHP (CCH1 and CCH2, respectively). After a 7-d adaptation period, all piglets in CC, CCA, CCH1 and CCH2 were orally inoculated with 5 mL of 5 × 106 CFU/mL ETEC. Seven days after the challenge, piglets were euthanized for collection of intestinal tissues and subsequent analyses. Statistical analyses were performed using the Mixed procedure SAS 9.4. Inoculation with ETEC significantly reduced (P < 0.05) average daily gain (ADG) and increased feed conversion ratio (FCR) and fecal scores. Supplementation with 5.0 g/kg CMHP tended to improve FCR during the post-challenge and overall experimental periods (P ≤ 0.09), while aureomycin and 5.0 g/kg CMHP reduced fecal scores on 3 and 4 dpc compared with the CC group (P < 0.05). Histological analysis revealed that ETEC challenge impaired jejunal morphology, while 2.5 g/kg and 5.0 g/kg CMHP improved the villus height-to-crypt depth ratio (P < 0.05). Significantly impaired intestinal barrier function was observed following ETEC challenge, as indicated by increased FITC-D flux and reduced TEER (P < 0.05), while 5.0 g/kg CMHP increased TEER values and occludin mRNA expression compared with the CC group (P < 0.05). Following ETEC challenge, plasma TNF-α levels increased, and jejunal TLR2 and TLR4 expression was upregulated. Supplementation with 5.0 g/kg CMHP significantly downregulated IL-6, TNF-α, TLR2, and TLR4 mRNA expression in the jejunum (P < 0.05). Overall, CMHP supplementation, particularly at 5.0 g/kg, attenuated diarrhea, intestinal inflammatory responses and improved intestinal barrier integrity in ETEC-challenged weaned piglets.

title: Cochineal Carmine‐Incorporated Poly(Lactic Acid) Films: Effects of Pigment Concentration on Physicochemical, Barrier, and Functional Properties
summary: ABSTRACT Active packaging based on biodegradable polymers incorporating bioactive compounds offers a sustainable alternative to fossil‐based materials. This study developed biodegradable PLA films by casting using sunflower oil as a plastic
content: ABSTRACT Active packaging based on biodegradable polymers incorporating bioactive compounds offers a sustainable alternative to fossil‐based materials. This study developed biodegradable PLA films by casting using sunflower oil as a plasticizer, soy lecithin as an emulsifier, and cochineal carmine at concentrations of 0.12 (PLA12), 0.18 (PLA18), and 0.36 (PLA36) mL g −1 PLA as a natural antioxidant dye. Films containing cochineal carmine exhibited reduced UV–visible light transmittance, increased redness, and maintained color stability during 30 days of storage at 40°C. Higher dye concentrations (PLA18 and PLA36) improved mechanical strength, opacity, UV protection, crystallinity, and oxygen barrier properties compared with the unpigmented films, while the pigmented films also exhibited pH‐responsive color behavior. Carminic acid release was detected in the fatty food simulant, and the PLA36 formulation notably delayed sunflower oil oxidation compared with PET packaging. Morphological and FTIR analyses indicated interactions between the film components without substantial changes in the characteristic PLA absorption bands. These biodegradable films show potential for active and smart food packaging applications, particularly for foods susceptible to light‐ and oxygen‐induced deterioration.

title: Field-Based Biomass and Carbon Stock Estimation and Landsat-Derived Spatial Patterns in Tula Highland, Gombe State, Nigeria
summary: Highland vegetation is poorly represented in Nigeria’s carbon accounting. We estimated aboveground (AGB) and belowground biomass (BGB) and biomass carbon stocks in Tula Highland, Gombe State, and examined their relationship with Landsat-der
content: Highland vegetation is poorly represented in Nigeria’s carbon accounting. We estimated aboveground (AGB) and belowground biomass (BGB) and biomass carbon stocks in Tula Highland, Gombe State, and examined their relationship with Landsat-derived vegetation indices. Woody vegetation was inventoried in 13 one-hectare plots, spaced 1 km apart, between February and June 2025. AGB was estimated with allometric equations, BGB with a fixed root-to-shoot ratio of 0.26, and carbon with a fraction of 0.47; litter was reported separately. Landsat 8 OLI imagery for 2020–2024 was used to compute NDVI, SAVI and ARVI. Mean densities were 23.55 Mg ha⁻¹ for AGB (95% CI 10.27–36.82) and 6.12 Mg ha⁻¹ for BGB, a combined 29.67 Mg ha⁻¹ (13.95 Mg C ha⁻¹), with large variation among plots (0.18–108.62 Mg ha⁻¹). Summed over the plots, AGB and BGB were 306.14 and 79.60 Mg (181.29 Mg C). Because BGB is a fixed fraction of AGB, it carries no independent information; a ratio of 0.56 would raise mean total biomass to 36.74 Mg ha⁻¹. A three-index linear model gave an adjusted R² of 0.986 (AIC = 173.93) for the calibration plots, but the small sample, near-collinear indices and lack of independent validation limit confidence in spatial predictions. Model-derived mean AGB rose by 16.99% between 2020 and 2024; this reflects spectral change, not measured biomass accumulation or carbon sequestration. The results are a preliminary baseline and show the need for more plots, repeated inventories and formal uncertainty assessment.

title: Improving hydrological partitioning simulations by incorporating subsurface critical zone structure in an alpine catchment on the northeastern Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
summary: Study region The Qianhuli catchment is located in the upstream region of Shaliu River watershed on the northeastern Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, China. It comprises south-facing and north-facing hillslopes and a valley. Study focus Hydrological p
content: Study region The Qianhuli catchment is located in the upstream region of Shaliu River watershed on the northeastern Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, China. It comprises south-facing and north-facing hillslopes and a valley. Study focus Hydrological partitioning describes the allocation of precipitation among evapotranspiration, surface runoff, subsurface runoff, snow sublimation, deep percolation, and subsurface storage. Accurately quantifying hydrological partitioning is essential for assessing water resources, but simplified subsurface critical zone (CZ) representations obscure spatial storage and drainage differences. We incorporated soil and underlying weathered bedrock thicknesses measured by ground-penetrating radar into the Cold Regions Hydrological Modelling platform. Three schemes representing shallow soil, uniform CZ profiles based on observed means, and observed CZ heterogeneity were evaluated. New hydrological insights for the region The heterogeneous scheme achieved a validation Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency of 0.77, compared with 0.48 and 0.52 for the shallow and uniform schemes, respectively. Simulated surface runoff dominated the south-facing hillslope (60.6% of total runoff), whereas subsurface runoff dominated the north-facing hillslope (78.5%), where subsurface storage was more than twice as large. Evapotranspiration was also higher on the north-facing hillslope. These contrasts suggest that layer thickness and hydraulic characteristics jointly regulate water storage and lateral drainage, while soil moisture differences may influence evapotranspiration. This work demonstrates that representing subsurface CZ heterogeneity is important for improving land surface models and reducing uncertainty in alpine water resource predictions.

title: Spectral Characterization, X-Ray Crystallographic, and Computational Studies of Facial Tricarbonylrhenium(I) Complexes with 1,2-Diaminobenzene and 2-Picolylamine Ligands
summary: Abstract Herein, facial tricarbonylrhenium(I) complexes: fac -[Re(CO) 3 (H 2 dab)Br] ( 1 ) (H 2 dab = 1, 2-diaminobenzene) and fac -[Re(CO) 3 (Hpica) 2 ]Br ( 2 ) (Hpica = 2-picolylamine) were synthesized and comprehensively characterized us
content: Abstract Herein, facial tricarbonylrhenium(I) complexes: fac -[Re(CO) 3 (H 2 dab)Br] ( 1 ) (H 2 dab = 1, 2-diaminobenzene) and fac -[Re(CO) 3 (Hpica) 2 ]Br ( 2 ) (Hpica = 2-picolylamine) were synthesized and comprehensively characterized using Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) and Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, Ultraviolet-visible (UV–vis) spectrophotometry, Time-of-Flight mass spectrometry (ToF-MS), elemental analysis (EA), and single crystal X-ray diffraction (XRD). The solid-state crystal structures reveal that 1 and 2 exhibit coordination modes where the H 2 dab coordinates bidentately through the amino nitrogens, while the Hpica organic ligands render ‘ 2 + 1’ N pyridyl N amino and N amino coordination modes, respectively. The single X-ray crystal structures of 1 and 2 , along with their respective Density Functional Theory (DFT)-optimized structures, show good conformational agreement, with low root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) values, thus validating the parameters used for DFT and TD-DFT computations. Acquired experimental UV–vis and FTIR spectral data for 1 and 2 were correlated with the respective simulated spectral data to facilitate the interpretation of the observed spectral bands.

title: An electrically driven multimodal soft robot enabled by a monolithic heterolayer elastomer
summary: Soft robots powered by active materials can navigate complex environments through multimodal locomotion. However, prevailing designs typically rely on a single active material within multi-component architectures, which often leads to high
content: Soft robots powered by active materials can navigate complex environments through multimodal locomotion. However, prevailing designs typically rely on a single active material within multi-component architectures, which often leads to high structural complexity and “soft-stiff” interfacial challenges. Here, we present an electrically driven, entirely soft robot based on a monolithic heterolayer elastomer integrating a processable high-performance dielectric elastomer and a liquid crystal elastomer. In this “soft-soft” structure, the liquid crystal elastomer functions as a reconfigurable compliant skeleton to program the equilibrium states, while the dielectric elastomer serves as a fast-responsive artificial muscle driving dynamic motion. Through independent control of the two active materials, the robot demonstrates bidirectional crawling at 2.3 cm·s−1, leaping over 2.5 body lengths, climbing on a 20° slope, and controlled rolling. Our approach establishes a paradigm for creating soft robots with high structural integrity, payload‑to‑weight ratio, and controllability for deployment in unstructured environments. Soft robots are promising for complex applications, though typical robots rely on a single active material limiting applications. Here the authors design artificial muscle using dielectric elastomers and liquid crystal elastomers for multimodal locomotion.

title: From Mirror‐Image Biomolecules to Cross‐Chirality: Advances and Applications
summary: Native nucleic acids and proteins are homochiral biopolymers: the sugar moieties in nucleic acids are D-configured, whereas the amino acids in proteins are predominantly L-configured. By contrast, mirror-image nucleic acids are built from L
content: Native nucleic acids and proteins are homochiral biopolymers: the sugar moieties in nucleic acids are D-configured, whereas the amino acids in proteins are predominantly L-configured. By contrast, mirror-image nucleic acids are built from L-ribose (in L-RNA) or L-2-deoxyribose (in L-DNA), rather than from their D-configured counterparts. Although the mirror-image central dogma exhibits perfect theoretical symmetry, its experimental reconstruction remains challenging, particularly with respect to the efficient synthesis of system components and their precise assembly and regulation to achieve functional integration. Recent technological breakthroughs have rendered this goal increasingly feasible. The accumulated technical capabilities have brought about a novel cross-chiral paradigm that fundamentally extends beyond single-chiral replication, enabling mutual replication and synergistic interactions between left- and right-handed biomolecules. This review systematically surveys recent technological advances, covering macromolecular synthesis, the development and validation of tools for system operation, and conceptual breakthroughs in cross-chirality. It further examines how these developments collectively propel the field from theoretical frameworks toward practical applications, while also raising profound safety and ethical concerns.

title: Transcranial Doppler after traumatic brain injury: from flow-velocity snapshots to a multimodal physiological phenotype
source: The Egyptian Journal of Neurosurgery : the official publication of the Egyptian Society of Neurological Surgeons/Egyptian journal of neurosurgery
summary: Abstract Background After traumatic brain injury (TBI), cerebral arterial flow velocity and Doppler waveform characteristics may change over hours or days. Serial transcranial Doppler (TCD) can document these changes at the bedside, althoug
content: Abstract Background After traumatic brain injury (TBI), cerebral arterial flow velocity and Doppler waveform characteristics may change over hours or days. Serial transcranial Doppler (TCD) can document these changes at the bedside, although their interpretation depends on acquisition conditions and concurrent systemic physiology. Main body This focused narrative review examines repeated TCD acquisition, longitudinal velocity and pulsatility patterns, the feasibility of extended recordings, and their use in selected clinical circumstances, including suspected perfusion abnormalities and post-traumatic vasospasm. Studies demonstrate that repeated measurements are feasible and that some Doppler findings are associated with clinical outcomes. Differences in sampling intervals, insonated vessels, physiological conditions, comparator measures and statistical adjustment, however, make independent prognostic value difficult to establish. Associations involving pressure-derived autoregulation measures or circulating biomarkers cannot be taken as validation of TCD trajectories. The available studies support careful comparison of recording conditions and interpretation alongside clinical examination, imaging and indicated invasive monitoring, but do not establish a validated serial-TCD prediction rule or treatment algorithm. Conclusion Serial TCD provides complementary longitudinal information in adult TBI. Standardized prospective studies are needed to determine its reproducibility, additional clinical value and effects on patient-important outcomes before specific trajectory thresholds or management pathways can be recommended.

title: Construction of Pyridine‐Containing Covalent Organic Frameworks for Broadband Nonlinear Optical Responses
summary: ABSTRACT The structural diversity of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) makes them promising candidates for nonlinear optical (NLO) materials. However, their NLO responses at 1550 nm, a key wavelength in optical telecommunications, remain r
content: ABSTRACT The structural diversity of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) makes them promising candidates for nonlinear optical (NLO) materials. However, their NLO responses at 1550 nm, a key wavelength in optical telecommunications, remain rarely reported. Here, we report that pyridine‐containing COF thin films exhibit a broadband NLO response across the visible to near‐infrared regions, including prominent fifth‐order optical nonlinearity at 1550 nm. The bipyridine‐based COF (TpBpy) exhibits a stronger NLO response than the pyridine‐based COF (TpApy), with NLO coefficients approximately four to five times higher. Characterization using X‐ray diffraction, X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and Fourier‐transform infrared spectroscopy reveals differences in crystallinity, porosity, and chemical structure between the two COFs. These differences, together with the conjugation and enol‐to‐keto tautomerization characteristics of their linkers, may contribute to more extended electronic delocalization in TpBpy and its enhanced NLO response. These findings highlight the potential of pyridine‐containing COFs for NLO applications in the telecommunication window.

title: Fucoidan in lung cancer treatment: a comprehensive review of therapeutic applications and mechanisms
summary: Lung cancer is a common malignancy in many countries and places a substantial mortality burden on public health systems worldwide. Despite recent advances in diagnosis and treatment, standard therapies often cause severe adverse effects and
content: Lung cancer is a common malignancy in many countries and places a substantial mortality burden on public health systems worldwide. Despite recent advances in diagnosis and treatment, standard therapies often cause severe adverse effects and lead to drug resistance. These limitations highlight the need for safer and more effective treatment options. Fucoidan, a natural sulfated polysaccharide derived from marine brown algae, exhibits antitumor, antifibrotic, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant activities, supporting its potential biomedical applications. Although interest in its biological activities has grown, research specifically addressing its therapeutic role in lung cancer remains limited. The molecular mechanisms underlying its effects on lung cancer cells are also incompletely understood. This review examines the pharmacological effects of fucoidan against lung cancer and evaluates its potential as an adjuvant therapeutic agent.

title: Aerosol Cross‐Boundary‐Layer Transport and Its Microphysical Impacts on Stratiform Clouds: Insights From Two‐Case Aircraft In Situ Observations
summary: Abstract Aerosol‐cloud interactions represent one of the largest uncertainties in climate forcing estimates, particularly for stratiform clouds whose extensive coverage and low cloud bases render them highly susceptible to planetary boundar
content: Abstract Aerosol‐cloud interactions represent one of the largest uncertainties in climate forcing estimates, particularly for stratiform clouds whose extensive coverage and low cloud bases render them highly susceptible to planetary boundary layer (PBL) processes. However, observational constraints on how diurnally varying PBL dynamics modulate aerosol vertical transport and cloud microphysical responses are limited. Here we address this gap using aircraft in situ observations from two flights over Nanning, a subtropical monsoon region in southern China, to investigate aerosol cross‐layer transport at the PBL top and its impacts on stratiform cloud microphysics. Our measurements reveal a bidirectional transport mechanism that varies distinctly between day and night. In the daytime case (29 October 2020,10:05–13:33 BST), a developing mixed boundary layer combined with subsidence in the lower free troposphere drives entrainment of free‐tropospheric aerosols into the PBL. This elevates aerosol number concentration (Na) near the PBL top, substantially increasing cloud droplet number concentration (Nc) in the lower cloud layer while reducing both droplet effective diameter (Ed) and spectral dispersion ( ε ). Upper cloud layers exhibit lower Na and Nc but larger Ed and enhanced ε . In the nighttime case (2 November 2020, 14:04–17:42 BST), aerosols vented from the PBL into the residual layer are subsequently lifted by updrafts to 2,000–3,000 m, increasing cloud‐top Nc while decreasing Ed and ε . These findings provide key evidence for vertically heterogeneous aerosol‐cloud interactions under varying PBL regimes. It is important to clarify that these two cases represent different diurnal states rather than a continuous diurnal cycle, and they are treated as a comparative experiment rather than continuous observation. While the two‐case comparison precludes definitive generalization, consistent patterns across multiple vertical profiles offer robust observational support for the proposed mechanisms and provide critical constraints for improving aerosol‐cloud interaction parameterizations in climate models.

title: Ablative Heat-Shield Sizing for a Mars Direct-Entry Capsule: Heat Load, Ablator Mass and Margin Budgets
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This paper presents a computed design study of a planetary entry system on a single stated operating principle: a phenolic-impregnated carbon ablator shield protects the capsule by sacrificing itself in a controlled way — its resin pyrolyze
content: This paper presents a computed design study of a planetary entry system on a single stated operating principle: a phenolic-impregnated carbon ablator shield protects the capsule by sacrificing itself in a controlled way — its resin pyrolyzes, its char layer radiates and insulates, and the mass it loses carries heat away — and the shield is sized directly from the integrated heat load, so the sizing study, not the material, is the design product. The system is a 900 kilogram direct-entry Mars capsule of 3.5 metre diameter entering at 6.10 kilometres per second, with peak heating evaluated at a density of 0.0018 kilograms per cubic metre over a stated heating pulse, sized with a PICA-class ablator of stated effective ablation enthalpy. The design target is a complete shield sizing: peak heating rate, integrated heat load, required ablator areal mass including the structural floor allowance, shield mass and shield mass fraction, each computed and each carrying its margin policy openly. Peak deceleration is 13.1 Earth gravities, peak heating is 179 watts per square centimetre, the heat load is 113 megajoules per square metre, and the thermal protection mass is 114 kilograms, a fraction 0.127 of the entry mass. This work is a computed design study for civilian planetary science, with no targeting or weapon application. Its subject is the safe delivery of scientific payloads through a planetary atmosphere, and its numbers are simulated from stated assumptions rather than measured on hardware.

title: Fluorescence lifetime imaging of NAD(P)H and flavin: A practical introduction to studying metabolic heterogeneity in living samples
summary: Fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) of cellular autofluorescence allows metabolism to be visualised in living systems without exogenous labelling. By measuring the decay characteristics of NADH, NADPH and flavin autofluorescence
content: Fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) of cellular autofluorescence allows metabolism to be visualised in living systems without exogenous labelling. By measuring the decay characteristics of NADH, NADPH and flavin autofluorescence, FLIM can be used to investigate metabolic heterogeneity within intact cells, tissues and developing organisms while preserving spatial and temporal context. Despite increasing adoption, newcomers to the field often encounter difficulties in experimental design, data analysis and metabolic interpretation. This primer therefore aims to provide a practical introduction to the principles and implementation of autofluorescence FLIM. The photophysics of NAD(P)H and flavins are summarised and the instrumental requirements for FLIM are introduced. Key aspects of experimental design are considered and approaches to fluorescence decay analysis are reviewed. The metabolic insights that can be obtained from the fitted parameters are discussed alongside the limitations of interpreting fluorescence lifetimes as direct measures of pathway activity. These concepts are illustrated through a case study in which NAD(P)H FLIM was used to identify a previously unrecognised metabolic gradient during the development of hearing. The primer advances the view that, while a sensitive reporter of metabolic state, autofluorescence FLIM alone is best viewed as a powerful hypothesis-generating tool. When combined with targeted perturbations and orthogonal validation approaches, it provides a uniquely informative means of characterising metabolism within complex living systems.

title: Porous polymeric nanocomposites for biomedical applications
summary: Date seed, and bullock pod nanoparticles with up to 1 wt.% were used as reinforcement in polypropylene to develop biomedical materials. Microstructural, mechanical and antimicrobial tests were conducted. The maximum compressive strength rec
content: Date seed, and bullock pod nanoparticles with up to 1 wt.% were used as reinforcement in polypropylene to develop biomedical materials. Microstructural, mechanical and antimicrobial tests were conducted. The maximum compressive strength recorded was 29.535 MPa ± 3.83 MPa at 0.2 wt.% date seed nanoparticle addition to the polypropylene matrix. This implies a 78 % increase. Comparison of properties of the polypropylene nanocomposites with bovine tibia trabecular bone show that compressive strength values of 0.6 wt.% bullock pod reinforced polypropylene (27.403 MPa ± 1.02 MPa), 0.2 wt.% date seed reinforced polypropylene (29.535 MPa ± 3.83 MPa), and 0.4 wt.% hybrid particle reinforced polypropylene (26.129 MPa ± 1.63 MPa), are greater than the 17.5 MPa ± 3.2 MPa of bovine tibia trabecular bone. The flexural strength of polypropylene reinforced with 0.6 wt.% bullock pod was 21.706 ± 2.03 MPa, exceeding the value of 18.7 MPa reported for bovine tibial trabecular bone. In contrast, the polypropylene composite reinforced with 0.2 wt.% date seed exhibited a lower flexural strength of 14.13 MPa ± 1.14 MPa. Furthermore, antimicrobial examinations indicated that date seed, bullock pod, and the 0.6 wt.% bullock pod‐reinforced polypropylene composite contain phytochemicals with potential antimicrobial properties.

title: The effects of submaximal exercise on acid–base balance in people with long COVID
summary: Abstract Better pathophysiological understanding of long COVID (LC) is required, and disruption of acid–base regulation has been proposed as a potential mechanism underlying exercise intolerance observed in LC; however, empirical evidence r
content: Abstract Better pathophysiological understanding of long COVID (LC) is required, and disruption of acid–base regulation has been proposed as a potential mechanism underlying exercise intolerance observed in LC; however, empirical evidence remains limited. Accordingly, this study aims to systematically characterise day‐to‐day variation in acid–base status in individuals living with LC. Thirty people (19 female) with a confirmed diagnosis of LC or 15 healthy controls (CON; 8 female) completed three study visits. Participants completed two submaximal cardiopulmonary exercise tests (CPETs) separated by 24 h. Pre‐ and post‐exercise fingertip capillary blood samples were collected on both CPET days for acid–base balance (pH, HCO 3 − , anion gap, K + , Na + , Cl − and ionized calcium (iCa 2+ )) and lactate. Subgroup analysis was conducted for those presenting with metabolic acidosis between LC and CON. Whole group analysis revealed no differences between LC and CON for acid–base balance ( P > 0.05) or CPET variables ( P > 0.05). However, a subgroup analysis determined that following CPET1, 17% ( n = 5/30), and following CPET2, 33% ( n = 10/30) of those with LC demonstrated metabolic acidosis, with small to large effect sizes (0.20 → 0.80) between LC and CON for pH, HCO 3 − , anion gap, K + , Na + , Cl − , iCa 2+ and lactate. For CON, metabolic acidosis was identified for 6% ( n = 1/18) on CPET day 1 and 11% ( n = 2/18) on CPET day 2. Our findings suggest that some people with LC may experience acid–base balance disturbances following repeated submaximal exercise. Accordingly, a pathological subgroup is hypothesised, and these findings should provoke independent validation.

title: Introducing the Dangers of PM2.5 and Self-Protection Measures Against Air Pollution to Elementary School Students
summary: Exposure to fine particulate matter (PM2.5) is an air pollution issue that poses risks to respiratory health, including among school-aged children. Education regarding the dangers of PM2.5 and personal protective measures is essential for f
content: Exposure to fine particulate matter (PM2.5) is an air pollution issue that poses risks to respiratory health, including among school-aged children. Education regarding the dangers of PM2.5 and personal protective measures is essential for fostering environmental health awareness from an early age. This community service initiative aimed to provide students at SD Inpres BTN IKIP I Makassar with an understanding of the hazards of PM2.5 and the proper use of face masks. The implementation method included the presentation of educational material using visual aids, a demonstration of the steps for putting on and removing a mask, and an interactive quiz. The outcomes of the activity demonstrated that the education covered an introduction to PM2.5, sources of pollution, health impacts, personal protection measures—incorporating the "3L" concept—and the practical application of wearing a mask. This initiative served as an environmental health learning tool that combined information with hands-on practice. Similar educational efforts should be conducted on an ongoing basis, supported by more structured evaluation

title: Accessibility-guided targeting of NRF2-responsive long noncoding RNA NMRAL2P alters a distinct gene expression program and reduces non-small cell lung cancer proliferation
summary: Aberrant activation of the antioxidant transcription factor NRF2 promotes non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) survival and therapy resistance, but downstream effectors beyond redox regulation remain incompletely defined. Transcriptome profil
content: Aberrant activation of the antioxidant transcription factor NRF2 promotes non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) survival and therapy resistance, but downstream effectors beyond redox regulation remain incompletely defined. Transcriptome profiling of lung and NSCLC cells identified the pseudogene-derived long noncoding RNA LOC344887/NMRAL2P as consistently associated with NRF2 activity. The NMRAL2P locus produces three predominant, nuclear-localized isoforms whose expression depends on NRF2 across normal lung, lung adenocarcinoma, and lung squamous carcinoma cells. In-cell SHAPE-MaP identified accessible regions within NMRAL2P transcripts, guiding antisense gapmer design. NMRAL2P depletion inhibited NSCLC cell proliferation and increased sensitivity to cisplatin. Transcriptome analysis revealed that NMRAL2P depletion altered a restricted gene expression program involving cell adhesion and MAPK signaling, with responses distinct from those observed following NRF2 depletion. Core NRF2 antioxidant target genes were largely unaffected by NMRAL2P depletion. These findings support a model in which NRF2 induces NMRAL2P to sustain a distinct gene expression program that contributes to NSCLC proliferation and survival. NMRAL2P represents an RNA effector downstream of NRF2 that links oncogenic NRF2 activity to cellular functions beyond canonical antioxidant responses, providing a potential point of intervention in NRF2-active lung cancers and motivating further investigation of the mechanisms connecting this nuclear RNA to signaling pathways.

title: The Radical Truth: Why [Mn(CO) 5 ] 2 Outperforms Dinuclear Metal Carbonyls of Fe, Ru, Co, and Mo as a Photoinitiator
summary: ABSTRACT Dimanganese decacarbonyl, [Mn(CO) 5 ] 2 ( Mn 2 ), is a leading photoinitiator and has found applications in halogen atom transfer (XAT) reactions, as an initiator for polymerization and as a promotor for element‐hydrogen bond activ
content: ABSTRACT Dimanganese decacarbonyl, [Mn(CO) 5 ] 2 ( Mn 2 ), is a leading photoinitiator and has found applications in halogen atom transfer (XAT) reactions, as an initiator for polymerization and as a promotor for element‐hydrogen bond activation. However, Mn 2 is a privileged reagent as related dimers, M 2 , [Fe(η 5 ‐C 5 H 5 )(CO) 2 ] 2 ( Fe 2 ), [Ru(η 5 ‐C 5 H 5 )(CO) 2 ] 2 ( Ru 2 ), [Mo(η 5 ‐C 5 H 5 )(CO) 3 ] 2 ( Mo 2 ), [Co(CO) 4 ] 2 ( Co 2 ), and [Mn(CO) 4 (PPh 3 )] 2 ( MnP 2 ) have not found similar wide‐spread applications, despite undergoing essentially identical light‐induced M─M bond cleavage to reveal 17‐electron radicals, M . In this work, time‐resolved infra‐red spectroscopy on timescales from ps → mins has been applied to understand the special position occupied by Mn 2 compared to the other initiators. This revealed that, with the exception of Co , all the radicals M react with O 2 at close to the diffusion‐controlled limit to give superoxido complexes M‐O 2 . In all cases but for the unique Mn system, these superoxido complexes irreversibly decompose to generate CO 2 through an intramolecular coupling reaction between CO and O 2 ligands; an intermediate metal oxido complex was observed for Mo . The complicated interplay between formation of the superoxido complexes, dimerization to reform M 2 and C─I bond activation is investigated in each case revealing the key features needed for 17‐electron radicals to participate in downstream synthetic transformations.

title: Boosting Oxygen Transport with Nanoporous Graphdiyne for High‐Capacity Li−O 2 Batteries
summary: ABSTRACT Li−O 2 batteries have attracted extensive attention due to their potential to achieve several times higher energy density than Li‐ion batteries. However, the actual discharge capacity and rate performance still fall short of practi
content: ABSTRACT Li−O 2 batteries have attracted extensive attention due to their potential to achieve several times higher energy density than Li‐ion batteries. However, the actual discharge capacity and rate performance still fall short of practical requirements, as cathodes made of dense carbon black particles hinder the fast diffusion of O 2 deep into the cathode during discharge, thus severely limiting cathode utilization. In this work, we introduce graphdiyne (GDY) into the cathode to accelerate O 2 transport. GDY is a two‐dimensional material with intrinsic nanopores that allow O 2 molecules to pass through. When incorporated into carbon‐black cathodes, GDY particles forms pathways of low diffusion resistance that facilitate O 2 diffusion deep into the cathode. The accelerated O 2 transport, which is supported by gas permeability measurement, enhances the discharge capacity of the battery by over 4 times to 10.36 mAh cm −2 , equivalent to 950 mAh g −1 (Li2O2+carbon) . Characterization of the discharged cathode reveals that GDY introduction substantially changes the growth of the discharge product, lithium peroxide, promoting its formation both in the form of larger particles and deeper throughout the cathode, thereby contributing to higher discharge capacity. Our findings demonstrate a new strategy for accelerating mass transport to improve cathodes utilization, and ultimately realizing high‐energy‐density Li−O 2 batteries.

title: Orogenic Gold Mineralization at Bangbu in Tethyan Himalaya Linked to Devolatilization of the Sedimentary Sequences in Passive Continental Margin
summary: ABSTRACT The mechanisms driving the formation of orogenic gold deposits during continental collisions remain enigmatic. This study integrates field observations with geochemical analyses, including whole‐rock assays of Au, As, Sb and S in m
content: ABSTRACT The mechanisms driving the formation of orogenic gold deposits during continental collisions remain enigmatic. This study integrates field observations with geochemical analyses, including whole‐rock assays of Au, As, Sb and S in metasedimentary host rocks and in‐situ δ 3 4 S, δ 1 8 O and Pb isotope measurements on ore minerals, to reveal the metal and fluid sources for the collision‐related Bangbu gold deposit in the Tethyan Himalaya (southern Tibet, China). Analytical results reveal that the Triassic–Jurassic carbonaceous slates and phyllites of the Indian passive margin sequence are enriched in Au–As–Sb–S and show depletion in these elements in higher‐grade metamorphic equivalents, indicating mobilization of gold and volatiles during prograde metamorphism. Ore pyrites from both early massive quartz–sulphide veins (Stage I) and later fine‐grained veins (Stage II) have uniform Pb isotope ratios identical to those of the Triassic strata, while the δ 3 4 S values (+1‰ to +2‰) of pyrite from these veins and the wall rock Triassic phyllite are uniform. Quartz veins yield δ 1 8 O quartz of ∼16‰, corresponding to δ 1 8 O fluid values of ∼5.5‰–6.9‰, consistent with a metamorphic water origin. Collectively, these results indicate that gold at Bangbu was sourced from devolatilization of the Indian passive‐margin sedimentary sequences (Triassic strata) during the Himalayan collision.

title: Evaporation and kinetic characteristics of soybean oil-ethanol secondary droplets during micro-explosion
summary: Abstract Soybean oil is one of the important sources of sustainable aviation fuel, and the study of soybean oil mixed with ethanol can provide important data support for the development and utilization of soybean oil. In this experiment, th
content: Abstract Soybean oil is one of the important sources of sustainable aviation fuel, and the study of soybean oil mixed with ethanol can provide important data support for the development and utilization of soybean oil. In this experiment, the evaporation, micro-explosion and the number and distribution characteristics of four kinds of mixed fuel droplets made of soybean oil and ethanol under different temperatures were studied by controlling the nitrogen flow rate (7.9 L/min) and the oxygen flow rate (2.1 L/min) to simulate the air atmosphere by using the test platform of micro-explosion characteristics of mixed fuel and the moving droplet tracking technology. No combustion occurred during the experiment. It took 10 ms, 1ms, 5ms and 1ms for S80E20, S70E30, S60E40 and S50E50 droplets to expand from the beginning to fully form secondary droplets, respectively. The evaporation rate of droplets is mainly affected by the temperature and micro-explosion intensity of two factors. The S80E20 droplet was distorted repeatedly before micro-explosion, and the secondary droplet distortion formula was established. Through calculation, it was found that the maximum distortion of S80E20 droplet before micro-explosion had exceeded 0.7, and the secondary droplet distortion produced after micro-explosion of S80E20 droplet was all above 0.05, with the maximum value exceeding 0.25.

title: Diatom‐Inspired Hierarchical Macro‐Mesoporous AuPd/ZnO with Topology‑Induced Metal‐Support Interactions for Ultrasensitive Monitoring of Bacterial Volatile Biomarkers
summary: ABSTRACT Inspired by the hierarchical porous architecture of diatom frustules, we report a biomimetic hierarchically ordered macroporous mesoporous AuPd/ZnO composite as a high‐performance sensing platform for trace detection of 3 ‐hydroxy‐
content: ABSTRACT Inspired by the hierarchical porous architecture of diatom frustules, we report a biomimetic hierarchically ordered macroporous mesoporous AuPd/ZnO composite as a high‐performance sensing platform for trace detection of 3 ‐hydroxy‐2‐butanone (3H2B), a critical volatile biomarker of Listeria monocytogenes. Here, the deliberate design of high curvature mesopores as topological traps to anchor AuPd nanocrystals, proposing a topology‐induced metal‐support interaction mechanism that triggers interfacial electronic restructuring. This confinement‐driven modulation optimizes oxygen reactivity and reduces the reaction energy barrier, enabling MEMS sensor with an ultralow detection limit of 9.7 ppb and high response (R a /R g = 74.4) to 10 ppm 3H2B at 150°C, significantly outperforming conventional porous materials. In situ spectroscopy and DFT calculations reveal that Pd sites within the AuPd alloy serve as primary electron donors, facilitating 3H2B dehydrogenation and oxidation. Furthermore, a portable wireless module integrated with a random forest algorithm allows accurate identification of 3H2B in complex mixtures, validating real‐time monitoring of bacterial growth in food. This work not only establishes a paradigm for precision synthesis of hierarchically porous materials but also provides profound insights into interfacial science by leveraging topological confinement to tailor electronic structures for interfacial catalytic performance and food safety applications.

title: Metabolomics and bioassay-guided characterization identifies bioactive polyphenols in Acacia dealbata leaf and bark extracts
summary: INTRODUCTION: Acacia dealbata, native to southeastern Australia, has documented traditional uses but remains underexplored as a source of bioactive metabolites. Comprehensive, bioassay-guided phytochemical characterization is needed to iden
content: INTRODUCTION: Acacia dealbata, native to southeastern Australia, has documented traditional uses but remains underexplored as a source of bioactive metabolites. Comprehensive, bioassay-guided phytochemical characterization is needed to identify the bioactive compounds present in the plant. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to identify the bioactive phytochemicals responsible for antioxidant and antimicrobial activities of A. dealbata leaf and bark extracts using an integrated metabolomics and natural products chemistry workflow. METHODS: Leaf and bark samples were extracted using solvents of varying polarity (n-heptane, ethyl acetate, methanol, water, and water: acetonitrile: isopropanol, 2:3:3). Extracts were evaluated for antioxidant and antimicrobial activities and characterised using an LC-MS/MS-based metabolomics workflow incorporating MZmine, GNPS molecular networking, SIRIUS in silico annotation, and taxonomically informed metabolite annotation (TIMA). Bioactive extracts were fractionated by preparative HPLC, followed by bioactivity-guided assessment, quantitative LC-MS analysis using standards, and NMR spectroscopy. RESULTS: Methanol leaf extract and ethyl acetate bark extract exhibited the strongest antioxidant and antimicrobial activities. Preparative fractionation identified flavonoids and glycosides as the dominant metabolite classes in both extracts, while terpenoids and alkaloids were also abundant in leaf fractions. Quantitative LC-MS identified rutin as the predominant compound in leaf bioactive fractions, whereas catechin, epigallocatechin, and procyanidin B2 predominated in bark fractions. NMR confirmed enrichment of flavonoid O-glycosides and simple phenolics in leaf fractions and flavan-3-ols and proanthocyanidins in bark fractions. CONCLUSION: This integrated workflow linked metabolomic profiling with bioactivity, demonstrating that A. dealbata leaves and bark are promising sources of bioactive polyphenols that can act against oxidative stress and infectious diseases.

title: Effects of pectin-chitosan nanoliposomes delivering 5-methyltetrahydrofolate on gastrointestinal fate and gut microbiota modulation
summary: 5-methyltetrahydrofolate (5-MTHF) is the bioactive folate form, but gastric instability limits its application. We previously developed pectin-chitosan double-layer nanoliposomes (P-CH-NL) for 5-MTHF delivery. This study investigated their
content: 5-methyltetrahydrofolate (5-MTHF) is the bioactive folate form, but gastric instability limits its application. We previously developed pectin-chitosan double-layer nanoliposomes (P-CH-NL) for 5-MTHF delivery. This study investigated their gastrointestinal fate and interactions with human gut microbiota using simulated digestion and in vitro fermentation models. Following upper gastrointestinal transit, the P-CH-NL structure was degraded by colonic microbiota, releasing 5-MTHF, which was putatively converted into active tetrahydrofolate (THF) via metabolic demethylation. Concurrently, the core-shell architecture of the polysaccharide coatings enhanced total short-chain fatty acids (SCFA) production, specifically promoting acetate, propionate, and butyrate generation. Furthermore, 16S rRNA sequencing revealed P-CH-NL beneficially modulated the microbiota composition by enriching core polysaccharide degraders such as Bacteroides , which concurrently decreased the Firmicutes/Bacteroidota ratio, and suppressing opportunistic pathogens ( Fusobacterium , Escherichia-Shigella ). In conclusion, by structurally mitigating the inherent antimicrobial limitations of chitosan, P-CH-NL exhibits a dual function of partial colonic retention and a prebiotic-like effect (not a formal prebiotic by ISAPP criteria), providing an experimental basis for developing functional foods to improve folate bioavailability and modulate gut microecology.

title: Influence of die face geometry on material flow, thermomechanical history, and microstructure in friction extrusion
summary: Friction extrusion (FE) is a solid-phase process that can produce high-performance composites with homogeneous microstructures and low porosity via industrially scalable routes. However, the influence of die face geometry on material flow,
content: Friction extrusion (FE) is a solid-phase process that can produce high-performance composites with homogeneous microstructures and low porosity via industrially scalable routes. However, the influence of die face geometry on material flow, thermomechanical history, and microstructure remains unclear. This work uses an experimentally validated smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) framework to quantify die-geometry effects during FE of AA1100 (O temper) rods for grid-conductor applications. Five dies are examined: flat (F), scrolled with (S-CB) and without (S) a counterbore, and conical scrolled with (CS-CB) and without (CS) a counterbore. The flat die exhibits a narrow sticking zone and pronounced slip near the orifice, leading to localized strain rate/temperature fields and strong core-edge gradients in plastic strain. Scrolls enlarge the effective processing zone and improve mixing by promoting interfacial sticking, whereas conical faces reduce contact pressure and homogenize thermomechanical fields. Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) shows that CS and CS-CB yield the finest dynamically recrystallized grains. A Zener-Hollomon parameter-grain size relationship is further established, providing a physics‑based metric for FE die and process design.

title: Highly Ductile PETG / POE /Fe 3 O 4 Multi‐Responsive Shape‐Memory Polymer for 4D Printing
summary: ABSTRACT In this work, we fabricated PETG/POE/Fe 3 O 4 nanocomposites via melt blending at a fixed 4:6 PETG‐to‐POE mass ratio with varying Fe 3 O 4 loadings, aiming to develop a magnetic–near‐infrared dual‐responsive shape‐memory polymer fo
content: ABSTRACT In this work, we fabricated PETG/POE/Fe 3 O 4 nanocomposites via melt blending at a fixed 4:6 PETG‐to‐POE mass ratio with varying Fe 3 O 4 loadings, aiming to develop a magnetic–near‐infrared dual‐responsive shape‐memory polymer for 4D printing. SEM images showed a gradual morphological shift from a sea‐island to a co‐continuous structure as Fe 3 O 4 content increased. Tensile testing gave a peak elongation at break of around 109%. DMA is the primary means to identify the glass‐transition region near 80°C, with DSC providing auxiliary support. Combined with TGA, they confirm no thermal degradation occurs during 3D printing. The composite with 20 phr Fe 3 O 4 showed good shape fixity, recovery performance, and cyclic stability: it achieved 94% recovery under an alternating magnetic field, over 95% under NIR irradiation, and 97.5% recovery within 38 s under synergistic actuation. Sequential stimulus switching also retained high recovery, supporting the material's multi‐mode operational adaptability. Finally, bionic palm and flower structures 3D‐printed with this filament exhibited programmable and controllable deformation under dual stimuli, and this work offers a theoretical and practical reference for multi‐responsive shape‐memory materials in 4D printing.

title: Influence of a Single Nitrogen Atom on the π–π Stacking Interaction in Coronene Dimers: An EDA, QTAIM, and NCI Computational Analysis
summary: Abstract Intermolecular aromatic interactions, also known as π–π stacking, are of great importance in chemical and biological materials science. This field of study has remained important for at least three decades and spans a broad multidi
content: Abstract Intermolecular aromatic interactions, also known as π–π stacking, are of great importance in chemical and biological materials science. This field of study has remained important for at least three decades and spans a broad multidisciplinary range. Doping aromatic systems with heteroatoms, such as nitrogen, can influence these interactions and significantly alter their properties. Still, the exact cause of the altered π–π interactions in aromatic aggregates from heteroatom doping remains debated. In this work, we evaluate changes in the electronic and structural properties of coronene dimers upon introducing a single nitrogen heteroatom. Calculations use CAM–B3LYP–D3/6–311G(d,p) level of theory, along with EDA, QTAIM, and NCI analyses. Our results show that nitrogen subtly enhances π–π interactions between coronene monomers. The strength of these interactions varies with the substitution site. Aggregation becomes stronger with increased N–N distance when pyridinic–N is the substituent, if the same arrangement is considered (twisted or parallel–displaced). When graphitic–N is substituted at an intermediary position, the degree of slipping between monomers mainly governs aggregation, regardless of the arrangement. In the central ring, graphitic–N promotes the formation of a covalent C–C bond between the monomers, promoting a 10 kcal mol–1 increase in interaction energy. The results indicate that dispersive forces, such as pancake bond, remain the primary driver of aggregation, with nitrogen only slightly altering the electronic charge distribution. Energy decomposition analysis indicates that dispersion remains the dominant stabilizing contribution, while the type and position of the nitrogen atom locally modulate the electronic environment and promote distinct geometrical reorganizations of the π–π interface, thereby affecting the interaction strength and preferred stacking arrangements.

title: The environment and the industry-level inward and outward greenfield FDI: evidence from 30 Chinese Provinces and 32 economic sectors
summary: This study examines the association between inward and outward greenfield foreign direct investment (GFDI) and CO2 emissions across 32 economic sectors and 30 Chinese provinces. Using a unique dataset combining proprietary FDI Markets data
content: This study examines the association between inward and outward greenfield foreign direct investment (GFDI) and CO2 emissions across 32 economic sectors and 30 Chinese provinces. Using a unique dataset combining proprietary FDI Markets data on GFDI by industry, province, and source/destination world region, we construct a province–industry-level model that controls for the Environmental Kuznets relationship, capital assets, and industry, province, and world-region effects. We disentangle the correlation patterns across the industrial distribution of GFDI, as well as the provincial distribution of GFDI. In addition, we examine the GFDI–emissions correlation by source world region for inward GFDI and by destination world region for outward GFDI. The main results indicate that inward GFDI is positively associated with CO2 emissions, primarily in heavy industries and in more developed Chinese provinces. Notably, outward GFDI is also positively associated with CO2 emissions in China, driven by its correlation in light industries.

title: Kinetic balancing for near-equilibrium growth of defect-suppressed lead bromide perovskite single crystals
summary: Controlling crystallization pathways for solution-grown lead-bromide perovskites remains a major unresolved challenge. Herein, we present a ligand-regulated crystallization strategy that achieves near-equilibrium growth for lead-bromide per
content: Controlling crystallization pathways for solution-grown lead-bromide perovskites remains a major unresolved challenge. Herein, we present a ligand-regulated crystallization strategy that achieves near-equilibrium growth for lead-bromide perovskite single crystals. Such regulation mitigates kinetic imbalance during crystal growth, thereby suppressing non-equilibrium defect incorporation, improving lattice coherence, and facilitating spatially uniform crystal growth. This strategy is applicable to a representative set of lead-bromide perovskites. Specifically, the resulting CsPbBr3 single crystals exhibit a high resistivity of 5.1 × 1010 Ω·cm and carrier mobility up to 93.95 cm2·V−1·s−1. Reduced electron-phonon coupling weakens optical-phonon scattering and raises the effective thermally activated conduction barrier from 0.43 to 0.71 eV, extending stable bias operation from 40 to 200 V·mm−1. These advances enable sensitive and stable ionizing-radiation detection under both photon-counting and charge-integrating modes. Overall, this work establishes a general kinetic-design principle for defect-suppressed, near-equilibrium crystallization of lead-bromide perovskites, enabling reliable high-field operation for ionizing-radiation detectors. A ligand-regulated crystallization strategy achieves near-equilibrium growth of lead bromide perovskite single crystals, suppressing defects and improving quality. The resulting CsPbBr3 crystals enable stable, sensitive ionizing-radiation detection.

title: The Top Ways to Optimize Humanity's Outlook This Century
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Humanity’s long-term outlook in the twenty-first century depends on a single overarching imperative: accelerating sustainable global economic convergence while building polycrisis resilience across the world’s fastest-growing, highest-vulne
content: Humanity’s long-term outlook in the twenty-first century depends on a single overarching imperative: accelerating sustainable global economic convergence while building polycrisis resilience across the world’s fastest-growing, highest-vulnerability regions. The defining structural challenge of the period from 2026 to 2100—what this monograph formalizes as the Central Asymmetry of the 21st Century—is geographic, demographic, and financial. Nearly 100% of net global population growth and the fastest urbanization this century will occur in parts of Sub-Saharan Africa (1.30B to 3.48B), South Asia (2.05B to a 2.42B mid-century peak), Latin America, and the Middle East and North Africa that confront the steepest physical climate survivability risks—extreme wet-bulb heat, hydrological volatility, soil degradation, and compounding disease vectors—accumulating 331.5 billion vulnerable person-years (rising from 3.45 billion exposed people in 2026 to 4.88 billion by 2100). Simultaneously, aging high-income economies hold 78.5% of frontier R&D capacity and benefit from low sovereign and infrastructure borrowing costs (3%–4%), whereas emerging economies face punitive costs of capital (9%–15%+ WACC) and historical technology diffusion lags of 25 to 40 years. Because fiscal capital and planetary boundaries are finite, developing nations cannot replicate twentieth-century fossil-fueled industrialization, nor can global policy rely on slow, sequential, single-sector aid. The objective is not simply to develop faster, but to develop in ways that make humanity simultaneously more prosperous, technologically capable, environmentally sustainable, and resilient. To operationalize this thesis, H Heuristics establishes a unified Six-Concept Intellectual Architecture—linking Sustainable Global Convergence, Innovation Diffusion, Development Economics, Green Convergence, Human Development, and Polycrisis Adaptation and Resilience—and introduces twelve canonical theoretical concepts, including Sustainable Convergence, Adaptive Convergence, Polycrisis-Adjusted Development, Sustainable Diffusion, Developmental Resilience, Anticipatory Development, Multidimensional Development Optimization (MDO), Resilience-Oriented Urbanization, Convergent Technology Diffusion, Preventive Development Economics, Demographic Resilience, and Productive Sustainability. Rather than evaluating projects in isolated silos, we construct two complementary quantitative evaluation systems scored on a 100-point scale: The Six-Dimension Structural Evaluation Matrix (EC 20%, HD 20%, TD 15%, EI 15%, AC 15%, DR 15%):Identifies Water Infrastructure, Desalination & Universal WASH (85.5/100) and Heat-Resilient "Sponge" Cities (85.0/100), followed by a three-way tie at 84.5/100 among Girls’ Secondary Education, Climate-Resilient Agriculture, and Distributed Solar & Storage, and followed by the Clean Cooking Transition (82.0), Digital Public Infrastructure (80.5), and Online Learning & Upskilling (79.0), as the ce

title: Reinforcing the Physical and Thermal Properties of Poly(Vinyl Alcohol‐Acrylamide) Using AgNO 3 ‐ ZrO 2 NPs : Innovative Nanocomposites for Optical and Energy‐Related Devices
summary: ABSTRACT Eco‐friendly polymer nanocomposites with enhanced opto‐electric features and thermal stability have become essential for a broad range of potential applications. In this study, cost‐effective sol–gel and solution‐casting methods we
content: ABSTRACT Eco‐friendly polymer nanocomposites with enhanced opto‐electric features and thermal stability have become essential for a broad range of potential applications. In this study, cost‐effective sol–gel and solution‐casting methods were used to prepare zirconium dioxide nanoparticles (ZrO 2 NPs) and 2.5–10 wt% ZrO 2 /silver nitrate (AgNO 3 )/polyvinyl alcohol‐polyacrylamide (PVA‐PAM) nanocomposites for possible optoelectronic and energy storage applications. X‐ray diffraction (XRD) peaks of the matrix lessened and broadened following the loading of ZrO 2 NPs up to 5 wt%. FE‐SEM and mapping analyses revealed the presence of Ag and Zr with uniform distribution. FTIR results indicated a physical interaction between blend chains and ZrO 2 NPs. The direct optical bandgap of AgNO 3 /PVA‐PAM decreased from 3.8 to 3.4 eV at 5.0 wt%, and then increased to 3.65 eV at 10 wt% ZrO 2 NPs. The absorption index, refractive index, and other optical constants can be tuned by ZrO 2 NPs content. The films demonstrated high thermal stability, with melting temperatures varying according to the content of ZrO 2 NPs. The influence of ZrO 2 NPs on the dielectric constant, loss tangent, modulus, and Cole‐Cole profile was reported. The enhancements in the physical properties, coupled with improved thermal stability, position these films as strong candidates for potential applications in optoelectronics and supercapacitors.

title: Investigating Seasonality in Sulfate Presence and Radiative Forcing in the North Pacific
summary: Abstract Sulfate aerosols, formed from the atmospheric oxidation of sulfur dioxide (SO 2 ), contribute to global cooling through both direct and indirect radiative effects. However, uncertainties remain in their seasonal and spatiotemporal
content: Abstract Sulfate aerosols, formed from the atmospheric oxidation of sulfur dioxide (SO 2 ), contribute to global cooling through both direct and indirect radiative effects. However, uncertainties remain in their seasonal and spatiotemporal distributions along with their radiative impacts, particularly in relation to anthropogenic emissions and downstream burden.
