title: Fully biocatalytic stereodivergent conversion of levulinic acid to enantiopure γ-valerolactone
summary: γ-Valerolactone (GVL) is a biomass-derived platform chemical with broad industrial applications, while its enantiopure forms are valuable chiral building blocks for fine-chemical synthesis. Here, we developed a fully biocatalytic Escherichi
content: γ-Valerolactone (GVL) is a biomass-derived platform chemical with broad industrial applications, while its enantiopure forms are valuable chiral building blocks for fine-chemical synthesis. Here, we developed a fully biocatalytic Escherichia coli whole-cell cascade for the stereodivergent conversion of levulinic acid (LA) to enantiopure ( R )- or ( S )-GVL. The modular system integrates stereocomplementary LA reduction by engineered dehydrogenases, formate dehydrogenase (FDH)-dependent nicotinamide cofactor regeneration, and 4-hydroxyvalerate (4HV) lactonization by periplasmically targeted engineered paraoxonase-1 (ePON1). Periplasmic targeting enhanced apparent whole-cell GVL formation from 4HV by 8.2-fold relative to the non-targeted construct. The integrated one-pot whole-cell cascades produced ( R )-GVL and ( S )-GVL in 64.5% and 52.0% yields, respectively, with >99.9% enantiomeric excess for both products, exceeding the maximum 4HV-to-GVL lactonization fraction previously reported for a PON1-based biological GVL production system. The cascade was further applied to LA-containing streams generated from food-waste-derived biomass. These streams naturally contained co-produced formate at approximately 1.0–1.5 molar equivalents relative to LA, closely matching the stoichiometric reducing-equivalent requirement for FDH-dependent cofactor regeneration and enabling bioconversion without exogenous formate supplementation. Using these biomass-derived streams, GVL yields reached up to 38.3% and 70.0% through the ( R )- and ( S )-routes, respectively. Importantly, formate, which would otherwise contribute to the downstream separation burden during LA purification, was directly utilized as an intrinsic reducing-power source, potentially reducing both separation requirements and the need for external formate supplementation. These results establish a modular whole-cell strategy for highly enantioselective and stereodivergent GVL production while coupling renewable LA upgrading with direct valorization of a biomass-derived coproduct.

title: Response-associated changes in DHA and in vitro involvement of PPARγ-RXRα signaling in macrophage immunometabolic modulation following HIFU ablation
summary: High-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) induces local tissue ablation and subsequent immune and metabolic changes, but the relationship between these changes and macrophage function remains unclear. We prospectively followed 57 patients wi
content: High-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) induces local tissue ablation and subsequent immune and metabolic changes, but the relationship between these changes and macrophage function remains unclear. We prospectively followed 57 patients with uterine fibroids undergoing HIFU and analyzed longitudinal plasma, urine, and hair metabolomes at four time points. Candidate metabolites were further examined in THP-1-derived macrophages using functional assays, cellular metabolomics, RNA sequencing, pathway inhibition, and patient-serum treatment. Single-cell transcriptomic data were also analyzed to assess macrophage-related cellular interactions in fibroid tissue. Among the metabolites detected, docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) showed response-associated changes across all three biospecimens. In in vitro assays, DHA treatment was associated with increased migration, phagocytosis, ACP activity, IL-10 secretion, and M2-associated gene expression, while reducing TNF-α, IL-6, iNOS, and intracellular lipid accumulation. DHA also altered fatty-acid and central-carbon metabolism and was associated with changes in PPAR signaling. Pharmacological inhibition of PPARγ or RXRα attenuated the DHA-induced functional and metabolic responses, implicating the involvement of the PPARγ-RXRα pathway. Serum from patients with sustained high HIFU response similarly enhanced macrophage phagocytosis, an effect that was reduced by pathway inhibition, though this cannot be attributed exclusively to DHA. Single-cell analysis further contextualized macrophage interactions with stromal and immune cell populations in fibroid tissue, though treatment- or DHA-induced dynamics cannot be directly inferred from this dataset. Overall, these findings suggest that response-associated changes in DHA may be linked to macrophage functional remodeling after HIFU through the involvement of PPARγ–RXRα signaling, providing a basis for further investigation of post-ablation immunometabolic responses.

title: Engineering properties, durability, microstructural, and sustainability characteristics of concrete made with LECA aggregate as an alternative to conventional coarse aggregate
summary: The purpose of this research is to examine M25 grade concrete which incorporates unsoaked Light Expanded Clay Aggregate (LECA) as a substitute at 0% – 50% levels. Performance of freshly mixed concrete was evaluated based on slump test. Hard
content: The purpose of this research is to examine M25 grade concrete which incorporates unsoaked Light Expanded Clay Aggregate (LECA) as a substitute at 0% – 50% levels. Performance of freshly mixed concrete was evaluated based on slump test. Hardened concrete was tested for density, compressive strength, split tensile strength and flexural strength at 28 days. The mixes were also assessed for durability through acid and sulphate mass loss, water absorption and Rapid Chloride Penetration Testing (RCPT). Micro-structural characteristics were evaluated using Scanning Electron Microscopy-Energy Dispersive X-ray (SEM–EDX) analysis and sustainability was evaluated using both embodied energy and carbon (CO₂) emissions. The results also showed that a strong linear relationship exists between compressive strengths and densities (R 2 ≈ 0.98). Based on the experimental results, LECA replacement levels of 20–25% gave the most favourable trade-off between compressive strength retention and concrete density reduction, giving compressive strengths of 17–19 MPa (compared to 31.45 MPa for the control mix) while reducing concrete density by 15–20%. In terms of durability, although indications of increased water absorption, chloride penetration ability and mass loss were noted as the LECA content increased these levels exhibited acceptable levels of performance as per the American Concrete Institute (ACI) 213R-14. SEM–EDX analysis showed that the interfacial transition zone became more refined. There was less accumulation of calcium hydroxide, which helped create stronger mechanical bonding between the aggregate and the paste. The use of LECA increases the embodied energy of concrete but reduces its density, thereby lowering the dead load on the structure and may contribute to long-term sustainability benefits such as reduced operational and structural demand.

title: Tambaqui ( Colossoma macropomum ) Production in Recirculating Aquaculture Systems ( RAS ): Evidence, Management Requirements and Research Gaps
summary: ABSTRACT Tambaqui ( Colossoma macropomum ) is an important commercial fish species in Latin America and Asia, where its production primarily relies on pond farming and net cage culture. The need for more controlled and sustainable productio
content: ABSTRACT Tambaqui ( Colossoma macropomum ) is an important commercial fish species in Latin America and Asia, where its production primarily relies on pond farming and net cage culture. The need for more controlled and sustainable production systems has increased interest in recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS). This narrative review, based on a structured literature search, synthesizes current evidence on tambaqui production in RAS throughout its production cycle. Available studies demonstrate successful production from larviculture and juvenile rearing through fattening and broodstock development, including induced reproduction. The review also examines management practices involving stocking density, temperature, feeding and nutrition, behavioral management, feed restriction, and anesthetics during handling. Evidence is strongest for larviculture and juvenile rearing under controlled experimental conditions, whereas fattening and broodstock production are promising but require further commercial‐scale validation. Despite these advances, further research is needed to validate the available findings across larger and commercial‐scale systems, improve the reporting of engineering and operational parameters, and expand knowledge on carrying capacity, techno‐economic performance, energy demand, long‐term fish welfare, and genetic management. Overall, RAS represents a technically viable and promising strategy for tambaqui production. However, commercial expansion requires system‐specific validation integrating biological performance, fish welfare, engineering efficiency, energy use, and economic viability.

title: Multi-parametric study of heterogeneous kinetics and burn rate regime transitions in carbohydrate-KNO3 solid energetic mixtures
summary: This study presents a parametric investigation into the physical, thermodynamic, and localized linear reaction kinetics of KNO 3 and carbohydrate-based renewable solid propellant formulations evaluated as sustainable alternatives to traditi
content: This study presents a parametric investigation into the physical, thermodynamic, and localized linear reaction kinetics of KNO 3 and carbohydrate-based renewable solid propellant formulations evaluated as sustainable alternatives to traditional pyrotechnic compositions. Five distinct fuel-oxidizer matrices, including Sorbitol, Sucrose, Dextrose, a 50/50 Sucrose-Sorbitol blend, and a classic black powder benchmark, were evaluated across twenty-five formulation variations to isolate the coupled effects of condensed-phase molecular structure, oxidizer particle size distributions, moisture-induced thermal sinks, and heterogeneous transition metal oxide catalysts (Fe 2 O 3 ) paired with reactive carbon additives. Structural packing characterization showed that sucrose-based matrices achieved peak packing efficiency, yielding a minimum baseline porosity of 4.73% and a relative density of 0.953. Linear burn rate testing conducted at 0.1 MPa demonstrated that shifting from fine ( 45 to 75 μ m ) to coarse ( > 250 μ m ) oxidizer fractions significantly depressed linear burn rates ( r b ) , while an average moisture uptake of ∼ 2.23 wt % introduced significant endothermic phase-change sinks that degraded r b by up to 46% in highly hygroscopic matrices. Pearson correlation tracking across grouped datasets reveals an exploratory statistical shift in the underlying combustion mechanisms: baseline carbohydrate formulations are heavily governed by a morphologically influenced regime dictated by bulk porosity and molecular complexity, whereas the incorporation of transition metal oxides (Fe 2 O 3 ) and reactive carbon black, transitions the flame front into a thermochemically dominated propagation regime heavily dictated by the adiabatic flame temperature ( R = + 0.933 ). Under optimized catalytic conditions, the sucrose-based matrix achieved a peak burn rate of 9.85 mm / s , fundamentally outperforming the metallized pyrotechnic benchmark ( 8 . 50 mm / s ). These findings provide a unified empirical framework explaining how physical inter-particle transport barriers interact with gas-phase thermochemical kinetics to dictate solid-phase deflagration behavior.

title: Achieving Cyclic Structural Stability in 20% Si/C Anodes via a Hydroxyl-Rich Ternary Copolymer Binder
summary: Abstract Silicon (Si) is a promising anode material for high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries owing to its high theoretical specific capacity of ~3600 mAh g⁻¹. However, its large volume change during cycling causes severe mechanical deg
content: Abstract Silicon (Si) is a promising anode material for high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries owing to its high theoretical specific capacity of ~3600 mAh g⁻¹. However, its large volume change during cycling causes severe mechanical degradation and rapid capacity fading. Herein, we developed a series of functional binders by terpolymerizing acrylic acid and acrylonitrile with different functional monomers to improve the mechanical stability of Si/carbon (Si/C) anodes. In particular, hydroxyl-containing 2-hydroxyethyl acrylate (HEA) and 2-hydroxypropyl acrylate (HPA) promote hydrogen bonding with the Si surface and impart self-healing capability to the resulting PAHEA and PAHPA binders, whereas ethoxyethoxyethyl acrylate (EEA), without hydroxyl functionality, does not exhibit this behavior. The 20% SiC anodes with PAHEA and PAHPA deliver discharge capacities of 650.91 and 644.13 mAh g⁻¹, respectively, at 0.1C. Corresponding 1 Ah pouch cells retain 81.26% and 78.22% of their initial capacities after 600 cycles at 1C. These results demonstrate that hydroxyl-functionalized copolymer binders can effectively enhance the structural stability and cycling durability of Si/C anodes, providing a practical strategy for the development of high-performance silicon-based batteries.

title: Clinical advances in proton spatially fractionated radiation therapy
summary: Abstract Spatially fractionated radiation therapy (SFRT) intentionally creates a heterogeneous dose distribution within a tumor, with alternating high-dose peaks and low-dose valleys. This approach offers a different route to dose escalatio
content: Abstract Spatially fractionated radiation therapy (SFRT) intentionally creates a heterogeneous dose distribution within a tumor, with alternating high-dose peaks and low-dose valleys. This approach offers a different route to dose escalation for bulky, locally advanced tumors and lesions near organs at risk. Proton SFRT (pSFRT) combines this spatial heterogeneity with the finite range of protons, rapid distal dose fall-off, and pencil beam scanning. It may therefore reduce dose outside the target while preserving intratumoral peak-valley patterns. Current pSFRT platforms include proton GRID, proton LATTICE, and proton minibeam radiation therapy, but their clinical maturity differs markedly. Available studies support the technical feasibility and short-term tolerability of pSFRT and suggest potential benefits in tumor control and symptom relief across several cancer types. However, the evidence base is limited by cohort sizes, substantial disease heterogeneity, variability in treatment approaches, frequent use of subsequent radiation therapy or systemic therapy, and relatively short follow-up periods. No included comparative clinical study demonstrated an advantage over photon SFRT or conventional proton therapy. Additional barriers include range and motion uncertainty, inconsistent characterization of peak and valley doses, patient-specific quality assurance, limited radiobiological modeling, and uncertain patient selection. This review examines the evolution of SFRT, the physical rationale for proton delivery, the main pSFRT techniques, published human evidence, and current translational challenges. It also outlines priorities for dose-reporting standards, multicenter prospective studies, and rational integration with systemic therapies, and highlights major unresolved questions that must be addressed before broader clinical application.

title: Janus Vapor‐Gap Membrane Coupling Superhydrophobic Evaporation and Superhydrophilic Condensation for Pressure‐Driven Desalination
summary: ABSTRACT Pressure‐driven distillation (PD) has emerged as a transformative technology for harnessing non‐conventional water resources, leveraging hydraulic pressure to accelerate vapor generation and transport across vapor‐gap membranes. De
content: ABSTRACT Pressure‐driven distillation (PD) has emerged as a transformative technology for harnessing non‐conventional water resources, leveraging hydraulic pressure to accelerate vapor generation and transport across vapor‐gap membranes. Despite its promise, the paradigm of conventional PD is fundamentally constrained by overlooked thermodynamic energy barrier, which severely limits overall process efficiency. Herein, we report the first conceptualization and fabrication of an ultra‐selective Janus vapor‐gap membrane engineered explicitly for PD, featuring a superhydrophilic, highly crystalline, and defect‐free covalent organic framework (COF) layer that decisively overcomes this limitation. The Janus membrane embodies a bilayered architecture with the upper layer functions as a vapor generation zone, sustaining a robust gas‐liquid interface for efficient evaporation, while the lower layer serves as a confined condensation zone that significantly reduces the energy barrier for vapor‐to‐liquid phase transition. This strategic spatial decoupling of evaporation and condensation enables a synergistic enhancement of the entire PD process. The resulting Janus membrane achieves near‐complete rejections of nonvolatile solutes. In practical desalination scenarios, it demonstrates outstanding anti‐fouling and chlorine resistance. This work not only highlights the potential of crystalline porous materials in PD technology, but also provides a pathway for architected Janus membranes that transcend the efficiency limits of conventional desalination processes.

title: Short-term PM10 exposure and hospital admissions for respiratory illness in children under five in Rio de Janeiro: a distributed lag study with negative-control evaluation of fifteen estimators
summary: Abstract Daily time-series studies of air pollution and health rest on modeling choices that fit statistics cannot validate, since a bias shared by every candidate model is invisible to criteria computed on the same data. This study linked
content: Abstract Daily time-series studies of air pollution and health rest on modeling choices that fit statistics cannot validate, since a bias shared by every candidate model is invisible to criteria computed on the same data. This study linked daily hospital admissions for respiratory illness among children under five in Rio de Janeiro to daily PM10 from eight municipal monitoring stations over 2011 to 2019, fitting a negative binomial distributed lag model across a 14-day window. Every estimator was refitted to exposure series shifted by one and two whole years, which preserves seasonality while breaking day-to-day correspondence, so any surviving association is not an exposure effect. Across 37,137 admissions, a 10 µg/m³ increase in PM10 was associated with a 3.75% rise in admissions (95% CI 0.63 to 6.97), of which same-day exposure recovered only 1.67%, and an estimated 449 admissions (80 to 795) were attributable to concentrations above the World Health Organization 2021 daily guideline. Eleven of fifteen estimators passed the control and four neural estimators failed. Seasonal adjustment at four degrees of freedom per year returned a near-null estimate whose shifted controls reached 6.53 percentage points, revealing broken identification rather than absence of an effect.

title: Honeycombs Across Material Classes: A Mechanism‐Based Review of Design Strategies
summary: ABSTRACT Honeycomb cores and related lattice and triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures provide lightweight load support, energy absorption, recovery, and multifunctionality, but their performance can degrade when material, manuf
content: ABSTRACT Honeycomb cores and related lattice and triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures provide lightweight load support, energy absorption, recovery, and multifunctionality, but their performance can degrade when material, manufacturing route, interfaces, or component boundaries change. This review examines how cell‐wall bending, buckling, folding, self‐contact, and load transfer interact across service conditions. Studies of conventional, auxetic, chiral, graded, hierarchical, and folded honeycombs, sandwich panels, and related lattice and TPMS structures made from polymers, polymer composites, metals, and ceramics are compared at three levels: cell‐scale mechanisms, progressive‐collapse control, and structural integration. Geometry biases the available deformation modes, while constitutive behavior, rate sensitivity, fracture, viscoelasticity, reinforcement, interfaces, and manufacturing defects influence the active mode and collapse sequence. Curvature, grading, hierarchy, folding, multimaterial design, and reinforcement can redistribute deformation and delay localization, subject to initial peak force, densification strain, joint integrity, and process variability. Transfer from cells to components requires characterization of as‐manufactured geometry, defects, face‐core load transfer, environmental exposure, repeated loading, and service‐level validation. The review therefore separates geometry‐driven improvements from manufacturing effects and specifies a qualification path from material coupons and cells to panels and components.

title: Retaining Atmospheric and Biogenic Carbon in the Global Materials Economy
summary: As the world faces the prospect of exceeding 1.5°C of warming, cutting emissions remains the priority. But bringing temperatures back down will also require removing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. This new UNEP working paper, Retaining
content: As the world faces the prospect of exceeding 1.5°C of warming, cutting emissions remains the priority. But bringing temperatures back down will also require removing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. This new UNEP working paper, Retaining Atmospheric and Biogenic Carbon in the Global Materials Economy, explores how materials used in buildings, infrastructure and everyday products could help retain atmospheric carbon, turning industrial value chains from sources of emissions into potential carbon stores. The paper examines the technologies, policies, standards and investments needed to scale these solutions, while ensuring credible climate benefits.

title: Effect of Lanthanum Doping on Spray‐Deposited ZnO Thin Films for Carbon Monoxide Gas‐Sensing Applications
summary: Carbon monoxide (CO) detection is crucial in several areas, such as environmental monitoring, industrial safety, and health care, due to its colorless, odorless, and highly toxic nature even at low concentrations. In this study, we report t
content: Carbon monoxide (CO) detection is crucial in several areas, such as environmental monitoring, industrial safety, and health care, due to its colorless, odorless, and highly toxic nature even at low concentrations. In this study, we report the effect of lanthanum (La) doping (0.2–0.8 at%) on zinc oxide (ZnO) thin films to develop a cost‐effective, efficient, and eco‐friendly room‐temperature CO gas sensor. A low‐cost spray deposition method was used to fabricate pure and La‐doped ZnO thin films to examine their optical, morphological, structural, and CO gas‐sensing characteristics. X‐ray diffraction (XRD) investigation confirmed the formation of a hexagonal wurtzite structure free of secondary phases. Surface morphology analyzed by atomic force microscopy (AFM) revealed a nonmonotonic fluctuation (11.2–44.4) in root‐mean‐square (RMS) roughness with doping concentration, reflecting changes in grain development and refinement. UV–vis spectroscopy showed that films are highly transparent (>80%) across the visible to near‐infrared region. Gas‐sensing results showed that La doping greatly improves sensing performance; 0.6 at% La‐doped film showed the highest response (142%) with fast, repeatable response/recovery behavior (24.4 s/44 s) at room temperature, whereas pure ZnO showed a modest response. These findings highlight the significance of optimal La doping concentration for effective CO gas detection.

title: Language Model Empowered Cross-Scale Framework for Urban Air Pollution Monitoring, Diffusion Analysis and Early Warning
source: Transactions on Environment Energy and Earth Sciences
summary: Modern urban morphology and local meteorological conditions create significant variations in pollutant dispersion across scales. Under global climate change and rapid urbanization, air pollution threatens public health and sustainable devel
content: Modern urban morphology and local meteorological conditions create significant variations in pollutant dispersion across scales. Under global climate change and rapid urbanization, air pollution threatens public health and sustainable development, yet traditional monitoring fails to address both micro-level protection and macro-level governance—especially within the “street canyon–residential area” microenvironment where daily human activity concentrates. To bridge this gap, this study first develops an LLM-enhanced CFD system with atmospheric stability metrics to model pollutant dispersion from street canyons to residential areas. Since micro-level research cannot cover large regions, we further propose a context-aware human-machine collaborative drone framework integrating multimodal sensing, XGBoost prediction, and natural language interaction for autonomous surveillance, source localization, and short-term alerts. Results show that under stable conditions, peak CO in street canyons exceeds 80 µg/m³—over three times higher than under unstable conditions (5–35µg/m³)—with high-concentration plumes traveling long distances to downstream residential areas. The drone system achieves 0.34 m localization accuracy, a 1‑hour CO prediction RMSE of 2.3 µg/m³, 98% natural language interpretation accuracy, and sub‑3‑minute response to sudden pollution events. This cross-scale framework unifies micro-mechanisms and macro-monitoring, offering a practical solution for urban air quality management and healthy city construction.

title: Punched zinc-aluminium electrodes for efficient treatment of soap wastewater: Original scientific paper
source: Journal of Electrochemical Science and Engineering
summary: This study investigates the efficiency of the electrocoagulation process using punched zinc and aluminium electrodes for the treatment of soap and detergent wastewater. Although the industry generates relatively small volumes of effluent du
content: This study investigates the efficiency of the electrocoagulation process using punched zinc and aluminium electrodes for the treatment of soap and detergent wastewater. Although the industry generates relatively small volumes of effluent during production, significant environmental concerns arise from its widespread domestic and industrial discharge. The objective was to optimize key operational parameters for maximum chemical oxygen demand (COD) and turbidity removal. Experimental design was carried out using response surface methodology with a Box-Behnken design to evaluate the effects of voltage, electrolysis time, and electrode distance. Optimal conditions were identified at 30 V, 60 min electrolysis time, and 2 cm electrode spacing, achieving removal efficiencies of 87.22 % for COD and 85.7 % for turbidity. Statistical analysis using ANOVA confirmed the reliability of the quadratic model, showing strong agreement between predicted and experimental results. The findings demonstrate that punched electrodes significantly enhance EC performance, and further development of advanced electrode materials could improve treatment efficiency.

title: Microstructure regulation of hollow AuAg alloy nanobowls toward high-performance electrochemical urea biosensing
summary: AuAg alloys possess excellent electrical conductivity and biocompatibility. AuAg alloy nanobowls (AuAg NBs) were fabricated using a self-assembled polystyrene microsphere film as the template via an in situ galvanic replacement reaction bet
content: AuAg alloys possess excellent electrical conductivity and biocompatibility. AuAg alloy nanobowls (AuAg NBs) were fabricated using a self-assembled polystyrene microsphere film as the template via an in situ galvanic replacement reaction between Ag and HAuCl4. The AuAg NBs exhibited a hierarchical hollow architecture consisting of large bowl-like structures containing smaller bowls. By employing the AuAg NBs as an electrode-modifying material and integrating them with urease, we constructed a glassy carbon electrode (GCE)/AuAg NBs/urease electrochemical sensor for the detection of urea. The unique hierarchical nanobowl structure provides a large electrochemically accessible surface area for urease immobilization, while density functional theory (DFT) calculations using a simplified Gly-His model indicate a favorable local adsorption tendency on AuAg NBs. In addition, the excellent biocompatibility of the AuAg alloy helps preserve the bioactivity of urease, enabling the specific recognition and catalytic hydrolysis of urea. The as-prepared sensor exhibited a good linear response with a detection limit as low as 6.7 μM. The GCE/AuAg NBs/urease electrode exhibited a 135.5% higher potential response than the GCE/AuAg NPs/urease electrode. Urea in tear fluid is a potential biomarker for the diagnosis of dry eye disease (DED). Furthermore, the AuAg NBs were applied to screen-printed electrodes, demonstrating the potential of this platform for tear-based urea sensing and future point-of-care applications related to DED screening.

title: Photoexcited Charge Dynamics in Plasmonic Copper Nanoparticles Combined with Copper Oxides Studied by Transient Absorption Spectroscopy
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
summary: Abstract The steady-state and ultrafast optical properties of Cu2O and CuO thin films─both as standalone materials and in combination with Cu nanoparticles to form metallic-core@oxide-shell structures─are studied. By combining transient abs
content: Abstract The steady-state and ultrafast optical properties of Cu2O and CuO thin films─both as standalone materials and in combination with Cu nanoparticles to form metallic-core@oxide-shell structures─are studied. By combining transient absorption spectroscopy and steady-state optical measurements, the carrier and plasmon dynamics governing these oxide and oxide–metal hybrid systems have been elucidated. For Cu2O, above-bandgap excitation reveals photobleaching and photoinduced absorption associated with the 1s-like violet exciton. The transient response exhibits a biexponential decay that suggests an ultrafast relaxation into dark excitons, which are long-lived and from which the recombination takes place. In Cu@Cu2O, excitation of the localized surface plasmon resonance induces a transfer of excitation from the Cu core to the Cu2O shell, resulting in a perturbation of the excitonic signal of Cu2O. In CuO and Cu@CuO, complex transient spectral features indicate the presence of short- and long-lived components, while enhanced CuO-related photoinduced absorption in Cu@CuO following visible light excitation is ascribed to the presence of Cu nanoparticles. Overall, these findings demonstrate that coupling Cu nanoparticles with their oxides in a core–shell geometry enhances light–matter interaction across visible wavelengths, enabling a more efficient coupling of the visible and IR ranges to these semiconductors.

title: Immune functions of vascular structural cells are endothelial communication, smooth muscle transdifferentiation and lymphatic immune regulation
summary: The vascular wall maintains structural integrity, regulates blood flow, and supports tissue functions and homeostasis. Evidence also shows that its structural cells participate in immune sensing, inflammation and tissue remodeling. Vascular
content: The vascular wall maintains structural integrity, regulates blood flow, and supports tissue functions and homeostasis. Evidence also shows that its structural cells participate in immune sensing, inflammation and tissue remodeling. Vascular endothelial cells (ECs), vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs), and lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs) encounter different combinations of inflammatory, metabolic, mechanical, microbial, tissue and intracellular immune-derived signals. We propose here that their anatomical locations and cell-intrinsic programs shape distinct, context-dependent immune functions of vascular structural cell types. ECs act as immune communicators at the blood-tissue interface. In response to inflammatory cues, they produce cytokines and chemokines, express adhesion molecules, regulate vascular permeability, and direct leukocyte recruitment. VSMCs respond to persistent vessel wall stress through phenotypic plasticity, secretomes and transdifferentiation, adopting cell states that may support repair and plaque stability or contribute to fibrosis, calcification, and disease progression. LECs combine innate sensing with regulation of immune cell trafficking, antigen handling, peripheral tolerance, adaptive immune responses, and fluid balance. Single-cell transcriptomic studies also identify immune-associated signatures in other vascular structural cell populations, including fibroblasts and pericytes. However, these populations remain candidates whose immune functions require spatial lineage-resolved and functional validation. Together, ECs, VSMCs, and LECs illustrate complementary ways in which structural cells contribute to vascular immune regulation. Defining the novel mechanisms and disease contexts of these responses may reveal opportunities to moderate vascular inflammation and remodeling for development of new disease therapeutics.

title: Diffuse interstellar bands in nearby galaxies with MaNGA: environmental trends with metallicity, extinction, ionization, and star-forming activity
source: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
summary: Abstract Diffuse interstellar bands (DIBs) are absorption features of uncertain origin observed in the optical and near-infrared spectra of stars and galaxies. Although their correlation with dust extinction is well established, the physica
content: Abstract Diffuse interstellar bands (DIBs) are absorption features of uncertain origin observed in the optical and near-infrared spectra of stars and galaxies. Although their correlation with dust extinction is well established, the physical conditions governing their strength across different interstellar medium (ISM) environments remain poorly understood. We investigate the environmental dependence of the DIB λ5780 using spatially resolved MaNGA spectroscopy for 837 nearby galaxies spanning a broad range of stellar masses, star-formation rates, and ISM properties. Stellar and nebular parameters are derived via spectral fitting, while DIB absorption is measured from high-signal-to-noise spatially binned residual spectra. We detect the DIB λ5780 in 159 galaxies and report the most distant spatially resolved DIB detection to date, at 232 Mpc. The DIB λ5780 equivalent width correlates positively with both stellar and gas-phase extinction. DIB λ5780 is preferentially detected in regions of high extinction, near- or super-solar metallicity (12 + log (O/H) ≳ 8.5), and moderate specific star-formation rates (−10.5 ≲ log (sSFR/yr−1) ≲ −9). By contrast, it falls below our detection threshold in metal-poor or strongly ionized environments. It is rarely detected in regions with little or no recent star formation, with the few detections in such environments occurring primarily in regions driven by composite ionization. Our results indicate that DIB λ5780 is preferentially detected, within the sensitivity limits of the MaNGA data, in dust-rich, chemically evolved, and moderately ionized environments.

title: Exhumation Patterns Along the Eastern Foothills of Colombia Using Low Temperature Thermochronology and 3D Thermo‐Kinematic Modelling: Implications for Hydrocarbon Play Analysis
summary: ABSTRACT The Nunchía syncline located within the Colombian Eastern Foothills coincides with a depocenter, which was structurally controlled by the contractional deformation of the Guaicaramo and Yopal reverse faults during the Oligocene–Mio
content: ABSTRACT The Nunchía syncline located within the Colombian Eastern Foothills coincides with a depocenter, which was structurally controlled by the contractional deformation of the Guaicaramo and Yopal reverse faults during the Oligocene–Miocene. The syncline preserves a thick sedimentary succession primarily sourced from the Guyana Craton, with contributions from recycled sediments of the Eastern Cordillera and Venezuelan Andes. To constrain the regional thermal and exhumation history, we integrated new detrital ZHe ages with existing apatite fission‐track (AFT) and AHe datasets using ZRDAAM and Pecube thermokinematic modelling. Modelling across three key sectors—the Monterralo anticline, southwestern Nunchía syncline, and northeastern Nunchía syncline—reveals a complex, multi‐stage exhumation history characterised by three distinct events in each zone. In the Monterralo anticline and southwestern sector, exhumation spans Oligocene to late Miocene, with average denudation rates varying between moderate and high intervals. Notably, the northeastern Nunchía syncline records a well‐defined early exhumation phase during the Eocene, followed by accelerated cooling pulses in the late Oligocene and late Miocene. Our models suggest that nearly half of the modern relief was established during the Palaeocene–Eocene, with the current topography largely attained by the late Oligocene, except for the northeastern sector where significant relief amplification occurred more recently. These localised exhumation and burial phases align with major orogenic activity in the adjacent Eastern Cordillera and Venezuelan Andes. The identification of robust pre‐Oligocene exhumation provides compelling evidence for Eocene deformation and erosional denudation within the foothills, which is much earlier than previously recognised. This early tectonic activity could have controlled stratigraphic pinch‐outs and structural inversions, underscoring the potential for large, underexplored hydrocarbon traps analogous to those proven in neighbouring southern structural provinces.

title: Untersuchung des Einflusses von zwei ausgewählten Schadgasen auf die Tiergesundheit mittels Anwendung von Schadgassensoren in Masthühnerställen
source: Electronic Theses of LMU Munich (Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München)

title: Multifunctional Thermo‐Electronic Smart Fabrics Integrating Radiative Cooling and Energy Harvesting for Self‐Powered Intelligent Perception
summary: ABSTRACT Wearable smart fabrics with integrated thermal regulation and energy autonomy represent a transformative advancement in next‐generation wearable technologies. However, achieving synergistic multifunctionality with a signal platform
content: ABSTRACT Wearable smart fabrics with integrated thermal regulation and energy autonomy represent a transformative advancement in next‐generation wearable technologies. However, achieving synergistic multifunctionality with a signal platform remains a significant challenge. Herein, we present a multifunctional thermal management and self‐powered smart fabric (TMSPF) that seamlessly integrates passive radiative cooling (PRC) and triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) through a rationally designed functional architecture. The unique all‐fiber structure enables TMSPF good breathability and self‐cleaning properties, thereby providing a dry and comfortable microenvironment for the wearer. Notably, benefiting from the excellent dielectric properties of BaTiO 3 and interconnected porous fiber architecture, the TMSPF achieves excellent PRC capability (a maximum cooling temperature of ∼18.9°C under direct sunlight and a maximum cooling power of 105.9 W m −2 at daytime), as well as enhanced triboelectric output (170 V, 977 mW m −2 ) and high sensitivity (88.72 V kPa −1 ), enabling applications in power supply and intelligent perception. Moreover, TMSPF demonstrates broad application prospects in personal thermal management and raindrop energy harvesting. This synergistic integration effectively addresses the intrinsic trade‐off between energy harvesting and thermal comfort in conventional wearables. This work provides valuable insights into the design and fabrication of next‐generation wearable electronics with integrated thermal and energy functionalities.

title: Earth’s planetary-scale lake storage phenology
summary: Abstract Lakes, Earth’s largest store of liquid surface freshwater, record upstream hydroclimatic variability while mediating downstream flows(ref.1-4). This dual role is encoded in lake storage phenology – the magnitude, timing, and shape
content: Abstract Lakes, Earth’s largest store of liquid surface freshwater, record upstream hydroclimatic variability while mediating downstream flows(ref.1-4). This dual role is encoded in lake storage phenology – the magnitude, timing, and shape of seasonal storage changes – whose planetary organization and human modification remain poorly understood(ref.4-6). Here, we use wide-swath satellite altimetry(ref.7) to unveil storage phenology across 5.1 million lakes ≥1 ha worldwide through a four-level framework: individual-lake variability, planetary-scale cycle, recurrent archetypes, and process interpretation via storage–flow coupling. Individual-lake variability, structured by landscape setting, totals 3,047.5–3,571.2 Gt (74.4–119.2% above previous estimates(ref.5,6)), with reservoirs contributing disproportionately and smaller lakes exhibiting greater volume-normalized variability. Phenological asynchrony attenuates these fluctuations to a planetary-scale seasonal cycle of 636.7–928.8 Gt, roughly tripling river-channel variability(ref.8). Seven archetypes organize this diversity into coherent seasonal patterns, including a high-variability monsoonal mode whose late-season filling opposes global storage recession, dampening planetary variability by 40.1%. While lake storage often retains the seasonal signature of naturalized upstream flow, phase delays of ≥6 weeks characterize nearly half of natural-lake and three-quarters of reservoir storage variability, revealing substantial mediation through hydrologic memory and human regulation. These findings establish lake storage phenology as a measurable dimension of the terrestrial water cycle, linking hydroclimate, storage mediation, and anthropogenic imprint across scales.

title: Impedance‐Based Characterization of Oxidation Damage in C f /SiC Ceramic Matrix Composites
source: International Journal of Applied Ceramic Technology
summary: ABSTRACT Carbon fiber‐reinforced SiC ceramic matrix composites (C f /SiC composites) exhibit distinct oxidation damage characteristics at different temperatures, posing challenges for their nondestructive evaluation. This study combines imp
content: ABSTRACT Carbon fiber‐reinforced SiC ceramic matrix composites (C f /SiC composites) exhibit distinct oxidation damage characteristics at different temperatures, posing challenges for their nondestructive evaluation. This study combines impedance spectroscopy with microstructural characterization to assess oxidation damage in C f /SiC composites exposed to air at 800 and 1100°C. Microstructural observations showed that oxidation at 800°C predominantly degraded the carbon fibers and fiber/matrix interfaces. By contrast, oxidation at 1100°C promoted the growth of a surface SiO 2 layer, which partially impeded further oxygen ingress. Correlation analysis reveals that the low‐frequency capacitive response in the impedance spectroscopy was strongly associated with fiber/matrix interface oxidation and the resulting mass loss, whereas the high‐frequency capacitive response correlated closely with the thickness of the surface oxide layer. These findings demonstrate that impedance responses in different frequency ranges are selectively sensitive to distinct forms of oxidation damage. This work provides an experimental basis for the nondestructive characterization of oxidation damage in C f /SiC composites using impedance spectroscopy.

title: Multi‐Energy Coupling in Hierarchical Textiles for Photo‐Thermal‐Electric Conversion
summary: ABSTRACT Solar interfacial evaporation and thermoelectric generation coupled systems show promising application potential in seawater desalination and energy harvesting. However, a portion of the heat generated by photothermal conversion is
content: ABSTRACT Solar interfacial evaporation and thermoelectric generation coupled systems show promising application potential in seawater desalination and energy harvesting. However, a portion of the heat generated by photothermal conversion is used for interfacial evaporation, while the remaining heat continuously dissipates to the thermoelectric generator (TEG) module and the surrounding environment. Without proper regulation, such disordered heat dissipation not only reduces the evaporation heat utilization efficiency but also weakens the temperature difference driving force of TEG, thereby limiting the simultaneous enhancement of water‐power cogeneration. In this study, a sandwich evaporator (SE) system is proposed based on solar absorption pathway optimization and hierarchical heat flow regulation. A polypyrrole photothermal layer is in situ constructed on cotton, and a V‐shaped structure is employed to enhance solar harvesting, achieving efficient photothermal conversion. An independent water supply layer is introduced to suppress ineffective heat conduction. Meanwhile, a water‐cooling layer is integrated at the cold sink of TEG, enabling synergistic cooling and waste heat evaporation. Finally, SE achieves an evaporation rate of 2.18 kg·m −2 ·h −1 and a peak power density of 224.15 mW·m −2 under 1 kW·m −2 solar radiation. This system demonstrates good energy conversion performance, providing an effective strategy for efficient solar‐driven water‐power cogeneration in off‐grid environments.

title: Engineering Surface Reconstruction of Perovskite Oxides through Vanadium Doping and Alkalinity Regulation for Enhanced Oxygen Evolution
summary: Abstract Lattice oxygen participation in perovskite electrocatalysts can significantly enhance oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity, yet it often compromises long-term durability due to severe surface reconstruction and bulk degradation
content: Abstract Lattice oxygen participation in perovskite electrocatalysts can significantly enhance oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity, yet it often compromises long-term durability due to severe surface reconstruction and bulk degradation. Here, we deliberately engineer surface reconstruction to reconcile activity and stability by preconstructing a highly active and robust (oxy)hydroxide layer on a perovskite oxide. A vanadium-doped perovskite, SrFe0.25Co0.25Ni0.18V0.02Mo0.3O3 (SFCNM-V0.02), is rationally designed, in which V-doping facilitates rapid OH–-induced reconstruction. Preimmersion in concentrated KOH accelerates the formation of a dense and stable amorphous (oxy)hydroxide layer that suppresses bulk dissolution while serving as the dominant catalytic active phase. Consequently, SFCNM-V0.02 delivers a low overpotential of 265 mV at 10 mA cm–2 and exceptional operational stability exceeding 1100 h in 1 M KOH. Furthermore, by correlating the degree of surface reconstruction with catalytic activity, we analyzed the origin of the pH-dependent variation observed in this work, which provides useful implications for appropriately evaluating pH-dependent behaviors in electrocatalysis. This work demonstrates that controlled surface reconstruction fundamentally governs OER performance in perovskite oxides and provides practical design principles for durable, high-efficiency OER electrocatalysts.

title: Unveiling fibre alignment in 3D-printed FRCC using particle cleansing considering combined effects of nozzle size, fibre length, and volume fraction
summary: Fibre alignment strongly influences the mechanical behaviour of 3D-printed fibre-reinforced cementitious composites (FRCC). However, conventional characterisation methods such as μCT, BSE imaging, and mechanical testing require long prepara
content: Fibre alignment strongly influences the mechanical behaviour of 3D-printed fibre-reinforced cementitious composites (FRCC). However, conventional characterisation methods such as μCT, BSE imaging, and mechanical testing require long preparation time and cannot support rapid evaluation. This study proposes a particle cleansing method that enables fibre orientation to be assessed within approximately 1 h. By dissolving the fresh cementitious matrix using an ethanol–water solution at a flow rate of 50 mL/min, fibre networks were exposed with minimal disturbance and captured. The method successfully differentiated randomly distributed fibres in mould-cast FRCC samples (average angle at 45.8°) from aligned fibres in 3D-printed FRCC samples (average angle at 11.1°). Furthermore, the combined effects of fibre volume fraction and length on fibre alignment under nozzle extrusion were investigated. Specifically, under the constraint of a narrower nozzle, higher fibre volume fractions (up to 2.0%) and increased fibre lengths (up to 18 mm) collectively enhanced fibre alignment along the extrusion direction, which potentially contributed to the improvements in ultimate tensile strength and strain capacity. This study not only provides a fast and practical tool for fresh-state fibre orientation characterisation but also offers novel mechanistic insights into enhancing fibre alignment in 3D-printed FRCC.HighlightsNovel particle cleansing rapidly assesses fibre alignment in 3D-printed FRCC.Cleansing results are highly consistent with cross-sectional BSE imaging analysis.Higher fibre volume fractions significantly enhance fibre alignment during extrusion.Extending fibre length also yields superior alignment along the printing direction.Narrower nozzles amplify combined fibre alignment driven by fibre length and dosage.

title: A general multi-criteria decision-support framework through energy-seismic life cycle cost evaluation of exterior wall systems
summary: Enhancing the performance of residential buildings requires the integrated consideration of energy efficiency and seismic resilience within a life cycle cost (LCC) framework. This study proposes a general decision-support multi-criteria met
content: Enhancing the performance of residential buildings requires the integrated consideration of energy efficiency and seismic resilience within a life cycle cost (LCC) framework. This study proposes a general decision-support multi-criteria methodology for assessing the LCC performance of exterior wall configurations (EWCs) in mid-rise reinforced-concrete (RC) residential buildings. The methodology jointly accounts for operational energy and carbon costs, initial construction costs, and seismic repair costs over the building life cycle by integrating analytical thermal transmittance (U-value) calculations, DesignBuilder-based energy simulations, and LCC analysis. The proposed framework is demonstrated and validated through a representative case study involving residential buildings in Türkiye. In line with the national thermal standards, Türkiye’s six climate zones were grouped into three clustered climate categories based on overlapping thermal requirements and market constraints. For each category, 36 baseline EWCs were generated by combining alternative masonry units, insulation materials, and exterior finishes. A Pareto-optimality-based screening was then applied to identify eight EWCs that provide the best trade-off between unit construction cost and thermal transmittance. These configurations were subsequently evaluated in the six climate zones where they meet regulatory limits, and across four seismic design categories defined by national seismic standards, yielding a total of 144 climate-seismic EWC scenarios. The findings reveal that the EWCs with the lowest unit construction cost yield the minimum LCC, underscoring the decisive role of unit construction cost in early-stage decision-making.

title: Design, Synthesis, Biological Evaluation, Molecular Docking, Pharmacophore Modelling and 3D-QSAR Analysis of Novel Substituted Imidazolidine Derivatives as Potential Antimicrobial Agents
summary: The present study reports the combined experimental and computational approaches to investigate the antimicrobial potential of 104 structurally diverse substituted imidazolidine derivatives. Selected compounds were synthesized based on thei
content: The present study reports the combined experimental and computational approaches to investigate the antimicrobial potential of 104 structurally diverse substituted imidazolidine derivatives. Selected compounds were synthesized based on their docking results and characterized by IR, 1H NMR and 13C NMR spectroscopy and mass spectrometry. Their antimicrobial activity was assessed in vitro against selected bacterial and fungal strains. Among the tested compounds, derivatives 47 and 52 exhibited the strongest activity, with compound 47 showing antibacterial activity comparable to that of amoxicillin. Molecular docking studies against lanosterol 14α-demethylase (CYP51; PDB ID: 1E9X) were performed to explore the possible interactions of the compounds within the enzyme-binding pocket. Compounds 47 and 52 achieved docking scores of -10.4 and -10.3 kcal/mol, respectively, while compounds 15, 18 and 21 each recorded a score of -10.2 kcal/mol. The docked complexes exhibited hydrogen bonding, π-π stacking, π-cation, π-alkyl and hydrophobic interactions. Pharmacophore modelling identified one hydrogen-bond acceptor feature, one hydrophobic feature and three aromatic-ring features associated with the activity profile. The optimized three-dimensional quantitative structure–activity relationship (3D-QSAR) model yielded an (R2) value of 0.6682, a (Q2) value of 0.3463, a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.7497 and a stability value of 0.847. Analysis of the steric, electrostatic and hydrophobic contour maps provided further insight into the influence of substituent identity and spatial arrangement on antimicrobial activity. The experimental findings identify compounds 47 and 52 as promising candidates for further optimization of imidazolidine-based antimicrobial agents.

title: A mechanistic insight into the role of triplet states in excited-state deactivation of dibenzothiophene: a new fate for green chemistry
summary: The environmental impact of petroleum derivatives is a current threat which needs to be studied and tackled in the present and near future. In this context, obtaining new insight about the degradation and remediation possibilities of polyar
content: The environmental impact of petroleum derivatives is a current threat which needs to be studied and tackled in the present and near future. In this context, obtaining new insight about the degradation and remediation possibilities of polyaromatic sulphur heterocycles, and particularly dibenzothiophene, is a challenge requiring the full attention of the academic community. Thus, we have studied the dibenzothiophene excited state decay from a theoretical perspective, resorting to multiconfigurational methods, in order to obtain a full photophysical picture which until now was incomplete. Our results reveal the transitory generation of triplet species which supports the possible reactivity and desulphurization processes which were recently reported for this system.

title: Antimicrobial and cytotoxic activities of Ag/AgCl nanoparticles biosynthesized by Bacillus cereus against multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa from hospital environments
summary: Hospital surfaces can serve as reservoirs for multidrug resistant (MDR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa․ Continuous and effective surface-directed decontamination strategies are required․ The current study investigates the use of Bacillus cereus-bio
content: Hospital surfaces can serve as reservoirs for multidrug resistant (MDR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa․ Continuous and effective surface-directed decontamination strategies are required․ The current study investigates the use of Bacillus cereus-biosynthesized Ag/AgCl nanoparticles as an antimicrobial surface-directed decontamination strategy for drug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolated from hospital samples․ An environmental screening of three hospitals found P. aeruginosa in 23 of 224 environmental swabs (10․3%), with sinks being the most contaminated sampling location (39.1% of positive samples)․ Phenotypic profiling revealed a concerning resistance spectrum: 26.1% MDR, 13% XDR, and 4.3% PDR, including a 13.0% incidence of colistin resistance. This is the first time that Ag/AgCl NPs have been biogenic produced from Bacillus cereus biomass‚ incorporating hospital environmental surveillance and the antimicrobial resistance profile with Ag/AgCl NPs biosynthesis and functional characterization toward MDR‚ XDR‚ and PDR local P. aeruginosa isolates‚ as well as the antibacterial and antibiofilm activity assessment of the synthesized Ag/AgCl NPs․ Comprehensive physicochemical characterization (UV-Vis, FTIR, XRD, TEM, FESEM, and zeta potential) confirmed the production of quasi-spherical, face-centered cubic (FCC) Ag/AgCl nanoparticles with a mean crystallite size of 9.58 nm and a zeta potential of − 30.7 mV, indicating moderate to good colloidal stability. The NPs demonstrated robust antibacterial activity, with a MIC of 24 µg/mL against all six tested P. aeruginosa strains, and achieved near-complete biofilm inhibition at concentrations ≥ 24 µg/mL. The Ag/AgCl nanoparticles had cytotoxicity in HaCaT keratinocytes lower than MIC concentration (IC50 = 13.8 µg/mL; SI = 0․575)‚ and the excessive cytotoxicity against normal cells may limit their clinical usage․ Nevertheless‚ additional studies may be required to pursue the use of unmodified Ag/AgCl nanoparticles as antimicrobial agents on vertical and horizontal surfaces in hospitals to eliminate drug-resistant P. aeruginosa from inanimate reservoirs․ Studies to optimize and standardize surface-disinfection methodologies will help determine the practical and safety implications of these systems․ These findings support the potential application of the biosynthesized Ag/AgCl nanoparticles in environmental surface decontamination; however, their effectiveness and safety on hospital surfaces require validation in standardized surface-based and simulated environmental models.

title: Gravitational pinning and commensurability constrain a rigid-sheet thermo-magnetic mechanism for laser-driven levitating graphite
summary: Pyrolytic-graphite sheets levitating above checkerboard magnet arrays can be translated by a scanned laser, but the origin of this motion remains undetermined. In the standard thermo-magnetic explanation, local heating weakens the diamagnet
content: Pyrolytic-graphite sheets levitating above checkerboard magnet arrays can be translated by a scanned laser, but the origin of this motion remains undetermined. In the standard thermo-magnetic explanation, local heating weakens the diamagnetic susceptibility and pulls the sheet toward the beam. Here we test this explanation at the level of transport by combining the checkerboard field, heat flow on the sheet, Curie-law susceptibility and self-consistent levitation height in a driven-washboard model without fitted transport parameters. The central result is gravitational pinning, i.e. after vertical re-equilibration the leading barrier scale is set by weight and geometry and is independent of the magnetic-energy prefactor, and uniform heating stiffens the barrier ( \(+11.2\%\) for a 300 K overheat at the enhanced coupling). The photothermal perturbation contains only the lattice harmonics of the magnet array, so it reshapes the wells but supplies neither an incommensurate trap nor a dc tilt. Across a 700-point operating map at a thousand-fold enhanced coupling, the model produces pinning, intra-well libration and occasional impulsive kicks, but no sustained beam-following transport, and matching the barrier force alone requires effective Curie constants of 37.9–48.7 K. Sheet deformation, current-driven forces and gas-mediated actuation remain candidate mechanisms, and we propose direct tests of each.

title: Engineering Local Solvent Environments in Eutectic Hydrogel Electrolytes for Wide‐Temperature Flexible Energy Storage
summary: ABSTRACT Hydrogel electrolytes for wide‐temperature flexible energy storage must sustain ion transport while preserving network integrity and electrode–electrolyte contact. Here, a polyacrylamide‐based eutectic hydrogel electrolyte (PDL) is
content: ABSTRACT Hydrogel electrolytes for wide‐temperature flexible energy storage must sustain ion transport while preserving network integrity and electrode–electrolyte contact. Here, a polyacrylamide‐based eutectic hydrogel electrolyte (PDL) is formed by light‐triggered polymerization in a medium comprising a Zn(ClO 4 ) 2 ·6H 2 O/ethylene glycol deep eutectic solvent (DES), water and sodium lignosulfonate (SLS). Spectroscopy and molecular calculations support coupled interactions among water, ions, cosolvent and polymers. Comparisons across formulations reveal that DES/H 2 O lowers the low‐temperature transition and improves mass retention, whereas SLS further strengthens local interactions, jointly promoting ion transport, mechanical integrity and adhesion. PDL retains an ionic conductivity of 29.1 mS cm − 1 at −40°C, exhibits a low‐temperature transition at −57.3°C, and reaches tensile and adhesion strengths of 400.4 and 321.8 kPa, respectively. Flexible symmetric supercapacitors operate from −40 to 60°C, deliver 16.3 Wh kg − 1 at 376.2 W kg − 1 , and retain 85.2% capacitance after 2000 cycles at −40°C and 77.1% after 10000 cycles at 60°C. The devices also tolerate bending and static loading and power electronic loads across the operating‐temperature range. Local‐solvent‐environment engineering thus provides a route to coordinate wide‐temperature ion transport with mechanical robustness and interfacial stability.

title: Preparation of Ether-free Polycarbazole-Based Anion Exchange Membranes and Regulation of Cations on Membrane Properties and Fuel Cell Performance
summary: Abstract Quaternized ether-free aromatic polymers from superacid-catalyzed polycondensation are excellent candidates for high-performance anion exchange membranes (AEMs). Most current studies mainly focus on cation-modified carbon-aromatic
content: Abstract Quaternized ether-free aromatic polymers from superacid-catalyzed polycondensation are excellent candidates for high-performance anion exchange membranes (AEMs). Most current studies mainly focus on cation-modified carbon-aromatic AEMs. However, the structure–property relationship of cation-functionalized heteroaromatic polyarylene systems is still insufficiently understood. This work develops a series of carbazole-based ether-free AEMs with different side-chain quaternary ammonium (QA) cations, including conventional trimethylammonium, charge-delocalized imidazolium, and N-cyclic piperidinium and quinuclidinium. All membranes share the same polycarbazole backbone. Thus, the side-chain cation structure primarily determines membrane comprehensive performance. QPC-TMA with trimethylammonium groups exhibits the highest hydroxide conductivity at 80 °C, owing to its high ion exchange capacity and well-developed microphase separation. In comparison, QPC-QUI with bulky quinuclidinium groups shows outstanding alkaline and oxidative stability under harsh aging conditions. It shows least conductivity loss (2.65% loss for 1080 h) and weight loss (0.81% loss for 72 h).In fuel cell tests, the QPC-QUI-based AEM achieves a peak power density of 998 mW cm–2, which is higher than QPC-TMA (928 mW cm–2). This work proves that rational cation structural design of ether-free heteroaromatic polymers is a reliable strategy to prepare high-conductivity and durable AEMs for electrochemical energy applications.

title: Resident bacteria and niche chemistry gatekeep host-specific colonization by commensal fungi
summary: Abstract Bacterial colonization resistance against fungi is well established, but its role in fungal commensalism remains unclear. Kazachstania pintolopesii , a stomach-tropic fungal commensal, dominates the mouse gastrointestinal (GI) trac
content: Abstract Bacterial colonization resistance against fungi is well established, but its role in fungal commensalism remains unclear. Kazachstania pintolopesii , a stomach-tropic fungal commensal, dominates the mouse gastrointestinal (GI) tract despite the presence of resident bacteria. To investigate how mouse-derived strains withstand bacterial colonization resistance, we compared mouse- and guinea pig-derived isolates of this species. Unlike the mouse isolate (Kp-M), the guinea pig isolate (Kp-GP) failed to colonize the mouse GI tract. Resident bacteria imposed this barrier: Kp-GP colonized germ-free mice, and vancomycin-mediated depletion of gastric Lactobacillus permitted robust colonization. Cell-free supernatant from aerobically grown Lactobacillus johnsonii isolated from the mouse stomach selectively killed Kp-GP through an H₂O₂- and low-pH-dependent mechanism, consistent with chemistry supported by the oxygen-containing gastric environment. Genomic and transcriptomic analyses revealed that Kp-GP is triploid, carries deletions in oxidative stress response genes, including the peroxiredoxin gene AHP1 , and fails to induce AHP1 expression following supernatant exposure. Pharmacological neutralization of H₂O₂ and reduction of gastric acidity allowed Kp-GP colonization in mice. Together, these findings identify gastric Lactobacillus and the oxidizing niche they establish as gatekeepers of fungal colonization and reveal that successful establishment by a fungus depends on its ability to withstand bacterial colonization resistance.

title: Peat, Diesel, and Seaweed: Poetic Inquiry in the Coastal Communities of Northwest Highlands of Scotland
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This chapter draws from a project exploring how people in coastal communities in the northwest highlands of Scotland feel and think about climate action. It was a poetic inquiry and so this narrative of the project findings is mostly expres
content: This chapter draws from a project exploring how people in coastal communities in the northwest highlands of Scotland feel and think about climate action. It was a poetic inquiry and so this narrative of the project findings is mostly expressed in poetry. The project was driven by the need to achieve net zero carbon emissions in ways that are both practical and benefit local people by supporting livelihoods and wellbeing. In the spirit of ‘staying with the trouble’ (Haraway 16), it was intended to encourage people to express their concerns but also to dream about a better future. Poetic inquiry methods were used as I am a poet, in order to encourage participation from people who might not engage with traditional scientific or social science research (Fernández-Giménez 2019) and because it would ensure that the research would not disconnect participants’ knowledge and thinking from embodiment and emotion (Leggo 2008, Vincent 2018, Faulkner 2020).

title: Diffusion-enhanced GFlowNet for solving vehicle routing problems
source: Singapore Management University Institutional Knowledge (InK) (Singapore Management University)
summary: Traditional neural solvers for solving vehicle routing problems (VRPs) often suffer from limited solution diversity, motivating the development of Generative Flow Network (GFlowNet)-based models.However, the effectiveness of these models is
content: Traditional neural solvers for solving vehicle routing problems (VRPs) often suffer from limited solution diversity, motivating the development of Generative Flow Network (GFlowNet)-based models.However, the effectiveness of these models is frequently constrained by insufficient flow expansion in high-reward regions, limiting their ability to distribute probability across promising solution routes.The deeper exploration could yield superior results.Diffusion models, in contrast, provide stronger structural guidance for exploration.These two paradigms are naturally complementary: GFlowNet can supply edge-level signals for diffusion to embed, while diffusion can guide broader exploration.Leveraging this synergy, we propose Diffusion-Enhanced GFlowNet (DEG), a novel framework that integrates GFlowNet with a diffusion model to encourage richer flow expansion toward highreward regions and derive higher-quality solutions.Specifically, DEG exploits GFlowNet's inherent diversity to generate edge-specific backward signals, applies the stochastic noise schedule of diffusion to perturb these signals, and then denoises them within the GFlowNet paradigm.To further improve scalability, we introduce a specialized decoder capable of dynamically adapting to diverse problem scales.Extensive experimental evaluations on synthetic and real-world datasets, including instances with up to 10,000 nodes, demonstrate that DEG consistently achieves favorable performance compared to baseline methods.The code is available at https://github.com/ZHANG-NI/DEG.Recent neural solvers for VRPs can be broadly categorized into Autoregressive (AR) and Non-Autoregressive (NAR) models.AR models, such as those based on pointer networks and Transformer 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026).

title: Exposure to wildfire smoke and risk of mortality and hospitalization among hemodialysis patients in the Western United States: Effect modification by extreme heat events.
summary: Background: Climate change is increasing the extent of wildfires and extreme heat events (EHEs) in the Western United States. Our objective was to estimate the risk of all-cause mortality and hospitalization among end-stage kidney disease (
content: Background: Climate change is increasing the extent of wildfires and extreme heat events (EHEs) in the Western United States. Our objective was to estimate the risk of all-cause mortality and hospitalization among end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) patients after exposure to wildfire smoke, EHEs, and the combined occurrence of wildfire smoke and EHE. Methods: ), and EHE exposure for each hemodialysis facility. We employed a time-stratified case-crossover using conditional quasi-Poisson to estimate rate ratios (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). A likelihood ratio test was used to assess potential interaction effects between wildfire smoke and EHEs, along with stratified analyses to estimate effect modification by EHEs. Results: was associated with a 1% increase in the risk of hospitalization (RR: 1.01; 95% CI: 1.00, 1.03) at lag 0. We observed considerably higher risk of mortality when patients were simultaneously exposed to wildfire smoke plume and EHE (RR: 1.92; 95% CI: 1.71, 2.17) compared with wildfire smoke plume alone (RR: 1.02; 95% CI: 0.95, 1.10). We did not observe significant effect modification by EHE for all-cause hospitalization. Conclusions: These findings suggest that patients with ESKD are at a higher risk of mortality after exposure to wildfire smoke, particularly in the presence of EHEs.
