title: Green Economic Convergence
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Green Economic Convergence establishes an empirical and policy framework demonstrating that economic catch-up and environmental sustainability are reinforcing complements rather than competing objectives. Rather than replicating the coal- a
content: Green Economic Convergence establishes an empirical and policy framework demonstrating that economic catch-up and environmental sustainability are reinforcing complements rather than competing objectives. Rather than replicating the coal- and carbon-intensive industrialization pathways of the nineteenth and twentieth centuries under delayed Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) assumptions, emerging and developing economies (EMDEs) can capture a clean latecomer advantage—narrowing disparities in income, productive capabilities, technological advancement, and living standards through green technology diffusion, sustainable industrialization, clean infrastructure, and institutional capacity building. Synthesizing a 184-economy PPP CO2/GDP panel (2000–2022), Malmquist–Luenberger green total-factor productivity (GTFP) club analysis, Kaya identity decomposition, IRENA hardware learning curves (2010–2025), IEA World Energy Investment and Cost of Capital Observatory benchmarks, and World Bank/ESMAP/WHO Tracking SDG 7metrics, the report advances five central findings: Relative Decoupling Is Broadly Underway, Yet Scale Still Drives Emissions: Carbon intensity per PPP dollar of GDP fell in 124 of 184 economies between 2000 and 2022 (global median drop of 21%), though rapid EMDE GDP scale expansion (+68%) outpaced energy efficiency (-24%) and clean fuel substitution (-11%). Convergence Is Conditional, Not Automatic: Economies sort into distinct Malmquist–Luenberger convergence clubs governed by institutional quality, utility bankability, STEM skills, and technological absorption capacity. Hardware Economics Favor Leapfrogging: Between 2010 and 2024, utility-scale solar PV LCOE fell 90% to $44/MWh and utility battery storage (BESS) installed costs dropped 93% to ~$192/kWh (with further ~30% declines in 2025), placing firm solar-plus-storage at $54–$82/MWh—below new coal or imported LNG across major emerging corridors. Capital-Market Asymmetries—Not Technology Costs—Block Catch-Up: Clean-to-fossil investment stands at 12:1 in advanced economies and 6:1 in China versus 2:1 in other EMDEs, where borrowing costs (11.7% average clean WACC vs. ~4.6% OECD baseline) erase natural renewable cost advantages. Human Inclusion Anchors Convergence Legitimacy: Closing Sub-Saharan Africa’s 970 million clean-cooking deficit (within a 2.0–2.1 billion global deficit) and electrification gap alongside foreign-exchange guarantees, digital grid modernization, and green industrial value-chain upgrading can lift aggregate EMDE per-capita income toward 50.3% of the OECD average by 2040 while avoiding $4.3 trillion in stranded fossil assets.

title: Impact of continuous low-pH acidification on nitrogen retention and gaseous emissions from raw and separated pig slurry
summary: Livestock manure management is a major source of N H 3 and greenhouse gas emissions, representing a critical environmental challenge for intensive animal production systems. Although slurry acidification is a well-established technique for
content: Livestock manure management is a major source of N H 3 and greenhouse gas emissions, representing a critical environmental challenge for intensive animal production systems. Although slurry acidification is a well-established technique for reducing gaseous emissions, most studies have focused on one-time applications targeting pH values between 5.0 and 6.0. In contrast, the effectiveness and acid requirements of continuous acidification at low pH throughout storage have not been comprehensively evaluated. The aim of this work is to evaluate the effectiveness of a continuous acidification strategy -maintaining a target pH of 5.0- combined with solid-liquid separation, and to assess its effects on slurry physicochemical composition, gaseous emissions, and acid consumption. A controlled experiment was conducted with raw and separated slurry samples where sulphuric acid was applied with weekly adjustments to maintain the target pH. Gaseous emissions were quantified using open dynamic ( N H 3 and C O 2 ) and closed static chamber ( C H 4 ) techniques. Results demonstrated that the adopted approach achieved a near-complete abatement of N H 3 emissions (97%–100%) and full suppression of C H 4 emissions. C O 2 emissions were significantly reduced by 36%–80% depending on slurry type and experimental week. Furthermore, the treatment enhanced nitrogen retention, preventing a 40%–44% loss of total ammoniacal nitrogen and total Kjeldahl nitrogen observed in the non-acidified slurry, while organic matter degradation was inhibited. These findings identify continuous low-pH acidification as a promising approach that warrants further investigation in both controlled environments and real-farm conditions to fully assess its effectiveness and evaluate its technical and economic feasibility.

title: Spatial mismatch of territorial carbon balance and supply-chain carbon flow: regional carbon compensation in China
summary: Under the context of the “dual carbon”strategy, resolving the spatial mismatch between regional carbon emission production and consumption and establishing a fair and reasonable inter-regional carbon compensation mechanism are crucial to ac
content: Under the context of the “dual carbon”strategy, resolving the spatial mismatch between regional carbon emission production and consumption and establishing a fair and reasonable inter-regional carbon compensation mechanism are crucial to achieving synergistic green emission reductions. From the dual perspectives of production and consumption, this study systematically calculates the production-side carbon balance of 30 Chinese provinces from 2001 to 2020. Utilizing a multi-regional input-output (MRIO) model, it tracks the consumption-side embodied carbon flows in inter-provincial trade across four typical periods: 2002, 2007, 2012, and 2017. Building upon these findings, a Spatial Durbin Model (SDM) is employed to reveal the spatial spillover effects and driving mechanisms of the carbon balance.The findings indicate that: (1) The production-side carbon balance exhibits an overall deficit. From 2001 to 2020, provincial emissions surged before plateauing, with deficit centers increasingly concentrating in energy bases like Shanxi and Inner Mongolia. (2) Interprovincial trade drives a pronounced west-to-east and north-to-south embodied carbon transfer. Eastern coastal regions (e.g., Guangdong, Beijing, Shanghai, and Zhejiang) rely heavily on external resource inputs for consumption, with the power and heat supply sector acting as the primary transfer channel. (3) Interprovincial net emissions display significant positive spatial spillovers. While economic growth directly widens local deficits, technological innovation and enterprise scaling foster collaborative cross-regional mitigation. Moreover, stricter neighboring environmental regulations and downstream demand shift heavier emission burdens onto high-elevation supplier provinces. (4) Under the 2017 national unified clearing mechanism, fourteen consumer provinces (including Shandong, Jiangsu, Guangdong, Beijing, and Shanghai) served as compensation payers, whereas sixteen supplier provinces (including Sichuan, Yunnan, Heilongjiang, and Inner Mongolia) were compensation recipients. This study aims to rectify the bias in carbon responsibility allocation from the accounting perspective, thereby providing a scientific basis for decision-making to optimize China’s horizontal ecological fiscal transfers and safeguard the green development rights of resource-based regions.

title: Global Forest Carbon Project Evaluation System
source: VNU Journal of Science Policy and Management Studies
summary: In response to growing concerns over the reliability of nature-based solutions, this research scrutinizes the systems governing forest carbon projects at national, regional, and project levels. The findings demonstrate significant heterogen
content: In response to growing concerns over the reliability of nature-based solutions, this research scrutinizes the systems governing forest carbon projects at national, regional, and project levels. The findings demonstrate significant heterogeneity in evaluation criteria, highlighting a critical misalignment between policy mandates and field-level execution. Significant deficits in transparency and quantification accuracy are identified as primary drivers of over-crediting risks, which fundamentally undermine global climate targets. To rectify these failings, the study proposes an integrated assessment architecture that combines high-resolution technological verification with inclusive social safeguards, providing a blueprint for high-integrity carbon markets.

title: REVIEW OF CARBON DIOXIDE STORAGE AND INJECTION IN HYDROCARBON WELLS
summary: This current article reviews the methods for storing carbon dioxide (CO2) and its injection into hydrocarbon wells. The study seeks to explore the importance of carbon dioxide storage as a strategy for reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Inj
content: This current article reviews the methods for storing carbon dioxide (CO2) and its injection into hydrocarbon wells. The study seeks to explore the importance of carbon dioxide storage as a strategy for reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Injecting CO2 into oil /gas fields' geological formations to combine CO2 sequestration with better oil recovery is a viable long-term option for reducing global warming. It describes techniques used to inject CO2 into wells, the specific conditions required, and the benefits of enhancing oil recovery through enhancing fluid mobility and lowering oil viscosity. However, there are several issues with CO2 injection, including viscous fingering and CO2 channeling, which lead to low sweep efficiency, early gas breakthrough, and low ultimate oil recovery. The resident brine in geological formations is acidified by injected CO2, which causes chemical interactions with the minerals. In addition to affecting reservoir and wellbore integrity, reservoir infectivity, long-term compaction, and cap rock sealing capability, reactions can change the rock's hydraulic and mechanical characteristics. The review showed that while there are many advantages to CO2 storage and injection, there are also challenges that need to be addressed for safe and effective implementation. This review examines the main state-of-the-art strategies for safely storing carbon dioxide (CO2) and its injection into hydrocarbon wells for oil or gas recovery. The attempts to study CO2 adsorption/desorption for EOR/EGR applications in conventional depleted sandstone and carbonate reservoirs under typical reservoir conditions are highlighted in this review. The methodology includes a literature review and analysis of current practices in CO2 storage and injection. The review discussed and clarified that CO2 storage can enhance oil recovery and reduce climate impact while highlighting technical and regulatory challenges involved in the processes.

title: Connections between Environmental Education, Health and the Environment in the Context of Sustainable Development in Portugal
source: Fronteiras Journal of Social Technological and Environmental Science
summary: Sustainable development, as a political and pedagogical project, requires a critical articulation between environmental education, health, and public policies, understood as inseparable dimensions of social and environmental justice. In the
content: Sustainable development, as a political and pedagogical project, requires a critical articulation between environmental education, health, and public policies, understood as inseparable dimensions of social and environmental justice. In the Portuguese context, this articulation has been progressively incorporated into normative and strategic frameworks, in line with global sustainability agendas. This article presents a narrative literature review of a descriptive and interpretative nature, aiming to critically analyze the articulation between education, health, and the environment, as well as its limits and potential as a field of educational and political intervention. The results reveal a significant discursive convergence in the recognition of the interdependence among these domains, although largely confined to the normative level. A persistent dissociation between institutional discourse and the practical implementation of public policies is observed, marked by sectoral fragmentation, weak intersectoral coordination, and territorial inequalities. Environmental education emerges as a central axis in promoting critical literacies and active citizenship; however, its insufficient integration into curricula and educational policies limits its transformative potential. The study underscores the need for integrated and critical approaches oriented toward social and environmental justice.

title: Knowledge and attitude toward energy and environmental sustainability in Islamic schools around Indonesia’s capital
summary: This study investigates Islamic junior high school students’ perceptions and attitudes toward energy and environmental sustainability in the buffer regions surrounding Indonesia’s new capital city. While the new capital is envisioned as a s
content: This study investigates Islamic junior high school students’ perceptions and attitudes toward energy and environmental sustainability in the buffer regions surrounding Indonesia’s new capital city. While the new capital is envisioned as a sustainable forest city, limited research has examined how students in these areas understand and respond to energy and environmental challenges within an Islamic educational context aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). A quantitative descriptive-correlational design was employed, involving 925 students from ten Islamic junior high schools. Data were collected using a validated questionnaire measuring three perception dimensions (conceptual understanding, knowledge, and issue awareness) and three attitude dimensions (affective, certainty, and behavioral). Descriptive statistics and Pearson correlation analysis were applied. Findings indicate that students’ perceptions and attitudes are predominantly at a moderate level. Conceptual understanding was relatively strong, whereas awareness of real environmental issues was weaker. Students’ attitudes across affective, certainty, and behavioral domains were also moderate. A positive but weakly significant correlation (r = 0.175) was found between perception and attitude, suggesting that cognitive understanding alone does not sufficiently shape pro-environmental attitudes. These findings highlight the need for environmental education in Islamic schools that integrates real-world issues, experiential learning, and Islamic value-based environmental stewardship. Not applicable.

title: Sustainable Global Economic Convergence
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Sustainable Global Economic Convergence (H Heuristics Report HH-2026-33) examines how emerging and developing economies can narrow global disparities in productivity, income, and living standards while transitioning toward clean, resource-e
content: Sustainable Global Economic Convergence (H Heuristics Report HH-2026-33) examines how emerging and developing economies can narrow global disparities in productivity, income, and living standards while transitioning toward clean, resource-efficient, and climate-resilient economic systems. Challenging the conventional assumption that rapid industrialization requires an initial phase of high pollution and fossil-fuel dependence, the report demonstrates that economic development and environmental stewardship act as mutually reinforcing complements. When evaluated across unified national and household balance sheets, environmental degradation is already a severe macroeconomic drag—exemplified by fine particulate air pollution (PM2.5) costing roughly $8.1 trillion globally each year (approximately 6.1% of world GDP, and reaching 9%–10% of GDP across burdened South Asian corridors)—whereas clean electrification, urban transit efficiency, resource productivity, and hazard resilience directly expand productive capacity and real welfare. The analysis traces how coordinated policy and capital deployment across six structural pillars can decouple economic catch-up from historical carbon and ecological traps. Across the Global South, roughly 90% of future urban expansion through 2050 remains unbuilt, offering a narrow 15-to-20-year window across rapidly growing Asian (+1.2 billion projected urban residents) and African (~3× urban population growth) cities to lock in compact mass-transit and flood-resilient infrastructure rather than high-emission sprawl. Simultaneously, plummeting renewable-plus-storage costs allow latecomer industrializers to deploy competitive utility-scale solar and firm clean power rather than imported fossil generation, while UNEP material-footprint findings (21.6 tonnes per capita in high-income economies versus 3.7 tonnes per capita in low-income nations) underscore that circular industrial efficiency in wealthy economies is essential to preserve ecological and material space for foundational infrastructure buildout elsewhere. Strengthening human capabilities—by eliminating indoor smoke from polluting cooking fuels, reducing pollution-driven cognitive and health losses, halving learning poverty, and building green technical skills—further compounds total factor productivity growth. Crucially, realizing this convergence pathway hinges on overcoming capital-cost asymmetries and closing a 12×–14× adaptation financing shortfall, where roughly $30 billion in annual public international adaptation flows lags far behind the $340–365 billion needed annually by developing economies despite proactive adaptation generating 4.8×–9.2× resilience returns. title: Sovereign AI for Jute: A Triple-Lock Architecture for Traceability, Carbon Mapping, Sustainability, Income Equity and Innovation in the Golden Fibre Sector
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Jute is grown by millions of smallholders, almost entirely in two producing countries of the Ganges–Brahmaputra delta, and is now asked to prove what it claims: that its fibre is traceable, that its carbon advantage is real, that its produc
content: Jute is grown by millions of smallholders, almost entirely in two producing countries of the Ganges–Brahmaputra delta, and is now asked to prove what it claims: that its fibre is traceable, that its carbon advantage is real, that its production is sustainable, and that the people who grow and process it share in the value of a green material. Each of those proofs is a data problem, and each is increasingly answered by artificial intelligence: satellite crop maps, fibre-grading vision, methane estimators, price models and product passports. If those systems are owned, trained and governed elsewhere, the sector will export its data and import its own evidence at a rent. This paper sets out a jute-specific sovereign AI architecture that prevents that outcome. It applies the Triple Lock developed in the author's KSCCN work: a Data Lock, a Compute and Model Lock and a Governance and Application Lock that must close together, tested against the civic triad of autonomy, agency and franchise and the public triad of authority, responsibility and accountability. The resulting Jute Sovereign AI Stack has five layers (data sovereignty and governance, compute, models, applications and institutions) and five application modules: fibre-to-product traceability; carbon mapping and sequestration and credit accounting; sustainability of water, retting, soil and biodiversity; farmer income and equity; and innovation in composites, geotextiles and bio-materials. The paper formalises lock closure, adapts the author's CES sovereign-capability function and the EPI/EVI dual-core metric to the sector, and adds module equations for traceability completeness, avoided emissions, creditable carbon and grower value share. Re-using the companion carbon model, it shows why measurement is the first investment: the climate result of a reusable jute sack turns negative once retting methane exceeds about 1.89 t CO₂e per tonne of fibre, inside a published range of 0.10–2.52 t. A 60-month, four-phase deployment roadmap with lock-closure gates, a key performance indicator set and a risk register complete the design. Numbers from models are illustrative; sector figures come from institutional and peer-reviewed sources.

title: The Effects of the CO2 Emissions, Fdi, and Trade Openness on the Economic Growth with the Moderating Role of Renewable Energy: Empirical Evidence in Asean Countries
source: VNU Journal of Science Policy and Management Studies
summary: This study investigates the carbon emissions, foreign direct investment and trade openness affecting the economic growth in ASEAN countries and the moderating role of renewable energy use in these countries from 2001 to 2020 by the Mixed-ef
content: This study investigates the carbon emissions, foreign direct investment and trade openness affecting the economic growth in ASEAN countries and the moderating role of renewable energy use in these countries from 2001 to 2020 by the Mixed-effects ML regressions. The study found that there is a positive impact of renewable energy and trade openness on economic growth in ASEAN countries. Meanwhile, the issue of emissions continues to go hand in hand with economic growth, requiring ASEAN to continue to study how growth in the relationship between environment and economy. A notable result is that artificial energy reduces the impact but at a very small level on economic growth, which also raises policy issues for green growth in the impact of attracting investment and growth in ASEAN countries in the future. In particular, issues related to environmental pollution, CO2 emissions, trade openness, foreign direct investment, renewable energy in their impact on the growth of ASEAN economies.

title: Environmental short-term risk assessment in 66,651 cases of urgent hospital admissions among patients with IBD in Poland
summary: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) incidence is rising worldwide, yet evidence on short-term associations between environmental exposures and urgent IBD hospitalisations remains limited in population-based evidence, particularly in Poland, a
content: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) incidence is rising worldwide, yet evidence on short-term associations between environmental exposures and urgent IBD hospitalisations remains limited in population-based evidence, particularly in Poland, a country at the stage of emergence. A nationwide time-stratified case-crossover, including the cohort of 66,651 cases of urgent hospital admissions among patients with Crohn’s disease or ulcerative colitis recorded as either a primary or comorbid diagnosis, was conducted in Poland between 2012 and 2019. A two-stage analytical framework was applied; exploratory nationwide screening evaluated 49 environmental exposures at lags 0–10, followed by targeted urban follow-up analyses; pooled multi-city, and Warsaw-specific levels. Conditional logistic regression was used to estimate odds ratios (ORs) per interquartile-range (IQR) increase, with Benjamini–Hochberg correction for multiple testing. At multicity stage the same-day NO 2 and NOₓ showed the strongest associations (NO 2 : OR 1.081, 95% CI 1.050–1.113; NOₓ: OR 1.056, 95% CI 1.030–1.082; both BH-adjusted p < 0.001 in multicity analysis). Solar radiation at lag 3 showed the strongest association among meteorological factors. Joint exposure to high NO 2 and high solar radiation at lag 3, or high NO 2 and temperatures > 20 °C at lag 0, was associated with 17% and 9% higher odds of urgent IBD hospital admission of patients aged 19–60, respectively. Associations were most consistent among group of working-age adults aged 19–60 years, urban residents, and patients with ulcerative colitis. Overall, the findings indicate short-term associations between ambient air pollution, particularly nitrogen oxides, meteorological conditions, and urgent IBD hospitalisations in Poland, while the observed joint exposure patterns warrant further investigation.

title: AVALIAÇÃO ESPACIAL E TEMPORAL DA QUALIDADE DA ÁGUA DO RIO URAIM SOB DIFERENTES PRESSÕES ANTRÓPICAS EM PARAGOMINAS, PARÁ
summary: As transformações no uso e ocupação da terra podem comprometer a qualidade das águas superficiais, especialmente em bacias hidrográficas submetidas à expansão urbana e agropecuária. Este estudo objetivou avaliar as variações espaciais e tem
content: As transformações no uso e ocupação da terra podem comprometer a qualidade das águas superficiais, especialmente em bacias hidrográficas submetidas à expansão urbana e agropecuária. Este estudo objetivou avaliar as variações espaciais e temporais da qualidade da água do Rio Uraim, em Paragominas, Pará, considerando possíveis associações com pressões antrópicas. A pesquisa apresentou caráter descritivo e exploratório, com abordagem predominantemente quantitativa, abrangendo dez pontos de amostragem distribuídos ao longo do trecho investigado, em campanhas realizadas em janeiro e abril. Foram analisados parâmetros físicos, químicos e microbiológicos, interpretados individualmente e de forma integrada, utilizando como referência comparativa os padrões da Resolução CONAMA nº 357/2005 para águas doces de Classe 2. Os resultados evidenciaram aumento da demanda bioquímica de oxigênio (DBO) e redução da turbidez em todos os pontos na campanha de abril, além de variações nas concentrações de nutrientes e coliformes termotolerantes, com alterações mais expressivas entre P6 e P10. Embora os valores de DBO e oxigênio dissolvido tenham atendido aos limites de referência considerados, foram identificados valores de pH inferiores à faixa estabelecida, concentrações elevadas de fósforo total e coliformes termotolerantes em determinados pontos e turbidez superior a 100 UNT em parte das amostras. Essas diferenças sugerem possíveis associações com as condições naturais da bacia e as pressões decorrentes das atividades humanas, sem permitir estabelecer relações causais diretas. A ausência de valores finais do Índice de Qualidade da Água (IQA) e de dados hidrológicos simultâneos limitou a avaliação quantitativa integrada e a interpretação da influência sazonal. Conclui-se que o Rio Uraim apresenta heterogeneidade espacial e temporal nos indicadores de qualidade da água, evidenciando a necessidade de monitoramento contínuo e de estratégias integradas de conservação e gestão dos recursos hídricos.

title: Greenwashing In The Indian Textile Industry: Challeges And Sustainable Governance
source: HPNLU Journal of Environment & Disaster Management
summary: The textile and fashion industry have a significant importance to the economy and employment in India. This industry is continually under scrutiny due to its environmental impacts, including water pollution, high carbon emissions, and chemi
content: The textile and fashion industry have a significant importance to the economy and employment in India. This industry is continually under scrutiny due to its environmental impacts, including water pollution, high carbon emissions, and chemical waste. Many companies claim to adopt sustainable product practices in response to this surveillance. The textile and fashion industry have started claiming falsely that have led to new serious issue of Green washing – “the false marketing of products as sustainable and environmentally friendly without any substantive action to make them so”. The problem of Green washing in India by the textile industry will be examined thoroughly. This paper will examine misleading sustainable claims and their effect on consumers and environmental health. It will also analyse the legal framework addressing this issue. This paper will also recommend possible approaches, such as strengthening legal regulation, enforcing independent sustainability audits, and providing consumer access to combat the issue of green washing. India can become genuinely sustainable in the textile industry by ensuring transparency and accountability. There must be a balance between environmental responsibility and economic growth for a better future.

title: Metered-dose inhalers in sustainable healthcare: balancing environmental impact
source: Journal of Environmental Science and Health Part C
summary: This review critically examines the dual clinical and environmental imperatives associated with metered-dose inhalers (MDIs) in the context of sustainable healthcare. A comprehensive literature review was conducted using databases including
content: This review critically examines the dual clinical and environmental imperatives associated with metered-dose inhalers (MDIs) in the context of sustainable healthcare. A comprehensive literature review was conducted using databases including PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect, focusing on publications related to inhaler propellants, life-cycle environmental impact, regulatory transitions, and emerging low-global-warming-potential (GWP) technologies. Although the healthcare sector contributes approximately 4.5% of global greenhouse gas emissions, MDIs account for only about 0.03% of annual global emissions. Nevertheless, their high-GWP propellants make them a focal point for decarbonization strategies. The review highlights the historical transition from chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) to hydrofluoroalkanes (HFAs), evaluates the life-cycle carbon footprint of MDIs, and discusses emerging alternatives such as low-GWP propellants including HFC-152a and HFO-1234ze(E). In parallel, propellant-free inhalation technologies, eco-design principles, renewable energy integration in manufacturing, and circular supply-chain approaches are identified as key enablers of sustainability. Advances in propellant chemistry, device engineering, and manufacturing sustainability demonstrate that meaningful reductions in the environmental impact of inhalation therapy are achievable. Aligning respiratory care with global climate objectives is both ethically necessary and technically feasible, without compromising therapeutic efficacy or patient outcomes.

title: A case of late recurrence of breast cancer with solitary metastasis in right lung 30 years after surgery
source: The Journal of the Japanese Association for Chest Surgery

content: 75歳女性．45歳時に他院で右乳癌に対し乳房全摘術を施行され，術後1年間ホルモン療法施行，その後，再発無く終診となった．両下肢の脱力で前医受診時のCT検査で右肺上葉S3に径13 mm，辺縁整な充実性結節を認め当院紹介となった．気管支鏡下生検にて腺癌と診断された．PET-CTでは他臓器転移は認めず，右上葉肺腺癌cT1bN0M0，Stage IA2と考え，右肺上葉切除＋ND2a-1を施行した．術後病理検査で乳癌の肺転移と診断された．術後30年経過した乳癌の転移は想定していなかったが，病理医に乳癌の既往歴を伝えることで転移の術前診断は可能であった．乳癌の孤立性肺転移では切除により根治が期待できるが，術前に治療選択肢としてのホルモン療法の提示や術式として区域切除の選択も可能であったため，病理診断医に病歴に関する正確な情報提供を行う事が重要で，反省すべき点であった．

title: Early smoking-related lung function changes in biochemically verified current, former, and never smokers
summary: Conventional spirometry is relatively insensitive to early subclinical smoking-related lung injury. We therefore assessed a broad panel of lung function endpoints and their repeatability in biochemically verified smoking-status groups. Forc
content: Conventional spirometry is relatively insensitive to early subclinical smoking-related lung injury. We therefore assessed a broad panel of lung function endpoints and their repeatability in biochemically verified smoking-status groups. Forced oscillation technique (FOT), spirometry and single-breath diffusing capacity (DLCO) were performed at baseline and after 7 ± 3 days in 170 healthy adults classified as current (55), former (60) or never smokers (55) using self-report, exhaled-CO, and a comprehensive biomarker-of-exposure panel. Repeatability was high for spirometry and good for FOT metrics. Standard spirometric indices and traditional FOT resistance/reactance measures did not differ between current and never smokers, but within-breath expiratory–inspiratory resistance differences were greater in current smokers, with significantly higher Δexp–insp R5 values in current smokers than in never smokers (median 0.57 vs. 0.23; p = 0.002) and former smokers (median 0.57 vs. 0.33; p = 0.006). DLCO% and KCO% were lower in current versus never smokers. A significant difference in KCO% was found between current and never smokers (median 94% vs. 106%; p = 0.0003) and between current and former smokers (94% vs. 102%; p = 0.02). Within-breath oscillometry indices and KCO% appear more sensitive than conventional spirometry for detecting early smoking-related functional changes supporting their use as repeatable endpoints in cessation/switching studies.

title: Scanning tunnelling luminescence at the single molecule limit: A perspective
summary: Scanning tunnelling microscope-induced luminescence (STML) is transforming scanning probe microscopy from a tool that images and manipulates matter into one that directly probes the excited-state dynamics governing chemistry at the single-m
content: Scanning tunnelling microscope-induced luminescence (STML) is transforming scanning probe microscopy from a tool that images and manipulates matter into one that directly probes the excited-state dynamics governing chemistry at the single-molecule level. By coupling atomic-scale spatial resolution with optical spectroscopy, STML provides unique access to charge transfer, molecular excited states, and ultrafast relaxation pathways that are inaccessible to conventional scanning tunnelling microscopy alone. In this perspective, we highlight the recent advances that have established STML as a powerful platform for studying molecular dynamics and reactions. We first discuss the experimental innovations that have enabled efficient photon detection within the STM junction, before reviewing time-resolved techniques that extend temporal resolution down to picoseconds. We then examine how STML reveals molecular excited-state manifolds and the electronic pathways that underpin light emission and energy relaxation. Finally, we explore the emerging application of STML to single-molecule chemical reactions, arguing that direct optical access to excited-state dynamics offers a new framework for understanding and ultimately controlling chemical transformations with atomic precision.

title: A Theory of Surface Net Longwave Radiation
summary: Surface net longwave radiation is an important term in the surface energy balance. Despite this, we lack simple, quantitative theory for clear-sky (𝐿 𝑁 ) and all-sky (𝐿′ 𝑁 ) surface net longwave radiation (defined as positive upward). We pr
content: Surface net longwave radiation is an important term in the surface energy balance. Despite this, we lack simple, quantitative theory for clear-sky (𝐿 𝑁 ) and all-sky (𝐿′ 𝑁 ) surface net longwave radiation (defined as positive upward). We propose a simple, diagnostic theory of 𝐿 𝑁 and 𝐿′ 𝑁 using simplified spectral (i.e., non-gray) radiative transfer, including a partially transparent atmospheric window with absorption dominated by the water vapor continuum. We show that 𝐿 𝑁 may be written as the product of the Planck function in the atmospheric window evaluated at the near-surface air temperature, the spectral width of the atmospheric window, and a dimensionless net cooling efficiency, predicted to vary between one and 1/5 for conditions typical of the modern Earth. The theory accurately reproduces reanalysis 𝐿 𝑁 as a function only of near-surface relative humidity and air temperature, and it extends naturally to 𝐿′ 𝑁 , given cloud fraction as an additional input. It requires only one globally-fixed spectroscopic parameter, fit using a line-by-line radiative transfer code applied to an idealized atmosphere. The theory is used to explain why 𝐿 𝑁 lies in a relatively narrow range (40-150 W m −2 ) for conditions typical of the modern Earth (and similarly for 𝐿′ 𝑁 ), and why empirical gray gas models for downwelling surface longwave radiation often predict a lower bound on the broadband emissivity of approximately 2/3. It is also used to understand why near-surface variables alone are, empirically, sufficient to model 𝐿 𝑁 , even though the full atmospheric profile is required to model equivalent fluxes at the top-of-atmosphere.

title: Automated pavement construction using 3D-printed concrete geocell to improve rutting performance
summary: Abstract While 3D concrete printing (3DcP) is widely used in the field of building construction, limited research has focused on its usage in road construction applications. Previously, a conceptual idea was proposed to use the aggregate-be
content: Abstract While 3D concrete printing (3DcP) is widely used in the field of building construction, limited research has focused on its usage in road construction applications. Previously, a conceptual idea was proposed to use the aggregate-bed 3D printing technique to create confinements similar to plastic geocell in unbound granular pavement layers. This study experimentally evaluates the rutting performance of pavement section confined by 3DcP geocells through laboratory-scale plate load tests under cyclic loading. Experimental results show that the 3DcP geocell outperforms the conventional plastic geocell in the short term. However, both systems provided similar confinement efficiency over the long term, which is attributed to interlayer debonding within the concrete geocell under repetitive loading. Despite that, the 3DcP geocell reduced rutting by 50% compared to the unconfined specimen, demonstrating its potential as an alternative to plastic geocell. The performance of the 3DcP geocell can be further improved by optimising the shape of the geocell confinement and increasing its mechanical strength.

title: Green Transport Transition: A Comparative Analysis of Kerala with Other Selected States
source: International journal of sustainable rural development.
summary: The transportation sector in India is a significant contributor to environmental pollution, primarily due to its reliance on fossil fuels. With growing awareness of climate change, the adoption of green transportation has emerged as a vital
content: The transportation sector in India is a significant contributor to environmental pollution, primarily due to its reliance on fossil fuels. With growing awareness of climate change, the adoption of green transportation has emerged as a vital strategy for reducing carbon emissions. This research paper based on secondary data, investigates the penetration of green transport in greenery state, Kerala relative to other Indian states. It analyses key factors such as green vehicle registration trends, the development of charging infrastructure, government policies, and green initiatives in public transport. The study also explores the adoption of green vehicles, the policy measures driving the shift, and the challenges hindering the transition. This study reveals that while Kerala has achieved relatively good annual growth in green transport, it still lags behind some of the larger states. It found that limited charging infrastructure, low consumer green awareness and modest government incentives are hampering green transition. So there may be some room for more policies, incentives and support for the EV ecosystem. The findings offer valuable insights into Kerala’s comparative performance in promoting sustainable transportation, highlighting best practices and areas for improvement.

title: A long-term VIIRS-derived dataset of chlorophyll-a, suspended particulate matter, and water clarity for lakes in China (2012–2025)
summary: Inland lakes are important components of regional and global biological and biogeochemical cycles, yet consistent long-term observations of lake water quality remain limited. Here we present CLOWP (China Lake Optical Water Properties), a sa
content: Inland lakes are important components of regional and global biological and biogeochemical cycles, yet consistent long-term observations of lake water quality remain limited. Here we present CLOWP (China Lake Optical Water Properties), a satellite-derived dataset of chlorophyll-a (Chl-a), suspended particulate matter (SPM), and Secchi disk depth (Zsd) for 720 lakes (>10 km 2 ) across China from February 2012 to February 2025. The dataset was generated from the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) observations using a unified processing framework optimized for optically complex inland waters. Chl-a was retrieved using a deep neural network model, while SPM and Zsd were estimated using semi-empirical and semi-analytical algorithms, respectively. Atmospheric correction, data quality screening, and temporal compositing procedures were applied to reduce uncertainties associated with cloud contamination, aerosol effects, and spatial heterogeneity. The final products are provided as monthly composites at 750 m spatial resolution. Validation against in situ measurements showed good overall agreement, with overall R 2 values of 0.79–0.89 and median absolute percentage error values of 22.2–39.7% across the three parameters. The dataset captures substantial spatial and temporal variability in lake water quality across different climatic and ecological regions in China. CLOWP provides a consistent and openly accessible long-term record of inland water properties and supports applications in water quality assessment, ecosystem monitoring, and studies of environmental change in Chinese lakes.

title: Low-Carbon Mass Concrete in Vietnam: A Life Cycle and Cost Analysis
source: Journal of Construction Engineering and Management
summary: Abstract This study aims to address the environmental and economic challenges of mass concrete production by evaluating the integration of industrial waste by-products, such as ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBFS), fly ash (FA), and
content: Abstract This study aims to address the environmental and economic challenges of mass concrete production by evaluating the integration of industrial waste by-products, such as ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBFS), fly ash (FA), and waste crushed sand, into 50-MPa concrete mixtures. The objective is to identify sustainable alternatives to traditional cementitious materials through life cycle assessment (LCA), cost analysis, and multicriteria evaluation. This study adopts an integrated assessment framework that jointly incorporates chilled-water energy modeling, allocation sensitivity of industrial by-products, and cost analysis within a mix-specific cradle-to-gate LCA. Three mixtures were examined, including M1 (50% GGBFS + 50% OPC), M2 (20% FA + 80% pozzolanic cement), and M3 (low-heat cement). M1 demonstrated the lowest global warming potential (280.75 kg CO 2 - eq / m 3 ) and outperformed others in eight environmental impact categories, with minimal effects on human health [4.44 × 10 −4 disability-adjusted life years (DALY)] and resources (11.9 USD2013). M2 offered strong environmental performance and the lowest cost (USD 43.5/m 3 ), achieving savings of up to USD 32,400 for 4,000 m 3 compared with M3. M3 showed the highest emissions and cost. The results affirm that using waste-derived materials can significantly reduce environmental burdens and improve the economic feasibility of mass concrete.

title: Consumers’ knowledge of the environmental footprint of food categories: evidence from a controlled experiment without and after label exposure
summary: Purpose The study aims to investigate whether consumers are able to correctly assess the environmental footprint of food categories and whether exposure to environmental labels during a shopping task improves their knowledge. Design/methodo
content: Purpose The study aims to investigate whether consumers are able to correctly assess the environmental footprint of food categories and whether exposure to environmental labels during a shopping task improves their knowledge. Design/methodology/approach A total of 577 non-student participants completed a knowledge test after being exposed, during a shopping task, to one of six environmental labelling formats or no label at all. The test assessed three dimensions: the ability to rank food categories by environmental impact (ordinal ranking), estimate the magnitude of impact differences between categories (cardinal ranking) and perceive within-category footprint variability. Responses from labelled and unlabelled groups were compared to evaluate both overall and format-specific impacts on knowledge. Findings Participants were relatively accurate in identifying the most and least impactful food categories but significantly underestimated the scale of differences between them – especially the gap between red meat and other food groups. Within-category variability was generally overestimated. Exposure to environmental labels only slightly improved knowledge, with modest gains observed for the fish and fruits, vegetables and pulses categories. One label format, which benchmarked impact within food categories, actually worsened knowledge by reinforcing existing misconceptions. Research limitations/implications Findings are limited to immediate effects from a single shopping task. Long-term exposure to labels may yield different results. Moreover, the knowledge test design (using a 0–100 slider) may be subject to framing effects. Practical implications Consumers underestimate the environmental benefits of switching between food categories – particularly from animal-based categories (and especially red meat) to plant-based categories – and overestimate those within categories. Policymakers should help consumers identify the most impactful dietary changes. Caution is warranted when using category-based benchmarking, as it may mislead consumers and promote less effective dietary shifts. Social implications This study highlights the importance of improving consumer knowledge about the environmental impact of food choices. By identifying gaps and misperceptions in how individuals compare broad food categories, the findings support the development of environmental labels that can guide more sustainable dietary decisions. Enhancing public understanding at this level is essential for fostering collective behavioural shifts towards lower-impact diets, contributing to climate and environmental goals through informed consumer action. Originality/value This study introduces a novel method to measure consumer environmental knowledge and is among the first to evaluate the effect of short-term exposure to environmental labels on such knowledge. It distinguishes between types of knowledge – ordinal, cardinal and variability-related – providing a nuanced understanding of

title: Subsidy Governance, Regulatory Design and the Delivery Gap in Global Green Hydrogen Deployment, 2025-2026
summary: Public subsidy governance now determines whether the global green hydrogen market turns announced capacity into delivered capacity. Next Move Strategy Consulting values the green hydrogen market at USD 10.03 billion in 2025 and projects USD
content: Public subsidy governance now determines whether the global green hydrogen market turns announced capacity into delivered capacity. Next Move Strategy Consulting values the green hydrogen market at USD 10.03 billion in 2025 and projects USD 86.44 billion by 2030, a compound annual growth rate of 53.8%. Evidence from 2025 and 2026 shows that this trajectory rests on policy instruments rather than on cost parity. The International Energy Agency cut its announced 2030 low-emissions hydrogen pipeline from 49 to 37 million tonnes per year, and only about 4 million tonnes per year is operational, under construction or at final investment decision. The third European Hydrogen Bank auction selected thirteen projects, and two Nordic countries hold more than three quarters of their combined capacity. In the United States, the 45V construction deadline moved from 2033 to 2028, federal grants for 223 projects were cancelled, and Air Products booked exit charges of about USD 2.9 billion. China reported more than one million tonnes per year of capacity installed or under construction, while European electrolyser makers reported steep revenue declines alongside rising orders. Risk is allocated unevenly among taxpayers, carbon-market payers, developers, equipment suppliers and host economies. For investors and public decision-makers, delivery depends on offtake certainty, infrastructure financing and regulatory stability more than on announced scale.

title: The Impact of Market Dominance by Quick Commerce on Stakeholders
source: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)
summary: Quick commerce (Q-commerce) has reshaped retail through rapid delivery of daily essentials, generally within 10-30 minutes, using hyperlocal fulfilment centres, digital platforms and flexible delivery networks. This paper examines how the e
content: Quick commerce (Q-commerce) has reshaped retail through rapid delivery of daily essentials, generally within 10-30 minutes, using hyperlocal fulfilment centres, digital platforms and flexible delivery networks. This paper examines how the expansion and concentration of Q-commerce services affect consumers, local retailers, employees, investors, technological innovation, the economy and environmental sustainability. The study is based on the supplied research project, including its survey of 85 respondents and reported interviews with five delivery personnel. The evidence suggests a combination of benefits and pressures. Consumers gain speed, convenience and access to products, while smaller and more frequent orders may encourage impulse purchases. Large platforms stimulate innovation in logistics and digital payments, yet smaller retailers can struggle to match heavily funded pricing and delivery networks. The sector creates jobs while also raising concerns about unstable gig earnings, worker safety and social protection. Survey respondents additionally identified packaging waste, delivery emissions and limited transparency as significant issues. The central conclusion is that quick commerce can generate economic and consumer value, but continued growth needs to be balanced with fair competition, stronger worker safeguards, responsible pricing, transparent disclosure and more sustainable operations. Survey findings in this paper describe respondent perceptions; they do not, by themselves, establish a causal or legal finding of market abuse.

title: COMBUSTION AND EMISSION ANALYSIS FOR COMPRESSION IGNITION ENGINE FUELED BY BLENDS OF RICE BRAN OIL AND CONVENTIONAL DIESEL
summary: This study compares the performance and emission characteristics of waste rice bran oil (RBO) with conventional diesel in a diesel engine. Tests conducted at compression ratios of 16.5, 17.5, and 18.5 revealed a trade-off between efficiency
content: This study compares the performance and emission characteristics of waste rice bran oil (RBO) with conventional diesel in a diesel engine. Tests conducted at compression ratios of 16.5, 17.5, and 18.5 revealed a trade-off between efficiency and performance. Direct use of RBO caused higher brake thermal and volumetric efficiencies due to its well combustion. Although, high viscosity and density which hinder fuel atomization and air–fuel mixing, resulting in incomplete combustion. However, RBO produced lower emissions of carbon monoxide (CO), unburnt hydrocarbons (UHC), and carbon dioxide (CO₂) than diesel. Despite this, it showed higher brake specific fuel consumption (BSFC) and less efficient air–fuel ratio (AFR) control. Nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions increased slightly with RBO use. Overall, while RBO reduces harmful emissions and provides a sustainable use for waste oil, its high viscosity limits engine performance, requiring further optimization for practical diesel engine applications

title: Can state-led collaborative supply chain governance catalyse decarbonization of firms and supply chains? Evidence from China’s supply chain innovation and application pilot
summary: State-led collaborative supply chain governance (SLCSCG) models bring together governments, businesses, and other key stakeholders while emphasizing a top-down design, central coordination, and local implementation. We employ EDGAR grid emi
content: State-led collaborative supply chain governance (SLCSCG) models bring together governments, businesses, and other key stakeholders while emphasizing a top-down design, central coordination, and local implementation. We employ EDGAR grid emission data for 3,851 A-share listed firms over the sample period 2011–2022 and adopt a difference-in-differences (DID) identification strategy. We estimate that, on average, China’s city-level supply chain innovation and application pilot (CLSCIAP) policy, a distinctive example of SLCSCG, has reduced carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions by 10.0%. We have identified mechanisms that mitigate firms’ abnormal investments, promote their carbon disclosure, and improve supply chain proximity, which are explicitly targeted by the policy tasks. Further analysis reveals an asymmetric policy spillover effect, from treated customers to their upstream suppliers, demonstrating the pivotal role of customer firms in decarbonizing supply chains. Building on two unresolved questions of how state coordination supports decarbonization and how policy effects propagate along supply chains, this study provides a new empirical basis for understanding the roles of central authority and multi-stakeholder collaboration in green governance. It also demonstrates that such an integrated policy achieves significant emission reduction effects via complementary firm-level and supply-chain-level channels, verifying its effectiveness and scalability in promoting sustainability transitions.

title: A Dynamic MILP Framework for Multi-Stage Food-Grain Supply Chain Optimization: A Case Study of Jharkhand’s Public Distribution System
source: International Journal of Mathematics Trends and Technology
summary: Food-grain supply chains involve several activities such as procurement, processing, transportation, storage, and distribution. In the Public Distribution System (PDS) of India, these activities are closely connected because procured paddy
content: Food-grain supply chains involve several activities such as procurement, processing, transportation, storage, and distribution. In the Public Distribution System (PDS) of India, these activities are closely connected because procured paddy has to be processed in rice mills before the milled rice can be stored and distributed to different demand locations. This study develops a dynamic Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model for a four-stage food-grain supply chain consisting of procurement centres, rice mills, warehouses, and PDS distribution points. The model considers milling recovery, period-wise milling capacity, procurement availability, route activation, warehouse capacity, inventory balance, demand fulfilment, opportunity cost, and shortage penalty. Transportation costs are calculated from inter-node distances using the applicable Jharkhand Government transportation-rate structure. The model is tested through computational experiments using the East Singhbhum network and is further examined using observed procurement-stage data and a calibrated downstream representation of the Seraikela-Kharsawan district network. For the East Singhbhum simulation, the total system cost decreases from INR 76,102,850.08 under the baseline allocation to INR 75,105,464.62 with the proposed MILP, giving a reduction of 1.31%. Sensitivity analysis further shows that PDS demand and transportation cost have relatively strong effects on total system cost, while paddy availability, milling capacity, and milling recovery affect both cost and systemic shortage over the tested ranges. For the Seraikela-Kharsawan network, the calibrated validation gives a reduction in total system cost from INR 7,813,080.15 to INR 7,114,689.99, corresponding to 8.94%, while maintaining the prescribed paddy throughput and zero shortage. The Stage-1 transportation calculation was also checked using the Modified Vogel’s Approximation Method (VAM), with a difference of 0.84% between the manual and MATLAB-based calculations. The results indicate that the proposed model can be used to evaluate food-grain flows, processing capacity, inventory, transportation expenditure, and PDS demand fulfilment in a multi-stage network.

title: A Design-Oriented Typology of Product Take-Back Systems for Circular Value Retention
summary: Abstract Background Product take-back systems are central to circular economy implementation, yet many recoverable products and materials still end up landfilled or downgraded to low-value treatment. This loss reflects misalignment among pr
content: Abstract Background Product take-back systems are central to circular economy implementation, yet many recoverable products and materials still end up landfilled or downgraded to low-value treatment. This loss reflects misalignment among product and service design, recovery pathway structure, and the behavioral conditions that shape consumer returns. Objectives Reverse logistics, circular strategy, and behavioral research have examined these dimensions independently. However, integrated design-oriented approaches linking value retention, participation conditions, and recovery feasibility remain limited. This study examines how design decisions shape intake quality and recovery outcomes in product take-back systems. Methods A structured search initially identified 127peer-reviewed records and 48 complementary practice-based sources. Following duplicate removal, screening, and eligibility assessment, 118 sources were included in the final analytical dataset, comprising 92 peer-reviewed publications and 26 practice-based cases. Cases were coded using six analytical criteria capturing operational, behavioral, and recovery conditions. The analysis integrates R-strategy hierarchies, Capability Opportunity Motivation Behaviour (COM-B) participation conditions, and Design-for-X (DfX) principles. Results Cross-case synthesis identified eight recurring take-back strategies. These were consolidated into five higher-order solution clusters: Direct Product Reuse, Functional Restoration, Industrial Re manufacturing, Component and Material Recovery, and Risk Mitigation. Higher-value pathways were associated with design features and return-system configurations that preserved product integrity, reduced contamination, and lowered behavioral friction at the point of return. Conclusions The resulting interpretive approach links value-retention strategies with operational, behavioral, and design conditions. It offers indicative DfX considerations for exploring alignment between take-back systems and contextually feasible recovery pathways.

title: Beyond production: Valuing and modelling farmers' practices for ecosystem services provision in Mediterranean olive growing
summary: The crucial role of ecosystem services (ESs) for both human well-being and biodiversity is becoming increasingly apparent. Consequently, mitigating potential impacts that could jeopardise these services presents a significant challenge in o
content: The crucial role of ecosystem services (ESs) for both human well-being and biodiversity is becoming increasingly apparent. Consequently, mitigating potential impacts that could jeopardise these services presents a significant challenge in our contemporary world. The Mediterranean basin harbours a wealth of natural ecosystems deeply interwoven with human activities, particularly in the agricultural sector. Within this context, olive cultivation emerges as a notably complex and thoroughly documented case. It yields a spectrum of advantages, encompassing the creation of valuable commodities alongside the provision of vital regulatory services, such as carbon sequestration. This paper aims to implement specific assessment models for ESs, operating within the Life Cycle framework for olive orchards situated across various Mediterranean countries. The featured case studies are differentiated by their diverse cultivation techniques, categorised as Sustainable Technological Solutions (STS) and non-STS based on the adoption of agroecological practices. To evaluate the ESs provided by olive cultivation, a hybrid methodology integrating Geographic Information System (GIS) capabilities with traditional Life Cycle Assessment was employed. Provisioning services were assessed utilizing the EPS2015 framework, while regulating services were quantified through LANCA indicators implemented within GIS software. The results indicate that STS and non-STS olive farms can differ across the selected indicators, with the patterns remaining context dependent and, for raster-derived regulating services, sensitive to spatial data sources and resolution. Given the close relationship between the presented ecosystem services and the specific agronomic techniques employed in olive groves, their environmental and economic quantification is paramount. This measurement allows for a better understanding of how the adoption of diverse management strategies can influence the sustained delivery of these benefits to the natural world and, consequently, to human well-being.

title: Moisture-conditioned hydrothermal responses associated with planted- and natural-forest change scenarios across China
summary: Abstract Changes in planted forests (PF) and natural forests (NF) can affect regional temperature and relative humidity (RH), but their relative responses under contrasting water conditions remain unclear. We incorporated prescribed PF and
content: Abstract Changes in planted forests (PF) and natural forests (NF) can affect regional temperature and relative humidity (RH), but their relative responses under contrasting water conditions remain unclear. We incorporated prescribed PF and NF spatial distributions and their associated satellite-derived vegetation and radiative properties into Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) sensitivity experiments to examine scenario-based hydrothermal responses across China. Spatial and seasonal comparisons were combined with forest-area–leaf-area-index (LAI)-normalized sensitivities, surface-energy decomposition, continuous moisture-gradient analysis, and humidity-pathway diagnostics. The simulated responses were strongly conditioned by regional water availability. In humid Southern China, the PF scenario produced spring cooling of − 0.316 K and an RH increase of + 0.999%, with April responses reaching − 0.730 K and + 2.349%, respectively. A similarly strong early-season response occurred in the Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau, whereas PF cooling in the relatively water-limited Loess Plateau was delayed until May–June. After differences in forest-area and LAI changes were jointly considered, the PF scenario retained comparatively high temperature and humidity sensitivities in Southern China and the Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau. This result indicates that their stronger PF responses were not attributable solely to the larger magnitude of the prescribed vegetation perturbations. The surface-energy decomposition provided a physical explanation for this regional contrast. Cooling in Southern China and the Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau was dominated by latent-heat contributions of − 0.217 and − 0.276 K, respectively, indicating that sufficient water availability supported evapotranspiration-related cooling. In the relatively water-limited Loess Plateau, by contrast, the latent-heat contribution of − 0.108 K was substantially offset by + 0.187 K of sensible heating. The PF−NF contrast changed in both magnitude and direction across the evaporative-fraction gradient, indicating a nonlinear dependence on background water conditions. Continuous soil–water interaction analyses showed a consistent tendency toward relatively stronger PF-associated cooling and moistening with increasing water availability, although the interaction magnitude remained uncertain. Together, these results show that sufficient water availability supports stronger and earlier PF-associated evapotranspiration, latent-heat cooling, and near-surface moistening, whereas water limitation strengthens sensible-heat compensation and makes the PF−NF contrast weaker, delayed, or less consistently differentiated. Because the experiments prescribe forest distributions and satellite-derived surface properties rather than complete forest-type-specific physiological traits, the findings represent moisture-conditioned scenario responses rather than universal intrinsic differences between PF and NF.

title: Secondary Sphere Modification Tunes C–OH Bond Cleavage and Redistributes Rate Control in Electrocatalytic CO2 Reduction by Molecular Cr Complexes
summary: Abstract Mitigating the contribution of anthropogenic carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions to global climate change has motivated the development of earth-abundant transition-metal catalysts capable of electrochemically reducing CO2 to value-adde
content: Abstract Mitigating the contribution of anthropogenic carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions to global climate change has motivated the development of earth-abundant transition-metal catalysts capable of electrochemically reducing CO2 to value-added chemical products. It has previously been demonstrated that bipyridine-based CrN2O2 complexes can selectively reduce CO2 to carbon monoxide (CO) under electrochemical conditions. To improve the kinetic parameters (turnover frequency) of this catalyst family, the effect of adding –OMe pendent substituents to the bipyridine backbone of the ligand structure was explored. Here, two catalysts bearing different numbers and positions of –OMe pendent groups are reported and analyzed with respect to their impact on the proton-transfer step that accompanies C–OH bond cleavage as a part of the catalytic cycle for CO2 reduction. Combining the observed isotope effect for each catalyst with an intrinsic value computed for that catalyst resolves the contributions of CO2 binding and C–OH bond cleavage to rate control individually, giving varying degrees of rate control for CO2 binding across the series. Separating the underlying rate constants shows that, across the series, the rate constant for C–OH cleavage varies by about two orders of magnitude, whereas that for CO2 binding varies by less than a factor of two. This work suggests that the addition of –OMe groups can provide a kinetic enhancement compared to complexes without the substituents; however, the benefit is tempered by shared rate control with the CO2 binding step of the reaction, which was previously shown to contribute to the observed rate.

title: Monitoring Water in Vegetation: Mind the Gap Between Satellite Remote Sensing and Field Scale Approaches
summary: Abstract Purpose of The Review Understanding vegetation water dynamics is crucial for monitoring ecosystem health, improving fire risk assessment, and modelling land–atmosphere feedbacks. This review examines how satellite remote sensing ca
content: Abstract Purpose of The Review Understanding vegetation water dynamics is crucial for monitoring ecosystem health, improving fire risk assessment, and modelling land–atmosphere feedbacks. This review examines how satellite remote sensing can help monitor the vegetation water status (with information about water content and water potential) and identifies the major gaps that currently hinder reconciling satellite data with field-based measurements. It aims to establish bridges across spatial scales to enhance the current monitoring framework for vegetation water status from regional to global levels. The paper mostly focuses on passive microwave remote sensing, which is appropriate for sensing water across different vegetation layers at regional to global scales, and at which the amount of research work and data products are limited. Recent Findings Recent research has established and expanded global in situ and remote sensing datasets of live fuel moisture content (LFMC) and water potential (Ψ). Also, new passive microwave satellite products offer improved sensitivity to canopy water dynamics at coarse scales. However, efforts to reconcile remote sensing and field data are hampered by point-to-pixel scale mismatches and by a limited understanding of how satellite data relates to ecophysiological processes. Emerging concepts such as ecosystem pressure–volume (EPV) curves (with the potential of footprint-scale representativeness) and new satellite VOD-based approaches provide promising pathways to infer water content and water potential from space. Developments in multi-frequency microwave remote sensing further open new opportunities to monitor vertical gradients of water status in plants and to study the sensitivity of microwaves to water across plant tissues. Summary Bridging remote sensing and point-scale research in ecohydrology requires harmonized datasets for validation and comparison of products (here we focus on LFMC products) and new frameworks to monitor water content and water potential. In this paper, we review research progress towards these goals. This will enable large-scale monitoring of vegetation water dynamics, advancing our understanding of plant responses to drought for entire ecosystems and improving spatially-resolved predictions of biosphere–atmosphere interactions.

title: FARMERS’ AWARENESS AND KNOWLEDGE OF CLIMATE SMART AGRICULTURAL PRACTICES AMONG SORGHUM FARMERS IN NORTHWESTERN NIGERIA
source: FUDMA Journal of Animal Production and Environmental Science
summary: The study analyzed farmers’ awareness and knowledge of climate smart agricultural practices on Sorghum production in Northwestern Nigeria. A total of 334 sorghum farmers were sampled using a multi-stage sampling procedure. Primary data were
content: The study analyzed farmers’ awareness and knowledge of climate smart agricultural practices on Sorghum production in Northwestern Nigeria. A total of 334 sorghum farmers were sampled using a multi-stage sampling procedure. Primary data were collected using structured questionnaires. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, CSAP awareness index, and CSAP knowledge scale. The results of the socio-economic characteristics revealed that the mean age of sorghum farmers was 50 years; male dominated (71.9%) Most of the respondents had household sizes of 10-17 persons (34.4.0%) and farming experience ranging from 4 to 21 years (58.3%). The Awareness of CSA practices was generally higher for basic practices than for technical ones with (58.7%) fall within the moderate awareness (40-69), 36.5% with high awareness (70-100) and only 4.8% exhibit low awareness (1-39). Knowledge level of sorghum farmers revealed that farmers are knowledgeable on CSA practices such as noticing any changes in weather patterns over the past years (82.63), how organic manure or compost can be used to improve Sorghum production (80.54), how mulching can improve soil moisture (79.94), aware of improved post-harvest storage methods that reduce losses (76.95) and have you heard about climate-smart agricultural practices (75.75). The overall knowledge score of the sorghum farmers reveals that only 6.7% (75) of the farmers had adequate knowledge of CSA practices, while 93.3% (259) scored below the 80% mastery threshold. The study concluded that sorghum farmers had awareness of CSA practices and inadequate knowledge of CSA practices. It was recommended that Agricultural Development Programmes (ADPs) should ensure regular visits to sorghum farmers. Extension agents should conduct field demonstrations on practices with low adoption, ADPs, research institutes, and NGOs should organize practical village level training sessions before each cropping season and demonstration farms should be established within farming communities to showcase the benefits of practices.

title: IDENTIFY AND SELECT NEW AI ALGORITHM FOR MULTIPLE SEQUENCE ALIGNMENT BASED ON SOME EVALUATION CHARACTERISTICS
summary: This research paper opens new ways for multiple sequence alignments (MSA) that use artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms. Where, Due to a lack of evaluation papers for MSA. Fulfilling this lack is a necessity in the bioinformatics field.
content: This research paper opens new ways for multiple sequence alignments (MSA) that use artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms. Where, Due to a lack of evaluation papers for MSA. Fulfilling this lack is a necessity in the bioinformatics field. To begin with, made a probe on MSA research papers. In addition, analyze these methods. Furthermore, evaluation metadata, then gathered data extracted from the research papers into the table of evaluation methods. Based on these characteristics or metadata, we select an AI algorithm called Augmented random search (ARS). As a result, an evaluation table that contains 8 features (objective functions (quality metrics), parameters or hyperparameter, assessment criteria, benchmark datasets, collect reference alignments, MSA algorithm, analyze and interpret results, and biological relevance) and mapped MSA problem on ARS. This paper adds new knowledge for artificial intelligence and multiple sequence alignment in the bioinformatics field. On the one hand, current research uses genetic algorithm (GA) and Reinforcement learning (RL) to solve MSA problems efficiently, on the other hand, there is an algorithm that beats GA and RL in a performance called Augmented random search (ARS)

title: Agricultural economic responses to ecoclimate teleconnections induced by forest loss
summary: Forest disturbances are increasing globally, altering vegetation in ways that can affect distant agricultural systems through ecoclimate teleconnections. We examine how large-scale U.S. regional forest loss with C3 grass replacement affects
content: Forest disturbances are increasing globally, altering vegetation in ways that can affect distant agricultural systems through ecoclimate teleconnections. We examine how large-scale U.S. regional forest loss with C3 grass replacement affects agricultural production and markets. We integrate climate simulations, econometric yield models, and an agricultural sector model to trace impacts from vegetation change through climate anomalies to yields, land allocation, prices, and welfare, while isolating vegetation-driven effects from greenhouse-gas forcing. Teleconnection-induced yield responses are spatially heterogeneous. Soybean yields decline, particularly in the Southern Plains, while wheat gains occur there and corn responses are muted. This shifts regional crop mixes and increases total production by 1–3%, lowering crop prices, increasing consumer surplus, and reducing producer surplus, with small positive net agricultural welfare effects. Our study excludes forest-sector impacts and ecosystem-service losses and therefore does not imply that forest loss is beneficial. Forest loss across 14 U.S. regions can affect distant climates. Linking these teleconnections to crop yields and agricultural markets reveals soybean losses, wheat gains, 1–3% higher total production, lower crop prices, and small net gains in agricultural welfare.

title: Development of Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP) Models in Python to Optimize Last-Mile Distribution Routes in an SME
source: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
summary: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) that produce perishable food often plan last-mile distribution reactively, which raises fuel consumption, extends working days and forces vehicles to return to the plant for additional product. This
content: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) that produce perishable food often plan last-mile distribution reactively, which raises fuel consumption, extends working days and forces vehicles to return to the plant for additional product. This study develops and evaluates vehicle routing problem (VRP) models implemented in Python for a family-owned cheese SME located in Apaxco de Ocampo, State of Mexico, which serves about 35 commercial destinations per day with more than 900 kg of product using two light trucks of 600 and 800 kg. The research followed the Design Thinking approach in five phases. The empathize and define phases characterized the current operation, three delivery corridors and the isolated fuel cost of each destination. The ideate phase formulated a heterogeneous capacitated VRP with working-day limits, multiple trips and order release times. The prototype phase implemented the model in Python using a Clarke-Wright savings heuristic, a simulated annealing metaheuristic and an exact mixed-integer verification solved with HiGHS. In the test phase, three scenarios were compared under identical orders, vehicles and assumptions: the current dispatching rules, a static scenario with all orders ready at 07:00 and a dynamic scenario with staggered production releases. Under the dynamic scenario, the model reduced the travelled distance from 382.0 to 285.4 km (25.3 %), daily fuel cost from MXN 1,293 to MXN 966, trips from six to four and minutes beyond the working day by 61.2 %. When production and dispatch were synchronized, distance fell to 152.8 km (60.0 %) with two trips and no overtime. A Monte Carlo experiment with 30 simulated days yielded a mean distance reduction of 35.1 %, and the exact verification confirmed the optimal sequence of every route. The results show that route optimization must be accompanied by the synchronization of production and dispatch.

title: Carbon-Star Wind Acceleration Budget and Shell Age of S Cephei
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This paper computes a self-contained budget for S Cephei from published observational values, with every derived number produced by the deposited computation script. S Cephei is a carbon-rich Mira with one of the faster winds among the clas
content: This paper computes a self-contained budget for S Cephei from published observational values, with every derived number produced by the deposited computation script. S Cephei is a carbon-rich Mira with one of the faster winds among the classical long-period variables and a detached-shell history suggested by its far-infrared emission. The adopted inputs are a pulsation period of 487 days, a luminosity of 7300 solar luminosities at an effective temperature of 2100 K, a mass-loss rate of 1e-05 solar masses per year and a terminal expansion speed of 20.5 km/s. From those inputs the calculation derives the stellar radius, mean density and pulsation constant, the wind number density at the dust condensation radius, at ten stellar radii and at a thousand astronomical units, the kinetic power and momentum flux of the outflow, and the shell mass and envelope depletion time implied by the present rate. The headline results are: stellar_radius_Rsun = 645.0; mean_density_kg_m3 = 8.39e-06; pulsation_constant_Q_days = 0.0376; momentum_ratio_to_L_over_c = 1.39; kinetic_power_Lsun = 0.346; number_density_at_condensation_cm3 = 2210000000.0; shell_mass_Msun = 0.08; envelope_depletion_time_yr = 60000.0.
