Even at this star's brisk 20.5 km/s, the kinetic power is 0.346 solar luminosities against a radiated 7300.0 solar luminosities, so the energy budget closes with a wide margin; the binding constraint is momentum, at 1.39 times the single-scattering value. The shell age to a tenth of a parsec is 4770.0 years, and the mass expelled in that span approaches the 0.08 solar masses computed for the adopted window. The wind of S Cephei is fast because carbon dust couples well, not because the star spends an unusual share of its energy on the outflow. The calculation is presented with its inputs, relations and sensitivities stated openly, so that any revised period, distance or mass-loss rate can be substituted and the budget recomputed directly.

title: Development Aid and Infant Mortality in Nigeria
source: Lafia Journal of Economics and Management Sciences
summary: Despite receiving substantial foreign development assistance, Nigeria continues to record relatively high infant mortality rates, raising important questions about the effectiveness of external aid and the extent to which domestic public in
content: Despite receiving substantial foreign development assistance, Nigeria continues to record relatively high infant mortality rates, raising important questions about the effectiveness of external aid and the extent to which domestic public investment can improve child health outcomes.The study examines the short-run and long-run effects of development aid, government health spending, education spending, and primary school enrolment on infant mortality using the Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) framework.The ARDL bounds testing procedure confirms a long-run equilibrium relationship among the variables.Empirical findings indicate that government spending on health care and education significantly reduces infant mortality in the short run, highlighting the need for continued government investment in the social sector.Development aid, by contrast, has a negligible short-run effect and offers no guarantee of sustaining health improvements.However, primary school enrolment shows a strong long-run relationship with infant mortality, underscoring the importance of human capital development and maternal education.Overall, the findings suggest that domestic policies, institutional capacity, and investment in health and education systems are critical complements to development aid in improving its effectiveness.The study recommends improving health financing, expanding access to education, and strengthening health governance around aid utilization to sustain reductions in infant mortality in Nigeria.

title: AGILE GOVERNANCE FOR GLOBAL CIRCULAR ECONOMY TRANSITIONS: AN INTEGRATED FRAMEWORK FROM BRAZIL'S POST-COP30 EXPERIENCE
summary: Agile governance constitutes an adaptive approach to public policy, whose application to the circular economy presents challenges in emerging economies. This study develops an analytical framework for the circular economic transition in Bra
content: Agile governance constitutes an adaptive approach to public policy, whose application to the circular economy presents challenges in emerging economies. This study develops an analytical framework for the circular economic transition in Brazil's post-COP30 context. The research draws on an integrative review of scientific publications, government documents, and institutional reports from 2020 to 2026, systematized through thematic analysis guided by Multi-Level Governance Theory and Adaptive Co-Management. The findings identify eight components organized into three interdependent dimensions: Institutional Governance; Implementation Capacity; and Learning, Monitoring, and Accountability. These dimensions constitute the Integrated Agile Governance Framework (IAGF), connecting institutional coordination, social participation, adaptive experimentation, green finance, and continuous learning. The analysis highlights policy coherence, institutional adaptability, and stakeholder coordination within multi-level arrangements. Grounded in the Brazilian experience, the framework provides analytical references for emerging economies, contributing to improved public policies, integrated governance instruments, and the sustainability of contemporary circular economic transitions.

title: TYPE I COLLAGEN AND MULTI-WALLED CARBON NANOTUBE BIOCOMPOSITES FOR TISSUE ENGINEERING: AN IN VITRO EVALUATION OF CELLULAR RESPONSES
summary: Tissue engineering aims to develop biomaterials that support cellular responses. This study evaluated the biocompatibility of type I collagen and multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT) biocomposites in murine 3T3 fibroblasts. Collagen matrice
content: Tissue engineering aims to develop biomaterials that support cellular responses. This study evaluated the biocompatibility of type I collagen and multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT) biocomposites in murine 3T3 fibroblasts. Collagen matrices (1.6–2.4 mg/mL) and formulations containing MWCNTs at 0.6%, 1.2%, 2.4%, and 4.8% (v/v) were analyzed. Cellular responses were assessed using MTT, LIVE/DEAD, cell migration, and EdU incorporation assays. Collagen alone did not cause statistically significant changes in cellular metabolism or viability. In the biocomposites, the addition of 1.2% MWCNTs was associated with mean increases of 89% and 29% in metabolic activity in formulations containing 2.0 and 2.2 mg/mL collagen, respectively. In contrast, the 4.8% concentration was associated with reduced metabolic activity. Cell viability remained preserved across the evaluated formulations. The addition of 0.6% MWCNTs was associated with a 9.54% increase in cell migration compared with collagen alone, whereas no statistically significant changes in proliferation were observed. These findings indicate that cellular responses vary according to biocomposite composition and the biological parameter assessed. The results provide preliminary evidence supporting further investigation of these formulations. Additional studies are needed to characterize their properties and determine their potential applications in tissue engineering.

title: The triadic convergence in Industry 5.0: Orchestrating resilient supply chains, agile project management, and algorithmic Islamic banking through smart contracts and green sukuk
summary: Contemporary global value networks and capital-intensive infrastructure projects face an existential crisis driven by geopolitical disruptions, persistent inflation, and the fragile leverage of conventional interest-based debt. Although Sup
content: Contemporary global value networks and capital-intensive infrastructure projects face an existential crisis driven by geopolitical disruptions, persistent inflation, and the fragile leverage of conventional interest-based debt. Although Supply Chain Management (SCM), Project Management (PM), and Islamic Banking (IB) have evolved rapidly in isolation, a unified framework integrating all three is absent. This article bridges that gap by formulating the Triadic Convergence Framework (TCF), a novel cyber-physical-financial architecture operating within the human-centric and sustainable ethos of Industry 5.0. Grounded in Transaction Cost Economics, Agency Theory, Dynamic Capabilities Theory, and the socio-ethical axioms of Maqasid al-Shariah, this study employs a multi-layered conceptual and mathematical modeling approach. It synthesizes Q1 literature across artificial intelligence, blockchain-enabled Supply Chain Finance, Agile-Hybrid Project Management, and Islamic Sustainable Finance. Furthermore, it formulates a deterministic mathematical model linking Earned Value Management indices with automated, smart-contract-driven Islamic financing disbursements (Parallel Istisna’a and Tokenized Murabaha) verified by IoT Digital Twins. The integration of AI-driven Digital Twins and permissioned blockchain ledgers resolves the historical operational bottleneck of Islamic banking: the high transaction cost of verifying physical asset existence and ownership transfer across multi-tier supply networks. By coupling real-time physical project milestones with smart-contract-governed Green Sukuk and Musharakah pools, the proposed architecture eliminates moral hazard and principal-agent asymmetries inherent in conventional project finance. Our comparative structural analysis demonstrates that synchronizing Agile sprint backlogs with Sharia-compliant asset-backed liquidity buffers dampens the supply chain bullwhip effect, prevents contractor working-capital starvation, and enforces verifiable ESG compliance. This study establishes a rigorous mathematical and algorithmic bridge between project earned value metrics, multi-tier supply chain inventory flows, and Sharia-compliant contract execution. It provides institutional policymakers, project directors, and Islamic FinTech architects with an actionable blueprint for transitioning from debt-fragile operations to antifragile, asset-anchored, and ethically governed Industry 5.0 ecosystems.

title: Soil storage and growth media shape culture-based recovery of pyrophilous bacteria and fungi from burned soils
summary: Increasingly frequent and severe fires worldwide underscore the need to understand how pyrophilous microbes survive, thrive, and drive post-fire ecosystem regeneration. However, characterizing their traits through omics and phenotypic assay
content: Increasingly frequent and severe fires worldwide underscore the need to understand how pyrophilous microbes survive, thrive, and drive post-fire ecosystem regeneration. However, characterizing their traits through omics and phenotypic assays is limited by the lack of cultured isolates. Here, we collected burned soils after a severe California shrubland wildfire and used a culturomics approach to test how culture media type and soil storage method affected the abundance and diversity of pyrophilous bacteria and fungi. Using fresh soils, we compared three media types: rich media (Lysogeny Broth [LB] for bacteria; Malt Yeast Agar [MYA] for fungi), oligotrophic Reasoner’s 2A (R2A), and a newly developed pyrogenic organic matter (PyOM) media. We also evaluated four soil storage methods using rich media: air-drying, refrigeration at 4°C, and freezing at –80°C with or without glycerol. R2A recovered the greatest richness of bacterial and fungal genera, although PyOM medium isolated several taxa not recovered on other media. For bacteria, freezing soils at –80°C without glycerol preserved the greatest genus richness, whereas freezing with glycerol preserved the greatest species richness. For fungi, freezing at –80°C without glycerol preserved the most species while maintaining genus richness comparable to fresh and refrigerated soils. These findings guided the development of a culture collection of more than 500 pyrophilous bacterial and fungal isolates. Lessons learned from media type and soil storage can also be applied to the cultivation of environmental soil microbes from many habitat types and improve culture collections of fastidious microbes.

title: Top pruning and phosphorus fertilization improve female cone yield potential and modify nitrogen and phosphorus allocation in grafted Pinus massoniana clones
summary: Abstract Top pruning is an effective way to produce "orchard-style" forest seed orchards, and phosphorus (P) fertilization can improve the reproductive ability of Masson pine (Pinus massoniana) to some extent. However, it is necessary to de
content: Abstract Top pruning is an effective way to produce "orchard-style" forest seed orchards, and phosphorus (P) fertilization can improve the reproductive ability of Masson pine (Pinus massoniana) to some extent. However, it is necessary to determine the absorption and distribution of carbon (C) and nitrogen (N) nutrients by applying phosphorus fertilizer under top pruning. Two clones, high-yielding (209) and low-yielding (225), were tested in a pot experiment with 15N markers during early floral primordium. Calcium magnesium phosphate fertilizer was applied at doses of 0 g/plant (P0), 200 g/plant (P2), and 400 g/plant (P4) to the test plots without top pruning (N-TP) and with top pruning (TP). Overall, top pruning promoted female cone formation in high-yielding P. massoniana clones and significantly affected the downward movement of the fruiting layer, the density of female cones in the lower branches increased by 25.45%~64.97% after top pruning. However, their impact on the formation of female cones in low-yield clones was limited. Top pruning altered the variation of C:N, N:P ratios by increasing C, N and P contents of lower branches. Compared with no top pruning, the C:N ratios of lower branches of 209 and 225 clones increased by 5.79%~27.38% and 2.57%~13.60% after top pruning, respectively. At flowering period, the distribution ratios of N and P in high-yielding female cones increased by 175.0% and 46.3% after top pruning, respectively, indicating that top pruning promoted the absorption of N and P content to female cones. The interaction effect between top pruning and P fertilizer had a significant impact on female cone density, The application of P fertilizer can improve the N harvesting ability of P. massoniana under top-pruning measures, especially by increasing the C:N ratio in the second layer of coniferous branches in the lower part of the tree and promoting the distribution of N to female flower heads, which is beneficial for improving seed yield. On the whole, top pruning causes changes in the spatial structure of trees, affecting the redistribution of nutrients and promoting the distribution of N and P to female cones; The application of phosphorus fertilizer not only regulates the carbon to nitrogen ratio of needles, but also improves the N and P nutrient absorption capacity of P. massoniana under the combination of top pruning measures, which helps to distribute nutrients to organs related to the formation of female cones. The study confirmed that top pruning and phosphorus fertilization increased the probability of high yield and altered the nutrient distribution characteristics in P. massoniana.

title: Mergers of Consumer Cooperatives
summary: Problem definition: Consumer cooperatives are consumer-owned and managed enterprises that aim to achieve buyer power and maximize their members’ welfare. Recently, several cooperatives in major economies, such as the United Kingdom (UK), It
content: Problem definition: Consumer cooperatives are consumer-owned and managed enterprises that aim to achieve buyer power and maximize their members’ welfare. Recently, several cooperatives in major economies, such as the United Kingdom (UK), Italy, and Switzerland, have merged to increase their buyer power and achieve lower prices for their members. We analyze how these mergers affect market outcomes, consumer welfare, supplier profits, and social welfare. Methodology/results: We build a game-theoretic model of a two-tier supply chain where multiple consumer cooperatives procure a product from a market on behalf of their member consumers. Multiple suppliers produce for this market and can increase their supply by incurring a scale-up cost. We show that mergers of consumer cooperatives enable consumers to retain more income to purchase other goods, thereby improving consumer welfare. However, mergers also induce suppliers to reduce production, causing each consumer to receive less of the product supplied, thereby reducing consumer welfare. We find that this underproduction is even more pronounced in industries with low scale-up costs. Thus, we show that cooperatives merge and benefit member consumers only when the pre-merger number of cooperatives or the production scale-up cost exceeds a certain threshold. Despite the benefits to member consumers, mergers always harm suppliers, can harm other consumers, and reduce social welfare in the absence of substantial synergy gains. We further show that greater horizontal or vertical differentiation among cooperatives increases the benefit of mergers. Managerial implications: Mergers of cooperatives make a nuanced impact on consumer welfare and social welfare due to their effects on wholesale prices and production incentives. Policymakers should weigh mergers’ benefits for member consumers against their harm to other consumers and social welfare.

title: Stochastic Programming for Dynamic Temperature Control of Refrigerated Road Transport
summary: Temperature control in refrigerated delivery vehicles is critical for preserving product quality, yet existing approaches neglect critical operational uncertainties, such as stochastic door-opening durations and heterogeneous initial produc
content: Temperature control in refrigerated delivery vehicles is critical for preserving product quality, yet existing approaches neglect critical operational uncertainties, such as stochastic door-opening durations and heterogeneous initial product temperatures. We propose a framework to optimize cooling policies for refrigerated trucks on fixed routes by explicitly modeling these uncertainties while capturing all relevant thermodynamic interactions in the trailer. To this end, we integrate high-fidelity thermodynamic modeling with a multistage stochastic programming formulation and solve the resulting problem using stochastic dual dynamic programming. In cooperation with industry partners and based on real-world data, we set up computational experiments that demonstrate that our stochastic policy consistently outperforms the best deterministic benchmark by 35% on average as well as a rolling two-stage approach while being computationally tractable. In a separate analysis, we show that by fixing the duration of temperature violations, our policy operates with up to 40% less fuel than deterministic policies. Our results demonstrate that pallet-level thermal status information is the single most crucial piece of information in the problem and that it can be used to significantly reduce temperature violations. Knowledge of the timing and length of customer stops is the second-most important factor, and together with detailed modeling of thermodynamic interactions, it can be used to further significantly reduce violations. Our analysis of the optimal stochastic cooling policy reveals that preemptive cooling before a stop is the key element of an optimal policy. These findings highlight the value of sophisticated control strategies in maintaining the quality of perishable products while reducing the carbon footprint of the industry and improving operational efficiency. Supplemental Material: The online appendix is available at https://doi.org/10.1287/trsc.2025.0329 .

title: Spatial modelling of available aluminum in glacial till: informing a boreal forest soil carbon predictor
summary: Boreal forest soils store 30 % of global forest soil carbon, making them a crucial component of the carbon cycle. However, climate change at high latitudes is increasing temperatures and producing unpredictable precipitation patterns. Soil
content: Boreal forest soils store 30 % of global forest soil carbon, making them a crucial component of the carbon cycle. However, climate change at high latitudes is increasing temperatures and producing unpredictable precipitation patterns. Soil organic carbon (SOC) formation and stabilization is tied to precipitation patterns, thus climate change will inevitably influence the stability and longevity of boreal forest SOC. The current size and distribution of this reservoir is poorly understood, creating uncertainty under current and future climate scenarios. Previous research demonstrates mineral soil properties may be used to model boreal forest SOC accurately. The surface slope, depth of carbon enriched horizon, and climate characteristics are important parameters for modelling SOC and can generally be obtained or estimated via remote sensing. However, information about the availability of reactive aluminum – non-crystalline forms capable of interacting with organic matter to form stable carbon rich organometal complexes in mineral soils – is not widely available but is controlled by the weatherable aluminum in soil parent material. To bridge this gap, the Newfoundland and Labrador till geochemistry dataset was used here to map and model weatherable aluminum availability in glacial till across the island of Newfoundland as a function of geology and climate. The Random Forest Algorithm was employed to develop two models: one relying solely on the strength of geological and climatic variables, and the other drawing additionally on the spatial context of sample points. The first model performed well ( R 2 =0.60), however, adding a spatial component increased the performance of the second model ( R 2 =0.71). Bedrock type and proximity of the samples to certain units were indicated to be the strongest controls on aluminum availability, while environmental factors were less influential. Additionally, model uncertainty was calibrated empirically and mapped spatially, providing reliable and actionable information about the confidence of predictions over the study area. This project demonstrates the value of predictive geospatial modelling for till geochemistry mapping and delivers key aluminum availability predictions useful for future efforts in deriving SOC reservoir estimates across Newfoundland.

title: Smart strategy for built environment optimization: In-situ test and orthogonal experiment in traditional ethnic dwellings
summary: Maintaining indoor thermal comfort usually increases energy consumption from HVAC systems, making the development of passive retrofit strategies important. This study focuses on traditional dwellings in the cold high-altitude region of nort
content: Maintaining indoor thermal comfort usually increases energy consumption from HVAC systems, making the development of passive retrofit strategies important. This study focuses on traditional dwellings in the cold high-altitude region of northwestern Sichuan, China, aiming to balance thermal performance improvement with the preservation of their architectural and cultural value. Field measurements, simulation modeling, standardized scoring, orthogonal experimental design, and simulation validation were integrated to evaluate passive retrofit strategies. The orthogonal experiment reduced the full-factorial design space from 8,748 possible combinations to 81 representative cases. The optimal strategy was identified as building form A, orientation S360, SEPS wall insulation, window construction 5, and WWR i. This strategy increased the proportion of thermally comfortable hours from 7.8 % in the baseline case to 24.0 %, corresponding to an increase of 16.2 percentage points. The study demonstrates that indoor thermal comfort in traditional dwellings in cold high-altitude regions can be substantially improved while preserving architectural appearance and cultural value. The findings provide a transferable methodological reference for traditional dwellings facing the dual challenge of heritage conservation and thermal performance improvement.

title: Endemic innovation: territorial anchoring, knowledge recombination, and innovation-driven development
summary: Innovation research has established that innovation is territorially differentiated, yet existing approaches do not fully specify when a place-specific resource or capability is constitutive of an innovation rather than merely contextual. T
content: Innovation research has established that innovation is territorially differentiated, yet existing approaches do not fully specify when a place-specific resource or capability is constitutive of an innovation rather than merely contextual. This conceptual article introduces Endemic Innovation (EI) as an innovation category defined by causal territorial anchoring and knowledge-intensive transformation. EI is an innovation implemented in use or introduced to a market whose distinctive value depends causally on, and remains at least partly anchored in, either a place-specific biophysical resource or condition or a path-dependent capability embedded in a territorial trajectory. It arises from a non-trivial, knowledge-intensive transformation of that territorial foundation, often by recombining territorially embedded knowledge with complementary external knowledge or technologies. We distinguish resource/condition-anchored from capability-anchored forms, which differ in endogeneity and rate of change. We also separate constitutive criteria from enabling conditions and contingent outcomes such as sustainability, inclusion, local value capture, and international diffusion. Structured empirical illustrations clarify the framework’s range and boundary conditions, while a provisional, theory-informed process heuristic translates it into testable decision points without claiming a universal sequence. The contribution is a bounded, falsifiable construct, applicable across economies but strategically relevant where territorial assets and capabilities provide underused pathways for innovation-led development.

title: Late-Stage Fluorosulfurylation Using Sulfuryl Fluoride Bound within a Metal–Organic Framework
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
summary: Abstract Organic S(VI) fluorides have garnered substantial interest for covalent drug discovery and chemoproteomics due to their ambient stability and unique electrophilic reactivity. Sulfuryl fluoride (SO2F2) is the ideal reagent for the s
content: Abstract Organic S(VI) fluorides have garnered substantial interest for covalent drug discovery and chemoproteomics due to their ambient stability and unique electrophilic reactivity. Sulfuryl fluoride (SO2F2) is the ideal reagent for the synthesis of various S(VI)–F moieties, yet it is a toxic greenhouse gas, often making it incompatible with laboratory settings. Developing a strategy for handling SO2F2 that is amenable to high-throughput reaction discovery would enhance its utility in the laboratory without necessitating specialized equipment or extensive safety measures. Herein, we report a strategy to safely store reactive SO2F2 within a metal–organic framework (MOF) for its facile application to the synthesis of electrophilic, bioactive molecules. The solid SO2F2–Mg2(dobdc) reagent can be stored for at least five months with minimal gas loss due to the strong yet reversible interaction between SO2F2 and Mg2+ centers in the MOF, as confirmed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Using this reagent, we prepare a range of drug-like arylfluorosulfates, primary and secondary acyclic sulfamoyl fluorides, saturated N-heterocyclic sulfamoyl fluorides, and N-heteroarene sulfamoyl fluorides, the last of which cannot be accessed using sulfonium salt alternatives to SO2F2 due to the requirement for strongly basic conditions. These findings represent the first experimental study of SO2F2 adsorption within a MOF and the first use of MOFs for late-stage fluorosulfurylation, paving the way toward a general approach to carefully handling dangerous, reactive gases as solid reagents.

title: DDA-BNN v1.0: a morphology-aware surrogate model for the optical properties of black carbon-containing particles
summary: Black carbon (BC) is the most strongly absorbing component of atmospheric aerosol and significantly impacts Earth's energy balance. The optical properties of BC-containing particles depend on particle-level variability in size, chemical com
content: Black carbon (BC) is the most strongly absorbing component of atmospheric aerosol and significantly impacts Earth's energy balance. The optical properties of BC-containing particles depend on particle-level variability in size, chemical composition, and internal morphology. Such particle-level details are not easily represented in large-scale atmospheric models. Existing parameterizations typically assume idealized particle geometries (e.g., homogeneous spheres or concentric core–shell spheres) and homogeneous mixing, which can yield biased predictions and provide no quantitative estimate of model-form uncertainty at the single-particle level. In this work, we present a probabilistic framework for predicting the optical properties of individual BC-containing particles using a hybrid Bayesian neural network (BNN) model trained on discrete dipole approximation (DDA) simulations. The hybrid BNN is a flexible combination of deterministic and Bayesian layers allowing for more realistic treatment of particle optical properties and quantification of uncertainty. The hybrid BNN model predicts extinction efficiency, single-scattering albedo, and asymmetry parameter and returns predictive uncertainty that can be decomposed into aleatoric (data-driven variability) and epistemic (uncertainty due to limited training coverage) components. We show that the hybrid BNN outperforms homogeneous-sphere and core–shell Mie approximations for calculating extinction and scattering-sensitive quantities ( Q ext , SSA and g ), while maintaining comparable accuracy for absorption-related metrics. We further demonstrate how epistemic uncertainty highlights under-sampled regions of particle parameter space, enabling targeted design of future DDA simulations that most effectively reduce model uncertainty. This uncertainty-aware surrogate provides a practical pathway for incorporating realistically complex particle morphologies into parameterizations of aerosol optical properties, which will ultimately improve the reliability of model-based assessments of BC impacts on the atmosphere.

title: Evidence-Based Workflows and New Approach Methods for the Safe and Sustainable Design of Innovative Products
summary: Abstract The transition toward Safe and Sustainable by Design (SSbD) chemicals and materials necessitates a fundamental shift from reactive hazard assessment to predictive, mechanism-based innovation governance. Traditional animal-based tox
content: Abstract The transition toward Safe and Sustainable by Design (SSbD) chemicals and materials necessitates a fundamental shift from reactive hazard assessment to predictive, mechanism-based innovation governance. Traditional animal-based toxicology and late-stage risk assessment approaches are increasingly inadequate to address the pace, complexity, and sustainability expectations of modern product development. This article examines how New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), including in silico modeling, in vitro systems, and quantitative in vitro to in vivo extrapolation (QIVIVE), can serve as an integrated knowledge engine supporting the SSbD framework. We discuss how these methodologies provide a pathway to integrate human-relevant mechanistic evidence into Next Generation Risk Assessment (NGRA), supporting SSbD decisions through tiered, hypothesis-driven workflows. Emphasis is placed on mechanistic anchoring via Adverse Outcome Pathways (AOPs) and digital workflow integration aligned with FAIR data principles. By aligning mechanistic toxicology with exposure science and digital decision-support systems, integrated NAM workflows provide a scientifically robust strategy for advancing transparent and sustainable chemical innovation. The convergence of SSbD and NGRA represents a transformative opportunity to enhance human and environmental protection while fostering responsible technological progress.

title: Sea ice variability and links to East Siberian permafrost carbon remobilization during the last glacial-interglacial transition
summary: Sea ice plays a central role in the polar climate system, and its rapid decline in the Arctic over recent decades has altered surface albedo and the exchange of heat and gases between the ocean and atmosphere. Investigations of earlier warm
content: Sea ice plays a central role in the polar climate system, and its rapid decline in the Arctic over recent decades has altered surface albedo and the exchange of heat and gases between the ocean and atmosphere. Investigations of earlier warming events, such as the Preboreal/Early Holocene (PB/EH, 11–8 kyr B.P.), Bølling-Allerød (B/A, 14.7–12.9 kyr B.P.), and Dansgaard Oeschger event 3 (DO-3, 28–27.5 kyr B.P.), likely hold clues on climate system responses to changes in Arctic sea ice. This study explores the history of sea ice over the Southern Lomonosov Ridge and its potential relation to permafrost carbon remobilization. Sea ice conditions over the last 27 kyrs were reconstructed through a combination of the sea ice biomarker IP 25 (Ice Proxy 25) and marine phytoplankton biomarkers (brassicasterol and dinosterol) from the chronologically well-constrained core 31-PC, sampled at the Southern Lomonosov Ridge during the SWERUS-C3 expedition in 2014. The reconstruction allowed for a direct comparison with previously published terrestrial organic carbon (terrOC) remobilization history from the same core. Our findings revealed a seasonal sea ice cover between 27–26 kyr B.P. after the DO-3 warm event, which likely caused more heat and moisture transport from ocean to land and strengthened permafrost thawing along the nearby coastline. A perennial sea ice cover then developed and persisted throughout the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM) to the Younger Dryas (YD), including the entire B/A warm period. Due to sea-level rise during Meltwater Pulse 1A (MWP 1A, 14.7–13.5 kyr B.P.), terrOC remobilization during B/A was rapid but its magnitude smaller when compared to PB and DO-3 in 31-PC, and other records from the Arctic. These records collectively suggest that sea-level rise, rather than sea ice conditions, exerts the primary control on coastal erosion during B/A, while we propose that the perennial sea ice cover may have limited wave-induced coastal erosion of the continental shelf bordering the Southern Lomonosov Ridge. A sharp reduction and breakup of the perennial sea ice was observed from the PB to the Early Holocene. Contrary to the B/A, Meltwater Pulse 1B during PB triggered significant coastal erosion and terrOC remobilization concurrent with the sea ice decline. The absence of sea ice in parallel to larger coastal erosion compared to B/A implies the role of waning sea ice in enhancing permafrost carbon mobilization along the coastline in this period. In accordance with sea ice records from other Arctic seas, the Holocene record exhibited a period of gradual sea ice expansion. Taken together, these findings highlight sea ice extent as a possible factor regulating coastal permafrost carbon remobilization during the last deglaciation.

title: Formation of rotating supergiants via stellar mergers in dense clusters: Implications for black hole natal spins
source: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
summary: Abstract We investigate how massive stellar mergers in young star clusters imprint on black hole spin distributions and the implications for gravitational wave sources. While mechanisms like hierarchical mergers and binary accretion can for
content: Abstract We investigate how massive stellar mergers in young star clusters imprint on black hole spin distributions and the implications for gravitational wave sources. While mechanisms like hierarchical mergers and binary accretion can form rapidly spinning black holes, our central hypothesis is that angular momentum transferred during stellar mergers substantially affects the spins of the merger products and resulting black holes, with some merger products evolving into collapsar-like objects that retain thick accretion disks enabling efficient spin up. This is in contrast to the general expectation that black holes form with small spins, having shed most of their envelope angular momentum via winds and expansion before core collapse. Using roughly 150 N-body models generated with the Cluster Monte Carlo code, CMC, we analyze stellar mergers that lead to black hole formation, prioritizing “significant” events with mass ratio q > 0.1. After identifying optimal candidates, we explore stellar structure and post-merger evolution implications with MESA models to capture angular momentum injection and pre-collapse profiles most relevant for BH natal spin. In our current dataset representative of Milky Way-like globular clusters, up to roughly half of black holes are formed from such mergers, with roughly 10% from “significant” mergers. Angular momentum estimates indicate substantial spin-up during the merger, and trends with mass ratio and stellar properties suggest strong correlations with the final black hole spin. In some cases, dimensionless spin parameters of a ≃ 0.5 or more are expected. This process has important implications for the dynamical formation and retention of gravitational wave sources in clusters.

title: Process-level contributions to uncertainty in aerosol effective radiative forcing: a perturbed parameter ensemble with ICON–HAM
summary: Changes in aerosols since the preindustrial era have altered the top-of-the-atmosphere radiation balance by scattering and absorbing solar radiation (aerosol–radiation interactions, ARI) and indirectly interacting with clouds (aerosol–cloud
content: Changes in aerosols since the preindustrial era have altered the top-of-the-atmosphere radiation balance by scattering and absorbing solar radiation (aerosol–radiation interactions, ARI) and indirectly interacting with clouds (aerosol–cloud interactions, ACI), known as aerosol effective radiative forcing (ERF aer ). ERF aer persistently remains one of the most uncertain components in climate projections, due to imperfect representations of aerosol and cloud processes in climate models. Here, we construct a perturbed parameter ensemble (PPE) with the aerosol–climate model ICON2.6.4–A–HAM2.3 (hereafter ICON–HAM) to quantify key sources of ERF aer uncertainty. We perturb 42 aerosol and cloud parameters over 383 PPE members. Parametric uncertainties in aerosol and cloud processes yield a 90 % credible range of −1.42 to −0.65 W m −2 for ERF aer (mean: −1.04 W m −2 ) for the period 2024–2025. The parameters related to emissions (anthropogenic sulfur dioxide, natural dimethyl sulfide, and emitted particle size) dominate ACI uncertainty and hence ERF aer uncertainty (80 %), while absorption-related parameters (anthropogenic black carbon emissions and aerosol refractive indices) drive ARI uncertainty (60 %). Cloud parameters account for 13 % of ERF aer uncertainty, mainly via convection and entrainment processes. The sensitivity analysis of model diagnostics to parameters reveals that many present-day aerosol and cloud observables share dominant causes of uncertainty with ACI and ARI forcing, highlighting the potential for constraining ERF aer using existing space- and ground-based measurements. Notably, model biases against SPEXone and MODIS observations coincide spatially with parametric uncertainties, suggesting that much of these biases may be mitigated through appropriate constraint with observations, while the remainder requires structural model developments in combination with improved observations.

title: Climate-Dyna Deep Hedging for XVAs: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning, Residual Climate HVA, and Hedge-Instrument Discovery
source: ACM International Conference on AI in Finance (ICAIF)
summary: For a trading desk, residual climate HVA is the climate cost left after its inherited hedge and any admissible overlay have been taken into account; it therefore cannot be inferred from a stand-alone stress loss. We obtain this residual by
content: For a trading desk, residual climate HVA is the climate cost left after its inherited hedge and any admissible overlay have been taken into account; it therefore cannot be inferred from a stand-alone stress loss. We obtain this residual by comparing paired climate-on and baseline worlds and reoptimizing the overlay for each hedge universe, which also turns hedge-instrument discovery into a valuation problem: an instrument is useful to the extent that it lowers the optimized residual cost. The linear-Gaussian case has an exact finite-horizon Riccati solution; Climate-Dyna starts from that hedge and learns the remaining nonlinear correction from paired world-model rollouts, with an independent gate deciding whether to deploy the update. In controlled semi-synthetic EU ETS experiments calibrated to public data, the inherited hedge lowers the mean climate charge from 1.517 to 0.906; the learned overlay reaches 0.831 against the finite-environment optimum of 0.821. Separate control tests show \(93\%\) lower regret than replay with one quarter of the trajectories; adaptation using 25 target transitions retains \(60.7\%\) of the exact-assisted gain.

title: To Repair or Replace? Consumer decision pathways and their influence on the environmental assessments of repairing
summary: Repairing products is a central strategy within the Circular Economy to extend product lifespans. However, current Life Cycle Assess-ments (LCAs) often rely on inconsistent assumptions regarding lifetime extension and frequently overlook th
content: Repairing products is a central strategy within the Circular Economy to extend product lifespans. However, current Life Cycle Assess-ments (LCAs) often rely on inconsistent assumptions regarding lifetime extension and frequently overlook the environmental impact of social practices in the context of repair processes. This study develops a framework to structure potential repair pathways that con-sumers can choose and a methodology to evaluate their environmental impact. To demonstrate this approach, the methodology is ap-plied to selected pathways, being categorized into the two main distinct pathways "Self-Service" and "Repair Services" to contrast them with the “Replace” pathway, i.e. buying the same product. A lifespan-based factor is used to identify environmental break-even points, allowing for comparisons of different pathways. The methodology is applied to three case studies – a hand blender, a smartphone, and a pair of jeans – using Carbon Footprint and Material Footprint as primary indicators. Environmentally relevant consumer decisions concern the mode of transportation (car, bicycle, mail, public transport) and the use of specialized repair tools. The results indicate that transportation, particularly the use of passenger cars to reach repair shops, can significantly increase environmental impacts, even ne-gating the benefits of repair. Furthermore, the acquisition of specialized tools for one-time self-repairs can be a relevant environmental burden illustrating that product replacement may be sometimes the more environmentally sustainable choice. The study concludes that the lifespan factor provides a robust tool for consumer behavior decision-making. Finally, it highlights that "design to repair" must also consider the optimization of the repair service systems to minimize transport-related emissions and the ones related to repair tools.

title: From sludge to supper: biosolids as a potential source of microplastics in the food chain
summary: Microplastics are widely documented as arriving in municipal wastewater from diverse sources such as clothing fibers, tire shreds and cosmetics. Wastewater treatment works typically remove 70–99% of microplastics from the aqueous phase befo
content: Microplastics are widely documented as arriving in municipal wastewater from diverse sources such as clothing fibers, tire shreds and cosmetics. Wastewater treatment works typically remove 70–99% of microplastics from the aqueous phase before discharging treated water back to the aquatic environment. However, rather than being eliminated, the microplastic burden is merely transferred to and concentrated in the sewage sludge created by the treatment process. This sludge is typically subjected to varying levels of treatment to form biosolids but the microplastics remain and can potentially enter agricultural soils when biosolids are spread to land as a nitrogen- and phosphate-rich fertilizer or soil amendment. Here, it may become part of the food chain, providing a pathway to human ingestion of microplastic via plant uptake, animal grazing and leaching back to watercourses. This potential route for human exposure to microplastics is of concern, particularly considering the additional contaminants that also concentrate to sludge and can follow the same route to reach humans. Alternative methods of sewage sludge disposal such as landfilling and incineration also have major shortcomings and governments with available landbank wish to retain land application as an option. This paper therefore evaluates where intervention is possible across the entire pathway from source, via wastewater and biosolids, to soil and the food-chain. We evaluate appropriate options to reduce the microplastic burden both upstream by reducing their inputs at source and downstream along the land-based food chain through innovative changes in the end-of-pipe handling of biosolids and sludge using techniques such as vermicomposting, thermal treatments and other emerging developments, and we investigate how current evidence can inform policy and practice.

title: Evidence of an Inverted U‐Shaped Relationship Between a Multilayered Gender Diversity Criterion and Greenhouse Gas Emissions: Insights From FTSE350
summary: ABSTRACT This paper examines the possible effect of women's representation at three organisational levels, including the boardroom, senior management and the workforce, on reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions using an unbalanced panel of
content: ABSTRACT This paper examines the possible effect of women's representation at three organisational levels, including the boardroom, senior management and the workforce, on reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions using an unbalanced panel of FTSE350 firms over the period 2010–2020. Using quantile regression, we document an inverted U‐shaped effect of gender diversity on GHG emissions across three organisational levels. This association is contingent on a minimum critical mass of women being present on the three organisational levels. This evidence implies that gender diversity at the board level is not enough; it must be supported by adequate gender diversity across the organisation to optimise corporate efforts to combat environmental threats. Our evidence offers practical implications and suggests agendas for future studies that could build on our research.

title: AN ANALYSIS OF FACTORS INFLUENCING SUSTAINABLE CONSUMPTION BEHAVIORS AMONG GENERATION Z IN KAZAKHSTAN
summary: This study explores the attitudes and behaviors of Generation Z in Kazakhstan toward sustainable consumption and considers implications for marketers seeking to engage this environmentally conscious demographic. Drawing on a survey of 329 u
content: This study explores the attitudes and behaviors of Generation Z in Kazakhstan toward sustainable consumption and considers implications for marketers seeking to engage this environmentally conscious demographic. Drawing on a survey of 329 university students, the research examines factors influencing Gen Z’s sustainable behaviors, including environmental concern, social influence, and perceptions of sustainable product pricing. The results reveal a significant positive correlation between environmental concern and engagement in sustainable practices, indicating that Gen Z shows a preference for eco-friendly products and brands committed to sustainability. Given the higher prices of eco-friendly options, pricing remains an important consideration in Gen Z’s sustainable purchasing decisions. Findings emphasize the importance of transparent communication and authentic sustainability practices in building trust and loyalty with this demographic. Marketers should align their strategies with Gen Z’s values by adopting pricing approaches that support eco-friendly choices and leveraging social media to foster communities of conscious consumers.

title: The dwarf galaxy NGC 185: The flagship of Andromeda's dwarf galaxies for the study of evolved stellar populations
summary: Reaching galaxies at 10--15 Mpc with HST and JWST requires star formation history (SFH) diagnostics that do not rely on the faint main sequence turn-off. We investigate whether horizontal branch (HB), red clump (RC), and red and asymptotic
content: Reaching galaxies at 10--15 Mpc with HST and JWST requires star formation history (SFH) diagnostics that do not rely on the faint main sequence turn-off. We investigate whether horizontal branch (HB), red clump (RC), and red and asymptotic giant branch (RGB, AGB) stars can fill this role for dwarf elliptical galaxies, using NGC 185 as a test case. Because the colour and magnitude of HB and RC stars depend on the mass their progenitors lose along the RGB, constraining this mass loss is an essential prerequisite for any SFH derived from these evolved populations. We used stellar evolution models of low- and intermediate-mass stars as inputs to population synthesis simulations that reproduce the colour distribution and luminosity function of stars in the $(m_ F606W -m_ F814W ,, F814W )$ diagram. The study of the stars populating the HB was used to derive the distance modulus and reddening, the average mass loss suffered by the stars during the ascending on the RGB and the SFH occurred during the ancient epochs, before 7 Gyr ago. The luminosity function of the RC gives us constraints on the recent SFH ($<8 $). We then analysed the AGB population, the sole contributor to the galaxy's dust budget, and combined it with IRAC- photometry to characterise the dust properties of objects on the red side of the colour-magnitude diagram. Gyr Spitzer The distribution of HB stars yields a reddening of E(B-V)=0.20 mag and a distance modulus of DM=24.10 mag for NGC 185. The average mass lost by low-mass stars during the RGB phase is ̊m (0.22± 0.01),M_⊙. The 5% uncertainty is based on the assumption of a single metallicity, rm Z=0.002, while the possible degeneracy including age and helium content would increase the uncertainty to about 10%. Star formation was concentrated at early epochs, with half of the stars formed more than 11 Gyr ago. The morphology of the HB indicates essentially no metallicity spread among stars older than 8 Gyr, whereas the slope of the RGB suggests that part of the stars younger than 5--6 Gyr are slightly enriched in metals. We compare the resulting SFH with earlier reconstructions based on deep HST photometry reaching the MSTO, and use the modelled AGB population to test the AGB /N_ RGB --T90 relation proposed for dwarf galaxies. Once RGB mass loss is adequately constrained, evolved stars can provide a reliable SFH for dwarf elliptical galaxies well beyond the reach of MSTO-based methods. We discuss the implications for more distant systems and the remaining uncertainties in the underlying stellar models.

title: Preventing Circular Supply Chain Leakage: A Strategic Pathway to Businesses' Net‐Zero Targets
summary: ABSTRACT Circular supply chains can support net‐zero transitions, yet resources may be lost, diverted, degraded, or fail to return to productive use. This study conceptualizes circular supply chain leakage (CSCL) and examines how intermedia
content: ABSTRACT Circular supply chains can support net‐zero transitions, yet resources may be lost, diverted, degraded, or fail to return to productive use. This study conceptualizes circular supply chain leakage (CSCL) and examines how intermediaries help organizations prevent it. Drawing on an extended resource‐based view (ERBV), the study analyzes 33 main‐study interviews with participants representing third‐party logistics providers, recycling experts, circular‐economy consultants, and green suppliers. The findings distinguish three forms of leakage, that is, material leakage, value leakage, and recovery/reintegration leakage. Twelve capabilities are identified and organized into four interconnected mechanisms, namely: visibility and diagnosis, resource retention and recovery, innovation and adaptive reconfiguration, and network mobilization and collective action. The study extends ERBV by conceptualizing leakage prevention as a distributed capability challenge requiring intermediaries to connect organizational resources, relationships, knowledge, and recovery networks. It offers managerial and policy implications for strengthening circular resource flows while positioning leakage prevention as a potential pathway toward net‐zero targets, rather than a demonstrated emissions‐reduction outcome.

title: Establishing expected performance for residential air-to-water heat pumps under real-world conditions
summary: Abstract As heat pumps become increasingly prevalent in residential buildings, discrepancies between expected and achieved efficiency can increase operating costs and undermine confidence in this technology. Yet, determining whether individ
content: Abstract As heat pumps become increasingly prevalent in residential buildings, discrepancies between expected and achieved efficiency can increase operating costs and undermine confidence in this technology. Yet, determining whether individual installations perform as expected remains challenging because efficiency strongly depends on operating conditions. Conventional assessments based on absolute efficiency thresholds cannot distinguish demanding operating conditions from additional performance shortfalls, while scalable methods for establishing installation-specific expectations are lacking. Here, we develop an approach to estimate expected heat pump efficiency under actual operating conditions, combining thermodynamic relationships, product-specific laboratory data, and field measurements. Validated using 176 heat pumps, the approach achieves a median absolute percentage error of 7.03%. Applying the method to 10,087 installations, we identify 5.1% with both low absolute efficiency and substantial deviations from expected performance. Systems falling below 80% of expected performance exhibit 2.3 times the incidence of subsequent recorded service contacts, whereas conventional absolute efficiency thresholds show no substantial difference between groups. These findings establish a scalable basis for assessing whether individual heat pumps perform as expected, enabling targeted performance monitoring and supporting greater transparency and efficiency in residential heating.

title: Key Points and Operational Mechanisms of the IMO Net-Zero Framework and Emission Reduction Cost Analysis for Different Fuels on an 86K Bulk Carrier
source: SAE technical papers on CD-ROM/SAE technical paper series
summary: In April 2025, the International Maritime Organization (IMO) held the 83rd session of the Marine Environment Protection Committee (MEPC) in London, the United Kingdom. During this crucial meeting, extensive discussions and in-depth negotiat
content: In April 2025, the International Maritime Organization (IMO) held the 83rd session of the Marine Environment Protection Committee (MEPC) in London, the United Kingdom. During this crucial meeting, extensive discussions and in-depth negotiations were carried out regarding the mid-term greenhouse gas (GHG) reduction measures under the newly proposed Net-Zero Framework (NZF). The NZF establishes a medium-term regulatory framework featuring a dual compliance structure consisting of basic and direct compliance. Its core components include the Greenhouse Gas Fuel Standard (GFS), the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Pricing (GEP), and Flexible Compliance (FC). Among these, the GFS is positioned as the core regulatory instrument, given that it directly governs the carbon intensity of marine fuels, thereby providing the foundational driver for the industry's transition towards zero or near-zero fuels and technologies (ZNZs). The implementation of this framework will systematically restructure the entire industrial chain of international shipping, including marine power system research and development, new-type ship design and construction, green fuel production, storage, supply, bunkering and certification, seafarers' professional training, as well as daily shipping operation and management. It will inevitably bring about profound and far-reaching impacts on the technological route, investment layout, operational mode, and competitive landscape of the global maritime industry. Against this background, this paper focuses on the NZF, systematically clarifying its formulation background, core institutional components, and practical operational mechanisms. Taking an 86K bulk carrier as the research object, this study carries out a detailed case analysis to reveal the actual challenges and response pathways for shipowners and operating enterprises under the new regulatory system. On this basis, this paper further proposes targeted coping strategies and practical reference suggestions for the shipping industry to adapt to and comply with the upcoming NZF requirements, so as to provide decision support for the sustainable and low-carbon development of the maritime sector.

title: Beyond Energy Nationalism: Contractual Lock-In, Gas Export Diversion, LNG Trading Hubs, and Asymmetric Energy Security in Indonesia Singapore Natural Gas Relations
source: Journal on Political Sciences & International Relations
summary: This qualitative literature review examines the economic, contractual, infrastructural, and environmental consequences of diverting Indonesian natural gas exports from Singapore toward domestic users. It distinguishes Indonesian pipeline ga
content: This qualitative literature review examines the economic, contractual, infrastructural, and environmental consequences of diverting Indonesian natural gas exports from Singapore toward domestic users. It distinguishes Indonesian pipeline gas from shipborne liquefied natural gas (LNG), Singapore-based LNG trading and transshipment, and final Singaporean gas consumption. Using recent peer-reviewed literature and contemporaneous official information, the study critically assesses claims that a small temporary supply reduction implies negligible bilateral dependence or that export interruption necessarily triggers financial default and gas flaring. The synthesis identifies asymmetric but conditional vulnerabilities: Singapore may replace a limited pipeline shortfall through diversified procurement, while Indonesian producers can face revenue and financing risks if domestic offtake or contractual settlement is inadequate. Conversely, a connected and creditworthy domestic customer may create significant economic value through greater electricity reliability and industrial activity. A conceptual framework links physical flows, gas sales agreements, project-finance covenants, infrastructure absorption, political credibility, and methane outcomes. The study concludes that sound resource nationalism requires reconciled gas-flow accounting, scenario-based netback and welfare analysis, contract-specific impact assessments, infrastructure readiness, and credible environmental safeguards. It offers a practical decision framework for balancing Indonesian domestic energy needs, producer bankability, and bilateral commercial relationships without treating an isolated percentage as decisive evidence

title: Research on Charging Strategies for Electric Logistics Vehicles Considering Time-of-Use Electricity Prices
source: SAE technical papers on CD-ROM/SAE technical paper series
summary: Against the backdrop of the “dual-carbon” goals and the rapid development of urban cold chain logistics, electric logistics vehicles have been widely deployed due to their advantages of low emissions and low operating costs. However, their
content: Against the backdrop of the “dual-carbon” goals and the rapid development of urban cold chain logistics, electric logistics vehicles have been widely deployed due to their advantages of low emissions and low operating costs. However, their operational performance is still constrained by limited driving range, uncertain charging behavior, and fluctuations in time-of-use electricity prices. Charging strategy selection plays a critical role in determining distribution cost and system efficiency. To address the charging decision-making problem of electric logistics vehicles under time-of-use electricity pricing, this paper develops an optimization model with the objective of minimizing total charging cost. The model incorporates practical operational constraints, including vehicle load capacity, state of charge safety thresholds, and customer time windows. A genetic algorithm is employed to solve the model, and case studies based on the Solomon dataset are conducted to compare distribution routes and charging costs under partial charging and full charging strategies. The results show that the partial charging strategy enables flexible “on-demand charging”, effectively reducing charging volume and charging time, thereby lowering total charging cost. In contrast, the full charging strategy improves driving range reliability and ensures delivery continuity. The findings provide decision support for logistics enterprises to select appropriate charging strategies under time-of-use electricity pricing.

title: Shear Stability of Hybrid Fiber-Reinforced Composite Wing and Airworthiness Static Test Verification Method
source: SAE technical papers on CD-ROM/SAE technical paper series
summary: In this paper, the airworthiness compliance of hybrid fiber-reinforced composite wings is analyzed, focusing on the analysis of shear stability, and the theoretical analysis, numerical simulation, and experimental research are carried out s
content: In this paper, the airworthiness compliance of hybrid fiber-reinforced composite wings is analyzed, focusing on the analysis of shear stability, and the theoretical analysis, numerical simulation, and experimental research are carried out systematically. Carbon fiber and glass fiber are used to form a hybrid reinforced epoxy resin system. In the process of testing the properties of the material, the nonlinear constitutive relationship of the material is grasped. In this study, the first-order shear deformation theory and classical laminated theory are used to construct a reasonable model to analyze the shear stability of the wing structure. With the help of refined three-dimensional finite element simulation, the analysis of the parameters is carried out, and the impact of the ply sequence, skin thickness, and the proportion of ±45° plies on the critical load is analyzed. In this study, the static test scheme is designed according to the requirements of China Civil Aviation Regulations Part 25 (CCAR-25) airworthiness, and the ultimate shear load is simulated by four-point bending. During monitoring of the structural response, a variety of technologies are used, including acoustic emission, displacement, and strain. The test results show that when the structure reaches 105% of the design load, it will be unstable. There is a certain deviation between the simulated buckling load and the experimental one, but it is within the acceptable range, which shows that the numerical simulation is reliable. In this study, the whole technical path is constructed, including material characterization, stability analysis, and experimental verification, which can provide a reference for the airworthiness compliance of hybrid fiber composite wings.

title: Forest cooling is not natural-vegetation cooling: pair-specific and environmentally conditioned land-cover thermal contrasts across India
summary: Abstract Land cover is often treated as a fixed warming or cooling agent, with natural vegetation assumed to be cooler than human-modified surfaces. Here, we challenge this assumption by quantifying land-surface temperature contrasts (ΔLST)
content: Abstract Land cover is often treated as a fixed warming or cooling agent, with natural vegetation assumed to be cooler than human-modified surfaces. Here, we challenge this assumption by quantifying land-surface temperature contrasts (ΔLST) among seven major land-cover classes across India using two decades (2003–2022) of satellite observations and a spatially matched moving-window framework complemented by environmental-gradient, statistical and machine-learning analyses. Of 21 possible pairwise contrasts, 17 were sufficiently co-located for analysis. During daytime, forests were the coolest surface, cooler than cropland in 99.6% of matched pairs (mean ΔLST = -2.32°C) and urban land in 97.6% (-2.57°C). However, this cooling was forest-specific: savanna, shrubland and grassland were collectively cooler than cropland in only 33.0% of comparisons and averaged 0.73°C warmer. At night, 11 of 17 contrasts reversed sign, forests became warmer than cropland (+ 0.40°C), and urban land was warmer than all vegetated surfaces. Thermal contrasts varied across biogeographic zones and responded nonlinearly to environmental gradients, with breakpoints at background temperatures of 29–44°C and evapotranspiration-to-potential-evapotranspiration ratios of 0.09–0.40. Forest cooling relative to cropland peaked at intermediate evaporative conditions, whereas water-stressed non-forest vegetation was substantially warmer than neighbouring cropland or urban land. Biophysical attribution identified albedo as the dominant daytime predictor for 12 of 16 contrasts, whereas vegetation structure, productivity and latent heat exchange governed others. These findings establish that land-cover thermal effects are pair-specific, temporally variable and environmentally conditioned, challenging generalized assumptions about natural-vegetation cooling and informing land-surface modelling and nature-based cooling strategies.

title: Integrated Reactive CO2 and NH3 Capture and Conversion to Ammonium Carbamate: Material Design toward Low-Concentration Sources
summary: Abstract Carbon dioxide (CO2) and ammonia (NH3) emissions are responsible for global warming and eutrophication, among other causes. Ionic liquids (ILs) stand out as versatile designer absorbent/catalyst materials that contribute to the cap
content: Abstract Carbon dioxide (CO2) and ammonia (NH3) emissions are responsible for global warming and eutrophication, among other causes. Ionic liquids (ILs) stand out as versatile designer absorbent/catalyst materials that contribute to the capture and conversion of both gases. This work focuses on the efficient and innovative use of ILs in NH3 and CO2 integrated capture and conversion (ICC) to produce ammonium carbamate (AMC) using an efficient self-regenerating catalytic system operating at room temperature, with spontaneous product separation by precipitation. Experimental ICC tests were carried out using 10 ILs, with remarkable structural differences, and different NH3 and CO2 partial pressure and experimental times. Two different optimization routes were explored by tuning the IL material features through molecular design: (i) an NH3-driven mechanism using IL as the physical absorbent and (ii) a CO2-driven mechanism using IL as the reactive capture agent, selected to promote high CO2 chemical absorption and activation and easy IL regeneration and AMC removal. The use of an IL as a reactive capture agent strongly improves the process performance with fast ICC rates even at low NH3 and CO2 partial pressures, highlighting the CO2-driven approach as a versatile ICC technology capable of efficiently treating diluted NH3 and CO2 streams to produce value-added AMC products.

title: A Nonreacting Hydroxy Group Enhances Criegee Intermediate Reactivity through Secondary Hydrogen Bonding
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
summary: Abstract The reaction of stabilized Criegee intermediate CH2OO with acetone cyanohydrin, (CH3)2C(OH)CN, provides competing O–H insertion and 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition pathways at the hydroxy and nitrile groups, respectively. We used cavity
content: Abstract The reaction of stabilized Criegee intermediate CH2OO with acetone cyanohydrin, (CH3)2C(OH)CN, provides competing O–H insertion and 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition pathways at the hydroxy and nitrile groups, respectively. We used cavity ring-down spectroscopy to measure CH2OO decay rates in the presence of excess (CH3)2C(OH)CN at different concentrations, yielding a bimolecular rate coefficient of (4.1 ± 0.3) × 10–12 cm3 s–1 at 10 Torr and 294 K, nearly 2 orders of magnitude larger than those of typical CH2OO + R–CN reactions and 1 order of magnitude larger than those of CH2OO + R–OH reactions. Potential energy surface calculations at the B3LYP-D3(BJ)/aug-cc-pVTZ level identify that the lowest-energy pathway corresponds to 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition at the nitrile site, during which the adjacent hydroxy group forms an O–H···(OOCH2) hydrogen bond that decreases the transition state (TS) enthalpy by 18 kJ mol–1 (298 K). This hydrogen-bond-assisted TS stabilization enabled by favorable functional-group proximity is interpreted to drive the enhanced Criegee intermediate reactivity.

title: Development drivers, CO2 emissions and ecological footprint in developing economies, 2000 to 2025: research database and R code
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: A documented panel of the 163 economies that the World Bank classified as low or middle income in at least one fiscal year from FY2001 to FY2025, with the R script that runs the whole analysis. The panel covers 2000 to 2025: 4,238 country-y
content: A documented panel of the 163 economies that the World Bank classified as low or middle income in at least one fiscal year from FY2001 to FY2025, with the R script that runs the whole analysis. The panel covers 2000 to 2025: 4,238 country-years and 119 columns. It is the research database of the doctoral dissertation "AI-Enhanced Modeling of Development–Environment Interactions in Developing Economies: Integrating Econometric and Explainable Machine Learning Approaches" (Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences, MATE, 2026) and of the journal manuscripts drawn from it. The panel holds two outcomes, CO2 emissions per capita and the ecological footprint of production per capita, and eight explanatory variables: population growth, GDP per capita growth, trade openness, urbanization, the renewable share of final energy, industry value added, energy intensity and mean years of schooling. It also holds alternative and extra series, sample flags and two break dummies. Every value of the ten core variables has a status (published, second source, estimate, nowcast or national source). 83 values come from national statistical sources under written rules, each with its publishing body, table and link. 46 gaps in the explanatory variables are filled by multiple imputation in 50 datasets. The R script reads the data file and produces every result table, from the checks of the database to the last robustness check: panel models, Random Forest, XGBoost, SHAP values and the checks on the 50 imputed datasets. A full run takes about 12 hours on a laptop. One series is left out of the data file. The 3,900 values of CO2 per capita that are computed from the IEA-EDGAR CO2 file of EDGAR 2026 are empty, because that file is licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 and its licence does not allow a database built from it to be shared. The file itself is included unchanged under its own licence, and the script computes the values again from it. The 250 values from the Global Carbon Budget are included, and so is the Global Carbon Budget series (column co2_pc_gcb). The column biomass_cooking (WHO Global Health Observatory) is empty because of the WHO terms of use. No result uses it. README.md says how to run the script. LICENSES.md gives the licence of each part and the terms and the citation of every source. Please also cite the sources of the series you use.

title: The Hidden Carbon Cost of Extreme Low Temperatures: Fiscal Support for Agriculture and Agricultural Carbon Emissions in China
summary: Extreme low-temperature events are among the meteorological hazards that affect agricultural production in China, yet their association with agricultural carbon emissions remains insufficiently understood. Using a balanced panel of 31 Chine
content: Extreme low-temperature events are among the meteorological hazards that affect agricultural production in China, yet their association with agricultural carbon emissions remains insufficiently understood. Using a balanced panel of 31 Chinese provinces from 2010 to 2023, this study employs a two-way fixed-effects model to examine the relationship between extreme low-temperature exposure, measured by the annual number of extreme low-temperature days (LTD), and crop-production-related carbon emissions. The results show that one additional LTD is associated with an increase of 0.298 ten thousand tons of carbon emissions. A one-standard-deviation increase in LTD (17.8 days) corresponds to approximately 5.3 ten thousand tons, equivalent to about 2% of the sample mean. The positive association is statistically significant in major grain-consuming regions, but not in major grain-producing or production–marketing balance regions. Pairwise Wald tests provide limited evidence of differences across groups, with only the difference between marketing and production–marketing balance regions being marginally significant at the 10% level. The interaction between LTD and fiscal support for agriculture is negative, whereas that between LTD and agricultural labor is positive, suggesting that these resources may be associated with different patterns of emission responses to extreme cold. An accounting-based decomposition indicates that the aggregate association is concentrated in fertilizer, pesticide, and diesel-related emissions, while the estimated responses of plastic film, sown area, and irrigated area are statistically insignificant. These component estimates are accounting-based evidence rather than causal mediation effects. Although instrumental-variable estimates provide additional evidence, potential endogeneity of fiscal support, the use of annual temperature indicators that do not distinguish crop growth stages, and the limitations of province-level aggregate data constrain causal interpretation. The findings highlight the potential carbon implications of agricultural adjustment to extreme cold and the importance of coordinating climate adaptation and agricultural emission-reduction policies.

title: Steering Anaerobic Digestion toward Coproduction of Biomethane and Short-Chain Carboxylic Acids
summary: Abstract Anaerobic digestion is a key technology for converting organic waste into energy sources and biofertilizers, yet the potential to simultaneously produce industrial value-added products is largely untapped. Thus, this study aims to
content: Abstract Anaerobic digestion is a key technology for converting organic waste into energy sources and biofertilizers, yet the potential to simultaneously produce industrial value-added products is largely untapped. Thus, this study aims to explore the anaerobic bioprocessing concept of producing short-chain carboxylic acids from agricultural residues and manure combined with biomethane production. Four semicontinuous anaerobic reactors with a working volume of 5 L were operated under mesophilic conditions (37 °C) and continuously mixed at 60 rpm. Two reactors (MS1 and MS2) were fed with cow manure and straw, while the other two reactors (MSF1 and MSF2) were fed with cow manure, straw, and food waste slurry. The results showed that at a high organic loading rate (7 gvs/L·d), microorganisms produced short-chain carboxylic acids, reaching up to 25 ± 5 mM (2.0 ± 0.2 g/L) in each reactor. Simultaneously, biomethane production persisted at a rate of 5318 ± 281 mL/d (152 ± 8 mL/gvs·d) for MS1 and MS2, and 6801 ± 29 mL/d (194 ± 1 mL/gvs·d) for MSF1 and MSF2. These findings demonstrate that optimizing anaerobic digestion for both energy carriers and industrial chemical precursors enhances the economic value of organic waste, thereby advancing green technologies for renewable chemical production and offering valuable insights for the development of efficient biorefinery processes.

title: Adaptive deep reinforcement learning-based model reference control for battery electric vehicles under dynamic urban driving conditions
summary: However, to meet the increasing demand for BEVs, there should be effective controllers that would provide proper functionality for managing different traffic situations and ensuring vehicle stability and efficiency. On the other hand, in so
content: However, to meet the increasing demand for BEVs, there should be effective controllers that would provide proper functionality for managing different traffic situations and ensuring vehicle stability and efficiency. On the other hand, in some situations, current control solutions may not be sufficient when dealing with the different traffic conditions on urban streets. The proposed study provides an innovative ADRL-MRC solution that would be helpful in addressing control-related problems of BEVs in a complicated urban environment. The algorithm with its adaptive approach through Deep Reinforcement Learning and MRC stability would help achieve proper speed management under the conditions of dynamism. The all-terrain design of an electric vehicle, which includes its battery system, a buck converter, an inverter, BLDC motor, drivetrain, and other elements, was designed by using the MATLAB/Simulink 2023a software.

title: Nitrogen Fertilizer Reduction with Organic Residue Incorporation Mitigates Soil Organic Carbon Mineralisation by Regulating Microbial Community and CAZyme Genes
summary: The co-application of organic matter and nitrogen (N) fertiliser has been recommended as an environmentally friendly practice. However, excessive N fertiliser use contributes to carbon (C) loss and several environmental problems. Our study
content: The co-application of organic matter and nitrogen (N) fertiliser has been recommended as an environmentally friendly practice. However, excessive N fertiliser use contributes to carbon (C) loss and several environmental problems. Our study aims to analyse the effects of reducing mineral N application under supplemental organic residue on organic C mineralisation and its microbial mechanisms. Therefore, a 120-day incubation experiment was conducted to assess the effects of incorporating 13C-labelled pruning branch residue combined with different N levels (225, BRN1; 180, BRN2; 160, BRN3; and 140 mg N·kg−1, BRN4) on CO2 emission, soil microbial community and functional genes in apple orchard soil. All treatments increased CO2 efflux and induced a positive priming effect (PE), expressed as promoted native soil organic C mineralisation. BRN1 produced the highest positive PE, followed by BRN2 and BRN4, and the lowest PE was observed under BRN3. We highlight the importance of plant- and bacteria-derived biomass (indicated by peptidoglycan) decomposition rather than the composition and structure of microbial communities in regulating organic C decomposition in response to pruning residue and N addition. In addition, reduced N treatments decreased abundance of C-degrading genes for plant-derived (hemicellulose, lignin) and bacteria-derived biomass (peptidoglycan) as compared with BRN1. Four near-complete bacterial genome bins were strongly correlated with PE; three of these bins were assigned to Actinomycetota and one to Acidobacteriota. Moreover, structural equation modelling indicated CAZyme-encoding genes had a stronger association with PE than microbial community. Collectively, coupling branch residue with N reduction has great potential for mitigating soil C loss.
