The optimal amount of N reduction should be further evaluated based on the fruit yield in the field.

title: Cost-Effective Microwave-Assisted Synthesis of Nanomaterials for Direct Alcohol Fuel Cell Applications
source: International Journal of Electrical and Electronics Engineering
summary: A low-cost, computer-controlled modification of a domestic microwave oven is developed to achieve precise, programmable control of microwave irradiation during the polyol synthesis of fuel cell catalysts, a level of control previously restr
content: A low-cost, computer-controlled modification of a domestic microwave oven is developed to achieve precise, programmable control of microwave irradiation during the polyol synthesis of fuel cell catalysts, a level of control previously restricted to costly, laboratory-grade microwave reactors. Platinum-on-Carbon (Pt/C) catalysts are synthesized by the polyol method using two heating sources, a conventional stirring hotplate and the modified microwave oven operated under intermittent heating, and are compared with a commercial Pt/C (20 wt.%) catalyst. The microwave-assisted route reduces the heating stage of the synthesis from 3 h to 15 min and yields a catalyst with crystallite size, electrochemically active surface area, and ethanol oxidation activity comparable to those of the conventionally synthesized and commercial references. These results show that a domestic microwave oven adapted with programmable control is a viable and accessible tool for the laboratory-scale synthesis of fuel cell electrocatalysts.

title: Nutrient removal by Eichhornia crassipes and its impact on the water column and its biomass production
summary: Abstract High nutrient concentrations in water bodies cause eutrophication. This promotes the presence, development, and uncontrolled growth of invasive species, such as Eichhornia crassipes . Its use for bioremediation in confined environm
content: Abstract High nutrient concentrations in water bodies cause eutrophication. This promotes the presence, development, and uncontrolled growth of invasive species, such as Eichhornia crassipes . Its use for bioremediation in confined environments is being considered as a biomass utilization strategy. This is due to its potential for removing nutrients from the water column. To test this, a mesocosm bioassay was conducted with two treatments: a control and one enriched with commercial fertilizer. Physicochemical parameters (dissolved oxygen, pH, and electrical conductivity) and the dynamics of nutrient concentrations (P and N) were evaluated in each treatment. Ten E. crassipes organisms were placed in each mesocosm. The morphology of three randomly selected individuals was measured, recording length and maximum diameter of the petiole, length and width of the leaf blade, and root length. The results show the plant's removal potential as nutrient concentrations decreased: NT by 11.42% and PT by 33.14% throughout the mesocosm. An improvement in physicochemical conditions was also observed, with dissolved oxygen increasing from 0.8022 mgL-1 to 2.4388 mgL-1 and pH from 6.5 to 7.5. This demonstrates the plant's removal efficiency, its buffering capacity of physicochemical parameters in the water column, and its ability to keep nutrients suspended in the water column.

title: Slow Mono-energetic Positron Beams for Defect Characterization in Materials Science
summary: Slow mono-energetic positron beams allow the non-destructive and depth-resolved investigation of open-volume defects in materials. By varying the implantation energy, near-surface regions, thin films, interfaces and damaged layers can be pr
content: Slow mono-energetic positron beams allow the non-destructive and depth-resolved investigation of open-volume defects in materials. By varying the implantation energy, near-surface regions, thin films, interfaces and damaged layers can be probed from the surface to depths of several micrometres. Positron annihilation lifetime spectroscopy (PALS) provides information on the size and type of defects, while Doppler-broadening spectroscopy (DBS) and coincidence Doppler-broadening spectroscopy (CDBS) are sensitive to defect concentrations and the chemical environment of the annihilation site. In combination with in situ conditions, such as temperature variation, illumination, or applied electric fields, slow-positron beams can also be used to study defect charge states, metastable defect configurations, and defect dynamics. This contribution briefly introduces the method and its experimental possibilities, using selected examples for vacancy-related defects and charge-state transitions, identification of radiation-induced damage, and the determination of free-volume sizes in polymeric materials.

title: Managing trade-offs among energy productivity, yield, and nutrient-use efficiency in rice–greengram rotations under nitrogen management and zinc biofortification in Alfisols
summary: Rice-based cropping systems in South Asia face declining resource-use efficiency, increasing dependence on external energy inputs, and rising environmental costs from fertilizer-intensive production. The combined effects of integrated nutri
content: Rice-based cropping systems in South Asia face declining resource-use efficiency, increasing dependence on external energy inputs, and rising environmental costs from fertilizer-intensive production. The combined effects of integrated nutrient management and zinc biofortification on energetics, nutrient-use efficiency, and carbon efficiency in rice–pulse rotations remain inadequately quantified. Field experiments (2021–2023) evaluated productivity, system energetics, nutrient-use efficiency, and carbon intensity of a rice–greengram system under four nitrogen and four zinc management practices in a split-plot design on tropical Alfisols of eastern India. Energy and carbon indices were estimated using standard energy equivalents and input-related emission coefficients. Substituting 25% of recommended nitrogen with farmyard manure recorded the highest two-year mean system grain yield (6161 kg ha−1), net energy return (182.5 × 10³ MJ ha−1), energy ratio (14.98), and energy productivity (0.472 kg MJ−1), with the lowest carbon intensity (61.8 kg CO2e t−1 grain equivalent). Higher fertilizer intensification increased input energy and carbon intensity disproportionately to yield gains, indicating diminishing energetic returns. Zinc biofortification, particularly combined soil and foliar application, further improved sustainability ranking. Moderate nutrient intensification with organic substitution and targeted zinc biofortification can enhance productivity while reducing energy and carbon costs in rice–pulse systems.

title: Nanosensors for Societal Benefits
summary: Curtailing pollution of air, water, and soil to the minimum achievable level is essential to ensuring a good quality of life for all living creatures inhabiting our planet: humans, animals, and plants. Because environmental problems origina
content: Curtailing pollution of air, water, and soil to the minimum achievable level is essential to ensuring a good quality of life for all living creatures inhabiting our planet: humans, animals, and plants. Because environmental problems originate from human tasks, the environment becomes a sociological topic. To enforce regulatory standards for pollution monitoring caused by life-threatening effluents and emissions from anthropogenic activities, there is a dire need for ultrasensitive nanosensors. Nanosensors for air pollutants include devices for detecting particulate matter and harmful gases such as carbon monoxide, sulfur dioxide, nitrogen dioxide, ozone, and volatile organic compounds. Among nanosensors for water pollution, the devices described are those for pathogens, namely E. Coli , Vibrio Cholerae and Cholera toxin, Pseudomonas Aeruginosa and Legionella Pneumophila ; metals such as mercury (II), lead (II), As(III), Cr(VI), Cd 2+ and Cu 2+ ions; and pesticides such as DDT, 2, 4-D, carbofuran, methomyl, dimethoate, atrazine, paroxon-ethyl, acetamiprid, HB, MLT, and DTCs.

title: RenovaBio, environmental efficiency scores, and the cost of debt: evidence from Brazilian biofuel firms
summary: Purpose This study aims to investigate whether the environmental efficiency scores assigned to Brazilian biofuel firms under the RenovaBio program affect their cost of debt. Specifically, it examines whether a regulated, standardized and ex
content: Purpose This study aims to investigate whether the environmental efficiency scores assigned to Brazilian biofuel firms under the RenovaBio program affect their cost of debt. Specifically, it examines whether a regulated, standardized and externally verified environmental-performance metric can influence creditors’ risk assessments and borrowing conditions in an emerging economy, with particular emphasis on the highly leveraged Brazilian sugar-energy sector. Design/methodology/approach This study uses panel data from Brazilian biofuel-producing firms participating in RenovaBio, covering the 2020/2021, 2021/2022 and 2022/2023 crop years. Financial data were obtained from Balanços Patrimoniais and Valor Pró, while environmental efficiency scores and biofuel information came from the ANP. The relationship between RenovaBio efficiency scores and the cost of debt was estimated using panel regressions, with a random-effects specification as the main model, robust standard errors clustered at the firm level and additional robustness checks using lagged RenovaBio scores. Findings The results show that RenovaBio environmental efficiency scores are negatively associated with the cost of debt, but the relationship is not statistically significant. This suggests that creditors in the Brazilian sugar-energy sector do not yet systematically incorporate these environmental performance signals into lending conditions. Firm size and asset tangibility are associated with lower borrowing costs, while the Selic interest rate increases them. Robustness tests using lagged RenovaBio scores confirm the absence of a statistically significant effect, indicating that traditional financial characteristics remain more influential in creditors’ risk assessments. Social implications Broader access to affordable green credit could support investment, preserve jobs and generate positive spillovers in biofuel-producing regions. Audited environmental efficiency scores may also contribute to reducing local environmental harms and improving public health. However, policymakers should prevent the benefits of sustainability-linked financing from being disproportionately captured by large firms. Combining environmental certification with targeted support and capacity-building initiatives for smaller producers may help promote a more inclusive and just transition toward a low-carbon economy. Originality/value This study provides novel evidence on the financial implications of a regulated, policy-certified environmental-efficiency metric, rather than relying on voluntary ESG disclosures or composite sustainability indicators. By examining RenovaBio’s standardized, externally verified, LCA-based efficiency score and its relationship with borrowing costs, the study extends the literature on environmental performance and corporate finance. It also contributes evidence from the Brazilian sugar-energy sector, offering insights into how climate-related regulatory instruments may interact with c

title: Responses of microbial colonies, rice growth, and yield performance to salt stress under different substrate conditions
summary: Salt stress is one of the major abiotic stresses limiting rice production, and substrate conditions play a key role in salt stress response. The substrates in this study included S1 (river sand); S2 (river sand: laterite: peat moss = 8:1:1)
content: Salt stress is one of the major abiotic stresses limiting rice production, and substrate conditions play a key role in salt stress response. The substrates in this study included S1 (river sand); S2 (river sand: laterite: peat moss = 8:1:1); S3 (river sand: laterite: peat moss = 6:2:2); S4 (river sand: laterite: peat moss = 4:3:3); S5 (laterite: peat moss = 1:1); S6 (laterite). Each bucket contained the same volume of substrate and the same mass of NaCl with fresh water as a control. In this study, yield was significantly positively correlated with thousand seed weight, setting rate, nutrient content (total phosphorus, total nitrogen, total potassium, and organic matter), significantly negatively correlated with pH, and not significantly correlated with Na + and Cl − content. Under salt stress, the richness and diversity of the microbial communities in S1 and S4 were significantly reduced compared with their respective non-salt controls, while no significant changes occurred in S2 and S5. Salt stress increased the relative abundance of “stress tolerant” phenotypes in the S1 substrate, and Ellin6067 and MND1 had a high contribution to this phenotypes in TY1. This study provides a theoretical basis for optimizing the microecology of saline soil and salt tolerant cultivation of rice.

title: Hydrogen and Battery Energy Storage for Resilient High-Renewable Microgrids: A Multi-Objective Assessment of Cost, Emissions and Employment Under Uncertainty
summary: Stand-alone microgrids with high renewable shares need storage for daily and multi-day balancing. This study compares hydrogen, battery and hybrid storage in five configurations, with and without diesel backup, for a South African residenti
content: Stand-alone microgrids with high renewable shares need storage for daily and multi-day balancing. This study compares hydrogen, battery and hybrid storage in five configurations, with and without diesel backup, for a South African residential load. A bus-resolved mixed-integer linear programming model with open hourly data (2012–2021) trades off cost, diesel emissions and employment by ε-constraint analysis; a robust counterpart covers cost, discount-rate and employment-factor uncertainty and 10 weather years. Per kWh delivered, electricity from the compromise designs cost 0.71–1.29 $/kWh; normalising by generation, which includes 30–45% curtailment, understates it 4–7-fold. The hydrogen–battery hybrid was the least-cost fully renewable option (1.30 versus 1.96 and 2.06 M$ with hydrogen or batteries alone), with the battery cycling daily and the tank providing 71 h of autonomy. Robust designs served the load in all 10 years. The findings held under unit-commitment, reserve and wear constraints and across design years, loads, sites and Monte Carlo samples. Carbon prices at EU ETS levels did not displace battery–diesel supply, whereas a 75% cut in hydrogen equipment costs made the diesel-free hybrid equally cheap. Hydrogen adds the most value as a reserve for prolonged deficits, combined with batteries.

title: Analysis of European Energy Transition Policies and Their Interactions: Mixed Risks for Sustainability and Competitiveness
summary: European Union energy transition policy has developed through successive layers of climate, energy security, industrial and electricity market measures. This structured critical review examines identifiable cross-policy mechanisms within th
content: European Union energy transition policy has developed through successive layers of climate, energy security, industrial and electricity market measures. This structured critical review examines identifiable cross-policy mechanisms within three interaction families: energy security, decarbonisation and strategic/industrial autonomy; carbon pricing and industrial competitiveness; and electrification, system capacity and implementation. An evidence-contingent Structured Cross-Policy Interaction Analysis (SCPIA) organises 18 policy pairs and 28 outcome-specific records, distinguishing policy design, implementation evidence, observed effects, modelled effects and prospective risks. Classification is outcome-specific and permits abstention when evidence is insufficient. Of the 28 admitted outcomes, 21 receive a class (11 reinforcing, eight trade-offs and two direct conflicts) and seven remain justified abstentions; 22 rest mainly on legal design rather than observed effects. The same policy pair can reinforce one outcome while implying a prospective trade-off for another, as in the coordination of the EU carbon border adjustment with the phase-out of free emission allowances. Two human assessors examined a purposively selected subset of 15 outcome records and agreed on the initial reported interaction and class assignments in all 15; subsequent source-threshold assessment is recorded separately. The review contributes a traceable, evidence-sensitive procedure for comparing cross-policy interactions and integrates substantive findings across three EU energy transition policy families.

title: Disentangling spatial patterns and driving factor interactions of urban soil heavy metals using machine learning with multi-source heterogeneous data: A case study in Nanjing, China
summary: Abstract To elucidate the spatial differentiation characteristics and driving mechanisms of heavy metals in soils across the Nanjing urban area, this study integrated four machine-learning (ML) algorithms combined with ordinary kriging (OK)
content: Abstract To elucidate the spatial differentiation characteristics and driving mechanisms of heavy metals in soils across the Nanjing urban area, this study integrated four machine-learning (ML) algorithms combined with ordinary kriging (OK), local indicators of spatial association (LISA), SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and structural equation modeling (SEM). Predictive modeling, spatial mapping, and mechanistic interpretations were conducted using heavy metal concentration data from 229 urban soil samples and multi-source environmental covariates. The results revealed that the coefficients of determination (R²) for the optimal ML models applied to the test set ranged from 0.7221 to 0.9491 across the four heavy metals. Moran’s I values for Cd, Pb, and Cu were 0.275, 0.218, and 0.212, respectively, indicating varying degrees of positive spatial autocorrelation. In contrast, the Moran’s I value for Zn was only 0.048, suggesting a relatively weak overall spatial autocorrelation with pronounced local patchiness. Spatial predictions derived from two ML–OK coupling strategies revealed a complex spatial pattern characterized by multi-element accumulation in the historic urban core area, localized hotspots in construction-disturbed areas in the southwest, anomalous enrichment in northern areas affected by historical mining or industrial activities, and a transition toward lower concentrations in peripheral areas. SHAP analysis indicated that the spatial distributions of Pb and Zn were primarily associated with multiple heavy metal combined contamination, whereas Cu was influenced by anthropogenic inputs and adsorption-mediated immobilization by soil organic matter and minerals. Cd was more sensitive to competitive interactions among multiple heavy metals, hydrological transport, and construction disturbance. The explained spatial variance based on SEM of the four heavy metals ranged from 76.8% to 96.3%, further validating the differences among the various elemental driving pathways.

title: Future Temporalities and Advocacy Coalition Framework: Latin American's Hybrid Approach
summary: ABSTRACT The Advocacy Coalition Framework assigns a structural role to time in explaining policy change, arguing that major transformations unfold over a decade or more. This article questions that premise in contexts of cultural heterogene
content: ABSTRACT The Advocacy Coalition Framework assigns a structural role to time in explaining policy change, arguing that major transformations unfold over a decade or more. This article questions that premise in contexts of cultural heterogeneity and ontological plurality, where actors may hold divergent conceptions of the future. Drawing on critical and decolonial perspectives, it reorganizes the Future Temporalities Coalitions Framework from previous research. To propose a re‐specification of the Advocacy Coalition Framework's temporal architecture for Latin America, a qualitative comparative reinterpretation of three published studies on Access and Benefit‐Sharing policies in Colombia, Brazil, and Peru is conducted. Two studies apply the Advocacy Coalition Framework, and one employs a hybrid version incorporating future temporalities. The analysis shows that the Advocacy Coalition Framework explains coalition stability and policy change when actors share similar temporal assumptions. Tensions emerge when global regulatory regimes interact with local ontologies that conceptualize time differently. Reinterpreting deep core beliefs as carriers of temporal ontologies expands the framework's analytical capacity. By integrating temporal plurality as a dimension of conflict, the Future Temporalities Coalitions Framework enhances contextual sensitivity and extends the Advocacy Coalition Framework's applicability to transnational governance settings.

title: ADULTERANTES E CONTAMINANTES EM CACHAÇAS BRASILEIRAS: UMA REVISÃO DE LITERATURA SOBRE TÉCNICAS ANALÍTICAS, CONTROLE DE QUALIDADE, LEGISLAÇÃO E IMPACTOS NA PRODUÇÃO E COMERCIALIZAÇÃO
summary: Esta revisão de literatura aborda o levantamento bibliográfico referente a adulterantes, contaminantes, métodos analíticos, controle de qualidade, legislação e consequências para a produção e comercialização de cachaças no Brasil. Entre 201
content: Esta revisão de literatura aborda o levantamento bibliográfico referente a adulterantes, contaminantes, métodos analíticos, controle de qualidade, legislação e consequências para a produção e comercialização de cachaças no Brasil. Entre 2016 e 2026, artigos científicos, dissertações, teses e trabalhos de conclusão de curso) foram analisadas. Além de métodos para autenticação e identificação de adulterações, os estudos focam principalmente em contaminantes como carbamato de etila, pesticidas, HPA (hidrocarbonetos policíclicos aromáticos), cobre, chumbo, arsênio; e outros compostos, incluindo metanol, acroleína, furfural, 5-hidroximetilfurfural e acidez. A literatura apresenta ampla utilização de cromatografia gasosa e líquida, espectrometria de massas, espectrometria de absorção atômica, voltametria, fluorescência, espectroscopia NIR e MIR e ferramentas quimiométricas. Os resultados mostram diferenças relacionadas à origem das amostras, aos sistemas de destilação, às condições de produção e aos procedimentos de preparo e análise. Além disso, também se verifica o crescimento do uso de metodologias rápidas, portáteis e não-invasivas (não-destrutivas) para a triagem e autenticação. A qualidade da cachaça é influenciada pelo controle preventivo do processo, pela utilização de métodos analíticos com desempenho adequado e pela conformidade com os requisitos regulatórios.

title: Beyond The Recycled Label: Production Route, Carbon Accounting and Mechanical Evidence in the Assessment of Recovered Steel for Civil Infrastructure
summary: Civil infrastructure requires steel that performs reliably, efficiently and enables a strong foundation. However, the production process of steel also causes the emission of greenhouse gases. Therefore, this paper seeks to answer the questi
content: Civil infrastructure requires steel that performs reliably, efficiently and enables a strong foundation. However, the production process of steel also causes the emission of greenhouse gases. Therefore, this paper seeks to answer the question as to whether steel made using recovered material can aid in the reduction of greenhouse-gas emissions all the while fulfilling the basic requirements of civil infrastructure. This review examines the process of how steel is produced, the different available methods that are available for assessing its environmental effects, understanding the mechanical performance of the material and how each of these factors are taken into consideration while building different projects. Classifying steel as the primary or recycled only answers a part of the question. The overall impact varies on other different factors such as the source of electricity, furnace inputs, the manufacturing process and the method of calculation that is used. The reviewed literature does not support a single carbon value or a mechanical disadvantage for recycled steel. The finished product is therefore assessed using the evidence relevant to the source material properties and the application that it’s intended for. The proposed study intends to combine steel origin data, laboratory tests and carbon calculations. At this stage in time, this merely stands as a research proposal, and no experimental results from that study have been reported here.

title: Effective solvent-free synthetic method for obtaining benzoate-pentafluorobenzoate europium(III) compound
summary: An effective solvent-free synthetic method for obtaining a mixed-anion europium(III) coordination compound has been proposed.The approach is based on the interaction of europium acetate with molten benzoic H(bz) and pentafluorobenzoic H(F5b
content: An effective solvent-free synthetic method for obtaining a mixed-anion europium(III) coordination compound has been proposed.The approach is based on the interaction of europium acetate with molten benzoic H(bz) and pentafluorobenzoic H(F5b) acids, which allows the preparation of the coordination polymer [Eu(H(bz))(bz)(F5b)2]n.The structure, supramolecular arrangement, and photoluminescent properties of the compound significantly differ from those of the previously obtained compounds [Eu(EtOH)2(F5b)(bz)2]n and [Eu(EtOH)(F5b)2(bz)]n with coordinated ethanol molecules, which were synthesized by conventional methods.

title: Hydrogen Without Burial: Splitting Methane into Hydrogen and Solid Carbon with ARBOK-HYCARB
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Blue hydrogen is hydrogen made from natural gas with the carbon dioxide of the reaction captured and injected underground. The route keeps the chemistry of steam reforming and adds a second industry to it: capture units, pipelines and geolo
content: Blue hydrogen is hydrogen made from natural gas with the carbon dioxide of the reaction captured and injected underground. The route keeps the chemistry of steam reforming and adds a second industry to it: capture units, pipelines and geological storage that must hold for centuries. The world makes about 100 million t of hydrogen a year and emits close to 1 billion t of CO2 doing so. This paper compares the blue route with direct splitting of methane into hydrogen and solid carbon, and describes ARBOK-HYCARB, a catalytic process of this kind at TRL 4. In ARBOK-HYCARB methane is split on the ARBOK catalyst; the carbon leaves the unit as a solid product and no carbon dioxide is formed in the reaction. The paper gives the reaction balance, the mass balance of the two products, the items that leave the cost sheet of a hydrogen producer, and the scale of the question for the United States and for the world. This preprint has not been peer reviewed.

title: A Dual-Purpose Of Breakthrough Transformation: Low-Cost And Decarbonization Approach Using Eco-Friendly Microbubbles For Enhanced Oil Recovery In Kawengan Field
source: Journal of Bioresources and Environmental Sciences
summary: Indonesia is witnessing a rise in CO₂ emissions but also deals with oil recovery issues—has to import 30% needs of oil and gas to reach its daily target. Many methods are used for oil recovery like carbonated water flooding, but these will
content: Indonesia is witnessing a rise in CO₂ emissions but also deals with oil recovery issues—has to import 30% needs of oil and gas to reach its daily target. Many methods are used for oil recovery like carbonated water flooding, but these will require chemicals (surfactants and polymers) to produce foam. Carbon Capture, Storage, and Utilization (CCUS)-Microbial Enhanced Oil Recovery, a combination between CO₂ capture technology and biodegradable oil recovery method is a promising solution. Based on formation matching and laboratory testing data, we propose a new approach using a bacteria—Gordonia terrae—to produce biosurfactants with bacterial consortium activity that will be mixed with microbubbles so it becomes a good fluid displacement that can reach small cracks in the reservoir rock optimally. This innovation utilizes CO₂ emissions from gas wells in the Gundih Field to produce microbubbles, which are collected at the Gundih Central Processing Plant (CPP) and injected into the Kawengan Field, 37 km from the CPP to reduce emissions. With the method of Surface Response (RSM-CCD) Analysis, the results revealed impressive mechanical properties including a change in contact angle from 159◦ to 31◦, a reduction of Interfacial Tension from 23.96 to 1.26 mN/m and an S(C) close to zero (-0.18). This means that it ensured findings of the best microbacterial medium by comparison of bacterias used before, serves up to a 25% oil recovery. In conclusion, we present this innovation that serves the best option to still use surfactant in microbubbles but cheaper and also environmentally safe in impacting the dual objectives—utilizing carbon emission and improving oil recovery in feasible Kawengan Field without damaging the formation integrity. This significance increases as the industry strives to meet global sustainability targets to dependence on fossil feedstocks for any synthetic surfactants in the future.

title: Climate, Poverty, and Food Security Dynamics in the Gulf Cooperation Council Countries: A Panel VAR Analysis
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines the dynamic relationships among climate‐related indicators, poverty, and food security using panel cointegration and panel vector autoregression (PVAR) methods for the six Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countrie
content: ABSTRACT This study examines the dynamic relationships among climate‐related indicators, poverty, and food security using panel cointegration and panel vector autoregression (PVAR) methods for the six Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries: Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates over the period 2000–2024. The empirical results indicate a long‐run equilibrium relationship among the variables, suggesting that food security and carbon emissions are associated with long‐term poverty dynamics. At the same time, the effects of temperature and other climate‐related indicators appear to be more temporary. In the short run, poverty and food security are primarily associated with their own innovations, whereas food security and climate‐related factors become more relevant to poverty dynamics over longer horizons. These findings represent dynamic associations within the estimated panel model rather than direct causal effects. The results highlight the potential importance of integrated social protection, food security, and climate adaptation strategies for supporting sustainable poverty reduction in the GCC region.

title: The Photon's Plan (Volumes I–IV): A Philosophical and Mathematical Consistency Proposal on the Energy-Information Ground of the Universe
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This four-volume work presents a philosophical and mathematical consistency proposal examining whether structures across micro and macro scales in the universe can be coherently read as different forms of a single conserved energy-informati
content: This four-volume work presents a philosophical and mathematical consistency proposal examining whether structures across micro and macro scales in the universe can be coherently read as different forms of a single conserved energy-information ground, with light-related information encoded directly in the state of the photon. Rather than claiming empirical proof or introducing new physical laws, this study systematically tests the proposition against established physics using a strict three-tier classification: [S] Standard Physics (experimentally or mathematically established), [Y] Interpretation (readings consistent with standard physics), and [H] Hypothesis (unsupported yet non-contradictory theoretical propositions). Volume I (Philosophical Framework) outlines the conceptual boundaries, addressing the photon not merely as an external carrier ("envelope") but as the physical manifestation of information itself ("letter"), quantum memory limits, black hole information capacity, and measurement outcomes across quantum experiments (Cosmic Bell Test, spontaneous emission, single-photon photosynthesis, and polarization measurements). Volume II (Mathematical Framework) provides the corresponding physical equations—ranging from energy-momentum relations (E = hν, E = mc²) and Landauer's principle (W_min = k_B T ln 2) to Bekenstein-Hawking entropy, quantum state vectors, and Bell-CHSH inequalities—demonstrating internal consistency without attributing agency or consciousness to the photon. Expanding this foundation into a complete tetralogy, Volume III (Philosophical Synthesis) abolishes artificial micro-macro divisions by exploring zero-point vacuum fluctuations, holographic surface encoding from DNA biophotons to black hole bounce dynamics, dark energy as cosmic horizon tension, and carbon-silicon physical intelligence. Volume IV (Mathematical Consistency Audit) audits these propositions against vacuum Maxwell electrodynamics, Casimir boundary conditions, Planck-scale unitarity, Gertsenshtein photon-graviton conversion, the holographic UV/IR resolution of the 10^120 vacuum discrepancy, and substrate-independent Landauer bounds.

title: Chromium pollution and its effects on soil health, microbial diversity, and sugarcane production in the Vellore sugarcane belt: a metagenomic and geochemical assessment
source: World Journal of Microbiology and Biotechnology
summary: Abstract Disposal of tannery effluent has elevated soil chromium (Cr) across the Vellore sugarcane belt of southern India, yet its integrated consequences for soil health, bacterial communities and sugarcane productivity remain poorly chara
content: Abstract Disposal of tannery effluent has elevated soil chromium (Cr) across the Vellore sugarcane belt of southern India, yet its integrated consequences for soil health, bacterial communities and sugarcane productivity remain poorly characterised. Nine composite soil samples from a recognised tannery-affected belt were pre-stratified into High, Low and Near-threshold Cr sites. Soils and irrigation water were geochemically characterised for total and speciated heavy metals and profiled by full length (V1-V9) 16​S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing on an Oxford Nanopore GridION. Soil total Cr increased from 29.10 ± 0.14 to 180.51 ± 2.95 mg kg − 1 , the alkaline-extractable Cr (VI) fraction rising from 2.92 ± 0.09 to 52.07 ± 0.11 mg kg⁻¹ and co-occurring Cd and Ni increasing across strata. Soil pH shifted alkaline (7.74 to 8.48), organic carbon declined by up to 31.7% and exchangeable Ca and Mg by up to 40.4%. Tissue Cr followed root > shoot > leaf but peaked at Near-threshold rather than High Cr sites, indicating bioavailability-driven uptake. Cane and stalk fresh weight declined 25.8–31.3% at High Cr sites, whereas sucrose, Brix, purity and fibre remained largely unchanged. Alpha diversity followed a threshold structured rather than linear dose response, with observed richness in High Cr levels reduced to 74–76% that in Low Cr levels alongside parallel declines in Shannon diversity and Pielou’s evenness. NMDS resolved three non-overlapping community clusters. A Cr-resilient core ( Sphingomonas panacis , Nitrospira lenta ) persisted alongside elevated prediction of azoR/acpD and chrA abundance, defining a chromium-tolerance signature in tannery-impacted sugarcane soils.

title: Operando pH Measurements of OER within a Porous Oxygen-Evolving Electrode
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
summary: Abstract Three-dimensional porous electrodes, such as those in membrane electrode assemblies, are widely employed in electrochemical devices due to their high surface area and achievable current density. The heterogeneous internal structure
content: Abstract Three-dimensional porous electrodes, such as those in membrane electrode assemblies, are widely employed in electrochemical devices due to their high surface area and achievable current density. The heterogeneous internal structure of the porous electrode microenvironment engenders local concentration gradients owing to mass transport constraints. Localized microenvironments with properties distinct from those of the bulk solution are especially prevalent for electrocatalytic reactions that produce or consume protons, as local basic or acidic environments may significantly influence the energy efficiency and selectivity of proton-coupled electron transfer reactions that are necessary for small-molecule activation. Here, we develop an operando method employing polymer-bound fluorescent sensors (PFS) to directly quantify local pH and the internal proton gradient in a porous electrode for the oxygen evolution reaction catalyzed by IrOx supported on indium-tin oxide (ITO). The PFS uncovers notable pH gradients within a 3-μm-thick layer of the OER electrode in unbuffered electrolyte, even at low current density. Proton transport dynamics were found to be influenced significantly by the proton adsorption properties of the ITO support, revealing a previously unrecognized role of the oxide support in modifying the local pH gradient. The PFS method should prove useful in the study and evaluation of electrochemical devices, including fuel cells, bipolar and other ion-conducting membranes, and electrolyzers.

title: Histologic Evalution of Adult Wistar Rats Kidney Exposed to Generator Fumes, Petrol, Herbicides, Electrocution and Starvation for Infarction
summary: Introduction: The increasing human population has led to the use of agrochemicals for weeding which improve food production, likewise the use of fuel and other amenity which has exposure human to various stressors is on the increase. Aim: T
content: Introduction: The increasing human population has led to the use of agrochemicals for weeding which improve food production, likewise the use of fuel and other amenity which has exposure human to various stressors is on the increase. Aim: This study histologically assessed the effect of these various stressors such as generator fumes, petrol, paraquat herbicides, electrocution and starvation in Adult Wistar rats’ kidneys. Methodology: It was centered on 42 rats, randomly divided into six groups (1-6): control (normal room air), exposed to generator fumes, paraquat herbicides, electrocution, starvation and petrol respectively. The weight of each rat was recorded and analysed using one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) for significant difference between each stressor group against control. At interval, the rats were sacrificed, kidneys were harvested, tissue processed, photomicrographs were reported. Result: Findings demonstrate significant weight loss in starvation, and no much changes among other groups except the petrol-exposed groups. The histologic architecture of the rat's kidney placed on starvation showed acute renal injury, while kidney of generator fumes had peritubular spaces and a darker glomerulus when stained with Masson trichrome probably due to carbon monoxide. An irregular vascular wall pointing to an acute kidney and glomerular injury showing signs of infarction when observed in the electrocution group. Conclusion: There was no significant weight loss in rats exposed to petrol, paraquat, generator fumes, and electrocution, but starvation led to a marked reduction in body weight and death. Histological assessment showed signs of acute kidney injury such as tubular damage, dilated capillaries, and glomerular changes especially in the generator fume, electrocution, and starvation groups. In contrast, the kidneys of rats in the petrol, paraquat, and control groups appeared normal. Both Hematoxylin and Eosin and Masson’s Trichrome stains showed similar results, with no signs of fibrosis, supporting the accuracy and consistency of the observed changes.

title: Non-Identity and Compensation for Climate Change: The Not-So-Minor Difference Claim
summary: Abstract This paper examines the implications of the Non-Identity Problem (NIP) for real-world climate change-related duties, responding to Lukas Tank’s Minor Difference Claim. Tank argues that robust climate action (involving mitigation, a
content: Abstract This paper examines the implications of the Non-Identity Problem (NIP) for real-world climate change-related duties, responding to Lukas Tank’s Minor Difference Claim. Tank argues that robust climate action (involving mitigation, adaptation, and compensation) is already required to respond to the foreseeable negative effects on individuals whose identities are fixed, so accepting (or “biting the bullet” on) the NIP makes only a minor difference to our climate change-related duties. We challenge this view by arguing that accepting the NIP makes a not-so-minor difference for compensatory climate duties. First, it affects their extent. Second, it generates highly unequal compensatory claims both across individuals born at different times ( intragenerational difference ) and among those exposed to the same climate impacts at different times ( intertemporal difference ). We conclude that one must either accept these implications or develop a strategy to resolve or avoid the NIP.

title: High-Pressure Grinding Rolls in Mineral Comminution Circuits: A Critical Review of Ore Competency, Circuit Integration, Energy Efficiency, Operational Performance, and Techno-Economic Sustainability
source: Journal International Review of Research Studies
summary: High-pressure grinding rolls (HPGR) offer a compression-based alternative or complement to conventional mineral comminution. However, their value depends on ore response and circuit context, not nominal specific energy alone. This critical
content: High-pressure grinding rolls (HPGR) offer a compression-based alternative or complement to conventional mineral comminution. However, their value depends on ore response and circuit context, not nominal specific energy alone. This critical review examines particle-bed breakage, mineralogical and mechanical applicability, circuit integration, energy normalization, roll wear, downstream liberation, predictive modeling, and techno-economic and environmental trade-offs. The evidence is organized by laboratory, pilot, and industrial scale, with particular attention to differences in feed and product specifications, recirculation, availability, and downstream processing boundaries. The synthesis indicates that improved particle breakage and microcracking do not automatically translate into higher metallurgical recovery, and that equipment-level efficiency cannot establish whole-plant superiority without a common functional basis. The paper proposes a conditional selection framework combining representative ore testing, validated mass–energy balances, downstream response, reliability, and uncertainty analysis. Gaps remain in public industrial datasets, wear-adjusted lifecycle comparisons, and transferability of numerical models across ore types. The review identifies the need for evidence-matched comparisons and explicit validation of source-specific quantitative claims; the methodology reports bibliographic verification status and limitations.

title: Endogenous deiodinase-mediated conversion of T4 to T3 stimulates calcification in corals
summary: In vertebrates, thyroid hormones (TH) are synthesized predominantly as the prohormone thyroxine (T4), which is converted into biologically active triiodothyronine (T3) by iodothyronine deiodinases (DIOs). Although iodothyronines have been d
content: In vertebrates, thyroid hormones (TH) are synthesized predominantly as the prohormone thyroxine (T4), which is converted into biologically active triiodothyronine (T3) by iodothyronine deiodinases (DIOs). Although iodothyronines have been detected across several invertebrate lineages, their origin, activation mechanisms, and physiological roles, particularly in early-diverging metazoans, remain poorly understood. Here, we showed that T4 and T3 stimulated calcification in the octocorals Corallium rubrum and Sarcophyton sp. In vivo injection, competitive ELISA measurements, pharmacological inhibition experiments, and phylogenetic analyses demonstrated that evolutionarily conserved DIO homologues mediated the conversion of T4 into T3. Feeding experiments further revealed that planktonic prey constituted a major exogenous source of iodothyronines and shaped their concentrations in coral tissues. Together, these findings indicate that dietary iodothyronines and their DIO-mediated activation regulate calcification in octocorals, supporting conservation of key elements of a cellular iodothyronine pathway linking environmental availability to coral biomineralization.

title: Determinan Kualitas Laporan Keuangan Koperasi Syariah: PeranKualitas Sumber Daya Manusia, Sistem Informasi Akuntansi, danPemanfaatan Teknologi Informasi di Kabupaten Lumajang
summary: This research to analyze the determinants of financial statement quality for Sharia cooperatives in Lumajang Regency by examining the roles of human resource quality, accounting information systems, and information technology utilization, b
content: This research to analyze the determinants of financial statement quality for Sharia cooperatives in Lumajang Regency by examining the roles of human resource quality, accounting information systems, and information technology utilization, both individually and simultaneously. This research employs a quantitative explanatory research approach. The research population consists of Sharia cooperatives in Lumajang Regency, with sampling conducted via purposive sampling based on criteria requiring cooperatives to be registered, Sharia-based, and active. Data analysis was performed using multiple linear regression, accompanied by validity and reliability tests, classical assumption tests, partial tests (t-test), simultaneous tests (F-test), and the coefficient of determination (R²). The results indicate that human resource quality is a determinant that has a positive and significant effect on the quality of financial statements. Accounting information systems also have a positive and significant effecton financial statement quality. Information technology utilization has a positive and significant effect and serves as the most dominant determinant in enhancing the quality of Sharia cooperative financial statements. Simultaneously, these three determinants significantly influence the quality of financial statements. This research recommends enhancing human resource competence through training, strengtheningaccounting information systems, and optimizing information technology utilization to support the preparation of accurate, reliable, relevant, and timely financial statements.

title: BEYOND THE FRAGRANCE: CULTURAL STORYTELLING, SACRED-IMAGE SENSITIVITY, AND CONSUMER RESPONSES TO INCENSE PACKAGING—A MIXED-METHODS STUDY OF CYCLE PURE AGARBATTI IN INDIA
source: EPH - International Journal of Business & Management Science
summary: What happens when a heritage incense brand uses cultural stories on packaging that consumers will ultimately discard? This mixed-methods study examines how consumers and cultural stakeholders respond to proposed culture-led packaging for Cy
content: What happens when a heritage incense brand uses cultural stories on packaging that consumers will ultimately discard? This mixed-methods study examines how consumers and cultural stakeholders respond to proposed culture-led packaging for Cycle Pure Agarbatti in India. The research combines a reported overall survey sample of 160 respondents with four regional focus-group cohorts and depth interviews involving consumers, ritual practitioners, temple priests and an academic informant. Survey responses indicate broad initial interest in regionally themed packs, storytelling and limited editions, alongside stated willingness among some respondents to pay a modest premium. The qualitative accounts complicate this enthusiasm. Participants distinguish routine household purchases from gifting occasions and repeatedly emphasize fragrance quality, affordability, authentic representation and the handling of sacred imagery after use. The most consequential tension arises when reverential images are placed on disposable cartons. Integrating both strands, the paper proposes a Cultural Representation–Responsibility–Response framework for designing and testing culturally responsible packaging. Findings are exploratory: varying item-level response counts, non-representative sampling and qualitative summaries limit statistical generalization. The study contributes a context-sensitive account of cultural packaging in an everyday worship-adjacent product category and identifies practical questions for responsible brand experimentation.

title: Response of Tomato to Indole-3 Acetic Acid-Based Bio-Stimulant Application Derived from Shallot Bulbs
source: Bulletin of University of Agricultural Sciences and Veterinary Medicine Cluj-Napoca Agriculture
summary: Indole-3-acetic acid is a crucial phytohormone that regulates plant growth and development and is increasingly used as an active ingredient in biostimulants. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of an IAA-based bio-stimulant made from s
content: Indole-3-acetic acid is a crucial phytohormone that regulates plant growth and development and is increasingly used as an active ingredient in biostimulants. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of an IAA-based bio-stimulant made from shallot bulbs on the growth, flowering, and yield of tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.). The experiment used a Randomised Complete Block Design with different shallot bulb extract concentration applied at specific growth stages. Growth parameters, including plant height, and reproductive traits, such as flower cluster formation, fruit number, and yield, were systematically measured. Results indicated that applying shallot bulb extract enhanced vegetative growth compared to untreated plants. Plants treated with a low shallot bulb extract(2.5 mL/L) produced more flower clusters and fruits, leading to a notable increase in total yield. Conversely, higher IAA concentrations tended to suppress growth responses, demonstrating a dose-dependent effect of IAA on tomato physiology. These findings suggest that proper application of IAA-based bio-stimulants can effectively promote tomato growth and productivity. The study underscores the importance of optimising IAA concentration and application strategies to maximise the agronomic benefits of bio-stimulants while avoiding potential inhibitory effects. The results provide a scientific basis for developing sustainable, bio-stimulant-based management practices in tomato cultivation.

title: Natural and anthropogenic factors associated with agricultural productivity in selected Sub-Saharan African countries: The role of water resources
summary: This study examines the relationships between selected natural and anthropogenic factors and agricultural productivity in 18 Sub-Saharan African countries over the period 1990–2020, using panel data from the FAOSTAT database. Agricultural p
content: This study examines the relationships between selected natural and anthropogenic factors and agricultural productivity in 18 Sub-Saharan African countries over the period 1990–2020, using panel data from the FAOSTAT database. Agricultural productivity is measured as kilocalories produced per hectare of agricultural land. The explanatory variables include fertilizer use, agricultural water withdrawal, agricultural sector contribution to water stress, population, and agricultural land per capita. The Hausman test supports the use of a fixed-effects specification. The results indicate a positive and statistically significant association between population and agricultural productivity, while agricultural land per capita is negatively associated with productivity. Fertilizer use and agricultural water withdrawal are not statistically significant. The agricultural sector's contribution to water stress exhibits a positive coefficient in the baseline model; however, this association is not statistically significant when assessed using the wild cluster bootstrap procedure (p = 0.1641). This finding should therefore be interpreted with caution and does not imply that greater water stress improves agricultural productivity. The results highlight the importance of considering demographic pressures, land availability, and water-related constraints when examining agricultural productivity in Sub-Saharan Africa. The study points to the relevance of improved water resource management, efficient land use, and sustainable agricultural practices, while recognizing the limitations of country-level aggregate data and the correlational nature of the findings.

title: Examining urban expansion and spatial morphological evolution in Shillong city using geospatial techniques
summary: Abstract The rapidly expanding physical footprint of the cities have fundamentally reshaped peri-urban land use and land cover patterns, embodying the complex nature of neoliberal urbanisation in the Global South. While studies in India hav
content: Abstract The rapidly expanding physical footprint of the cities have fundamentally reshaped peri-urban land use and land cover patterns, embodying the complex nature of neoliberal urbanisation in the Global South. While studies in India have largely focused on major metropolitan cities such as Kolkata, Mumbai, Delhi, etc., the contemporary urban growth trajectories of small and medium sized cities remain unexplored. Addressing the gap, this study investigates the spatio-temporal nature of Shillong city’s urban expansion from 2004 to 2024 using geospatial technique. Drawing upon the insights gained from field observation of two peri-urban villages, we have also identified several key factors contributing to urban sprawl. Results indicate that the built-up area amplified from 11.6 sq. km (6.48% of study area) in 2004 to 47.03 sq. km (26.27% of study area) in 2024. The north-eastern quadrant emerges as the primary hotspot for urban expansion. Moreover, the swiftly increasing Shannon entropy and Landscape Expansion Index values reveal city’s evolution towards a more polycentric urban form with edge-expansion as the dominant sprawl typology. This transformation aligns with elements of both classical sector and multiple nuclei theory, signifying the role of highways, market forces, local planning choices and favourable terrain factor as potential growth stimuli. By illuminating these patterns, our study may assist on ground implementation of Shillong Master Plan with spatially differentiated planning approach, focusing on regulating sprawl and promoting sustainable land-use practices.

title: An exploratory evidence map of mechanisms, field evidence, and research gaps in plant-soil microbiome interactions for sustainable agriculture based exclusively on PubMed-indexed records
summary: Soil microorganisms mediate nutrient turnover, carbon storage, disease suppression, and plant stress tolerance, yet the evidentiary distance between microbial measurements and agronomic outcomes remains poorly defined. An evidence map is ne
content: Soil microorganisms mediate nutrient turnover, carbon storage, disease suppression, and plant stress tolerance, yet the evidentiary distance between microbial measurements and agronomic outcomes remains poorly defined. An evidence map is needed that states exactly what has been reported, in which study settings, and with what reporting gaps. An exploratory evidence map of PubMed-indexed records published from 1 January 2015 to 29 September 2026 was conducted. A Boolean query combining soil, rhizosphere, and plant microbiome concepts with crop and agricultural terms was executed on 29 September 2026 through the NCBI E-utilities. Records were deduplicated by identifier and normalised title, screened with prespecified automated title/abstract rules, and classified with lexical tags for evidence domain, study design, geography, intervention class, and crop type. Tag accuracy was quantified on 194 manually annotated records drawn from seven strata, and precision, recall, and 95% Wilson confidence intervals were computed. Of 11,061 records identified, 4 duplicates and 573 records excluded at screening left 10,484 screen-positive records. Tags indicated microbial inoculants (6,695; 63.9%), climate or environmental stress (2,748; 26.2%), nutrient cycling (2,453; 23.4%), and plant health or disease (2,377; 22.7%). An explicit field design was stated in 1,256 records (12.0%), with a validation-adjusted field share of 22.1% (95% CI 13.1%—37.5%). Economic outcomes appeared in 593 records (5.7%) and negative or null result signals in 392 (3.7%). Manual validation gave precision of 93.3% for eligibility, 90.0% for the inoculant tag, 84.0% for the stress tag, and 100% for geographic tagging. Within the PubMed-indexed literature, field verification, economic outcomes, and negative or null results are under-represented relative to controlled-environment and molecular studies. The map defines a PubMed-specific retrieval landscape, and the quantified gaps specify what a subsequent multi-database, study-level systematic review should verify.

title: Social Factors and Survival After a Childhood Central Nervous System Tumor in Sweden, Denmark, and Finland: A Register‐Based Cohort Study
summary: Studies suggest that survival after a childhood central nervous system (CNS) tumor varies across social factors, but findings are inconsistent and largely based on older cohorts. We aimed to determine whether social factors were associated
content: Studies suggest that survival after a childhood central nervous system (CNS) tumor varies across social factors, but findings are inconsistent and largely based on older cohorts. We aimed to determine whether social factors were associated with childhood CNS tumor survival and explored how this association has evolved over time in three Nordic countries. This register-based cohort study included children aged 0-19 years diagnosed with a CNS tumor during 1993-2022 in Sweden, Denmark, and Finland (aged 0-15 years, 1993-2016 in Finland). Parental educational level was examined in all three countries. Additional individual-level (parental country of birth, employment status, cohabitation, and household disposable income) and area-based (education, income) social factors were studied in Sweden and Denmark. Using Cox regression models, we estimated adjusted hazard ratios (aHR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) to evaluate the association between social factors and 10-year all-cause mortality. Among 4703 children diagnosed with CNS tumors, social factors were not uniformly associated with mortality across the study period. Among children diagnosed 1993-2007, lower maternal and area-based educational levels were associated with higher mortality (comparing least vs. most educated groups: aHR, 95% CI maternal education: 1.30, 1.03-1.65; area-based education: 1.36, 0.99-1.88). Among children diagnosed 2008-2022, children with one Nordic and one non-Nordic parent had higher mortality than children with only Nordic parents (aHR: 1.54; 95% CI: 1.09-2.19). In conclusion, while education-related disparities seem to have diminished in recent years, emerging differences by parental country of birth warrant continued monitoring.

title: Evaluating the sustainability of shrimp aquaculture in Vietnam: stakeholder perceptions across production intensification systems
source: Journal of Agribusiness in Developing and Emerging Economies
summary: Purpose This study examines stakeholder perceptions of the importance of 21 sustainability themes across 4 Vietnamese shrimp farming systems. It also assesses associations between respondent characteristics and a separate ranking of perceiv
content: Purpose This study examines stakeholder perceptions of the importance of 21 sustainability themes across 4 Vietnamese shrimp farming systems. It also assesses associations between respondent characteristics and a separate ranking of perceived system sustainability. Design/methodology/approach Using the Sustainability Assessment of Food and Agriculture Systems (SAFA) Guidelines, 94 respondents each rated 21 themes across 4 systems, yielding 84 ordinal ratings per respondent. Questionnaires were administered in person to 56 respondents and completed online by 38. Theme-specific Friedman tests accounted for repeated observations, with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment across 21 omnibus tests and, separately, 126 paired Wilcoxon comparisons. Cumulative-link mixed models provided an ordinal sensitivity analysis. Ridge-penalised multinomial regression examined the separate ranking outcome. Findings Differences across systems were supported for 18 of the 21 themes after adjustment for multiple testing. Corporate ethics, rule of law and biodiversity showed no supported omnibus differences. Super-intensive farming generally received the highest ratings for the importance of addressing sustainability issues. These ratings concern perceived priorities rather than measured performance. First-rank counts were 27, 7, 5 and 55 for super-intensive, intensive, semi-intensive and extensive/improved extensive/integrated systems, respectively. Age and self-reported knowledge were positively associated with selected ranking contrasts. These associations provide secondary evidence because two outcome categories were small. Research limitations/implications The purposive sample comprised 52 consumers, 36 business stakeholders and 6 experts. Its size and composition limit generalisation. Survey mode, fixed question order, unmeasured familiarity with production systems, concentrated high ratings and seven uniform response profiles may have influenced the findings. Sparse ranking categories limit prediction and practical interpretation of the multinomial model. Social implications Promoting sustainable shrimp farming systems also aligns with MARD’s approved “Sustainable aquaculture development plan in the Mekong Delta to 2030” (Decision No. 3550/QÐ-BNN-TCTS, August 2021), which aims to develop regional aquaculture sustainably. Originality/value The study applies the SAFA themes to comparisons of shrimp farming systems rated by the same stakeholders. By distinguishing the importance assigned to individual issues from an overall sustainability ranking, it explains how these two forms of judgement contribute different evidence to sustainability assessment.

title: A Digital Bridge to the Heart of the Silk Road: How the City of Osh Uses Technology to Attract Tourists
summary: This article examines the theoretical, methodological, and practical aspects of developing mechanisms to enhance the investment attractiveness of the tourism sector in the Osh region within the context of global digital transformation and t
content: This article examines the theoretical, methodological, and practical aspects of developing mechanisms to enhance the investment attractiveness of the tourism sector in the Osh region within the context of global digital transformation and the transition towards sustainable development principles. The authors provide a comprehensive analysis of the synergistic effects arising from the integration of advanced information and communication technologies, particularly the specialized digital platform "Open Osh," and environmental innovations as key determinants of enhancing the competitiveness of the destination. The study offers an in-depth examination of the institutional role of the NGO "Destination Osh" and international initiatives, including the Partnership for Action on Green Economy (PAGE) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), in modernizing the region’s recreational infrastructure and promoting the adoption of low-carbon technologies among small and medium-sized enterprises. Based on the SWOT analysis conducted, the study identifies the strategic advantages, weaknesses, and growth potential of the tourism market in the Osh region. It presents practical cases of the successful implementation of renewable energy sources and resource-efficiency systems. The recommendations proposed focus on scaling up digital services, fostering a cluster-based approach, and promoting green finance. Taken together, these measures can help minimize investment risks, reduce the carbon footprint of the tourism sector, and ensure long-term, inclusive economic growth at the regional level.

title: Uncoupling traits, colonization, and benefits: genotype-dependent growth promotion by endophytic bacteria in Poaceae, including perennial Kernza
source: World Journal of Microbiology and Biotechnology
summary: Thinopyrum intermedium (Kernza) is a perennial Poaceae crop with potential benefits for soil health and contributes to climate change mitigation. In this study, we investigated whether bacterial functional traits and abundance predict growt
content: Thinopyrum intermedium (Kernza) is a perennial Poaceae crop with potential benefits for soil health and contributes to climate change mitigation. In this study, we investigated whether bacterial functional traits and abundance predict growth responses across different Poaceae species. From 21 investigated bacterial strains representing endophytic and rhizosphere strains, five endophytes (Labedella endophytica FR-P-L-64, Pseudomonas lini FR-P-R2-32, Pantoea sp. GT2-2-ED1, Pseudomonas stutzeri ISE-12, Streptomyces phaeochromogenes ISE-4) were selected based on their plant-growth promoting (PGP) traits related to phytohormone production, nutrient assimilation, and stress alleviation. Phenotypic profiling revealed substantial metabolic diversity among the selected strains: P. lini FR-P-R2-32 showed the broadest spectrum of substrate utilization, while S. phaeochromogenes ISE-4 utilized only 10 of the 94 substrates. The strains were evaluated for their ability to promote plant growth in different Poaceae hosts, including two wheat cultivars, two perennial ryegrass varieties, and the perennial grain crop Kernza. Plant responses to inoculation were genotype-dependent: only S. phaeochromogenes ISE-4 increased shoot and root dry weight in Kernza and wheat cv. Euforia, whereas the remaining strains produced neutral or negative effects. Strain-specific quantitative PCR targeting the 16 S rRNA gene revealed distinct colonization patterns in shoots and roots including systemic, organ-specific, and limited colonization. Regression models indicated that post-inoculation endophyte abundance was positively or negatively associated with plant biomass, depending on the plant genotype. These findings highlight​ the importance of host genotype in determining the effectiveness of bacterial bioinoculants. This study provides the first functional characterization of bacterial endophytes isolated from T. intermedium.

title: Management and farmer knowledge mitigate environmental constraints on landrace rye performance
summary: Landraces, especially of rye (Secale cereale L.), have emerged as viable crops for organic and small-scale farmers on marginal agricultural lands. This on-farm study investigates landrace rye cultivation by examining how environment, farmer
content: Landraces, especially of rye (Secale cereale L.), have emerged as viable crops for organic and small-scale farmers on marginal agricultural lands. This on-farm study investigates landrace rye cultivation by examining how environment, farmers’ management strategies and social context are related to overall performance of landrace rye. The study included 37 fields at 28 organic farms, seven different landraces of rye (of spring-, autumn- and midsummer-sown types): most of the farmers growing rye landraces in Sweden. Using interviews, participatory observation and sampling in the fields, we collected data on crop performance, soil data, landscape structure, and farmers’ management strategies and networks. Projections to Latent Structures analysis (PLS) was used to understand how management strategies and environment were related to rye performance. We found that farmers’ access to knowledge of landrace cereal cultivation through experience and networks was associated with better rye performance and with less winter damage (Variable of Importance in the Projection /VIP >1). In contrast, fertilisation and high seed rates co-varied with lower yields and higher weed cover. High grain content of minerals, particularly Fe, Zn and Mg, was associated with high soil organic matter and a large proportion of leys in the crop rotations. Suitability of the growing conditions as indicated by production zone and landscape parameters was not important for overall rye performance (VIP<1). The midsummer-sown landrace rye (Svedjeråg) provided comparably high grain and straw yield, low weed cover and high nutrient content, also under marginal conditions, and was not associated with high winter damage. Our study indicates that landraces, especially midsummer-sown rye, can contribute to improving the sustainability of organic agriculture under marginal growing conditions. This may particularly be the case under low-input management and when farmers have experience or access to networks focused on landrace cereal cultivation.

title: Lifecycle Environmental Impact Analysis of Emerging Energy Storage Technologies in the GCC Context
summary: The high pace of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region renewable electricity expansion has increased the strategic significance of energy storage technologies that can stabilize grids that have a high level of solar penetration and seve
content: The high pace of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region renewable electricity expansion has increased the strategic significance of energy storage technologies that can stabilize grids that have a high level of solar penetration and severe climatic conditions. Although, the deployment objectives have improved, the eco-friendliness of storage technologies throughout lifecycle is not studied sufficiently on arid, high temperature, and water-limited environments. This paper is a structured lifecycle assessment (LCA) review of some of the emerging and scalable energy storage technologies applicable to the GCC including lithium-ion batteries, solid-state batteries, flow batteries, pumped hydro storage, compressed air energy storage, gravity storage, and green hydrogen-based storage systems. This review is based on the synthesis of peer-reviewed lifecycle data by the application of a cradle-to-grave analytical framework congruent with the ISO 14040/44 principles that present carbon intensity, material criticality, water dependency, land transformation, operational degradation at extreme heat, and end-of-life management pathways. Special attention is given to the role of regional specificity, the reliance on desalination, exposure to dust, and higher ambient temperatures, as well as centralized electricity markets, as the factors altering the environmental performance profiles. The analysis finds considerable trade-offs: electrochemical batteries have high upstream material and manufacturing costs, and have better modular scalability; mechanical storage opportunities have low material sensitivity, but have space and geologic limitations; H 2 -based storage has the potential to be used over the long term, but is still energy- and water-intensive. The research ends with a set of policy implications concerning sustainable deployment plans in accordance with the long-term goal of decarbonization in GCC.

title: Understanding Regional Inequalities and In‐Migration Beyond the Gentrification Debate: Towards a Research Agenda on Housing and Lifestyle ‘Affordabilities’
source: Transactions of the Institute of British Geographers
summary: ABSTRACT In this paper, I propose a novel framework—‘affordabilities’, combining affordability, mobilities and affordances—to analyse the contingent construction of affordable lifestyles through interactions between relative inequalities an
content: ABSTRACT In this paper, I propose a novel framework—‘affordabilities’, combining affordability, mobilities and affordances—to analyse the contingent construction of affordable lifestyles through interactions between relative inequalities and spatial relations. Through a focus on internal migration, I demonstrate that affordability is not an absolute quality confined to place or property, but plural and emergent through relative inequalities and relational spatial affordances. Addressing calls to reappraise the widespread application of the gentrification concept and more fully account for other migration flows alongside gentrification, I contend that an affordabilities lens helps explain the coexistence of relatively privileged forms of internal migration alongside out‐migration and welfare migration and highlights the trade‐offs involved in becoming ‘priced‐in’. Presenting a qualitative case study of a geographically and economically peripheral region in Wales (United Kingdom), I distinguish affordabilities from gentrification in scale (regional vs. neighbourhood), affordability and affordance (‘anywhere’ vs. ‘somewhere’), lower perceived prestige and transformation, coexistence with other mobility flows and the cost of affordability. In doing so, the paper provides an additional lens through which to interrogate relatively privileged in‐migration counterflows to economically peripheral regions. I conclude by highlighting avenues for further investigation through this approach.

title: Studi Literatur : Jenis, Proses Pengolahan, dan Persyaratan Mutu Air Untuk Keperluan Farmasi
summary: Water is an essential component in the pharmaceutical industry, serving as a raw material, solvent, and supporting medium for production processes. Therefore, water treatment and quality control are necessary to ensure the safety and qualit
content: Water is an essential component in the pharmaceutical industry, serving as a raw material, solvent, and supporting medium for production processes. Therefore, water treatment and quality control are necessary to ensure the safety and quality of pharmaceutical products. This study aims to review the types of pharmaceutical water, water treatment technologies, and applicable quality requirements. The method used was a literature review based on secondary data from scientific articles obtained through Google Scholar, PubMed, ScienceDirect, and ResearchGate, covering the period from 2020 to 2026. A total of 14 articles were selected and analyzed narratively based on their relevance to water types, treatment processes, and quality control. The findings indicate that Purified Water (PW) and Water for Injection (WFI) have different quality requirements according to their intended uses. Treatment technologies include reverse osmosis, filtration, deionization, ultrafiltration, electrodeionization, and distillation. The main quality parameters include conductivity, Total Organic Carbon (TOC), microbial contamination, and endotoxins. Regular monitoring and contamination control are essential to maintain pharmaceutical water quality.

title: Behavioral Dynamics of Ecological Transition Among Forestry Management Entities: Evidence from Agroforestry in Southwest China
summary: Promoting the ecological transition (ET) of forestry management entities (FMEs) is essential for advancing sustainable forestry development and supporting the green transition of rural areas. This study investigates the decision-making mech
content: Promoting the ecological transition (ET) of forestry management entities (FMEs) is essential for advancing sustainable forestry development and supporting the green transition of rural areas. This study investigates the decision-making mechanisms underlying ET in agroforestry systems by integrating multiple-case analysis with evolutionary game theory. Based on field investigations of forestry enterprises, forestry cooperatives, and family forest farms in Guangxi, Guizhou, and Yunnan provinces, key propositions concerning transition costs, expected benefits, and government intervention are identified and incorporated into an evolutionary game model. The model examines strategic interactions among FMEs under bounded rationality, and numerical simulations are used to assess the dynamic effects of different factors on the evolutionary pathways of ET. The results indicate the following. (1) Transition costs constitute the primary constraint on proactive ET. FMEs are willing to adopt proactive transition strategies when costs remain within a reasonable range, whereas their willingness declines significantly once costs exceed a critical threshold. (2) Higher direct, synergistic, and additional benefits, together with government incentives, significantly increase the likelihood of proactive ET and accelerate the convergence of the evolutionary system toward a stable proactive equilibrium. (3) Government regulation exhibits a clear threshold effect: moderate regulatory intensity promotes ET, whereas excessively stringent regulation increases compliance costs and weakens transition incentives. The findings suggest that reducing transition costs, enhancing transition benefits, and establishing balanced incentive and regulatory mechanisms are essential for promoting the ET of FMEs. Policy recommendations are proposed to improve agroforestry transition policies and provide theoretical support and practical guidance for advancing high-quality forestry development.

title: Exosome-based topical formulations as adjuncts to fractional Nd: YAG laser for postoperative facial scars
summary: Commercial topical formulations marketed as exosome skin boosters are increasingly used as adjuncts to laser treatment, but their additional benefit for postoperative facial scars remains uncertain. This randomized controlled trial allocate
content: Commercial topical formulations marketed as exosome skin boosters are increasingly used as adjuncts to laser treatment, but their additional benefit for postoperative facial scars remains uncertain. This randomized controlled trial allocated 150 patients to fractional 1064-nm Nd laser treatment followed by a control hydrogel, a human-derived formulation, or a plant-derived formulation (50 per group). Five treatment sessions were performed at 2-week intervals. Outcomes were assessed at baseline and 2 weeks after the final session using the modified Vancouver Scar Scale (mVSS), patient and observer components of the Patient and Observer Scar Assessment Scale (POSAS), and grayscale intensity (GSI) quantified from Mark-Vu images using ImageJ. Eleven participants were lost to follow-up, leaving 139 participants in the complete-case analysis: 46, 47, and 46 in the respective groups. Both adjunctive formulation groups showed significantly greater reductions in mVSS, observer POSAS, and GSI than the control group. Patient POSAS improved over time but did not demonstrate a significant time × group interaction. No statistically significant difference was detected between the human-derived and plant-derived formulations; equivalence was not established.
