No serious adverse events were reported during the observed period. Adjunctive formulations were associated with additional short-term improvements in clinician-rated scar outcomes and an exploratory optical measure, without a demonstrated additional patient-reported benefit. These findings apply to the complete formulations and do not establish an exosome-specific effect, sustained scar remodeling, or long-term safety.

title: Geographical Indications As A Catalyst For Sustainable Traditional Crafts: A Case Study Of Gujarat’s Artisanal Heritage
source: HPNLU Journal of Environment & Disaster Management
summary: Geographical Indications (GI) serve as a powerful tool for protecting traditional arts and crafts while promoting sustainability. In Gujarat, a state known for its rich cultural heritage, GI certification has played a crucial role in preser
content: Geographical Indications (GI) serve as a powerful tool for protecting traditional arts and crafts while promoting sustainability. In Gujarat, a state known for its rich cultural heritage, GI certification has played a crucial role in preserving artisanal crafts, ensuring economic stability for artisans, and fostering environmental sustainability. This paper examines how GI certification benefits traditional crafts such as Kutch Embroidery, Patan Patola, Surat Zari, Ajrakh Block Printing, and Tangaliya Shawls by enhancing market recognition, preventing cultural appropriation, and supporting eco-friendly production methods. The study explores three key dimensions of sustainability: economic, environmental, and socio cultural. Economically, GI certification boosts rural livelihoods by securing fair prices and reducing the dominance of mass-produced imitations. Environmentally, many GI-tagged crafts in Gujarat use natural dyes, organic fabrics, and traditional handloom techniques, which have a lower carbon footprint than mechanized alternatives. Socio-culturally, GI protection ensures the intergenerational transmission of skills, preventing the decline of traditional craftsmanship in the face of modernization. Despite these advantages, challenges persist, including a lack of awareness among artisans, market accessibility issues, and threats from mechanized imitations. Through case studies and policy analysis, this paper assesses the extent to which GI certification contributes to sustainability in Gujarat’s artisanal sector and proposes strategies for strengthening its impact. The research concludes that while GI protection has significantly enhanced the sustainability of Gujarat’s traditional arts and crafts, greater policy support, digital marketing initiatives, and artisan cooperatives are necessary to maximize its long-term benefits. The study highlights the need for sustainable entrepreneurship models, government incentives, and international collaborations to further empower artisans and preserve Gujarat’s artistic legacy. This paper provides a roadmap for integrating GI protection with sustainability goals, ensuring that traditional arts and crafts continue to thrive in an evolving global market.

title: Mitochondrial mass and cell ratio: predictors of maternal-specific imprinted methylation levels in ART-produced embryos
summary: Infertile couples worldwide seek assisted reproductive technologies (ARTs) to help conceive biological children. Even when treatment is successful, there is increased risk for perinatal complications, including preterm birth, intrauterine g
content: Infertile couples worldwide seek assisted reproductive technologies (ARTs) to help conceive biological children. Even when treatment is successful, there is increased risk for perinatal complications, including preterm birth, intrauterine growth restriction, low and high birth weight, and genomic imprinting disorders. Consequently, there is a need to investigate effects of ARTs on oocytes and preimplantation embryos, simultaneously, for metabolism (mitochondria), development and genomic imprinting. We hypothesized that ARTs disrupt mitochondrial dynamics and function, altering embryo developmental rates and maintenance of imprinted methylation during preimplantation development. To address this, we used a mouse model to determine relationships between these processes across multiple preimplantation stages. We observed that superovulation disrupted mitochondria in mouse oocytes, including decreased mean total and active mitochondrial mass, and altered mitochondrial distribution in superovulated MII oocytes. In preimplantation embryos, mean active mitochondrial mass was decreased in morula and blastocyst-stage embryos, with outer cells possessing asymmetric distribution of active mitochondria mass and increased superoxide levels. Further comparison of No ART controls to ART-produced blastocysts revealed lower inner:outer cell ratios, higher cavity:blastocyst volume ratios, lower mean total mitochondrial mass/cell, and lower mean active mitochondrial mass/cell. Regression analyses demonstrated that mitochondrial mass and inner:outer cell ratio independently predicted maternal Snrpn and Kcnq1ot1 methylation loss in ART-produced blastocysts, respectively. This contrasted with paternal H19 methylation. ART treatment acted as the primary driver of paternal methylation loss, with altered blastocyst variables acting downstream of ART treatment. Overall, this work provides novel linkages between metabolism, embryo developmental rates and genomic imprint regulation in preimplantation embryos.

title: A 96-well Platform for Maintaining Age-Synchronized Caenorhabditis elegans Populations Without Chemical or Genetic Intervention
summary: Caenorhabditis elegans (C. elegans) is a well-established model for investigating the mechanisms of aging and age-related disorders. However, maintaining age-synchronized populations of C. elegans without genetic or pharmacological interven
content: Caenorhabditis elegans (C. elegans) is a well-established model for investigating the mechanisms of aging and age-related disorders. However, maintaining age-synchronized populations of C. elegans without genetic or pharmacological interventions presents significant challenges, given their high reproductive rate. The traditional method for maintaining an age-synchronized population for multi-day studies without interventions is labor-intensive and low-throughput. To address these limitations, a novel method was developed to sustain age-synchronized populations in a 96-well plate liquid culture format for up to 12 days without custom-made apparatuses. The feasibility of this method was substantially improved by optimizing the surface composition of the multi-well plate and disposables and refining culture parameters. To facilitate unbiased phenotype assessment throughout the lifespan, we used a Wmicrotracker ONE reader to monitor worm movement and viability. The overall fitness decline with aging using our method is comparable to that of worms maintained on solid culture. Lastly, using transgenic C. elegans carrying tauopathy, we demonstrated that our optimized platform yields a Z-factor in the range of 0.65-0.68 at Day 3 and Day 5 adult worms, which is well above commonly used quality thresholds for multi-well screening assays. Our method simplifies age-synchronized population maintenance, enhances progeny separation, and reduces per-assay consumable costs by reusing mesh filters and batch-treated labware, enabling screening of compounds and RNAi libraries. These advancements greatly enhance the versatility of C. elegans as a model organism, offering a scalable platform for genetic and compound screening and for comprehensive investigations into drug discovery and disease mechanisms.

title: Board NGO Experience and Corporate ESG Performance: The Moderating Role of Organizational Psychological Capital
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines the association between directors with non‐governmental organization (NGO) experience and firms' environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance, as well as the moderating role of organizational psycholo
content: ABSTRACT This study examines the association between directors with non‐governmental organization (NGO) experience and firms' environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance, as well as the moderating role of organizational psychological capital (OPC). Using 1659 firm‐year observations from UK FTSE 350 companies between 2012 and 2021, we combine manually collected board data with natural language processing to measure OPC from annual‐report narratives. The results show that NGO‐experienced director representation is positively associated with ESG performance, particularly its environmental and social dimensions. We find limited evidence suggesting that OPC may strengthen the positive association between NGO‐experienced director representation and ESG performance. The study extends emerging research on NGO‐experienced directors by examining overall ESG performance and identifying OPC as a complementary organizational resource that may condition this association. The findings contribute to corporate governance, sustainability, and organizational psychology research and offer implications for boards, investors, and policymakers.

title: How commerce influences health and oral health
summary: There is increasing recognition that commercial factors can influence health and oral health both negatively and positively. This narrative review summarises the tactics used to market sugar, tobacco and alcohol, products that can be harmfu
content: There is increasing recognition that commercial factors can influence health and oral health both negatively and positively. This narrative review summarises the tactics used to market sugar, tobacco and alcohol, products that can be harmful to oral health. This article considers options open to governments and official agencies to combat the adverse influence of commerce on oral health. It also examines the role of the dental care system itself as a commercial determinant. Finally, it also reviews how commercial determinants can positively influence oral health.Dental professionals need to be aware of the influence of commercial actors on oral health. Such knowledge can enable them to act as advocates for health and oral health improvement and to engage meaningfully in wider societal debates.

title: Oil Price Uncertainty and Stock Returns in Tehran Stock Exchange as a sanctioned emerging market: An ARDL Bounds Testing Approach
summary: Abstract The purpose of this paper is to investigate the relationship between uncertainties of crude oil prices, and the Tehran Stock Index (TEPIX), under the conditions of economic sanctions, in the Tehran Stock Exchange. Using a Bounds Te
content: Abstract The purpose of this paper is to investigate the relationship between uncertainties of crude oil prices, and the Tehran Stock Index (TEPIX), under the conditions of economic sanctions, in the Tehran Stock Exchange. Using a Bounds Testing Approach of Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) model, research has been done during the period from 2012 to 2022. The results show that short and long-run oil price movements do not have relationship with market returns. Inflation does not have relationship with the market returns in the long run but have negative relationship in the short time. Changings of dollar prices has positive relationship with the market returns in the short and long run. Also, there is negative relationship between economic sanctions and stock index in the long run and not in the short run. This is one of the few empirical researches on the relationship between oil price uncertainty and stock returns in the context of Iran market and the first empirical research that studies the relationship in an economy under economic sanctions. The findings have significant policy implications for policymakers as they provide a reasonable explanation for the oil-based economy countries' stock market responses to various oil price changes. Considering the extension of sanctions to countries like Russia in recent years, results of this research will be able to shed light to economic situation of countries under similar sanctions.

title: Advanced biomedical materials and drug delivery systems for gastrointestinal applications: current understanding and future perspectives
summary: The gastrointestinal (GI) tract is a major site of ulcerative, inflammatory, and neoplastic diseases. It also functions as an important interface in systemic metabolic regulation. The effectiveness of current treatments is often limited by
content: The gastrointestinal (GI) tract is a major site of ulcerative, inflammatory, and neoplastic diseases. It also functions as an important interface in systemic metabolic regulation. The effectiveness of current treatments is often limited by poor drug stability and short residence times in the GI tract, insufficient exposure at the target site, and unnecessary systemic exposure. These limitations are compounded by regional pH changes, digestive enzymes, mucus turnover, peristaltic clearance, immune surveillance, and microbial metabolism. Advanced biomedical materials, including mucoadhesive hydrogels, stimuli-responsive nanoplatforms, metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), and extracellular matrix (ECM)-derived scaffolds, are increasingly being developed to protect cargo, prolong mucosal residence, enable site-selective release, support tissue repair, and modulate immune or microbial processes. However, selecting a suitable material and delivery strategy for different GI diseases remains challenging. This review examines physiological barriers to drug delivery in the GI tract, classifies advanced biomaterials and delivery systems by therapeutic function and platform type, and evaluates their applications across GI diseases with attention to administration routes, target sites, therapeutic outcomes, and clinical translation. Finally, we discuss future priorities for route-specific material design, human-relevant evaluation, and the safe development of advanced delivery systems. This review aims to provide a practical reference for selecting appropriate biomaterials and delivery systems for GI disease treatment and for guiding their further development toward clinical use.

title: Moringa leaf extract seed priming enhances antioxidant defense and soybean productivity under subtropical heat stress
summary: Climate-induced heat stress disrupts soybean production by inducing excessive accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS). This is the first study evaluated whether seed priming with natural organic substances (Moringa leaf extract [MLE]
content: Climate-induced heat stress disrupts soybean production by inducing excessive accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS). This is the first study evaluated whether seed priming with natural organic substances (Moringa leaf extract [MLE] 3%, guava fruit juice 2%, lemon juice 3%) induces thermotolerance more effectively than synthetic agents (KCl 0.05%, iron 0.05%) or hydro-priming under subtropical heat stress. A split-plot randomized complete block design with three replications was used, where two sowing dates (15 August, 1 September) were main plots and seven seed priming treatments (including an untreated control) were subplots. Data were collected on stand establishment, antioxidant enzyme activities, chlorophyll and oil content, and yield components. Sowing date showed no significant effect (p > 0.05). Priming treatments significantly affected all measured parameters (p < 0.05). MLE 3% produced the highest seed yield (1.6 vs. 0.85 t ha−1), germination (85.2 vs. 73.9%), and antioxidant enzyme activities, particularly SOD (+ 19.3%), CAT (+ 8.5%), and APX (+ 13.8%), compared with the control. Guava juice 2% was the second-most effective treatment. Priming with 3% MLE provided the most consistent benefits across all measured traits, suggesting its potential as an economically feasible strategy for improving soybean productivity under heat stress. This is among the first field studies comparing multiple natural and synthetic seed-priming agents under subtropical heat stress. This approach offers a promising, context-dependent strategy that warrants further validation through multi-location, multi-season trials before widespread recommendation for heat-prone subtropical soybean production.

title: Editorial: Emerging methodological perspectives and responses to business challenges
summary: Emerging methodological perspectives and responses to business challengesVolume 46, Issue 4 of ABAC Journal continues the journal's engagement with research across tourism, logistics, entrepreneurship and business management, with sustained
content: Emerging methodological perspectives and responses to business challengesVolume 46, Issue 4 of ABAC Journal continues the journal's engagement with research across tourism, logistics, entrepreneurship and business management, with sustained attention to sustainability and organizational challenges (Chumwichan & Meesing, 2025).The three articles contribute distinct methodological, empirical and theoretical perspectives to these research directions.Their contributions are presented through two complementary themes.The first builds on the journal's engagement with configurational and necessity-based approaches, emphasizing methodological considerations that support meaningful measurement and interpretation.The second examines environmental risks and resource constraints across different business contexts, highlighting the roles of organizational practices and institutional mechanisms in addressing these challenges. Emerging methodological perspectives in business researchPrior research published in ABAC Journal reflects increasing engagement with methodological approaches that capture complex relationships beyond conventional neteffect explanations, particularly in sustainable tourism research.Recent studies have combined partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA) to distinguish influential factors from necessary conditions, identifying moral norms as necessary for sustainable behavior adoption (Fakfare, Sertsri, Hemapanpairo, & underlying sustainable tourism outcomes (Manosuthi, 2025), as well as research distinguishing influential low-carbon attributes from conditions necessary for sustainable tourist behavior membership thresholds.An exploratory pilot illustrates how measurement ambiguity and sensitivity to analytical thresholds can affect the interpretation of configurational findings.The study thus title: FinTech Development and Corporate Innovation: Implications for ESG Performance and Financial Resilience - An Exploratory Study of Indian Listed Companies
summary: The study being reviewed has both theoretical and practical qualities. The study aims to introduce the framework linking Fintech evolution to corporate innovation and ESG performance, along with the financial resilience testing through the
content: The study being reviewed has both theoretical and practical qualities. The study aims to introduce the framework linking Fintech evolution to corporate innovation and ESG performance, along with the financial resilience testing through the analysis of empirical data from India. There are nine companies that do not have relations to financial activities of the study. All of them will be analysed in the period of FY2023-FY2025 (27 case studies). To analyse these 27 companies ROA and operating margin ratio will be used along with statistical procedures. The data for fiscal years FY2023-FY2025 reveals that the sales growth was 15.39%, operating profit growth was at the level of 16.97%, the net profit growth constituted 33.76%, and cash flows growth equalled 37.91%, while borrowing decreased by 9.90%. The Debt/Assets ratio fell from 15.49% to 12.55% (p = 0.049, Cohen’s dz = −0.77). The relationship between ROA and CFO/assets was very strong (r = 0.774, p < 0.001) and the inverse relationship between ROA and the ratio of Debt/assets (r = −0.631, p < 0.001) was confirmed using rank-based tests. The results indicate that it is possible to achieve financial resilience and present a clear empirical basis for general claims about links between FinTech, innovation, and ESG. The study must avoid unfounded causal claims and establish a basis for future research with larger samples in India.

title: The Domestication of Business Sustainability Research
summary: Over the past 30 years, sustainable business has become a legitimate domain of academic research and teaching. This was accomplished by a process of “strategic domestication,” fitting the domain within the evaluative logic of the dominant m
content: Over the past 30 years, sustainable business has become a legitimate domain of academic research and teaching. This was accomplished by a process of “strategic domestication,” fitting the domain within the evaluative logic of the dominant mainstream. But unfortunately, in gaining recognition and authority, today’s sustainable research has lost much of the critical edge of its original focus and moral justification. Further, it now suffers some of the same pathologies of mainstream management research, being disconnected from the real-world issues of the 21st century. But by undoing the domestication process and stepping outside the norms of mainstream scholarship, the field can help revitalize mainstream business research by redirecting attention to the big questions around the grand challenges of the 21st century and not the incremental preferences of the academic journals. Instead of fitting sustainability into existing market systems, the question is how to reshape those systems around sustainability.

title: An Adaptive One Map Framework for Developing the Sanjiangyuan Natural Resource Monitoring Network in High Altitude Cold Regions
summary: Abstract Natural resource monitoring in the Sanjiangyuan region faces systemic constraints-scattered stations, incomplete parameters, inconsistent standards, and weak data-sharing-that limit refined management in a globally significant alpi
content: Abstract Natural resource monitoring in the Sanjiangyuan region faces systemic constraints-scattered stations, incomplete parameters, inconsistent standards, and weak data-sharing-that limit refined management in a globally significant alpine environment. The "One Map" concept, widely applied in territorial spatial planning, offers a framework for spatial unification, data integration, and application synergy. However, its conventional practice rests on three implicit premises-routine data acquisition, infrastructure accessibility, and routine inter-agency coordination-none of which hold in the high-altitude uninhabited areas of Sanjiangyuan. This paper develops an adaptive One Map framework for natural resource monitoring networks in high-altitude cold regions. Drawing on the logical framework approach, it constructs a five-tier analytical system of "objectives–missions–tasks–outputs–inputs," introducing an explicit mission layer covering data assurance, decision support, and scientific understanding. Three adaptive adjustments to the conventional One Map paradigm are proposed: a dual-precision station network responding to seasonal constraints on ground data acquisition; a "data bank plus decision theater" dual-platform architecture responding to communication and computing constraints; and an explicit mission layer anchoring multi-agency coordination. The resulting pathway-"dual-precision station network + dual platform + multiple applications"-links observational data from collection and quality control through to decision support. The framework offers a transferable reference for natural resource governance in ecologically sensitive high-altitude regions where conventional monitoring paradigms are not directly applicable.

title: Biosurfactants in wastewater treatment: recent advances in agro-waste valorization, production technologies, and environmental remediation
summary: Industrial, agricultural and municipal effluents are contaminated with a variety of pollutants, including hydrocarbons, heavy metals, dyes, pharmaceuticals and pathogenic microorganisms that have a great impact on the environment and on pub
content: Industrial, agricultural and municipal effluents are contaminated with a variety of pollutants, including hydrocarbons, heavy metals, dyes, pharmaceuticals and pathogenic microorganisms that have a great impact on the environment and on public health. Typical treatment technologies are expensive, pollute the environment as secondary pollutants, and are not very effective at remediating hydrophobic and persistent contaminants. Biosurfactants have proven to be eco-friendly alternatives, due to their biodegradability, they are low in toxicity and they possess surface activity along with the ability to improve the solubilization, emulsification and microbial degradation of the contaminant. This review critically discusses the recent developments in biosurfactant production by utilizing renewable agro-industrial wastes as sustainable feedstocks, emphasizing the roles of carbon source, biomass pretreatment methods, systems for microbial fermentation and optimization of the process for enhancing the production efficiency. Moreover, the review extensively covers the mechanisms involved in the uptake of hydrocarbons, heavy metals and other recalcitrant contaminants from wastewater using biosurfactants. The recent advancement in downstream processing such as acid precipitation, solvent extraction, membrane-based purification and foam fractionation is discussed regarding the recovery performance, economic viability and environmental impact. The existing challenges such as production costs, scaling up the process, product variability, and commercialization hurdles are also discussed along with the emerging solutions such as metabolic engineering, integrated biorefineries, and circular bioeconomy. In summary, this review has highlighted the increasing capability of biosurfactants as viable and sustainable wastewater treatment agents for the next generation of wastewater treatment technologies.

title: Урожайність плодів огірка різних товарних фракцій залежно від гібриду, біопрепаратів і мікродобрив за краплинного зрошення в умовах Південного Степу України

content: Миколаївський національний аграрний університетПостановка проблеми.Огірок (Cucumis sativus L.) належить до найпоширеніших овочевих культур світу, а його виробництво має важливе продовольче та економічне значення.Водночас у зоні Південного Степу України, що характеризується хронічним дефіцитом атмосферного зволоження, високим рівнем сонячної радіації та зростаючою частотою теплових аномалій, вирощування цієї вологолюбної культури є складним науково-практичним завданням.Аридизація клімату останніх років, збільшення тривалості бездощових періодів та почастішання екстремально перегрівання надземної частини рослин, порушення фотосинтетичної діяльності листкового апарату, зниження інтенсивності цвітіння та формування зав'язі.Саме тому важливого значення набуває пошук
