title: INTEGRASI KINERJA ESG, STRATEGI HIJAU, DAN KEBERLANJUTAN TERHADAP NILAI PERUSAHAAN DI NEGARA BERKEMBANG: SEBUAH TINJAUAN LITERATUR SISTEMATIS
summary: This study synthesizes empirical evidence on the relationship between ESG performance, green strategy, and sustainability practices and firm value in developing countries. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, the systematic literature revi
content: This study synthesizes empirical evidence on the relationship between ESG performance, green strategy, and sustainability practices and firm value in developing countries. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, the systematic literature review examines 27 articles published between 2021 and 2026 and indexed in Scopus, Web of Science, or Sinta 1–2. The synthesis shows that the ESG firm value relationship in developing countries tends to be positive but contingent: the effect weakens or turns negative in the short term, in heavily polluting industries, and when ESG controversies occur. Green strategy improves firm performance and value with a time lag, particularly when it targets core operations and is supported by policy incentives and long-term investors. The three constructs are complementary: green innovation and sustainability reporting quality link ESG to firm value, whereas merely formal or symbolic commitments do not create value. The study proposes four integrative propositions on timing, credibility, institutional support, and complementarity, together with a future research agenda.

title: Confronting the Evils of Extraction: Keeping Climate Ethics Engaged
summary: Abstract The two fundamental contentions of this article are that grave evil is systematically being done and that the perpetrators have great entrenched political power based in their carbon wealth that can be overcome only by broad coalit
content: Abstract The two fundamental contentions of this article are that grave evil is systematically being done and that the perpetrators have great entrenched political power based in their carbon wealth that can be overcome only by broad coalitions of politically active individuals. Since the evil consists of threats to the preconditions of civilized society, all humans have both strong self-interest and an unconditional duty to resist it and defend our way of life. This makes the broad coalitions that are necessary also possible. Since the perpetrators are politically powerful, resisting the threats they pose requires challenging their power and undermining their wealth. No firm can be allowed any longer simply to proceed to make climate change worse because it fits their established business model. Climate ethics has so far focused mainly on questions of justice and fairness - the ethics of cooperation. We need also to develop an ethics of confrontation, beginning with a lucid understanding of the supreme moral importance of what is at stake in this political struggle over whether the extractive business-as-usual can be permitted to continue on its own terms and, since it cannot, over how it can best be eliminated fast enough, We will see some basis in both political economy and recent experience to believe that, for example, concerted political action by broad political coalitions can overcome opposition and mobilize public institutions. But a much fuller ethically-infused and empirically-based strategy is needed for the great political battle of our time.

title: Heterogeneous Paths to Green Investment: how much do firms’ economic conditions matter in their decision to invest in environmental innovation?
summary: Abstract The green transition requires firms to undertake investments whose costs are immediate and whose returns are uncertain. Although stronger prior economic performance may ease resource constraints, weaker performance may also induce
content: Abstract The green transition requires firms to undertake investments whose costs are immediate and whose returns are uncertain. Although stronger prior economic performance may ease resource constraints, weaker performance may also induce firms to seek cost reductions and resource efficiency. We examine these competing mechanisms using an original dataset of 1,537 firms in Emilia-Romagna. We combine survey data on environmental investments undertaken in 2019–2023 with balance-sheet measures of profitability, productivity and growth in 2015–2018. The empirical strategy first applies cluster analysis to identify distinct economic performance- environmental investment profiles and then estimates pairwise logit models comparing investors and non-investors with broadly comparable prior economic conditions. Four profiles emerge. Profitability, productivity and growth do not translate into a common investment pattern: some firms invest without a clear prior economic advantage, while firms with stronger profitability and growth may remain weakly engaged. Across the pairwise comparisons, regulatory knowledge, external consulting, environmental subsidies and process innovation are systematically associated with membership in the investor profiles. The results show that prior economic performance does not map onto a single green investment trajectory. Rather, firms follow heterogeneous paths shaped by the interaction of economic conditions, internal capabilities, access to knowledge and policy support.

title: Moral obligation explains less than trust and peer observation in uncertified organic coffee–goat farming in East Java
summary: Abstract Smallholders throughout Indonesia's coffee sector apply organic and integrated practices while holding no organic certification, and therefore forgo the price premium that certification confers. Neither incentive-based nor purely m
content: Abstract Smallholders throughout Indonesia's coffee sector apply organic and integrated practices while holding no organic certification, and therefore forgo the price premium that certification confers. Neither incentive-based nor purely moral accounts of adoption explain this pattern well. We surveyed 600 smallholders operating integrated coffee–goat systems across three regencies of East Java, none of them certified, and evaluated the value–belief–norm chain against two alternative routes using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Every path in the chain is supported, yet the model accounts for 2.5% of variance in ascribed responsibility and, through personal norms alone, 10.7% of variance in adoption intention. Green trust, defined as confidence that the practice performs reliably, and perceived social support each relate to intention at least as strongly as personal norms do; together they raise explained variance to 27.4%. Perceived social support is statistically independent of every construct in the moral chain. Multigroup analysis indicates that the moral route operates among men but not among women. Where neither market reward nor third-party verification is available, adoption appears to rest on judgements about whether the practice works and on what neighbours are observed to do. Group certification and demonstration through complete conversion cycles address this constraint more directly than awareness campaigns.

title: Identifying the effective cost ratio and a model-consistent shadow carbon price in deteriorating item inventory systems: a deterministic inverse optimisation approach
summary: Firms in perishable goods supply chains leave a detailed trail of replenishment decisions, yet the cost structure behind those decisions, and the value a firm place on its own carbon emissions, stay hidden. This paper develops a determinist
content: Firms in perishable goods supply chains leave a detailed trail of replenishment decisions, yet the cost structure behind those decisions, and the value a firm place on its own carbon emissions, stay hidden. This paper develops a deterministic inverse optimisation framework that reads part of that hidden structure back out of observed behaviour. A forward inventory model for a deteriorating item shows that ordering, holding, spoilage and carbon costs collapse into an effective setup term and an effective holding term, so behaviour identifies only a single cost ratio and the deterioration rate; individual accounting costs are not recoverable from decisions alone. A two-stage estimator recovers the deterioration rate from the inventory balance linking orders to sales and the cost ratio from the optimality condition, then backs out a model-consistent shadow carbon price from the ratio and the firm’s known accounting costs. We prove which quantities are identified, characterise a confounding valley in which holding, spoilage and emission costs cannot be separated from decisions alone, and show the shadow price is recoverable only when the emission signature differs from the cost signature. A numerical study separates finite-sample dispersion from asymptotic bias, documents a bias floor that persists as the sample grows at fixed noise, tests recovery under realistic measurement error and heterogeneous products, validates a bootstrap bias correction, reports confidence interval coverage, and quantifies how often the recovered price is negative. The resulting claims about consistency, identification, and practical reliability are stated in the form that the theory and data jointly support.

title: Reading National and Chongqing Carbon Prices When Both Markets Quote
summary: Core market replication covers: (i) scripts that rebuild the daily CEA–CQEA panel, dual-quote co-movement facts, extra calendar and quote-rule checks, and figures from archived public national CEA series and exchange-published Chongqing pil
content: Core market replication covers: (i) scripts that rebuild the daily CEA–CQEA panel, dual-quote co-movement facts, extra calendar and quote-rule checks, and figures from archived public national CEA series and exchange-published Chongqing pilot quotes; and (ii) a written checklist for replicating Tables 2–4 on dual-quote days. Alternate public Hubei and Guangdong archives used for Table 4 concordance are documented under the experiment data folder with provenance notes; CQEA remains primary-archive only. Optional Supplementary-only pointers, not co-equal main questions, cover parameter tables for the CEA planning anchor and illustrative eco-cost calculations, plus any survey scripts if consulted. Methods and Supplementary Material document the definitions needed to re-run the dual-quote overlap sample, n = 275, and reported tables.

title: 3D visualisation of cellulose structures across length scales in hardwoods by multimodal X-ray imaging
summary: Abstract Hierarchical soft materials, such as wood and wood-based materials, possess complex structures extending from nano- to millimetre scales that critically influence their mechanical and chemical performance. Comprehensive multiscale
content: Abstract Hierarchical soft materials, such as wood and wood-based materials, possess complex structures extending from nano- to millimetre scales that critically influence their mechanical and chemical performance. Comprehensive multiscale characterisation is therefore essential for advancing the research and development of sustainable, bio-based materials. In this study, we demonstrate a three-dimensional multimodal X-ray imaging method of hierarchical structures by combining small- and wide-angle X-ray scattering computed tomography (SWAXS-CT) with high-resolution X-ray microtomography (μCT) in a single experiment, using wood as a representative example. SWAXS-CT enables the spatial mapping of nanoscale properties, e.g., crystallite size and orientation parameters of cellulose microfibrils, while μCT provides complementary information on microscale cellular structures. Spatial correlation of nanoscale structural parameters with cellular anatomy in birch and aspen samples facilitates the identification of differences in cellulose distribution, chain orientation, and microfibril structure across tissue types such as xylem, phloem, and tension wood. Additionally, we assess radiation dose implications and resolution trade-offs inherent to the combined experiments. This work underscores the effectiveness of complementary synchrotron X-ray imaging modalities for resolving the structure–property relationships in hierarchical lignocellulosic materials. Full-field microtomographic imaging enables the visualisation of cellular structures at centimetre to micrometre length scales, while SAXS and WAXS provide access to nanoscale and atomistic features of the cellulose microfibrils, i.e., the smallest structural components within the tissues

title: Analysis of contaminants and residues in beeswax samples after flooding: an exploratory study
summary: Extreme flooding events can lead to the spread or remobilisation of contaminants and residues from historical accumulations in sediments and from substances deposited in industrial agricultural and high-traffic areas. Beeswax that is expose
content: Extreme flooding events can lead to the spread or remobilisation of contaminants and residues from historical accumulations in sediments and from substances deposited in industrial agricultural and high-traffic areas. Beeswax that is exposed to floodwater may, over time, accumulate some of these substances, both because of its affinity for lipophilic substances and because of its ability to bind trace elements (TE) that are either dissolved or bound to particles. The aim of this exploratory study was to analyse beeswax with regard to general composition (dry matter, crude protein, ether extract, crude ash), TE, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) as well as pesticide and pharmaceutical residues after a flooding event. A total of 14 beeswax samples were analysed, including six samples from flood-affected locations. Eight samples from nearby locations not exposed to floodwater were used as control group. Flooded samples showed increased crude ash contents compared to the control samples, indicating an input of material into the wax during the flooding event. Median concentrations for several TE were elevated compared to the control, including Pb (median: 988 vs 87 ppb; p = 0.008), Zn (6715 vs. 514 ppb; p = 0.001) and Hg (4 vs. 1 ppb; p = 0.008). PAHs concentrations were elevated in the flood-affected samples. The median total concentration of all 16 PAHs analysed was 115 µg/kg in the flood-affected samples, compared to 16 µg/kg in the control samples. Differences were found between the sample groups for several substances (Mann–Whitney U test, p < 0.05). Pesticide residues occurred in both groups with high variability, but seemed to be independent of any flood-related trends. The results suggest that this specific flooding event contributed to the remobilisation of contaminants and residues, which were reflected in the beeswax. This might indicate possible safety issues for bee health or honey production, if flooded beeswax is reused in wax cycles.

title: Screening of 35 Chinese herbal medicines and metabolomic analysis of cortex moutan against Streptococcus agalactiae in tilapia
summary: Streptococcosis caused by Streptococcus agalactiae is a major bacterial disease affecting tilapia aquaculture worldwide, necessitating the development of safe and effective alternatives to conventional antibiotics. In this study, 35 Chinese
content: Streptococcosis caused by Streptococcus agalactiae is a major bacterial disease affecting tilapia aquaculture worldwide, necessitating the development of safe and effective alternatives to conventional antibiotics. In this study, 35 Chinese herbal medicines were screened for antibacterial activity against S. agalactiae using the disk diffusion and broth dilution methods. The minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) were determined, and untargeted metabolomics combined with multivariate analysis was performed to investigate the metabolic regulatory mechanisms of the most effective herbal extract. The results showed that Cortex Moutan (the root bark of Paeonia × suffruticosa Andrews), Folium Sennae, and Fructus Foeniculi exhibited in vitro antibacterial activity against S. agalactiae , with Cortex Moutan being the most effective, showing an inhibition zone diameter of 15.63 ± 0.52 mm, n=3, an MIC of 0.125 g/mL, and an MBC of 0.5 g/mL, as determined from three independent biological replicates. Notably, Folium Sennae and Fructus Foeniculi have been less studied against this pathogen, and their activity, observed here, represents a secondary contribution of this study. Metabolomics and VIP analyses revealed that several plant-derived compounds (e.g., emodin and graveoline) were detected at higher levels in the treatment group, and that key metabolic pathways, including the TCA cycle, amino acid metabolism, and the electron transport chain, may be affected. These findings provide preliminary in vitro evidence. Further in vivo validation is required before any aquaculture application.

title: Geomechanically and Geochemically Constrained Natural Hydrogen Prospectivity of the Manipur Ophiolite Complex and the Indo-Burma Range, Northeast India with a National Multi-Criteria Prospectivity Ranking
summary: Abstract Natural hydrogen (H₂) is an evolving underground energy asset, however its geological viability in India is yet inadequately defined. This research assesses ten methods for hydrogen creation and release within Indian geological reg
content: Abstract Natural hydrogen (H₂) is an evolving underground energy asset, however its geological viability in India is yet inadequately defined. This research assesses ten methods for hydrogen creation and release within Indian geological regions, incorporating published petrological, geochemical, and structural data from the Manipur Ophiolite Complex (MOC) and the Indo-Burma Range. A twelve-criterion weighted prospectivity framework is enhanced by serpentinization screening, a significant hydrogen-generation estimation, and three quantitative sensitivity evaluations. Three-dimensional fault-plane traction analyses investigate Coulomb slip vulnerability under representative principal-stress conditions. A hypothesized stress–aperture closure principle assesses comparative fracture transmissivity and Monte Carlo variations also assess the responsiveness of prospectivity rankings. A geographical excerpt from the World Stress Map 2025 provides stress-orientation scenarios without serving as a direct gage of shallow MOC stress intensities. The documented ultramafic compositions and extensive serpentinization point to good source rock conditions. The overall MOC prospectivity score is 8.39 out of 10. Still, the key intra-belt goals have very similar scores, and the hydraulic properties of fractures, the effectiveness of trapping, and direct examples of subsurface hydrogen are still unknown. The proposed rankings and volumetric evaluations function as screening tools instead of confirmed accumulations or recoverable resources. Focused fluid extraction, structural assessment, and subsurface investigations are essential to validate hydrogen charge, migration and preservation.

title: Electrochemical Evaluation of Organic and Aqueous Fractions of Mahonia nepalensis Bark Extract for Corrosion Inhibition
summary: Natural plant extracts have attracted considerable attention as environmentally friendly corrosion inhibitors. This study investigated the corrosion-inhibition performance of organic and aqueous fractions from Mahonia nepalensis bark extrac
content: Natural plant extracts have attracted considerable attention as environmentally friendly corrosion inhibitors. This study investigated the corrosion-inhibition performance of organic and aqueous fractions from Mahonia nepalensis bark extract using electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) and potentiodynamic polarization. The results showed that the aqueous fraction exhibited higher inhibition efficiency than the organic fraction under the investigated conditions. EIS measurements revealed inhibition efficiencies of 94.50% and 65.72% for the aqueous and organic fractions, respectively, while potentiodynamic polarization measurements showed efficiencies of 87.64% and 64.62%, respectively. The superior performance of the aqueous fraction indicates that polar, water-soluble phytochemicals play a dominant role in the inhibition mechanism, providing stronger adsorption, better surface protection, and higher overall inhibition compared to the organic fraction. These findings demonstrate the potential of Mahonia nepalensis bark extract, particularly its aqueous fraction, as a promising plant-derived corrosion inhibitor in acidic environments.

title: How GHRM creates firm value: a firm-level explanation through carbon footprint reduction
summary: Purpose This study explores how Green Human Resource Management (GHRM) translates into measurable organizational outcomes by examining the mediating role of carbon footprint (CF) reduction in the relationship between GHRM and financial perf
content: Purpose This study explores how Green Human Resource Management (GHRM) translates into measurable organizational outcomes by examining the mediating role of carbon footprint (CF) reduction in the relationship between GHRM and financial performance. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the Ability–Motivation–Opportunity (AMO) framework, this study develops and tests a firm-level model linking GHRM practices, CF reduction, and financial performance. Using data from 1,845 large firms, Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) is applied to examine the mediating role of externally verified CF (CO2e emissions) in the relationship between GHRM and financial performance (ROA, ROE, and ROS). Findings GHRM significantly reduces firms' CF, with the motivation dimension emerging as the most robust predictor of environmental outcomes. Mediation analysis confirms that CF reduction serves as a core mechanism transforming behavioral green initiatives into market- and stakeholder-related financial gains (ROE and ROS), while the direct effect on asset efficiency (ROA) requires longer operational horizons. Research limitations/implications This study focuses on large firms, which are more likely to verify CF externally, restricts generalizability to SMEs. Future research should adopt longitudinal and multi-method designs, examine sectoral variations, and explore how cultural and organizational contexts shape GHRM effectiveness (Mousa and Othman, 2020). Comparative studies across emerging and developed economies could clarify whether external verification mitigates institutional voids equally across contexts. Practical implications From a practical standpoint, these findings suggest that GHRM should not be treated as symbolic compliance but as a strategic driver of efficiency, legitimacy, and profitability. HR leaders should embed sustainability across the talent management cycle – from recruitment and training to evaluation and rewards – explicitly linking practices to measurable CF reduction. This requires both technical capacity and cultural alignment: selecting candidates who share sustainability values, fostering motivation through incentives, and empowering leaders as catalysts for innovation and inclusion. Opportunities provided through collaborative teams can sustain engagement and reduce the risk of employee fatigue (Dumont et al., 2017). Social implications By linking GHRM practices to externally verified CF reductions, this study highlights how organizations can move beyond symbolic compliance and build objective legitimacy. Such credibility strengthens public trust, reduces reputational risks, and aligns corporate behavior with societal expectations for transparency and sustainability. Verified reductions also contribute to broader social welfare by mitigating environmental impact, enhancing quality of life, and fostering consumer and investor confidence. title: Sustainability Budgeting and Economic Value Added of Listed Manufacturing Firms in Nigeria
source: SIAR-Global Journal of Humanities Management & Educational Review
summary: The manufacturing sector in Nigeria faces dual pressures of profitability and sustainability compliance following the adoption of IFRS S1 and S2 by the FRCN in 2024 and the NGX Sustainability Disclosure Guidelines 2023. This study examines
content: The manufacturing sector in Nigeria faces dual pressures of profitability and sustainability compliance following the adoption of IFRS S1 and S2 by the FRCN in 2024 and the NGX Sustainability Disclosure Guidelines 2023. This study examines the effect of sustainability budgeting on long-term shareholder wealth measured by economic value added (EVA) of listed manufacturing firms on the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX). Specifically, the study decomposes sustainability budgeting into environmental cost budgeting (ECB), Employee welfare and care budgeting (EWCB), and Sustainable technology and innovation budgeting (STIB). The study made use of an ex post facto research design, with secondary data obtained from thirty manufacturing firms listed on NGX covering 2020-2025. Content analysis scoring 0 4 was used to measure sustainability budgeting. a panel fixed-effects regression with robust standard errors (specify the variance estimator and clustering level) was employed. The findings reveal that all three dimensions have positive and statistically significant associations (unless causal identification is established) on EVA. The study concludes that sustainability budgeting is a value-creating strategy that enhances economic profit after deducting the cost of capital. The study recommends institutionalization of sustainability budgeting lines in master budgets and mandatory assurance.

title: Priced In? EU Climate-Policy Milestones, Carbon Prices and European Sector Stocks from 2020 to 2026
source: Journal of risk and financial management
summary: Between 2020 and 2026, the European Union first tightened its climate policy, raising its 2030 target, reforming the Emissions Trading System (ETS) and adopting a carbon border adjustment mechanism (CBAM), and then loosened parts of it by a
content: Between 2020 and 2026, the European Union first tightened its climate policy, raising its 2030 target, reforming the Emissions Trading System (ETS) and adopting a carbon border adjustment mechanism (CBAM), and then loosened parts of it by allowing for international credits, delaying ETS2 and weakening the Market Stability Reserve. This study asks whether these milestones were news for financial markets. It examines the reactions of ten STOXX Europe 600 sectors, EU carbon allowances (EUAs), Brent crude, clean-energy equities and green bonds to 19 EU announcements: nine tightening, seven loosening and three mixed. The analysis combines market-model event studies with parametric, rank and randomisation tests, false discovery rate control, power calculations, tests of event-induced variance, regressions of asset reactions on the carbon-price reaction and identification through heteroskedasticity. Four findings emerge. First, no asset shows a net-tightening abnormal return that survives correction for multiple testing; the 95% bootstrap intervals rule out two-day effects larger than about 1.5% for carbon-intensive sectors and 1.6% for EUAs. Second, the carbon market did not react in the direction implied by the legal content of the announcements: EUA reactions matched the classification in only six of 16 events, and EUA volatility was not higher on announcement days. Third, evidence that the announcements raised return variance is fragile: it survives randomisation inference only for Brent at the 10% level. Fourth, larger carbon-price reactions on announcement days were associated with lower green bond returns, but this association does not survive multiple-testing correction and identification through heteroskedasticity is weak. Advance pricing during the legislative process is consistent with these results, but so are limited power, offsetting effects and the gap between legal content and market surprise.

title: Assessments of biogas production potential from municipal solid waste and agricultural/horticultural waste in Tehran Province, Iran
summary: Rapid urbanization, rising energy demand, and environmental degradation highlight the need for bio-based renewable energy sources. This study evaluates the bioenergy potential of MSW and agricultural and horticultural wastes in Tehran Provi
content: Rapid urbanization, rising energy demand, and environmental degradation highlight the need for bio-based renewable energy sources. This study evaluates the bioenergy potential of MSW and agricultural and horticultural wastes in Tehran Province, Iran. For MSW, two scenarios were used to account for uncertainty in biogas yield. The conservative scenario uses a measured yield of 82 Nm³ /t from a pilot study. The optimistic scenario uses 200 m³ /t as a technical benchmark from the literature. The results show that the organic fraction of MSW delivered from transfer stations to the Aradkooh complex could produce 114.03–278.13 million m³ /year of biogas. This could support a total power generation capacity of 27.81–71.31 MW. Azadegan had a biogas potential of 24.59–59.98 million m³ /year followed by Hakimiyeh, with a potential of 16.54–40.35 million m³ /year. These two transfer stations had the largest municipal contributions. Agricultural bioenergy potential was mainly found in crop-producing counties such as Rey, Pishva, and Varamin. Horticultural waste was more common in the northern orchard areas, including Damavand and Shemiranat, as well as Shahriyar in the west. Transitioning to closed anaerobic digestion systems and landfill gas extraction could contribute to reducing uncontrolled Aradkooh’s leachate, odor, and methane emission while fulfilling long-term regional energy targets.

title: Local Formic Acid: Single-Atom Iron on Graphene Turns Methane into Formic Acid at the Point of Use with the ARBOK-FORMIC Module
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Formic acid is a commodity that travels. About 1.1 million t a year are consumed, mostly as an 85% technical solution, by silage, leather, textile and natural rubber industries that stand in the countryside, far from the few plants that mak
content: Formic acid is a commodity that travels. About 1.1 million t a year are consumed, mostly as an 85% technical solution, by silage, leather, textile and natural rubber industries that stand in the countryside, far from the few plants that make it. Published 2026 price assessments for the same product moved in opposite directions within one quarter: down by 12% in Germany and 14% in Japan, up by 17% in Saudi Arabia and 11% in Turkey. The industrial route (carbon monoxide, methyl formate under about 40 atm, hydrolysis with a large water excess and distillation in several columns made of corrosion-resistant alloy) can only be run at large scale. We describe ARBOK-FORMIC, a 20-foot container module placed on any methane source. Methane and a mild oxidant meet single iron atoms bound by nitrogen (FeN₄) in multilayer graphene, which lead oxidation through methanol to formic acid at room conditions, without carbon monoxide, without pressure and without a column train. Water is removed by deep vacuum at 6–10°C and returned to the cycle. One tonne of methane gives up to 2.9 t of formic acid, worth USD 1,600–2,600 against about USD 700 for the methanol the same tonne would give. A farm biogas unit of 1 million m³ a year corresponds to almost 2,000 t of acid, and a flare of 100 million m³ a year to up to 190,000 t, a sixth of the world market. Keywords: formic acid, methane, single-atom iron, thermally expanded graphite, flared gas, biogas, deep vacuum, modular chemistry, silage, hydrogen carrier

title: Effects of a Silicic Acid and Fructo-oligosaccharide Feed Additive in Nursery Pig Diets With or Without Pharmacological Levels of Zinc
source: Kansas Agricultural Experiment Station Research Reports
summary: A total of 360 nursery pigs (DNA 600 × 241; initially 12.8 ± 0.03 lb) were used in a 42-d study to determine the effects on growth performance and fecal dry matter (DM) of a silicic acid (SA) and short-chain fructo-oligosaccharide (FOS) fee
content: A total of 360 nursery pigs (DNA 600 × 241; initially 12.8 ± 0.03 lb) were used in a 42-d study to determine the effects on growth performance and fecal dry matter (DM) of a silicic acid (SA) and short-chain fructo-oligosaccharide (FOS) feed additive included in nursery pig diets with or without pharmacological levels of zinc (Zn) from zinc oxide. At approximately 19 d of age, pigs were weaned, blocked by initial BW, and allotted to one of four dietary treatments in a generalized randomized block design with 18 replicates per treatment. Diets were formulated in three phases and fed from d 0 to 10, 10 to 24, and 24 to 42. The four dietary treatments were arranged in a 2 × 2 factorial with main effects of SA/FOS feed additive (none or 0.5 lb/ton of complete feed; Improx, Addix Biotech, Weston, FL) and pharmacological levels of Zn from ZnO (none or 2,990 mg/kg added in phase 1 and 2,018 mg/kg in phase 2). All diets contained 110 mg/kg Zn from the base trace mineral premix. Pens of pigs were weighed on d 0, 10, 17, 24, 35, and 42 to determine growth performance, and on d 10 and d 24 of the study, fecal samples were collected from three pigs per pen to determine fecal DM. There were no interactions between SA/FOS and pharmacological levels of Zn throughout the study. Overall (d 0 to 42), pharmacological levels of Zn improved d 42 BW, ADG, ADFI, and F/G (P ≤ 0.007). Fecal DM at both d 10 and 24 was higher (P ≤ 0.015) in pigs fed pharmacological levels of Zn. There were no main effects observed for SA/FOS throughout the trial. In conclusion, there were no interactive effects between SA/FOS and pharmacological levels of Zn, as well as no main effects observed for SA/FOS throughout the study. Pigs fed pharmacological levels of Zn had improved ADG, ADFI, F/G, and fecal DM throughout the nursery period.

title: Multinationals and Community Development. Citizens' Assessment of Multinationals' Impacts Towards Building Environmental Justice
summary: ABSTRACT This article examines how citizens assess multinational enterprises' impacts on local communities to inform justice‐oriented practices towards achieving more just relationships between multinationals and local communities. Using a
content: ABSTRACT This article examines how citizens assess multinational enterprises' impacts on local communities to inform justice‐oriented practices towards achieving more just relationships between multinationals and local communities. Using a novel mixed‐methods research design grounded in environmental justice, this research examined the views of the citizens of the Huasco Valley in Chile regarding the impacts of two closed and two operating multinationals on communities. Ninety‐one citizens responded to a survey and 15 were interviewed; their responses were quantitatively and qualitatively analyzed. Community citizens assess multinational projects and all justice dimensions as unjust, leading to a sense of injustice. This research also ranks justice variables, identifying their relative weights and effects to build just multinationals‐community relationships and suggests that mainstream justice is insufficient to understand how to build justice and that alternative approaches are required to redefine environmental justice. This article advances environmental justice and sustainability management literature by highlighting the relevance and limitations of mainstream justice variables, proposing a justice framework based on the variables' weights and effects, and underlying other justice approaches to consider when assessing multinationals' impacts on communities. Findings suggest justice should be understood as a contextually grounded and historically informed process shaped by unequal power relations, ecological concerns, and competing knowledge systems.

title: Valorization of methanotrophic bacterial biomass as a sustainable protein source for aquaculture: A case study with juvenile rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss)
summary: Methanotrophic bacteria convert methane, a potent greenhouse gas, into protein-rich biomass. A Type II methanotroph, Methylocystis sp. MJC1, was cultivated in a gas bioreactor, yielding biomass with a crude protein content of 53.86% protein
content: Methanotrophic bacteria convert methane, a potent greenhouse gas, into protein-rich biomass. A Type II methanotroph, Methylocystis sp. MJC1, was cultivated in a gas bioreactor, yielding biomass with a crude protein content of 53.86% protein on a dry cell weight basis, and 2.3 kg was produced in three large-scale batch fermentations. This methanotrophic bacterial protein (MBP) was evaluated as an alternative to fishmeal (FM) in juvenile rainbow trout ( Oncorhynchus mykiss ). Five diets replacing FM with MBP at 0% (CON), 12.5% (RP12.5), 25% (RP25), 37.5% (RP37.5) and 50% (RP50) were fed for 8 weeks, followed by a Vibrio anguillarum challenge. FM replacement significantly affected Fulton's condition factor (K), hepatosomatic index (HSI), plasma total cholesterol, lysozyme activity and post-challenge survival time. K was elevated in RP12.5 and HSI in RP50 ( P < 0.05). Plasma total cholesterol was reduced in all MBP-fed groups compared to the control ( P < 0.05), and lysozyme activity was higher in RP37.5 than in RP50 ( P < 0.05). After challenge, survival time decreased linearly with increasing MBP replacement, with a higher hazard of death in RP37.5 and RP50 than in the control ( P < 0.05). Complete practical diets replacing FM with MBP up to 25% did not induce detectable adverse effects on growth performance, protein utilization, selected physiological parameters, immune- and antioxidant-related responses, or post-challenge survival under the present experimental conditions. However, the absence of clear performance enhancement and the limited consistency of immune-related responses suggest that MBP is a promising partial FM replacement candidate rather than a fully validated functional alternative.

title: Volatile Additive‐Assisted Processing of Organic Photovoltaics in Ambient Air
summary: ABSTRACT Organic photovoltaics (OPVs) have achieved power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) exceeding 20% in laboratory‐scale cells, yet their scalable manufacturing remains challenging because of the difficulty in controlling molecular assemb
content: ABSTRACT Organic photovoltaics (OPVs) have achieved power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) exceeding 20% in laboratory‐scale cells, yet their scalable manufacturing remains challenging because of the difficulty in controlling molecular assembly during film formation under ambient conditions. Here, we report a volatile‐additive‐mediated kinetic regulation strategy for efficient OPV fabrication in ambient air without post‐deposition thermal treatment. By incorporating the highly volatile additive 2,4‐dichlorotoluene (DCT) into the photoactive‐layer ink, we modulate the film‐solidification process and regulate molecular assembly in non‐fullerene acceptor‐based blends. The rapid evaporation of DCT promotes compact molecular packing and reduces water accessibility within the active layer. As a result, OPV cells fabricated entirely in ambient air achieve PCEs exceeding 20%, approaching the performance of devices processed under an inert atmosphere. This strategy is further extended to large‐area OPV modules, demonstrating high efficiency and reproducibility. These findings establish volatile‐additive‐mediated kinetic control as a practical approach to efficient and scalable OPV manufacturing under ambient conditions.

title: Moral Imagination in Climate Communication
source: Etikk i praksis - Nordic Journal of Applied Ethics
summary: There is an urgent need for climate action by people in the richer parts of the world, for example, politicians and producers, but also ordinary citizens. Many people are concerned about climate change but remain mainly inactive, many are d
content: There is an urgent need for climate action by people in the richer parts of the world, for example, politicians and producers, but also ordinary citizens. Many people are concerned about climate change but remain mainly inactive, many are disengaged and some continue to dismiss climate change. The present study investigates how moral imagination can be used in communication at various societal levels to overcome obstacles to climate action. Communication is not sufficient to solve the problem of inaction. Binding political agreements at a global level are of key importance. However, communication improved by moral imagination is necessary in undertaking such coercive measures by democratic means. A three-step model for attaining this goal is proposed. The first step is to use moral imagination to discern what is morally relevant in the specific communicative situation. The second step is to use moral imagination to put oneself as communicator empathetically in the place of the recipient to understand the recipient’s specific obstacles to climate action. The third step is to use moral imagination to envision the full range of possible responses to the specific obstacles and to determine which response could be the most effective. It is explored how moral imagination in a concrete way can be used in responding to obstacles by applying the imaginative tools of framing, narrative, metaphor and prototype structure. Keywords: climate change; cognitive science; communication; ethics; moral imagination

title: Greening Hyderabad’s Built Environment Through Low-Carbon Construction Materials: Problems, Solutions and an Implementation Framework for Public Projects, Corridors and High-Rise Housing
source: International Research Journal on Advanced Engineering Hub (IRJAEH)
summary: Hyderabad is expanding rapidly through large public programmes and high-rise development, yet most green-city initiatives address land, water and energy and give limited attention to the construction materials that determine a structure’s e
content: Hyderabad is expanding rapidly through large public programmes and high-rise development, yet most green-city initiatives address land, water and energy and give limited attention to the construction materials that determine a structure’s embodied carbon, durability and waste footprint. This paper examines how conventional concrete-and-brick construction can be made substantially greener without abandoning it. Through a desk-based review of Indian standards, published literature, State policy announcements and project data, nine material-related problems affecting Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC) works, the Outer Ring Road (ORR) corridor, HITEC City and tall residential buildings are identified, and a specific solution is proposed for each. The solutions cover cement and concrete mix strategies, recycled aggregates from construction and demolition (C&D) waste, lightweight walling, cool and permeable surfaces, durability measures, road-corridor materials, procurement and Schedule of Rates reform, incentives and verification, and supply-chain and skills support. An illustrative calculation shows that, under stated assumptions, replacing 30% of the cement in a concrete mix with fly ash lowers its cement-related emissions by about 29%, and replacing 50% with ground granulated blast-furnace slag (GGBS) lowers them by about 46%. The paper proposes a model specification, pilot projects with defined performance indicators, and a 36-month roadmap.

title: ADOPTION OF ON-FARM TREE PLANTING AND AGROFORESTRY AMONG SMALLHOLDER FARMERS IN NIGERIA: A NARRATIVE REVIEW OF ECONOMIC, EXTENSION AND INSTITUTIONAL DRIVERS (2020–2026)
source: FUDMA Journal of Animal Production and Environmental Science
summary: Trees on farms can raise household income, restore degraded soils and buffer smallholders against climate variability, yet uptake among Nigerian smallholders remains uneven, and evidence on why farmers adopt is scattered across localised, m
content: Trees on farms can raise household income, restore degraded soils and buffer smallholders against climate variability, yet uptake among Nigerian smallholders remains uneven, and evidence on why farmers adopt is scattered across localised, mostly cross-sectional studies. This narrative review synthesises peer-reviewed evidence published from 2020 to 2026 on the economic, extension and institutional drivers of adoption of on-farm tree planting and agroforestry among smallholder farmers in Nigeria, situating it within wider sub-Saharan African and global reviews. Because the evidence is small and heterogeneous, a narrative rather than a systematic design was adopted. PRISMA 2020 was used only as a reporting guide for transparency in identification, screening and inclusion, not to claim systematic-review status, and the SWiM guideline governed the directional vote-count synthesis. Evidence was identified through targeted, non-exhaustive retrieval, and eligible studies reported empirical determinants, motivations or barriers of adoption. Reported adoption ranged from about one-third of farmers in Kaduna State to more than 85% in Ondo State, a spread that mainly reflects differences in how adoption is defined. Economic drivers centred on timber and livelihood income, high establishment costs, limited credit and long gestation periods; extension drivers on scarce technical support, minimal government extension reach relative to non-governmental organisations, and limited awareness; and institutional drivers on insecure land tenure, weak cooperative and policy support, and poor seedling supply. Age, education, gender and household size showed inconsistent effects, whereas tenure security, credit, extension contact and perceived benefits were the most consistently reported enablers or constraints. Adoption is therefore shaped less by awareness of tree benefits than by the economic and institutional environment. Tree tenure should be secured, low-cost seedlings and credit linked to farmer groups, and extension reinvigorated through demonstrations; future studies should use panel, mixed-methods and comparative designs that measure adoption intensity and persistence.

title: Novel Deep Eutectic Solvent-based Vortex-Assisted Dispersive Liquid–Liquid Microextraction of Sm from End-of-Life Sm-Co Permanent Magnets and A Green Analytical Metrics Assessment
summary: Rare earth elements are important for sustainable technologies and their recovery from waste Sm-Co magnets is essential to reduce supply shortages. Quantitative samarium analysis is therefore vital for recycling workflows in sustainable e-w
content: Rare earth elements are important for sustainable technologies and their recovery from waste Sm-Co magnets is essential to reduce supply shortages. Quantitative samarium analysis is therefore vital for recycling workflows in sustainable e-waste management. Herein, we propose a green, vortex-assisted dispersive liquid-liquid microextraction method employing a novel hydrophobic deep eutectic solvent to preconcentrate samarium ions. Waste Sm-Co magnets were leached in 3 M HNO3 to solubilize Sm ions, which were subsequently complexed at pH 5.0. The Sm-ARS (Alizarine red S) complex was extracted into a eugenol-based hydrophobic DES, with vortex agitation at 2800 rpm ensuring efficient phase separation. Quantification of the enriched analyte was performed via UV-Vis spectrophotometry at 590 nm. Experimental parameters including pH, λmax, extraction duration, volume of chelating agent, extraction solvent volume and their type, centrifuge speed, interfering foreign ions, etc. was analyzed. These parameters were systematically optimized and the analytical figures of merit, such as the limit of quantification (6.26 µg/L), limit of detection (1.87 µg/L) and enrichment factor (40), were investigated under optimal experimental conditions. This methodology provides a sustainable, high-performance alternative to conventional extraction procedures. The environmental profile was rigorously appraised using the analytical eco-scale, the green analytical procedure index, the analytical GREEnness metric and the blue applicability procedure index. These results affirm the approach as a robust, sustainable alternative solution to conventional extraction procedure for the precise quantification of samarium.

title: Listeria monocytogenes in the Genomic Era: Persistence Mechanisms, Disinfectant Tolerance, Virulence Diversity, and Evolving Food Safety Challenges in Ready‐to‐Eat Food Systems
summary: ABSTRACT Listeria monocytogenes is a ubiquitous Gram‐positive bacterium and the causative agent of listeriosis, one of the most lethal foodborne diseases, with case fatality rates of 20%–30% in susceptible populations. It grows at refrigera
content: ABSTRACT Listeria monocytogenes is a ubiquitous Gram‐positive bacterium and the causative agent of listeriosis, one of the most lethal foodborne diseases, with case fatality rates of 20%–30% in susceptible populations. It grows at refrigeration temperatures, tolerates salt and modified atmosphere packaging, and survives exposure to quaternary ammonium compound (QAC) disinfectants. These traits make it a persistent threat in ready‐to‐eat (RTE) food systems. Whole‐genome sequencing (WGS) and core genome multilocus sequence typing (cgMLST) now resolve the population structure of this pathogen at unprecedented resolution. This review synthesizes the genomic basis of virulence, persistence, and disinfectant tolerance. It covers virulence islands (LIPI‐1 to LIPI‐4), internalins, stress survival islands (SSI‐1/SSI‐2), and mobile genetic elements that carry QAC and biocide tolerance. Two genomic risk categories are examined. Hypervirulent clonal complexes are groups of closely related strains over‐represented in severe human disease relative to food. Persistent strains are genotypically indistinguishable isolates recovered repeatedly from one facility over months to years. We also assess biofilms, antimicrobial resistance, and the effect of tolerance on sanitation efficacy. The main contribution of this review is an integrated framework for genomic surveillance. We show how WGS can be embedded in environmental monitoring, HACCP, and ISO 22000 systems, and how it connects to the 2024 EU criteria revision, EU Regulation 2025/179, and the U.S. zero‐tolerance policy. A One Health workflow linking human, food, and environmental genomic data is proposed to support proactive listeriosis risk management.

title: Finance durable et pilotage de la performance ESG dans un monde VUCA : Une analyse bibliométrique des outils de contrôle face aux transitions écologiques
source: Revue Internationale des Sciences de Gestion
summary: Cette étude examine la structuration de la littérature sur la finance durable et le pilotage de la performance environnementale, sociale et de gouvernance (ESG), afin d’éclairer l’adaptation des outils de contrôle de gestion aux situations
content: Cette étude examine la structuration de la littérature sur la finance durable et le pilotage de la performance environnementale, sociale et de gouvernance (ESG), afin d’éclairer l’adaptation des outils de contrôle de gestion aux situations de volatilité, d’incertitude, de complexité et d’ambiguïté (VUCA). Le corpus comprend 160 documents (articles et revues de littérature) indexés dans le Web of Science Core Collection et publiés entre 2015 et 2025, sélectionnés selon un protocole documenté (requête, filtres, nettoyage et tri de pertinence). Les analyses de co-occurrence, de collaboration et de couplage bibliographique, réalisées avec VOSviewer et Bibliometrix, sont présentées avec leurs paramètres et leurs indicateurs quantitatifs. Les résultats montrent la centralité de la responsabilité sociale et de la gouvernance, l’émergence récente des thèmes de performance ESG, d’incertitude et de résilience, et la faible centralité des instruments internes de pilotage. Les clusters algorithmiques sont distingués de trois axes de synthèse interprétative : gouvernance et risques, divulgation et performance, adaptation organisationnelle. Une discussion conceptuelle relie chaque dimension VUCA à un besoin de pilotage, à un mécanisme de contrôle et à des conditions de pertinence. La contribution réside dans cette typologie et dans un agenda de validation empirique ; elle ne démontre pas l’efficacité des outils proposés. Le recours à une seule base documentaire et la taille modeste du corpus constituent les principales limites de l’étude.
