title: Cubic Platinum-Group Metal Nanostructures: Syntheses, Growth Mechanisms, and Catalytic Applications
summary: Platinum-group metals (PGMs) are essential for heterogeneous catalysis. Their scarcity and soaring cost make efficiency-driven, property-optimized catalysts imperative. The catalytic performance of PGMs is strongly influenced by their expos
content: Platinum-group metals (PGMs) are essential for heterogeneous catalysis. Their scarcity and soaring cost make efficiency-driven, property-optimized catalysts imperative. The catalytic performance of PGMs is strongly influenced by their exposed crystal facets, particularly the {100} facets in face-centered cubic (fcc) structures, which exhibit unique catalytic properties. This review focuses on the synthesis and growth mechanisms of PGM nanocubes (NCs) enclosed by {100} facets, highlighting key strategies for their precise control. Two primary approaches—one-pot synthesis and seed-mediated synthesis—are discussed, along with factors influencing NC formation, such as reducing agents, solvents, precursors, reaction temperatures, surfactants, and facet-directing agents. The growth mechanisms of PGM NCs are also analyzed to provide insights into morphology control and enable tailored design for enhanced catalytic performance. This review summarizes three decades of advances to guide the development of PGM-based nanomaterials with optimized properties.

title: Consequences of delays in repairing installations—an analysis of risks and environmental costs
summary: Regular renovations of water supply, sewer, and central heating systems in residential buildings are essential to maintaining their functionality. Delaying such work leads to system failures which, due to the concealed and underfloor routin
content: Regular renovations of water supply, sewer, and central heating systems in residential buildings are essential to maintaining their functionality. Delaying such work leads to system failures which, due to the concealed and underfloor routing of the systems, cause damage to building partitions and necessitate the restoration of building components. This results in a broader scope of work and a greater volume of waste. Various renovation strategies were analysed in buildings constructed using traditional methods, assessing the impact of delayed renovation schedules on the technical condition of the structures and the scope of necessary work. The aim of the study was to develop a method for planning system renovations that minimises construction waste, utilising the PRPSF ageing model. The analysis covered three maintenance strategy models: optimal repair intervention, delaying maintenance, and complete abandonment of maintenance activities. Results of the analysis of models for different scopes of maintenance confirm the necessity of conducting renovations on schedule, as delays increase the amount of waste and the risk of degradation, requiring the identification of hazards, risk assessment, and monitoring of corrective actions.

title: H2O2-Assisted Photocatalytic Degradation of Methylene Blue Dye Using Green-Synthesized Zirconia Nanoparticles
summary: The extensive use of organic dyes across textile, paper, and wool industries has significantly contributed to environmental pollution, as their release into water bodies poses a persistent ecological challenge. To address this issue, nanopa
content: The extensive use of organic dyes across textile, paper, and wool industries has significantly contributed to environmental pollution, as their release into water bodies poses a persistent ecological challenge. To address this issue, nanoparticle-based photocatalysts have emerged as a promising and sustainable approach for dye degradation under light exposure. In this study, zirconia (ZrO2) nanoparticles were synthesized via a green, eco-friendly route using Curcuma longa extract and evaluated as photocatalysts for the degradation of methylene blue (MB), a dye commonly used in Nepal. The synthesized nanoparticles were characterized using Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and UV–visible spectroscopy. FTIR analysis confirmed the successful formation of ZrO2, with characteristic absorption bands observed at 747 cm-1 and 499 cm-1, corresponding to Zr–O–Zr and Zr–O stretching vibrations, respectively. XRD analysis revealed a mixed monoclinic–tetragonal crystal structure with an average crystallite size of 14.57 nm. The photocatalytic degradation of MB was carried out under natural sunlight in the presence of ZrO2 NPs at two catalyst dosages, 15 mg and 20 mg. The 20 mg ZrO2 NPs achieved a higher degradation efficiency of 53.39% compared to 40.77% for the 15 mg-loaded NPs. These findings demonstrate that green-synthesized ZrO2 nanoparticles are potential, low-cost photocatalysts for the remediation of organic dye-contaminated water.

title: Thermodynamic-guided tailoring of single-atom coordination environments via oxygen chemical potential for efficient C-N coupling
summary: Systematic and precise regulation of coordination environments in single-atom catalysts (SACs) remains challenging due to thermodynamic constraints and kinetic traps. Herein, we report a thermodynamic-guided strategy to tailor the local coo
content: Systematic and precise regulation of coordination environments in single-atom catalysts (SACs) remains challenging due to thermodynamic constraints and kinetic traps. Herein, we report a thermodynamic-guided strategy to tailor the local coordination of Fe single atoms on CoWO4 support by regulating oxygen chemical potential. Via fine-tuning hydrogen partial pressure during pyrolysis, a series of Fe1Ox SACs is synthesized with well-defined Fe-O coordination numbers ranging from 3 to 6. Combining operando characterizations and density functional theory calculations, Fe1O4 is identified as the optimal configuration for hexamethylenetetramine (HMTA) electrosynthesis, which delivers balanced kinetics by moderating free water dissociation for *NH3 generation and strengthening HCHO chemisorption via pronounced Fe 3d-O 2p orbital hybridization near the Fermi level. As a result, the Fe1O4 SAC achieves a HMTA yield of 0.21 mmol h−1 cm−2 with 83.04% Faradaic efficiency at 1.75 V and stability over 200 h in a flow cell. This work establishes a universal thermodynamic approach for precise coordination engineering of single-atom electrocatalysts and provides a general paradigm for kinetically balancing complex multi-intermediate electrocatalytic systems. Precise control of single-atom coordination is hindered by thermodynamic and kinetic constraints. Here, the authors report tuning Fe-O coordination on CoWO4 via oxygen chemical potential control. Optimal Fe1O4 boosts hexamethylenetetramine electrosynthesis with high yield, efficiency and stability.

title: Exploring India's agroecology landscape for sustainable and transformative agricultural food systems: a systematic literature network analysis
summary: This study employs a systematic literature network analysis to examine India's agroecology (AE) landscape and its potential to transform agricultural food systems toward sustainability. Although researchers emphasize the relevance of AE, th
content: This study employs a systematic literature network analysis to examine India's agroecology (AE) landscape and its potential to transform agricultural food systems toward sustainability. Although researchers emphasize the relevance of AE, this review reveals persistent challenges, including ecological degradation from input-intensive practices, the exclusion of smallholders and women from access to resources, and limited institutional support for agroecological transitions. While AE offers a holistic framework for resilience, its integration into mainstream policy and research remains fragmented. The key themes include environmental sustainability gaps, socioeconomic vulnerabilities and undervalued indigenous knowledge. Future research should prioritize localized agroecological models, interdisciplinary approaches and participatory methods that empower farmers as co-creators of knowledge. To strengthen policy directions toward sustainable agricultural food systems, policies must embed AE into national strategies, reorient subsidies toward ecosystem services, and strengthen community-based institutions. By aligning ecological integrity with social justice, India can achieve transformative agricultural systems that secure livelihoods, empower vulnerable communities and sustain ecosystems for future generations.

title: Framing Leadership in the Energy Sector: Discursive Strategies for Communicating Sustainability and Corporate Values
summary: Framing Leadership in the Energy Sector explores how language and discourse shape leadership, influence corporate narratives, and drive sustainable transformation in one of the world’s most critical industries. While leadership has traditio
content: Framing Leadership in the Energy Sector explores how language and discourse shape leadership, influence corporate narratives, and drive sustainable transformation in one of the world’s most critical industries. While leadership has traditionally been analyzed through decision-making and strategy, this book shifts the focus to the power of written communication—how leaders construct authority, frame meaning, and align corporate messaging with evolving environmental and societal expectations. Drawing on insights from discourse analysis, rhetorical studies, and leadership communication, the book examines the linguistic and textual strategies that leaders use to establish credibility, manage uncertainty, and mobilize action in the energy sector. It considers how sustainability commitments are framed in corporate documents, policy discourse, and public engagement, revealing the strategic construction of narratives around decarbonization, technological innovation, and stakeholder trust. The book explores how leaders employ metaphorical, ethical, and persuasive frames to align their messaging with corporate values, industry norms, and global climate policies. It also highlights the leader's identity as a writer in written discourse, demonstrating how language serves as a mechanism of power, legitimacy, and influence. Offering a rich, interdisciplinary perspective on leadership communication, this book will be of great interest to students, scholars and practitioners researching and working in the fields of energy transitions, corporate communication, and leadership.

title: Harvest index and yield of sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas L.) impacted by genotype and harvest time
summary: The study was developed to determine the stage of maximum bulking, appropriate indices of maturity, and to monitor qualitative changes during the development of tuberous roots of sweet potato. Seven genotypes, viz ., G 1 (BAU Sweet potato 2
content: The study was developed to determine the stage of maximum bulking, appropriate indices of maturity, and to monitor qualitative changes during the development of tuberous roots of sweet potato. Seven genotypes, viz ., G 1 (BAU Sweet potato 2), G 2 , G 3 (BAU Sweet potato 4), G 4 (BAU Sweet potato 3), G 5 (BARI Sweet potato 2), G 6 (BAU Sweet potato 1), and G 7 , were evaluated at six harvest times, viz ., H 1 (3.0), H 2 (3.5), H 3 (4.0), H 4 (4.5), H 5 (5.0), and H 6 (5.5 months after vine planting). Genotype interaction x harvest time had a significant effect on all the traits. The highest number of leaves per plant was recorded in G 4 H 1 , while the longest vines were recorded in G 6 H 6 , as in G 7 H 6 . Leaf area was the maximum in G 7 H 3 and was comparable to G 7 H 4 , G 5 H 6 , G 7 H 6 , and G 7 H 5 . In the physiological aspect, the nitrogen balance index was the highest in G 2 H 2 , the flavonoid index was the highest in G 3 H 5 , and the chlorophyll and anthocyanin indices were the highest in G 7 H 6 . The highest tuberous root weight and total yield were recorded from G 5 H 6 , followed by G 4 H 6 with the highest harvest index. The highest tuberous roots per plant, root length, root diameter, dry matter content, and total soluble solids content were recorded in G 1 H 4 , G 4 H 3 , G 5 H 6 , G 3 H 4 , and G 2 H 4 , respectively. Correlation and multivariate analyses revealed significant associations among morpho-physiological, yield and quality-related traits of sweet potato. The genotype × harvest time combinations G 5 H 6 , G 5 H 5 , G 6 H 6 , G 6 H 5 , and G 4 H 5 showed comparatively superior performance for yield and tuberous root-related characters.

title: Aging-Aware Attention-Driven Transformer Reinforcement Learning Framework for Sustainable Hybrid Battery Energy Management in Electric Vehicles
source: International Journal of Electrical and Electronics Engineering
summary: Battery degradation is another important constraint of the hybrid electric vehicle systems, where the standard approach to energy management focuses on short-term fuel efficiency and does not consider the long-term health of the battery. In
content: Battery degradation is another important constraint of the hybrid electric vehicle systems, where the standard approach to energy management focuses on short-term fuel efficiency and does not consider the long-term health of the battery. In this paper, a proposal has been made on an Aging-Aware Attention-Driven Transformer Reinforcement Learning (AAT-DRL) framework of intelligent hybrid battery energy management. Transformer-based temporal feature encoding, along with actor-critic reinforcement learning architecture, is combined in the model to encode patterns that are sensitive to degradation such as temperature, current stress and depth-of-discharge. The multi-objective reward is developed with an aim to optimize the energy efficiency, thermal safety and battery life. The framework is tested at standard driving cycles (UDDS, NEDC and WLTP). In the results, it is shown that the degradation index has reduced by 38%, the SOC has become more stable and thermal fluctuations have been reduced, with a peak efficiency of 95.3%, which is a better performance than the state-of-the-art DRL methods. The solution offers a healthy, scalable and battery management system for the next generation based on the proposed approach.

title: Impact of artificial intelligence pilot policy on household medical burden: A quasi-experimental study based on the China Family Panel Studies
summary: Abstract Artificial intelligence policy is usually judged on innovation and output. What it does to the way households pay for medical care is a different question, and a far less examined one. This paper takes that question up. China’s Nat
content: Abstract Artificial intelligence policy is usually judged on innovation and output. What it does to the way households pay for medical care is a different question, and a far less examined one. This paper takes that question up. China’s National New Generation Artificial Intelligence Innovation and Development Pilot Zones were designated in three approval cohorts covering 18 cities, and that staggered rollout, paired with four waves of the China Family Panel Studies (2016–2022), gives us a quasi-natural experiment that can be taken to a staggered difference-in-differences design. Designation cuts real household medical expenditure by roughly 37% in the fully adjusted specification (\(\:\beta\:\) = −0.470 on log(1 + expenditure), \(\:\rho\:\) < 0.01; −0.372 with fixed effects alone). Catastrophic health expenditure (CHE) becomes about 6.0 percentage points less likely (\(\:\beta\:\) = −0.060, \(\:\rho\:\) < 0.01; −0.055 with fixed effects alone). Both estimates survive. Alternative clustering, winsorised controls, restricted samples, and placebo assignment of treatment status leave them where they stand. Insurance enrolment rises, household health status improves, and Internet use increases; each carries part of the effect. Gains in financial protection are not confined to particular institutional settings; formal interaction tests reject equality across subsamples only for long-term care insurance pilot status, and the effect is smaller where other health policies are already in force. Industrial policy aimed at AI may therefore double as social protection. How much of it households keep depends on the institutions around them.

title: Does Competitive Pressure Matter in the Nexus Among Environmental Commitment Capability, Green Procurement Practices and Green Market Performance?
source: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
summary: ABSTRACT Although prior studies acknowledge the importance of environmental commitment to sustainable organisational outcomes, they report inconsistent performance returns from environmental commitment capability, suggesting that strategic
content: ABSTRACT Although prior studies acknowledge the importance of environmental commitment to sustainable organisational outcomes, they report inconsistent performance returns from environmental commitment capability, suggesting that strategic intent alone is insufficient unless it is channelled through effective organisational routines and shaped by competitive conditions. Thus, drawing on the natural resource‐based view and institutional theory, this study examines how environmental commitment capability influences green market performance through green procurement practices and how competitive pressure conditions this process. Using firm‐level survey data from 220 Ghanaian firms, we analysed the data using structural equation modelling and the PROCESS Macro. The results showed that environmental commitment capability has a positive influence on green market performance both directly and indirectly through green procurement practices. The results further show that competitive pressure strengthens the indirect relationship, that is, external market forces amplify the effectiveness of environmentally oriented procurement initiatives. By integrating internal capability development with external institutional and competitive contingencies, this study advances sustainability and supply chain literature by explaining how environmental commitment is translated into market value. The findings of the study further identify green procurement as a central transmission mechanism and position competitive pressure as a boundary condition that determines when environmental commitment becomes strategically meaningful, rather than merely symbolic.

title: Design for Disassembly for a Circular Economy in Construction: a Systematic Literature Review of Reversible Structural Connections
summary: Abstract Most of the focus of buildings lies in the construction and use phases, but rarely on the end-of-life phase. Currently, demolition is seen as the most economically and convenient approach to dispose of a building although it genera
content: Abstract Most of the focus of buildings lies in the construction and use phases, but rarely on the end-of-life phase. Currently, demolition is seen as the most economically and convenient approach to dispose of a building although it generates a significant fraction of the construction industry’s waste. Deconstruction is touted as a promising approach to reducing the demolition waste through reuse, repair and recycling of building materials and products. However, deconstruction of current buildings is economically and technically challenging as opposed to their demolition, as most building connections are permanent fixtures. Design for disassembly (DfD) in buildings requires a thorough understanding of reversible building connections which this study investigates. This study presents a systematic literature review of reversible connections between building structural elements, analysing connection types, the circular economy (CE) objectives driving DfD, and the construction systems and structural materials associated with elements designed for deconstruction. The findings reveal that research predominantly focuses on steel, concrete, and steel–concrete construction systems, with particular emphasis on designing for component reuse. Reversibility is primarily achieved through fastening with and without connection accessories and interlocking mechanism. The review identifies significant opportunities to expand research on structural DfD connections for timber and emerging bio-based construction materials. Further research should also explore broader applications of topological interlocking and innovative construction technologies, particularly additive manufacturing, to facilitate disassembly, component recovery, and circularity in the built environment.

title: Impact of Commonly Used Preservatives and Daily Used Chemicals on Human Health: A Review
summary: Hazard is not the only measure of exposure to food preservatives or other chemicals that are used in everyday life. It is influenced by dose, route, duration, susceptibility and whether the substance is authorized and used according to its
content: Hazard is not the only measure of exposure to food preservatives or other chemicals that are used in everyday life. It is influenced by dose, route, duration, susceptibility and whether the substance is authorized and used according to its limits. This article covers food additives, preservatives, chemical contaminants, food adulteration and human health issues. The evidence suggests that when used within the limits of the regulations, authorized additives can be used to limit microbial spoilage and the risk of food-borne diseases; however, when used in excess, they may be involved in allergic reactions, gastrointestinal effects, endocrine or metabolic disturbances, neurotoxicity, carcinogenic risk etc., and when consumed over long periods of time, contamination and illegal adulteration can lead to adverse effects. In recent literature, too, mixture exposure is highlighted and the potential for changes to the gut barrier and to the gut microbiome due to additives is discussed; here the data is very heterogeneous from experimental to human studies. Risk reduction is achieved by regulation, accurate labeling, better processing, sanitary handling and intelligent food selection, not banishment of all additives.

title: Crossing the Redline: Colonial Land Zoning and Rural Wealth in Namibia
summary: Abstract. Colonial land zoning policies have shaped access to land, markets, and public services for large parts of the population on the African continent over decades. Quantitative evidence on whether the impacts of colonial zoning on lan
content: Abstract. Colonial land zoning policies have shaped access to land, markets, and public services for large parts of the population on the African continent over decades. Quantitative evidence on whether the impacts of colonial zoning on land use and rural wealth persist until today remains scarce. This paper estimates the long-run association of Namibia’s colonial zoning policies with the International Wealth Index, a contemporary wealth proxy derived from satellite data. We exploit spatial variation in exposure to and duration of zoning regulations, drawing on 8,639 rural and peri-urban settlements. Using historical analysis, covariate matching with spatially lagged controls, and regression analyses, we find that settlements in regions that were only temporarily disadvantaged by colonial zoning are as well off today as settlements in regions that received preferential treatment during various colonial periods. However, settlements north of Namibia’s Redline, an active veterinary zoning policy dating back to the 19th century, exhibit significantly lower average wealth than settlements in the rest of the country. Our analysis of historical documents and reconstructions of agricultural expansion dynamics suggests that forced migration, the expansion of commercial agriculture, and mining are key mechanisms behind our results. As such, our findings are consistent with the idea that colonial institutions can generate persistent economic divides and carry direct implications for spatially targeted land reform and rural development policy in Namibia.

title: Coupling Complementary Pathways in a Bacterial Co-culture Enables 4-Aminophenol Removal during Paracetamol Degradation
summary: Pharmaceutical biodegradation can generate potentially toxic metabolites that persist after the parent compound has been removed, posing additional risks to aquatic environments. Microbial co-cultures offer a promising strategy to address t
content: Pharmaceutical biodegradation can generate potentially toxic metabolites that persist after the parent compound has been removed, posing additional risks to aquatic environments. Microbial co-cultures offer a promising strategy to address this challenge by combining complementary metabolic capabilities to remove both pharmaceuticals and their harmful transformation products by coupling complementary degradation pathways. Here, we investigated a two-species co-culture combining the paracetamol-degrading bacterium Delftia P1 with Microbacterium lacus to enable subsequent 4-AP removal. While Delftia P1 efficiently degraded paracetamol, it accumulated 4-AP as a dead-end metabolite. M. lacus was selected to complement this metabolic limitation because its genome contains a homolog of sadB, a monooxygenase gene involved in 4-AP transformation. The relative abundance of the two strains strongly influenced 4-AP removal, with the highest efficiency achieved at a Delftia P1:M. lacus cell-density ratio of 1:100, corresponding to an OD600nm ratio of 1:10. At this ratio, the co-culture achieved complete removal of paracetamol and 4-AP within 6 and 24 h, respectively. Its capacity was tested in wastewater, where 100% of paracetamol were removed within 4 h and no accumulation of 4-AP was observed within 24 h. These findings demonstrate the potential of cocultivating bacteria with complementary metabolic capabilities to address both pharmaceutical contamination and transformation-product accumulation. Moreover, the highest 4-AP removal was achieved when M. lacus was present at a 100-fold higher cell density than Delftia P1, highlighting the importance of considering relative cell densities when designing co-cultures.

title: Designing Trust and Verifiability in Digital Energy Systems
summary: The renewable energy transition is restructuring electricity systems, necessitating the coordination of many spatially distributed and heterogeneous actors and assets. This coordination requires data sharing to ensure efficient, secure, and
content: The renewable energy transition is restructuring electricity systems, necessitating the coordination of many spatially distributed and heterogeneous actors and assets. This coordination requires data sharing to ensure efficient, secure, and sustainable operation. At this scale, actors can no longer trust the data they receive from often unknown counterparties, and manually verifying each sender and datum becomes prohibitively inefficient. Verification must therefore become digital and automatable to scale. While such verifiable data sharing promises to create value through co-creation, the data carrying this value are often sensitive, and disclosure risks loss of control and competitive or privacy-related harm. A data-sharing dilemma results: data create value only once a relying party can establish that they are correct, yet establishing this must not force those who hold the data into indiscriminate disclosure. Positioned at the intersection of Information Systems, Green IS, and Energy Informatics, this dissertation asks how verifiable data sharing and the necessary trustworthy infrastructure can be designed to support value creation in decentralized digital energy systems while addressing privacy concerns and loss-of-control risks. Integrating nine research papers within the Design Science Research paradigm, it addresses a theoretical and design-oriented gap along a single arc: from the value drivers and acceptance requirements that make verifiable data sharing worthwhile, through the design knowledge that realizes it, to the governance conditions under which that knowledge creates value at system scale. The overarching finding is that verifiability is not a substitute for trust but a means of relocating it, from the counterparties an actor shares data with toward the technologies and infrastructures that mediate data sharing. This trust shift recurs across the explanatory and the design argument. On the explanatory side, three value drivers emerge. Technology-enabled data sovereignty reshapes the interplay of trust, control, and perceived risk, enabling control instead of reliance on a counterpart's goodwill. Sustainability data create value through purpose-fit and not availability, and digital verifiability turns a credence attribute into a credibility signal that outperforms third-party certification at the point of choice. Acceptance of these applications turns not on social influence, as in classical acceptance models, but on comprehensibility and trust in technology. On the design side, the dissertation contributes layered design knowledge: it derives generalizable design principles for cross-organizational energy and sustainability data sharing. It then develops a trustworthy infrastructure, the Trust Diamond and its Decentralized Flexibility Provision Architecture, in which revocable delegation substitutes a verifiable data lineage for trust in the intermediary. And it designs mechanisms that render individual claims verifiable under p

title: When Does Sustainable Storytelling Foster Advocacy Intention? The Mediating Roles of Perceived ESG Authenticity and Emotional Brand Resonance, and the Moderating Role of Green Scepticism in Digital Ecosystems
source: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
summary: ABSTRACT Amid widespread greenwashing and consumer scepticism, brands struggle to convert sustainability commitments into advocacy intention. This study examines sustainable digital storytelling encompassing narrative environmental framing
content: ABSTRACT Amid widespread greenwashing and consumer scepticism, brands struggle to convert sustainability commitments into advocacy intention. This study examines sustainable digital storytelling encompassing narrative environmental framing (NEF), interactive sustainability co‐narration (ISC), and temporal impact visualisation (TIV) as a distinct communicative mode. Drawing on narrative transportation, signalling, and attribution theories, we develop a moderated‐mediation model linking these storytelling dimensions to sustainable consumption advocacy intention (SCAI) through perceived ESG authenticity (ESGA) and emotional brand resonance (EBR), with green scepticism (GSCP) as a boundary condition. A three‐wave, time‐lagged survey of 512 Vietnamese consumers confirms that all three storytelling dimensions enhance ESGA and EBR, which in turn predict advocacy intention, with no statistically significant residual direct effects of storytelling on advocacy. However, green scepticism attenuates these effects, diminishing compelling narratives' motivational impact. This study extends narrative transportation theory to the sustainable digital branding domain, identifies a dual cognitive‐affective pathway through which storytelling generates advocacy intention, and establishes green scepticism as a boundary condition that attenuates advocacy conversion even when authenticity and resonance perceptions are strong.

title: Molecular point-of-care testing for infectious diseases and antimicrobial resistance: integrated biosensing technologies, evidence maturity, and clinical and one health translation
summary: Effective infectious-disease management requires diagnostic results early enough to inform isolation, referral, and antimicrobial treatment. Molecular point-of-care testing (POCT) addresses this need, but analytical sensitivity alone does n
content: Effective infectious-disease management requires diagnostic results early enough to inform isolation, referral, and antimicrobial treatment. Molecular point-of-care testing (POCT) addresses this need, but analytical sensitivity alone does not establish readiness for clinical use. This critical narrative review examines molecular POCT as an integrated sample-to-answer biosensing system. It connects CRISPR-Cas recognition, isothermal amplification, microfluidic sample handling, nanomaterial-assisted preparation and transduction, and smartphone readout with contamination control, matrix tolerance, multiplexing, calibration, and reagent stability. Respiratory infections, sexually transmitted infections, and antimicrobial-resistance (AMR) testing illustrate different clinical decision windows. We propose a five-domain framework distinguishing mechanistic feasibility, analytical characterization, clinical accuracy, usability and operations, and clinical utility and implementation. A structured comparison of representative primary studies applies the framework while separating authentic clinical specimens from contrived samples and reaction time from complete workflow time. The framework is an interpretive reporting aid, not a validated readiness score. Clinically evaluated cartridge systems provide stronger evidence of diagnostic accuracy and intended-user operation than many emerging prototypes; however, randomized evidence shows that rapid pathogen identification does not necessarily reduce antibiotic prescribing. Genotypic resistance detection is therefore distinguished from phenotypic susceptibility testing and from host-response or antimicrobial-residue measurements. A focused One Health section examines transferable engineering constraints in foodborne-pathogen detection, irrigation-water surveillance, and antimicrobial-exposure monitoring. Priorities for translation include internal process controls, transparent invalid-result reporting, prospective evaluation in intended-use settings, reproducible manufacturing, affordability, secure connectivity, and explicit links between a test result and an appropriate action.

title: Lubricant Oil Degradation, Condition Monitoring, and Service Life Estimation: A Review
source: Journal of the American Oil Chemists Society
summary: ABSTRACT Lubricant oil is often changed on fixed time schedules, even though its real condition depends on load, temperature, and contamination, so good oil is discarded in some cases and degraded oil stays in service in others, which adds
content: ABSTRACT Lubricant oil is often changed on fixed time schedules, even though its real condition depends on load, temperature, and contamination, so good oil is discarded in some cases and degraded oil stays in service in others, which adds cost and waste and raises the risk of gearbox and hydraulic system failures. Degradation, monitoring, and life prediction are usually reviewed separately, so the links between them remain unclear. This review summarizes how oil type, including mineral, synthetic, bio‐based, nano‐, and ionic‐liquid lubricants, and operating loads cause degradation, including thermal‐oxidative degradation, additive depletion, viscosity breakdown, acid number increase, and water and particle contamination. It compares offline monitoring methods such as viscometry, Fourier‐transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), ferrography, particle counting, elemental analysis, and online methods such as dielectric, capacitive, inductive, optical, and multi‐sensor fusion by what they measure and where they can be used. It also assesses health index and RUL models, including machine learning, deep learning, fuzzy logic, stochastic degradation models, and digital twins, regarding how they support oil change decisions within one life cycle framework. The literature, which comprises about 230 sources from 2017 to the present, was collected from Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and SpringerLink. No single method, sensor, or model captures lubricant degradation under real operating conditions. Condition monitoring is shifting from laboratory analysis to integrated online multi‐sensor systems, and predictive models must balance accuracy, interpretability, data demand, and industrial readiness. The main gap is the limited integration across degradation, sensing, and prediction, together with the lack of standardized benchmarking and laboratory‐to‐field validation. Hybrid physics‐informed and data‐driven models, virtual sensors, and digital twins are promising routes to condition‐based and predictive maintenance and to optimizing oil change intervals, additives, and formulations, with potential environmental and economic benefits.

title: Greening Governance in the Gulf: From CSR Strategy to Resource Efficiency
source: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
summary: ABSTRACT Strategic CSR commitment does not, by itself, establish how sustainability reaches resource‐use practices. We distinguish strategic commitment, environmental management capability, and operational execution as analytical roles that
content: ABSTRACT Strategic CSR commitment does not, by itself, establish how sustainability reaches resource‐use practices. We distinguish strategic commitment, environmental management capability, and operational execution as analytical roles that can develop iteratively. Using LSEG and World Bank data, we analyze an unbalanced panel of 281 publicly listed GCC firms with 1398 firm‐year observations from 2010 to 2024. The main models use 1100 observations. Two‐step System‐GMM estimates show positive CSR associations with reported resource‐use performance and environmental pillar scores. The CSR coefficient remains positive when the environmental pillar enters the resource‐use model, a pattern consistent with partial mediation. Green buildings and audit committee expertise have negative interactions at different model stages, with uneven evidence across institutional groups. These estimates concern reported ESG scores rather than physical reductions in resource consumption. Because resource use contributes to the environmental pillar, the mediation pattern cannot independently establish a capability mechanism. The contribution is a bounded account of how strategy, reported environmental performance, infrastructure, and oversight relate within listed GCC firms.

title: Phytonutrient, phytochemical, bioactivity, and genetic fidelity profiling of meta-Topolin-derived plants of an underutilised medicinal herb Solanum virginianum L
summary: The rising trends in pathogen multidrug-resistance, malnutrition, and population growth have become globally concerning issues. These may be addressed by harnessing the nutritional and ethnomedicinal potential of underexploited wild plants
content: The rising trends in pathogen multidrug-resistance, malnutrition, and population growth have become globally concerning issues. These may be addressed by harnessing the nutritional and ethnomedicinal potential of underexploited wild plants like Solanum virginianum . This study has focused on profiling several nutritional and medicinal bioactive components and characterize bioactivities of S. virginianum to evaluate its promising prospects, and develop a sustainable mass production system for the plant. Initial LC-MS/MS screening of the methanolic leaf-crude-extract of the plant has shown the presence of 17 distinct pharmacologically important phenolic, flavonoid, saponin, and alkaloid compounds. Maximum shoot multiplication (42.10 ± 0.06) and root numbers (15.10 ± 0.15) were observed in MS + 0.2 mg/l thiadiazuron + 0.2 mg/l meta- Topolin and ½ MS + 1.0 mg/l indole-3-butyric acid media. The regenerated plants were proven to be genetically similar with mother plant using inter-simple sequence repeat (ISSR) and start-codon targeted (SCoT) markers. The regenerants were also found to be similar to or slightly better than the mother plants in terms of soluble proteins, amino acids (glycine, phenylalanine, threonine, valine), vitamin B and C, steroidal alkaloids (khasianine, solamargine, solasodine, solanine, solasonine), and 14 different phenolic acids (caffeic acid, chlorogenic acid) and flavonoids (luteolin, myricetin). The regenerated and source plants also showed comparable antioxidant activity (DPPH, ABTS, FRAP) and antimicrobial activity against multidrug-resistant uropathogens. This study provides a comprehensive account of the nutritional and medicinal prospects of S. virginianum , along with a reproducible micropropagation protocol. These information can be helpful in future investigations related to possible commercial exploitation of the plant in the pharmaceutical or food industries.

title: How Does Global Economic Volatility Shape Agricultural Resilience? Institutional, Structural, and Technological Evidence from China's Provincial Panel Data (2000–2022)
summary: The study draws on provincial panel data from 31 administrative units in China spanning 2000 to 2022. In light of these significant methodological considerations, an Agricultural Economic Resilience Index (AERI) indicates that the multiface
content: The study draws on provincial panel data from 31 administrative units in China spanning 2000 to 2022. In light of these significant methodological considerations, an Agricultural Economic Resilience Index (AERI) indicates that the multifaceted nature of resilience requires construction across three dimensions — resistance, recovery, and adaptability. Study shows three analytical approaches applied. However, the analysis demonstrates that three key lines of inquiry appear relevant: identifying shock transmission mechanisms from the global economy, conducting cross-national comparisons with major agricultural producers, and decomposing the underlying economic logic of resilience formation. Given that the significant findings reveal important patterns, the results shows that China's agricultural economy demonstrated considerable resilience across three representative global shock episodes. Additionally, the evidence indicates that the mean composite AERI reached 0.681, and the average supply-chain recovery period was 1.8 years. Results show outcomes compare favorably to Brazil and India. Nevertheless, the significant findings shows that institutional, structural, and technological factors contributed elasticity coefficients of 0.312, 0.231, and 0.186, respectively. Furthermore, the evidence demonstrates that institutional factors appear to account for the largest share among these contributors. Thus, the key results indicates that two structural weaknesses stand out: a persistent decline in soybean self-sufficiency and pronounced regional imbalances in digital agriculture adoption. Notwithstanding these important structural concerns, the significant findings shows that China's agricultural resilience could follow a compound generative logic characterized by institutional primacy, structural support, and technology-enabled adaptation. Data shows study offers empirical reference for policy design. However, the evidence demonstrates that this study may provide a substantive empirical reference for resilience-oriented agricultural policy design in emerging economies.

title: Biodegradability of Polyethylene Plastics by Individual and Co-cultured Bacterial Isolates
summary: Abstract The extensive dependence on polyethylene-based products has contributed to their persistence in the environment, accounting for about 64% of global plastic waste and posing serious ecological and public health risks. Conventional d
content: Abstract The extensive dependence on polyethylene-based products has contributed to their persistence in the environment, accounting for about 64% of global plastic waste and posing serious ecological and public health risks. Conventional disposal methods such as incineration and landfilling further intensify pollution, emphasizing the need for eco-friendly alternatives. This study explores the biodegradation of polyethylene plastics using bacteria isolates obtained from soil samples collected across three sites in Kumasi, Ghana. Degradation efficiency was assessed through weight loss analysis and Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) to determine changes in the polymer functional groups. Response Surface Methodology (RSM) was employed to evaluate the effect of pH, temperature, and incubation time on bacterial growth and degradation process. A total of eleven bacterial isolates were identified using Matrix-Assisted Laser Desorption Ionization-Time of Flight Mass Spectrometry (MALDI-TOF), with Bacillus cereus being the most prevalent. Optimization analysis revealed that temperature, pH and incubation time significantly influenced degradation, with optimal conditions predicted at 25°C, pH 9- and 21-days incubation respectively. Co-cultures demonstrated higher degradation efficiency than single isolates, supported by elevated laccase activity indicating synergistic enzymatic interactions. FTIR analysis showed polymer modification, showing changes in asymmetric and symmetric C-H stretching peaks in all treatments except Bacillus cereus. In conclusion, the results demonstrate that co-cultured microbes enhance polyethylene degradation through metabolic cooperation and increased enzyme activity, highlighting the potential of microbial synergy as a sustainable strategy for plastic waste management.

title: Electron diffraction determines crystal structures from all ten acalabrutinib samples spanning anhydrates, hydrates, and solvates
summary: Abstract Microcrystal electron diffraction can determine crystal structures from pharmaceutical powders, but its performance across a diverse set of routine-origin solid forms from one highly polymorphic compound has not been systematically
content: Abstract Microcrystal electron diffraction can determine crystal structures from pharmaceutical powders, but its performance across a diverse set of routine-origin solid forms from one highly polymorphic compound has not been systematically evaluated. We evaluated ten acalabrutinib forms selected from more than thirty identified forms and spanning anhydrates, hydrates, and solvates. Samples came from routine screening, preparation, or scale-up without purpose-grown single crystals or morphology optimization; selection was independent of apparent crystallinity, morphology, and anticipated diffraction quality. Electron diffraction determined crystal structures from all ten crystalline powder samples. Nine corresponded to selected forms, while one yielded a different form following solid-form conversion. Mother-liquor preservation combined with cryogenic preparation most consistently enabled determination of labile hydrate and solvate structures. Integration with conventional characterization detected conversions and resolved ambiguous solvent and water contents. Here, we establish a systematic single-compound benchmark supporting direct crystal-structure determination from diverse pharmaceutical crystalline powders in routine solid-form workflows.

title: Shield or Bottleneck? Navigating ESG Sustainability Uncertainty in Global Supply Chains: Asymmetric Evidence From Developed and Developing Economies
summary: ABSTRACT This study investigates the dynamic impact of the ESG‐Based Sustainability Uncertainty Index (ESGUI) on the Global Supply Chain Pressure Index (GSCPI) across five developed (USA, Germany, France, Japan, UK) and five developing econ
content: ABSTRACT This study investigates the dynamic impact of the ESG‐Based Sustainability Uncertainty Index (ESGUI) on the Global Supply Chain Pressure Index (GSCPI) across five developed (USA, Germany, France, Japan, UK) and five developing economies (China, India, Brazil, Mexico, Vietnam) using monthly data from November 2002 to June 2025. To capture multi‐horizon nonlinearities and tail dependence across distribution quantiles at the individual country level, and to empirically evaluate group‐level structural heterogeneity across economic cohorts, we employ Wavelet Kernel‐Based Regularized Least Squares (WKRLS), complemented by Wavelet Quantile Regression (WQR) and Wavelet Quantile Granger Causality (WQGC), Panel Quantile Regression (PQR) with multiple breaks as complementary dual‐verification procedures. Empirical findings reveal a fundamental macro‐structural asymmetry: in developed nations, heightened sustainability uncertainty acts as a structural “bottleneck”, exhibiting a significant positive long‐term impact on supply chain pressures due to rigid compliance burdens and accumulated regulatory costs. Conversely, developing economies turn this uncertainty into an adaptive “shield”, displaying a dominant negative relationship as agile supplier diversification and nearshoring realignment alleviate logistical friction within sustainable supply chain management (SSCM). Crucially, decoupling green transition uncertainties from global logistics networks supports resilient infrastructure (SDG 9) and responsible production patterns (SDG 12). To manage this divergence, policymakers should implement transparent regulatory timelines, targeted green logistics subsidies, and AI‐driven predictive compliance strategies.

title: Assessing energy justice in low-carbon transitions: Can system dynamics modeling contribute?
summary: The growing awareness of asymmetries in low-carbon transitions has intensified efforts to integrate energy justice into quantitative assessment tools. However, guidance remains limited on how to incorporate justice considerations into model
content: The growing awareness of asymmetries in low-carbon transitions has intensified efforts to integrate energy justice into quantitative assessment tools. However, guidance remains limited on how to incorporate justice considerations into modeling processes while preserving their normative and context-dependent character. This study proposes a conceptual-methodological meta-framework for systematically relating energy justice to system dynamics (SD) modeling. Rather than prescribing an operational modeling framework, the meta-framework provides structured guidance on how justice concerns and tenets, spatial and temporal scales, and stakeholder perspectives can and should inform problem framing, operationalization, model development, and interpretation. This paper examines the meta-framework's usefulness through a retrospective and reflexive analysis of research activities on Portugal's electric vehicle (EV) transition conducted between 2021 and 2025. The analysis illustrates how justice considerations shape model boundaries, indicator selection, causal structures, and the interpretation of model outputs, while simultaneously exposing key limitations in operationalization and normative assumptions. The contributions and limitations of SD modeling for this type of assessment are also discussed. Particularly, SD should not be used as a standalone tool for justice assessment, but as one component of a broader, methodologically plural approach. Overall, this work provides conceptual and methodological guidance for more explicit and reflexive integration of energy justice into quantitative assessments of low-carbon transitions.

title: The Drivers of ESG Uncertainty: Evidence from G7 Countries
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines how geopolitical risk, economic policy uncertainty, and tourism uncertainty are associated with ESG uncertainty across G7 countries using monthly data from November 2002 to February 2025. The findings reveal pos
content: ABSTRACT This study examines how geopolitical risk, economic policy uncertainty, and tourism uncertainty are associated with ESG uncertainty across G7 countries using monthly data from November 2002 to February 2025. The findings reveal positive and statistically significant associations between these three sources of uncertainty and ESG uncertainty, alongside substantial differences across countries. The analysis also identifies differential changes in ESG uncertainty between European and other G7 economies following the Russia–Ukraine war, although evidence of pre‐existing differences calls for caution in drawing causal conclusions. Theoretically, the study advances the understanding of ESG uncertainty as a multidimensional phenomenon shaped by geopolitical, policy‐related, and sector‐specific uncertainty rather than financial‐market conditions alone. It also highlights the importance of country‐specific exposure in explaining heterogeneous uncertainty relationships. From a practical perspective, the findings support clearer regulatory roadmaps; integrated monitoring of geopolitical, policy‐related, and tourism uncertainty; and scenario‐based ESG investment planning adapted to national and sectoral exposure. These recommendations offer practical guidance for policymakers, firms, and investors while remaining conditional on the study's associational evidence.

title: Emerging Electrospun Materials: Advanced Functionalized Nanofibers, Biopolymer Composites, and Functional Nanostructures
summary: This book provides an integrated and forward‑looking perspective on the design, synthesis, and application of electrospun nanomaterials, with particular emphasis on biopolymer‑based fibers, sustainable nanoparticle production, and functiona
content: This book provides an integrated and forward‑looking perspective on the design, synthesis, and application of electrospun nanomaterials, with particular emphasis on biopolymer‑based fibers, sustainable nanoparticle production, and functional nanostructures for biomedical and catalytic use. Drawing on recent advances in electrospinning science, green chemistry, and nanocomposite engineering, this volume explores how polymer‑solvent interactions, mathematical modeling, machine learning, and environmentally responsible synthetic routes can be combined to create high‑performance materials with tailored properties. The work highlights the scientific principles that govern fiber formation, structural control, and surface functionalization, while addressing the challenges associated with reproducibility, scalability, and multifunctionality. Integrates electrospinning science with sustainable nanoparticle synthesis and biopolymer engineering in a single, coherent framework Presents advanced methodologies for process optimization, including mathematical programming and data‑driven modeling, enabling readers to design electrospun fibers with controlled morphology, enhanced performance, and improved reproducibility Provides practical experimental insights on biopolymer‑based scaffolds, collagen‑poly(vinyl alcohol) systems, and surface biofunctionalization strategies, offering valuable guidance for researchers working in tissue engineering and biomedical materials Introduces environmentally responsible fabrication routes such as green metallic nanoparticle synthesis and deep eutectic solvent processing, giving readers access to sustainable alternatives that reduce environmental impact without compromising material functionality Demonstrates real functional applications, including antimicrobial behavior, catalytic activity, and porous‑structure formation, allowing readers to understand how nanostructured biopolymers can be translated into practical technological solutions This book informs researchers and practitioners seeking innovative pathways for developing next‑generation materials. It is intended for graduate students, academics, and professionals in materials science, chemical engineering, biotechnology, and related fields who require a comprehensive and technically rigorous resource on sustainable nanofiber and nanocomposite technologies.

title: Intercropping delivers multidimensional benefits in smallholder agrifood systems: the case of taro–cowpea–maize cultivation in South Pacific Island countries
summary: Introduction Smallholder farming systems in the South Pacific face increasing challenges from climate variability, soil degradation, labour constraints, and poor dietary diversity. Conservation agriculture (CA) has been promoted as a pathwa
content: Introduction Smallholder farming systems in the South Pacific face increasing challenges from climate variability, soil degradation, labour constraints, and poor dietary diversity. Conservation agriculture (CA) has been promoted as a pathway to improve the productivity and resilience of these systems, yet evidence of its economic, social, and climate-adaptation benefits remains limited. Methods This study evaluated a Milpa -inspired taro ( Colocasia esculenta L., Schott)–cowpea ( Vigna unguiculata L., Walp.)–maize ( Zea mays L.) intercropping system in representative smallholder farms in Samoa and Fiji using the Value-Ag integrated assessment framework. Whole-farm profitability, risk, adoption potential, and regional economic impacts under historical conditions and four projected climate scenarios. Food and nutrition security indicators were also assessed. Results and Discussion Model simulations indicated that the CA system was projected to outperform traditional taro monocropping across all climate scenarios. Whole-farm net profit was projected to increase by 67%–73% in Samoa and 55%–63% in Fiji over a 10-year period, driven by enterprise diversification, higher crop and livestock productivity, and reduced input requirements. The CA system was also projected to increase economic return while reducing downside risk, with the greatest relative benefits occurring under hotter and drier climate conditions. Adoption modelling projected peak adoption levels of 17%–54% in Samoa and 28%–50% in Fiji over 18–20 years, resulting in regional profit gains of 4%–14% and 5%–10%, respectively. Energy and protein production were estimated to increase by 73%–275% and 226%–834%, respectively. These results suggest that diversified taro-based intercropping has the potential to improve farm profitability, increase food production, and support climate adaptation in Pacific smallholder farming systems.

title: Understanding contextual determinants of smart environmental control technology adoption and perceived thermal comfort in Nigerian buildings
source: Journal of Asian Architecture and Building Engineering
summary: Nigeria’s rapid urbanisation, unreliable electricity supply, rising cooling demand, and climate pressures have intensified the need for energy-efficient building solutions. This study examines contextual determinants associated with Smart E
content: Nigeria’s rapid urbanisation, unreliable electricity supply, rising cooling demand, and climate pressures have intensified the need for energy-efficient building solutions. This study examines contextual determinants associated with Smart Environmental Control Technology (SECT) adoption and Perceived Thermal Comfort (PTC) in residential and commercial buildings in Lagos and Ibadan, Nigeria. The study adopted a quantitative cross-sectional survey design. Fuzzy TOPSIS was used to prioritise eight contextual determinants, while regression analysis examined the association between the determinants and SECT adoption and between SECT adoption and PTC. Electricity reliability (β = 0.352, p < 0.001), affordability (β = 0.284, p < 0.001), technology awareness (β = 0.241, p < 0.001), environmental awareness (β = 0.198, p < 0.001), and digital literacy (β = 0.172, p < 0.001) were among the strongest positive predictors of SECT adoption. SECT adoption was also positively associated with PTC (β = 0.683, R2 = 0.467, p < 0.001). Fuzzy TOPSIS similarly prioritised electricity reliability, affordability, and technology awareness. The findings indicate that smart-building adoption in Nigeria is shaped by interacting infrastructural, economic, technological-capability, and socio-cultural conditions. Because the evidence is cross-sectional and PTC is self-reported, the findings are interpreted as associations and predictive relationships rather than causal effects. The study provides a context-sensitive decision framework for supporting user-centred smart-building strategies in developing-country settings.

title: When the Carbon Registry Is Wrong: Finality, Correctability and Loss Allocation in Asian Carbon Markets
source: Asian Journal of Law and Economics
summary: Abstract A registry error can leave two parties claiming the same carbon allowance. This article asks when an error should still be reversed and who bears the loss once it cannot be. Comparing China, Korea and Vietnam with European Union la
content: Abstract A registry error can leave two parties claiming the same carbon allowance. This article asks when an error should still be reversed and who bears the loss once it cannot be. Comparing China, Korea and Vietnam with European Union law, it ranks remedies by their social cost. An error found before a good-faith acquisition should normally be reversed. After a good-faith acquisition or an accepted surrender, the recorded transfer should normally stand, leaving the original holder a money claim. The registry operator should bear its processing errors and users their input mistakes; a pooled fund should cover only registry-error losses that ordinary claims cannot recover. Any replacement allowance must be offset. China makes the registry decide who holds an allowance, Korea authorises correction and Vietnam requires reconciliation, but none settles how correction affects a good-faith acquirer, a completed surrender or the original holder.
