title: INVESTMENT MANAGEMENT
summary: This book discusses investment management. It covers the basic concepts and scope of investment management, the investment decision-making process, risk and return analysis in investments, investment instruments in financial markets, the ro
content: This book discusses investment management. It covers the basic concepts and scope of investment management, the investment decision-making process, risk and return analysis in investments, investment instruments in financial markets, the role of fundamental analysis in investment decisions, and the role of technical analysis in investment planning. Investment is a crucial activity in financial management because investment decisions determine how available resources are allocated to generate future economic benefits. From a management perspective, investment is more than simply purchasing stocks, bonds, mutual funds, or other assets. It is a process that includes goal setting, identifying needs and constraints, analyzing opportunities, measuring risk and return, forming a portfolio, implementing, monitoring, evaluating, and continuously adjusting decisions. Developments in financial markets have expanded investment options for individuals and organizations. Investors now have access to a variety of asset classes, capital market instruments, collectiveinvestment products, and technology-based strategies. In Indonesia,developments in investment management have also been accompanied by a strengthening of the regulatory framework. In 2025, the Financial Services Authority (OJK) emphasized the development and strengthening of investment management in the capital market, while the 2025 Capital Market Pocket Book updated its material with market developments through 2025, including carbon trading and financial derivatives with underlying securities (OJK, 2025; OJK, 2026). In addition to technical and financial aspects, this subchapter also highlights the role of management accounting information in providing relevant differential data and sensitizing readers to the influence of behavioral finance, which often traps investors in decision-making. By understanding all elements of this process,readers are expected to be able not only to make more rational and measured investment decisions but also to develop a disciplined and adaptive mindset to the ever-changing dynamics of the capital market.

title: Differentiable Programming for Differential Equations: A Review
summary: Abstract. The differentiable programming paradigm is a cornerstone of modern scientific computing. It refers to numerical methods for computing the gradient of a numerical model’s output. Many scientific models are based on differential equ
content: Abstract. The differentiable programming paradigm is a cornerstone of modern scientific computing. It refers to numerical methods for computing the gradient of a numerical model’s output. Many scientific models are based on differential equations, in which differentiable programming plays a crucial role in calculating model sensitivities, inverting model parameters, and training hybrid models that combine differential equations with data-driven approaches. Furthermore, recognizing the strong synergies between inverse methods and machine learning offers the opportunity to establish a coherent framework applicable to both fields. Differentiating functions based on the numerical solution of differential equations is nontrivial. Numerous methods based on a wide variety of paradigms have been proposed in the literature, each with pros and cons specific to the type of problem investigated. Here, we provide a comprehensive review of existing techniques to compute derivatives of numerical solutions of differential equations. We first discuss the importance of gradients of solutions of differential equations in a variety of scientific domains. Second, we lay out and compare the mathematical foundations of the various approaches. Third, we cover computational considerations and explore the solutions available in modern scientific software. Last but not least, we provide best practices and recommendations for practitioners. We hope that this work accelerates the fusion of scientific models and data and fosters a modern approach to scientific modeling.

title: Ensemble forecasting of ERCOT efficiency and residual price variability using GFDL-CM4 climate projections
summary: This paper investigates the climate-induced reliability issues within the Texas ERCOT grid by developing a multi-phase ensemble learning forecasting infrastructure. Meteorological variable forecasts from the CMIP6 GFDL-CM4 climate model wer
content: This paper investigates the climate-induced reliability issues within the Texas ERCOT grid by developing a multi-phase ensemble learning forecasting infrastructure. Meteorological variable forecasts from the CMIP6 GFDL-CM4 climate model were synthesized to project operational efficiency and residual price variability (deviations of residential prices from an inflation-adjusted baseline attributable to projected efficiency) from 2025 to 2050. Random forest regression and a hybrid SARIMA–XGBoost structure were used to estimate power plant generation and corresponding fuel consumption across seven major energy sources, achieving tolerance accuracies up to 93.7%. Renewables were projected with the most severe efficiency deficits, with wind and solar averaging 8.14% and 12.44% per month, respectively, over the forecasting range. A supporting Gaussian process model was directly trained on the projected efficiencies and estimated long-term losses of $29.8 billion for residential consumers and $31.4 billion for retail energy providers under moderate conditions. Risk analysis identified key vulnerable climate zones and dominant predictive weather variables, namely heat-related metrics. Mitigation recommendations were developed based on model outputs, including the deployment of resilient technologies (e.g., anti-icing systems and perovskite PVs), integrated energy storage, and time-of-use pricing mechanisms.

title: Alternating Methods for Large-Scale AC Optimal Power Flow with Unit Commitment
summary: Security-constrained unit commitment with alternating current optimal power flow (SCUC-ACOPF) is a central problem in power grid operations that optimizes commitment and dispatch of generators under a physically accurate power transmission
content: Security-constrained unit commitment with alternating current optimal power flow (SCUC-ACOPF) is a central problem in power grid operations that optimizes commitment and dispatch of generators under a physically accurate power transmission model while encouraging robustness against component failures. SCUC-ACOPF requires solving large-scale problems that involve multiple time periods and networks with thousands of buses within strict time limits. In this work, we study a detailed SCUC-ACOPF model with a rich set of features of modern power grids, including price-sensitive load, reserve products, transformer controls, and energy-limited devices. We propose a decomposition scheme and a penalty alternating direction method to find high-quality solutions to this model. Our methodology leverages spatial and temporal decomposition, separating the problem into a set of mixed-integer linear programs for each bus and a set of continuous nonlinear programs for each time period. To improve the performance of the algorithm, we introduce a variety of heuristics, including restrictions of temporal linking constraints, a second-order cone relaxation, and a contingency screening algorithm. We quantify the quality of feasible solutions through a dual bound from a second-order cone program. To evaluate our algorithm, we use large-scale test cases from Challenge 3 of the U.S. Department of Energy s Grid Optimization Competition that resemble real power grid data under a variety of operating conditions and decision horizons. The experiments yield feasible solutions with an average optimality gap of 1.33%, demonstrating that this approach generates near-optimal solutions within stringent time limits.

title: Inside the battery box: a cross-technology assessment of PFAS uses, functions, and substitution potential
summary: Understanding where and why per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) are used in batteries is essential for evaluating their substitution potential, yet detailed information across battery technologies is scarce. We analyzed more than 56
content: Understanding where and why per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) are used in batteries is essential for evaluating their substitution potential, yet detailed information across battery technologies is scarce. We analyzed more than 5600 submissions to the Annex XV public consultation on the proposed universal PFAS restriction in the European Union and extracted information reporting use, associated substance(s), and stated function(s) of PFASs in batteries. 341 records were compiled into a database using our structured Battery Use & Function Framework that incorporates the Functional Substitution Framework. Among these records, 78 contained sufficient information to qualify as a potential PFAS use and were organized into 36 potential PFAS uses, accounting for overlaps. Each potential PFAS use was evaluated using supporting evidence from previous use-mapping studies, input from battery stakeholders, teardown-analysis studies, and other targeted academic literature. Across all lines of evidence, two PFAS uses in batteries were contradicted, indicating already large-scale availability of PFAS-free alternatives, while 16 PFAS uses were confirmed, primarily in cathode components across several battery technologies and chemistries. PFAS-free alternatives were identified for 13 PFAS uses across battery applications, with an additional five uses showing PFAS-free options for certain applications within the broader use category. The findings indicate that few technical barriers remain for substituting PFASs in most battery components. Our mapping provides a detailed foundation for future alternatives assessments, supports essential-use evaluations, and highlights opportunities and challenges relevant to monitoring and recycling.

title: Participation, procedural fairness and policy acceptability: A quasi-experimental field study of workplace travel planning
source: Transportation Research Part A Policy and Practice
summary: Parking restrictions are among the most effective tools available to organisations and local authorities seeking to manage transport demand and reduce commuting emissions. Yet their implementation often fails when commuters question their l
content: Parking restrictions are among the most effective tools available to organisations and local authorities seeking to manage transport demand and reduce commuting emissions. Yet their implementation often fails when commuters question their legitimacy, highlighting the need to better understand the conditions under which such measures gain acceptability during the development stage. This study examines whether involving commuters in the development of restrictive travel measures increases their acceptability, applying policy acceptance and deliberative democracy literatures to an organisational transport context for the first time. Using a quasi-experimental field design embedded in a travel plan development process at a UK university (N = 486, data collected between 15/09/2025 and 05/12/2025), we compare standard consultation via a travel survey with enhanced involvement via deliberative workshops. Mediation analysis shows that workshop participation increased perceived procedural fairness, which in turn increased policy acceptability, replicating and extending Liu et al.’s (2020) participation–fairness–acceptability pathway to an organisational setting. A significant negative direct effect indicates that deliberation simultaneously raised critical scrutiny, producing inconsistent mediation. Trust in the organisation emerged as a precondition of participation: deliberative engagement increased acceptability among those who already trusted the institution. For local authorities and organisations developing restrictive travel policies, these findings suggest that deliberative involvement can build the legitimacy necessary for effective implementation where institutional trust has already been established, and where the process is designed to be genuinely fair and inclusive.

title: Sorbates from 1,1-Dialkylsubstituted Alkenes and 3-Haloacrylic Esters via Pd(II)-Isohypsic Catalysis: Focus on Terpenes
summary: Limonene and other 1,1-dialkylsubstituted alkenes undergo a regioselective Pd(II)-catalyzed C-H/C-X coupling with (E) and (Z)-3-bromoacrylates affording 4,4-disubstituted sorbate derivatives as mixtures of geometrical isomers (16 examples).
content: Limonene and other 1,1-dialkylsubstituted alkenes undergo a regioselective Pd(II)-catalyzed C-H/C-X coupling with (E) and (Z)-3-bromoacrylates affording 4,4-disubstituted sorbate derivatives as mixtures of geometrical isomers (16 examples). This coupling, unknown to date for the synthesis of 1,3-dienes, follows a mechanism distinct from the well-known Mizoroki-Heck, and works where the Mizoroki-Heck fails. Density functional theory (DFT) computations allowed to propose a plausible mechanism for this transformation.

title: Soil and host-tree associations with Tuber aestivum's ITS abundance in productive Istrian oak forests
summary: Abstract Understanding the ecological drivers of Tuber aestivum productivity in natural oak forests remains limited despite the species’ broad ecological niche and rising economic value. We characterised 65 productive plots of T. aestivum a
content: Abstract Understanding the ecological drivers of Tuber aestivum productivity in natural oak forests remains limited despite the species’ broad ecological niche and rising economic value. We characterised 65 productive plots of T. aestivum associated with Quercus pubescens and Q. cerris in forest stands of the Istrian peninsula, Croatia. At each plot, we applied a paired sampling design consisting of two systematically collected soil samples: one taken beneath the harvested ascocarp and the other taken 5 m outside the visible brûlé or tree crown area, yielding a total of 130 samples. We quantified soil physical–chemical properties (pH and texture), macronutrients (C, Ca, K, N and P), and mycelial abundance by qPCR (ITS2 copies g⁻¹ soil). Across the study area, a positive relationship between clay content and mycelial abundance emerged as the most consistent, highlighting the importance of soil water retention in T. aestivum mycelial development. In contrast, higher N levels and imbalanced K: Ca ratios were associated with lower mycelial abundance, particularly in Q. pubescens stands, whereas P showed a marginal, host‑dependent positive trend detectable only in Q. pubescens . Trends of increasing and decreasing median pH and nutrient values were detected between paired samples, with these patterns differing between host tree species. Altogether, our results indicate that T. aestivum mycelial development is promoted by clay-rich soils in oak forests and demonstrate the value of paired sampling for disentangling host- and soil‑driven processes in wild T. aestivum ecosystems.

title: The primary energy fallacy in energy transitions
summary: Abstract The global energy system remains dominated by fossil fuels, often cited as evidence that replacing them with renewables is unrealistic. Here we show that this view rests on a systematic misinterpretation of energy system size - the
content: Abstract The global energy system remains dominated by fossil fuels, often cited as evidence that replacing them with renewables is unrealistic. Here we show that this view rests on a systematic misinterpretation of energy system size - the primary energy fallacy - that arises when energy systems are compared using primary energy inputs rather than delivered energy services. Using global energy flow analysis grounded in the Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory World Energy Flow framework and IEA energy balances, we compare today’s fossil-fuel-based system with a stylised highly electrified scenario delivering the same level of useful energy services. We find that system-wide losses (rejected energy) fall by 61%, while the contribution of ambient environmental heat captured by heat pumps rises approximately twentyfold; under conventional energy-balance conventions this corresponds to a fall in primary energy inputs of nearly half. Our results show that primary energy metrics increasingly misrepresent system scale as electrification advances, with important implications for energy system analysis and policy. We recommend that energy-system analysis and policy lead with system-loss and useful-energy indicators while continuing to report primary energy as a translation for readers anchored in conventional accounting.

title: Effect of Foeniculum vulgare seed phenolic extract as a natural additive on the physicochemical, microbiological, antioxidant, and organoleptic quality of traditional Algerian J’ben cheese during storage
summary: Abstract Chemical additives widely used in the agri-food industry have raised increasing concerns because of their potential adverse effects on human health. Thus, there is growing interest in replacing synthetic additives with natural alte
content: Abstract Chemical additives widely used in the agri-food industry have raised increasing concerns because of their potential adverse effects on human health. Thus, there is growing interest in replacing synthetic additives with natural alternatives capable of preserving food quality and safety. In this context, the present study aimed to evaluate the effect of incorporating a phenolic extract from fennel ( Foeniculum vulgare ) seeds as a natural food additive on the quality of J'ben, a traditional Algerian cheese, during 15 days of refrigerated storage at 4°C. J'ben cheese, produced by mixed coagulation, was supplemented with a phenolic extract of fennel seeds obtained by hydroethanolic maceration (80:20, ethanol/water, v/v). The extract was incorporated into the cheese at concentrations of 0% (control), 1%, 2%, and 3% (w/w), and the resulting products were evaluated during 15 days of refrigerated storage at 4°C. Physicochemical, microbiological, and sensory analyses were performed on both the experimental cheeses and the fennel seed extract. The results demonstrated that the hydroethanolic extract of Foeniculum vulgare exhibited strong antioxidant activity, attributable to its high content of total phenolic compounds (9.2 mg GAE/mL extract) and flavonoids (0.68 mg QE/mL extract). Microbiological analyses further revealed that the extract possessed antimicrobial activity against several pathogenic and spoilage microorganisms while simultaneously promoting the growth of beneficial lactic acid bacteria, highlighting its potential prebiotic effect. Physicochemical parameters, including moisture content, fat content, dry matter, pH, and acidity, exhibited variations among the experimental cheeses during storage. However, the most significant finding of this study was the substantial reduction in malondialdehyde (MDA) levels observed in cheeses supplemented with 3% fennel extract compared with the control. This decrease can be attributed to the strong antioxidant activity of the extract, as demonstrated by the DPPH and FRAP assays. Furthermore, sensory evaluation revealed that the incorporation of fennel seed phenolic compounds positively influenced the freshness, aroma, and colour of the cheeses.

title: Structural Reorganisation and Reduced In Vitro Digestibility of Jackfruit Seed Starch Induced by Sequential Hydrogen Peroxide Oxidation and Heat–Moisture Treatment
summary: Abstract Hydrogen peroxide oxidation and heat–moisture treatment (HMT) modify starch through distinct mechanisms, yet little is known about how their sequential application affects starch structure and digestibility. This study evaluated th
content: Abstract Hydrogen peroxide oxidation and heat–moisture treatment (HMT) modify starch through distinct mechanisms, yet little is known about how their sequential application affects starch structure and digestibility. This study evaluated the structural reorganisation and in vitro digestibility of jackfruit seed starch subjected to hydrogen peroxide oxidation followed by HMT. Oxidation resulted in a degree of oxidation of 1.26% and slightly disrupted the ordered structure, reducing relative crystallinity from 18.4% to 16.8% and the A 1047 /A 1022 ratio from 0.684 to 0.666. In contrast, subsequent HMT promoted structural reorganisation and granule aggregation, increasing relative crystallinity to 23.4% and the A 1047 /A 1022 ratio to 0.709. These structural changes were accompanied by a marked shift in digestibility: rapidly digestible starch decreased from 68.5% in native starch to 18.8% after sequential treatment, while resistant starch increased from 15.7% to 55.6%. Correspondingly, the hydrolysis index decreased from 70.76 to 17.81, with the predicted glycaemic index decreasing from 78.56 to 49.49. Together, these findings suggest that HMT-induced structural reorganisation following oxidation is closely associated with reduced enzymatic susceptibility in jackfruit seed starch, providing a useful dual-modification approach for tailoring starch structure and digestibility.

title: Groundwater Management: Combating the Sinking Feeling
source: Notices of the American Mathematical Society
summary: Management mechanisms have been adopted to track and regulate groundwater usage. Market-driven frameworks, essential to navigate the decades-old legal governance intricacies, are a major part of these solutions. This article surveys the nex
content: Management mechanisms have been adopted to track and regulate groundwater usage. Market-driven frameworks, essential to navigate the decades-old legal governance intricacies, are a major part of these solutions. This article surveys the nexus of emergent mathematical and statistical research themes linked to this topic.

title: Advancements in Fused Deposition Modeling: Materials, Processes, and Emerging Trends in Polymer Additive Manufacturing
source: Journal of Research and Applications in Mechanical Engineering
summary: Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) has become a leading technology in polymer additive manufacturing due to its versatility, cost effectiveness, and accessibility. This review explores the current advancements, material innovations, and emergi
content: Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) has become a leading technology in polymer additive manufacturing due to its versatility, cost effectiveness, and accessibility. This review explores the current advancements, material innovations, and emerging trends within FDM, particularly focusing on high performance polymers and composite materials. Key materials like PEEK (Polyetheretherketone), PEI (Polyetherimide), and PPSU (Polyphenylsulfone) are discussed in terms of their mechanical, thermal, and chemical properties, as well as their applications across industries such as aerospace, automotive, and medical devices. The incorporation of fiber and particle reinforced composites has significantly enhanced FDM capabilities, offering improved strength, rigidity, and thermal resistance for demanding applications. Moreover, the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT) is poised to revolutionize the FDM process by enabling predictive maintenance, and real time monitoring. However, challenges such as printability, cost, and material limitations continue to hinder broader adoption, especially for high performance composites and advanced materials. The review concludes by highlighting areas for future research, and material development, which are essential for unlocking the full potential of FDM in both prototyping and end use production.

title: School Meals as Climate Policy: “As Long as It Tastes Good”
summary: Reducing greenhouse gas emissions from food consumption requires dietary changes, yet policies supporting such changes remain limited. Nevertheless, measures to reduce the carbon footprint of school meals are being implemented in several co
content: Reducing greenhouse gas emissions from food consumption requires dietary changes, yet policies supporting such changes remain limited. Nevertheless, measures to reduce the carbon footprint of school meals are being implemented in several countries. This thesis examines the potential of school meals to foster low-carbon food consumption, within and beyond school, focusing on policy outcomes, policy conditions and policy design.Two of the four papers draw on a controlled intervention in six Swedish schools, four of which introduced dishes with less red meat and other high-emission ingredients (low-carbon recipes). One analyses effects on food taken, plate waste and meal satisfaction; the other examines students’ perceptions of low-carbon recipes and of all-vegetarian days. The remaining two draw on a survey of public acceptability of such measures in France, Poland and Sweden, and interviews on the design of school meal climate policies with officials responsible for school meals in Swedish municipalities.In the intervention, low-carbon recipes reduced the carbon footprint of the menu by 20% without significant negative effects on these outcomes. Although students recognised that red meat has a higher carbon footprint than vegetarian food, they described their food choices as guided primarily by taste, satiety and familiarity, and expressed slightly stronger support for low-carbon recipes than for all-vegetarian days. Public support for such measures was around neutral: significantly higher than for a tax on high-emission foods, but lower than for subsidies and labelling. Municipal strategies primarily sought to reduce emissions by changing meal composition and presentation. Their main potential beyond school therefore appears to lie in repeated exposure to low-carbon meals, which may build familiarity, habits and norms.Overall, the thesis shows that school meal climate policies can reduce the carbon footprint of public meals without significantly undermining student acceptance, particularly when changes fit students’ expectations of an acceptable meal. The findings raise questions about how quickly and visibly changes should be introduced, and whether targets should consider consumption outside school. School meals may contribute to wider shifts towards low-carbon food consumption alongside other policies, but how school meal climate policies can best be designed for this remains to be examined.

title: Production Cost Efficiency, Profit Maximization, and Input Substitution in the Manufacturing Industry: A Narrative Review
summary: Global manufacturing industries face profound structural transformations driven by robotic automation, relative factor-price volatility, rising product-market markups, and stringent decarbonization mandates. Although extensive empirical and
content: Global manufacturing industries face profound structural transformations driven by robotic automation, relative factor-price volatility, rising product-market markups, and stringent decarbonization mandates. Although extensive empirical and theoretical literatures have investigated production cost efficiency, profit maximization, and input substitution individually, these research streams remain largely fragmented across industrial organization, macroeconomics, and productivity econometrics. This article presents a comprehensive narrative review synthesizing foundational duality axioms and recent empirical breakthroughs published between 2014 and 2026 across Capital–Labor–Energy–Materials (KLEM) manufacturing systems. Following a structured narrative review protocol, we critically evaluate four thematic domains: the shift from Cobb–Douglas and symmetric Constant Elasticity of Substitution (CES) functions to flexible translog and task-based automation architectures; micro-versus-macro empirical estimates of input substitution elasticities (where plant-level capital–labor complementarity, 0.40 ≤ σ ≤ 0.50, coexists with higher industry reallocation elasticities, σ ≈ 0.70); stochastic frontier decompositions of technical and shadow-price allocative cost inefficiency; and the divergence between cost minimization and variable profit maximization under rising market power and financial frictions. We conclude with an integrative methodological synthesis and a future research agenda for industrial economists.

title: Giải pháp thúc đẩy chuyển đổi kép tại Việt Nam
source: Tạp chí Kinh tế và Phát triển
summary: Chuyển đổi kép, với sự kết hợp giữa chuyển đổi số và chuyển đổi xanh, đang trở thành xu hướng phát triển chiến lược của nhiều quốc gia trong bối cảnh biến đổi khí hậu và quá trình số hóa nền kinh tế diễn ra ngày càng sâu rộng. Nhiều quốc gi
content: Chuyển đổi kép, với sự kết hợp giữa chuyển đổi số và chuyển đổi xanh, đang trở thành xu hướng phát triển chiến lược của nhiều quốc gia trong bối cảnh biến đổi khí hậu và quá trình số hóa nền kinh tế diễn ra ngày càng sâu rộng. Nhiều quốc gia và tổ chức quốc tế đã coi chuyển đổi kép là nền tảng của mô hình tăng trưởng bền vững, trong đó chuyển đổi xanh đóng vai trò định hướng nhằm giảm phát thải carbon, sử dụng hiệu quả tài nguyên và thúc đẩy phát triển kinh tế tuần hoàn, còn chuyển đổi số đóng vai trò công cụ quan trọng giúp tối ưu hóa quản lý tài nguyên, nâng cao hiệu quả sản xuất và thúc đẩy đổi mới sáng tạo. Tại Việt Nam, chuyển đổi xanh và chuyển đổi số là hai trong bốn chuyển đổi đóng vai trò trung tâm trong quá trình chuyển đổi mô hình tăng trưởng, và đang được thúc đẩy mạnh mẽ thông qua các chiến lược quốc gia về chuyển đổi số và tăng trưởng xanh. Nghiên cứu dưới đây sử dụng kết hợp phương pháp định tính và định lượng, gồm tổng quan tài liệu, phân tích kinh nghiệm quốc tế, khảo sát thực tế doanh nghiệp và tham vấn chuyên gia để đánh giá quá trình thực hiện chuyển đổi kép tại Việt Nam. Kết quả cho thấy Việt Nam đã đạt được một số kết quả tích cực trong từng quá trình chuyển đổi số và chuyển đổi xanh, song mức độ gắn kết giữa hai quá trình còn hạn chế; do đó, cần tăng cường tích hợp theo hướng chuyển đổi kép nhằm phát huy hiệu ứng cộng hưởng trong nâng cao năng suất, giảm phát thải và đổi mới mô hình tăng trưởng.

title: Biogenic Carboxylation of Granular Activated Carbon via Citrus aurantiifolia Juice for Fluoride Removal
summary: Abstract Excess fluoride (F⁻) in potable water matrices poses a critical global public health threat, including endemic dental and skeletal fluorosis across vulnerable populations. Conventional defluoridation techniques like electrocoagulat
content: Abstract Excess fluoride (F⁻) in potable water matrices poses a critical global public health threat, including endemic dental and skeletal fluorosis across vulnerable populations. Conventional defluoridation techniques like electrocoagulation and ion exchange are frequently constrained by prohibitive operational cost, complex synthesis protocols, and infrastructure limitations in decentralized settings. Herein, we demonstrate a surface functionalization approach for granular activated carbon (GAC) using raw Citrus aurantiifolia (lime) juice as a naturally derived, citric-acid-rich modifying agent. The procedure employs food-grade, non-hazardous materials as an alternative to conventional analytical-grade chemical reagents. Following modification, surface carboxyl-group concentrations increased from 1.26 mmol/g for GAC to 1.98 mmol/g for lime-modified GAC (LGAC) and 1.85 mmol/g for citric acid modified GAC (CAGAC). XPS showed a corresponding increase in surface oxygen content, from 5.92 at% (GAC) to 12.29 at% (CAGAC) and 21.28 at% (LGAC), with distinct C–O and O–C = O contributions on LGAC. Despite a 47% reduction in BET surface area, LGAC exhibited an empirical maximum monolayer adsorption capacity (q max ) of 1.63 mg/g, making its thermodynamic performance statistically identical ( p > 0.05) to CAGAC (1.65 mg/g) and yielding > 85% enhancement over unmodified GAC (0.88 mg/g). Geochemical speciation modeling (PHREEQC) further elucidated a possible immobilization pathway in LGAC via localized aqueous metal-F⁻ complexation dynamics, which were absent in synthetic CAGAC systems. Robust sorption kinetics were maintained across environmentally pertinent pH range (pH 4.0–8.0) and under competitive ionic strength conditions with co-existing groundwater anions. Fixed-bed continuous-flow experiments with multicomponent synthetic groundwater showed that LGAC’s column capacity was 26% higher than that of GAC and ~ 89% of that of CAGAC. These findings validate Citrus aurantiifolia juice as a food-grade, bio-derived modifier, thereby lowering synthesis barriers and offering a practical approach for point-of-use (POU) defluoridation in resource-constrained settings.

title: Modular engineering of aromatic metabolism in Corynebacterium glutamicum enables protocatechuic acid and gallic acid production
summary: Protocatechuic acid (PCA) and gallic acid (GA) are valuable phenolic compounds with diverse pharmacological activities, including antioxidant and antitumor properties, and have broad applications in the food, cosmetic, chemical, and pharmac
content: Protocatechuic acid (PCA) and gallic acid (GA) are valuable phenolic compounds with diverse pharmacological activities, including antioxidant and antitumor properties, and have broad applications in the food, cosmetic, chemical, and pharmaceutical industries. However, the industrial production of these compounds remains limited by the insufficient performance of current microbial cell factories, resulting in low productivity and high manufacturing costs. Here, an efficient biosynthetic platform based on Corynebacterium glutamicum was systematically established for the production of PCA and GA. Through reconstruction of the PCA biosynthetic pathway, elimination of competing branches in the shikimate pathway, enhancement of the key rate-limiting enzyme, and modulation of the glucose uptake system to increase phosphoenolpyruvate supply, metabolic flux was effectively redirected toward PCA accumulation, resulting in the engineered strain PCA16 achieving a PCA titer of 19.8 g/L in shake-flask fermentation. Building on this platform, GA biosynthesis was established by introducing a mutant pobA from Pseudomonas aeruginosa and further strengthening the shikimate pathway, enabling strain GA06 to produce 7.86 g/L GA in shake-flask fermentation. Upon scale-up in a 5 L bioreactor, GA production was further increased to 25.66 g/L, representing the highest reported titer for GA production using C. glutamicum to date. Overall, this work demonstrates the strong potential of C. glutamicum as a robust microbial chassis for efficient production of PCA and GA, and provides a versatile platform for the biosynthesis of PCA-derived aromatic compounds.

title: Hybrid Markov Regime-Switching and Hurdle modeling of last-mile livestock logistics in Ukraine under systemic volatility
summary: Abstract This study examines the transformation of last-mile logistics in Ukraine’s livestock supply chains under conditions of prolonged systemic volatility and infrastructure disruption. A hybrid analytical framework is proposed that inte
content: Abstract This study examines the transformation of last-mile logistics in Ukraine’s livestock supply chains under conditions of prolonged systemic volatility and infrastructure disruption. A hybrid analytical framework is proposed that integrates Random Forest Recursive Feature Elimination (RF-RFE) for preliminary predictor screening, a two-state Markov Regime-Switching (MRS) model for identifying latent logistics regimes, and a two-part Hurdle model for separately estimating disruption probability and conditional freight-cost intensity. The empirical analysis uses a verified monthly panel dataset covering 2023–2025 across three contrasting regional logistics nodes - Kyiv, Vinnytsia, and Lviv - and incorporates energy, security, market, transport, and infrastructure-related indicators. The MRS results identify two statistically distinct and persistent freight-cost regimes, with the systemic-crisis regime characterized by a 21.8% higher mean Freight Cost Per Ton and a longer expected duration than the operational-stability regime. The Hurdle estimates show that Security Alerts and Power Outage Hours are positively associated with the probability of logistics disruption, while Power Outage Hours and Fuel Price Volatility are positively associated with conditional freight-cost intensity; regional comparisons further reveal heterogeneous exposure to systemic shocks. Counterfactual technological scenarios further indicate that combining AI-assisted dynamic routing with decentralized autonomous and light electric transport solutions could reduce the estimated sensitivity of freight costs to energy disruptions by approximately 24.2%. The findings demonstrate the value of combining latent-regime identification, sequential disruption modeling, and technological scenario analysis for assessing the resilience of livestock last-mile logistics under persistent infrastructure and security shocks.

title: Scalability Scope and Limitations of Potential Innovations and Renewable Energy Sources to Sustain Small Holder Farming Families and Various Ecosystems in India-Local to Global Relevance
summary: The soil, water and air pollution are posing a huge threat to soil, underground water aquifers, oceans, various ecosystems, food chain, human, animals (land, aquatic both), various species health and our environment. Efficiently recapturing
content: The soil, water and air pollution are posing a huge threat to soil, underground water aquifers, oceans, various ecosystems, food chain, human, animals (land, aquatic both), various species health and our environment. Efficiently recapturing carbon emissions through agroforestry, increasing area under forests along with increasing the use of renewable sources in hybrid mode can put a halt on this pattern. Biogas/Biofuels along with necessary engine changes, can control vehicular carbon emissions to a great extent. There is need to increase use of vermi-compost, in-situ crop residue management techniques, green manuring, farm yard/poultry manures, pulse-cereal intercropping/diversification, eco-friendly integrated pest management techniques, biodegradable plastic, jute bags and use of crop residue biochar, sunflower seed husk and its biochar as a bioremediation to treat industrial waste with heavy metals. A new and innovative eco-friendly Parkash Bioherbal water reservoir is proposed. Neem, Moringa oleifera and seaweed products can be used as biopesticides, bioinsecticides, biofertilizers to enhance crop growth in an organic way. The technologies and implementation to minimize and treat industrial/domestic waste at source before discharge into the marine system are urgently required so as to enhance the oceans’ capacity to maintain carbon cycle.

title: Socioeconomic, Environmental, and Digital Determinants of Life Expectancy in Andorra: A Comparative Analysis with EU and EFTA Countries
summary: Abstract Background European life expectancy is driven by complex socioeconomic, environmental, and digital determinants. This ecological study provides a macro-regional assessment of European longevity across 32 nations (EU27, EFTA, and An
content: Abstract Background European life expectancy is driven by complex socioeconomic, environmental, and digital determinants. This ecological study provides a macro-regional assessment of European longevity across 32 nations (EU27, EFTA, and Andorra), establishing an optimized predictive framework to isolate key structural drivers of population lifespans, with a specific focus on the unique sociodemographic position of the Principality of Andorra. Methods Utilizing a 5-year post-pandemic dataset (2020–2024), feature selection was conducted via LASSO regression paired with variance inflation factor diagnostics to eliminate severe multicollinearity. An optimized multivariate ordinary least squares regression model was fitted to identify independent structural predictors of life expectancy. Additionally, Hierarchical Cluster Analysis using Ward’s minimum variance method was applied to classify nations based on shared socioeconomic and demographic profiles. Results This research reveals a novel, previously undescribed statistical relationship correlating country-level digital literacy indicators to extended life expectancy. The optimized multivariate ordinary least squares model explained 95.9% of cross-national longevity variance (adjusted R 2 = 0.959). The super-aging index demonstrated the strongest positive association with life expectancy, whereas a widening sex-specific longevity gap and ambient sulfur dioxide pollution presented the primary negative constraints. Andorra occupies the leading edge of this health landscape, sustaining a 5-year stationary mean life expectancy of 83.68 years (behind only Switzerland and Liechtenstein), while Andorran women achieve the highest life expectancy at birth across the European continent (86.20 years). Territorially, Andorra exhibits unique sociodemographic characteristics: while its low environmental emissions, high labor participation, and digital assets act as effective public health safeguards, baseline data reveal elevated income inequality alongside record-low demographic dependency ratios. Hierarchical Cluster Analysis further demonstrates that European small nations share a cohesive regional branch defined by unique scale-related structural profiles, suggesting that small nations can offer vital paradigm models for optimized health infrastructure. Conclusions European longevity is driven by demographic expansion and air quality. In addition, country digital literacy is newly correlated to extended population lifespans. Microstates like Andorra, at the forefront of European longevity, leverage scale-related structural advantages and specifical challenges. Small nations offer vital paradigm models for optimized health infrastructure.

title: Green Growth or Growth First? Carbon Intensity and Provincial Development Paths in Vietnam
source: International Journal of Advanced Multidisciplinary Research and Studies
summary: Vietnam has committed to net-zero emissions by 2050 while aiming to reach high-income status by 2045. Whether these two goals can be pursued together depends heavily on what happens inside its provinces, where growth is planned, power plant
content: Vietnam has committed to net-zero emissions by 2050 while aiming to reach high-income status by 2045. Whether these two goals can be pursued together depends heavily on what happens inside its provinces, where growth is planned, power plants are sited and industrial parks compete for investment. This paper documents the current situation using newly available satellite- and asset-based emission estimates from Climate TRACE for all 63 pre-2025 provinces (2021–2024), combined with provincial GRDP and population statistics and national series from the Global Carbon Project and the World Bank. The analysis is descriptive and does not estimate causal relationships. At the national level, CO₂ emissions rose almost sevenfold between 2000 and 2025, faster than real GDP, and coal’s share of fossil CO₂ climbed from 38% to 58%. Only after 2020 did the economy move into weak decoupling (elasticity 0.22). At the provincial level, the carbon intensity of output differs by a factor of 46, from 8 t CO₂e per billion VND in Bắc Ninh to 368 t in Bình Thuận. Ten provinces emit 51.5% of gross greenhouse gases while producing 34.5% of output. A simple income-by-intensity typology identifies four development paths. Twenty “cleaner growth” provinces generate 62.4% of GRDP with a quarter of emissions. Twelve “growth first” provinces, mostly hosts of coal power, steel, cement and coal mining, account for 51.0% of emissions but only 16.2% of GRDP. The remaining provinces are either carbon-intensive and lagging, often because of rice-paddy methane or resource industries, or low-carbon by default. Emissions rose fastest between 2021 and 2024 in some cleaner-growth provinces where new coal units came online. The results suggest that Vietnam’s low-carbon transition is, in practice, a question of a small number of host provinces, and that provincial green-growth targets should distinguish between emissions generated for local value added and emissions generated to supply the national grid.

title: Guest editorial: Geopolitical risk: current knowledge and future directions
summary: Financial markets and firms increasingly operate in an environment shaped by geopolitical tensions, including trade conflicts, military confrontations, sanctions, and strategic decoupling [1].These events introduce uncertainty that is disti
content: Financial markets and firms increasingly operate in an environment shaped by geopolitical tensions, including trade conflicts, military confrontations, sanctions, and strategic decoupling [1].These events introduce uncertainty that is distinct from traditional macroeconomic shocks because they originate in political interactions between states rather than domestic policy choices.Understanding how this geopolitical risk is transmitted into financial markets and corporate decision-making has therefore become a central question in modern finance.This special issue identifies current trends in geopolitical risk, introduces cutting-edge research on the topic, and explores the most impactful avenues for future research.Geopolitical risk is a broad topic encompassing economic and political uncertainty, as well as trade policy.Firms and other market participants respond to uncertainty by cultivating political connections, adjusting investment activity, and seeking government support.The articles in this issue provide a view into this diverse spectrum.Tarkom and Graham (2026) develop a novel measure of public economic sentiment and show that lower sentiment is associated with lower firm investment.They note that uncertainty over sentiment reduces a firm's perceived growth opportunities and lowers demand for both equity and debt financing.Kothari and Ferris (2026) examine corporate investment from a different perspective by generating AI agents that mimic S&P 500 CEOs.These surveyed CEO proxies view corporate political contributions as strategic investments.Nahidi (2026) explores the possible use of a US blockchain-based sovereign wealth fund (SWF).Nahidi notes that an SWF with decisions recorded publicly on a blockchain can bolster fiscal credibility in the eyes of investors.Evenett et al. (2026) find that US pension funds also appear to adjust their capital allocations in response to protectionist activity (tariffs and subsidies), reducing investment in countries with more distorted relationships with the USA.Firms have several techniques for reducing exposure to geopolitical risk.Fudali and Pérez-Amuedo (2026) show that subsidy recipient firms experience lower idiosyncratic volatility in the future.These subsidies can come from the local, state, or federal levels.Subsidies often reduce volatility by providing a more consistent cash flow stream than firms could generate from other sources.Baran and Tamanna Khan (2026) note that firms also respond to increased uncertainty by delaying adjustments to assets and employment.Politically active firms are the most likely to delay expansions during periods of high uncertainty.To offset portfolio volatility during chaotic periods, diversification into lowly correlated or safe-haven assets has long been used.Hossain et al.
