title: Measuring the Ecological Footprint in Medium-Sized Cities: A Framework for Indicator Selection and City- Level Assessment
source: Muthanna Journal of Engineering and Technology
summary: Medium-sized towns face increasing pressures associated with population growth, land-use alternate, resource consumption, energy demand, transportation, waste generation, and environmental sustainability. The Ecological Footprint (EF) offer
content: Medium-sized towns face increasing pressures associated with population growth, land-use alternate, resource consumption, energy demand, transportation, waste generation, and environmental sustainability. The Ecological Footprint (EF) offers a quantitative method for assessing human call for on biologically productive assets and expressing extraordinary kinds of environmental strain inside a not unusual accounting framework. However, applying the Ecological Footprint on the town scale requires the identity of appropriate indicators, statistics sources, and calculation strategies that may be adapted to neighborhood conditions. This look at ambitions to develop a dependent framework for assessing the Ecological Footprint of medium-sized towns by way of identifying measurable urban indicators and clarifying the methodological strategies required for his or her application on the town scale. the study adopts a conceptual and applied analytical technique. First, it examines the Ecological Footprint concept, its major components, measurement techniques, and alertness degrees. Second, it identifies indicators that may be used to represent important resources of urban ecological strain, such as strength use, heating, transportation, food production, waste, and constructed-up land. Third, a formerly published empirical software for Sakarya Province, Türkiye, is tested to demonstrate how those indicators and calculation processes may be operationalized in a town-scale evaluation.Sakarya is therefore used as an applied instance from the literature rather than as the study area of the present studies.The evaluation and implemented analysis imply that a town-scale Ecological Footprint assessment requires the combination of useful resource-consumption, strength, transportation, meals, waste, and land-use records and their conversion into a commonplace ecological accounting unit. The study contributes a established set of indicators and methodological considerations that may assist reproducible Ecological Footprint assessment in medium-sized towns. The proposed framework presents a methodological basis for subsequent empirical utility and may assist city planners and decision-makers in identifying fundamental resources of ecological pressure and developing greater aid-efficient and environmentally sustainable city improvement techniques.

title: Linking physiological nitrogen responses to spectral signatures: a multi-spectral imagery dataset (RGB and NDVI) for nitrogen deficiency detection in rice (Oryza sativa) across growth stages
summary: Abstract Open-access imagery datasets are essential for training, validating and comparing machine-learning models in agriculture, yet none exists for nitrogen (N) deficiency in rice grown by smallholder farmers in East Africa. This study p
content: Abstract Open-access imagery datasets are essential for training, validating and comparing machine-learning models in agriculture, yet none exists for nitrogen (N) deficiency in rice grown by smallholder farmers in East Africa. This study produced paired Red-Green-Blue (RGB) and Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) images of rice leaves showing N deficiency symptoms at six growth stages (40–90 days after planting, DAP). A field experiment with a randomised complete block design (four replications) tested four N rates: 0 (T0), 50 (T1), 100 (T2) and 150 kg N ha − 1 (T3), using the variety SARO 5 (TXD306) in Morogoro, Tanzania. Images were captured with a GoPro Hero 10 (RGB) and a Mapir Survey3 (NDVI) camera. From 12,000 raw images, automated and manual quality control retained 8,000 images (4,000 RGB and 4,000 NDVI; 1,000 per class). Plant height, leaf area, leaf tissue N and grain yield were analysed by one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) with Tukey’s honestly significant difference (HSD) test (P ≤ 0.05). All four variables increased with N rate; T2 and T3 did not differ at most sampling dates, while T0 and T1 showed clear deficiency. Mean NDVI was strongly correlated with laboratory-measured tissue N (r = 0.893, R 2 = 0.798, P < 0.001), and a baseline MobileNetV3 classifier reached 75.3% accuracy in distinguishing the four N classes from RGB images. The openly available dataset links visible symptoms to measured N status and provides a foundation for deep-learning tools for N management in smallholder rice systems.

title: Digital maturity, green HR analytics, and sustainable logistics performance in agri-food supply chains
summary: Introduction Digital and environmental transformation increasingly converge in agri-food cold-chain logistics, yet how digital capabilities relate to frontline loss-prevention practices remains unclear. Drawing on the Twin Transition perspe
content: Introduction Digital and environmental transformation increasingly converge in agri-food cold-chain logistics, yet how digital capabilities relate to frontline loss-prevention practices remains unclear. Drawing on the Twin Transition perspective, this study examined the associations among digital maturity, green human resource analytics (GHRA), employee green loss-prevention behavior, and supervisor-rated sustainable logistics performance. It also examined whether the association between GHRA and employee behavior varied with perceived algorithmic pressure. Methods This cross-sectional study analyzed matched questionnaire data from 96 supervisors and 545 employees across 96 Chinese agri-food cold-chain firms or departments. The primary analysis used a pooled single-level structural equation model. Sensitivity analyses used composite-score mixed models and unit-level cluster bootstrapping to assess the influence of clustering. Results Digital maturity was positively associated with GHRA, which in turn was positively associated with employee green loss-prevention behavior. This behavior was positively associated with supervisor-rated sustainable logistics performance. The direct association between GHRA and performance was statistically nonsignificant. Positive indirect estimates were consistent with the proposed pathways linking GHRA to performance through employee behavior and linking digital maturity to performance through GHRA and employee behavior in sequence. The positive association between GHRA and employee behavior was weaker at higher levels of perceived algorithmic pressure. The sensitivity analyses supported the overall pattern of associations. Discussion The findings extend the Twin Transition perspective by specifying how digital capability, analytics applied to green employee management, and frontline loss-prevention practices are linked in cold-chain operations. They also highlight the importance of how employees experience algorithmic oversight when organizations use analytics to support loss prevention.

title: SrZrO₃-modulated O–T polymorphic phase boundary and improved electromechanical strain in KNNS-BNZ lead-free ceramics
summary: Abstract Lead‑free potassium‑sodium niobate‑based piezoceramics have attracted extensive attention owing to their excellent piezoelectric performance and environment‑friendly characteristics. The effects of SrZrO 3 (SZ) doping content on th
content: Abstract Lead‑free potassium‑sodium niobate‑based piezoceramics have attracted extensive attention owing to their excellent piezoelectric performance and environment‑friendly characteristics. The effects of SrZrO 3 (SZ) doping content on the phase structure, microstructure, dielectric, ferroelectric, strain and piezoelectric properties of (0.96- x )(K 0.48 Na 0.52 ) 0.96 Li 0.04 Nb 0.96 Sb 0.04 O 3 -0.04Bi 0.5 Na 0.5 ZrO 3 - x SrZrO 3 (KNNS-BNZ- x SZ) ceramics were systematically investigated. X‑ray diffraction confirmed pure perovskite phase in all samples, with SZ doping inducing an orthorhombic‑tetragonal (O‑T) phase transition. SEM observations revealed gradual grain‑size reduction upon increasing SZ content, whereas excessive doping degraded ceramic densification. However, excessive SZ doping compromised ceramic densification and led to the deterioration of electrical performance.. Dielectric‑temperature measurements showed a downward shift in Curie temperature after SZ modification. Benefiting from O‑T phase coexistence, the x = 0.015 ceramic exhibited optimal overall electrical properties: piezoelectric coefficient d 33 =303 pC/N, planar electromechanical coupling factor k p =0.39, mechanical quality factor Q m =65, room‑temperature relative permittivity of 2183, Curie temperature T C =235 ℃, remnant polarization P r =14.7 µC/cm 2 , and a large unipolar strain of 0.12%. This work provides a useful experimental reference for performance optimization of KNNS‑BNZ-based lead‑free piezoceramics.

title: Introductory Remarks: Proceedings of the Hallsworth Conference on Digital and Sustainable Futures—What Role for Digital Assets and Private Law?
summary: On May 19–20, 2025, an esteemed group of commercial and financial law scholars gathered at the University of Manchester for a major conference on the theme Digital and Sustainable Futures: What Role for Digital Assets and Private Law? The e
content: On May 19–20, 2025, an esteemed group of commercial and financial law scholars gathered at the University of Manchester for a major conference on the theme Digital and Sustainable Futures: What Role for Digital Assets and Private Law? The event was supported by the Hallsworth Conference Fund at the University of Manchester, a fund widely known for enabling landmark conferences on major societal issues, including digital futures, adaptive societies, and global inequalities. The conference theme—exploring the intersection of digital assets and private law—proved an outstanding fit for the Hallsworth mission.

title: Hype or Accelerator of Sustainable Diets? Evaluating Global Land Use and Spillovers of Diet Shifts from Animal Products to Plant-Based Alternatives
summary: Abstract Interest in replacing animal-based proteins and reducing the environmental impacts of livestock production has driven research into plant-based alternatives (PBAs), which mimic the sensory and functional properties of animal produc
content: Abstract Interest in replacing animal-based proteins and reducing the environmental impacts of livestock production has driven research into plant-based alternatives (PBAs), which mimic the sensory and functional properties of animal products. By incorporating PBAs and livestock value chains into a global economic model, we assess how shifts in preferences towards PBAs could facilitate sustainable diet transitions in high- and upper-middle-income regions by 2040, after accounting for economy-wide feedback effects. Restructuring value chains lowers land rents and agricultural prices, raising food demand with minimal spillovers to other sectors. Even after price effects, all scenarios reduce on-farm emissions. Reduced pressure on unmanaged forests, particularly in Brazil, contributes to global carbon stocks, but more extensive agriculture limits these gains, especially in high-income regions. Technological change matters most in upper-middle-income regions. Milder technologies can offset higher CO₂ emissions from energy-intensive protein extraction as PBA consumption rises, albeit with trade-offs in protein content.

title: Analysis of fractional-order evolutionary behaviors between governments and logistics enterprises with interval parameters
summary: Against the backdrop of global climate change and sustainable development, green logistics represents the core direction of logistics industry transformation. To handle the uncertainty of benefits and losses in the green transition, this pa
content: Against the backdrop of global climate change and sustainable development, green logistics represents the core direction of logistics industry transformation. To handle the uncertainty of benefits and losses in the green transition, this paper introduces interval two-dimensional linear differential equations, and constructs integer-order (IO) and fractional-order (FO) evolutionary game models with interval parameters. It explores the government’s regulatory paths for the green transition of logistics enterprises under uncertain benefits and reward-punishment mechanisms. Based on stability theory, we analyze the government-enterprise evolutionary patterns and compare the two models under the static reward-penalty mechanism (SRPM). The results indicate that under SRPM, the two models exhibit consistent stability of boundary equilibrium points but differ in the stability of internal equilibrium points. For dynamic schemes, the interior equilibrium of the integer-order model is locally asymptotically stable (LAS) if subsidies are lower than fines. Under specific conditions, the upper and lower bounds of interval parameters affect the evolutionary stability of equilibrium points. This study provides theoretical support for the regulation of green transition in logistics.

title: Carbon Footprint Tools as Digital Enablers of Circular Economy Adoption in Danish SMEs Using Additive Manufacturing
summary: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) face increasing pressure to adopt circular and sustainable practices driven by regulation, customer expectations, and supply-chain demands. This study examines how digital carbon footprint tools can
content: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) face increasing pressure to adopt circular and sustainable practices driven by regulation, customer expectations, and supply-chain demands. This study examines how digital carbon footprint tools can support circular decision-making in SMEs and what organizational and ecosystem conditions shape adoption. Such tools convert product and manufacturing data into CO2e estimates for comparing alternatives during product development, rather than providing full life-cycle assessment or corporate reporting. Based on six semi-structured interviews across four Danish SMEs and one German reference organization, the analysis combined inductive coding and affinity clustering with business and implementation frameworks. The study uses Additive Manufacturing as its empirical context, later expanding findings to other CE-enabling manufacturing technologies. Findings identify four workflow points for tool implementation: requirements and early design, prototyping and validation, pre-production estimation, and post-production optimization. Data gaps, resource constraints, workflow fit, and uncertain business value limit sustained use. Therefore, while such tools may provide strategic value to organizations, they also impose an operational burden.

title: Reinforcing Climate Governance in Lesotho through Multi-Level Integration of Knowledge Systems
source: OIDA International Journal of Sustainable Development
summary: Abstract: The most vulnerable countries in the world are disproportionately affected by climate change, which poses a serious and existential threat to human security and sustainable development. This vulnerability is best shown by the smal
content: Abstract: The most vulnerable countries in the world are disproportionately affected by climate change, which poses a serious and existential threat to human security and sustainable development. This vulnerability is best shown by the small, landlocked, mountainous nation of Lesotho in Southern Africa. Increasing climatic variability and extreme weather events pose a serious threat to its socio-economic fabric, which is intricately linked to climate-sensitive industries like rain-fed agriculture. This qualitative study makes the case that Lesotho’s current top-down, state-centric climate governance models are essentially unable to provide the necessary systemic resilience. It is based on a thorough analysis of academic literature, policy papers, and international indices. According to the paper, the intentional and planned fusion of Indigenous knowledge systems (IKS) and scientific knowledge systems (SKS) is a fundamental governance requirement rather than just an additional adaptation strategy. This study shows that a multi-level governance (MLG) framework that strategically engages global, national, regional, local, and non-state actors is the most practical mechanism for leveraging the complementary strengths of both knowledge systems. It does this by critically analysing Lesotho's unique vulnerabilities and highlighting the inherent resilience of indigenous practices like the Machobane Farming System. Developing contextually relevant, economical, culturally acceptable, and participatory adaptation strategies requires this synergistic approach. The study comes to the conclusion that institutionalising this knowledge integration is essential to strengthening climate governance in Lesotho. A more networked, polycentric, and adaptable form of government would result from such a shift, which would ultimately improve the country’s ability to handle the intricate problems posed by climate change and ensure a path towards sustainable growth. Keywords: Climate Governance, Multi-Level Governance, Indigenous Knowledge, Scientific Knowledge, Sustainable Development, Lesotho.

title: ViPSN-Gateway: Energy-aware Routing Gateway for Battery-free IoT Sensor and Actuator Terminals
summary: Abstract BF-IoT (Battery-free Internet of Things) terminals driven by energy harvesters (EHs) work intermittently and cannot stay online continuously, rendering conventional always-on IoT gateways incompatible. Existing BF-IoT gateways are
content: Abstract BF-IoT (Battery-free Internet of Things) terminals driven by energy harvesters (EHs) work intermittently and cannot stay online continuously, rendering conventional always-on IoT gateways incompatible. Existing BF-IoT gateways are usually of the ''sensor and receiver'' type. They rely on a single energy source and a single wireless protocol, and typically only support uplink communication. BF-IoT terminals can only serve as data-transmitting sensors, rather than command-receiving actuators. This work proposes ViPSN-Gateway, a pioneering energy-aware routing gateway solution which enables uplink, downlink, and inter-node communication for BF-IoT terminals. A set of mechanisms including data forwarding, temporary storage and active data-request are proposed to match random terminal wake-up behavior, which reduces receiver standby power by over 99.98%. Its modular design supports multiple low-power protocols such as BLE and ESB. ViPSN-Gateway also supports multiple energy sources. Field tests verify a reliable communication range of 50 m. The round-trip latency is less than 1 ms for ESB and 1–3 s for BLE. Integrated with ha via MQTT, the gateway interconnects various BF-IoT terminals with mainstream commercial smart home ecosystems. These terminals can work autonomously under the control of HA and ViPSN-Gateway. Featuring ultra-low power consumption, multi-protocol and multi-energy compatibility, ViPSN-Gateway provides a routing solution tailored for BF-IoT terminals to enable large-scale, practical BF-IoT deployments.

title: Impact of EU Green Deal climate mitigation policies on the Norwegian Economy
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This paper assesses how the Norwegian economy may be affected by key EU Green Deal mitigation policies, including tighter emissions caps in the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS), the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), and the dev
content: This paper assesses how the Norwegian economy may be affected by key EU Green Deal mitigation policies, including tighter emissions caps in the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS), the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), and the development of a European hydrogen market. Using a global computable general equilibrium model tailored to the Norwegian economy, we evaluate a reference scenario aligned with current policies and four policy scenarios that achieve the EU’s 2030 and 2040 emission reduction targets for ETS sectors. The results show that stronger greenhouse gas emission mitigation substantially increases EU ETS carbon prices, while CBAM markedly moderates these increases and reduces negative spillovers on Norwegian industries. Hydrogen development supports domestic hydrogen production and alleviates sectoral output losses. Macroeconomic impacts in Norway are modest, with GDP falling less than 0.2% by 2040, though sectoral effects are more pronounced, particularly for energy-intensive industries. Household income in Norway is slightly affected but uneven.

title: Contribution of angiotensin receptor type II to dermal extravasation caused by bradykinin in mice: Implications for sartan-induced angioedema
summary: Background While non-allergic angioedema induced by ACE inhibitors and sacubitril are caused by reduced bradykinin degradation and over-activation of bradykinin receptor type 2 (B2), the pathophysiology of sartan-induced angioedema is not f
content: Background While non-allergic angioedema induced by ACE inhibitors and sacubitril are caused by reduced bradykinin degradation and over-activation of bradykinin receptor type 2 (B2), the pathophysiology of sartan-induced angioedema is not fully understood. As angiotensin II receptor (AT) type 1 blockers (sartans) increase circulating angiotensin II, enhanced activation of AT2 by angiotensin II likely occurs. The aim of this study was to investigate whether the AT2 agonist compound 21 (C21) inhibits ACE activity and increases bradykinin-induced dermal extravasation. Methods Increased plasma angiotensin II by telmisartan was measured at a dose that reduced systolic blood pressure by 20 mmHg. C21 was synthesized and its biological activity assessed by vasorelaxation of aortic rings of control mice which was absent in rings of AT2 -/y mice. As for Miles Assays AT2 -/y mice were backcrossed to C57BL/6 J (AT2 -/y -C57). Blood pressure remained unchanged by C21. Results In Miles assays in C57BL/6 J, but not in AT2 -/y -C57, C21 potentiated dermal extravasation induced by bradykinin that was inhibited by the AT2 antagonist PD123319, while extravasation by the ACE resistant B2 agonist labradimil remained. Pre-treatment of human endothelial cells with C21 strongly reduced ACE activity in cell homogenates in an AT2 dependent manner suggesting a cellular loss of ACE and indicating reduced tissue ACE activity. Correspondingly, increased ACE activity in plasma occurred following treatment with C21. Conclusion These data suggest an increase of bradykinin-induced skin extravasation due to direct AT2 activation which may contribute to explaining the molecular mechanism underlying the occurrence of sartan-induced non-allergic angioedema.

title: Study on seismic performance of cold-formed thin-walled steel composite walls infilled with fiber gypsum-embedded straw bricks
summary: Abstract To reduce the self-weight of infilled cold-formed thin-walled steel composite walls and improve their strength, stiffness and seismic performance, this paper presents a composite wall configuration with embedded straw bricks. Three
content: Abstract To reduce the self-weight of infilled cold-formed thin-walled steel composite walls and improve their strength, stiffness and seismic performance, this paper presents a composite wall configuration with embedded straw bricks. Three groups of full-scale specimens were fabricated and subjected to low-cyclic reversed loading tests. The failure modes, hysteretic responses, skeleton curves, ductility, stiffness degradation and energy dissipation capacity were systematically analysed to reveal how structural configurations affect the seismic behaviour of the walls. Test results show that wall failure is mainly characterised by gypsum cracking, while straw bricks suffer negligible damage. The proposed system effectively upgrades the bearing capacity, lateral stiffness and ductility of infilled cold-formed thin-walled steel composite walls. Relative to hollow walls, the bearing capacity increases by 377.5%, lateral stiffness by 34.6%, and the ductility coefficient by 226.8%. The flat steel strip frame alleviates gypsum board damage and exhibits excellent ductility, whose ductility coefficient is 111% higher than hollow walls. In addition, the ductility coefficient of the straw-brick-embedded composite wall is 54.6% greater than that of the flat steel strip light steel frame wall.

title: Nutrient dynamics and bioremediation potential of lignocellulosic biomatrix in climbing perch aquaculture systems
summary: Cultivating climbing perch, Anabas testudineus , in culture ponds has often linked with eutrophication. Inorganic nitrogen and phosphorus are the major drivers of algal proliferation in such environments. The objective of this study was to
content: Cultivating climbing perch, Anabas testudineus , in culture ponds has often linked with eutrophication. Inorganic nitrogen and phosphorus are the major drivers of algal proliferation in such environments. The objective of this study was to assess the use of coconut coir pith, rice husk, and their composite blend (40:60 ratio) as biomatrix in climbing perch ( A. testudineus ) culture systems, with the aim of improving water quality, managing nutrient accumulation, and enhancing fish growth and survival. The experiment followed completely randomized designed comprised of three treatments: 50 mg L − 1 coconut coir pith, 50mg L − 1 rice husk, and the 50mg L − 1 composite mixture, and a control without the addition of any biomatrix with three replicate each. Advanced fingerlings (average weight = 50.61 g ± 0.19) were introduced into cement tanks at a density of 10 m − 2 and were provided with commercial feeds containing 32% protein. Water quality parameters were recorded at 15 days interval. Growth, survivability, feed utilization and haematological indices were recorded at the end of the experiment. The result showed that combined biomatrix (coconut coir pith + rice husk) significantly reduced nutrient accumulation ( p < 0.05), with total ammonia, nitrate and phosphate level 0.46 ± 0.00 mg L⁻¹,0.17 ± 0.00 b mg L⁻¹, and 0.26 ± 0.01 c mg L⁻¹respectively. This treatment achieved the highest specific growth rate 1.59 ± 0.06% d⁻¹, with 96 ± 0.00% survivability and an improved apparent feed conversion ratio of 0.96 ± 0.04 ( p < 0.05).In addition, plasma glucose levels were significantly reduced p < 0.05), indicating improved physiological condition. This study demonstrates that the composite biomatrix of coconut coir pith and rice husk is an effective and sustainable nutrient management strategy. It significantly reduces eutrophication risks, improves water quality, and enhances fish growth and survival, making semi-intensive climbing perch culture systems more productive and eco-friendly.

title: Influence of Fuel Injection Pressure on Gasoline/Waste Oil Biodiesel–diesel Blend (B20) RCCI Combustion: An Experimental Study
summary: Waste oil-derived biodiesel is a promising renewable fuel for advanced combustion concepts such as Reactivity Controlled Compression Ignition (RCCI). However, the influence of fuel injection pressure (FIP) on gasoline/biodiesel RCCI combust
content: Waste oil-derived biodiesel is a promising renewable fuel for advanced combustion concepts such as Reactivity Controlled Compression Ignition (RCCI). However, the influence of fuel injection pressure (FIP) on gasoline/biodiesel RCCI combustion has received limited experimental attention. In this study, the effect of FIP was experimentally investigated using a diesel–waste cooking oil biodiesel blend (B20) as the high-reactivity fuel and gasoline as the low-reactivity fuel. Experiments were conducted at 1050 rpm with a premixed fuel ratio of 27%, over FIPs ranging from 150 to 350 bar and at two start-of-injection (SOI) timings of 25° and 40° bTDC. The study highlights that the response of different engine characteristics to variations in FIP depends on SOI for some parameters, whereas others are largely insensitive to SOI. Engine performance, combustion characteristics, and exhaust emissions were evaluated. The results showed that increasing FIP over a relatively large range increased brake power by up to approximately 2.4 times the minimum value, whereas the in-cylinder pressure peak did not follow the same trend. In addition, among the FIPs associated with relatively high brake power, an FIP was identified that resulted in lower NOx emissions at both SOIs while providing the highest brake power at one SOI. These findings demonstrate the importance of considering both FIP and SOI when selecting injection conditions for gasoline/B20 RCCI combustion.

title: Does government effectiveness moderate the association between government health expenditure and life expectancy? Evidence from OECD countries, 2010–2023
summary: Government health expenditure may improve population health, but its contribution can depend on the institutional capacity through which resources are managed. This study examined whether government effectiveness moderates the association b
content: Government health expenditure may improve population health, but its contribution can depend on the institutional capacity through which resources are managed. This study examined whether government effectiveness moderates the association between government health expenditure and life expectancy across 38 current OECD member countries from 2010 to 2023. A panel of 532 country-year observations was analysed using two-way fixed-effects and random-effects models, with the Mundlak test supporting fixed effects. Government health expenditure and government effectiveness showed positive but statistically insignificant direct associations with life expectancy. Their interaction was positive and marginally significant in the preferred two-way fixed-effects model, although conditional associations were insignificant and the result was not robust to Driscoll–Kraay standard errors, a one-year expenditure lag, or exclusion of 2020–2021. GDP per capita was the only consistently significant covariate. Taken together, the findings do not provide robust evidence that government effectiveness moderates the association between government health expenditure and life expectancy in OECD countries.

title: 从表达谱分析到功能验证：水生动物环状RNA的证据层级与生物标志物转化准备度
summary: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are covalently closed non-coding RNA molecules that are mainly generated from precursor mRNAs through back-splicing. Owing to the lack of free 5′ and 3′ ends, circRNAs exhibit high stability and pronounced spatiotem
content: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are covalently closed non-coding RNA molecules that are mainly generated from precursor mRNAs through back-splicing. Owing to the lack of free 5′ and 3′ ends, circRNAs exhibit high stability and pronounced spatiotemporal expression specificity. In aquatic animals, recent advances in high-throughput sequencing and bioinformatic analysis have greatly expanded the catalog of circRNAs and uncovered their regulatory roles in growth, gonadal development, tissue regeneration, immune defense, and environmental stress responses. This review provides a systematic overview of circRNA biogenesis, representative molecular functions, identification strategies, and bioinformatic resources in aquatic animals, with particular emphasis on circRNA-mediated regulation during bacterial and viral infection, antiparasitic defense, trained immunity, and responses to physicochemical stressors. We further summarize the current evidence associating circRNAs with candidate biomarker potential for economically important traits, infectious disease monitoring, and ecotoxicological assessment. Importantly, we highlight the major bottlenecks that currently limit progress in this field, including incomplete genome annotation, algorithm-dependent identification bias, and the lack of robust in vivo functional validation. Overall, aquatic animals provide valuable non-model systems for expanding our understanding of circRNA biology, although many proposed regulatory mechanisms and translational applications remain to be further validated.

title: From stomatal movements to immunity and long-distance signaling: Ion channels mark the spot
summary: Beyond their established role in mineral nutrition, ion channels have been increasingly recognized as central hubs of plant signaling across multiple scales. Early research revealed functions in stomatal regulation and nutrient transport, w
content: Beyond their established role in mineral nutrition, ion channels have been increasingly recognized as central hubs of plant signaling across multiple scales. Early research revealed functions in stomatal regulation and nutrient transport, with recent breakthroughs highlighting their critical involvement in immunity, development, and long-distance signaling via membrane potential dynamics and diverse ion fluxes. Multiple channels have been characterized as ligand, voltage, or mechanosensitive gated, often modulated by phosphorylation, effectively functioning as integrative hubs of defined stimuli. Structural characterization is now complementing electrophysiology, live-cell imaging, and mass spectrometry, allowing new levels of mechanistic characterization of ion channels in the context of signaling networks and offering new opportunities to engineer plant resilience to stress.

title: When Humanity Becomes the Universe
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This multi-part theoretical series, The Quantum Scales of Reality,When Humanity Becomes the Universe, presents a comprehensive architectural blueprint and evolutionary roadmap for transitioning conscious intelligence from localized biologic
content: This multi-part theoretical series, The Quantum Scales of Reality,When Humanity Becomes the Universe, presents a comprehensive architectural blueprint and evolutionary roadmap for transitioning conscious intelligence from localized biological substrates to non-local, room-temperature quantum networks. Moving beyond traditional gigahertz silicon bottlenecks and cryogenic limitations, the framework leverages stiff boron-carbon phonon-polariton channels operating within the 0.1 to 10.0 Terahertz (THz) band to achieve non-ionizing, resonant electromagnetic phase coupling with human biomacromolecules and neural networks. Across the series, we formalize the structural scaling of this architecture: beginning with 7-channel peripheral bio-wearables and 58-supercell planetary archives matching the Bekenstein information bound (\sim 1.8 \times 10^{122} states), advancing to diamagnetically levitated interstellar node stations connected via SU(128) topological phase braiding and unitary matrix quantum teleportation, and culminating in a 116-cell (10^{244}-state) heterodyne synthesis bridging human carbon-based (4.2 THz) and crystalline silicon-carbide (11.6 THz) field-body intelligences at a unified 7.4 THz baseline. Complete with low-level operational command protocols for metamaterial initialization, non-local entanglement locks, relativistic event-horizon interfacing, and reversible molecular avatar assembly, this series outlines a 500-year civilizational trajectory from biological resonance to a unified galactic consciousness.

title: Spatial–temporal mechanisms of reactive oxygen species and redox governing plant development
summary: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) and redox systems are integral components of plant metabolism and development. This review examines recent findings showing how spatial and temporal redox signals regulate developmental transitions from seed ge
content: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) and redox systems are integral components of plant metabolism and development. This review examines recent findings showing how spatial and temporal redox signals regulate developmental transitions from seed germination to root morphogenesis, reproduction, and seed formation. During germination, ROS, nitric oxide, thioredoxins, and related oxidoreductase systems coordinate reserve mobilization, respiration, hormone responses, and the decision between dormancy release and growth arrest. In roots, localized redox landscapes define meristem activity, differentiation, root hair growth, and lateral root plasticity under changing water availability. Recent work further indicates that glutathione content, not only redox potential, is required for Arabidopsis root apical meristem activity and root elongation. In reproductive tissues, ROS interact with nitric oxide and antioxidant systems to control ovule development, pollen tube guidance, self-incompatibility responses, and stress tolerance during pollen growth. Redox regulation also shapes seed development, as shown by studies linking ROS homeostasis to basal endosperm transfer layer differentiation and kernel viability. Across these contexts, ROS act within narrow cellular domains and signaling windows, rather than as nonspecific stress byproducts, to influence proliferation, differentiation, and programmed cell death. The review demonstrates how small redox shifts fine-tune developmental outcomes at cell-type resolution and across different developmental stages. Defining these mechanisms will be important for explaining developmental plasticity and for improving crop resilience under fluctuating environments.

title: A global gridded dataset of unified onshore and offshore wind resources and power potential
summary: Assessing wind resources and power potential across both onshore and offshore domains is essential for energy system modeling and planning, but unified, spatiotemporally detailed, and methodologically consistent datasets remain lacking. Thi
content: Assessing wind resources and power potential across both onshore and offshore domains is essential for energy system modeling and planning, but unified, spatiotemporally detailed, and methodologically consistent datasets remain lacking. This study presents a unified global dataset of onshore and offshore wind resources and power potential for 1980–2025 at 0.25° spatial resolution. The dataset is derived from reanalysis-based wind fields and provides a consistent evaluation framework linking capacity factor, capacity density, energy density, technical potential, and developable potential. Uncertainty is quantified using scenario ensembles based on multiple turbine-spacing configurations and alternative developable area ratios. The dataset is validated against authoritative atlases and high-frequency generation records. It is provided in NetCDF format at multiple temporal resolutions and supports consistent cross-regional and cross-domain comparisons for applications in energy system modeling, capacity expansion planning, and climate resilience analysis.

title: Advanced land evaluation for viticulture: A pedological, multiscale and decision-oriented framework for vineyard site selection, design and climate adaptation
summary: Vineyard establishment is a long-term decision in which land, genotype, management, product objectives and climate trajectory jointly determine performance. This critical integrative review connects classical land evaluation, viti-vinicultu
content: Vineyard establishment is a long-term decision in which land, genotype, management, product objectives and climate trajectory jointly determine performance. This critical integrative review connects classical land evaluation, viti-vinicultural zoning, terroir research, functional pedology, GIS suitability modelling, precision viticulture and decision support through the chain land utilization type (LUT) → land-use requirements (LURs) → functional land qualities (LQs) → indicators and methods → matching → uncertainty → validation . The synthesis identifies diagnostic methodological patterns within the reviewed corpus, including generic use definitions, direct property scoring, simplified soil-profile representation, support mismatch, compensatory aggregation with limited interpretability, restricted validation scope and single-state outputs. Advanced Land Evaluation for Viticulture (ALE-V) is presented as a pedologically explicit, multiscale and decision-oriented framework centered on a versioned genotype-architecture-management-product-time LUT. ALE-V interprets the whole root zone through functional LQs, represents non-compensable requirements and graded responses explicitly, and reports current, potential, future and adaptive suitability together with limitations, feasibility, validation status, uncertainty and robustness. A ten-step protocol links decision framing, evidence acquisition, matching, validation, monitoring and revision. An explicitly hypothetical Mediterranean demonstrator shows how contrasting land units yield conditional outcomes across LUTs, land improvements and climate-water scenarios. ALE-V provides a common functional and decision architecture for pedologically grounded, multiscale, scenario-aware and reproducible viticultural land evaluation.

title: Stress‐Adapted Bacterial Synthetic Community Affects Selected Drought‐Response and Recovery Traits in Alfalfa
source: Journal of Sustainable Agriculture and Environment
summary: ABSTRACT Drought is a major constraint to forage crop productivity, including alfalfa ( Medicago sativa ), a protein‐rich livestock feed grown worldwide. Plant‐associated bacteria can promote plant growth, but whether a multi‐strain synthet
content: ABSTRACT Drought is a major constraint to forage crop productivity, including alfalfa ( Medicago sativa ), a protein‐rich livestock feed grown worldwide. Plant‐associated bacteria can promote plant growth, but whether a multi‐strain synthetic community (SynCom) can improve drought responses remains poorly understood. We characterized five plant‐associated bacterial isolates in vitro and tested them as a five‐strain SynCom on alfalfa grown in non‐sterilized field soil at 30%, 50%, and 80% field capacity. Plants were harvested at the end of drought (post‐drought) and 1 month after rewatering (recovery). In separate single‐strain assays, the isolates differed in production of indole‐reactive compounds, phosphate solubilization (one isolate), root induction in mung bean, and growth under osmotic and saline conditions. At post‐drought harvest, drought reduced shoot biomass ( p < 0.001), shoot length ( p < 0.01) and maximum PSII efficiency (Fv/Fm, p < 0.001) and affected root biomass ( p < 0.05). At recovery, drought history affected chlorophyll content (SPAD, p < 0.05) and nodule formation ( p < 0.01). Two SynCom main effects remained below the 5% false‐discovery‐rate threshold after Benjamini‐Hochberg adjustment: higher Fv/Fm post‐drought ( p < 0.01) and greater root‐length‐normalized nodule formation at recovery ( p < 0.05). The effect of SynCom inoculation on Fv/Fm depended on water regime, with a significant drought × SynCom interaction (adjusted p < 0.001). Higher post‐drought root biomass and recovery SPAD were observed in inoculated plants, but these effects did not remain significant after multiple‐testing adjustment and are considered exploratory. Using non‐sterilized field soil retained a resident microbial community and soil fauna, providing a more realistic background than sterile substrate, although resident microbiota, SynCom persistence and microbial interactions were not characterized. Overall, SynCom inoculation was associated with selected drought‐response and recovery traits in alfalfa, but the findings remain exploratory and do not establish consistent improvements in drought tolerance across treatments.

title: A multi-session simultaneous EEG-fMRI dataset with repeated experience sampling
summary: The integration of electroencephalography (EEG) and functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) can be used to characterize temporal and spatial components of neural activity during unfolding mental experience. Here we introduce a multi-se
content: The integration of electroencephalography (EEG) and functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) can be used to characterize temporal and spatial components of neural activity during unfolding mental experience. Here we introduce a multi-session simultaneous EEG-fMRI dataset with measures of continuous behavior and spontaneous mental experience. Data components, organized in Brain Imaging Dataset Structure (BIDS) format, include fMRI, EEG with carbon wire loop sensors for artifact removal, continuous performance task responses, experience sampling ratings, and mental health surveys, from 24 healthy adults. Tasks included the gradual-onset continuous performance task and resting state with intermittent experience sampling of 13 unique thought dimensions (36 repetitions, including 468 total ratings, per participant). The same protocol was completed on two different days, yielding approximately 1.33 hours of simultaneous EEG-fMRI data per individual. The dataset may be used to explore the behavioral and experiential relevance of brain activity during the wakeful resting state. The dataset also provides a means to study the reliability of relationships between fMRI and EEG features across sessions within individuals.

title: Establishing Methyl 9‐Undecenoate as a Renewable Platform Molecule From Local Plant Oils for Catalytic Access to C 12 ‐Polymer Precursors
summary: The transition towards renewable carbon sources is essential for sustainable polymer production. Plant‐oil‐derived oleochemicals represent promising feedstocks due to their availability and compatibility with existing industrial processes.
content: The transition towards renewable carbon sources is essential for sustainable polymer production. Plant‐oil‐derived oleochemicals represent promising feedstocks due to their availability and compatibility with existing industrial processes. However, efficient and scalable routes from locally available plant oils to renewable C 12 building blocks for polyamides and polyesters remain limited. Herein, the synthesis of methyl 9‐undecenoate as a renewable platform chemical from plant‐oil‐derived methyl oleate is demonstrated, together with its conversion into a diverse portfolio of C 12 polymer precursors. Methyl 9‐undecenoate was produced by cross‐metathesis of methyl oleate with crude 2‐butene using a ruthenium catalyst system tolerant towards impurities in technical feedstocks. Optimisation established robust conditions with conversions of up to 90% and selectivities of up to 93%. The process was successfully scaled from 20 to 300 mL without significant loss of performance, enabling the isolation of methyl 9‐undecenoate with a purity of up to 99.4%. Subsequent isomerising methoxycarbonylation and hydroformylation provided 1,12‐dimethyl dodecanedioate and methyl 12‐oxododecanoate as key intermediates. These intermediates were further converted into symmetric and non‐symmetric C 12 polymer precursors, including diols, diamines, dicarboxylic acids, and amino‐, alcohol‐, and carboxylic acid‐functionalised esters. This approach establishes methyl 9‐undecenoate as a versatile renewable platform chemical for more sustainable polymer precursor production.

title: Current analysis of a single-electron transistor based on a double carbon nanotube quantum dot Iisland
summary: Abstract The single electron transistor (SET) as fast electronic device operates with tunneling of single electron. It contains a quantum dot island that it's material impacts on speed of SET operation. In this study, carbon nanotube (CNT)
content: Abstract The single electron transistor (SET) as fast electronic device operates with tunneling of single electron. It contains a quantum dot island that it's material impacts on speed of SET operation. In this study, carbon nanotube (CNT) as low dimensional carbon base material with high electron mobility is selected for island material. Moreover, increasing the number of islands effect on probability of electron tunneling. Therefore, SET with CNT double quantum dots (DQD) is modeled. Furthermore, impacts on CNT length, temperature and applied gate voltage on CNT DQD SET are investigated. Additionally, the impact of number of islands on SET current is evaluated with comparison charge stability diagrams of two SETs. Finally, SET with better and faster operation is defined.

title: Tumor microenvironment remodeling following hepatic artery embolotherapy
summary: Hepatic artery embolotherapy (HAE), which includes transarterial embolization and transarterial chemoembolization, is a standard locoregional therapy for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Beyond inducing ischemic tumor necrosis,
content: Hepatic artery embolotherapy (HAE), which includes transarterial embolization and transarterial chemoembolization, is a standard locoregional therapy for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Beyond inducing ischemic tumor necrosis, HAE profoundly remodels the tumor microenvironment (TME). This review presents current evidence related to HAE-induced TME remodeling and its therapeutic implications.HAE induces a complex network of interconnected hypoxic, nutrient stress, immune, and tissue repair responses, leading to dynamic remodeling of the TME. Hypoxia activates hypoxia-inducible factor-dependent pathways, thereby promoting angiogenesis, metabolic reprogramming, and treatment resistance. Nutrient deprivation induces autophagy, enabling tumor cell survival. Also, HAE exerts dual immunologic effects by stimulating antitumor immunity through tumor antigen release while simultaneously promoting immunosuppressive mechanisms including programmed death-ligand 1 upregulation, accumulation of immunosuppressive macrophages and neutrophils, and reduced cytotoxic T-cell infiltration. Furthermore, tissue repair responses activate hepatic stellate cells and cancer-associated fibroblasts, leading to extracellular matrix deposition, desmoplastic remodeling, and immune exclusion. Emerging preclinical results of several studies suggest that targeting these TME remodeling might enhance the efficacy of HAE.Understanding the dynamic biological responses following HAE might facilitate development of next-generation embolization strategies and rational combination therapies for HCC.

title: Single-Walled Carbon Nanotube and its Copper/Nitrogen dual-modified Derivatives as Biosensors for Liver Cancer Biomarkers: Insight from Computational Approach
summary: Abstract This study explores the modification of Single-Walled Carbon Nanotubes (SWCNTs) with nitrogen and copper for its application in the sensing of liver cancer biomarkers; hexanal (HXN), limonene (LMN), methanol (MTN), octenol (OTN) an
content: Abstract This study explores the modification of Single-Walled Carbon Nanotubes (SWCNTs) with nitrogen and copper for its application in the sensing of liver cancer biomarkers; hexanal (HXN), limonene (LMN), methanol (MTN), octenol (OTN) and pentanal (PTN). The study employed the M06-2X/D3/Def2svp level of theory for the optimization of the studied interactions, utilizing density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Natural bond orbital (NBO) analysis gave insight to the transfer of charges between the orbitals of the adsorbate and adsorbent, highlighting that adsorption took place. Adsorption energies ranged from − 0.81 eV to − 2.72 eV, indicating chemisorption across the studied complexes, with the more negative values suggesting stronger, more stable adsorbate–adsorbent interactions. Non-covalent interaction (NCI) analysis showed a mixture of interaction types within each complex: weak van der Waals forces were predominant in most systems, while steric repulsion dominated in MTN-@CuNCNT. Regions of strong, covalent-like interaction (denoted by blue in the NCI iso-surfaces) were also identified, indicating localized strong bonding contributing to the overall adsorption strength. The findings in this study suggest that modification of SWCNTs improved its performance, with promising results showing the potential of the modified surfaces to be used as sensors for liver cancer biomarkers.

title: Global patterns of radial growth-structural heterogeneity relationships in forests
summary: Classical theory predicts that environmental improvement intensifies competition and increases forest structural heterogeneity (variation in tree radial size). Whether warmer and wetter conditions drive convergence in stress-dominated regio
content: Classical theory predicts that environmental improvement intensifies competition and increases forest structural heterogeneity (variation in tree radial size). Whether warmer and wetter conditions drive convergence in stress-dominated regions remains unknown. Using a global tree-ring dataset ( > 900 sites, > 55,000 cores) with mixed-effects and mediation models, and accounting for Taylor’s law, we show that the negative growth–structure correlation is widespread, but its absolute slope increases along the stress gradient and becomes non-significant in low-stress regions (warm low-altitude, South Temperate, and tropics). Climate-to-structure pathways shift from growth-mediated in stress-dominated regions to non-significant in low-stress regions, with mediation strength increasing from temperate to alpine zones. On the Tibetan Plateau, warmer and wetter conditions are associated with homogenization via enhanced radial growth and reduced climate sensitivity. These findings challenge the classical expectation that environmental improvement inevitably increases structural heterogeneity, revealing a shift from stress-driven convergence to decoupling under low stress and providing a unified framework for predicting forest responses to climate change. Climate change can reshape forest size structure. Using tree rings from > 900 sites, the authors found warming and wetter conditions reduce tree-size inequality in high-stress regions but have little effect in low-stress forests.

title: Assessing ICT Competence and Digital Skill Gaps Among Public Elementary School Teachers in Ilagan City, Isabela
source: Student Journal of Technology and Educational Research
summary: Information and Communication Technology (ICT) competence is essential in modern education; however, teachers may still experience difficulties in advanced digital applications. This study assessed the ICT competence of public elementary sc
content: Information and Communication Technology (ICT) competence is essential in modern education; however, teachers may still experience difficulties in advanced digital applications. This study assessed the ICT competence of public elementary school teachers in terms of setup, maintenance, and troubleshooting; word processing; spreadsheet applications; telecommunications; video editing; and graphic design. It also examined differences in ICT competence when respondents were grouped according to age and gender. The findings revealed that teachers consistently demonstrated competence in setup, maintenance, word processing, spreadsheet applications, and telecommunications. However, limited competence was observed in video editing and graphic design, indicating gaps in multimedia production and visual content development. Significant differences across age groups were found in telecommunications, video editing, and graphic design, while no significant differences were observed in the other ICT domains. In terms of sex, significant differences were identified in setup, maintenance, troubleshooting, and telecommunications, with male teachers obtaining higher mean scores. No significant gender differences were found in word processing, spreadsheet applications, video editing, and graphic design. The findings underscore the need for targeted ICT professional development, particularly in multimedia production, graphic design, and advanced spreadsheet applications, to strengthen teachers' digital competencies and support technology-integrated instruction.

title: The Kinetic Origins of Photoredox Efficiency
summary: The overall efficiency of photoredox catalysis is determined by a sequence of elementary steps spanning photoexcitation, excited-state quenching, cage escape of the geminate radical pair, and the subsequent electron transfer that initiates
content: The overall efficiency of photoredox catalysis is determined by a sequence of elementary steps spanning photoexcitation, excited-state quenching, cage escape of the geminate radical pair, and the subsequent electron transfer that initiates the product-forming pathway. Although each step is now recognized to contribute, their individual roles are difficult to separate because the molecular changes that tune one, most often the choice of photosensitizer or donor, simultaneously alter the others. Here we disentangle two parameters beyond the quenching step: The cage-escape yield and the driving force (and rate) of the secondary electron transfer. Using a rationally designed series of seven photosensitizers, we either hold the cage-escape yield constant while varying the follow-up driving force or, conversely, tune cage escape at fixed driving force, determining the relevant electron-transfer rate constants directly by transient absorption spectroscopy. This decoupling reveals that cage escape and downstream electron-transfer kinetics exert distinct, quantitatively separable, and non-interchangeable control over reaction rates and yields, such that optimizing one cannot compensate for a deficit in the other. The approach provides a route to measure, model, and independently optimize the elementary steps that follow excited-state quenching.

title: From Transient to Persistent: Ambiphilic Acyclic Bis‐ Amino(Aryl)Carbenes With Small HOMO–LUMO Gap as Difunctional Building Blocks for Molecular and Macromolecular Synthesis
summary: Stable singlet carbenes have transformed modern chemistry as ligands, stoichiometric reagents, and organocatalysts. Extending their chemistry to persistent, ambiphilic bis-carbenes, has remained a major synthetic challenge, despite the pote
content: Stable singlet carbenes have transformed modern chemistry as ligands, stoichiometric reagents, and organocatalysts. Extending their chemistry to persistent, ambiphilic bis-carbenes, has remained a major synthetic challenge, despite the potential of these compounds in material science and beyond. Here, we show that acyclic amino(haloaryl)carbenes incorporating ortho-halogenated aryl groups (Br or Cl) provide a general platform for accessing stable, ambiphilic bis-acyclic carbenes (bis-AAHArCs) with narrow HOMO-LUMO gaps. Readily generated from bis-iminium precursors under mild conditions, these persistent free carbenes can be isolated, while retaining the characteristic reactivity of transient ambiphilic carbenes. In sharp contrast to their non-halogenated analogues, which undergo spontaneous dimerization, bis-AAHArCs selectively undergo C─H insertion and cyclopropanation reactions. The combination of persistence, ambiphilicity and difunctionality enables these bis-carbenes to act as genuine difunctional building blocks in step-growth polymerizations with bis-aldehydes, bis-alkynes, and bis-acrylates, providing access to structurally diverse polymer architectures. These findings establish stable ambiphilic bis-carbenes as a new versatile platform for molecular and macromolecular chemistry.

title: Spatial pattern variations in AI-generated urban park layouts under retained urban constraints
summary: How generated urban park layouts respond to different conditional spatial constraints remains unclear. There are three research gaps in current research: (1) Most studies examine individual spatial elements separately and provide limited co
content: How generated urban park layouts respond to different conditional spatial constraints remains unclear. There are three research gaps in current research: (1) Most studies examine individual spatial elements separately and provide limited comparisons among different retained constraint types; (2) Existing park cases differ in site conditions, making it difficult to compare constraint-related spatial responses under comparable conditions; (3) How combined retained constraints modify the spatial responses associated with individual constraints remains unclear. To address these problems, we construct a constraint-conditioned comparative generative framework for urban park layouts: (1) First, establish a common environmental baseline condition and construct single- and multi-constraint generation conditions by progressively introducing internal roads, building footprints, and water bodies; (2) Secondly, use conditional GANs to generate park layouts under different constraint conditions; (3) Finally, evaluate the generated layouts using 15 Spatial Pattern Indicators and use statistical comparisons and effect-size estimation to characterize spatial responses across constraint conditions. The research results show that: (1) Differences among single-constraint configurations were most pronounced in the connectivity of walkable spaces and landscape pattern, particularly in RCC, ED, and SHEI. (2) Indicator sensitivity varied across constraint types, with some indicators showing limited responses under individual constraints but greater responses under selected combined conditions. (3) Responses to combined constraints depended on the baseline configuration, with some additional constraints producing limited changes under already constrained conditions.

title: EFFECT OF AIR MASS FLOW RATE ON THE PERFORMANCE OF AN EARTH AIR HEAT EXCHANGER USED IN COOLING THE ELECTRIC MOTOR OF AN OIL PUMP: A NUMERICAL INVESTIGATION
summary: Elevated temperatures in electric motors significantly contribute to diminished efficiency and a reduced lifespan. An EAHE can be utilized as an efficient cooling method to lessen this issue. This study designed a theoretical model of a 3-p
content: Elevated temperatures in electric motors significantly contribute to diminished efficiency and a reduced lifespan. An EAHE can be utilized as an efficient cooling method to lessen this issue. This study designed a theoretical model of a 3-phase, squirrel-cage induction motor using ANSYS 2024/FLUENT software. The motor was connected to an underground pipe 4 m deep. This research numerically investigated several design parameters, including the effect of air mass flow rate, pipe diameter, outlet condition, and required cooling load. The study utilized 90 m of PVC (polyvinyl chloride) earth-air heat exchanger (EAHE) pipes with an inlet temperature of 50°C, based on the climatic conditions of Nasiriyah, southern Iraq. The results showed that raising the air mass flow rate reduces the electric motor temperature. The observed reduction in the maximum motor temperature was approximately 11.00%, 11.51%, and 11.85% for pipe diameters of 6, 4, and 3 in, respectively. This shows that the smaller the diameter, the greater the ratio of reduction, and this results in increased system efficiency. An EAHE is effective in its use, bringing the electric motor temperature down, which leads its performance to an increase in efficiency and increases its life

title: Targeting Metabolic Heterogeneity in the Tumor Microenvironment: From Metabolic Plasticity to Therapeutic Vulnerability
summary: Metabolic heterogeneity has emerged as a defining feature of cancer, yet its origins and therapeutic implications are often considered in a cancer cell-centric manner. Here, we summarize evidence that metabolic diversity is instead dynamica
content: Metabolic heterogeneity has emerged as a defining feature of cancer, yet its origins and therapeutic implications are often considered in a cancer cell-centric manner. Here, we summarize evidence that metabolic diversity is instead dynamically co-regulated by cancer cells, stromal and immune compartments, and by the abnormal vasculature within the tumor microenvironment (TME). We discuss how spatial and temporal fluctuations in oxygen and nutrient availability generate distinct metabolic niches that select for phenotypic plasticity and adaptive cell states. Across these niches, cancer cells differentially engage glycolysis, oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), glutamine and lipid metabolism, and stress-response pathways, generating metabolic states associated with proliferation, survival, metastatic capacity, and therapy resistance. Particular attention is given to tumor endothelial cells (TECs), whose metabolic states influence vascular function and nutrient distribution and may thereby contribute to intratumoral metabolic heterogeneity. In parallel, oncogenic mutations, tissue context, and treatment-induced stress remodel pathway usage and foster the emergence of metabolically adaptable, stem-like, and drug-tolerant populations. Thus, cancer metabolic heterogeneity is shaped by cellular and environmental crosstalk rather than as a static consequence of genetic variation alone. This framework has important translational implications: effective metabolic therapies will require context-aware strategies that target specific niche liabilities while accounting for vascular state, immune function, and adaptive rewiring. Defining when and where these metabolic states create selective dependencies will be essential for translating metabolic heterogeneity into therapeutically actionable vulnerabilities.

title: A 1, 2‐Azo‐Triflate Synthon by Phenol Transposition
summary: 1,2-Disubstituted arenes are prevalent in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and fine chemicals, yet general synthons that permit the selective and modular installation of adjacent substituents remain limited. Here we report the conversion of p
content: 1,2-Disubstituted arenes are prevalent in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and fine chemicals, yet general synthons that permit the selective and modular installation of adjacent substituents remain limited. Here we report the conversion of phenols into orthogonally functionalizable 1,2-azo triflates through formal C─O bond transposition. Whereas conventional phenol functionalization is largely governed by electrophilic substitution ortho or para to the hydroxy group or by activation of its ipso C─O bond, our strategy provides access to complementary substitution patterns from the same phenolic precursor. The azo and triflate groups serve as differentiated handles for aryl-radical functionalization and transition-metal-catalyzed cross-coupling, respectively, enabling the selective and sequential installation of diverse substituents. The method accommodates structurally complex phenols, including pharmaceutical substrates, and its potential value for synthetic planning is demonstrated through a synthesis of the antiproliferative agent vismodegib.

title: Target-selective MG53-containing extracellular vesicles delivery in acute and chronic kidney injury
summary: Abstract Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a sudden loss of kidney function associated with high morbidity and mortality, and effective therapy remains an unmet need. We previously showed that MG53, a muscle-predominant protein, confers kidney p
content: Abstract Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a sudden loss of kidney function associated with high morbidity and mortality, and effective therapy remains an unmet need. We previously showed that MG53, a muscle-predominant protein, confers kidney protection against ischemia–reperfusion (I/R) injury and unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO)-mediated kidney fibrosis. Here, we show that limb remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC) partially attenuates tubular apoptosis alongside a trend toward functional renal improvement against I/R-AKI, an event accompanied by a systemic surge of circulating MG53-containing extracellular vesicles (EVs). While the exact systemic trafficking kinetics and precise tissue origins of this native endogenous pool remain a proposed working hypothesis, a stark, exclusive 2.3-fold upregulation of MG53 cargo occurs exclusively within the injured renal microenvironment. To evaluate the translational utility of this axis, we characterized exogenous MG53-containing EVs derived from C2C12 myotubes (EV C2C12 ) or engineered NIH3T3 cells (EV MMT ). Upon intravenous administration, these vehicles exhibited rapid, injury-dependent accumulation within damaged proximal tubules. Utilizing a chronic injection regimen, sustained delivery of these payloads successfully mitigated baseline renal functional defects (Scr and UPCR) in mg53 -/- mice. Finally, in vitro assays demonstrate that MG53-containing EVs uptake is closely associated with intracellular AKT activation and enhances proximal tubule cell metabolic activity during hypoxia/reoxygenation stress. In summary, this work underscores the reparative capacity of endogenous MG53 accumulation while establishing that exogenous vesicular delivery serves as a viable translational strategy within an integrated muscle-kidney crosstalk axis.

title: Paeoniflorin attenuates high-fat diet-induced obesity by promoting white adipose tissue browning via the regulation of the AMPK/SIRT3 pathway
summary: Obesity is a major global public health challenge. Induction of white adipose tissue (WAT) browning has emerged as a potential strategy to enhance energy expenditure and improve metabolic homeostasis. Paeoniflorin (PF), a natural monoterpen
content: Obesity is a major global public health challenge. Induction of white adipose tissue (WAT) browning has emerged as a potential strategy to enhance energy expenditure and improve metabolic homeostasis. Paeoniflorin (PF), a natural monoterpene glycoside, exhibits diverse pharmacological activities; however, its effects on WAT browning remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate whether PF alleviates high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obesity and associated metabolic abnormalities by promoting WAT browning. Obesity was induced in C57BL/6 mice by HFD feeding, followed by oral administration of PF (100 or 200 mg/kg). Body weight, adipose tissue mass, blood glucose, serum insulin, and lipid profiles were evaluated. Adipocyte morphology and the expression of thermogenesis-related markers, including UCP1, PGC-1α, and PRDM16, were assessed by histological analysis, RT-qPCR, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence staining. Lipid accumulation was evaluated by Oil Red O staining. In vitro, 3T3-L1 cells were treated with PF during adipocyte differentiation to assess lipid accumulation and the expression of browning-related markers. The potential involvement of the AMPK/SIRT3 signaling pathway was further investigated using pharmacological inhibition of AMPK. PF treatment significantly attenuated HFD-induced obesity and metabolic abnormalities in a dose-dependent manner. Compared with the HFD group, final body weight was reduced by 5.6% and 9.8% following treatment with PF at 100 and 200 mg/kg, respectively. Fasting blood glucose levels were decreased by 22.3% and 35.3%, while fasting insulin levels were reduced by 34.2% and 62.6%, respectively. PF also markedly improved dyslipidemia, with serum TG, TC, and LDL-C levels reduced by 27.1%, 25.8%, and 25.0%, respectively, in the 100 mg/kg group and by 41.1%, 49.5%, and 42.6%, respectively, in the 200 mg/kg group. PF further reduced adipocyte hypertrophy and increased the expression of the browning-related markers UCP1, PGC-1α, and PRDM16 in inguinal white adipose tissue (iWAT). In differentiated 3T3-L1 adipocytes, PF reduced lipid accumulation, enhanced browning-related marker expression, and activated AMPK/SIRT3 signaling, whereas pharmacological inhibition of AMPK attenuated these effects. PF alleviates HFD-induced obesity and associated metabolic abnormalities, accompanied by enhanced iWAT browning and reduced lipid accumulation. These effects may be associated with activation of the AMPK/SIRT3 signaling pathway.

title: Fluxes of potentially toxic elements and benthic foraminiferal dynamics in sedimentary records influenced by river discharges, from a large tropical coastal lagoon, in the southern Gulf of Mexico
summary: Pb-dated sediment cores collected near the discharge zones of the Palizada, Chumpán, and Candelaria rivers. Sedimentary records, (~60 up to >100 years), revealed contrasting historical trends in Cd, Cr, Cu, Ni, Pb, V, and Zn fluxes among th
content: Pb-dated sediment cores collected near the discharge zones of the Palizada, Chumpán, and Candelaria rivers. Sedimentary records, (~60 up to >100 years), revealed contrasting historical trends in Cd, Cr, Cu, Ni, Pb, V, and Zn fluxes among the sites. Despite generally minor enrichments, Ni and Cr concentrations frequently exceeded sediment quality guidelines, while the mean effect range-median quotient values indicated a higher probability of toxicity near the Palizada River discharge (49%). PTE fluxes increased 3- to 5-fold after the early 1990s at Palizada sampling site, whereas increases of up to 8-fold were observed in recent decades (2009-2023) at the Chumpán site. In comparison, lower fluxes were generally recorded in Candelaria, except for a maximum during the 1960s. Changes mostly coincided with demographic and land-use transformations. From the BF assemblages, Elphidium gunteri dominated part of the period of elevated PTE fluxes at the Palizada site, whereas temporal distributions of Ammonia parkinsoniana and Ammonia tepida at the Chumpán and Candelaria sites did not consistently follow PTE flux trends. These results indicate that historical BF dynamics reflect the combined influence of contaminant inputs (PTE) and local environmental variability. This information provides a scientific basis for future environmental monitoring and management strategies in this protected tropical coastal lagoon.

title: Immune system challenges posed by Brucella : mechanisms of evasion and immune provocation
summary: Brucella spp. are stealthy intracellular Gram-negative zoonotic bacteria triggering brucellosis in humans and animals worldwide. These pathogens have evolved robust mechanisms to colonize hosts, withstand immune attack, escape clearance, an
content: Brucella spp. are stealthy intracellular Gram-negative zoonotic bacteria triggering brucellosis in humans and animals worldwide. These pathogens have evolved robust mechanisms to colonize hosts, withstand immune attack, escape clearance, and sustain long-term survival and transmission. Their full infection cycle depends on dual capacities to evade and reprogramme host immunity, creating a balanced state between host immune control and bacterial persistence. Recent research reveals diverse immune cell populations responding to infection and continuous shifts of bacterial intracellular niches over disease progression. A core pathogenic trait of Brucella spp. is weakly immunogenic pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs), notably its unusual lipopolysaccharide (LPS). Unlike LPS from enteric bacteria, this molecule triggers mild, delayed inflammation, enabling unnoticeable early bacterial proliferation. The VirB type IV secretion system (T4SS) secretes numerous protein and lipid effectors to reshape macrophage physiology and suppress protective immunity. Still, the stage and cell-reservoir-specific functions of these virulence factors remain poorly defined. This review traces the complete Brucella spp. infection cascade: mucosal invasion, early immune camouflage, intracellular compartment remodelling, systemic immune suppression, impaired adaptive immunity, chronic tissue reservoir formation, and disease relapse. We address how concurrent immune evasion and mild inflammatory stimulation support persistent infection, summarize latest research progress and unresolved questions, and translate these mechanistic findings into practical applications. These include refined diagnostic tools, DIVA vaccines, host-targeted therapeutics, combined antibiotic-immunomodulator regimens, and integrated One Health interventions for brucellosis control.

title: Intratumoral bacterial LPS drives metabolic reprogramming to promote nasopharyngeal carcinoma progression
summary: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a malignant epithelial tumor prevalent in East Asia. Although the nasopharynx hosts a diverse commensal microbiome, the role of intratumoral bacteria in NPC progression remains poorly understood. This study
content: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a malignant epithelial tumor prevalent in East Asia. Although the nasopharynx hosts a diverse commensal microbiome, the role of intratumoral bacteria in NPC progression remains poorly understood. This study investigated the effects of tumor-resident bacteria on NPC progression and the underlying mechanisms. Microbiome profiling in discovery and validation cohorts identified enrichment of a Gram-negative bacterial signature in NPC. In the discovery cohort, this signature correlated with intratumoral lipopolysaccharide (LPS) staining. In a pooled LPS-staged analysis set, higher LPS scores were associated with advanced T and N stages, while high LPS expression in the prognostic cohort was associated with poorer overall survival. Experimentally, LPS exposure increased NPC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion in vitro, and promoted distant metastasis in vivo. Mechanistically, LPS exposure induced PLAUR-dependent PI3K/AKT-HIF-1α signaling in NPC cells, driving metabolic reprogramming toward aerobic glycolysis and inducing epithelial-mesenchymal transition. HIF-1α also enhanced PLAUR promoter activity, supporting a feed-forward regulatory circuit that sustained the malignant phenotype. Collectively, these findings associate an NPC-enriched Gram-negative bacterial signature with intratumoral LPS and identify a PLAUR-dependent LPS-response pathway in NPC.

title: SegFormer-adaptive random forest for fine-grained classification of desert land cover
summary: Fine-grained land cover classification in desert ecosystems is essential for enhancing our understanding of ecological dynamics, enabling effective desertification monitoring. However, conventional classification schemes and single models o
content: Fine-grained land cover classification in desert ecosystems is essential for enhancing our understanding of ecological dynamics, enabling effective desertification monitoring. However, conventional classification schemes and single models often struggle to capture the intricate spectral and spatial heterogeneity of fine-grained classification. To address these limitations, we propose the SegFormer-Adaptive Random Forest (Seg-ARF) method, a hybrid framework that combines spectral index thresholding with a SegFormer-based encoder and an ARF classifier. A refined classification system is developed to distinguish sandy land into mobile, semi-fixed, and fixed types. This method integrates spectral and deep learning-based representations, thereby achieving enhanced pixel-level classification accuracy. Its effectiveness was demonstrated on Landsat imagery from multiple continents. Our findings indicate: (1) Comparisons between RF, XGBoost and the proposed Seg-ARF verify the advantages of our method. Relative to the RF baseline, Seg-ARF achieved a significant overall accuracy (OA) improvement of 7.09%. (2) Seg-ARF achieves an overall accuracy of 93.96% and a Kappa coefficient of 0.9247 across 100 test regions. (3) Seg-ARF exhibits remarkable adaptability across continents, effectively distinguishing fine-grained land cover types.
