The Seg-ARF method provides a scalable and transferable solution for large-scale desert mapping and long-term monitoring, with significant potential for applications in desertification mitigation.

title: Molten salt electrochemical separation of aluminum for end-of-life magnesium upcycling
summary: The sustainable supply of primary magnesium, critical material for society’s lightweight and low-carbon transition, is challenged by the huge energy-intensity and environmental burden. Recycling end-of-life (EoL) magnesium shows great resou
content: The sustainable supply of primary magnesium, critical material for society’s lightweight and low-carbon transition, is challenged by the huge energy-intensity and environmental burden. Recycling end-of-life (EoL) magnesium shows great resource and environmental advantages. However, the conventional remelting process is insufficient to separate impurity elements contaminated in EoL magnesium products and results in resource downcycling. This study focused on the separation of the aluminum, the most typical alloying element in magnesium alloys, using molten salt electrolysis method. The electrochemical dissolution behavior of aluminum from solid- and liquid-state magnesium anode was investigated, respectively. The results show that aluminum dissolution in solid-state anode electrolysis is strongly phase-depending, whereas is primarily controlled by the intrinsic element’s electrochemical dissolution potential in liquid-state anode electrolysis. Controlling the anode potential below −2.80 V vs. Cl 2 /Cl − (673 K) and −2.10 V vs. Cl 2 /Cl − (943 K), or the anodic current density not exceed 100 mA cm −2 (673 K) and 600 mA cm −2 (943 K), for solid- and liquid-state anode electrolysis, respectively, is critical for magnesium upcycling from aluminum contaminated magnesium to high purity secondary magnesium (>99.95 wt.%) by preventing aluminum dissolution and deposition. The findings provide the theoretical support for the development of efficient and environmentally upcycling process for EoL magnesium.

title: Regioselective [4+2] Cycloaddition Between 3‐Hetero‐Substituted 1,2‐Benzynes and 2‐Oxime‐Substituted Furan Derivatives
summary: The [4+2] cycloaddition of 3-hetero-substituted 1,2-benzynes with 2-oxime-substituted furans proceeds with high regioselectivity due to the electron-donating ability of the oxime functionality. In contrast to 2-hydrazone-substituted furans,
content: The [4+2] cycloaddition of 3-hetero-substituted 1,2-benzynes with 2-oxime-substituted furans proceeds with high regioselectivity due to the electron-donating ability of the oxime functionality. In contrast to 2-hydrazone-substituted furans, which preferentially undergo nucleophilic addition of the amino group, 2-oxime-substituted furans favor cycloaddition over competing nucleophilic pathways. Computational studies based on frontier molecular orbital (FMO) analysis, condensed Fukui indices, the aryne distortion model, and reaction energy profiles were in good agreement with the observed regio- and chemoselectivities. The obtained cycloadducts can be readily converted into naphthols or naphthalenes through aromatization or reductive aromatization, and the oxime functionality can be further transformed into a formyl group. This method provides a simple and regioselective route to 1-hetero-8-carbonylnaphthalene derivatives, which are otherwise difficult to access, thereby aiding the synthesis of more complex polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and natural products.

title: Gradual Transition of Temperature During the Heinrich Stadial 1 Period Across China: Evidence From Branched GDGTs
summary: Abstract The Heinrich Stadial 1 (HS1) interval (18–14.6 kyr BP) is regarded as a pivotal window for exploring the underlying temperature dynamics. However, the issue of temperature variations during this period remains controversial. Here w
content: Abstract The Heinrich Stadial 1 (HS1) interval (18–14.6 kyr BP) is regarded as a pivotal window for exploring the underlying temperature dynamics. However, the issue of temperature variations during this period remains controversial. Here we generate a well‐dated, high‐resolution (∼30 years), growth temperature record over the past 30,000 years from Sihailongwan Maar Lake in northeastern China, using bacterial lipid branched glycerol dialkyl glycerol tetraethers (brGDGTs). The results reveal that low temperatures prevailed from 18 to ∼16 kyr BP, after which temperatures increased by ∼2.5°C until the end of the HS1 period. When combined with published brGDGT‐based records from across China, it is evident that low temperatures were more pronounced in northern China, whereas a distinct pattern emerged in southern China, where temperatures began to decline gradually during this interval. This suggests that the cold pulse signals originating from high‐latitude regions may have weakened as they propagated toward southern China, although they still caused a temperature decrease. An increase in greenhouse gases (CO 2 and CH 4 ) may have driven this shift, partially offsetting the impact of the cooling pulse on temperature variations in southern China.

title: Beyond Certification: A Multi-Quantitative Post-Occupancy Evaluation of Indoor Environmental Quality in a Platinum-Certified Subtropical University Building
source: International Journal of Architectural Engineering Technology
summary: Green building certification formally evaluates building performance, while it may not fully capture occupants’ experiences of indoor environmental quality (IEQ) during post-occupancy use. This study presents a post-occupancy evaluation (PO
content: Green building certification formally evaluates building performance, while it may not fully capture occupants’ experiences of indoor environmental quality (IEQ) during post-occupancy use. This study presents a post-occupancy evaluation (POE) of a BEAM Plus Platinum-certified academic building at the Macau University of Science and Technology (MUST), using a quantitative evaluation approach that combines a questionnaire survey of occupant satisfaction (n = 108, 90.0% valid response rate) with in-situ physical measurements of key IEQ parameters, including carbon dioxide (CO₂), total volatile organic compounds (TVOC), formaldehyde (HCHO), PM₁₀, thermal conditions, and operational sound level, supplemented by DIALux simulation of artificial-lighting performance. The survey and field measurements were conducted in three classrooms on three days between March 28 and April 11, 2025, during the transition period between classes in a Spring semester. The results indicated that the five IEQ categories received mean scores ranging from 3.65 to 3.94 on a five-point scale, with visual environmental quality being the best while ventilation effectiveness being the worst. In terms of the specific items, natural ventilation adequacy and local overheating/overcooling received the lowest mean scores of 3.47 and 3.14, respectively. Short-term classroom CO₂ concentrations peaked at 897 ppm, and TVOC ranged between 0.001 and 0.008 mg/m³. Thermal measurements showed inter-room variation, with mean temperatures ranging from 23.99 °C to 25.23 °C (a differential of 1.24 °C). Operational sound levels ranged from 46.3 to 57.2 dB(A) in the monitored classrooms. Interpreting occupant feedback with in-situ measurements offers practical, user-centered evidence that bridges the gap between green building certification and actual building performance. The findings provide actionable guidance for follow-up IEQ monitoring and operational optimization in university classrooms.

title: Rhizospheric pH mediated thermo-signalling coordinates root growth under heat stress
summary: Abstract Heat stress events pose a major threat to global agriculture due to elevated air and soil temperatures. While plant roots regulate their growth in response to elevated soil temperatures, they appear to rely on thermosensory mechani
content: Abstract Heat stress events pose a major threat to global agriculture due to elevated air and soil temperatures. While plant roots regulate their growth in response to elevated soil temperatures, they appear to rely on thermosensory mechanisms distinct from those used by shoots. Here, we report pH as a key component of a thermo-signaling mechanism that regulates temperature-dependent root responses via ROS-mediated control of cell cycle dynamics in Arabidopsis thaliana . At moderately high temperatures, alkalization of meristematic and transition zones increases superoxide (O₂⁻) levels, promoting cell division and root growth. Conversely, higher temperatures inhibit growth by increasing acidification and hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) accumulation in these zones. Elevating external pH buffers this acidification, reduces H₂O₂ levels, and confers heat resistance. Our data support that this pH-mediated heat resistance is also effective under soil conditions. The heat-induced pH shifts are controlled by plasma membrane H⁺-ATPases (PM-H⁺-ATPases), which are under the control of the kinases TOT3 and TOI5. Our findings reveal an interesting pathway for plant adaptation to heat stress, linking pH, ROS and root thermomorphogenesis, with major implications for improving plant resilience in warming climates.

title: Beyond Lithiophilicity: Multistage Rate Matching in Lithium‐Metal Electrodeposition
summary: ABSTRACT Lithium (Li)‐metal deposition is commonly interpreted using static descriptors, including lithiophilicity, nucleation overpotential, ionic conductivity, or solid‐electrolyte interphase composition. Although these parameters provide
content: ABSTRACT Lithium (Li)‐metal deposition is commonly interpreted using static descriptors, including lithiophilicity, nucleation overpotential, ionic conductivity, or solid‐electrolyte interphase composition. Although these parameters provide valuable insights, none alone determines how an initially nucleated Li deposit evolves under sustained current. Here, we conceptualize Li electrodeposition as a dynamically coupled sequence involving Li + transport, interfacial entry, charge transfer, Li 0 surface redistribution, nucleation, and growth; desolvation is an interfacial‐entry process in liquid electrolytes. Li 0 surface redistribution denotes the lateral motion of newly reduced Li species before incorporation into a growing deposit, with surface diffusion as one possible mechanism. Uniform deposition requires multidimensional kinetic compatibility across these stages, rather than maximization of any individual step. In particular, Li 0 surface redistribution can bridge initial nucleation and subsequent lateral growth, while the decay of morphological perturbations provides a conceptual criterion for deposition stability. From this perspective, solvent chemistry, anions, additives, concentrated electrolytes, polymers, and solid electrolytes can be understood as upstream regulators that reshape the coupled rate chain. This framework shifts lithium‐metal design from optimizing isolated material properties toward engineering a dynamically self‐leveling deposition field through multistage rate matching.

title: Gill mucosal architecture and immune signatures in Atlantic salmon reared in different smolt production regimes
summary: Abstract Production environments strongly influence the health, welfare, and robustness of Atlantic salmon ( Salmo salar ). Challenges related to gill health in particular have emerged as a major welfare and production issue in salmon aquac
content: Abstract Production environments strongly influence the health, welfare, and robustness of Atlantic salmon ( Salmo salar ). Challenges related to gill health in particular have emerged as a major welfare and production issue in salmon aquaculture. Suboptimal rearing conditions can disrupt epithelial integrity, alter mucous cell dynamics, impair immunity, and compromise gas-exchange efficiency, ultimately resulting in reduced growth performance and greater susceptibility to disease. In this study, salmon were reared using three land‑based production regimes: a flow‑through system (FTS), recirculating aquaculture system (RAS), and partial reuse system (PRS). Fish were followed through smoltification, an extended land‑based post‑smolt phase, and a seawater period that simulated transfer to seawater. Gill health was evaluated using histopathology, machine learning-based quantitative image analysis, targeted gene expression profiling, and measurements of systemic immune markers. The functional effects of freshwater rearing history were assessed by subjecting fish to two experimental challenges with Neoparamoeba perurans , the aetiological agent of amoebic gill disease. The results showed that growth performance was broadly comparable across production regimes, although PRS-reared fish exhibited slightly lower final weight and length than RAS-reared fish at trial termination. Significant differences were observed in gill morphology, mucous cell composition, and immune‑related transcriptional profiles, but these patterns were predominantly explained by temporal progression rather than by clear effects of the rearing environment. Fish reared in RAS showed modulation of gill mucosal features and altered expression of genes associated with immune regulation and structural remodelling over time, which were accompanied by differences in circulating immune markers. Following repeated N. perurans challenge, gross gill scores and parasite loads were generally low across all groups, and RAS and PRS rearing did not increase the susceptibility to parasitic infection or associated gill pathology. The results indicate that land‑based production regimes influence gill structure and immune function in Atlantic salmon, but the detected differences were modest and largely time‑dependent. While system‑specific effects were measurable, they were not clearly distinguishable between production regimes.

title: The Oxygen Reduction Reaction over Pt Nanoparticles Studied with First-Principles-Based Kinetic Monte Carlo Simulations
summary: Abstract The oxygen reduction reaction is essential to reduce the dependence on fossil fuels. Although widely studied, the underlying reason for the onset overpotential of the reaction over Pt-based nanoparticles remains debated. Here, a fi
content: Abstract The oxygen reduction reaction is essential to reduce the dependence on fossil fuels. Although widely studied, the underlying reason for the onset overpotential of the reaction over Pt-based nanoparticles remains debated. Here, a first-principles-based kinetic Monte Carlo framework is developed to elucidate the main reaction mechanism, rate-determining steps, and the reason for the overpotential. Effects of the aqueous environment with directional hydrogen bonds are incorporated in the kinetic Monte Carlo simulations, and a framework for simulating linear sweep voltammetry is presented. We find that the overpotential originates from the high coverages of oxygen species (*O, *OH, and *H2O), which block sites for O2 adsorption. The kinetic simulations demonstrate that the effects of site-blocking can be tuned by the shape and size of the Pt nanoparticles. The lowest overpotential is obtained for particles in the size range between 3 and 6 nm with large fractions of (111) facets. The developed methods are general and facilitate the understanding and optimization of catalysts used in a range of electrochemical reactions.

title: Ancient refractory mantle domain in the Pacific lithosphere evidenced by mantle xenoliths from Tahiti and Moorea, Society Islands
source: Progress in Earth and Planetary Science
summary: Abstract Oceanic peridotites preserve records of both recent melting at mid-ocean ridges and ancient melt depletion, providing key insights into the long-term chemical evolution of the Earth’s mantle. Here we report mantle xenoliths from Ta
content: Abstract Oceanic peridotites preserve records of both recent melting at mid-ocean ridges and ancient melt depletion, providing key insights into the long-term chemical evolution of the Earth’s mantle. Here we report mantle xenoliths from Tahiti and Moorea in the Society Islands, which sampled the ~70 Myr-old Pacific lithosphere. These samples provide a unique opportunity to investigate the compositional structure and evolution of oceanic mantle far from the mid-ocean ridges. Among 40 investigated xenolith samples (3 lherzolites, 11 harzburgites, 20 dunites, 4 wehrlites, and 2 orthopyroxenites), refractory harzburgites yield unradiogenic 187 Os/ 188 Os ratios down to 0.11720, while the other lithologies are more radiogenic (0.12324–0.13945), displaying a bimodal distribution of Os isotopic compositions. The dunites, wehrlites, and orthopyroxenites are interpreted to have formed through extensive interactions between peridotites and infiltrating melts. High temperature (> 1000 °C) harzburgites and lherzolites host abundant CO 2 -rich fluid inclusions, suggesting metasomatic imprints associated with upwelling mantle plume-derived melts or fluids. The unradiogenic Os isotopic compositions of the refractory harzburgites indicate the presence of an ancient, depleted mantle domain that predates the formation of the ~70 Ma Pacific lithosphere. We interpret these refractory harzburgites as fragments of an ancient refractory mantle domain incorporated into the Pacific lithosphere. One possible origin of this mantle domain is transport and emplacement by the Pitcairn–Gambier plume located southeast of the Society hotspot. In this scenario, the refractory mantle domain was emplaced at the base of the young Pacific lithosphere, became incorporated into the lithospheric mantle, and was subsequently sampled as xenoliths during later Society plume volcanism. These observations highlight the role of mantle plumes in modifying and assembling heterogeneous mantle domains within oceanic lithospheric mantle through time.

title: Bipolar Depression with Secondary Psychosis Triggered by Polysubstance and Hyperhomocysteinemia: A Case ReportBipolar Depression with Secondary Psychosis Triggered by Polysubstance and Hyperhomocysteinemia: A Case Report
source: International Journal of Medical Science and Clinical Research Studies
summary: The intersection between early-onset mood disorders, substance use, and the development of psychotic conditions in adolescence represents a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge in psychiatric practice. This article presents a case report of
content: The intersection between early-onset mood disorders, substance use, and the development of psychotic conditions in adolescence represents a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge in psychiatric practice. This article presents a case report of a 17-year-old male with a history of persistent depressive disorder, hyperactivity, and multiple suicide attempts, who progressed to severe psychic disorganization ("schizophrenization") associated with cocaine use and severe nicotine dependence. The clinical evolution illustrates the complexity of differentiating between substance-induced psychosis and the prodrome of a primary psychotic disorder, as well as the impact of delirium secondary to nicotine withdrawal on mental disorganization. Therapeutic management required multiple pharmacological approaches, culminating in the consideration of atypical strategies due to refractoriness. We discuss the hypothesis of schizophrenization as an interpretative matrix, expanded by the concepts of self-medication of distress, alexithymia, limbic hypersignification in patients with Bipolar Affective Disorder, and Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) traits, offering a model to understand progressive destructuring in adolescents with multiple vulnerabilities.

title: Exploring the diversity of pyruvate:ferredoxin oxidoreductases
summary: Pyruvate:ferredoxin oxidoreductases (PFORs) are key enzymes in the anaerobic metabolism of numerous diverse organisms. Their significance extends far beyond the oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvate, their canonical reaction. PFORs support
content: Pyruvate:ferredoxin oxidoreductases (PFORs) are key enzymes in the anaerobic metabolism of numerous diverse organisms. Their significance extends far beyond the oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvate, their canonical reaction. PFORs support diverse physiological roles, including fermentation and carbon assimilation, and have been integrated into a wide range of metabolic networks, linking carbon flux to redox balance in many bacteria and archaea, as well as in selected eukaryotes. PFORs catalyze the reversible conversion of pyruvate to acetyl-coenzyme A coupled to the reduction of low-potential ferredoxin. This process relies on a catalytic mechanism involving a thiamine pyrophosphate cofactor and iron-sulfur clusters. The PFOR enzymes exhibit remarkable diversity in terms of structure (subunit composition, domain architecture, and quaternary organization), function and kinetics. This diversity reflects evolutionary adaptations to different biological contexts. In this review, we examine PFOR diversity from molecular and physiological perspectives, with a focus on the enzymes that have been biochemically characterized or at least demonstrated to exhibit PFOR activity.

title: Ultra‐Stable Phosphide Barrier Layer for Thermoelectric Bismuth Telluride
summary: ABSTRACT The long‐term reliability of bismuth telluride (BT) thermoelectric power generation devices is severely constrained by the lack of reliable barrier layers. In this work, Ni 2 P is proposed as an ultra‐stable barrier layer for N‐typ
content: ABSTRACT The long‐term reliability of bismuth telluride (BT) thermoelectric power generation devices is severely constrained by the lack of reliable barrier layers. In this work, Ni 2 P is proposed as an ultra‐stable barrier layer for N‐type BT (N–BT). The low thermodynamic driving force for interfacial reaction and the sluggish Ni migration in Ni 2 P together ensure the favorable chemical inertness of the Ni 2 P/N–BT interface, while atomic‐scale bonding endows the interface with high bonding energy, leading to the lowest interfacial contact resistivity (∼1 µΩ cm 2 ), highest bonding strength (∼20 MPa), and longest verified stable duration at 523 K (90 days) among reported barrier layer systems. The resulting seven‐pair BT thermoelectric device achieves a maximum energy conversion efficiency of 6.9% at a temperature difference of 230 K. This work not only addresses the long‐standing bottleneck in power generation applications of BT‐based devices since the 1950s, but also provides guidance for barrier layer design in other thermoelectric systems.

title: Molecular regulatory networks of salt stress response in rice: developmental plasticity and breeding implications
summary: With the escalating degradation of global environmental conditions, soil salinization has emerged as a significant threat to global food security, resulting in substantial losses in crop yields. As a staple food crop of paramount importance
content: With the escalating degradation of global environmental conditions, soil salinization has emerged as a significant threat to global food security, resulting in substantial losses in crop yields. As a staple food crop of paramount importance, the stability of rice yields and quality warrants close examination. Salinity induces acute osmotic stress and ion toxicity, leading to the excessive accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS). These oxidative stresses and the subsequent physiological cascades cause irreversible cellular damage throughout the growth and developmental cycle, severely limiting grain yield. This review summarizes recent advances in understanding the physiological and molecular responses of rice to salinity stress, focusing on developmental plasticity, spatiotemporal regulatory mechanisms of gene expression, and the complex networks of phytohormone crosstalk from 2020 onwards. Furthermore, this review identifies the current challenges of elucidating salt tolerance mechanisms and translating these insights into breeding programs, and proposes potential strategies for enhancing salinity adaptation. The aim of this work is to provide a comprehensive theoretical framework and actionable insights for future molecular-targeted breeding and germplasm innovation in rice.

title: Optimising the early stages of constructed wetland-microbial fuel cell lifecycle: a guide to plant selection, acclimatisation, and start-up
summary: ABSTRACT Diagram showing the lifecycle of a constructed wetland–microbial fuel cell (CW-MFC): design, construction, plant adaptation, start-up and operation. Each stage is illustrated with a photograph or drawing beside a central cross-sect
content: ABSTRACT Diagram showing the lifecycle of a constructed wetland–microbial fuel cell (CW-MFC): design, construction, plant adaptation, start-up and operation. Each stage is illustrated with a photograph or drawing beside a central cross-section of a planted cylindrical reactor containing layered gravel and electrodes. Constructed wetland-microbial fuel cells (CW-MFCs) progress through a life cycle from design to operation, during which wastewater is treated and power generated. Research has focussed on the operational phase, overlooking how the earlier phases of plant adaptation and start-up shape performance; the role of plants during these phases remains poorly understood. This study addresses that gap through a step-by-step framework for the initial phases of the CW-MFC life cycle, establishing a baseline that clarifies their function and improves rigour in the field. To the authors' knowledge, it is the first CW-MFC study to combine criterion-based plant selection with a parallel record of biomass development and open-circuit voltage through start-up. Four Australian native species (Phragmites, Juncus, Philydrum and Eleocharis) were selected, adapted, and assessed during start-up. The highest maximum power density was obtained in Juncus cells at 14.4 mW/m2, 4.2 times that of the control (3.45 mW/m2), followed by Phragmites at 12.6 mW/m2. Faster voltage establishment and better performance correlated with biomass growth rather than plant species, highlighting the role of growing plants in enhancing cell voltage and reducing start-up time. The results suggest that voltage output could act as a biosensor for plant biomass growth, although this rests on correlated time trends and requires further testing.

title: The aging human brain exhibits reduced hemodynamic and cerebrospinal fluid flow waves during sleep
summary: Abstract Aging reduces the quality and quantity of sleep, and sleep disruption is predictive of neurodegeneration and cognitive decline. Sleep loss could affect brain health through disruption of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) circulation, which
content: Abstract Aging reduces the quality and quantity of sleep, and sleep disruption is predictive of neurodegeneration and cognitive decline. Sleep loss could affect brain health through disruption of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) circulation, which is important for brain homeostasis. In young adults, large CSF flow waves appear during non-rapid eye movement sleep; however, whether sleep-dependent brain fluid physiology changes in aging is not known. Here we imaged large-scale CSF flow and hemodynamics in young (18–39 years) and older (60–84 years) adults during nighttime sleep. Sleep-dependent CSF flow was reduced in older adults, and was linked to reduced EEG slow wave power, decreased global hemodynamic oscillations and gray matter atrophy. Using sensory and vasoactive stimuli to drive CSF flow, we found that both neural and cerebrovascular changes contributed to this disruption. These results demonstrate reduced CSF flow during sleep in human aging, before disease onset, and identify parallel neural and hemodynamic mechanisms contributing to this decline.

title: Multi-scale simulations of wind farm impacts on nighttime near-surface temperature in complex terrain
summary: Various studies have shown that wind turbine wakes can induce temperature variations. Investigating these effects near the ground is particularly important for assessing their potential impact on vegetation and human activities. In this stu
content: Various studies have shown that wind turbine wakes can induce temperature variations. Investigating these effects near the ground is particularly important for assessing their potential impact on vegetation and human activities. In this study, the multi-scale Meso-NH/SURFEX/EOL modeling framework, which includes coupled atmosphere, land-surface and actuator models, is used to evaluate the impact of the Ensemble Éolien Catalan wind farm on ground and near-surface temperatures, as well as terrain-specific flow dynamics during a stable nocturnal radiative cooling event associated with frost risk in nearby vineyards. The simulations are performed using nested domains to dynamically downscale the atmospheric conditions from the operational weather forecast AROME-1.3km to a horizontal resolution of 5 m, allowing explicit representation of turbine wakes through rotative actuator disk representation. Turbine-induced meteorological variations are quantified by comparing simulations performed with and without the actuator model. The results reveal that near-surface meteorological responses arise from the combined influence of individual turbine wakes and the large-scale impact of the wind farm, which modifies the flow dynamics and temperature field. In the wind farm, a mean near-surface warming of approximately 0.4 °C is found, with localized temperature increases reaching up to 1.6 °C in the near wake of individual turbines. The strongest perturbations occur for turbines located within valleys, where strong temperature inversions enhance turbine-induced temperature changes. In addition, the wind farm shifts the position of a convergence zone associated with a katabatic flow by about 100–400 m, producing warming anomalies of up to 2 °C along the displaced meteorological front.

title: FluoVolt Staining Compromises Cell Viability and Morphology during Live-Cell Voltage Imaging
summary: Abstract Fluorescent voltage-sensitive dyes (VSDs) enable noninvasive, high-throughput optical monitoring of membrane potential in live cells but may introduce unintended experimental effects that complicate data interpretation. To address
content: Abstract Fluorescent voltage-sensitive dyes (VSDs) enable noninvasive, high-throughput optical monitoring of membrane potential in live cells but may introduce unintended experimental effects that complicate data interpretation. To address this, a key challenge is to characterize and minimize staining- and imaging-associated perturbations to optimize their reliable use across different cell types and imaging conditions. In this study, we systematically evaluate the VSD FluoVolt, its photobleaching, and its effects on cell viability, detachment, and morphology in cancer cell lines (GIN31 and SK-MEL-30) and primary human macrophages. Time-course imaging revealed cell-type-dependent photobleaching, with SK-MEL-30 cells exhibiting rapid fluorescence decay during imaging compared with other cell types. FluoVolt staining combined with excitation was associated with significant cell detachment in GIN31 and SK-MEL-30 cells and with reduced viability accompanied by pronounced morphological changes in GIN31 cells, characterized by a shift from an elongated to an amoeboid-like phenotype. Notably, morphological alterations were observed even in the absence of excitation, indicating that FluoVolt staining alone was also associated with measurable changes in cell morphology. Optimization of staining conditions using reduced dye and loading solution concentrations and incubation time significantly reduced these effects while maintaining measurable fluorescence. Collectively, these findings further characterize the effects associated with FluoVolt staining under the experimental conditions tested, highlight their dependence on cell type and imaging conditions, and emphasize the importance of protocol optimization for the reliable application of FluoVolt in live-cell imaging.

title: Dynamics of confined acoustic phonon modes in nanocrystalline silicon membranes
summary: We report femtosecond time-resolved measurements of confined acoustic phonons in free-standing nanocrystalline silicon membranes and compare them with the crystalline silicon counterpart. While the latter exhibit well-resolved higher-order
content: We report femtosecond time-resolved measurements of confined acoustic phonons in free-standing nanocrystalline silicon membranes and compare them with the crystalline silicon counterpart. While the latter exhibit well-resolved higher-order modes, a strong suppression of these modes is observed in nanocrystalline samples. The suppression is strongly frequency dependent and becomes more pronounced as the phonon wavelength approaches the characteristic grain size. Analysis of the phonon lifetimes reveals an additional frequency-dependent scattering mechanism in nanocrystalline silicon, with a scattering rate that scales approximately as $f^2$, where $f$ is the phonon frequency. The measured sound velocity is consistent with previous reports for nanocrystalline silicon and indicates an effective elastic response arising from multiple crystallographic orientations. These results establish coherent phonons as a sensitive probe of microstructure-dependent scattering in nanocrystalline materials and indicate that grain boundaries act as an effective spectral filter for high-frequency acoustic phonons.

title: Layered Double Hydroxide Nanoparticles Induce Composition-Dependent Cytotoxic and Phenotypic Effects in Mammalian Cells
summary: Abstract Layered double hydroxides (LDHs) are increasingly explored for agricultural, environmental, and biodelivery applications, but their composition-dependent effects on mammalian cells remain insufficiently defined. Here, we synthesize
content: Abstract Layered double hydroxides (LDHs) are increasingly explored for agricultural, environmental, and biodelivery applications, but their composition-dependent effects on mammalian cells remain insufficiently defined. Here, we synthesized Al–Ni, Al–Co, and Al–Cu LDH nanoparticles and evaluated their physicochemical properties and biological responses across exposure-relevant mammalian cell models. The formulations showed hydrodynamic diameters of approximately 200–300 nm, moderate dispersity, strongly positive surface charge, and characteristic lamellar LDH features. Cytotoxicity was assessed using MTT, Calcein-AM, and Hoechst–PI assays in HaCaT, A549, and HT-29 cells, representing dermal, pulmonary, and intestinal exposure contexts, together with NIH/3T3 fibroblasts as a sensitive comparative model. LDH toxicity was strongly dependent on metal composition and cell type, following a general trend where Al–Cu showed the highest overall cytotoxic activity, while Al–Ni and Al–Co produced responses dependent on the formulation and cell type. To detect cellular perturbations beyond overt viability loss, we applied high-content imaging using Live Cell Painting. Multiparametric single-cell profiling revealed composition- and dose-dependent alterations in acidic vesicle organization, nuclear texture, and cytoplasmic granularity. Notably, phenotypic deviations were detected at concentrations below those producing measurable effects in conventional viability assays, and linear discriminant analysis separated the phenotypic signatures induced by the three LDH formulations. Together, these findings show that LDH biological activity cannot be generalized across metal compositions and that high-content phenotypic profiling provides added sensitivity for detecting early cellular perturbations. This integrated approach supports composition-aware nanosafety evaluation and may inform the safer development of LDH-based technologies for agricultural and biotechnological applications.

title: Neighborhood Exposome at Birth and Trajectories of Epigenetic Age Acceleration Across Childhood
summary: Importance Epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) has been linked to increased disease risk in adults, yet its developmental trajectories and early-life neighborhood determinants remain poorly understood. Objective To examine whether there are a
content: Importance Epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) has been linked to increased disease risk in adults, yet its developmental trajectories and early-life neighborhood determinants remain poorly understood. Objective To examine whether there are associations between the neighborhood exposome at birth and EAA trajectories from early childhood through adolescence. Design, Setting, and Participants This longitudinal cohort study used data from Project Viva, a prebirth cohort that enrolled pregnant women in eastern Massachusetts from April 22, 1999, to July 31, 2002. Participants included 570 children with available peripheral blood DNA methylation data, complete neighborhood characteristics, and complete covariates. Data were analyzed from August 19, 2024, to August 21, 2026. Exposures Neighborhood exposome profiles at birth derived from 22 census tract–level characteristics across 4 domains (area deprivation, social fragmentation, population density, and environmental quality) using self-organizing maps. Main Outcomes and Measures EAA was calculated at 3, 8, and 13 years of age using the Horvath, Skin & Blood, and Wu epigenetic clocks. Trajectories were identified using latent class linear mixed models. Associations between neighborhood profiles and EAA trajectories were estimated using multinomial mixed models. Results Among 570 children (mean [SD] age at early childhood, 3.2 [0.4] years; 305 [53.5%] male), 3 EAA trajectory groups (stable, increasing, and decreasing for the Horvath and Skin & Blood clocks or low-baseline for the Wu clock) and 3 neighborhood profiles were identified. Compared with profile 1 (suburban, lowest adverse exposures [n = 278]), children born into profile 2 (urban, high residential instability and single-person households, and highway proximity [n = 168]) had greater odds of increasing EAA for the Wu clock (adjusted odds ratio, 1.67 [95% CI, 1.03-2.69]). Profile 3 (urban, high socioeconomic deprivation and pollution [n = 124]) showed no associations. Conclusions and Relevance In this longitudinal cohort study, birth into neighborhoods characterized by high residential instability and single-person households and highway proximity was associated with increasing Wu EAA trajectories across childhood. These findings suggest that early-life neighborhood conditions, encompassing both social and physical environmental factors, may represent targets for interventions aimed at reducing long-term disease risk. Further research is needed to clarify the implications of these findings for later health and prevention.

title: Engineering of halohydrin dehalogenase IcHheG via semi-rational design for enantioselective synthesis of (R)-5-phenoxymethyl-2-oxazolidinone
summary: Abstract Enantiomerically pure oxazolidinones are widely used as important chiral auxiliaries in organic synthesis; however, efficient methods for their preparation remain scarce. In this study, we report the engineering of halohydrin dehal
content: Abstract Enantiomerically pure oxazolidinones are widely used as important chiral auxiliaries in organic synthesis; however, efficient methods for their preparation remain scarce. In this study, we report the engineering of halohydrin dehalogenase Ic HheG from Ilumatobacter coccineus through semi-rational design to catalyze the enantioselective ring-opening of phenyl glycidyl ether (PGE) with cyanate, as well as the direct synthesis from the precursor 1-chloro-3-phenoxy-2-propanol, enabling the efficient synthesis of ( R )-5-phenoxymethyl-2-oxazolidinone. Through systematic single-point and combinatorial mutagenesis, we identified the optimal double mutant, Ic HheG-L103H/N196W, which exhibited markedly improved enantioselectivity, affording the product in 95% ee . Sequential kinetic resolution of 1-chloro-3-phenoxy-2-propanol using Ic HheG-L103H/N196W yielded ( R )-5-phenoxymethyl-2-oxazolidinone in 99% ee (49.5% yield) and ( S )-1a in > 98% ee . Molecular docking analysis of wild-type Ic HheG and the mutant L103H/N196W with PGE and 1-chloro-3-phenoxy-2-propanol revealed that alterations in the substrate-binding pocket increased the distances from ( S )-PGE and ( R )-1-chloro-3-phenoxy-2-propanol to the catalytic residues, likely accounting for the enhanced enantioselectivity. Collectively, this mutant holds great potential as a biocatalyst for the enantioselective synthesis of chiral ( R )-5-phenoxymethyl-2-oxazolidinone.

title: Satellite-driven monitoring of suspended sediment concentration in large river systems: an application to the Loire River, France
summary: Abstract Suspended sediment concentration (SSC) is a key indicator of river morphodynamics and water quality, yet long-term spatial monitoring remains limited because in situ measurements are sparse and discontinuous. By integrating field o
content: Abstract Suspended sediment concentration (SSC) is a key indicator of river morphodynamics and water quality, yet long-term spatial monitoring remains limited because in situ measurements are sparse and discontinuous. By integrating field observations with multispectral Landsat imagery, this study develops a satellite-based framework to estimate SSC along the Loire River (France) over the period 2005–2025 in low to medium flow conditions with an SSC below 100 mg/l. Reflectance data from Landsat 5, 7, 8, and 9 were extracted using Google Earth Engine and matched with in situ SSC measurements within a ± 5-day temporal window. A feed-forward neural network was trained to predict SSC from selected spectral bands (B2, B3, B4, B5, and B7), with separate models developed for low, intermediate, and high turbidity regimes to improve predictive stability, and then recombined to obtain a single model. This complete neural network achieved high performance ( R 2 = 0.941, RMSE = 3.78 mg/l, PBIAS = 6.53%). To enable large-scale operational mapping, the neural network predictions were approximated through a compact surrogate model based on quadratic feature expansion and ridge regression, maintaining strong accuracy in reproducing observed SSC ( R 2 = 0.890, RMSE = 5.17 mg/l, PBIAS = 9.92%). The surrogate model was implemented in Google Earth Engine to generate spatially continuous SSC maps along the river corridor. The proposed approach demonstrates the capability of combining machine learning and optical satellite imagery to efficiently reconstruct SSC patterns in the Loire River and provides a scalable framework for monitoring suspended sediment dynamics in large river systems, in particular during low to medium flow conditions.

title: Early Heat Stress in Wheat: Osmolytes and Antioxidants as Candidate Biochemical Indicators of Tolerance
summary: Heat stress is posing a serious threat to crop physiology due to a consistent increase in global temperatures. In crops, the seedling stage is the most temperature‐sensitive stage. The present study was conducted to identify candidate bioch
content: Heat stress is posing a serious threat to crop physiology due to a consistent increase in global temperatures. In crops, the seedling stage is the most temperature‐sensitive stage. The present study was conducted to identify candidate biochemical indicators associated with the early heat response of 18 wheat ( Triticum aestivum L.) genotypes at seedling stage to find the reason for good seedling establishment and high yield of wheat genotypes grown under early sown conditions. Twelve wheat genotypes, along with six heat tolerant check cultivars, were exposed to two temperature conditions, i.e., 25 °C (control) and 35 °C (high stress). A significant increase in proline content, α‐tocopherol, reducing and nonreducing sugars in 12‐days‐old seedlings genotypes was recorded at 35 °C. In high yielding wheat genotypes, increased total sugar content was accompanied by enhanced α‐amylase activity and reduced starch content. Antioxidative potential was upregulated at 35 °C via enhanced activities of superoxide dismutase (SOD) (47.03%–88.61%), ascorbate peroxidase (APX) (33.03%–88.73%), catalase (CAT) (47.37%–77.38%), peroxidase (POD) (24.10%– 66.64%), and glutathione reductase (GR) (24.01%–85.16%). Reactive oxygen species (ROS) indicators, viz., hydrogen peroxide (91.67% and 93.44%) and malondialdehyde (80.51% and 88.43%) content increased in low yielding genotypes EWS 171 and EWS 433 at 35 °C. Correlation analysis showed strong positive correlations among antioxidant enzymes (GR, APX, SOD, and POD) and sugars (sucrose and reducing sugar), indicating a possible physiological association among these traits under heat stress rather than a demonstrated regulatory pathway, while total free amino acids and H 2 O 2 showed significant negative correlations with these enzymes, suggesting their inhibitory or stress‐indicator roles. Moreover, principal component analysis (PCA) further elaborates the role of enzymatic and nonenzymatic antioxidants in plant defense mechanism under heat stress conditions and clearly indicates the distinct behavioral patterns of wheat genotypes under early sown conditions.

title: Precision studies of astrophysically relevant nuclear structure and reactions: from MAMI to MESA .
summary: Precision electron scattering has long been a powerful tool to probe nuclear structure and reaction mechanisms relevant for nuclear astrophysics. At Mainz, the MAMI accelerator and the upcoming MESA facility provide unique opportunities for
content: Precision electron scattering has long been a powerful tool to probe nuclear structure and reaction mechanisms relevant for nuclear astrophysics. At Mainz, the MAMI accelerator and the upcoming MESA facility provide unique opportunities for high-precision measurements at low energies. Dedicated experimental programs aim to investigate excited states in light nuclei as well as reaction cross sections that play a role in stellar environments. In this contribution, we will give an overview of the current and planned nuclear astrophysics program at MAMI and MESA. Motivated by potential future capabilities at Jefferson Lab in the energy range of roughly 10–100 MeV (and possibly up to a few hundred MeV), we will briefly discuss possible areas of complementarity between Mainz and Jefferson Lab.

title: A Unified Reactivity Scale Predicts Nonenzymatic Phosphoryl Transfer and Nucleophilic Catalysis in Water
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
summary: Abstract The transfer of phosphoryl groups plays a central role in biochemical energy metabolism. Understanding how such reactions could have occurred before the emergence of enzymes is thus crucial for elucidating the chemical foundations
content: Abstract The transfer of phosphoryl groups plays a central role in biochemical energy metabolism. Understanding how such reactions could have occurred before the emergence of enzymes is thus crucial for elucidating the chemical foundations of life. Although the factors governing the mechanisms of phosphoryl transfer in water are well understood, predicting whether a given nucleophile and phosphorylating agent will undergo productive phosphoryl transfer rather than hydrolysis remains difficult, thereby hindering the rational exploration of nonenzymatic phosphorylation reactions. Herein, we establish a quantitative reactivity scale that predicts absolute rate constants for nonenzymatic phosphoryl transfer reactions in water based on a linear free-energy relationship (LFER). Using high-throughput kinetics, we measured 11,520 phosphoryl transfer reactions for 145 unique combinations of nucleophiles and phosphorylating agents under varying reaction conditions. Mechanism-specific rate constants extracted from this data for 102 substrate pairs, together with values scraped from the literature, enabled us to parametrize an LFER that places 34 phosphorylating agents and 45 nucleophiles on a unified quantitative reactivity scale, enabling predictions across 14 orders of magnitude in reactivity. Finally, we show that the empirically derived reactivity parameters can be used to predict optimal nucleophilic catalysts by balancing the competing steps in catalytic turnover, as experimentally validated for the reaction of monoamidophosphate with pyridines. For phosphorylating agents of intermediate electrophilicity such as ATP, imidazole is predicted to be the optimal catalyst, offering a kinetic rationale for the prevalence of histidine residues in enzymatic phosphoryl transfer. Together, high-throughput kinetics and data-driven modeling establish a predictive framework for exploring nonenzymatic phosphoryl transfer reactions in water.

title: Phytoplankton pigment retrieval using remote sensing: methods, validation and evidence readiness
summary: Abstract Optical observations of phytoplankton pigments can extend aquatic monitoring beyond bulk biomass, although their value depends on how spectral information, reference measurements and validation are connected. This review synthesize
content: Abstract Optical observations of phytoplankton pigments can extend aquatic monitoring beyond bulk biomass, although their value depends on how spectral information, reference measurements and validation are connected. This review synthesizes pigment targets, observation systems and retrieval approaches in 107 studies published from 2020 to August 2025 and evaluates their evidence through six cumulative readiness levels. Chlorophyll-a and phycocyanin dominated the literature, while accessory pigments provided more detailed, often shared associations with community composition. Hyperspectral measurements supported spectral decomposition and multipigment estimation, whereas multispectral satellites provided repeated spatial coverage. Across these architectures, performance depended on optical conditions, measurement correspondence and the domain represented by validation. Structured independent validation was the first unmet requirement in 54.4% of direct retrieval configurations. No configuration met the operational criteria of the main rubric, although joint relaxation of transfer and implementation requirements changed this outcome. Cross-lake experiments and satellite applications showed that favourable predictive association could coexist with substantial concentration error, analytical variability or sensitivity to atmospheric correction. The findings support development that combines improved pigment discrimination with traceable analytical references and evaluation across relevant environments. Matching field sampling to the spatial and temporal support of image products, while maintaining quality control and uncertainty characterization, is necessary to translate retrieval advances into reliable environmental monitoring.

title: Informal green spaces as a strategic opportunity for urban rewilding in densely built environments
summary: Abstract Urban rewilding acts as a promising strategy for increasing urban resilience and biodiversity. It is noteworthy that the use of urban rewilding in densely built environments has not been widely explored. These environments, are cha
content: Abstract Urban rewilding acts as a promising strategy for increasing urban resilience and biodiversity. It is noteworthy that the use of urban rewilding in densely built environments has not been widely explored. These environments, are characterized by scarce land and acute socio-ecological conflicts. In this study, the potential of Informal Green Spaces (IGS) is investigated as strategic rewilding opportunities. To be specific, IGS show potential of spontaneous, low-maintenance sites. Haidian District, Beijing, was selected as a case study. On the basis of a GIS-based Urban Rewilding Opportunity Index (UROI), Urban Rewilding Opportunity Spaces (UROS) were mapped. In 35 plots of the dense built-up area in the Fifth Ring Road, field surveys were carried out. As indicated by the results, a spatial mismatch was found. Specifically, high UROI values were primarily reported in the mountainous areas and large parks. However, the highest abundance of IGS was identified in the relatively low UROIs in the dense urban core, which could take up 88.99% of the total IGS area and 88% of patch counts. Vacant lots were dominated by area of 72%. Besides, structure-associated and gap spaces were numerous but fragmented. Vegetation analysis indicated a “mid-layer deficiency”. The low shrub cover of 9.14% was identified. Notably, structure-associated IGS showed 100% vine cover. Furthermore, 64% of IGS patches were fully accessible. As revealed by the above-mentioned findings, IGS are not merely residual spaces, their vegetation and accessibility characteristics make them activation-ready. They are a critical, albeit neglected, resource for urban rewilding. These findings open new avenues for urban rewilding in densely built environments, with the potential to support urban regeneration while making cities wilder and more livable.

title: Neural dynamics track the approach to physical exhaustion
summary: Physical exhaustion has long been described through its cardiorespiratory and metabolic cost, while the neural dynamics of its approach remain largely unexplored. Here we recorded high-density electroencephalography in 28 trained cyclists d
content: Physical exhaustion has long been described through its cardiorespiratory and metabolic cost, while the neural dynamics of its approach remain largely unexplored. Here we recorded high-density electroencephalography in 28 trained cyclists during a maximal incremental test to characterise how neural dynamics change towards exhaustion. As physiological strain rose, oscillatory power shifted to lower frequencies, neural activity became more regular and predictable, and functional coupling extended to longer timescales. Participant-specific models built on neural dynamics tracked proximity to exhaustion with accuracy comparable to cardiorespiratory measures. Over the final minutes, neural features remained informative while cardiorespiratory measures lost accuracy. Models trained across participants still tracked proximity to exhaustion, but less precisely. The approach to exhaustion thus follows a common neural path, tuned to each individual.

title: Christian missionary activity and the dearth of conversions in the Arabian Gulf, 1800–1970: a comparative study with the Middle East and Sub-Saharan Africa
summary: Between the nineteenth and mid-twentieth centuries, Christian missionary organizations invested considerable resources in the Arabian Gulf, the broader Middle East, and sub-Saharan Africa, with dramatically divergent outcomes. Christianity
content: Between the nineteenth and mid-twentieth centuries, Christian missionary organizations invested considerable resources in the Arabian Gulf, the broader Middle East, and sub-Saharan Africa, with dramatically divergent outcomes. Christianity in sub-Saharan Africa grew from roughly nine million adherents in 1900 to over 380 million by 2000; missions in Egypt produced no more than 200 documented Muslim converts in a century; and in the Arabian Gulf, nearly a century of organized Protestant labor produced fewer than fourteen documented conversions among the Arab Muslim population across all stations. Drawing on peer-reviewed scholarship and primary missionary sources, this paper assembles the quantitative conversion evidence for all three regions and advances a multi-causal explanation centered on six factors: the social cost of apostasy operating through communal rather than judicial mechanisms; the fusion of Arab ethnic and Islamic religious identity; the political association of Christianity with Western aggression; the institutional resilience of Islamic scholarly networks; the enforced shift from evangelism to humanitarianism; and the Gulf’s pre-Islamic Nestorian Christian heritage and voluntary seventh-century transition to Islam. This final factor, largely absent from previous comparative analyses, constitutes the study’s most distinctive contribution.

title: Inflammation-driven epigenetic memory in infertility and chronic endometritis
summary: Chronic endometritis (CE) is a persistent, low-grade inflammatory condition of the endometrium, typically caused by microbial infections. CE is often asymptomatic, leading to frequent underdiagnosis. It is frequently identified during the a
content: Chronic endometritis (CE) is a persistent, low-grade inflammatory condition of the endometrium, typically caused by microbial infections. CE is often asymptomatic, leading to frequent underdiagnosis. It is frequently identified during the assessment of causes for infertility. Even after resolving the infectious etiology by antibiotic treatment, infertility persists in a number of patients. Emerging evidence from chronic inflammatory diseases affecting epithelial tissues, e.g., in the gut, suggests that inflammatory conditions can induce long-lasting epigenetic changes, e.g., in innate immune cells. Notably, tissues outside the immune system can also retain memory of inflammatory events and environmental insults via epigenetic modifications. This review summarizes how epigenetic changes can affect endometrial function, drawing on current knowledge of CE. It also discusses how inflammation prompts these changes. We propose that persistent epigenetic memory in both immune and non-immune endometrial cells plays a crucial role in sustaining CE-associated adversities, such as infertility. Future research should focus on pinpointing specific epigenetic patterns in CE and exploring how inflammation-induced memory leads to cellular dysfunction in the endometrium. Understanding these mechanisms will advance CE diagnosis and open doors to new treatment options for infertility, focusing on reversing the inflammatory memory retained upon treatment of CE.

title: Physical consistency and completeness in the data-driven modeling of microwave absorbing materials
summary: Machine learning (ML) has been applied to the modeling of microwave absorbing materials, including the prediction of electromagnetic parameters and reflection loss (RL), yet the physical consistency of such models is rarely examined. This p
content: Machine learning (ML) has been applied to the modeling of microwave absorbing materials, including the prediction of electromagnetic parameters and reflection loss (RL), yet the physical consistency of such models is rarely examined. This paper addresses two types of physical consistency problems in data-driven modeling: the physical inconsistency of predicted outputs and the physical incompleteness of input features. On the output side, we constructed a numerical integrator based on the Kramers-Kronig (KK) relation to test permittivity spectra output by ML models. The results show that none of the four examined spectra from three studies satisfied the KK relation, indicating that the model outputs markedly violate physical consistency. On the input side, we took a published MXene study as a case example. There is no thickness, which determines the RL jointly with other variables, in its feature space. Using physically consistent synthetic data, we conducted controlled experiments under two data settings and two partition schemes. It was found that without the thickness, the model captured only a limited part of the RL variance and could not distinguish the labels corresponding to different thicknesses. Adding the thickness restored the performance, with the R2 rising from 0.364 to 0.956 under the fullthickness setting. Finally, we further discussed three approaches to embedding the KK constraint into the modeling workflow. Our results suggest that physical consistency and completeness are necessary conditions for building reliable data-driven models, and that global integral constraints such as the KK relation cannot be learned implicitly from small samples.

title: Oxygen isotopes reveal a significant Middle Pleistocene transition from temperate rainforest to arid desert-like conditions in eastern Australia
summary: Reconstructing terrestrial palaeoenvironmental change during the Middle Pleistocene is essential for understanding ecosystem stability and resilience under long-term climatic forcing. However, well-dated, quantitative records from Australia
content: Reconstructing terrestrial palaeoenvironmental change during the Middle Pleistocene is essential for understanding ecosystem stability and resilience under long-term climatic forcing. However, well-dated, quantitative records from Australia remain limited. Fossil deposits at Mount Etna Caves, central eastern Queensland, preserve two taxonomically distinct faunal assemblages that have been interpreted as a substantial ecological transition from a diverse rainforest system to an arid-adapted faunal community. Previous interpretations of this transition have relied primarily on faunal evidence, with limited site-specific geochemical validation. Here, we integrate oxygen isotope (δ 18 O) analyses of fossil macropodid enamel with refined in-situ U-Th geochronology to reconstruct changes in hydroclimatic conditions across this transition. New U-Th ages better constrain deposition of the arid-adapted assemblage to a narrow interval between 199 ± 5 and 205 ± 4 ka. Fossils from older deposits (pre-280 ka) exhibit consistently low δ 18 O values (−2.59 ± 0.54 ‰), suggesting relatively humid conditions, whereas the younger deposit is markedly enriched (4.59 ± 1.92 ‰). Random Forest classification models trained on modern macropodine δ 18 O data suggest that pre-280 ka assemblages show strongest similarity with humid temperate forest environments analogous to modern temperate oceanic (Cfb-like) systems of southeastern Australia and highland New Guinea. In contrast, the post-205 ka assemblages show the strongest affinity with arid, hot desert (BWh-like) conditions characteristic of central Australia. This transition coincides with broader Middle Pleistocene climatic reorganisation centred on ∼270 ka, which may have contributed to sustained regional drying. These findings suggest that long-term climatic forcing may push ecosystems beyond hydroclimatic thresholds, resulting in major ecological reorganisation, altered species distributions, and reduced biogeographic connectivity. By providing a directly dated, multi-proxy terrestrial record, this study highlights how substantial environmental change during the Quaternary offers an important analogue for understanding ecosystem vulnerability under ongoing and future climate change.

title: The genus Ellobium Röding, 1798 (Gastropoda, Ellobiidae) in Vietnam: updated species accounts and the first country record of Ellobium tornatelliforme (Petit de la Saussaye, 1843)
summary: We provide the first voucher-based review of Ellobium Röding, 1798 (Gastropoda, Ellobiidae) in Vietnam and confirm four species. Ellobium tornatelliforme (Petit de la Saussaye, 1843) is recorded from Vietnam for the first time. We update th
content: We provide the first voucher-based review of Ellobium Röding, 1798 (Gastropoda, Ellobiidae) in Vietnam and confirm four species. Ellobium tornatelliforme (Petit de la Saussaye, 1843) is recorded from Vietnam for the first time. We update the distributions and habitat data of E. aurisjudae (Linnaeus, 1758), E. aurismidae (Linnaeus, 1758), and E. chinense (L. Pfeiffer, 1854) based on voucher specimens. An identification key and revised species accounts are provided, establishing a taxonomically verified baseline for future taxonomic, biogeographical, and conservation studies.

title: Lattice Defect‐Inspired Metastructures Enabling Ultralight and Mechanically Robust Broadband Microwave Absorbers
summary: ABSTRACT Additively manufactured lightweight lattice metastructures offer a promising route for electromagnetic interference (EMI) mitigation in aerospace systems, owing to their highly tailorable electromagnetic (EM) response and mechanica
content: ABSTRACT Additively manufactured lightweight lattice metastructures offer a promising route for electromagnetic interference (EMI) mitigation in aerospace systems, owing to their highly tailorable electromagnetic (EM) response and mechanical performance. However, progress is hindered by poorly understood structure–property relationships and the rapid loss of mechanical integrity due to ultrafine structures at low densities. Herein, we establish a quantitative structure–effective permittivity–absorption performance mapping and EM optimization framework based on effective medium approximation and transmission line theory. Inspired by crystal defect engineering, defect‐engineered octet‐truss (DOT) metastructures are introduced via this framework to overcome the trade‐off between mechanical strength and microwave absorption while pushing the density limit toward foam‐like regimes. DOTs achieve an exceptional effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 37.5 GHz (2.5–40 GHz, 15 mm thickness) and up to 3.8× higher compressive strength compared with conventional gradient octet‐truss (OT) counterparts. Furthermore, a strut–sheet hybrid DOT reaches an ultralow density of 0.09 g cm − 3 with great printability while maintaining a broad EAB of 35.6 GHz (4.4–40 GHz). The proposed optimization framework and design methodology could be applicable to additive manufacturing technologies with diverse material systems for developing high‐performance multifunctional lattice metastructure absorbers for EM compatibility in next‐generation aerial platforms.

title: Cuproptosis in the tumor microenvironment: metabolic–immune regulatory mechanisms and therapeutic potential
source: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
summary: Copper is an essential trace element involved in mitochondrial respiration, redox homeostasis, and numerous enzymatic reactions. Recent studies across multiple cancers have reported changes in tissue copper levels, circulating copper-relate
content: Copper is an essential trace element involved in mitochondrial respiration, redox homeostasis, and numerous enzymatic reactions. Recent studies across multiple cancers have reported changes in tissue copper levels, circulating copper-related indicators, and networks governing copper uptake, transport, and efflux. The discovery of cuproptosis, a copper-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by mitochondrial metabolism, further linked copper homeostasis to cell death regulation. Its key molecular features include copper binding to lipoylated tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle proteins, aggregation of lipoylated proteins, loss of iron–sulfur cluster proteins, and proteotoxic stress. Within the tumor microenvironment, heterogeneity in copper uptake and export, TCA cycle activity, ferredoxin 1 (FDX1) function, protein lipoylation, and redox buffering collectively shapes cuproptosis susceptibility, which cannot be reliably predicted by tissue copper content or a single metabolic phenotype alone. Preclinical studies of cuproptosis-inducing interventions have also reported damage-associated molecular pattern release, dendritic cell maturation, CD8 + T-cell infiltration, and myeloid-cell remodeling; however, these effects often coexist with oxidative stress, other forms of cell death, or multimodal therapies, and their mechanistic specificity for cuproptosis remains variable. This review examines cuproptosis from a tumor microenvironment perspective by integrating clinical and molecular evidence of altered copper homeostasis, defining the boundaries among copper dysregulation, general copper-related cytotoxicity, and cuproptosis, and discussing how copper availability, the FDX1–protein lipoylation axis, mitochondrial metabolic states, and microenvironmental adaptation influence susceptibility. We further evaluate immune effects according to the strength of available evidence and summarize therapeutic strategies involving copper ionophores, copper-homeostasis modulation, metabolic sensitization, nanodelivery, and combination immunotherapy. This framework clarifies the relationships among copper homeostasis, tumor metabolism, cuproptosis susceptibility, and immune responses, while highlighting priorities for mechanistic investigation and therapeutic translation.

title: Lipidomic analysis of postprandial mesenteric lymph from wild type and Dennd5b knockout mice.
summary: Chylomicrons are intestine-derived lipoproteins that transport dietary lipids from the intestine to the systemic circulation. Although the composition of chylomicrons may influence their peripheral metabolism and biological functions, the l
content: Chylomicrons are intestine-derived lipoproteins that transport dietary lipids from the intestine to the systemic circulation. Although the composition of chylomicrons may influence their peripheral metabolism and biological functions, the lipid composition of newly secreted chylomicrons remains incompletely characterized. In this study, we combined a conscious mesenteric lymph fistula model with mass spectrometry-based lipidomics to characterize changes in the intestinal lymph lipidome following duodenal lipid administration in wild type and Dennd5b-deficient mice, a model of impaired intestinal chylomicron secretion. In wild type mice, lipid administration significantly increased lymphatic triglyceride output and altered the abundance of multiple lipid species, including glycerolipids, glycerophospholipids, and sphingolipids. Notably, ceramides and hexosylceramides exhibited disproportionate increases relative to their abundance in the administered lipid. In contrast, Dennd5b-deficient mice exhibited a near-complete blunting of the postprandial lymphatic lipidomic response, with markedly attenuated export across multiple lipid classes. Genotype-dependent differences were also evident in baseline lymph, indicating that Dennd5b influences lymphatic lipid composition under both basal and postprandial conditions. Together, these findings demonstrate that the physiological impact of Dennd5b deficiency on intestinal lipid trafficking extends well beyond triglycerides, underscoring an essential role for Dennd5b-dependent chylomicron secretion in the coordinated lymphatic export of dietary and endogenous lipids.

title: Non-equilibrium resonance scattering in intramolecular charge transport drives conformational changes
summary: Abstract Intramolecular charge transport is conventionally described as proceeding along a static ground-state potential, with the carrier acting as a passive probe of a fixed electronic landscape. Here, using alkanethiolate-based molecular
content: Abstract Intramolecular charge transport is conventionally described as proceeding along a static ground-state potential, with the carrier acting as a passive probe of a fixed electronic landscape. Here, using alkanethiolate-based molecular junctions, we show that the carrier itself can drive conformational reorganization once the applied bias brings backbone-delocalized molecular orbitals into the transmission window. Combined electrical and in situ structural measurements resolve a threshold-activated transition to a gauche-defect state coincident with the onset of orbital-mediated transport. We rationalize this coupling through a quantum resonance scattering framework in which accessible orbitals act as scattering potentials that transiently host the injected charge, depositing energy into nuclear motion with an efficiency set by molecule–electrode coupling and Franck–Condon overlap. The framework quantitatively reproduces the measured response and predicts the enhanced behavior of amide-containing junctions. Together, these results suggest that charge-transport–structure feedback can be understood in terms of microscopic parameters governing resonance-mediated energy transfer, and that these parameters may be tuned through chemical design.

title: Enamel thickness in the stem hylobatid Kapi ramnagarensis (Primates, Hylobatidae)
summary: Abstract Enamel thickness has been extensively investigated in extant and fossil hominids, yet comparable data for hylobatids remain scarce. Existing studies are limited to Symphalangus syndactylus , Hylobates lar , and Hylobates muelleri a
content: Abstract Enamel thickness has been extensively investigated in extant and fossil hominids, yet comparable data for hylobatids remain scarce. Existing studies are limited to Symphalangus syndactylus , Hylobates lar , and Hylobates muelleri and are based on relatively small samples. These studies have characterized enamel thickness as thin in Symphalangus and Hy. lar and intermediate‐thin in Hy. muelleri . The polarity of these conditions within Hylobatidae also remains unresolved because stem representatives of the clade have only recently been discovered. Here, we used microcomputed tomography to examine lower third molar (M 3 ) enamel thickness in the stem hylobatid Kapi ramnagarensis from the Miocene Lower Siwaliks locality of Ramnagar. We also provide new comparative data from 19 M 3 s of extant hylobatids representing all four living genera. Average (AET) and relative (RET) enamel thickness were quantified from two‐dimensional virtual sections passing through the dentin horns of the two mesial cusps. The M 3 of the single Kapi specimen exhibits enamel thickness values within the range observed in extant hylobatids, albeit near the lower end of that distribution, with RET most closely matching that of Hoolock leuconedys . Parsimony‐based ancestral state reconstructions of M 3 RET using gap‐weighted coding hypothesize an intermediate‐thin enamel condition at the base of Hominoidea. Within Hylobatidae, the ancestral state was likewise reconstructed as intermediate‐thin enamel. Although RET provides valuable phylogenetic information, its interpretation remains challenging due to the limited data for early catarrhines and hominoids and the pervasive influence of homoplasy. Larger samples will help clarify patterns of enamel thickness variation within hylobatids and across Hominoidea.

title: Multi-source ecological indicators characterize contrasting responses to shrub encroachment in semi-arid grasslands
summary: Shrub encroachment is a widespread vegetation transition in semi-arid grasslands, with potentially contrasting effects on vegetation condition, surface thermal environments, water fluxes, and landscape configuration. However, the responses
content: Shrub encroachment is a widespread vegetation transition in semi-arid grasslands, with potentially contrasting effects on vegetation condition, surface thermal environments, water fluxes, and landscape configuration. However, the responses of these ecological attributes to shrub-encroached grassland (SEG) area proportion remain incompletely understood. Here, multi-source remote sensing observations from 2000 to 2020 were used to examine fractional vegetation cover (FVC), land surface temperature (LST), evapotranspiration (ET), and landscape metrics across the Xilin Gol grasslands, northern China. PG (pure grassland)–SEG comparisons were conducted using both all selected grids and spatially matched grids, while linear, nonlinear, and generalized additive models were used to characterize FVC responses. The results showed that FVC differences between SEG and PG grids were smaller and less consistent after spatial matching, and no clear breakpoint was identified in the continuous FVC response analyses. Matched comparisons revealed lower daytime LST in SEG grids during summer and higher daytime LST during winter, whereas the pronounced thermal contrasts observed in unmatched comparisons were substantially reduced after matching. Growing-season ET was generally lower in matched SEG grids than in PG grids during 2005–2020, and ET generally declined with increasing SEG area proportion. At the 3-km scale, landscape metrics exhibited distinct nonlinear response patterns: landscape shape complexity and diversity initially increased and subsequently declined at higher SEG area proportions, while grassland-class area dominance and aggregation generally decreased. These findings demonstrate that vegetation, thermal, hydrological, and landscape indicators provide complementary information on ecological variation associated with shrub encroachment. The observed patterns should be interpreted in light of environmental confounding, indicator-specific responses, and differences in analytical spatial scales.

title: Multi-temporal flood susceptibility mapping using Sentinel-1 SAR time-series and machine learning: case study of Sebkhet Ariana (NE Tunisia)
summary: Floods represent a recurrent natural hazard in Mediterranean coastal environments, driven by climate variability, low-lying topography, and land-use change. This study proposes a multi-temporal flood monitoring and susceptibility framework
content: Floods represent a recurrent natural hazard in Mediterranean coastal environments, driven by climate variability, low-lying topography, and land-use change. This study proposes a multi-temporal flood monitoring and susceptibility framework using Sentinel-1 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data for the Sebkhet Ariana coastal wetland, Tunisia. Monthly SAR composites were generated for September from 2019 to 2024. Flooded areas were extracted using histogram-based minimum error thresholding on VV-polarised backscatter. Multi-temporal observations were used to derive flood frequency indicators. A Random Forest model integrated SAR-derived flood frequency with environmental conditioning factors from Copernicus DEM and ESA WorldCover to produce a flood susceptibility map. Results show strong interannual variability, with recurrent flooding concentrated in low-lying and urban–agricultural transition areas. The Sentinel-1-derived patterns showed generally good correspondence with independent Sentinel-2/MNDWI observations, although the degree of agreement varied among monitoring periods, particularly during the anomalous 2023 conditions. Under a class-balanced independent buffered spatial validation design, the Random Forest model achieved an Overall Accuracy of 89.2% and a ROC-AUC of 0.953, demonstrating discrimination between flooded and non-flooded, confirming the effectiveness of combining SAR time series and machine learning for flood recurrence analysis and susceptibility mapping. The study provides a reproducible approach for flood monitoring in data-scarce coastal environments.

title: Sourdough Bioactives from Fermentation to Human Physiology: Biosynthesis, Bioavailability, Mechanisms and Clinical Evidence
summary: Sourdough is a metabolically active cereal ecosystem in which lactic acid bacteria, yeasts and endogenous flour enzymes transform carbohydrates, proteins and phytochemicals. These reactions can increase organic acids, release phenolic compo
content: Sourdough is a metabolically active cereal ecosystem in which lactic acid bacteria, yeasts and endogenous flour enzymes transform carbohydrates, proteins and phytochemicals. These reactions can increase organic acids, release phenolic compounds, generate peptides, form exopolysaccharides and, in strain- tand substrate-dependent systems, enrich γ-aminobutyric acid and selected vitamins. However, the detection of a compound in fermented dough does not establish physiological benefit: This narrative review organizes the evidence from precursor and microbial pathway to processing stability, gastrointestinal fate, mechanical and clinical effect.
