Appraisal was narrative, not a systematic review; evidence strength reflected design limitations, consistency, directness, precision and plausibility. Strong evidence supports acidification, phytate degradation, phenolic release and technological functions of exopolysaccharides. Mechanistic evidence for antioxidant, antihypertensive, immunomodulatory and microbiota-mediated effects is plausible but is dominated by chemical assays, cell models and studies of purified compounds. Human trials mainly examine postprandial glycaemia, gastrointestinal responses and satiety; their results are heterogeneous and do not establish that sourdough fermentation alone prevents chronic disease. Flour composition, strain identity, fermentation time, temperature, hydration and baking interact, making the final bread not the fermented dough the relevant exposure. Future work should employ chemically characterized breads, matched comparators, simulated digestion linked to targeted metabolomics, dose–response designs and adequately powered randomized trials. Sourdough is best viewed as a controllable biotransformation platform whose health value depends on the product-specific survival and bioavailability of its metabolites rather than on fermentation as a generic label

title: Succinylation in lung cancer: mechanisms, implications, and clinical perspectives
summary: As a form of protein posttranslational modification (PTM), succinylation involves the covalent addition of a succinyl moiety to specific residues (predominantly lysine) in proteins through an amide linkage, altering protein activity, stabil
content: As a form of protein posttranslational modification (PTM), succinylation involves the covalent addition of a succinyl moiety to specific residues (predominantly lysine) in proteins through an amide linkage, altering protein activity, stability, and intermolecular interactions. By influencing these molecular properties, succinylation contributes substantially to the control of cellular metabolism, intracellular signaling, and transcriptional regulation. Accumulating evidence suggests that abnormal succinylation is implicated in both the onset and progression of lung cancer. This review provides a systematic overview of the molecular processes through which succinylation participates in lung tumorigenesis and evaluates prospective treatment approaches and future directions with a focus on succinylation as a therapeutic target. Taken together, the available evidence supports further investigation of the biological relevance of succinylation to lung tumor biology and may promote the development and eventual clinical translation of therapies directed against succinylation-related pathways.

title: RiPPs in functional laboratory medicine: translational opportunities and class III lanthipeptides as a comparative case study
summary: Ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides (RiPPs) are genetically encoded natural products that undergo diverse enzymatic modifications to generate structurally constrained molecules with broad biological activities
content: Ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides (RiPPs) are genetically encoded natural products that undergo diverse enzymatic modifications to generate structurally constrained molecules with broad biological activities and substantial engineering potential. Their defined biosynthetic origins, target-recognition properties, structural stability, and genetic encodability make RiPPs attractive molecular resources for both natural product research and emerging function-oriented applications in laboratory medicine. In this review, we summarize the biosynthetic logic and structural diversity of RiPPs, with particular emphasis on class III lanthipeptides as a representative and underexplored subgroup of structural and biosynthetic innovation. We curate 19 structurally characterized and experimentally validated class III lanthipeptides and compare their taxonomic origins, biosynthetic gene cluster organization, precursor peptide features, LanKC-mediated modifications, ring topologies, maturation routes, and reported biological functions. The analysis reveals a strong representation of Actinobacteria, a predominance of Lab-containing architectures, considerable diversity in maturation strategies, and a substantial proportion of functionally unresolved members. Beyond this comparative analysis, we discuss the emerging potential of RiPPs in mechanism-informed antimicrobial susceptibility testing, functional molecular diagnostics, microbiome functional-state assessment, engineered molecular probes, and precision anti-infective strategies. Because most of these applications remain exploratory or preclinical, we further propose a six-level evidence framework that distinguishes BGC presence, transcriptional activity, mature product detection, target engagement, biological activity, and clinical validation. By integrating the diversity of class III lanthipeptides with the broader translational potential of RiPPs, this review provides a framework for linking biosynthetic information, structural innovation, molecular function, and future applications in functional laboratory medicine.

title: Vertical Atmospheric Moisture Change Across Global Hydroclimatic Regimes During the Past 50 Years
summary: Abstract The vertical structure of atmospheric moisture is important for understanding land–atmosphere interactions, energy exchange, and the hydrological cycle. However, how thermodynamic moistening potential is expressed in observed speci
content: Abstract The vertical structure of atmospheric moisture is important for understanding land–atmosphere interactions, energy exchange, and the hydrological cycle. However, how thermodynamic moistening potential is expressed in observed specific-humidity changes across the troposphere remains insufficiently understood. Here, we analyse monthly mean temperature and specific humidity from ERA5 for 1979–2025 across 37 pressure levels and five hydroclimatic regimes. We quantify the thermodynamic component using Clausius–Clapeyron (C–C) scaling and diagnose the remaining non-thermodynamic residual, with MERRA-2 and ERA5-Land used to assess consistency. Terrestrial atmospheric moistening exhibits pronounced vertical variations. The thermodynamic component remains positive across the analysed levels but decreases substantially with height, from approximately 0.22–0.34 g kg⁻¹ decade⁻¹ at 1000 hPa to 0.002–0.06 g kg⁻¹ decade⁻¹ at 500 hPa and near zero at 250 hPa. In the lower troposphere, negative residuals (approximately − 0.30 to − 0.17 g kg⁻¹ decade⁻¹) substantially offset the thermodynamic component. The relative magnitude of the thermodynamic component increases toward 500 hPa, as indicated by CR values rising from 0.05–0.46 at 1000 hPa to 0.69–1.05 at 500 hPa, before becoming less distinct near 250 hPa (− 0.12 to 0.34). Hydroclimatic differences reflect variations in the extent to which the residual offsets thermodynamic moistening potential. These results show that terrestrial atmospheric moisture change is not a vertically uniform response to warming. Instead, the realized specific-humidity response depends on both the thermodynamic moistening potential and its height- and regime-dependent offset by the residual. This framework provides vertically resolved constraints for evaluating atmospheric humidity changes in climate models and motivates further investigation of the physical processes underlying the residual.

title: Aging-associated cellular metabolic reprogramming in the pathogenesis of systemic sclerosis: current progress and therapeutic perspectives
summary: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a chronic autoimmune connective tissue disease characterized by microvascular injury, immune dysregulation, and progressive fibrosis affecting the skin and internal organs. The disease typically develops between
content: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a chronic autoimmune connective tissue disease characterized by microvascular injury, immune dysregulation, and progressive fibrosis affecting the skin and internal organs. The disease typically develops between 45 and 60 years of age, and patients with late-onset SSc often experience more aggressive disease progression and poorer clinical outcomes. Despite advances in disease management, effective therapies targeting the underlying pathogenic mechanisms remain limited. Emerging evidence suggests that metabolic alterations associated with aging, cellular senescence, and SSc may interact to influence fibroblast activation, endothelial dysfunction, immune-cell responses, and extracellular matrix remodeling. Alterations in glucose, lipid, amino acid, and mitochondrial metabolism have been reported in SSc and experimental models of fibrosis; however, their causal relationships with biological aging and disease progression vary in evidential strength. This review summarizes current evidence on metabolic remodeling in key cellular populations involved in SSc, discusses potential interactions among cellular senescence, metabolic regulation, and the fibrotic microenvironment, and evaluates emerging metabolism-targeted therapeutic strategies. Particular attention is given to distinguishing findings established in SSc from mechanisms inferred from aging research or other fibrotic diseases. A clearer understanding of these relationships may help identify disease-relevant metabolic pathways and guide future mechanistic and translational studies.

title: Cool-Burn Engineering: TRPV1-Blocking Menthol Pathway Insertion via TRPM8 Agonist Design in Capsicum
summary: RESEARCH SCOPE: This work involves computational design and genomic engineering of Capsicum annuum (chili pepper, Solanaceae family) and selected host plants. All genetic constructs, CRISPR-Cas9 guide RNAs, and metabolic pathway engineering
content: RESEARCH SCOPE: This work involves computational design and genomic engineering of Capsicum annuum (chili pepper, Solanaceae family) and selected host plants. All genetic constructs, CRISPR-Cas9 guide RNAs, and metabolic pathway engineering described herein target plant cells exclusively. No animal DNA, human DNA, mammalian cell lines, or biological materials of animal origin are involved in this research. This is fundamental plant biotechnology. Cool-Burn: Simultaneous TRPV1 and TRPM8 Activation in Capsicum annuum via Heterologous Expression of the Mentha × piperita Menthol Biosynthesis Pathway Scoville Splice Research Series · Paper 9 of 11 DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23743695 (Paper 1, primary reference) Iyengar Flavor Index methodology: 10.5281/zenodo.PAPER04 OVERVIEW This preprint reports the computational design and pathway modeling of a five-gene menthol biosynthesis cassette—cloned from Mentha × piperita—inserted into Capsicum annuum SS-0096 (Phoenix) to produce simultaneous activation of both TRPV1 (capsaicin receptor) and TRPM8 (cold/menthol receptor). No naturally occurring food crop achieves dual activation of these two thermosensory channels simultaneously. We designate this sensory phenotype "cool-burn." The work establishes the theoretical basis for a two-gene proof-of-concept construct and a complete five-gene pathway yielding projected menthol accumulation of 20–100 µg/g FW in ripe fruit, corresponding to an Iyengar Flavor Index — Cool (IFI-C) value of approximately 85,000. Capsaicin flux and TRPV1 activation (IFI-H: 2,956,310) are preserved to within 0.8% of wild-type. PATHWAY ARCHITECTURE All five enzymes were cloned from Mentha × piperita by Mahmoud and Croteau (2003; PNAS 100(24):14167–14172), the foundational reference for this pathway. The complete biosynthetic route from the universal terpenoid precursor GPP to (−)-menthol proceeds as follows: 1. MpLS — Limonene synthase 1 (UniProt: B0F4G4). Catalyzes GPP → (−)-limonene. Localized to the plastid via N-terminal transit peptide (~60 aa). This is the committed entry step into the monoterpene branch. Promoter in construct: CaMV35S (constitutive, to drive carbon into the pathway at all developmental stages). CAI native: 0.64; CAI optimized for C. annuum UCD10Xv1.1: 0.91. 2. MpCYP71D15 — Limonene-6-hydroxylase (UniProt: Q9XHE6). Catalyzes (−)-limonene → (−)-isopiperitenol. ER-anchored cytochrome P450; requires plastid-to-ER metabolite transfer. Promoter: CaMV35S. CAI native: 0.67; optimized: 0.89. 3. MpIPPO — Isopiperitenol oxidoreductase (UniProt: Q5C9I9). Catalyzes (−)-isopiperitenol → (−)-isopiperitenone. Short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase; cytosolic. Promoter: E8 (LeE8, tomato fruit-ripening, fruit-specific) to concentrate downstream flux in harvestable tissue. CAI native: 0.70; optimized: 0.93. 4. MpPIPR — Pulegone reductase (UniProt: Q6WAU0). Catalyzes (−)-pulegone → (+)-menthone. NADPH-dependent. Cytosolic. Promoter: E8 (fruit-specific). CAI native: 0.72; optimized: 0.92. 5. MpM

title: Optimizing construction-land allocation in urban agglomerations under carbon-sink spatial constraints: a case study of the Chang–Zhu–Tan urban agglomeration, China
summary: Rapid urbanization causes substantial carbon storage loss through construction-land expansion, while the spatial location of development can generate different carbon costs even at similar levels of land conversion. Translating these spatia
content: Rapid urbanization causes substantial carbon storage loss through construction-land expansion, while the spatial location of development can generate different carbon costs even at similar levels of land conversion. Translating these spatially differentiated carbon effects into information for future construction-land allocation therefore represents an important challenge for carbon sink conservation in territorial spatial planning. Taking the Chang–Zhu–Tan Urban Agglomeration (CZTUA), China, as a case study, this study integrates InVEST-based carbon-storage assessment, ecological-importance evaluation, landscape-network analysis, and PLUS land-use simulation within an analytical sequence linking historical carbon-loss identification, key carbon sink areas and their landscape relationships, and scenario-based construction-land constraints. The results show that: (1) from 1990 to 2020, construction land increased by 722.52 km 2 , with 95.36% of the converted land originating from cultivated land and forest, resulting in an estimated cumulative carbon-storage loss of 22.68 × 10 6 t. Development magnitude and carbon loss per unit of expansion varied differently across periods, indicating that the carbon effects of construction-land expansion were not determined by development magnitude alone. (2) A total of 1,395.81 km 2 of key carbon sink areas, 91 potential landscape corridors, 17 pinch points, and 48 barrier areas were identified, providing spatial information on both patch-level conservation value and landscape relationships. (3) The four 2030 scenarios produced distinct development and carbon-storage outcomes. CSS accommodated 46.14 km 2 more new construction land than EP while producing 1.85 × 10 6 t less carbon-storage loss. Under CSP, new construction land was further reduced to 68.21 km 2 , with an estimated carbon-storage loss of 1.97 × 10 6 t, indicating that both development capacity and spatial allocation shape the carbon consequences of construction-land expansion. By translating carbon-storage priorities and landscape relationships into scenario-based land allocation, the study provides a planning-oriented basis for differentiated construction-land management and carbon sink conservation at the urban-agglomeration scale.

title: Synergising Safeguards: A Legal Blueprint For Climate Change And Mangrove Conservation In Sundarbans
source: HPNLU Journal of Environment & Disaster Management
summary: The Sundarbans, a UNESCO World Heritage mangrove ecosystem spanning India and Bangladesh, plays an indispensable role in climate resilience, biodiversity conservation, and sustaining the livelihoods of over 4.5 million people. As a natural
content: The Sundarbans, a UNESCO World Heritage mangrove ecosystem spanning India and Bangladesh, plays an indispensable role in climate resilience, biodiversity conservation, and sustaining the livelihoods of over 4.5 million people. As a natural buffer against cyclones and storm surges and a significant carbon sink, this fragile delta ecosystem is increasingly threatened by rising sea levels, salinity intrusion, intensifying cyclonic activity, and large-scale deforestation driven by aquaculture expansion, unregulated tourism, and infrastructure development. While a substantial body of national and international law—ranging from the Convention on Biological Diversity and RAMSAR obligations to domestic forest and environmental protection statutes—purports to safeguard the region, this paper argues that fragmented jurisdictions, weak enforcement mechanisms, and the systemic exclusion of local and indigenous communities from governance have rendered these legal frameworks largely ineffective. Employing a doctrinal and analytical methodology, the paper examines the existing legal and policy architecture governing climate change and mangrove conservation in the Sundarbans, identifies critical enforcement and implementation gaps, and evaluates the socioecological consequences of continued degradation. It further proposes an integrated legal blueprint that harmonizes climate adaptation with conservation law, strengthens multi-level governance and regulatory coordination, incorporates traditional ecological knowledge, and fosters public-private and cross-border cooperation—including a proposed bilateral mangrove conservation treaty with Bangladesh. The paper concludes that a synergized legal and institutional response, grounded in stricter enforcement, community empowerment, and international collaboration, is essential to securing the ecological and socio-economic future of the Sundarbans.

title: Carbon Enrichment in the Sinking-Corrected Debris Composition of WD 1536+520
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The polluted white dwarf WD 1536+520 is analysed as an accretion accounting problem. From published element abundances and diffusion sinking times, the mass of each of oxygen, magnesium, silicon, iron and calcium currently held in the star'
content: The polluted white dwarf WD 1536+520 is analysed as an accretion accounting problem. From published element abundances and diffusion sinking times, the mass of each of oxygen, magnesium, silicon, iron and calcium currently held in the star's mixed layer is computed, divided by its sinking time, and summed into a total metal accretion rate of 1.024e+9 grams per second. The total metal mass presently visible is 3.163e+11 kilograms in a convection zone of 4.087e+14 kilograms. Correcting each element for its own sinking time gives a parent-body pattern with an iron-to-silicon molar ratio of 1.32, a magnesium-to-silicon molar ratio of 0.701, an oxygen excess fraction of -0.485 and an inferred water mass fraction of 0. The adopted debris disc mass of 4.000e+18 kilograms sustains the present rate for 1.238e+5 years, and the total event mass, disc plus visible inventory, is 6.698e-7 Earth masses, corresponding to a parent body of minimum radius 61.9 kilometres at the inferred mean density of 4.031e+3 kilograms per cubic metre. Every number is produced by the deposited script from the stated published inputs.

title: Structural and biochemical insight into allosteric regulation of the human 2-aminoadipic semialdehyde synthase
summary: Multiple clinically relevant inborn errors of metabolism occur in lysine degradation, yet the regulation of this biochemical pathway remains poorly understood. The initial rate-limiting step of lysine catabolism is catalyzed by the bifuncti
content: Multiple clinically relevant inborn errors of metabolism occur in lysine degradation, yet the regulation of this biochemical pathway remains poorly understood. The initial rate-limiting step of lysine catabolism is catalyzed by the bifunctional enzyme 2-aminoadipic semialdehyde synthase (AASS). Here, we report the cryo-EM structure of the full-length 400-kilodalton tetrameric AASS enzyme complex with substrates and products bound to both the lysine-2-oxoglutarate (LOR) and saccharopine dehydrogenase (SDH) catalytic domains. We also identified allosteric compounds that modulate the activity of AASS by reacting with cysteine-414 and shifting the pH optimum for biochemical activity. The mutagenesis of this allosteric Cys 414 has marked effects on the enzyme’s conformation and activity despite being more than 12 angstrom from the active site. We find that small changes near the hinge of an enzyme can have large effects on its catalytic properties. Last, targeting allosteric cysteines may be a general strategy for modulating enzyme activity by altering the dynamics of the enzyme.

title: Spatial Support and Operator Structure in GSTAR Models: Administrative Regions versus Regular Grids for Wildfire Hotspot Data
summary: Abstract This study examines the impact of spatial support transformation on the structure and stability of the Generalized Space-Time Autoregressive (GSTAR) framework. We explore two types of spatial representation: irregular administrativ
content: Abstract This study examines the impact of spatial support transformation on the structure and stability of the Generalized Space-Time Autoregressive (GSTAR) framework. We explore two types of spatial representation: irregular administrative regions and regular, high-density grid discretization. Administrative regions are typically defined by polygonal boundaries, and the heterogeneity of these polygons often leads to inconsistent neighborhood configurations and non-uniform spatial interactions. In contrast, regular grid discretization yields more structured, sparse spatial operators. Using spatio-temporal environmental data obtained from NASA FIRMS observations, GSTAR models were constructed using different spatial supports and evaluated based on spatial interaction structure, parameter stability, and forecasting characteristics. Beyond empirical comparison, this study investigates the structural properties of the resulting GSTAR operators, such as sparsity preservation, block-banded structure, and spectral properties within the regular grid topology. The results indicate that regular grid discretization is more efficient than irregular administrative aggregation at preserving local neighborhood interactions; this method produces spatial operators that are sparser, more localized, and spectrally controlled, which in turn leads to more stable and accurate spatio-temporal parameter estimation. On the other hand, forecasting accuracy proves to be highly dependent on the error measurement method: when compared at the original scale (without standardization), grid-based models yield lower absolute forecasting errors; However, once errors are standardized based on the variability of each spatial unit—an adjustment necessary given that spatially aggregated administrative data series tend to be structurally smoother—administrative support actually yields normalized errors that are comparable or even lower. We present both perspectives and argue that the primary structural advantage of grid support lies in operator sparsity and parameter stability, rather than in an absolute superiority in forecasting accuracy. These results demonstrate that spatial support is not merely a pre-processing step, but a structural element that fundamentally impacts the behavior of spatio-temporal operators.

title: ¹H NMR metabolomic signatures associated with oil-related bunch traits in within-family oil palm (Elaeis guineensis) progenies
summary: Abstract Background Oil palm ( Elaeis guineensis Jacq.) improvement relies on progeny testing, but bunch performance is expressed only after several years of field growth, and oil-related traits vary considerably even among genetically rela
content: Abstract Background Oil palm ( Elaeis guineensis Jacq.) improvement relies on progeny testing, but bunch performance is expressed only after several years of field growth, and oil-related traits vary considerably even among genetically related progenies. Whether early-stage leaf metabolism is associated with this variation is unknown. We therefore compared the spear leaf metabolomes of top- and bottom-performing palms selected within the same biparental crosses. Results Unopened spear leaves (leaf 0) were collected from 36 palms, one top and one bottom performer from each of 18 biparental crosses, and profiled by ¹H NMR. Top-class palms had higher mesocarp-to-fruit (+ 6.4%), oil-to-dry mesocarp (+ 4.4%) and oil-to-bunch (+ 22.4%) ratios than bottom-class palms (all P < 0.001). Of 123 metabolites identified, those with the highest variable importance in projection (VIP) scores, including guanidinoacetic acid, xylitol, methylguanidine, threonic acid and lysine, contributed to the class separation seen in partial least squares discriminant analysis. Several metabolites correlated with oil-related traits, notably L-arabitol (positively) and glutamine (negatively), but none remained significant after false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Six pathways were enriched (FDR < 0.01), led by alanine, aspartate and glutamate metabolism (impact 0.849) and including arginine biosynthesis, glyoxylate and dicarboxylate metabolism, and the TCA cycle. Five metabolite ratios discriminated the classes (AUC 0.790–0.814), the best being β-hydroxyisovaleric acid/methylguanidine (AUC = 0.814) and guanidinoacetic acid/pimelic acid (AUC = 0.806). Conclusions Within biparental crosses, top- and bottom-performing palms differed in spear leaf profiles involving carbon-conserving and nitrogen-related (amino acid and guanidino compound) metabolism, a pattern consistent with coordinated carbon–nitrogen metabolism supporting oil accumulation. The candidate metabolite ratios are leads for non-destructive early selection, but the extreme-group design, the small sample size and the absence of FDR-significant individual correlations mean that they must be validated in independent, unselected populations and environments before use in breeding.

title: Improving winter wheat yield estimation under heat stress with LUE frameworks and a HDD based harvest index
summary: Heat stress increasingly threatens crop production, yet its effects remain inadequately represented in remote sensing-based light-use efficiency (LUE) models. Consequently, these models may overestimate biomass accumulation and grain yield
content: Heat stress increasingly threatens crop production, yet its effects remain inadequately represented in remote sensing-based light-use efficiency (LUE) models. Consequently, these models may overestimate biomass accumulation and grain yield under high-temperature conditions because they do not fully capture heat induced limitations on either carbon assimilation or biomass allocation. This study aimed to improve the yield estimation of winter wheat by incorporating heat responses from both source (biomass accumulation) and sink (biomass allocation) perspectives into LUE frameworks. On the source side, two heat-calibrated LUE model variants, which combine transpiration-related constraints with Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI)-based Fraction of Photosynthetically Active Radiation (FPAR), were evaluated for improving aboveground biomass (AGB) estimation. On the sink side, a heat-responsive harvest index (HI) was calibrated from field observations using heat degree days (HDD). The analysis used Sentinel-2 imagery and field measurements collected from winter wheat fields on a large commercial farm near Ferrara, Italy, during 2020-2023. The newly parameterized LUE models improved AGB estimation only under heat conditions, whereas further incorporation of the HDD-based HI improved grain yield estimation under both heat and normal conditions, mainly by substantially reducing systematic overestimation. Specifically, under heat conditions, the combined source–sink parameterization increased yield-estimation accuracy to R2 = 0.508 and reduced absolute bias by 73%, relative to the best-performing baseline LUE model, VPM. Under normal conditions, the reparameterization improved yield estimation with R2 increasing by 22% and the absolute bias decreased by 60%, relative to VPM. The relative benefits of the two model components varied with environmental conditions. Source-side optimization provided greater improvements in heat years, whereas the heat-responsive HI contributed more under normal conditions. These findings highlight the need to take into account and quantify nonlinear heat effects on both carbon assimilation and biomass allocation to improve large-scale LUE-based crop yield estimation under increasingly frequent and intense temperature extremes.

title: Poly(isobutylene- alt -maleic anhydride)–Zinc Tetraphenylporphyrin Conjugates as Photodynamic Antimicrobial Materials with Plasmid DNA Degradation Properties
summary: Abstract The emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria underscores the urgent need for alternative antimicrobial strategies. In this study, we report the synthesis and characterization of poly(isobutylene-alt-maleic anhydride) (PMAL)
content: Abstract The emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria underscores the urgent need for alternative antimicrobial strategies. In this study, we report the synthesis and characterization of poly(isobutylene-alt-maleic anhydride) (PMAL) functionalized with amino tetraphenylporphyrin (TPP) and subsequent zinc metalation (PMAL-ZnTPP) as a photodynamic antimicrobial material. The potential of PMAL-ZnTPP to eradicate a wide range of pathogenic MDR bacteria and degrade the plasmid vectors that frequently carry antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes is evaluated. Amino porphyrin was covalently grafted onto PMAL through a nucleophilic acyl substitution (aminolysis) reaction, resulting in ring opening of the anhydride and formation of amide and carboxylic acid groups. The conjugates were characterized, confirming successful grafting and zinc coordination. Nanosecond transient absorption spectroscopy (ns-TAS) revealed the formation of a long-lived triplet excited state, with lifetimes of 245 μs in toluene and 360 μs in DMSO, which is essential for the generation of reactive oxygen species and underpins the antimicrobial photodynamic activity of photosensitizing polymers. PMAL-ZnTPP generates singlet oxygen with a quantum yield of 0.59 under visible-light irradiation. Antimicrobial evaluation against 14 bacterial strains, including clinically and environmentally relevant Gram-positive and Gram-negative species, demonstrated broad-spectrum activity, achieving log reductions in colony-forming units/mL (CFU/mL) ranging from 0.36 to 5.8 upon light exposure for 1 h compared to the controls. Plasmid DNA integrity analysis indicated that PMAL-ZnTPP-mediated photodynamic treatment induced plasmid damage both in isolated DNA and within bacterial cells. The non-water-soluble nature of PMAL-ZnTPP makes it well-suited for immobilized or dispersed decontamination applications. Its broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity and plasmid degradation properties make this an attractive material for further development where mitigation of AMR transmission is a priority.

title: Static–Dynamic Hybrid Covalent Networks Enable Scale‐Selective Molecular Confinement in Ultraflexible Phase Change Composites for Adaptive Thermal Management
summary: ABSTRACT Phase change materials (PCMs) offer high latent heat and near‐isothermal heat storage and release, making them attractive for thermal energy storage and regulation. However, melt leakage, low thermal conductivity, and solid‐state r
content: ABSTRACT Phase change materials (PCMs) offer high latent heat and near‐isothermal heat storage and release, making them attractive for thermal energy storage and regulation. However, melt leakage, low thermal conductivity, and solid‐state rigidity hinder the simultaneous achievement of dimensional stability, flexibility, interfacial adaptability, and multifunctional responsiveness at high energy‐storage densities. Here, we develop ultraflexible paraffin‐based composite phase change materials (CPCMs) using a hybrid static–dynamic covalent three‐dimensional network and graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs) as rapid heat‐transfer pathways. Static covalent bonds maintain network integrity, while exchangeable boronic ester moieties enable thermally triggered rearrangement. Experiment and simulation results demonstrate the cross‐linked network suppresses large‐scale cooperative migration of paraffin while preserving the local degrees of freedom required for reversible phase transitions. The resulting CPCM delivers a phase‐change enthalpy of 172.2 J/g and an ultra‐high fracture elongation of 1219.5%. GNP incorporation increases thermal conductivity to 2.07 W/m·K while retaining an enthalpy efficiency over 98.8%, together with excellent adhesion, self‐healing, recyclability, and shape memory. The material further enables efficient thermal regulation in electronics, wide‐temperature‐range batteries, solar thermal storage, and flexible wearable thermal management. This strategy provides a novel design route toward integrating high energy storage, ultraflexibility, structural stability, and dynamic interfacial adaptability in one phase‐change material system.

title: Forest community compositions and soil properties association in the Moist Temperate Forest across Northwestern Himalayan
summary: Abstract Forests play a critical role in climate mitigation strategies and act as a carbon sink. Complex ecological cycles play significant roles in balancing ecological forces and shaping species habitat, consequently community patterns an
content: Abstract Forests play a critical role in climate mitigation strategies and act as a carbon sink. Complex ecological cycles play significant roles in balancing ecological forces and shaping species habitat, consequently community patterns and structure. The community compositions and their relationship with soil have not yet been fully understood. We studied vegetation structure, community patterns, regeneration dynamics, soil physicochemical properties including soil organic carbon (SOC) in 14 forest communities at an elevational gradient (2400–3290 m) of Tarla Wildlife Sanctuary, India. Community structure and species diversity were quantified across 50 sites, and soil samples from 0–15 cm and 15–30 cm depths were analyzed to determine nutrient status. It was found that a conifer-mixed community dominated by Abies pindrow and Picea smithiana had the highest species richness. In contrast, a pure Quercus semecarpifolia community was rich in soil nutrients and showed positive associations with soil moisture and nutrient availability, thereby supporting greater SOC storage. While Surface soils had higher SOC % and key macronutrients (NPK) than subsurface soils, bulk density and coarse fragments increased with depth, negatively influencing carbon storage. Collectively, current findings revealed that the vegetation–soil relationship is very important for shaping forest structure and soil carbon dynamics across altitude gradients, and that mixed forests play an important role in sustaining nutrient cycling, carbon sequestration, and the path towards ecosystem resilience.

title: Substrate physicochemical properties and seedling performance of rubber tree seed-grafted seedlings: relative contributions of physical structure and chemical nutrients
summary: Introduction The physical structure and chemical nutrients of substrates jointly regulate seedling growth in container nursery production, but their relative contributions and interactions remain unclear, limiting precise substrate formulat
content: Introduction The physical structure and chemical nutrients of substrates jointly regulate seedling growth in container nursery production, but their relative contributions and interactions remain unclear, limiting precise substrate formulation. Rubber tree ( Hevea brasiliensis ) seed-grafted seedlings are important planting materials for the natural rubber industry, yet their lightweight substrate technology needs optimization. Methods Seed-grafted seedlings were grown in an inert control (CK, river sand: perlite = 1:1) and five substrate formulations: T1 (pure red soil), T2 (coco coir:peat = 1:1), T3 (red soil: coco coir: sheep manure = 5:3:2), T4 (sugarcane leaf residue: river sand: sheep manure = 4:4:2), and T5 (peat: coco coir: sheep manure: river sand = 3:3:2:2). Growth, physiological, and nutrient parameters were measured, and membership function, principal component, and variance partitioning analyses (VPA) were used to quantify independent and interactive effects of physical and chemical factors. Results Different substrates significantly affected growth, biomass, leaf nutrients, and photosynthetic pigments, while biomass allocation (stem > root > leaf) remained stable. Comprehensive evaluation ranked T2 highest (membership 0.74–0.79) and T3 lowest (0.15–0.20). T2 exhibited greater root development, which was associated with its low bulk density and high porosity; this may have partially compensated for the low inherent nutrient status of the substrate by increasing the absorptive area. Although T3 had higher leaf nitrogen, its high bulk density and low porosity were associated with inhibited root growth, causing luxury nutrient uptake and photoprotective compensation (carotenoid accumulation with decreased chlorophyll). VPA showed variation in height and diameter was statistically attributable to chemical nutrients alone (21%–22%), root elongation explained by physical structure alone (10%), and root diameter by their shared effect (3%), indicating clear functional differentiation. Discussion Optimizing substrate physical structure is more critical than stacking nutrient types. T2 is compositionally simpler, and recommended for lightweight rubber seed-grafted seedling cultivation in Xishuangbanna.

title: Exploring suspended sediment concentration determinants in mountain rivers using machine learning and structural equation modeling
summary: Study region The lower Jinsha River Basin, China, a mountainous basin with high sediment yield. Study focus Flood sediment transport in mountain rivers reflects interactions among hydrological and physiographic factors. This study combines
content: Study region The lower Jinsha River Basin, China, a mountainous basin with high sediment yield. Study focus Flood sediment transport in mountain rivers reflects interactions among hydrological and physiographic factors. This study combines flood-event identification, sediment rating curves, and hysteresis analysis to characterize temporal shifts in sediment transport, and then integrates data-driven models and pathway analysis to identify and quantify the main controls on daily suspended sediment concentration. New hydrological insights for the region Using 60,254 daily records from ten rivers (10²–10⁴ km²), we found lower sediment concentrations at comparable discharges in 2007–2020 than in 1970–1987, while clockwise discharge–sediment hysteresis persisted across the studied rivers. Among five data-driven models, the Artificial Neural Network (ANN) performed best overall, achieving NSE values of 0.743 and 0.714 in the two periods. SHAP analysis revealed interactions between current hydrological forcing and antecedent sediment conditions. PLS-SEM estimated positive direct effects of current discharge and antecedent sediment concentration on sediment concentration ( β = 0.794–1.030 and 0.680–0.695, respectively). Antecedent discharge showed a positive indirect effect through current discharge ( β = 0.719–0.952) and a negative direct effect ( β = −1.031 to −0.831). These findings indicate that daily sediment dynamics in the lower Jinsha River reflect both current discharge and antecedent sediment conditions, supporting their joint consideration in regional sediment monitoring and flood-related sediment assessment.

title: Methane dynamics in wetland ecosystems: mathematical model, properties of the initial–boundary value problem and verification of the numerical scheme
summary: Abstract A one-dimensional vertical model of dissolved methane dynamics in water-saturated peat is formulated and analysed. The model accounts for methanogenesis, Monod-type oxidation, molecular diffusion, ebullition with a threshold determ
content: Abstract A one-dimensional vertical model of dissolved methane dynamics in water-saturated peat is formulated and analysed. The model accounts for methanogenesis, Monod-type oxidation, molecular diffusion, ebullition with a threshold determined by the atmospheric, hydrostatic and capillary pressures, and plant-mediated transport represented by a point sink at the root uptake level; mass exchange with the atmosphere is imposed on the total flux at the surface by a Robin condition. For the problem with a truncated bubble flux, a weak formulation is introduced, and the existence, uniqueness and non-negativity of the weak solution and its continuous dependence on the initial data and the source are proved. The point sink is shown to be well defined without regularization and to be equivalent to an interface condition with a jump of the diffusive flux. For the stationary problem, the existence of a non-negative solution is established, together with its uniqueness and exponential stability under a smallness condition, and a sufficient condition for a zero bubble flux through the surface is obtained. A conservative monotone finite-volume scheme with exponential fitting of the fluxes, upwind evaluation of the bubble velocity and the implicit Euler method is constructed. Its MATLAB implementation is verified against two analytical steady-state solutions and by the method of manufactured solutions: the scheme conserves mass to machine precision and exhibits second-order spatial convergence without active ebullition and first-order convergence with active bubble transport and in time.

title: Uncertainty-weighted fuzzy clustering disentangles climate-stress VOC fingerprints and associated stress-dependent temperature sensitivity in urban trees
summary: Abstract Climate change increases the severity and frequency of heat and oxidative stress that plants experience, yet their simultaneous effects on biogenic volatile organic compounds (BVOCs) emissions remains poorly understood, complicatin
content: Abstract Climate change increases the severity and frequency of heat and oxidative stress that plants experience, yet their simultaneous effects on biogenic volatile organic compounds (BVOCs) emissions remains poorly understood, complicating the predictability of future air quality and climate. Here, canopy BVOC emissions from linden and chestnut trees were measured over a continuous two-month chamber experiment without stress, heat stress, and combined O₃ and heat stress. To untangle stress-associated BVOC fingerprints, we developed an unsupervised uncertainty-weighted fuzzy c-means (UWFCM) algorithm that directly incorporates compound- and measurement-specific analytical uncertainties into clustering. UWFCM identified monoterpenes (increased up to 3-fold) and sesquiterpenes (up to 22-fold) as the primary heat-stress markers in both species, while increased diterpenes characterized combined O₃ and heat stress in linden. Stress-induced de novo emissions resulted in carbon loss up to ~ 14% of net daytime carbon fixation, a substantial stress-related carbon reallocation. The temperature sensitivity of terpenoid emissions was strongly stress-dependent. These findings have important implications for global BVOC parameterizations, estimates of daytime NO x -driven ozone chemistry and secondary organic aerosol formation under future climate extremes.

title: Metabolomics and lipidomics in the differentiation of CIN 2 and CIN 3: an exploratory pilot study
summary: INTRODUCTION: High-grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN 2-3) is a precursor lesion to cervical cancer and, although it presents different probabilities of regression and progression, it is usually grouped together in screening and
content: INTRODUCTION: High-grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN 2-3) is a precursor lesion to cervical cancer and, although it presents different probabilities of regression and progression, it is usually grouped together in screening and managed similarly. However, the mechanisms that determine its evolution are still poorly understood, and standard treatment by conization can lead to reproductive complications such as subfertility and premature birth. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to identify metabolic and lipid signatures that can distinguish between CIN 2 and CIN 3 lesions using liquid chromatography-high-resolution mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS). METHODS: Tissue samples from the lesion and adjacent margin of 24 women with CIN 2-3 were subjected to metabolomic and lipidomic analysis by LC-HRMS. Multivariate statistical analyses, pathway analysis, and correlation were performed to understand these neoplasms' development and progression and identify potential metabolites and lipids to distinguish such lesions. RESULTS: Metabolomic and lipidomic analysis by LC-HRMS in cervical tissue identified molecular signatures with differential abundance between CIN 2 and CIN 3, highlighting patterns associated with the degree of lesion. Multivariate analyses highlighted metabolites (serine, glutamic acid, guanidine-6-monophosphate, succinic acid, mannose 6-phosphate, and taurine) and lipids (TG 49:1, TG 50:1, and TG 52:2) as the main contributors to the discrimination between the groups, suggesting relevant biological alterations in high-grade cervical lesions. CONCLUSION: Combination metabolomic and lipidomic approach enabled the identification of metabolites and lipids potentially involved in the pathogenesis of intraepithelial neoplasia (CINs). In addition, these identified metabolite and lipid panels are promising as complementary tools for future screening strategies for these lesions.

title: Insect-associated molecules at the plant immune interface: recognition, manipulation and resistance design
summary: Feeding and oviposition expose plants to insect-associated proteins, peptides, metabolites, enzymes and small RNAs. Depending on the delivery route, these molecules encounter tissue surfaces, wounds, the apoplast, vascular cells or intracel
content: Feeding and oviposition expose plants to insect-associated proteins, peptides, metabolites, enzymes and small RNAs. Depending on the delivery route, these molecules encounter tissue surfaces, wounds, the apoplast, vascular cells or intracellular compartments. Plant responses to these molecules range from defense activation to signaling diversion and immune suppression. Interpretation becomes difficult when release route, function and evidence strength are treated as interchangeable. We organize current evidence in a two-dimensional recognition-manipulation framework that treats plant recognition and host manipulation as independent, potentially co-occurring properties. The framework connects extracellular herbivore-associated molecular pattern (HAMP) perception and nucleotide-binding leucine-rich repeat receptor (NLR)-mediated effector recognition to recurrent host control points, including jasmonate-salicylate crosstalk, redox control, vesicle trafficking, protein turnover, autophagy, plasmodesmal callose and transcriptional regulation. The BISP-BPH14-OsNBR1 module provides a well-resolved example: BISP suppresses basal defense, triggers genotype-specific resistance and is subsequently cleared to attenuate immune activation. Chewing and piercing-sucking insects define illustrative feeding-mode endpoints, whereas gallers, miners and borers provide additional insect interfaces; spider mites are included only as non-insect arthropod comparators. We evaluate six independent evidence domains: candidate discovery, natural delivery, molecular activity, receptor or target engagement, organismal phenotype and ecological or agronomic context. Signal termination, growth recovery and yield protection are assessed separately. This framework prioritizes mechanisms for translational testing while retaining provisional candidates without imposing a universal resistance architecture.

title: Microscale patchiness controls resource acquisition in populations of foraging bacteria
summary: Chemotaxis, the ability of cells to detect and respond to chemical gradients, allows them to acquire nutrients, seek hosts, or escape toxins. However, directly measuring bacterial foraging in spatially structured nutrient environments has p
content: Chemotaxis, the ability of cells to detect and respond to chemical gradients, allows them to acquire nutrients, seek hosts, or escape toxins. However, directly measuring bacterial foraging in spatially structured nutrient environments has proven elusive. We developed a new approach to investigate bacterial foraging, on timescales from milliseconds to hours, when exposed to nutrient fluctuations and microscale patchiness mimicking realistic ocean conditions. We generated dynamic, patchy, nutrient landscapes in a large microfluidic arena and simultaneously tracked individual cells of the marine bacterium Vibrio anguillarum . Analyzing single-cell nutrient exposure for tens of thousands of cells revealed that the nutrient exposure and distribution of exposure among bacteria depend strongly on the spatiotemporal characteristics of the patchy landscape. Furthermore, bacterial trajectories revealed a progressive decrease of swimming speed counter-balanced by an increase in chemotactic precision, resulting in stable nutrient exposure over time. This work furthers our understanding of bacterial foraging strategies under ecologically relevant conditions.

title: Nanolayered CNT-biological fluid dynamics in porous media under inclined magnetic field effects
source: Arab Journal of Basic and Applied Sciences
summary: This study investigates the flow of a carbon nanotube (CNT)-based nanofluid in a non-Newtonian biological medium over porous surfaces, with particular emphasis on the effects of an inclined magnetic field and interfacial nanolayers. The gov
content: This study investigates the flow of a carbon nanotube (CNT)-based nanofluid in a non-Newtonian biological medium over porous surfaces, with particular emphasis on the effects of an inclined magnetic field and interfacial nanolayers. The governing nonlinear partial differential equations are transformed into a system of ordinary differential equations using suitable similarity transformations and solved numerically by the shooting method. The analysis considers heat and mass transfer in the presence of Brownian motion and thermophoresis, along with important engineering quantities such as the skin-friction coefficient, Nusselt number, wall shear stress, impedance, and flow rate. A benchmark comparison with published limiting-case data gives an overall mean absolute percentage error of approximately 0.681% across 32 tabulated values, supporting the numerical consistency of the present model. The results show that increasing the nanolayer thickness and CNT concentration improves the effective thermal conductivity and enhances heat transfer. The inclined magnetic field also influences the flow by introducing Lorentz forces, which modify the momentum and energy transport and increase the flow resistance. Overall, the study provides useful insights into the coupled thermal, mass-transfer, and flow characteristics of CNT-based nanofluids and their potential use in biomedical applications.

title: Climate Changes: The Poles Matter
summary: Abstract The polarregions influence the global climate through a number of processes. Through this paper we unreveal the most importamnt reasons why the cold region of our planet not only are in danger, but exert a pivotal role in a global
content: Abstract The polarregions influence the global climate through a number of processes. Through this paper we unreveal the most importamnt reasons why the cold region of our planet not only are in danger, but exert a pivotal role in a global context. The rapid warming of the Arctic is a manyfold issue driven by the interplay of Arctic amplification, Atlantification, and changes in atmospheric circulation and dynamics. The ice-albedo feedback mechanism, increased intrusion of warm Atlantic waters, alterations in the polar jet stream, and shifts in atmospheric dynamics collectively contribute to the accelerated warming of the Arctic. Understanding these processes is crucial for predicting future climatic changes and for developing strategies to mitigate the impacts of global warming on polarregions and beyond. The Arctic’s transformation has far-reaching implications, not only for local ecosystems and communities but also for global weather patterns and climate stability.

title: Where the tonnes go missing: a ledger of delivered versus design CO2 at commercial capture facilities
summary: Carbon capture and storage (CCS) is planned and counted by design capacity. The gap between design and delivery is known; where it opens is not. Earlier studies compared stated capacity with storage and named causes without sizing them. Of
content: Carbon capture and storage (CCS) is planned and counted by design capacity. The gap between design and delivery is known; where it opens is not. Earlier studies compared stated capacity with storage and named causes without sizing them. Of 38 commercial facilities in a fixed published population, 16 publish enough to compare reported with design CO2; this paper rebuilds their output from operator and regulator records and enters each shortfall against design in an evidence-coded tonne ledger. Their designs implied 181 Mt and they reported 126 Mt, a mixed-endpoint ratio of 0.69; the 11 that report injected or stored CO2 delivered 0.66. Of the 55.2 Mt shortfall, 35% can be assigned to one stage; 21% is quantified but not assigned, and 44% has no quantified cause. Most assigned tonnes were lost at the sink, as CO2 that Gorgon separated but could not inject and capacity Great Plains could supply beyond the contracts its plans name, and most of the rest at the source. Capture plants were assigned 0.9 Mt, but the record cannot rule out up to 8.5 Mt. Counting Gorgon from the year its field began supplying the plant would add 12.4 Mt to the shortfall, 8.4 Mt of it vented while its compression trains were rebuilt. The results describe the documented cohort only. A one-page annual return, filled in for Petra Nova, Gorgon and Snøhvit, shows that most of what operators would need to report already exists.

title: Interindividual variations in methane production in tree trunks in relation to the wood micro-environment and microbial communities
summary: Abstract Key message: Methane accumulates in the heartwood of two tree species independently of the presence of wetwood. Moisture or density drives anoxia, while species-specific microbial communities and early decay stages might promote me
content: Abstract Key message: Methane accumulates in the heartwood of two tree species independently of the presence of wetwood. Moisture or density drives anoxia, while species-specific microbial communities and early decay stages might promote methanogenesis.Methane (CH₄) accounts for approximately 20% of global warming. Recent evidence suggests that CH₄ accumulating in living tree trunks of some species can be produced internally by methanogenic archaea, yet the factors governing microbial community composition and activity within trunks remain poorly understood. This study characterises the microenvironment conducive to methanogenesis within the heartwood of two contrasting species: Cryptomeria japonica, prone to wetwood formation, and Fagus crenata, in which this phenomenon remains rare. In-situ CH₄ molar fractions, ex-situ potential production rates, physical and biochemical properties, and bacterial community composition were assessed. Elevated CH₄ molar fractions were consistently observed in the heartwood of both species, regardless the presence of wetwood. Anoxic conditions were driven by high moisture content in C. japonica, whereas high bulk density promoted oxygen limitation in F. crenata. Microbial communities differed markedly between species and among individuals, reflecting variations in methanogenic activity and internal decay state. Temporal dynamics of microbial communities emerged as key drivers of CH₄ production. A non-linear pattern was identified: early-stage wood degradation promotes CH₄ accumulation, whereas advanced degradation limits production.

title: Nutritional and functional group characterization of Kenaf (Hibiscus cannabinus) core biomass for potential bioremediation applications
summary: The use of non-toxic, non-abrasive kenaf bast and core fibres has been reported to be effective in bioremediation. This may be due to the absorbent and biosurfactant properties of kenaf core powder, which depend on the activities of the fun
content: The use of non-toxic, non-abrasive kenaf bast and core fibres has been reported to be effective in bioremediation. This may be due to the absorbent and biosurfactant properties of kenaf core powder, which depend on the activities of the functional groups of the bioactive compounds present in the core. These properties were evaluated to understudy the potential of kenaf core to remediate crude oil contaminated soil. The core of the kenaf plant harvested at ten weeks after planting was subjected to proximate and elemental analysis, Gas-Chromatography/Mass-Spectrometry (GC-MS) analysis, Fourier Transform Infra-red (FTIR) analysis, and Ultra-violet and Visible (UV-VIS) spectrum analysis, using standard procedures. Nutrient analysis shows comparatively high levels of dry matter, organic carbon, total nitrogen, and crude fibre, as well as iron (53%) and phosphorus in the kenaf core. These nutritional elements are vital for microorganisms to thrive and survive under adverse environmental stresses. GC-MS analysis shows five major peaks, 3, 4, 9, 1, and 6, corresponding to oleic acid, octadecanoic acid, 2-methyl-3,13-octadienol, n-hexadecanoic acid, and 1-Fluorodecane, respectively. These fatty acids increase hydrophobicity and oil adsorption, enabling fibres to absorb oil. Oleic acid, a bio-derived fatty acid with surfactant-like properties, may enhance microbial access to hydrocarbons, while tocopherols ensure stability during remediation. FTIR analysis indicates that the IR fingerprint of kenaf core powder, shows maximum peak values ranging from 519 to 3337 cm − 1 . The highest peak at 3336.6 cm − 1 indicates the presence of an amine functional group with N-H bond stretching, while the highest absorption peak for rhamnolipid was found at 2924.18 cm − 1 . The qualitative UV-Vis spectrum profile identified chromophoric systems consistent with conjugated compounds. While a definitive mechanism was not directly measured, our data strongly imply that these functional groups serve as critical baseline components in microbial adaptation. These findings suggest that such chemical structures could play a role in supporting microbial metabolic pathways, potentially offering valuable insights into how microorganisms adapt and endure under stressful environmental conditions, though direct experimental evidence is needed to confirm this hypothesis. Kenaf core contains essential nutrients and bioactive compounds that may stimulate microbial growth in crude oil-contaminated soil, making it a promising bioremediation agent.

title: A Triboelectric‐Hydrogel System for Mechano‐Metabolic Re‐Coupling in Skin Expansion: Recharging From Energy Crisis
summary: Skin expansion is an effective technique for reconstructing large skin defects, yet its clinical utility is constrained by a progressive decline in regenerative capacity of skin, largely due to an underlying cellular energy crisis. Electric
content: Skin expansion is an effective technique for reconstructing large skin defects, yet its clinical utility is constrained by a progressive decline in regenerative capacity of skin, largely due to an underlying cellular energy crisis. Electrical stimulation enhances mitochondrial energy production, while mechanical regulation optimizes energy allocation. We designed a biocompatible composite system (TP-PAM/G) capable of synergistic electro-mechanical regulation to re-energize tissue. The system comprises a triboelectric nanogenerator layer fabricated from thermoplastic polyurethane and poly(vinylidene fluoride) that harnesses the ubiquitous mechanical forces of expansion to generate sustained mild electrical stimulation, and a hydrogel layer synthesized from polyacrylamide and gelatin that redistributes heterogeneous stresses. TP-PAM/G exhibits excellent mechanical compliance and tissue adhesion, enabling stable, long-lasting electric stimulation in response to expander stretching. In vitro results demonstrated that this electrical stimulation promotes the proliferation and migration of fibroblasts and endothelial cells and enhances collagen synthesis and angiogenesis. These effects were underpinned by upregulated mitochondrial activity. In vivo studies on rats revealed that TP-PAM/G augmented energy supply by promoting mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, accelerating vascularization, pro-regenerative macrophage formation, collagen deposition, and tissue maturation of expanded skin. By transforming a pathological mechanical environment into a therapeutic resource, this electro-mechanical platform holds significant potential for clinical translation.

title: The role of riparian buffers in protecting stream water quality and habitat integrity: thresholds for freshwater management
summary: Abstract Freshwater ecosystems face multiple stressors from agriculture, dispersed urbanization, and forestry plantations (eucalyptus, coniferous), which degrade water quality and habitat integrity. To assess the effectiveness of riparian s
content: Abstract Freshwater ecosystems face multiple stressors from agriculture, dispersed urbanization, and forestry plantations (eucalyptus, coniferous), which degrade water quality and habitat integrity. To assess the effectiveness of riparian strips as ecological buffers, we selected 168 sites in Galicia (NW Iberian Peninsula). We applied a methodological approach to identify impacts at different spatial scales (basin, riparian and reach), along multiple pressure intensification gradients. Generalized Additive Models (GAMs) were fitted to compare different models including basin and riparian predictors alone, and combined models to predict water quality and habitat integrity variables. The combined models showed high significant predictive capacity for water quality, while performance was lower for habitat integrity variables. Relevant quantitative ecological thresholds concerning basin and riparian management practises were also identified: agriculture cover exceeding 15% and urban higher than 6% increased nitrogen and phosphorus exports to streams, while extensive agricultural over 8% seem to partially limit these inputs. Moreover, wider native riparian forest (> 7 m) generally showed lower nutrient concentrations and better habitat conditions compared to those with exotic riparian trees presence. However, higher tree density and steeper riparian slopes increased nitrogen inputs to streams while simultaneously benefiting in-stream habitat structure. We conclude that riparian forests can act as effective ecological buffers mitigating multiple pressures impact to streams, although basin-scale management remains essential. These results provide fundamental support for the ecological protection of rivers, as establishing limitations for basin scale activities and defining appropriate riparian characteristics are critical to maintaining good water quality and habitat integrity.

title: Hydrographic and sea ice gradients shape benthic ecosystem functioning through sediment characteristics and benthic functional structure in Nares Strait, Canadian Arctic
summary: Rapid changes in Arctic sea ice conditions are altering the quantity, quality, and timing of organic matter reaching the seafloor, thereby reshaping benthic ecosystem functioning. However, the exact mechanisms linking sea ice variability, b
content: Rapid changes in Arctic sea ice conditions are altering the quantity, quality, and timing of organic matter reaching the seafloor, thereby reshaping benthic ecosystem functioning. However, the exact mechanisms linking sea ice variability, benthic community structure, and sediment biogeochemical processes remain poorly understood. With its multiple forms and ages of sea ice, Nares Strait in the Canadian Arctic offers a unique natural laboratory for investigating how environmental gradients and benthic community structure jointly regulate benthic ecosystem functioning. Here, we incubated sediment cores from several locations in Nares Strait characterised by different sea ice conditions, ranging from first-year ice to multi-year ice, and measured oxygen and nutrient fluxes as proxies for ecosystem functioning. To investigate the relative importance of potential drivers, we also measured environmental variables, identified macrofauna and calculated a suite of taxonomic and functional diversity indices. Our analyses show that fluxes across the sediment-water interface varied significantly between the northern and southern regions of Nares Strait. Among individual predictors, the average proportion of deposit feeders and sea ice cover (days since ice-free) explained the largest proportions of flux variability (23% and 14%, respectively). Overall, benthic functional structure explained more variation in fluxes than taxonomic diversity. Environmental variables explained little additional variation once functional descriptors were included, while variance partitioning revealed that the shared environmental-functional component accounted for 25% of the total variation, representing more than half of the variation explained by out models (45%) and exceeding the unique contributions of either environmental or functional variables. This strong overlap indicates that benthic functional structure integrates the cumulative effects of environmental forcing on sediment biogeochemical functioning. Collectively, our findings suggest that hydrographic and sea ice gradients regulate benthic ecosystem functioning largely through their influence on sediment characteristics and benthic functional structure. Because Nares Strait encompasses environmental conditions representative of many Arctic marine systems, the mechanisms identified here provide a framework for predicting how continued sea ice decline may reshape benthic ecosystem functioning across the Arctic Ocean.

title: Balloon-based trace gas observations reveal Asian Summer Monsoon impact in the UTLS over Germany
summary: Abstract. For many important trace gases, precise observations in the upper troposphere and lower stratosphere (UTLS) are spatially and/or temporally sparse and/or inhomogeneous. This is particularly limiting in the UTLS as a highly variabl
content: Abstract. For many important trace gases, precise observations in the upper troposphere and lower stratosphere (UTLS) are spatially and/or temporally sparse and/or inhomogeneous. This is particularly limiting in the UTLS as a highly variable transition region between the troposphere and stratosphere. We here present a new and unique dataset obtained from weather balloon-based sensors across the summer of 2025. Between 27th May and 5th November, 46 balloons were launched on an almost weekly basis from near Jülich, Germany, typically reaching altitudes of around 30 km. Of those flights, 37 focused on trace gases, with 18 near-simultaneous double launches quantifying the vertical distribution of water vapour and ozone as well as multiple halogenated species; thus, enabling access to the temporal evolution of many key UTLS components over a period of about five months. We here focus mainly on ozone-depleting chlorinated very short-lived substances (Cl-VSLSs) with model-based surface-origin tracers to investigate the source regions of the air masses. In particular, we investigate the influence of the Asian Summer Monsoon region – a source of Cl-VSLSs such as CH2Cl2 – as the upper-level anticyclone exports air masses into the global northern hemispheric UTLS during the monsoon season. We find that the “background” lower stratospheric composition in summer and autumn is clearly impacted by the Asian monsoon-related stratospheric entrance pathway, and for Cl-VSLSs much more so than estimated in previous studies.

title: Gravitational Energy Release from Diamond Rain in Neptune and Uranus
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This paper examines the sinking of diamond formed from methane at depth, often described as diamond rain. Using only published input values and transparent formulae, the calculation addresses how much gravitational energy the slow sinking o
content: This paper examines the sinking of diamond formed from methane at depth, often described as diamond rain. Using only published input values and transparent formulae, the calculation addresses how much gravitational energy the slow sinking of carbon, separated from methane in the deep interior, can release over the age of each planet, and whether that release matters for the measured intrinsic heat flow. The headline results are: carbon_inventory_kg_neptune = 3.250e+24; carbon_inventory_kg_uranus = 2.750e+24; mean_sinking_rate_kg_s_neptune = 2.289e+07. The method, inputs and limitations are stated in full so that any reader can reproduce or rescale every number from the deposited calculation script. The central finding is that even under a generous once-over inventory assumption, the mean flux from sinking carbon is a small fraction of Neptune intrinsic flux and a modest fraction of the much weaker Uranian flux, so diamond rain is an interesting transport process rather than the main heat source. Agreement and disagreement with independent published estimates are reported at their actual size, and the conclusions are limited to what the budget arithmetic supports.

title: Skin‐Interfaced Wearable Device for Synchronically Harvesting High‐Entropy Body Energy and Monitoring Deep Tissue Temperature
summary: ABSTRACT Efficiently harvesting thermal energy from human skin poses formidable challenges owing to its high‐entropy characteristics. While Seebeck‐effect wearable thermoelectric devices can convert skin heat flux into electrical voltage, p
content: ABSTRACT Efficiently harvesting thermal energy from human skin poses formidable challenges owing to its high‐entropy characteristics. While Seebeck‐effect wearable thermoelectric devices can convert skin heat flux into electrical voltage, prevailing generators remain constrained in delivering sustainable energy and multifunctionality. This limitation stems from a fundamental trade‐off where the output voltage falls below the effective charging threshold, leaving the ultra‐low skin heat flux underexplored for physiological sensing. In this study, we report a skin‐interfaced wearable thermoelectric sensor and generator that synchronously harvests body high‐entropy energy and monitors deep tissue temperature (< 0.2°C). This dual functionality is enabled by a thermal meta‐design that guides inherently dispersed cutaneous heat flux into a vertical, one‐dimensional path through geometric confinement, ensuring signal fidelity for both sensing and energy conversion. To overcome the limited skin‐ambient temperature gradient, we introduce a reusable cooling hydrogel patch based on a dual‐mode evaporation mechanism, boosting the electrical output to 120 mV and power density to 45.7 μW cm –2 . Furthermore, during daily wear under an approximate 10 K skin‐environment temperature differential, the system achieved a sustained output of up to 34 mV. The integrated voltage boost‐storage circuit maintained the capacitor voltage at around 1.044 V, facilitating a sustainable power supply to electronic loads, and stabilized at approximately 5.2 V near full charge. The integrated system demonstrates continuous, multi‐parameter health monitoring powered solely by body heat. This research establishes a co‐design paradigm for concurrent deep body temperature monitoring and high‐entropy energy recovery, paving the way for self‐powered, multimodal integrated wearable devices.

title: Counterfactual Forest Foundation Model for Additionality Verification and Dynamic Valuation of Forest Carbon Sinks
summary: Reliable forest carbon credits require credible estimates of carbon storage without intervention, yet conventional counterfactual approaches often fail to capture pre-intervention forest dynamics, staggered protection timing and carbon perm
content: Reliable forest carbon credits require credible estimates of carbon storage without intervention, yet conventional counterfactual approaches often fail to capture pre-intervention forest dynamics, staggered protection timing and carbon permanence. To address these gaps, we develop a counterfactual forest foundation model (CF-FM) integrating masked spatio-temporal representation learning, doubly robust estimation for staggered adoption, empirical-Bayes partial pooling and permanence-adjusted valuation. CF-FM encodes historical forest-cover, disturbance and climate trajectories with neighbourhood context to estimate reserve-designation effects across cohorts and event times. We evaluate the framework using a 150,000-cell panel from south-west China, covering 138 nature reserves designated during 1995–2012, and a 40-repetition semi-synthetic benchmark. CF-FM achieves the lowest effect-surface root-mean-square error (0.00079) among six estimators, improving on its raw-covariate counterpart by 18.6%, with 97.7% empirical coverage of nominal 95% intervals. On the observed panel, its estimated average forest-cover effect is −0.05 percentage points, versus 7.64 percentage points from two-way fixed effects, highlighting sensitivity to counterfactual specification. A 20-year valuation scenario yields 11.1 CNY ha⁻¹ at 100 CNY per tCO₂e and a 3% discount rate. CF-FM thus links trajectory-informed causal inference to permanence-adjusted valuation, providing a framework for assessing forest-carbon additionality while making baseline and valuation uncertainty explicit.

title: Unimolecular Kinetics of Alkoxy Radicals: A Computational Approach to Understanding Branching Ratios
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
summary: Abstract Alkoxy and hydroxyalkoxy radicals are key intermediates in the reactions of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in the troposphere. The end products of these reactions contribute to secondary organic aerosol formation and ground-leve
content: Abstract Alkoxy and hydroxyalkoxy radicals are key intermediates in the reactions of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in the troposphere. The end products of these reactions contribute to secondary organic aerosol formation and ground-level ozone (O3). To understand the various unimolecular decomposition and isomerization reactions of these intermediates, we implement a composite form of ΔE, in which the correlation effects are captured using the LNO–CCSD(T) approach. Rate constants are computed using canonical transition state theory (TST) with correction factors for entropic, quantum, and pressure effects. The pressure dependence is evaluated using the chemically significant eigenvalue scheme for solving the master equation. Entropic effects are treated using the hindered rotor approximation to account for the anharmonicity caused by large-amplitude motion, along with the small-curvature tunneling correction to incorporate quantum effects. Because multidimensional tunneling approaches are computationally intensive, machine learning models are incorporated to reduce computation time and cost. The new theoretical framework agrees well with experimental results for both alkoxy and β-hydroxyalkoxy systems within a factor of 2. The proposed workflow can be extended to larger systems at a modest computational cost.

title: Multi-scenario ecosystem service trade-offs and ecological security patterns in the upper Yongding River Basin, China (1990-2024)
summary: Abstract Context. Balancing multiple ecosystem services (ESs) is a prerequisite for constructing a stable ecological security pattern (ESP); however, conventional ESP studies rarely account for service trade-offs when selecting conservation
content: Abstract Context. Balancing multiple ecosystem services (ESs) is a prerequisite for constructing a stable ecological security pattern (ESP); however, conventional ESP studies rarely account for service trade-offs when selecting conservation priorities. Therefore, explicitly linking these trade-offs to ESP dynamics is essential for evidence-based landscape conservation planning. Objectives. This study used the upper Yongding River Basin (44,006 km²), a key water source and ecological barrier for the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region, as the study area. We aimed to combine seven OWA weighting scenarios with ESP construction and evaluate the resulting network from 1990 to 2024. Methods. Six ESs were quantified using InVEST for 1990, 2000, 2010, and 2024. The OWA operator generated seven trade-off scenarios (weighting parameters 0.001–1000), and the preferred scenario under the tested metric was used with MSPA, Circuitscape and four graph-theoretic indices (α, β, γ, ρ) to construct and assess the ESP. Results. Scenario S5 (α = 2) achieved the highest average conservation efficiency in every period. The MSPA core share declined from 56.10% to 48.26%, while the bridge share increased to 40.86%. Ecological sources contracted from 23 patches (9,190.8 km²) in 1990 to 14 patches (5,852.4 km²) in 2024. The network became more compact and topologically redundant, even as habitats fragmented and sources consolidated. Protecting remaining primary sources and restoring bridge-class corridors could therefore improve connectivity at lower conservation cost. Conclusions. The workflow provides a basin-specific basis for balancing service trade-offs and supports conservation zoning and adaptive basin management. S5 is a local preference under the tested inputs and not a general rule.

title: Ultra-small bacteria and their phages discovered through metagenomics in a sub-arctic degrading permafrost ecosystem
summary: Patescibacteriota is a diverse bacterial phylum characterized by ultra-small cell size, streamlined genome, incomplete metabolism and episymbiotic lifestyle. While Patescibacteriota have been detected across a wide range of ecosystem types,
content: Patescibacteriota is a diverse bacterial phylum characterized by ultra-small cell size, streamlined genome, incomplete metabolism and episymbiotic lifestyle. While Patescibacteriota have been detected across a wide range of ecosystem types, their phages are not widely described. We utilized metagenomics to explore these less characterized parts of the microbiome in a sporadic permafrost ecosystem, with samples from palsa and peat soils, small ponds and streams. We retrieved 33 high-quality metagenome assembled genomes (MAGs) of Patescibacteriota, mainly from the classes Minisyncoccia and Saccharimonadia.
