Minisyncoccia was a dominant class in the thawing soils and thaw ponds, whereas the Saccharimonadia was more abundant in the frozen palsa soil layers. The distribution of the Patescibacteria classes was also reflected in their metabolic potential. For example, gluconeogenesis pathway was complete only in MAGs from the class Minisyncoccia, whereas cytochrome o ubiquinol oxidase was mainly found from the MAGs of the class Saccharimondia. The viral community analysis yielded 16 354 viral operational taxonomic units (vOTUs), which represented mainly tailed dsDNA viruses from the class Caudoviricetes. Based on genome size, 16 vOTUs were qualified as jumbophages and one as a megaphage. Similar to the bacterial community, the viral community composition differed across sample types. The most common hosts for bacterial viruses were phyla Pseudomonadota, Acidobacteriota and Actinomycetota. A further 196 vOTUs were in silico linked to Patescibacteriota hosts. The Patescibacteriota phages were diverse, with only two vOTUs representing the same genus. The relative abundance of Patescibacteriota-associated phages was especially high in frozen palsa soils, largely following the same pattern of abundance as Patescibacteriota.

title: Deep straw burialbuilds durable subsoil carbon sinks through fungal-mineral coupling
summary: Agricultural subsoils hold the largest untapped potential for soil carbon sequestration, yet what governs both the stabilization of carbon derivedfrom crop residueburialand the durability of the resulting sink remains unresolved.Here, we re
content: Agricultural subsoils hold the largest untapped potential for soil carbon sequestration, yet what governs both the stabilization of carbon derivedfrom crop residueburialand the durability of the resulting sink remains unresolved.Here, we resolve this by pairing 16-year and 4-year field trials of ditch-buried straw return (DB), both benchmarked against rotary-tillage straw return (RT) and combining 13C and 15N tracing with direct measurements of pore architecture, oxygen dynamics, iron speciation, and microbial physiology. DB raised SOC stocks across 0-50 cm by 42%, with 72% of the gain as mineral-associated organic carbon (MAOC). DB increased macroporosity by 332% and raised oxygen availability at 15–30 cm; this aeration in turn relieved the energetic constraint on fungi, enriching fungal α-diversity 5.3-fold. The resulting fungal nitrogen mining then eased the stoichiometric constraint on microbial growth and raised carbon use efficiency by 43–119%. Isotopic tracing showed DB routed far more plant-derived carbon into MAOC than RT (55–92% versus 7–46%), and that decomposition of SOC was suppressed by 71%. Fungal necromass co-precipitated with poorly crystalline iron oxides, which accounted for 57–73% of the MAOC pool. Thus, fungal-mineral coupling under deep straw burial overcomes abiotic constraints to transform subsoils into efficient carbon sinks, sequestering 11.53 Mg C ha-1over 16 years and offering dual benefits for agricultural productivity and climate mitigation.

title: Variable Controlling Mechanisms on the Effect of Winter Storms on Sea-Air Carbon Dioxide Exchange in a Large Shelf Sea
summary: Winter storms are expected to enhance sea-air carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) fluxes in shelf seas through wind-driven increase in gas transfer velocity, yet whether this enhances net uptake or release remains poorly constrained due to regional hete
content: Winter storms are expected to enhance sea-air carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) fluxes in shelf seas through wind-driven increase in gas transfer velocity, yet whether this enhances net uptake or release remains poorly constrained due to regional heterogeneity and scarce direct observations during storms. Here we use autonomous FerryBox observations of surface seawater p CO 2 across the North Sea to characterise sea-air CO 2 fluxes before, during, and after 39 major storms (2015-2020). Near-surface wind speed increased by 5.8 ± 2.3 m s -1 consistently across all regions confirming large-scale storm forcing. Regional clustering revealed contrasting changes in the CO 2 flux density: the carbon sink intensified in the permanently stratified region (change of −2.3 mmol m -2 d -1 ), whereas the carbon source intensified in the western region of freshwater influence (change of +13.0 mmol m -2 d -1 ). Across the study area, the change in seawater p CO 2 , rather than in wind speed, was the dominant predictor of CO 2 flux changes during storms. Wind speed change correlated significantly with flux change only for storms when the sea-air p CO 2 disequilibrium was preserved. A December 2016 storm case study showed significant area-integrated effects: the North Sea shifted from a weak net sink (−4.5 Gg C d -1 ) to a strong net source (+43.6 Gg C d -1 ) within a few days, with incomplete recovery up to one week after the storm. These findings indicate that seawater p CO 2 changes and precursory water column structure, not wind speed increase alone, govern the impact of large storms on the regional carbon cycle in heterogeneous shelf seas.

title: Associations of indoor air per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) exposure in schools with respiratory and skin outcomes in children: Single-pollutant, exposure-response, and mixture analyses
source: International Journal of Hygiene and Environmental Health
summary: Schools are important but under-characterized microenvironments for children's exposure to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), with potential health implications given children's greater susceptibility. We assessed associations betw
content: Schools are important but under-characterized microenvironments for children's exposure to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), with potential health implications given children's greater susceptibility. We assessed associations between indoor-air PFAS in schools and respiratory and skin outcomes in children using single-pollutant, dose-response, and mixture-based approaches. Indoor air PFAS were measured in 36 classrooms across 8 primary schools in Porto, Portugal, using passive sampling over 28 days. Health outcomes, including ever asthma, current asthma, wheezing, and eczema, were collected through standardized parent-completed questionnaires. After false discovery rate correction, perfluoropropane sulfonic acid (PFPrS) was associated with higher odds of ever asthma (aOR:1.12; 95%CI:1.04-1.27) and current asthma (aOR:1.26; 95%CI:1.06-1.50), whereas perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS) was associated with lower odds of both ever (aOR:0.80; 95%CI:0.54-0.98) and current asthma (aOR:0.66; 95%CI:0.36-0.89). Perfluorobutane sulfonic acid (PFBS; aOR:1.19; 95%CI:1.03-1.35) and 6:2 fluorotelomer acrylate (6:2 FTAcr; aOR:1.18; 95%CI:1.01-1.38) were associated with higher odds of wheezing, while 8:2 fluorotelomer alcohol (8:2 FTOH) was associated with higher odds of eczema (aOR:1.31; 95%CI:1.04-1.67). Mixture-weight analyses indicated contrasting contributions of individual PFAS, with PFBS and TFA contributing positively to ever asthma, 6:2 FTAcr showing the largest positive contribution to wheezing, and PFOS contributing negatively across respiratory outcomes. A simultaneous one-quantile increase in all PFAS was not associated with any of the health outcomes after correction. These findings indicate compound- and outcome-specific associations between indoor air PFAS and children's respiratory and skin health, while highlighting the complexity of evaluating co-exposure to multiple PFAS.

title: Cold Polymerization Enables a Hybrid Hydrogel for Coupling Electronic Devices to Skin
summary: Wearable electronic devices monitoring physiological signals from skin generate heat that can lead to skin irritation, burns, and reduced device lifespan. Current heat-managing materials involve trade-offs in performance, flexibility, stren
content: Wearable electronic devices monitoring physiological signals from skin generate heat that can lead to skin irritation, burns, and reduced device lifespan. Current heat-managing materials involve trade-offs in performance, flexibility, strength, and biocompatibility. Here, we report a heat-managing adhesive hydrogel for wearables that is simultaneously transparent to ultrasound waves, available for electronic recording, conformable to skin, durable and biocompatible. Our hydrogel integrates biomacromolecule gelatin with synthetic polyacrylamide. A cold crosslinking strategy is proposed to kinetically trap the gelatin-acrylamide mixture in a physical gel state prior to photocrosslinking, effectively preventing otherwise phase separation and yielding a transmitted and structurally stable hybrid hydrogel. In our hydrogel, gelatin absorbs heat through gel-sol transition, while its chemical crosslinking with polyacrylamide strengthens the material. The resulting hydrogel is an excellent coupling pad for ultrasound imaging and electroencephalogram recording, and functions as a strain sensor for monitoring human motion. This hybrid material system could be a universal material form coupling rigid devices to skin or coupling stretchable electronic devices to skin.

title: From MAB precursors to dynamic MBene interfaces: A mechanistic framework for working-state evolution and functional performance
source: Advances in Colloid and Interface Science
summary: Two-dimensional (2D) transition-metal borides (MBenes) have emerged as a chemically distinct family of layered materials whose behavior differs fundamentally from that of carbide- and nitride-based 2D systems. Unlike MXenes, experimentally
content: Two-dimensional (2D) transition-metal borides (MBenes) have emerged as a chemically distinct family of layered materials whose behavior differs fundamentally from that of carbide- and nitride-based 2D systems. Unlike MXenes, experimentally realized MBenes are governed by precursor-encoded complexity, whereby MAB precursor chemistry, synthesis history, surface terminations, defects, reconstruction, and oxidation collectively determine their electronic structure and functional response. Although recent studies have rapidly expanded the range of synthesized MBenes and demonstrated their potential across diverse applications, the mechanistic links connecting precursor chemistry, synthesis pathways, dynamic surface evolution, and operational performance remain insufficiently resolved. This Review develops a unified mechanistic framework that connects these factors to the working states of MBenes in electrocatalysis, photocatalysis, sensing, and electrochemical energy storage. Rather than treating MBenes as static two-dimensional boride lattices, we show that their experimentally relevant behavior is more consistently understood in terms of chemically heterogeneous and dynamically evolving interfaces whose active states depend on both synthesis history and operating conditions. We critically distinguish experimentally supported observations from computational predictions and mechanistic hypotheses, with particular emphasis on operando characterization, realistic computational models, and integrated experiment theory simulation approaches. By framing MBenes as synthesis-encoded, chemically adaptive materials, this Review establishes design principles for linking precursor selection and surface evolution to functional performance and provides a foundation for predictive, mechanism-driven MBene engineering.

title: High-resolution assessment and attribution of vegetation net primary productivity dynamics under changing socio-ecological conditions in the Zhengzhou Metropolitan Area, China
summary: Vegetation net primary productivity (NPP) provides a measure of ecosystem carbon assimilation and vegetation responses to environmental changes. The relative roles of climatic variability and anthropogenic effects in regulating NPP dynamics
content: Vegetation net primary productivity (NPP) provides a measure of ecosystem carbon assimilation and vegetation responses to environmental changes. The relative roles of climatic variability and anthropogenic effects in regulating NPP dynamics remain unclear in rapidly urbanizing landscapes. This study investigated NPP dynamics and their drivers in the Zhengzhou Metropolitan Area (ZMA), China, during 2000–2020 using a 30-m resolution NPP dataset generated by integrating Landsat-MODIS spatiotemporal fusion and the CASA model. A scenario-based attribution framework was applied to quantify the relative contributions of climatic variability and anthropogenic effects across different socio-ecological phases. NPP showed a significant increasing trend during 2000–2020, whereas the periods before and after the early-2010s transition exhibited a weak negative tendency and a positive tendency, respectively, neither of which was statistically significant at the regional scale. Vegetation degradation was concentrated in urban expansion and agricultural areas, while recovery was mainly distributed across mountainous ecosystems, ecological corridors, and urban green spaces. Anthropogenic effects represented the largest relative contribution of NPP changes, increasing from 54.20% in Phase I to 61.63% in Phase II. Climatic variability remained a contributor, although its relative contribution decreased after 2010. These findings indicate that vegetation responses to urbanization depend strongly on development stages and ecological management strategies, highlighting the importance of integrating urban development with ecological restoration and adaptive land management.

title: Towards spatio-temporal extrapolation of phase-field simulations with convolution-only neural networks
summary: Phase-field simulations of liquid metal dealloying (LMD) capture complex microstructural evolution but become prohibitively expensive over large domains and long time horizons. We introduce a fully convolutional, conditionally parameterized
content: Phase-field simulations of liquid metal dealloying (LMD) capture complex microstructural evolution but become prohibitively expensive over large domains and long time horizons. We introduce a fully convolutional, conditionally parameterized U-Net surrogate designed to extrapolate far beyond its training data in both space and time. The architecture combines convolutional self-attention, physically informed padding, and a flood-fill corrector to preserve accuracy under extrapolation, while conditioning on simulation parameters enables flexible time-step skipping and adaptation to varying alloy compositions. To eliminate the need for costly solver-based initialization, we couple the surrogate with a conditional diffusion model that generates synthetic, physically consistent initial conditions. Training uses simulations on small domains over short time spans; exploiting the convolutional nature of U-Nets, the trained surrogate then runs and extrapolates to longer horizons than classical numerical solvers can reach. Across multiple alloy compositions, the framework reproduces LMD physics accurately within the spatial and temporal ranges validated against direct numerical simulation (DNS). It predicts key quantities of interest and spatial statistics with relative errors typically below 5% in the training regime and under 15% during large-scale, long-horizon extrapolation. The framework delivers speed-ups of $${{{\mathcal{O}}}}(1{0}^{4})$$ over DNS, reducing weeks-long simulations to seconds and allowing the computational domain to expand beyond what conventional mesh-based discretizations permit. This work is a first stepping stone toward surrogate models for rapid screening, parameter studies, and uncertainty quantification in LMD.

title: Potential of point source imaging satellite instruments to infer diffuse methane emissions: a theoretical case study of the Near-Infrared Multispectral Camera (NIMCAM)
summary: Satellite measurements have revolutionized methane monitoring, yet persistent clouds and aerosols often limit global-survey instruments like TROPOMI in the tropics. This study evaluates the potential of the Near Infrared Multispectral Camer
content: Satellite measurements have revolutionized methane monitoring, yet persistent clouds and aerosols often limit global-survey instruments like TROPOMI in the tropics. This study evaluates the potential of the Near Infrared Multispectral Camera for Atmospheric Methane (NIMCAM), a high-resolution instrument (60 m pixels) designed for point sources, to quantify large-scale diffuse emissions across tropical Africa. Through Observing System Simulation Experiments (OSSEs), we compare an in-orbit demonstrator and small NIMCAM constellations (3 and 5 satellites) against synthetic data from the TROPOMI (TROPOspheric Monitoring Instrument) instrument. Using Sentinel-2 cloud probabilities and downscaled MODIS aerosol optical depth products, we find that NIMCAM's finer spatial resolution significantly increases clear-sky data yields. A 5-satellite constellation provides up to six times more clear-sky observations than TROPOMI. As masking criteria for clouds and aerosols become more stringent, the ratio of NIMCAM to TROPOMI random error (σNIM/σTROP) decreases. This occurs because TROPOMI's coarser footprint leads to a more rapid loss of data under strict thresholds. Using the GEOS-Chem chemical transport model and an ensemble Kalman Filter, we demonstrate that NIMCAM observations offer substantial added value in resolving tropical emissions. NIMCAM achieves higher uncertainty reduction than TROPOMI, particularly in regions and seasons where cloud and aerosol loading restrict coarser instruments. Our findings support using high-resolution methane technology to complement global surveys in monitoring diffuse tropical emissions.

title: SIP-enabled multi-omics reveals soil microbiome responses to drought and rehydration
summary: Soil microbial activity, and the balance of anabolic (carbon assimilating) and catabolic (CO2-releasing) processes, control the magnitude and direction of soil carbon fluxes. Soil hydration controls this activity, and with hydroclimate vola
content: Soil microbial activity, and the balance of anabolic (carbon assimilating) and catabolic (CO2-releasing) processes, control the magnitude and direction of soil carbon fluxes. Soil hydration controls this activity, and with hydroclimate volatility increasing across many regions, microbial responses to drought-rewetting cycles urgently require quantification. We conducted rainfall exclusion experiments at two Mediterranean-type field sites, coupling isotope labeling with multi-omics, to link microbial growth, greenhouse gas fluxes, and the carbon sources driving both. Rehydration shortened apparent cell generation times from years to days within minutes. High-intensity drought lengthened the lag before growth resumed, yet metagenomic inference indicated post-drought enrichment of rapid-growth phenotypes. Drought and rehydration shifted the soil metabolome, implicating specific osmolytes in the microbial response and suggesting metabolite diversity modulates microbial function. These results constrain soil microbial activity rates and mechanisms underlying drought-rewetting responses and motivate further study of carbon cycling under increasingly volatile hydroclimates. This study demonstrates that soil microbial growth rates are extremely slow under dry conditions, with rehydration causing a rapid increase in anabolic activity within days. These findings refine our understanding of microbial contributions to soil carbon cycling with a warming climate.

title: Methane in the Asian Monsoon anticyclone and global UTLS behavior observed in ACE-FTS satellite data
summary: Methane in the upper troposphere and lower stratosphere (UTLS) plays a critical role in atmospheric composition and radiative forcing, yet the processes governing its vertical structure and variability remain poorly understood. Here, we use
content: Methane in the upper troposphere and lower stratosphere (UTLS) plays a critical role in atmospheric composition and radiative forcing, yet the processes governing its vertical structure and variability remain poorly understood. Here, we use high-quality satellite observations from the Atmospheric Chemistry Experiment Fourier Transform Spectrometer (ACE-FTS) to characterize the vertical structure and global seasonal behavior of methane in the UTLS, with emphasis on the role of Asian Summer Monsoon (ASM). In the ASM, a maximum in methane concentration occurs near the tropopause, at a higher altitude than the corresponding carbon monoxide maximum. The largest relative enhancement for methane – the difference between air inside and outside the anticyclone – occurs above the tropopause and extends poleward to the north. This behavior contrasts with carbon monoxide, which is confined within the anticyclone. The seasonal cycle of methane near the tropical tropopause peaks in boreal autumn, following the summer peak in surface fluxes and deep convection. This phase lag reflects the combined effects of ASM transport and subsequent large-scale redistribution following the breakdown of the anticyclone. Positive anomalies occur in the tropical lower stratosphere in boreal winter, consistent with the upwelling branch of the Brewer–Dobson circulation (BDC). Beyond the seasonal cycle, ACE-FTS data show a pronounced hemispheric asymmetry in lower stratospheric methane trends, consistent with reported changes in other long-lived trace constituents. Together, these results provide new observational evidence that ASM transport imprints a distinct methane structure above the tropopause and plays a key role in shaping UTLS variability on a global scale.

title: Assessing lateral inflows to a sub-arctic stream using distributed temperature sensing, terrain metrics, and process-based modeling
summary: Groundwater–surface water interactions regulate streamflow persistence and thermal regimes by linking catchment subsurface water storage to surface hydrology. However, mapping locations of groundwater discharge remains challenging, particul
content: Groundwater–surface water interactions regulate streamflow persistence and thermal regimes by linking catchment subsurface water storage to surface hydrology. However, mapping locations of groundwater discharge remains challenging, particularly in high-latitude catchments with strongly seasonal hydrological cycle. We used high-resolution distributed temperature sensing (DTS) to monitor stream temperature at 2 m spatial and 30 min temporal resolution along a 2 km boreal headwater stream in northern Finland. Seasonal gradient-based thermal patterns were used to identify stream sections dominated by groundwater discharge. In addition, snowmelt periods were used to detect surface and near-surface flow contributions to the stream. We then compared DTS-derived patterns with terrain-based hydrological metrics (upslope contributing areas and topographic wetness index) and SpaFHy-2D hydrological model simulations to assess their ability to predict groundwater discharge and surface water inflow locations. Terrain-based predictions showed limited spatial agreement with DTS (17–40% recall), whereas SpaFHy-2D showed higher recall (83%) but limited spatial overlap (Jaccard index = 0.21). Modelled inflow discharge locations remained spatially consistent across seasons, while inflow magnitudes varied seasonally and were highest during snowmelt. DTS effectively detected groundwater–surface water interactions and exposed limitations of terrain metrics and hydrological models. In this peatland-esker sub-arctic catchment, groundwater discharge appeared to be influenced by hydrogeological heterogeneity that was not fully captured by surface topography, while a peatland drainage ditch enhanced lateral connectivity between peatlands and the stream.

title: Analysis of heat transfer due to steady MHD flow in a porous channel with Navier slip and convective boundary
source: Multiscale and Multidisciplinary Modeling Experiments and Design
summary: In this study, we investigated a steady magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) shear flow and heat transfer in a porous channel subject to Navier slip and asymmetric thermal boundary conditions, consisting of a convective lower wall and an isothermal up
content: In this study, we investigated a steady magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) shear flow and heat transfer in a porous channel subject to Navier slip and asymmetric thermal boundary conditions, consisting of a convective lower wall and an isothermal upper wall. The model describes the coupled effects of wall slip, magnetic forces, porous-medium suction/injection, viscous dissipation, internal heat generation/absorption, and Joule heating on fluid transport and thermal behaviour. The governing momentum and energy equations are nondimensionalised and solved analytically using the method of undetermined coefficients. Closed-form expressions are obtained for the velocity and temperature fields, from which the skin friction, mass flow rate, and Nusselt number are determined. The effects of the Reynolds, Peclet, Biot, Brinkman, magnetic, and slip parameters are examined for heat-source and heat-sink conditions, with and without Joule dissipation. The results show that magnetic effects and suction suppress the velocity field, while the influence of wall slip depends on its location. Increasing the Peclet and slip parameters generally reduces the fluid temperature, whereas increasing the Biot, magnetic, and Brinkman parameters enhances it. Injection and suction produce contrasting thermal responses, while Joule heating raises the temperature and partially offsets cooling caused by heat absorption. The findings demonstrate that the interaction between wall slip, magnetic effects, porous-medium transport, and asymmetric thermal boundary conditions plays a significant role in controlling heat transfer in MHD porous-channel systems.

title: New particle formation contribution to aerosol mass: regimes and implications for future urban environments
summary: New particle formation (NPF) is a major source of global aerosol number concentration yet its contribution to aerosol mass remains unclear. Here we propose a regime framework for NPF mass contributions using aerosol dynamic simulations cons
content: New particle formation (NPF) is a major source of global aerosol number concentration yet its contribution to aerosol mass remains unclear. Here we propose a regime framework for NPF mass contributions using aerosol dynamic simulations constrained by atmospheric measurements. We show that new particles can contribute more than 10 µg m −3 to particle mass under conditions characterized by high initial new particle concentrations, high condensable vapor production rates, and low background condensation sink (CS bg ). Among these influencing factors, the initial CS bg governs NPF mass contribution under the simulation conditions: NPF contributes significantly to aerosol surface area and mass at an initial CS bg of ∼ 0.001 s −1 (regime I), while its contribution becomes negligible when CS bg exceeds 0.01 s −1 (regime III). Results show that NPF events in urban Beijing occur mostly in a transition regime (initial CS bg 0.001–0.01 s −1 , regime II), in which the NPF mass contribution is also modulated by the mass accommodation coefficient of background particles, while events at a Finnish forest site fall in regimes I and II. Our simulations suggest that NPF mass contribution in urban environments with a declining CS bg will shift toward regimes I and II. This indicates that control of anthropogenic NPF precursors may represent an effective strategy for present and future particulate matter pollution in urban environments, which warrants further investigation.

title: Interpreting NADH fluorescence lifetime across timescales
summary: NADH fluorescence lifetime imaging is a widely used, label-free way to visualize cell metabolism, typically read as a balance between glycolysis and oxidative respiration. This reading assumes that the effective NADH-binding landscape remai
content: NADH fluorescence lifetime imaging is a widely used, label-free way to visualize cell metabolism, typically read as a balance between glycolysis and oxidative respiration. This reading assumes that the effective NADH-binding landscape remains sufficiently stable during the experiment. This assumption is generally best protected during brief perturbations, but can fail in two ways: slowly, as prolonged treatments or differentiation reshape the identity and abundance of NADH-binding enzymes over hours to days; and rapidly, as metabolites can transiently alter their engagement with NADH even without changes in protein abundance. In this Perspective, we outline when each concern applies and offer practical guidance for experimental design and interpretation.

title: Laundering efficiencies of extractors vs household machines on wildland fire contaminants
summary: Background Wildland firefighter gear typically consists of shirts and pants manufactured from textiles such as Nomex® and Kevlar. These materials provide a flame resistant barrier to the wearer but may be difficult to clean. Methods Twelve
content: Background Wildland firefighter gear typically consists of shirts and pants manufactured from textiles such as Nomex® and Kevlar. These materials provide a flame resistant barrier to the wearer but may be difficult to clean. Methods Twelve shirts worn in recent wildland fire events in the United States (US) were analyzed to determine contamination, specifically semi-volatile organic compounds (SVOCs) contamination so that best cleaning practices could be established. Several SVOCs, including phthalates and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), were identified. New Nomex® textiles used to construct wildland shirts and pants were contaminated and laundered under a range of temperature conditions using a commercial extractor at 40-60 °C (105–140oF) and a household machine at 29-49 °C (85–120°F) to determine cleaning efficiency between commercial (extractor) machines and household washers. Key results Results showed high removal rates (typically above 58%) for all of the chemicals using a temperature and g-forces controlled commercial extractor and a front-loading household washer with a cold/warm/hot selector and no g-force control. Conclusions This research suggests that a dedicated household-grade laundering machine may provide cleaning levels equivalent to commercial extractors for wildland gear. Implications The results may provide a new option for cleaning Nomex wildland protective clothing.

title: Planetary material is a major source of hydrogen in helium-atmosphere white dwarfs
source: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
summary: Abstract Many white dwarfs with helium-dominated atmospheres show traces of hydrogen in their spectra. On average, the total mass of hydrogen within their convective envelopes increases with age, but there is no consensus on the origin of s
content: Abstract Many white dwarfs with helium-dominated atmospheres show traces of hydrogen in their spectra. On average, the total mass of hydrogen within their convective envelopes increases with age, but there is no consensus on the origin of such hydrogen. Hypotheses include upward diffusion from hidden reservoirs deep within the envelope, or accretion, alongside heavier elements, of planetary material. We construct a simple model that includes both pathways, and test it using two independent samples of helium-atmosphere DB white dwarfs from the DESI and SDSS spectroscopic surveys, selected to have Gaia colours GBP − GRP > −0.25, corresponding roughly to 10 000 ≲ Teff ≲ 19 000 K. We find that at least 22 ± 2 per cent of the helium-atmosphere white dwarfs with detectable hydrogen must have accreted some of it from their planetary systems, via ices, hydrated minerals or atmospheres. We thus demonstrate that planetary hydrogen is a necessary ingredient to explain the spectral evolution of white dwarfs as a population, rather than only extreme hydrogen-enriched cases.

title: Understanding Cyanobacterial Harmful Algal Blooms: From Ecological Drivers and Impacts to Management
summary: Cyanobacterial harmful algal blooms are becoming more frequent and intense in many regions, threatening drinking water, irrigation, livestock watering and aquaculture, and some produce toxins that can harm people and animals. This paper exp
content: Cyanobacterial harmful algal blooms are becoming more frequent and intense in many regions, threatening drinking water, irrigation, livestock watering and aquaculture, and some produce toxins that can harm people and animals. This paper explains what drives blooms, how their toxins reach farms and food, and how long-term nutrient reduction and site-specific treatment can manage them.

title: A Global, Seasonally Resolved BGC-Argo Estimate of Deep Particulate Organic Carbon Flux
summary: Quantifying the global magnitude and variability of the biological carbon pump's deep flux remains challenging due to sparse, historically limited sediment-trap observations. Biogeochemical Argo (BGC-Argo) floats drifting at 1000 m depth of
content: Quantifying the global magnitude and variability of the biological carbon pump's deep flux remains challenging due to sparse, historically limited sediment-trap observations. Biogeochemical Argo (BGC-Argo) floats drifting at 1000 m depth offer a scalable alternative, combining particulate backscattering (bbp) sensors, transmissometers used as optical sediment traps (OST), and, on a subset of floats, Underwater Vision Profiler 6 (UVP6) cameras resolving particle size distributions. Using observations from 500 BGC-Argo floats (2012-2026), we derive regional and seasonal climatologies of particulate organic carbon (POC) flux at 1000 m and develop log10-linear models relating daily-averaged bbp spike height to OST-derived flux. A general model, fit across regions, explains substantial variance (R2=0.54), but a region-specific model is required south of the Polar Front in the Southern Ocean (SPF_SO; R2=0.89), consistent with distinct, diatom-dominated export dynamics; without this isolation, SPF_SO flux would be underestimated by about a factor of two. Applying these models globally, we obtain regional and seasonal POC flux climatologies broadly consistent with independent sediment-trap observations. The resulting global annual POC flux at 1000 m is 0.95-1.34 PgC yr⁻1, of which nearly 65% is estimated to be sequestered for a century or more. These results demonstrate the potential of the growing BGC-Argo fleet to deliver a sustained, high-frequency, global view of deep-ocean carbon flux, complementing sparse trap coverage and supporting the monitoring of the current and future deep ocean biological carbon pump.

title: Impacts of Biological Filtration on Disinfection Byproduct Control during Drinking Water Purification: A Critical Review
summary: Abstract Biofiltration, particularly biological activated carbon and sand filtration, is widely implemented as a low-chemical, energy-efficient barrier to attenuate disinfection byproduct (DBP) precursors. However, biofilters are living, ti
content: Abstract Biofiltration, particularly biological activated carbon and sand filtration, is widely implemented as a low-chemical, energy-efficient barrier to attenuate disinfection byproduct (DBP) precursors. However, biofilters are living, time-evolving ecosystems that can transition from a net “sink” to a net “source” of reactive precursors. This review synthesized evidence that biofiltration exhibits selective removal: hydrophobic and high-molecular-weight C-DBP precursors are preferentially removed, whereas hydrophilic N-DBP (e.g., HANs, NDMA) precursors readily break through and may be newly produced. The authors clarified the mechanistic basis of precursor generation, highlighting (i) biofilm turnover that releases intracellular organic matter enriched in amines and nucleic acids, (ii) continuous production and sloughing of soluble microbial products and extracellular polymeric substances that elevate protein-like DON, and (iii) media aging and stratification that diminish removal efficacy. Regression analysis estimated sink–source transition for N-DBP precursor removal at approximately log10(bed volumes) = 5.38 (∼240,000 bed volumes), a practical reference in drinking water treatment plants. Furthermore, the authors identified critical operational tipping points, including oxidant pre-exposure, temperature fluctuations, and nutrient stoichiometry, that can trigger this functional inversion. Finally, a risk-oriented framework is proposed, advocating for precursor-specific monitoring (e.g., fluorescence signatures) and intelligent process control to stabilize biofilter performance against emerging genotoxic risks.

title: Shaping of plant form for high output and concentrated boll formation using slow-release nitrogen application in summer direct seeding cotton
summary: High output and mechanized harvesting of summer direct seeding cotton (SDSC) require both high yield and concentrated boll setting. However, it is unclear how to achieve these goals using slow-release nitrogen fertilizer. We performed a fie
content: High output and mechanized harvesting of summer direct seeding cotton (SDSC) require both high yield and concentrated boll setting. However, it is unclear how to achieve these goals using slow-release nitrogen fertilizer. We performed a field experiment designed to enhance nitrogen use efficiency using a simplified fertilizer application method. The experiment, designed to examine the relationship between plant form and boll-setting speed, comprised three slow-release nitrogen rates (45, 90, and 135 kg N hm −2 ) and two application times (two-leaf and four-leaf stages). The experiment took place at Yangzhou University during the cotton growth seasons in 2021 and 2022. The results showed that the highest seed cotton yield (about 4000 kg hm −2 ) and boll-setting speed (more than 3.0 × 10 4 bolls hm −2 d −1 ) were achieved with 90 kg N hm −2 of slow-release nitrogen at the four-leaf stage. This treatment also achieved suitable agronomic nitrogen use efficiency (ANUE, 10.2–16.4 kg kg −1 ), nitrogen recovery efficiency (NRE, 52.4–54.8%) and partial factor productivity of nitrogen (PFPN, 39.9–40.7 kg kg −1 ), significantly outperforming the CK. There were significant quadratic regression relationships between plant height (PH), the ratio of fruit nodes to fruiting branches (RNB), and the total boll number and boll-setting speed. Fruit branch curvature (FBC) was correlated with population total boll number and boll-setting speed. Positive correlations were found between the fruit branch orientation value (FBOV) and the total boll number and boll-setting speed. These models indicated that a suitable PH (81.2–90.5 cm), RNB (2.6–2.7), low FBC (5.8–5.1 from the lower to upper sections), and high FBOV (36.7–46.5 from the lower to upper sections) comprised a suitable plant form for the tested conditions. The results suggest that plant form regulation by a one-time application of an appropriate slow-release nitrogen rate at the four-leaf stage could optimize SDSC production.

title: Exogenous gallic acid enhances growth, essential oil accumulation, and antioxidant defense of dill under soil moisture deficit
summary: OBJECTIVE: Dill (Anethum graveolens L.) is a valuable aromatic plant, but its cultivation in Egypt's sandy reclaimed soils is constrained by rapid soil moisture depletion. This study evaluated the effects of gallic acid (GA) on dill growth
content: OBJECTIVE: Dill (Anethum graveolens L.) is a valuable aromatic plant, but its cultivation in Egypt's sandy reclaimed soils is constrained by rapid soil moisture depletion. This study evaluated the effects of gallic acid (GA) on dill growth and biochemical responses under different moisture regimes. METHODS: Plants were grown at four field capacity (FC) levels (100, 80, 60, and 40%) and either left untreated or foliar-sprayed with GA (30 mg L⁻¹). Morphological, biochemical and essential oil characteristics were evaluated, and data were analyzed using two-way analysis of variance (ANOVA). KEY RESULTS: GA application improved biomass under full FC, increasing fresh and dry mass by 35.1% and 41.3%, respectively, compared with untreated plants at the same FC level. GA also enhanced essential oil production, with essential oil yield increasing by 70.3% at 60% FC compared with the corresponding untreated plants. At 40% FC, GA increased phenolic and flavonoid contents and DPPH radical-scavenging activity, with DPPH inhibition increasing by 10.7%. GA also promoted the accumulation of proline and antioxidant enzymes under severe moisture deficit. CONCLUSION: Foliar GA application enhanced biomass production, essential oil productivity, and antioxidant capacity in dill under reduced water availability, demonstrating its potential as a biostimulant for improving dill performance under moisture-deficit conditions.

title: Predicting soil-atmosphere CH 4 and CO 2 fluxes across several drained peatland forests with JSBACH-HIMMELI
summary: Abstract. Drainage and other land-use practices, including forestry, substantially influence soil carbon dynamics and associated greenhouse gas (GHG) exchange between boreal peatland soils and atmosphere. Besides the land-use, several site-
content: Abstract. Drainage and other land-use practices, including forestry, substantially influence soil carbon dynamics and associated greenhouse gas (GHG) exchange between boreal peatland soils and atmosphere. Besides the land-use, several site-specific environmental factors, such as water table level (WTL), soil temperature and vegetation regulate the peatland soil GHG balance. It is important to understand the interactions among these co-existing factors at site scale to improve estimates of soil GHG exchange at larger (e.g. regional) spatial scales. Process-based models are useful tools to make large scale estimations, but knowledge about how well the models can capture the variation among drained peatlands, and thus accurately simulate the soil GHG fluxes, are lacking. We simulated key environmental variables (water table level i.e. WTL and soil temperature) and soil–atmosphere methane (CH4) and CO2 (heterotrophic respiration) fluxes at six Finnish forestry-drained peatlands with a process-based JSBACH-HIMMELI model. Specifically, our focus was on evaluating the model performance and identifying the sources of uncertainty across multiple sites by using measurement data over several years from each site. The model predicted key environmental variables adequately well at each study site. In addition, we found that the there was more between-site variation in the prediction accuracy with the simulated CH4 fluxes (NMRSE 1.02–9.25) than with the simulated CO2 fluxes (NMRSE 0.62–1.24). Our study highlights WTL as the primary source of uncertainty in simulating the CH4 fluxes. The sites characterized by consistently deep WTL exhibited substantially better agreement between the model and measurement with the soil–atmosphere CH4 fluxes (RMSE 0.69–1.02 nmol m-2 s-1), than sites characterized by higher WTL (RMSE 1.04–9.70 nmol m-2 s-1). These discrepancies at high-WTL sites were associated with high anaerobic respiration peaks, which were enhanced by relatively thick modelled acrotelm (i.e. fast decomposing topsoil layer). Our results demonstrate that CH4 parameterization has only a minor influence on modelled CH4 fluxes, compared to WTL, but can nevertheless improve prediction accuracy, especially at sites characterized by high WTL.

title: Circulation, mixing, and biogeochemical exchange in the Gulf of Taranto
summary: Abstract. The Gulf of Taranto, between the Adriatic and eastern Mediterranean basins, is a gateway for water-mass exchange and transformation, yet its vertical mixing and the biogeochemical consequences remain poorly quantified. We present
content: Abstract. The Gulf of Taranto, between the Adriatic and eastern Mediterranean basins, is a gateway for water-mass exchange and transformation, yet its vertical mixing and the biogeochemical consequences remain poorly quantified. We present a full-depth transect across the Gulf entrance, sampled during the PIONEER-2023 cruise (November–December 2023), combining hydrography and velocity with dissolved oxygen, nutrients, dissolved inorganic carbon and total alkalinity. The section was occupied in a cyclonic state, with doming isopycnals in the upper 300 m lifting nutrient- and carbon-rich water. Water-mass-resolved transports describe an asymmetric but compensated exchange: a robust eastern surface inflow, a weaker, marginally resolved resident deep inflow, and an Adriatic-derived deep vein entering and leaving without a resolvable net contribution. Section-integrated budgets are indistinguishable from zero for every tracer, so the result is how exchange partitions among water masses, not a net budget. Finescale estimates reveal contrasting regimes around an oxygen minimum layer near 1000 m: double-diffusive above, internal-wave-driven below and in deeper sheared layers. Oxygen, dissolved inorganic carbon and alkalinity converge into the layer across both boundaries, preferentially from below, whereas nutrient fluxes are tracer-specific, phosphate and silicic acid differing in direction from nitrate. Because diapycnal exchange supplies oxygen from both sides, it erodes the minimum rather than sustaining it; its persistence requires consumption or advective terms a single survey cannot resolve. The Gulf thus acts as an active transformation zone rather than a passive conduit, modifying the ventilation state, nutrient content and carbonate chemistry of the water masses crossing it toward the Ionian Sea.

title: China's CO₂ Emissions and Human-Driver Indicators (1991–2024)
summary: This dataset accompanies the study "Opening the Black Box of Environmental Pressure" and provides annual data for China covering the period 1991–2024. It consists of China's CO₂ emissions data and 14 indicators used in the empirical applica
content: This dataset accompanies the study "Opening the Black Box of Environmental Pressure" and provides annual data for China covering the period 1991–2024. It consists of China's CO₂ emissions data and 14 indicators used in the empirical application of the Integrated White-Box (IWB) framework. The 14 indicators are organized into four dimensions: 1. Exchange capacity: energy consumption, transport, capital stock, water use, food consumption, carbon sinks, human capital, patents, and information. 2. Production concentration: land urbanization, industrial concentration, and population urbanization. 3. Quality of life: quality-of-life index. 4. Institutional quality: institutional quality index. These data are used to examine the co-evolution of China's carbon emissions and the four dimensions of the IWB framework over the study period. They provide the empirical inputs for the illustrative application of IWB, including the analysis of long-term indicator trajectories and exploratory relative-contribution analysis. The dataset is intended to support the examination and further use of the annual indicators in research on environmental pressure, economic organization, and the human drivers of environmental change. The empirical application is illustrative and exploratory.

title: Compromised sinks? Re-evaluating carbon dioxide removal potentials by closing climate impact loops
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: National Determined Contributions (NDCs) increasingly rely on forest-based mitigation, yet climate-driven risks such as wildfires fundamentally threaten forest carbon sink reliability while shifting CO2 concentrations could strengthen carbo
content: National Determined Contributions (NDCs) increasingly rely on forest-based mitigation, yet climate-driven risks such as wildfires fundamentally threaten forest carbon sink reliability while shifting CO2 concentrations could strengthen carbon uptake by boosting plant photosynthesis. Therefore, integrated assessment models (IAMs) estimates must account for these global dynamics to provide realistic mitigation potentials from forests. We present an integrated modelling approach using IAM-FIRE alongside the Global Change Analysis Model (GCAM) to evaluate these feedbacks simultaneously across various SSP-RCP scenarios using ESM-driven climate emulations. Our methodology employs a dynamic scalar-based approach to adjust default GCAM forest vegetation carbon density (VCD) based on projected fire carbon emissions and net primary productivity (NPP) from IAM-FIRE. We run 28 scenarios (4 baselines and 24 impact-enabled scenarios) and report global and regional implications. Results indicate that CO2 fertilization is the dominant global driver, with NPP scalars showing a significant upward trend which could reach a +30% growth increase by 2100 in high-forcing scenarios like SSP5-7.6. In contrast, the fire scalar impact is an order of magnitude weaker but dampens the rate of VCD growth in high-emission pathways. At the global level, the scaled scenarios have minor impacts on atmospheric CO2 concentrations, typically varying by less than 0.3% from baseline. However, divergences emerge regarding net terrestrial uptake (NTU) and regional implications. In SSP1, while NPP scalars provide an early NTU gain, forest expansion is reduced by 2100 due to weakening fertilization effect. Conversely, fire scalars cause a reduction in forest expansion in fire-prone regions like Latin America. The model responds to increased disturbance through land re-allocation, reducing the vegetation carbon stocks in some regions. These findings underscore the importance of accounting for several climate impacts and their socioeconomic implications to ensure that land-based mitigation strategies are realistic and resilient to future climatic realities.

title: The hostile bone niche: physicochemical stress as a driver of tumor adaptation, resistance, and pain
source: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
summary: Bone metastases are commonly interpreted through the biochemical “vicious cycle” in which tumor cells, osteoclasts, osteoblast-lineage cells, stromal cells, and immune cells exchange cytokines and growth factors that amplify skeletal coloni
content: Bone metastases are commonly interpreted through the biochemical “vicious cycle” in which tumor cells, osteoclasts, osteoblast-lineage cells, stromal cells, and immune cells exchange cytokines and growth factors that amplify skeletal colonization. Although this model remains essential, it does not fully explain why bone lesions become highly adaptive, therapy-resistant, painful, and spatially heterogeneous. In this review, we propose that the metastatic bone niche should be viewed as a hostile physicochemical ecosystem in which hypoxia, extracellular acidosis, elevated interstitial pressure, impaired transport, and abnormal matrix mechanics function as active selective pressures. As skeletal lesions expand, vascular disruption and altered remodeling may generate additional stress beyond normal marrow gradients, although the extent of these changes varies by lesion and remains incompletely measured in patients. In parallel, glycolytic tumor metabolism and osteoclast-mediated proton secretion acidify the extracellular space, thereby enhancing invasion, immunosuppression, osteolysis, and nociceptor activation. Pathological remodeling further alters matrix stiffness, mineral architecture, and mechanotransduction, shaping tumor-cell plasticity, dormancy, reactivation, and resistance. These stressors do not act independently; rather, they form reciprocal feedback loops that remodel tumor, bone, vascular, immune, stromal, and neural compartments. We discussed how this integrated framework helps explain metastatic persistence, remodeling imbalance, treatment failure, and cancer-induced bone pain across breast, prostate, lung, and selected primary bone malignancies. Finally, we highlight key knowledge gaps, including the need for spatially resolved measurements of oxygen, pH, pressure, and matrix mechanics in human bone lesions, as well as more faithful experimental models that reproduce the multistressor biology of skeletal metastasis.

title: Atmospheric dissolved organic carbon deposition closes a missing link in the global terrestrial carbon cycle
summary: Atmospheric organic carbon deposition acts as both a critical terminal sink for air pollutants and a substantial nutrient subsidy to terrestrial ecosystems. A substantial fraction of deposited atmospheric organic carbon reaches terrestrial
content: Atmospheric organic carbon deposition acts as both a critical terminal sink for air pollutants and a substantial nutrient subsidy to terrestrial ecosystems. A substantial fraction of deposited atmospheric organic carbon reaches terrestrial ecosystems as dissolved organic carbon through precipitation and canopy throughfall. However, this atmospheric dissolved organic carbon subsidy remains missing from current global carbon budgets. Here, we reconstruct global dissolved organic carbon deposition (1980–2020) by integrating machine learning with stable and radiocarbon isotope constraints. We estimate a global deposition flux of 612 Tg C yr⁻¹, rivaling global land-to-ocean export. Crucially, canopy interception dominates ( ~ 52% of the global flux) yet is systematically underestimated by chemical transport models. We further demonstrate that deposition has decoupled from rising precursor emissions, governed instead by shifting meteorological regimes. This persistent atmospheric input partially offsets lateral hydrological carbon losses, highlighting the atmosphere as an active conveyor linking atmospheric processes and terrestrial carbon cycling. Canopy interception dominates atmospheric deposition of dissolved organic carbon, according to a process-explicit reconstruction of dissolved organic carbon utilizing carbon isotope data and machine learning.

title: Characterising week-long South American biomass burning plume transport and in-plume formic acid evolution using IASI measurements and chemical box model
summary: Abstract. Formic acid (HCOOH) is a prevalent organic acid that influences rain acidity and aerosol properties. However, models largely underestimate its atmospheric abundance, particularly in biomass burning plumes. Here, we use the Infrare
content: Abstract. Formic acid (HCOOH) is a prevalent organic acid that influences rain acidity and aerosol properties. However, models largely underestimate its atmospheric abundance, particularly in biomass burning plumes. Here, we use the Infrared Atmospheric Sounding Interferometer (IASI) to track HCOOH evolution in ageing South American biomass burning plumes during the exceptionally active 2024 fire season. By integrating IASI retrievals of total column HCOOH (TCHCOOH) and carbon monoxide (TCCO) with atmospheric trajectory modelling, we analyse HCOOH changes over the rarely studied week-long period. We particularly focus on the free troposphere, consistent with satellite sensitivity and reported transport altitudes. We find that HCOOH formation is most pronounced between the day of emission (Day 0) and the following day (Day 1), with the TCHCOOH:TCCO ratio increasing by ∼5.7 ± 1.0 % day−1. Between Day 2 and Day 6, the TCHCOOH:TCCO ratio decays at ∼4.8 ± 0.8 % day−1 as HCOOH is lost, then stabilises by Day 8. Box modelling based on the UK Chemistry and Aerosol model, initialised in the free troposphere (850 hPa) using in-plume observations, captures the increase in HCOOH:CO on the first day (4.4 % day−1) but slightly underestimates it. The model identifies hydroxymethyl-methyl-α-lactone (HMML, an isoprene oxidation product), ethene, and acetylene as key HCOOH precursors. HMML might be influenced by vegetation-derived emissions. After Day 1, the simulated HCOOH:CO ratio declines smoothly (2.7 % day−1), dominated by OH oxidation. This work demonstrates a novel approach that combines different observations and methods to investigate atmospheric chemistry in biomass burning plumes over week-long timescales.

title: Growth and Yield of Hot Pepper (Capsicum Annuum L.) Varieties in Response to the Integrated Application of Npsb Fertilizer and Municipal-waste Compost at Arba Minch, South Ethiopia
summary: Abstract Hot pepper (Capsicum annuum L.) productivity in Ethiopia remains constrained by suboptimal nutrient management and lack of variety-specific fertilizer recommendations. This study evaluated the effects of integrated application of N
content: Abstract Hot pepper (Capsicum annuum L.) productivity in Ethiopia remains constrained by suboptimal nutrient management and lack of variety-specific fertilizer recommendations. This study evaluated the effects of integrated application of NPSB fertilizer and municipal-waste compost on growth, yield, and yield-related traits of three hot pepper varieties (Melka Shote, Mareko Fana, and Halaba Local) under irrigated conditions at Arba Minch, South Ethiopia. A field experiment was conducted during the 2024 cropping season using a randomized complete block design with a 3 × 5 factorial arrangement and three replications. Treatments comprised five integrated nutrient management strategies: (i) 10 t ha⁻¹ compost (100% organic), (ii) 7.5 t ha⁻¹ compost + 50 kg ha⁻¹ NPSB (75:25), (iii) 5 t ha⁻¹ compost + 100 kg ha⁻¹ NPSB (50:50), (iv) 2.5 t ha⁻¹ compost + 150 kg ha⁻¹ NPSB (25:75), and (v) 200 kg ha⁻¹ NPSB (100% inorganic). Data were subjected under the 'agricolae' package in R software (version 4.4.2).to two-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) following normalization procedures to meet assumptions of homogeneity of variance and normality of residuals. Shapiro-Wilk tests confirmed normal distribution of residuals (W > 0.95, p > 0.05) for all measured parameters after appropriate transformations where necessary. Levene's test verified homogeneity of variances across treatment combinations (p > 0.05). Treatment means were separated using Duncan's Multiple Range Test (DMRT) at p ≤ 0.05 significance level. Results showed that variety × nutrient management interaction significantly influenced most growth, phenological, fruit, and yield parameters (p ≤ 0.05). The Mareko Fana variety under the balanced 50:50 treatment (5 t ha⁻¹ compost + 100 kg ha⁻¹ NPSB) produced the tallest plants (77.78 cm), maximum canopy diameter (62.42 cm), and highest number of primary branches (14.66). Melka Shote under the 25:75 treatment (2.5 t ha⁻¹ compost + 150 kg ha⁻¹ NPSB) achieved the highest number of fruits per plant (119.1), while Mareko Fana with sole NPSB (200 kg ha⁻¹) produced the longest fruits (10.73 cm). For yield, Mareko Fana with sole compost (10 t ha⁻¹) recorded the highest total fresh yield (11.41 t ha⁻¹), whereas the 75:25 treatment (7.5 t ha⁻¹ compost + 50 kg ha⁻¹ NPSB) optimized marketable dry yield (3.46 t ha⁻¹) and total dry yield (4.04 t ha⁻¹) in the same variety. Halaba Local consistently performed poorly across all treatments, confirming its unsuitability for intensive integrated nutrient management. Soil chemical analysis revealed improvements in organic carbon, available phosphorus, and cation exchange capacity under treatments with higher compost proportions, particularly the 75:25 and 100% compost treatments. The integrated application of NPSB fertilizer and municipal-waste compost significantly enhanced hot pepper productivity with highly variety-specific responses. The balanced 50:50 treatment is recommended for optimizing vegetative growth and fruit quality

title: Eco-Hydrogeology and Engineering for the Conservation of Mediterranean Peatlands in Karst: An Interdisciplinary Case Study
summary: Peatlands in mid-latitudes are critical and rare ecosystems, acting as important carbon sinks and hydrological regulators. This study presents an interdisciplinary investigation (geological, hydrogeological and palaeoecological) of the Cala
content: Peatlands in mid-latitudes are critical and rare ecosystems, acting as important carbon sinks and hydrological regulators. This study presents an interdisciplinary investigation (geological, hydrogeological and palaeoecological) of the Calatañazor peat bog (Soria, Spain). Through geological mapping, geophysical prospecting, soundings and C14 dating, the evolution of the karst lagoon system is reconstructed. The results reveal a genesis linked to the closure of the valley by a barrier of calcareous tuffs during the Upper Pleistocene, and the sedimentation of lacustrine organic clays during the last glaciation, followed by a phase of active peat formation in the early Holocene (7590–5800 BP). Hydrochemical analysis and piezometric monitoring demonstrate that the peat bog functions as a regional discharge point for the Utrillas Facies aquifer, maintaining critical water table levels (0–1 m) and exerting a self-purifying effect (denitrification). Following decades of degradation caused by agricultural drainage, the research provides a scientific basis for its restoration through an analysis of its structure and hydrological functioning. It concludes that restoring the original water body is technically and hydrologically feasible, as the system exhibits an outflow character downstream, ensuring the conservation of the ecosystem without compromising local water resources. The engineering intervention, carried out between 2025 and 2026, consisted of creating a shallow lagoon and plugging strategic drains. The project demonstrates that the integration of palaeoecology and active management is key to the resilience of Mediterranean wetlands in the face of climate change.

title: PkM KTH Wana Mertha melalui Manajemen Ekowisata Mangrove Berbasis Blue Carbon di Desa Budeng
summary: Ekowisata mangrove merupakan instrumen vital bagi keberhasilan konservasi karbon biru dan pemberdayaan ekonomi pesisir. Namun, kelompok berbasis masyarakat sering menghadapi tantangan terkait manajemen pariwisata konvensional, pemantauan ka
content: Ekowisata mangrove merupakan instrumen vital bagi keberhasilan konservasi karbon biru dan pemberdayaan ekonomi pesisir. Namun, kelompok berbasis masyarakat sering menghadapi tantangan terkait manajemen pariwisata konvensional, pemantauan karbon yang belum terstandarisasi, serta integrasi teknologi yang terbatas. Program pengabdian masyarakat ini bertujuan memberdayakan Kelompok Tani Hutan (KTH) Wana Mertha di Desa Budeng, Kabupaten Jembrana, melalui pengembangan ekowisata mangrove berbasis karbon biru. Program ini menerapkan pendekatan Participatory Action Research (PAR) melalui lima tahapan sistematis: perencanaan, persiapan, implementasi solusi multidisiplin, pemantauan dan evaluasi, serta pengelolaan keberlanjutan. Intervensi multidisiplin tersebut mencakup tiga pilar utama: manajemen ekowisata, restorasi mangrove, dan penerapan teknologi informasi. Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan peningkatan signifikan di seluruh sektor (p < 0,001). Pengetahuan mitra dalam manajemen ekowisata meningkat dari 49,05% menjadi 89,00%, disertai dengan pembentukan paket wisata edukasi yang terstruktur serta diversifikasi empat produk hasil hutan bukan kayu (HHBK) dengan branding modern/kekinian. Pada pilar restorasi, tingkat pemahaman meningkat dari 72,00% menjadi 93,50%, didukung oleh penanaman berbasis spasial, modul pemantauan karbon terstandarisasi, dan papan informasi edukatif luar ruang. Selain itu, literasi digital dan penerapan TI meningkat dari 58,50% menjadi 92,50% melalui adopsi sistem pemantauan "Mangrove Tag" berbasis RFID/NFC dan platform pendaftaran pengunjung digital. Secara keseluruhan, inisiatif program PKM ini berhasil mentransformasi mitra menjadi kelompok wirausaha hijau yang mandiri.

title: Who benefits from watershed ecological compensation: Understanding the impact on farm households in vulnerable areas from a lifecycle perspective
summary: Watersheds, as complex socio-ecological systems, are among the most sensitive and vulnerable regions to human-environment interactions. While the ecological benefits of the watershed ecological compensation (WEC) policy have been widely rec
content: Watersheds, as complex socio-ecological systems, are among the most sensitive and vulnerable regions to human-environment interactions. While the ecological benefits of the watershed ecological compensation (WEC) policy have been widely recognized, limited attention has been paid to how farm households at different family life cycle (FLC) stages respond heterogeneously to WEC. Given the increasing trend of unequal livelihood vulnerability within watersheds, an urgent need exists for further exploration of how WEC policies impact the livelihood of vulnerable farm households. Drawing on survey data from 869 farm households, this study investigates the pathways through which WEC affects the sustainability of household livelihoods. The results show that WEC significantly enhances households’ livelihood capital, while labor allocation serves as an important mediating variable linking livelihood capital to household income. Further analysis reveals that the pathway “WEC→livelihood capital→labor allocation→household income” plays a pivotal role in promoting livelihood transitions. Furthermore, the FLC plays a moderating role in the relationship between WEC and households’ livelihood capital, with particularly pronounced effects along the pathway of labor resource reallocation. These findings reveal the behavioral mechanisms underlying farm households’ responses to WEC policies and offer empirical insights for advancing synergies between ecological conservation and sustainable rural livelihoods in transboundary watersheds.

title: Welding Metallurgy of Super Duplex Stainless Steel UNS S32750: A State-of-the-Art Review of GMAW Process Parameters, Microstructure–Property Relationships and Corrosion Performance
summary: Abstract Super duplex stainless steel UNS S32750 (SAF 2507) combines a pitting resistance equivalent number above 40 with high strength, but its properties depend on a ferrite–austenite balance that welding readily disturbs. Gas metal arc w
content: Abstract Super duplex stainless steel UNS S32750 (SAF 2507) combines a pitting resistance equivalent number above 40 with high strength, but its properties depend on a ferrite–austenite balance that welding readily disturbs. Gas metal arc welding (GMAW) is productive, yet GMAW-specific evidence for this alloy remains limited. A structured narrative review (emphasis 2018–2026) synthesised GMAW-specific findings, drew comparative mechanisms from gas tungsten arc, submerged arc and beam welding, and examined Gaussian process regression (GPR) for parameter optimisation. Data were converted to net heat input and grouped by corrosion test method. Weld-metal ferrite is governed by cooling time through 1200–800°C, nitrogen retention and ER2594 nickel over-alloying, whereas Cr₂N, secondary austenite and σ-phase arise mainly from multipass reheating and interpass temperature. Pulsed GMAW in Ar–He shielding with nitrogen backing met NORSOK M-601 requirements (30–70% ferrite, ≥ 27 J at − 46°C) in 33 mm plate at 1.2–1.6 kJ mm⁻¹ arc energy. Oxidising shielding additions introduce oxide inclusions that degrade pitting resistance. Electrochemical critical pitting temperatures fall from 58–92°C in base metal to 45–71°C in arc welds and rise linearly with austenite fraction. GPR-based Bayesian optimisation located welding optima within 12–25 experiments with quantified uncertainty, but has not yet been applied to super duplex GMAW. Fixed heat-input windows are incomplete because thickness, pass count and gas chemistry shift outcomes; above-guideline parameters are qualified only for heavy sections. Thermal-history-based qualification, nitrogen management, harmonised corrosion testing and constrained GPR optimisation of ferrite, toughness and pitting resistance are priorities.

title: Appraising Pilot-Scale Carbon Capture and Storage Projects: Making Informed Decisions for Realistic Modeling of Dynamic CO2 Storage Capacity
summary: Carbon capture and storage (CCS) has emerged as a critical pillar of climate mitigation efforts, yet its scalable deployment is constrained by capital-intensive investments, regulatory fragmentation, and an absence of standardized site eval
content: Carbon capture and storage (CCS) has emerged as a critical pillar of climate mitigation efforts, yet its scalable deployment is constrained by capital-intensive investments, regulatory fragmentation, and an absence of standardized site evaluation frameworks. This discussion paper advances a novel, decision-oriented methodology for pilot-scale CCS project appraisal, emphasizing the need to distinguish between commercialization and optimization pathways. By developing a systematic framework grounded in the capacity–injectivity–containment triad, and contextualized with metrics derived from analogous subsurface industries, the paper proposes a structured and defensible basis for model selection, site qualification, and early-phase feasibility assessment. The framework is tailored to support operators with limited financial resources by prioritizing small-scale, locally deployable projects and reducing epistemic uncertainty through explicit, objective-based parameterization. Through integrating reservoir characterization, performance metrics, and decision logic, this approach facilitates transparent project evaluation and risk management, ultimately promoting more confident, cost-effective CCS deployment while preserving environmental security and public trust.

title: Study of the ionization in air-breathing electric rockets with VLEO atmospheric propellants and typical laboratory mixtures
summary: Abstract This work investigates the ionization of atmospheric propellant in air-breathing electric propulsion (ABEP) systems for satellites operating in Very-Low Earth Orbit (VLEO). Plasma formation inside the ionization chamber of an air-b
content: Abstract This work investigates the ionization of atmospheric propellant in air-breathing electric propulsion (ABEP) systems for satellites operating in Very-Low Earth Orbit (VLEO). Plasma formation inside the ionization chamber of an air-breathing thruster is studied to gain insights on physical phenomena involved in ABEP technology. A time-dependent zero-dimensional model of the plasma chamber is formulated, that accounts for a comprehensive set of reactions for nitrogen, oxygen and argon. This model is implemented within a numerical framework to simulate plasma ignition at different operating parameters defined to describe geometry, intake behaviour, input power, magnetic field interactions, acceleration mechanism, and VLEO environmental conditions. The simulation results include the evolution in time of plasma density, composition and reaction rates during the ignition transient until stationary conditions. The study identifies the plasma ignition envelope by analysing the dependencies of plasma properties on mass flow rate, electron temperature, and ion-to-neutral residence times' ratio. The composition and density of the plasma are characterized across different regimes, revealing a transition between molecular and atomic ions dominance. NO+ ion is observed as an important constituent for low-plasma-density regimes, where molecular ions dominate. Comparison between results on different mixtures are performed and approximation laws to facilitate experimental validation are derived, which can help improving the accuracy of plasma diagnostic measurements for experimental conditions relevant to ABEP testing. Furthermore, it is shown that the use of argon as substitute of atomic oxygen in low-density air-like mixture plasma does not provide representative results.

title: Is Anthropogenic Climate Change Reversible? Results from CDRMIP on transient Earth system response under atmospheric CO 2 increase and decrease
summary: Abstract. To limit global warming at well-below 2°C above pre-industrial levels, large and sustained CO2 emission reductions are needed and it may be possible to use alongside carbon dioxide removal (CDR) methods to return atmospheric CO2 c
content: Abstract. To limit global warming at well-below 2°C above pre-industrial levels, large and sustained CO2 emission reductions are needed and it may be possible to use alongside carbon dioxide removal (CDR) methods to return atmospheric CO2 concentrations to lower levels, with the assumption that lower CO2 will rapidly lead to lower temperatures and reverse or limit other climate change impacts. Despite such assumption, a comprehensive understanding of the reversibility of the Earth system components is a persistent knowledge gap, which hinders our ability to assess future outcomes of decreasing anthropogenic forcing. Here we evaluate the reversibility of climate change through a multi-model analysis of how the Earth system and climate respond in the CMIP6 Carbon Dioxide Removal Model Intercomparison Project (CDRMIP) cdr-reversibility experiment. cdr-reversibility is an idealized CO2 concentration peak and decline experiment where atmospheric CO2 increases at 1% yr-1 from a pre-industrial level until 4 times its initial value, then decreases at 1% yr-1 until pre-industrial levels are again reached, at which point CO2 is held constant. A few modelled quantities reverse or overshoot initial levels, on the same timescale as the changes in CO2 forcing, such as the land and ocean net primary productivity or the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation – at least when viewed at the global annual mean level. However, when responding to decreasing CO2 concentration many properties exhibit time lags and hysteresis, e.g. changes in ocean and land carbon stocks or sea level. While some variables respond to mainly one specific driver, most show a hysteresis behaviour relative to all the considered driving forcers, namely surface air temperature, atmospheric CO2 or cumulative emissions. Due to such, the majority of the considered environmental variables would take long, many times longer than a human lifetime, to return to their unperturbed values (if this ever occurs). Therefore, exceeding and then reversing a climate target would have a clear legacy in the climate system even if CO2 concentrations return to pre-industrial levels.
