summary: Highlights from the Science family of journals
content: Highlights from the Science family of journals

title: Photocatalytic Coproduction of H 2 and H 2 O 2 : Mechanistic Insights, Material Design, and Challenges in the Two‐Electron Water Oxidation Reaction
summary: Photocatalytic coproduction of hydrogen (H 2 ) and hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) from pure water via the two‐electron water oxidation reaction (2e − ‐WOR) represents a novel approach toward sustainable solar‐to‐chemical energy conversion. Th
content: Photocatalytic coproduction of hydrogen (H 2 ) and hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) from pure water via the two‐electron water oxidation reaction (2e − ‐WOR) represents a novel approach toward sustainable solar‐to‐chemical energy conversion. This enables the parallel generation of two high‐added‐value products, offering a promising alternative to conventional systems. This review summarizes the latest advancements obtained using this approach and heterogeneous semiconductor photocatalysts. After introducing the fundamentals of photocatalysis, the thermodynamics, kinetics and mechanisms of water reduction and oxidation are discussed, accounting for the distinct competing pathways. Energetics and selectivity of H 2 O 2 production are assessed using free‐energy descriptors and volcano plot analysis. Stability of H 2 O 2 under photocatalytic conditions is examined, considering thermal, photochemical, and surface‐mediated decomposition processes. Material design strategies to promote photocatalytic H 2 /H 2 O 2 coproduction are critically analyzed and discussed. These include doping, defect engineering, morphology control, cocatalyst integration, and heterojunction formation. The aim of this review is to provide general guidelines for designing new efficient nanomaterials for photocatalytic H 2 /H 2 O 2 coproduction, minimizing H 2 O 2 degradation. Finally, it offers a critical assessment of reported approaches, providing insights into the current level of progress in this field: the experimental evidence underlying mechanism assignment is examined and organized into a hierarchy, against which the surveyed systems are classified.

title: Effects of farmyard manure and zinc application on yield and quality of kharif fodder sorghum
summary: A field study was conducted during the kharif season of 2024 at the Main Forage Research Station, Anand Agricultural University, Anand, Gujarat, to assess the effects of farmyard manure (FYM) and zinc application on the yield and quality of
content: A field study was conducted during the kharif season of 2024 at the Main Forage Research Station, Anand Agricultural University, Anand, Gujarat, to assess the effects of farmyard manure (FYM) and zinc application on the yield and quality of kharif fodder sorghum. The experiment comprised twelve treatment combinations involving two FYM levels (0 and 10 t/ha) and six zinc treatments: Z1 (0 kg Zn/ha), Z2 (12.5 kg Zn/ha), Z3 (25 kg Zn/ha), Z4 (12.5 kg Zn/ha followed by zinc-solubilising bacteria (ZnSB) soil application), Z5 (12.5 kg Zn/ha followed by 0.05 % Zn foliar application) and Z6 (12.5 kg Zn/ha followed by ZnSB soil application and 0.05 % Zn foliar application). The experiment was conducted in a factorial randomised block design (FRBD) with three replications. Application of 10 t FYM/ha significantly increased green fodder yield (421.50 q/ha), dry matter yield (128.93 q/ha), crude protein yield (11.94 q/ha), plant zinc content (29.91 mg/kg) and zinc uptake (41.07 g/ha), along with post-harvest available soil zinc (2.96 mg/kg) and ZnSB count, compared with the control. Among zinc treatments, Z6 produced higher green fodder yield (376.33 q/ha), dry matter yield (123.36 q/ha), crude protein yield (11.59 q/ha) and zinc content (29.64 mg/kg), while Z5 and Z6 recorded higher post-harvest available zinc (2.75 and 2.84 mg/kg respectively) and zinc uptake (41.99 g/ha) respectively. The FYM × zinc interaction was significant. F2Z5 produced higher dry matter (180.73 q/ha) and crude protein yield (18.61 q/ha), whereas F2Z6 recorded higher zinc uptake (64.03 g/ha) and post-harvest available zinc (3.40 mg/kg).

title: When trees become forests: Why definitions matter for conservation in India
summary: Forests are vital to the planet, offering a range of ecological, economic, and social benefits. However, in the Anthropocene era, forests are degraded by human activities and climate change, making the conservation and management of existin
content: Forests are vital to the planet, offering a range of ecological, economic, and social benefits. However, in the Anthropocene era, forests are degraded by human activities and climate change, making the conservation and management of existing forest resources necessary. A precise and consistent definition of what constitutes a forest is fundamental for effective global forest conservation and management. Forest definitions vary significantly across institutions, countries, and scientific disciplines. Inconsistent forest definitions lead to unreliable data, distorted funding allocations, and misinformed policy decisions. India's official reports claim substantial gains in forest cover, yet multiple independent assessments and even government data reveal significant losses of natural forests, raising serious concerns about the credibility and transparency of national forest statistics. These discrepancies largely arise from India's forest definition, which counts plantations and tree cover outside forested areas as forests while failing to distinguish them from natural forests, thereby masking biodiversity loss and ecological degradation. The Government and policymakers are producing forest assessments that may be technically correct, but are largely misleading. Additionally, the misclassification of Open Natural Ecosystems (ONEs), such as grasslands, as degraded forests has driven inappropriate afforestation initiatives with adverse ecological and economic consequences. There is an urgent need to update forest definitions so that forests and deforestation are measured consistently and precisely.

title: Vegetation complexity as a multi-dimensional indicator of soil organic carbon storage, but not nitrogen storage, in dryland ecosystems
summary: Soil organic carbon (SOC) and soil total nitrogen (STN) are essential for primary productivity and nutrient cycling in terrestrial ecosystems. Although their drivers have been extensively studied, the role of vegetation complexity in regula
content: Soil organic carbon (SOC) and soil total nitrogen (STN) are essential for primary productivity and nutrient cycling in terrestrial ecosystems. Although their drivers have been extensively studied, the role of vegetation complexity in regulating SOC and STN dynamics, along with the ecological processes involved, remains insufficiently understood. Using a multidimensional vegetation complexity index (VCI) and structural equation modeling, this study determines how vegetation complexity influences SOC and STN stocks and their ratio (SCN) in the 0–60 cm soil profile of dryland ecosystems in West Africa. We evaluated three non-mutually exclusive mediation pathways through which vegetation complexity may operate: (i) aboveground biomass (AGB; “vegetation quantity”), (ii) tree functional and phylogenetic diversity (“vegetation quality”), and (iii) their combination. We tested whether these pathways were sustained by plant–soil feedback mechanisms, while accounting for environmental filtering and human disturbance. SOC stock and SCN increased significantly with VCI, but STN stock did not. These VCI effects were statistically supported but modest and were mediated by AGB rather than by diversity attributes. Complementarily, SOC stock and SCN exhibited positive feedback on VCI via AGB, although these reciprocal effects changed with soil depth. Aridity and human disturbance were negatively associated with VCI, SOC and STN stocks, and SCN. Our findings highlight VCI as a multidimensional indirect predictor of SOC and SCN, but not STN, operating through the “vegetation quantity” pathway. These results underscore the importance of adopting VCI as a context-specific benchmark for ecosystem management in drylands, as promoting vegetation complexity can enhance carbon sink capacity and soil health.

title: Growing-season cold spells and photoperiod are linked to radial growth cessation in the alpine treeline shrub Alnus alnobetula
summary: Green alder (Alnus alnobetula) is a tall shrub that dominates the alpine treeline ecotone in the Central European Alps, yet its radial growth (RG) response to growing-season cold spells is unclear. We used dendrometers to quantify effects o
content: Green alder (Alnus alnobetula) is a tall shrub that dominates the alpine treeline ecotone in the Central European Alps, yet its radial growth (RG) response to growing-season cold spells is unclear. We used dendrometers to quantify effects of cold spells on RG of mature shoots at the treeline (2,150 m a.s.l.) in a year with several such events, and conducted complementary climate-chamber experiments on juvenile shoots. We hypothesized that abrupt temperature drops to near 0°C or slight freezing would prematurely halt RG (H1), and that, due to photoperiodic constraints, late-season cold spells would be more effective in terminating RG (H2). At the treeline, an early-season event (DOY 207) caused only a temporary halt in RG, contradicting H1. A mid-season event (DOY 219) halted RG in two thirds of mature shoots, and the remainder ceased after a late-season event (DOY 241), supporting H2. These divergent RG responses among individuals likely reflect differences in physiological status, such as carbohydrate reserves. In climate-chambers, an early-season experimental frost (−2.2°C) reduced but did not halt RG in juvenile shoots, whereas a later-season cold spell halted RG. Thus, in A. alnobetula, RG resilience to cold spells is linked to photoperiod and possibly developmental stage.

title: Management-sensitive enzymatic indicators of carbon and nutrient cycling in vegetable soils: implications for climate-resilient production systems
summary: Climate-resilient cropping systems require management practices that sustain soil biological functioning while supporting efficient carbon (C), nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) cycling. Soil extracellular enzymes are sensitive indicators of
content: Climate-resilient cropping systems require management practices that sustain soil biological functioning while supporting efficient carbon (C), nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) cycling. Soil extracellular enzymes are sensitive indicators of these processes, yet their responses to management remain poorly documented in vegetable production systems. This study evaluated six hydrolytic enzymes involved in C, N and P cycling together with fluorescein diacetate (FDA) hydrolysis across 50 commercial vegetable farms in Quebec, Canada (29 organic and 21 conventional), sampled at 0–10, 10–20 and 30–50 cm. Enzymatic stoichiometric ratios and an exploratory Soil Health Practice Index (SHPI) were also used to assess relationships between management practices and soil biological functioning. Three response patterns emerged. First, β-glucosidase (BG), cellobiosidase (CB) and xylosidase (XYL) showed limited sensitivity to management. Second, α-Glucosidase (AG) activity was higher in conventionally managed soils, with organic-to-conventional response ratios ranging from 0.51 to 0.67 across the soil profile. Third, N -acetyl-β-glucosaminidase (NAG) activity was 65% and 64% higher under organic than conventional management at 0–10 and 10–20 cm, respectively, whereas phosphatase (PHOS) activity was 57–69% higher across all three soil depths. FDA hydrolysis was 2.70- and 3.14-fold higher under organic than conventional management at 0–10 and 10–20 cm, respectively, with no significant difference at 30–50 cm. BG:NAG and BG:PHOS ratios were lower under organic management, indicating contrasting relative enzymatic investment in nutrient acquisition. Across farms, higher SHPI scores were positively associated with NAG ( r = 0.26 and 0.24 at 0–10 and 10–20 cm), PHOS ( r = 0.20 and 0.23) and FDA ( r = 0.32 at both depths), and negatively associated with AG ( r = −0.25 and −0.24), indicating that enzymatic responses also tracked a gradient of conservation-oriented practices. Among the indicators measured, AG, NAG, PHOS, FDA, BG:NAG and BG:PHOS were the most management-responsive. Overall, these results identify enzymatic indicators associated with management-related differences in soil biological functioning and highlight their potential for monitoring progress toward more climate-resilient vegetable production systems.

title: Daily Carbon Exchange in a Tropical Dry Evergreen Forest: Insights from Eddy Covariance and Multi-Sensor Remote Sensing
summary: Tropical dry evergreen forests retain a closed canopy during long dry seasons, yet their carbon exchange remains poorly measured. We analyzed 20 months (April 2024–December 2025) of eddy-covariance observations at Sakaerat, Thailand, includ
content: Tropical dry evergreen forests retain a closed canopy during long dry seasons, yet their carbon exchange remains poorly measured. We analyzed 20 months (April 2024–December 2025) of eddy-covariance observations at Sakaerat, Thailand, including a single-point CO2 storage term, gap filling, and flux partitioning. We assessed whether tower soil measurements and optical, thermal, and Sentinel-1 radar predictors improved daily net ecosystem exchange (NEE), gross primary productivity (GPP), and ecosystem respiration (Reco) estimates beyond tower meteorology. Estimated monthly NEE was negative throughout the record, including the dry season. Cumulative NEE over 1 January–17 December 2025 was −1043 g C m−2 (GPP 2620; Reco 1635 g C m−2). Uptake was stronger in the wetter, cooler second wet season, consistent with directly measured daytime fluxes. In the later held-out period, soil water content and temperature improved NEE and GPP estimates, while cross-calibrated Sentinel-1 backscatter improved GPP estimates. Optical and thermal products did not improve NEE and degraded GPP. These gains mainly tracked the interannual shift in flux level rather than daily variation. Better constraints on nighttime respiration are needed to confirm the magnitude of the carbon sink.

title: urban forest aboveground biomass datasets integrating GEDI and multi-source data (2020)
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Accurately quantifying urban forest carbon sinks is crucial for achieving the "dual carbon" strategic goals. The current multi-source remote sensing collaborative estimation of forest biomass still faces problems such as insufficient evalua
content: Accurately quantifying urban forest carbon sinks is crucial for achieving the "dual carbon" strategic goals. The current multi-source remote sensing collaborative estimation of forest biomass still faces problems such as insufficient evaluation of cross scale transfer effects of heterogeneous data, weak interpretability of machine learning features, and weak application of residual correction. By integrating GEDI LiDAR data with multi-source optical/radar remote sensing information, a set of Chinese urban forest aboveground biomass (AGB) estimation and multi-scale mapping products is constructed. This product integrates multiple sources of data such as GEDI L4A/L4B/Gridded biomass products, Landsat C2L2, MODIS09A1, PALSAR-2, SRTM DEM, etc. It combines Boruta to screen feature variables and introduces a residual correction model to generate urban forest aboveground biomass products, providing a reliable cross scale solution for accurate monitoring of urban carbon sinks. The processing flow is as follows: 1) Preprocessing and feature integration of multi-source data. Perform unified quality screening, resampling, and geographic registration on multi-source data to construct a feature set that includes vegetation indices, terrain factors, and spatial locations. 2) Estimation modeling of spot scale height. Using the AutoGluon ensemble learning framework, a vegetation canopy height estimation model is constructed by integrating multi-source features, and the feature combination is optimized through ablation experiments. 3) Regional scale mapping and residual correction. Based on the optimal model for spatial extrapolation, generate a continuous vegetation canopy height distribution map of urban areas; Further establish a residual learning model to correct system errors. 4) Multi resolution product generation and output. Based on the corrected model, pixel by pixel deduction is performed to output multi-scale vegetation canopy height products ranging from 30m to 1km for seven typical cities.

title: Deep coal fluidized loop-shredded mining technology and the in-situ mining mechanical behavior of coal
source: International Journal of Coal Science & Technology
summary: Abstract Deep coal fluidized mining is a disruptive technology for overcoming the depth limits of coal extraction. To achieve the industrial goal of deep coal fluidized mining—“no coal on the surface, no personnel underground”—traditional r
content: Abstract Deep coal fluidized mining is a disruptive technology for overcoming the depth limits of coal extraction. To achieve the industrial goal of deep coal fluidized mining—“no coal on the surface, no personnel underground”—traditional roadway layouts, mining methods, and hoisting‑transportation systems must be transformed. Accordingly, this study proposes an innovative deep coal fluidized loop-shredded mining (FLSM) concept, which resembles the hand‑tearing bread method. Using the central shaft of the coal seam block as the geometric center, intelligent mining equipment extracts coal sequentially from the outer ring toward the inner ring of the mining area. The proposed FLSM method integrates deep in-situ shield mining, crushing and separation, in-situ liquefaction, electrification, gasification, and in-situ negative-carbon backfilling. Considering the spatial geometric characteristics and structural features of the overlying strata under FLSM, a T-shaped mechanical model was established. An analytical solution for coal-rock stress, accounting for depth effects and the disturbance characteristics of the FLSM, was developed to support in-situ environmental simulation and testing. Based on the in-situ geo-stress environment, a numerical analysis model was constructed to analyze the spatiotemporal evolution of coal samples plastic zones and mining-induced stress under different coal pillar widths. As loop-shredded mining advances from the outer to the inner ring, vertical stress undergoes dynamic transfer, and the central coal pillar becomes a zone of high stress concentration. Laboratory measurements confirmed that peak deviatoric stress under FLSM is reduced by 38.6%, 30.6%, and 22.6%, respectively, compared with non-pillar mining, top coal caving mining, and protective seam mining.

title: Climate-driven functional and structural decoupling in urban agglomeration forest networks for ecosystem adaptive management
summary: Climate change reshapes forest ecosystems from individual trees to regional landscapes, yet adaptive forest management often overlooks mismatches between ecological function and spatial connectivity. We construct a network framework integra
content: Climate change reshapes forest ecosystems from individual trees to regional landscapes, yet adaptive forest management often overlooks mismatches between ecological function and spatial connectivity. We construct a network framework integrating functional diversity and landscape structure to simulate forest dynamics across the Pearl River Delta urban agglomeration from 2010 to 2100 under three climate pathways. The results show that the moderate-emission scenario (SSP245) can enhance functional performance predominantly within natural forests, whereas the high-emission scenario (SSP585) may yield short-term functional benefits for peri‑urban forests that cannot translate into improved landscape connectivity. While the regional forest network appears broadly stable, local forest patches exhibit highly divergent trajectories: some improve, others degrade, and many display uncoordinated shifts between function and structure. We categorize subnets into four climate response types, each requiring distinct management priorities. This transferable diagnostic framework pinpoints climate-vulnerable forest areas and enables planners to move beyond connectivity-centric strategies toward targeted, function-oriented climate adaptation. Climate change drives divergent and often mismatched shifts in forest function and connectivity across the Pearl River Delta, requiring response-specific management, based on network simulations integrating functional diversity and landscape structure under three climate pathways from 2010 to 2100.

title: Sea level rise and subsidence compound flood risks on the century-old Treasure Island
summary: Treasure Island, a century-old artificial landmass in San Francisco Bay, exemplifies the long-term climate vulnerabilities of reclaimed coastal lands under accelerating sea-level rise. Here we show, using historical records, multi-decadal s
content: Treasure Island, a century-old artificial landmass in San Francisco Bay, exemplifies the long-term climate vulnerabilities of reclaimed coastal lands under accelerating sea-level rise. Here we show, using historical records, multi-decadal satellite interferometric synthetic aperture radar, three-dimensional geomechanical modeling, and deep learning projections, that the island is undergoing persistent subsidence (5–11 mm yr−1) and lateral sliding (up to 6 mm yr−1) at its northwest corner. These patterns reflect the complex deformation within a compressible and heterogeneous foundation. Our analysis of land-water interactions projects that sea-level rise is likely to surpass subsidence as the dominant contributor to flood exposure by 2030, with high-emission scenarios indicating significant inland inundation risk by 2050. These findings reveal acute sustainability challenges for Treasure Island’s planned redevelopment and highlight the hidden risks inherent in aging artificial coastlines. While site-specific, this century-scale diagnostics provide a transferable framework for assessing relative sea-level rise and guiding adaptation on reclaimed coasts with similar geotechnical and climatic conditions. Treasure Island is subsiding by 5–11 millimeters per year and sliding by up to 6 millimeters per year, sea-level rise is projected to become the main driver of flood risk by 2030, with substantial inland inundation risk by 2050, according to satellite data, geomechanical modeling, and deep learning.

title: Ecotones modulate aboveground biomass patterns along an elevational gradient in a subtropical mountain
summary: Background and Aims: Ecological ecotones are critical transitional units characterized by high structural and functional heterogeneity within mountain forest ecosystems. Despite their known importance, the independent influence of ecotones
content: Background and Aims: Ecological ecotones are critical transitional units characterized by high structural and functional heterogeneity within mountain forest ecosystems. Despite their known importance, the independent influence of ecotones on spatial patterns of ecosystem functions—and their underlying driving mechanisms—across continuous elevational gradients remain poorly quantified. Methods: Here, we established continuous forest plots along a 900–1600 m elevational gradient on the southern slope of Daiyun Mountain, Southeast China. Integrating community surveys with edaphic, climatic, and topographic constraints, we estimated plant aboveground biomass (AGB) and employed Random Forest (RF) alongside Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) to disentangle the modulating effects of ecotones on AGB distribution and its structural driving pathways. Key Results: Our results indicated an overarching unimodal distribution of AGB along the elevational gradient, disrupted by a distinct biomass trough specifically located at the 1300 m ecotone. Crucially, the exclusion of this ecotone plot restored a smooth unimodal AGB–elevation trajectory, confirming the ecotone’s role in driving localized functional anomalies. Variable importance analyses demonstrated that while edaphic and climatic factors dominated AGB variation across the entire gradient, the explanatory power of topography surged significantly only when the ecotone was excluded. Furthermore, SEM revealed a fundamental shift in driving pathways within the ecotone: the direct effects of soil and climate on AGB were substantially buffered, shifting instead toward indirect modulation mediated by species diversity. In contrast, in non-ecotone plots, the driving pathways of various factors were more stable and clearly directed. Conclusions: Ecotones function as more than mere spatial transition zones; they are critical functional units that significantly modulate forest functions and their underlying driving mechanisms.

title: Thermal modeling of a rotary heat pump: effects of key parameters on performance
source: International Journal of Air-Conditioning and Refrigeration
summary: Abstract This study presents a transient thermal analysis of a rotary electrocaloric (EC) heat pump in which fluids circulate through channels bounded by electrocaloric material. The transient conjugate heat transfer problem is solved using
content: Abstract This study presents a transient thermal analysis of a rotary electrocaloric (EC) heat pump in which fluids circulate through channels bounded by electrocaloric material. The transient conjugate heat transfer problem is solved using both a finite-element model and a reduced-order analytical model. The reduced-order model predicts the cooling capacity with an average deviation of 8.08% from the finite-element solution while requiring significantly lower computational effort. Under the baseline operating conditions, the heat pump delivers a cooling capacity of 23.33 W, a coefficient of performance (COP) that includes electrical and mechanical power requirements of 22.827 and a relative Carnot efficiency of 7.79%. The analysis reveals the existence of a reverse heat pumping zone at the beginning of each heating and cooling stage, caused by the displacement of fluid transported from the previous stage, which reduces the net cooling capacity. Parametric calculations show that this reverse heat pumping effect becomes more pronounced at lower rotational speeds, lower fluid velocities, longer channel lengths, and larger temperature differences between the hot and cold reservoirs, ultimately limiting the operating range of the device. A conceptual tandem configuration employing alternating fluid inlets and inter-stage recirculation is proposed as a potential approach for increasing the achievable temperature span of a four-stage rotary electrocaloric heat pump to $$4.8349^{\circ}\textrm{C}$$ and the relative Carnot efficiency to 38.16%.

title: Carbon cycle feedback dependence on imposed land-use forcing
summary: Abstract Earth System Models used to quantify climate-carbon cycle feedbacks and remaining carbon budgets are initialised from pre-industrial land-use conditions, yet the real world has experienced centuries of land-use change. Whether the
content: Abstract Earth System Models used to quantify climate-carbon cycle feedbacks and remaining carbon budgets are initialised from pre-industrial land-use conditions, yet the real world has experienced centuries of land-use change. Whether the resulting land-surface state affects the diagnosed feedback parameters-concentration-carbon (β land ) and climate-carbon (γ land )-and the Transient Climate Response to cumulative Emissions (TCRE) remains poorly explored.Here we quantify how different initial land-use states-no land-use, pre-industrial, and present-day-affect carbon cycle feedback parameters in standard 1% CO 2 coupled and biogeochemically coupled simulations using HadCM3LC-Bris. Present-day land use reduces β land by 16% and makes γ land 8% more negative relative to no land-use, but the biophysical cooling from deforestation depresses the climate sensitivity parameter α, producing a net 8% reduction in TCRE at 2×CO 2 . This implies a systematic positive bias of ∼8% in TCRE diagnosed from pre-industrial-initialised experiments, corresponding to ∼40 GtCO 2 for a 1.5 • C carbon budget. At higher forcing, the land-use effect on TCRE diminishes as α differences converge while γ land continues to diverge. Our results highlight a baseline-dependent bias in current CMIP protocol design with direct implications for carbon budget estimates.

title: Atmospheric O 2 reveals a strengthening ocean carbon sink and a stagnant net land sink since 1990
summary: The global ocean and land biosphere absorb roughly half of fossil fuel carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions. The temporal evolution of these sinks remains difficult to quantify owing to data sparsity. Leveraging 30+ years of atmospheric oxygen
content: The global ocean and land biosphere absorb roughly half of fossil fuel carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions. The temporal evolution of these sinks remains difficult to quantify owing to data sparsity. Leveraging 30+ years of atmospheric oxygen (O 2 ) and CO 2 observations, we find that the ocean carbon sink increased by 0.63 ± 0.19 petagrams of carbon per year per decade (Pg C year −1 decade −1 ) (a mean of 2.8 ± 0.4 Pg C year −1 ), accounting for 35% of fossil emissions between 1990 and 2019. The net land sink shows no robust trend (with a mean of 1.0 ± 0.5 Pg C year −1 , accounting for 13% of fossil emissions), despite large decadal variability. These results challenge many process-based model simulations of the land and ocean sinks, questioning their ability to accurately predict future climate states.

title: An updated land emulator dataset for energy models and integrated assessment: GLOBIOM-G4M lookup tables for the new SSPs in the context of ScenarioMIP7
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Featuring multi-dimensional energy-land nexus and capturing the complex dynamics of the agriculture, forestry, and other land use (AFOLU) sectors without sacrificing computational efficiency remains a critical challenge in integrated assess
content: Featuring multi-dimensional energy-land nexus and capturing the complex dynamics of the agriculture, forestry, and other land use (AFOLU) sectors without sacrificing computational efficiency remains a critical challenge in integrated assessment modelling (IAM). To support the generation of new Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) for the ScenarioMIP-CMIP7 process, we developed a comprehensive updated set of GLOBIOM-G4M lookup tables available for IAMs and energy models. Operating as multidimensional land emulators, this updated dataset was generated utilizing an enhanced modelling pipeline that incorporates the latest SSPv3 macroeconomic drivers, novel agricultural add-on mitigation technologies, dynamic EAT-Lancet2 dietary shifts), alongside integrated updates in water, nutrient, and biodiversity modules. The resulting emulators provide detailed bioenergy cost-supply curves, agricultural market responses, and AFOLU marginal abatement cost curves (MACCs) across the SSP1-SSP5 as well as the Low Energy Demand (LED) pathways. Compared to CMIP6-era dataset, the updated lookup tables reveal deeper structural mitigation potential. For instance, in the SSP2 pathway and under a 100 USD/tCO₂eq carbon price, the rapid deployment of new agricultural technologies drives enhances the achievable net AFOLU CO₂ sink from approximately -1 GtCO₂/yr to -3 GtCO₂/yr under moderate bioenergy demand by the middle of the century. These emulators directly underpinned the land-use modelling for both the MESSAGEix-GLOBIOM-GAINS and WITCH-GLOBIOM frameworks in the ScenarioMIP7 intercomparison, demonstrating strong cross-model interoperability. To promote transparency and broader community usage, this dataset will be published as an open-access resource on Zenodo. This will enable standalone energy and IAM models to seamlessly integrate SSP-specific, cross-sectoral consistent land-system boundaries and dynamics, preventing unrealistic large-scale BECCS or afforestation deployments, and also reducing the computational burden of hard-linking full-scale endogenous spatial land model with energy models.

title: Falkner–Skan quaternary hybrid nanofluid dynamics and thermal transport with thermal radiation and aligned magnetic field
source: Journal of Taibah University for Science
summary: Despite growing interest in quaternary hybrid nanofluids (QHNFs) containing four distinct nanoparticles, the combined effects of magnetic field orientation and thermal radiation on Falkner–Skan wedge flow remain insufficiently understood. T
content: Despite growing interest in quaternary hybrid nanofluids (QHNFs) containing four distinct nanoparticles, the combined effects of magnetic field orientation and thermal radiation on Falkner–Skan wedge flow remain insufficiently understood. This study investigates the hydrodynamic and thermal behaviour of Al₂O₃–Cu–TiO₂–Ag/water QHNF over a wedge, focusing on the coupled influences of magnetic field orientation, pressure gradient, and thermal radiation. Similarity transformations reduce the governing equations to a system of ordinary differential equations, which is solved numerically using the Keller–Box method. Increasing the magnetic-field inclination angle from 0° to 90° increases the skin-friction coefficient and local Nusselt number by approximately 109.4% and 18.5%, respectively, for the wedge, compared with 149.2% and 25.0% for the flat plate. QHNF exhibits the highest heat-transfer performance among the NF, HNF, THNF, and QHNF formulations for both wedge and flat-plate configurations, whereas the skin-friction response is non-monotonic. The favourable pressure gradient associated with the wedge geometry and magnetic-field inclination modify the effects of thermal radiation on transport characteristics. These findings highlight geometry-dependent electromagnetic and radiative transport mechanisms relevant to high-temperature thermal management and provide useful insights for designing advanced nanoparticle-based heat-transfer systems.

title: Response of mung bean to exogenous applied sulphur and aspartic acid in hot arid region of Rajasthan
summary: Balanced nutrient management is a major concern in the present-day scenario, especially in soils of arid regions, which are low in soil fertility; hence, supplementation of sulphur (S) helps in plant growth and maintenance of soil health. T
content: Balanced nutrient management is a major concern in the present-day scenario, especially in soils of arid regions, which are low in soil fertility; hence, supplementation of sulphur (S) helps in plant growth and maintenance of soil health. The use of amino acids as biostimulants has gained widespread importance in recent times. L-aspartic acid (ASP) is one of the amino acids, which plays a key role in plant growth and stress management. No studies have reported the use of ASP in mung bean; therefore, the present study investigates the effect of graded levels of S application in soil and foliar application of ASP on growth and yield of mung bean. The field experiment was conducted during kharif 2024 and 2025 at Central Arid Zone Research Institute, Jodhpur in a split plot design containing four main plots (0, 20, 40 and 60 kg sulphur ha⁻¹) and four subplots (0, 40, 80 and 120 mg L⁻¹ aspartic acid) with 3 replications. Our research findings revealed that both S and ASP positively improved the growth parameters and yield of mung beans. Relative to the control, the improvement in plant height, leaf area index (LAI), dry matter production, specific leaf weight (SLW), crop growth rate (CGR), net assimilation rate (NAR) and grain yield was 18.3, 15.8, 47.2, 17.1, 52.8, 30.0 and 72.6 %, respectively, by S60 (pooled). Similarly, A120 produced 15.7, 15.1, 34.8, 8.6, 38.2, 19.2 and 25.3 % higher values for the above parameters compared to the control (pooled). The correlation analysis indicated a significantly positive correlation of grain yield with NAR at 25–45 days after sowing (DAS) (0.961 **) and at 45–65 DAS (0.937 **).

title: Global climate modeling of the Martian water cycle. I) Improved parameterizations of physical processes
summary: We implement four new physical parameterizations relevant to the water cycle in the Mars PCM (previously Mars Laboratoire de M{é}t{é}orologie Dynamique GCM)\,: the latent heat of ground ice sublimation, a temperature-dependent nucleation sc
content: We implement four new physical parameterizations relevant to the water cycle in the Mars PCM (previously Mars Laboratoire de M{é}t{é}orologie Dynamique GCM)\,: the latent heat of ground ice sublimation, a temperature-dependent nucleation scheme in cloud microphysics, differentiated albedos for water frost and perennial ice and scavenging of water ice clouds by CO2 particle formation. After a new tuning of the poorly known model parameters, we find that combining these parameterizations allows for an improved agreement of the modeled water cycle compared to Thermal Emission Spectrometer column-integrated vapor and ice retrievals. We show that latent heat cooling prevents the formation of surface liquid water at present and likely in the recent past on Mars. Using two albedos corrects the overestimation of the northern sublimation event, a major defect of the model. Our study highlights that each parameterization has indirect consequences amplified by the radiatively active clouds. We stress that the increasingly complex water cycle in the Mars PCM should be studied in the future using numerical methods tailored for climate modeling, in addition to the effect of each individual component.

title: Photorespiration does not act as a photoprotective electron sink under unstressed conditions
summary: Photosynthesis is comprised of two sets of reactions that must coordinate activities to maintain optimal efficiency and avoid harmful side reactions. The first set of reactions is light driven electron transfer, in a second set the electron
content: Photosynthesis is comprised of two sets of reactions that must coordinate activities to maintain optimal efficiency and avoid harmful side reactions. The first set of reactions is light driven electron transfer, in a second set the electrons are used for carbon fixation in the C3 cycle. In addition to the C3 cycle, electrons are used to drive photorespiration, the metabolic pathway that detoxifies the harmful product of the rubisco oxygenase reaction. It has been hypothesized that photorespiration is a photoprotective electron sink to avoid metabolic congestion that could lead to damage of the electron transport chain and reduced activity of photosystem II. To tease apart the impact of C3 and photorespiratory metabolic sink on both photosynthetic efficiency and photoprotection, we used chlorophyll a fluorescence coupled to gas exchange to probe the response of the electron transport chain to a wide range of metabolic poise, set by O2 and CO2 gas mixing. We found that, while metabolic flux correlated well with efficiency of photosystem II, fractional metabolic poise towards photorespiration was the largest metabolic determinant of long-lived downregulation of light harvesting at photosystem II. This long-lived downregulation does not correlate with observed D1 loss, suggesting accumulation of a quencher that is not damage to the photosystem. Together, these findings are contradictory to the proposed role of photorespiration as a photoprotective electron sink. Additionally, we have demonstrated that O2 concentration interacts with downregulation of photosystem II separately from the effects of O2 on metabolic poise which complicates the interpretation of photoprotection data generated when using O2.

title: A hierarchical multi-site ES-MDA framework for constraining coupled water-carbon parameters in eCLM across European plant functional types
summary: Water and carbon exchanges are coupled because carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) and water vapor loss occur through leaf stomata, yet land surface predictions remain uncertain because vegetation and soil parameters are poorly constrained and often cal
content: Water and carbon exchanges are coupled because carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) and water vapor loss occur through leaf stomata, yet land surface predictions remain uncertain because vegetation and soil parameters are poorly constrained and often calibrated independently at individual sites. We develop a hierarchical ensemble smoother with multiple data assimilation (H-ES-MDA) for the enCore Community Land Model (eCLM) that pools information across 38 European eddy-covariance sites. The framework estimates shared plant functional type (PFT) vegetation parameters while retaining site-level vegetation deviations and site-specific soil hydraulic parameters. Six assimilation scenarios combined soil moisture (SM), evapotranspiration (ET), net ecosystem exchange (NEE), with performance assessed in independent validation years. Joint assimilation of SM, ET, and NEE produced the most balanced improvements relative to prior simulations, improving median validation performance by 30–46% for SM, 7% for ET, and 18% for NEE, while avoiding the SM degradation observed with flux-only assimilation. Shared PFT posteriors retained substantial NEE skill for grasslands and evergreen needleleaf forests, whereas site-level deviations added little skill. A leave-one-site-out experiment for grasslands confirmed that shared NEE skill persisted at sites excluded from calibration. Transfer was weaker for deciduous broadleaf forest and cropland and did not consistently extend from NEE to unassimilated gross primary production and ecosystem respiration. Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence and Shapley attribution further showed that strong parameter updating does not necessarily imply predictive skill. Hierarchical multi-site assimilation therefore provides a direct way to test which parameter information can be shared regionally and which processes require local or improved model representation.

title: From joint evidence appraisal to a structured basis for managing vegetation carbon sinks in urban green spaces.
summary: Urban green spaces (UGSs) can contribute to climate mitigation through vegetation carbon sinks, but translating heterogeneous scientific evidence into planning and management remains difficult. Reported effect directions are not always cons
content: Urban green spaces (UGSs) can contribute to climate mitigation through vegetation carbon sinks, but translating heterogeneous scientific evidence into planning and management remains difficult. Reported effect directions are not always consistent, analytical support is uneven across factors, and scale applicability is often unclear. We synthesized 141 studies, identified 199 factors, and developed a joint assessment framework combining the consistency index (CI), which characterizes effect consistency, with the total weight of evidence (TWoE), which represents accumulated analytical support. The two measures captured distinct dimensions of the evidence profile: greater accumulated analytical support did not necessarily correspond to higher effect consistency. Under the reference thresholds, the framework identified 15 priority factors with relatively high effect consistency and substantial accumulated analytical support. These factors covered vegetation structure and attributes, green space amount and landscape configuration, urban and land use context, and management and maintenance. Based on the stability of their dominant effect directions, they were organized into core, calibration, and conditional candidate indicators, supporting intervention evaluation and key monitoring, contextual adjustment, and scenario comparison and supplementary evaluation, respectively. Their distributions across spatial scales informed a proposed pathway from evidence to decision making, covering baseline diagnosis, planning strategy, design solution, operation and maintenance, and monitoring and feedback. The framework introduces differentiated evidence appraisal between factor synthesis and practical translation, providing a structured basis for evidence use tailored to scale and context in UGS vegetation carbon sink management.

title: Photophysical insights on the phototoxicity of p -aminobenzoic acid
summary: P -aminobenzoic acid (PABA) is known to induce photosensitised reactions in the DNA. In this contribution we provide static multirreference (XMS-CASPT2) insight on the probable deactivation mechanism behind these reactions. PABA is excited
content: P -aminobenzoic acid (PABA) is known to induce photosensitised reactions in the DNA. In this contribution we provide static multirreference (XMS-CASPT2) insight on the probable deactivation mechanism behind these reactions. PABA is excited by UV-B radiation, which populates the bright second electronically excited state. Relaxation leads readily to the S 1 potential, where we found two minima of different character (ππ ∗ and nπ ∗ ). Ground state recovery via internal conversions within the singlet potentials is unlikely, thus confirming a triplet-mediated deactivation. All the explored pathways along the triplet surface from two different intersystem crossing funnels converge in the same T 1 minimum, that likely traps population for long times. Since no accessible thermal routes to the ground state have been found, the triplet state of PABA may be quenched in triplet-triplet energy transfer reactions to the nucleobases or molecular oxygen, thus explaining the photosensitising nature of PABA.

title: Traffic CO₂ Emissions and Roadside-Tree Carbon Sequestration along Pemuda Road in Surabaya, Indonesia
summary: Urban transportation is a major contributor to carbon emissions in high-mobility downtown corridors, while roadside vegetation is often expected to offset part of these emissions. Previous studies have compared transportation emissions with
content: Urban transportation is a major contributor to carbon emissions in high-mobility downtown corridors, while roadside vegetation is often expected to offset part of these emissions. Previous studies have compared transportation emissions with vegetation-based carbon offsets, but evidence remains limited for individual downtown road corridors using comparable annualised emission and sequestration measures. This study assesses the carbon balance along a 1.5-km segment of Pemuda Road in Surabaya by estimating annualised motor-vehicle CO₂ emissions and the carbon stock and annual sequestration of existing roadside vegetation. A 16-hour manual traffic count was conducted on 5 May 2023, and a roadside-vegetation survey conducted on 11 May 2026 identified 35 trees for aboveground-biomass estimation. The quantitative analysis integrates traffic counting, Vehicle Kilometres Travelled, vehicle emission factors, allometric biomass estimation, carbon-stock estimation, and scenario-based annual sequestration. The results show that motor vehicles generate 2,773.61 tonnes of CO₂ per year, while the 35 existing roadside trees store 85.77 tonnes of CO₂ equivalent. Under the main sequestration-to-storage scenario of 4.0%, annual vegetation sequestration is estimated at 3.43 tonnes of CO₂ per year, resulting in a net carbon deficit of 2,770.18 tonnes of CO₂ per year and a vegetation offset fraction of 0.124%. Sensitivity analysis confirms that the vegetation offset fraction remains below 0.2% across the tested scenarios. These findings demonstrate that roadside vegetation provides only a limited offset and should be positioned as a complementary mitigation strategy alongside public transport improvement, private-vehicle management, active mobility, and integrated low-carbon land-use planning.

title: Metsäojituksen ja ennallistamisen vaikutukset taimenpitoisiin virtavesiin
summary: Metsäojitus on muuttanut merkittävästi Suomen suoekosysteemejä ja valuma-alueiden hydrologiaa. Ojituksen seurauksena veden kulkeutuminen muuttuu, ja ojitusalueilta huuhtoutuu alapuolisiin vesistöihin kiintoainetta, ravinteita ja orgaanista
content: Metsäojitus on muuttanut merkittävästi Suomen suoekosysteemejä ja valuma-alueiden hydrologiaa. Ojituksen seurauksena veden kulkeutuminen muuttuu, ja ojitusalueilta huuhtoutuu alapuolisiin vesistöihin kiintoainetta, ravinteita ja orgaanista ainesta. Nämä muutokset heikentävät virtavesien ekologista tilaa ja vaikuttavat erityisesti ympäristöolosuhteille herkkiin lajeihin, kuten taimeneen (Salmo trutta). Tässä tutkielmassa tarkastellaan metsäojituksen vaikutuksia taimenen elinympäristöön ja menestymiseen Suomen virtavesissä sekä selvitetään, millaisilla ennallistamis- ja vesiensuojelutoimenpiteillä ojituksen haitallisia vaikutuksia voidaan vähentää. Metsäojituksen vaikutukset taimenen elinympäristöihin liittyvät erityisesti vedenlaadun, hydrologian ja uomien rakenteellisiin muutoksiin. Kiintoainekuormitus heikentää esimerkiksi kutusoraikkojen laatua ja mädin hapensaantia, kun taas ravinnekuormitus, veden tummuminen ja lämpötilan muutokset vaikuttavat taimenen ravinnonsaantiin, fysiologiaan ja lisääntymiseen. Lisäksi hydrologiset muutokset voivat vähentää taimenen eri elinkierron vaiheille soveltuvien elinympäristöjen määrää. Metsäojituksen haitallisia vaikutuksia pyritään vähentämään soiden ennallistamisella, valuma-alueen vesiensuojelutoimilla ja uomakunnostuksilla. Toimenpiteiden vaikutukset voivat kuitenkin vaihdella alueellisten olosuhteiden mukaan ja esimerkiksi ennallistaminen saattaa lisätä vesistökuormitusta lyhyellä aikavälillä. Taimenen elinympäristön tilan parantaminen edellyttääkin valuma-alueen ja virtavesien tarkastelua kokonaisuutena. Lisäksi tarvitaan pitkäaikaista tutkimusta ja seurantaa, jotta voidaan arvioida toimenpiteiden vaikutuksia vedenlaatuun, elinympäristöihin ja taimenkantojen kehitykseen.

title: Superoxide dismutase shapes manganese stoichiometry in Southern Ocean diatoms
summary: Quantifying the elemental stoichiometry of marine phytoplankton biomass is crucial for projections of primary production. In many cases, the mechanistic underpinnings of biomass stoichiometry are unclear. We combined metaproteomics, Bayesia
content: Quantifying the elemental stoichiometry of marine phytoplankton biomass is crucial for projections of primary production. In many cases, the mechanistic underpinnings of biomass stoichiometry are unclear. We combined metaproteomics, Bayesian statistical modeling, and geochemical measurements to quantify the contribution of superoxide dismutases to metal stoichiometry in natural populations of Southern Ocean diatoms. Our analyses indicate that a substantial amount of manganese (Mn) in diatoms in an Antarctic polynya can be attributed to superoxide dismutases (∼0.7 micromoles of Mn:moles of carbon; ∼20% of the total cellular Mn quota). We then used proteomic profiles of polar diatom cultures to identify environmental controls on superoxide dismutases and found that Mn limitation induces the depletion of Mn superoxide dismutases and an accompanying increase in nickel superoxide dismutase. Overall, we combined metaproteomic approaches to quantify proteome composition and connected these measurements to metal-to-carbon ratios and their responses to metal availability. Our approach provides a mechanism for directly parameterizing ecosystem-scale models with molecular measurements.

title: Cost-effective climate change mitigation through land sector contributions
summary: Abstract Climate change mitigation from Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use (AFOLU) comes with severe sustainability risks and faces major implementation challenges. Yet, the consequences of missing out on AFOLU mitigation potential fo
content: Abstract Climate change mitigation from Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use (AFOLU) comes with severe sustainability risks and faces major implementation challenges. Yet, the consequences of missing out on AFOLU mitigation potential for the transition of the energy sector and the achievability of climate objectives are not well understood. Here, using the Integrated Assessment Modeling framework REMIND–MAgPIE, we derive future mitigation pathways under different AFOLU policy portfolios. We show that, without AFOLU contributions to mitigation, limiting warming to 1.5 °C is out of reach within the twenty-first century and for keeping peak warming below 1.7 °C consumption loss relative to a current-policy baseline increases from 1.3% to 3.5%. A portfolio of options alleviates the burden of energy sector decarbonization and substantially reduces energy price markups, but puts the AFOLU sector under stress. We show that prudent policy measures, such as limiting total bioenergy use to 100 EJ yr −1 and restricting CH 4 and N 2 O pricing to US$75 per tonne of CO 2 equivalent, can largely attenuate this pressure by reducing the need for yield increases and diminishing food price markups without severely compromising the achievability of climate targets. Our findings highlight both the need for effective climate action in the AFOLU sector and the importance of balanced and judicious sectorally aligned policies.

title: Evaluation of Induction Thermography for the Detection of Cracks Due to Mechanical and Thermal Stress in WC-10Co-4Cr Coatings
summary: Abstract WC–Co-Cr coatings have exceptional mechanical properties including high hardness, wear resistance and corrosion resistance. However, under continuous wear or mechanical/thermal overloads, such as line loads in calender rollers or i
content: Abstract WC–Co-Cr coatings have exceptional mechanical properties including high hardness, wear resistance and corrosion resistance. However, under continuous wear or mechanical/thermal overloads, such as line loads in calender rollers or improper heating/cooling cycles, these coatings can develop defects like cracks and dents. Such damage compromises product quality, particularly in calendering processes where precise roller concentricity (single-figure micrometre range) is critical. This study investigates induction thermography as a non-destructive alternative for defect detection in WC-10Co-4Cr coatings. Coated C60 steel specimens with different surface roughness (conditions: ground and as-sprayed) were subjected to controlled mechanical (strains: 0.12% to 0.4%) and thermal stresses (thermal shock), inducing cracks with widths ranging from approx. 1 to 4.5 µm and depths up to the full coating thickness (≈ 400 µm). Both crack width and depth influenced the thermal contrast, with deeper cracks producing a stronger signal. Using the Fourier transform method and principal component analysis, induction thermography successfully identified cracks down to a minimum resolved width of ≈ 1 µm in ground and ≈ 1.7 µm in as-sprayed specimens, demonstrating its sensitivity to defect detection across different surface conditions. The results highlight the potential of this method to improve process reliability and product quality in high-precision applications by enabling non-invasive inspection.

title: Ubiquitin-dependent signal amplification in lipid saturation sensing
summary: Cellular membranes are dynamic platforms whose composition and biophysical properties are surveyed by sensor proteins to maintain homeostasis. Failure to preserve membrane homeostasis, however, results in cellular stress and organelle dysfu
content: Cellular membranes are dynamic platforms whose composition and biophysical properties are surveyed by sensor proteins to maintain homeostasis. Failure to preserve membrane homeostasis, however, results in cellular stress and organelle dysfunction. Using the prototypical lipid saturation sensor Mga2, we explored how weak physical cues that modulate rotational movements in the transmembrane region are converted into decisive biochemical outputs that ultimately control the production of unsaturated fatty acids. Using reconstituted systems and purified components, we quantitatively follow the ubiquitylation of Mga2 via the E3 ligase Rsp5. Kinetic modeling reveals that several rounds of ubiquitylation contribute to signal amplification and uncovers the first transfer of ubiquitin onto Mga2 as a kinetic gatekeeper. The minimal system composed of the sensor protein and a canonical E1-E2-E3 ubiquitylation cascade is sufficient to discriminate saturated and unsaturated membrane lipid environments even in the absence of deubiquitylating enzymes such as Ubp2. Our findings provide a mechanistic framework for how membrane property sensors convert weak, fluctuating physical cues into robust biochemical outcomes.

title: Plant hydraulic traits regulating productivity and drought resistance in boreal crops
summary: Plant hydraulics play a critical role in coordinating photosynthesis, water use, and hydraulic safety when facing water scarcity. The hydraulic traits of boreal crops and their relevance to productivity and drought resistance, however, rema
content: Plant hydraulics play a critical role in coordinating photosynthesis, water use, and hydraulic safety when facing water scarcity. The hydraulic traits of boreal crops and their relevance to productivity and drought resistance, however, remain poorly researched. In this study, we combined multi-year carbon and water flux measurements from two Finnish fields representing contrasting boreal cropping systems – a perennial forage grass mixture and an annual cereal crop (oats) – with a novel modelling framework coupling plant photosynthesis, hydraulics, and soil moisture dynamics to decipher the field-level effective hydraulic traits (i.e., apparent hydraulic traits) of the crops and their association with crop performance under varying drought conditions. The model reproduced the observed carbon and water fluxes well and revealed relatively low maximum whole-plant hydraulic conductance and conservative water-use strategies in both crops. Under drought, low hydraulic efficiency prevented soil water depletion and thereby supported high productivity through drought avoidance, whereas its advantage diminished under wetter conditions. Both crops were substantially more susceptible to atmospheric dryness than to low soil moisture, highlighting vapor pressure deficit as an important constraint on crop productivity under boreal conditions. The remaining discrepancy between the model-inferred apparent hydraulic traits and available empirical measurements for temperate crops indicates the need for more direct hydraulic measurements of boreal crops. Our findings further underscore the importance of incorporating crop hydraulic processes in process-based crop models to gain physiological insights into crop performance and to enhance their accuracy and predictive power under current and future climates.

title: Multi-centennial ocean biogeochemical responses to extended Shared Socioeconomic Pathways
summary: Despite their profound consequences for the global carbon cycle, multi-centennial ocean biogeochemical responses to anthropogenic greenhouse gas forcing remain poorly constrained. Here we investigate long-term oceanic responses to atmospher
content: Despite their profound consequences for the global carbon cycle, multi-centennial ocean biogeochemical responses to anthropogenic greenhouse gas forcing remain poorly constrained. Here we investigate long-term oceanic responses to atmospheric CO 2 forcing using the Model for Interdisciplinary Research on Climate, Earth System version 2 for Long-term simulations (MIROC-ES2L) Earth system model driven by extended Shared Socio-economic Pathway (SSP) scenarios through to the year 2500. Ocean–atmosphere p CO 2 disequilibrium exhibits strong scenario dependence. Under the low-emission scenario SSP1–2.6, oceanic CO 2 undersaturation gradually weakens and approaches near equilibrium by 2100. By contrast, under the high-emission scenario SSP5–8.5, rapid increase in atmospheric p CO 2 results in increasing undersaturation of CO 2 in the ocean over the 21st century. Thereafter, surface-ocean CO 2 supersaturation progressively expand into the equatorial and subtropical oceans between the mid–23rd and late 25th century. The Southern Ocean remains persistently undersaturated throughout the simulations, consistent with sustained influence from deep waters that are weakly affected by anthropogenic perturbations. Under SSP5–8.5, oceanic CO 2 uptake continues to increase until the late 21st century. Thereafter, it gradually weakens as surface-ocean p CO 2 approaches atmospheric levels, whereas the Southern Ocean remains a persistent carbon sink throughout the simulation. Across all scenarios, early oceanic p CO 2 changes are primarily driven by increases in dissolved inorganic carbon, whereas alkalinity becomes an increasingly important control from the mid–22nd century onward under SSP5–8.5. A progressive decline in the oceanic CO 2 buffering capacity, driven by cumulative CO 2 uptake, increases the sensitivity of surface-ocean p CO 2 to additional carbon uptake. The buffering capacity approaches its effective minimum levels by the late 22nd century. In parallel, enhanced upper-ocean stratification and a slowdown of the deep overturning circulation reduce the upward transport of high alkalinity waters to the surface. This results in a decline in surface-ocean alkalinity that further enhances the influence of alkalinity on surface-ocean p CO 2 during this period. Marine biological productivity and export vary significantly as a function of atmospheric CO 2 trajectory. It increases under low-emission scenarios but declines under sustained high-emission scenarios. The transition between the two behaviors occurs when pCO2atm reaches approximately 3 times the preindustrial level and is closely associated with the weakening of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation and the resulting nutrient redistribution. Thermal stress and nutrient limitation persist in regions such as the Arctic Ocean until the late 25th century even under SSP1–2.6, indicating a centennial-scale lagged response of marine ecosystems to atmospheric CO 2 forcing.
