title: Electronic Dynamics in Long Linear and Cyclic Polyynes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
summary: Abstract Carbyne─the one-dimensional sp-hybridized allotrope of carbon─has long been predicted to exhibit unique properties, yet its synthesis remains elusive. To probe its behavior, finite sp-carbon chains such as cumulenes and polyynes ha
content: Abstract Carbyne─the one-dimensional sp-hybridized allotrope of carbon─has long been predicted to exhibit unique properties, yet its synthesis remains elusive. To probe its behavior, finite sp-carbon chains such as cumulenes and polyynes have been studied. While much has been established about the ground-state properties of cumulenes and polyynes, our understanding of their photophysical dynamics, which gives critical insight into how electronic relaxation, structural reorganization, and spin formation evolve, has focused almost exclusively on short, linear systems, with little consideration of topology. Here, we investigate long 48-carbon linear and cyclic polyynes in the liquid phase using steady-state and ultrafast, temperature- and polarization-resolved optical and vibrational spectroscopy. We find highly delocalized ground states in both topologies, with softened Peierls distortion and reduced bond-length alternation relative to shorter chains. In contrast, the excited state singlet dipole depolarization mechanism and subsequent intersystem crossing are strongly dependent on chain length and topology. As in shorter polyynes, transient infrared spectroscopy shows that photoexcitation of long linear polyynes induces a cumulene-like excited-state geometry; however, this structural rearrangement is weaker and shorter-lived than in shorter analogues. Comparison with shorter-chain trends and theoretical predictions shows that the Huang–Rhys factor remains far below the ideal infinite-chain value at 48 carbons, suggesting that vibronic coupling grows more slowly at long chain length than expected from simple extrapolation. Our results reveal how topology influences the largely backbone-dominated electronic dynamics of long polyynes and refine our understanding of finite sp-carbon systems at longer chain lengths than previously accessible with such time-resolved methods.

title: A regional climate modeling investigation of wetland-related coupled hydrologic–atmospheric processes in central South America
summary: Abstract This study investigates how the Pantanal, one of the world’s largest tropical floodplains, modulates local and regional climate in central South America through coupled land–atmosphere processes. Using the RegIPSL regional climate
content: Abstract This study investigates how the Pantanal, one of the world’s largest tropical floodplains, modulates local and regional climate in central South America through coupled land–atmosphere processes. Using the RegIPSL regional climate modeling framework, two simulations covering the 1998–2019 period were conducted: one including an explicit floodplain scheme and one without it. The floodplain-enabled simulation exhibits a substantially improved representation of the hydrological cycle over the Pantanal and Upper Paraguay River Basin, particularly through enhanced evapotranspiration, increased moisture recycling, and more realistic river discharge. Results show that activating the floodplain scheme increases precipitation across most of the Pantanal and surrounding regions, primarily by raising the number of rainy days during the wet season. However, convection is suppressed over the most heavily flooded areas, consistent with wetland-breeze dynamics and stabilized boundary-layer conditions. At regional scales, enhanced evapotranspiration transforms the Pantanal into an atmospheric moisture source, increasing lower-tropospheric humidity, moist static energy, and convective potential downstream. The altered surface fluxes weaken the Chaco Low and modify the South American Low-Level Jet, reducing large scale atmospheric moisture transport over the Pantanal but strengthening it along the eastern Andes, ultimately increasing precipitation in parts of northern Argentina. These findings highlight the crucial role of tropical floodplains in shaping regional climate and underscore the importance of representing wetland processes in global and regional Earth system models. Because the model is too dry over the Pantanal during the wet season, the absolute magnitude of these responses should be interpreted with caution, while the simulated mechanisms and their spatial structure provide robust evidence for a floodplain-atmosphere feedback.

title: Seagrasses and macroalgae incorporate land-derived metal pollution while limiting its transfer through estuarine food webs
summary: Estuarine areas provide critical ecosystem services by supporting biodiversity, maintaining water quality, and supplying seafood resources. Anthropogenic activities can introduce harmful metals into estuarine systems, potentially threatenin
content: Estuarine areas provide critical ecosystem services by supporting biodiversity, maintaining water quality, and supplying seafood resources. Anthropogenic activities can introduce harmful metals into estuarine systems, potentially threatening these services. Edgartown Great Pond, Martha's Vineyard, MA, is a shallow, hydrologically restricted estuarine system hosting abundant benthic primary producers, including seagrasses ( Zostera marina , Ruppia maritima ) and macroalgae ( Polysiphonia sp. and others). We quantified concentrations of eleven metals in groundwater entering the pond and analyzed metal accumulation in benthic producers and higher trophic levels. Stable isotope signatures (δ 13 C, δ 15 N) were used to reconstruct the food web and determine trophic positions, allowing assessment of metal transfer through the system. Groundwater inputs contained measurable, though generally low, metal concentrations, with marginally elevated concentrations in two coves. Benthic primary producers accumulated all metals at concentrations several orders of magnitude higher than those in groundwater. Food web reconstruction indicated that seagrasses and macroalgae form the base of the pond's food web, supporting herbivores, detritivores, and predators. Regression analysis of metal concentrations and δ 15 N signatures revealed negative or non-significant relationships for all metals, consistent with biodilution rather than biomagnification. These results demonstrate that benthic primary producers may be able to sequester metal pollution and limit its transfer to consumers, possibly reducing pollutant accumulation within the food web. An ecosystem service like this could be critical for maintaining environmental quality and seafood safety. The protection, maintenance, and re-establishment of benthic primary producer populations may be essential to management and restoration strategies for developed coastal systems like Edgartown Great Pond.

title: Benthic cyanobacterial mats enhance nitrogen turnover in a eutrophic reservoir
summary: Abstract. Benthic cyanobacterial mats are widespread in eutrophic lakes, but their effects on sediment phosphorus (P), iron (Fe), and nitrogen (N) cycling are poorly quantified. We studied Microseira wollei, a mat-forming cyanobacterium cap
content: Abstract. Benthic cyanobacterial mats are widespread in eutrophic lakes, but their effects on sediment phosphorus (P), iron (Fe), and nitrogen (N) cycling are poorly quantified. We studied Microseira wollei, a mat-forming cyanobacterium capable of N2 fixation and toxin production, in Lake Wateree, South Carolina (USA). We sampled paired sites with and without mats at two locations in March and monthly from June through October 2023 (three dates per location), and measured P, Fe, and N concentrations in mat interstitial water and porewater, and N transformation rates and fluxes using 15N-labelled and unlabelled whole-core incubations. Porewater P and nitrate (NO3−) were higher beneath benthic mats in June and July and Fe was higher in June, September, and October, whereas ammonium (NH4+) was lower beneath mats in June. Potential denitrification rates did not differ on average between paired sites (24.2 ± 13.9 vs. 19.3 ± 12.2 µmol N m−2 h−1 with and without mats), but increased with mat thickness (r2 = 0.62). Potential dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium (DNRA) rates, measured as 15NH4+ production from added 15NO3−, were 2.3 times higher in mat-covered sediments (13.1 ± 4.4 vs. 5.8 ± 3.3 µmol N m−2 h−1) but remained smaller than denitrification, accounting on average for 39 % of total NO3− reduction in mat sediments and 29 % in bare sediments. The net N2 flux in unamended mat cores was directed from the water column to the sediments in all ten cores (−23.9 ± 32.2 µmol N m−2 h−1), suggesting that N2 fixation likely exceeded denitrification beneath mats, although the mean was not significantly different from zero or from that in cores without mats. M. wollei mats are therefore hotspots of N turnover: they enhance denitrification with increasing mat thickness, more than double DNRA, may support N2 fixation, and release P, Fe, and NH4+ from the sediments, complicating the management of eutrophic lakes.

title: Improved subglacial boundary conditions near Dome C, Antarctica, through rigorous integration of multi-campaign radar data and an ensemble stochastic simulation approach
summary: Subglacial bed topography is a fundamental boundary condition for ice-sheet flow, basal thermal regimes, and the preservation of palaeoclimate records, yet it remains highly uncertain across Antarctica. We use stochastic simulation methods
content: Subglacial bed topography is a fundamental boundary condition for ice-sheet flow, basal thermal regimes, and the preservation of palaeoclimate records, yet it remains highly uncertain across Antarctica. We use stochastic simulation methods to generate an ensemble of gridded (500 m) ice thickness and bed elevation near Dome C, and map bed elevation uncertainty accounting for impacts of data availability and basal roughness. New airborne radar measurements uncover previously undocumented sectors of the ice-bed interface and we integrate these with existing data using a rigorous approach to ensure nearby measurement compatibility. Our simulated bed shows improved representation of basal roughness between survey profiles, revealing regional roughness over 50 % higher than previous interpolations. We apply the ensemble to investigate uncertainty in meltwater routing, identifying well-constrained drainage away from the Dome C Plateau but poorly constrained outflow from Concordia Lake and parts of the Belgica Highlands. Topographic focussing of geothermal heat could lead to local anomalies up to ±30 % relative to the regional value, and several ice core drill sites are in a zone with potentially 12 % locally-reduced geothermal heating which could be favourable for deep ice layer preservation. This work demonstrates that the critical subglacial bed boundary condition is better represented by ensemble-based, stochastic simulations based on strictly cross-validated data rather than single deterministic interpolations, and simulated beds can improve the reliability of analyses with robust consideration of uncertainties in data-sparse regions.

title: A two-phase method of characteristics for heat pump expander design
summary: The greenhouse gases emissions due to the generation of energy through fossil fuels required for domestic heating could be reduced using electric heat pumps. Despite being well-known, heat pumps offer room for improvement, as it could be po
content: The greenhouse gases emissions due to the generation of energy through fossil fuels required for domestic heating could be reduced using electric heat pumps. Despite being well-known, heat pumps offer room for improvement, as it could be possible to recover energy from the expansion using a two-phase turboexpander. Since no robust design guidelines for two-phase turbines are available in the literature, the authors propose a methodology based on the method of characteristics (MOC). Despite its extension to real gases and fluid starting from two-phase condition, no method existed so far to handle fluid expanding from subcooled to fully two-phase conditions, as it usually occurs in heat pump expanders. The discontinuity in Mach number caused by the drop in speed of sound triggered by phase change prevented the application of usual series expansion methods. The proposed new general initialisation method holds for both single-phase, two-phase and subcooled liquid inlet conditions. A supersonic nozzle designed with the MOC is verified against a barotropic computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation considering different fluids (carbon dioxide, propane, R-1234ze(E)) and inlet conditions and the error is in all cases below 0.78%. Subsequently, the stator of a two-phase turbine is designed using the MOC and verified against both an inviscid and a viscous barotropic CFD simulation. The difference is below 1.18% when compared against the inviscid simulation and below 2.91% when compared against the viscous one. The promising results support the use of this new MOC as an initial design tool for this class of turboexpanders, for which no tried and tested guidelines are available.

title: Characterizing cryogenic chilldown and boil-off: A liquid nitrogen experimental study
summary: Cryogenic chilldown and boil-off directly impact the efficiency, safety and operational margins of any system that handles cryogenic fluids, including propulsion, storage and transfer applications. These processes arise from the interaction
content: Cryogenic chilldown and boil-off directly impact the efficiency, safety and operational margins of any system that handles cryogenic fluids, including propulsion, storage and transfer applications. These processes arise from the interaction between wall heat transfer, boiling regimes, and vapor-space dynamics, and are strongly influenced by geometry, initial thermal conditions, and operating procedures. As a result, well-resolved experimental data remain essential for the development and validation of transient two-phase models. This work presents an experimental investigation of liquid nitrogen chilldown and boil-off in a small-scale test facility composed of two cryogenic vessels, a feed tank and a return tank, connected by a horizontal transfer line. The setup is instrumented to measure temperature evolution, pressure and liquid levels, under controlled valve operations. Wall heat fluxes and mass flow rates are derived from these measurements through energy and mass balances. The influence of initial thermal conditions is examined by comparing chilldown into a pre-cooled transfer line with that of an ambient-temperature configuration under unpressurized flow. To assess the role of the driving mechanism, both unpressurized and pressurized flow transfer conditions are then considered for an ambient temperature transfer line and return tank. Boil-off behavior in the feed tank is characterized at different liquid fill levels and further investigated through controlled heating using an immersed electrical heater. A quantitative mass and energy balance framework is used to reduce the measurements to transfer efficiency, thermodynamic minimum chilldown demand, residual losses, and closed tank energy contributions. The results demonstrate that while pressure-driven transfer shortens the time by more than an order of magnitude at the expense of liquid retention, pre-cooling increases the transfer efficiency and reduces wall enthalpy demand by approximately a factor of three. Over the examined fill level range, sensible heating of the liquid dominates the closed tank energy budget for boil-off, providing a quantitative basis for evaluating the effect of liquid inventory on subsequent thermal evolution and hold-time. These findings quantify the trade-off between transfer speed and cryogen consumption and provide an experimentally supported basis for selecting chilldown strategies under different time and inventory constraints.

title: Quantifying the near-term response of the ocean CO 2 sink to reduced atmospheric carbon concentrations
summary: The ocean plays a critical role in sequestering carbon, yet how the air–sea carbon sink will respond to rapid reductions in atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) concentrations remains a key uncertainty for climate mitigation and carbon accoun
content: The ocean plays a critical role in sequestering carbon, yet how the air–sea carbon sink will respond to rapid reductions in atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) concentrations remains a key uncertainty for climate mitigation and carbon accounting. In this study, we utilize the ECCO-Darwin ocean biogeochemistry model to simulate the ocean's response to a range of near-term CO 2 mitigation scenarios which are simulated with reduced atmospheric carbon concentrations. Our results demonstrate an immediate but spatially heterogeneous weakening of the ocean carbon sink following reduced atmospheric forcing. Global air–sea carbon uptake decreases substantially within the first several years of mitigation, with the magnitude of the reduction scaling with the strength of the mitigation scenario. We find that the mitigation signal is primarily confined to the upper-500 m, reflecting dominant decadal-scale ventilation pathways. The most pronounced reductions in uptake occur in subtropical thermocline regions, western boundary currents, and the subpolar North Atlantic – regions characterized by intense ventilation and rapid air–sea equilibration. These findings align with recent CMIP-based long-term projections and observation-based inversions, confirming that the areas currently dominating anthropogenic carbon uptake are also the most sensitive to atmospheric forcing changes. Our results suggest that observational efforts to track impacts from reduced atmospheric carbon levels should be prioritized in these high-latitude and boundary current systems, where signals emerge earliest and most strongly. Ultimately, this study underscores the high sensitivity of the ocean carbon sink to changes in atmospheric forcing and highlights the necessity of sustained, strategically-placed observations to detect and attribute changes in the global carbon budget under future climate strategies.

title: Evaporation-driven nanowire self-assembly in an elongated droplet
summary: Drying of nanowire-laden elongated droplets is a ubiquitous process in printed electronics fabrication, where the resulting deposition pattern critically determines device performance by controlling nanowire alignment, connectivity, and per
content: Drying of nanowire-laden elongated droplets is a ubiquitous process in printed electronics fabrication, where the resulting deposition pattern critically determines device performance by controlling nanowire alignment, connectivity, and percolating charge-transport pathways. However, the physical understanding of evaporation-driven deposition is still largely derived from studies of spherical droplets on homogeneous substrates. This gap limits the ability to predict and control deposit morphology in realistic printing scenarios. Here, we use mesoscale lattice Boltzmann simulations to investigate the drying of nanowire-laden elongated droplets on wettability-patterned substrates, focusing on the effects of droplet geometry, nanowire interactions, and nanowire length. The elongated droplet geometry is found to intrinsically induce distinct axial and transverse inhomogeneities in the final deposit. Increasing the effective attraction between nanowires, which mimics changes in surface chemistry or solvent conditions, can improve electrical connectivity but also promotes clustering and local ordering, reducing structural uniformity. In contrast, increasing nanowire length yields a dual benefit by improving long-range connectivity while simultaneously enhancing deposit homogeneity. Our findings provide design guidance for balancing electrical transport and structural uniformity in evaporation-driven printed electronics.

title: Marine particles as underexplored hotspots for antimicrobial peptide discovery: an ecology-guided frontier in marine natural product bioprospecting
summary: The increasing global antibiotic resistance has created a pressing need for new antimicrobial drugs. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) come into the spotlight for their antibacterial properties, particularly against multidrug-resistant pathogen
content: The increasing global antibiotic resistance has created a pressing need for new antimicrobial drugs. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) come into the spotlight for their antibacterial properties, particularly against multidrug-resistant pathogens. Because AMPs typically mediate localized interference competition, we hypothesize that spatially confined, highly competitive microbiomes create ecological conditions that favor the evolution, expression, and diversification of AMPs, although spatial structure may equally promote niche partitioning, cooperative interactions, and producer–resistant coexistence. We therefore propose, as a working hypothesis, that marine particles represent promising yet underexplored reservoirs of untapped marine AMPs. Marine particles are ubiquitous throughout the ocean, ranging from the sunlit surface waters to the deepest hadal environments. They are densely colonized microhabitats where nutrient gradients, spatial proximity, chemical signaling, and interspecies competition among microorganisms converge—unique characteristics that position marine particles as natural laboratories for the evolution of novel AMPs. However, most marine microorganisms are challenging to cultivate. Fortunately, metagenomics is greatly expanding the scope of marine AMP discovery by enabling researchers to screen for elusive peptide-encoding genes and complex biosynthetic gene clusters in uncultivated microbial communities. Additionally, advancements in artificial intelligence are further transforming marine AMP bioprospecting by moving from passive exploration to active molecular understanding and navigation. This review synthesizes our current understanding of the microbial ecology and emerging technologies that drive marine AMP discovery, and explores the application potentials of marine AMPs in human medicine, agriculture, and mariculture.

title: Empirical screening of sesamol, melatonin, and spermidine combinations on growth, biochemical composition, and antioxidant responses of Nitzschia closterium under low-salinity stress
summary: Low-salinity stress, frequently caused by spring rainfall and estuarine fluctuations, is a major constraint on the large-scale cultivation of marine diatoms and can disrupt their growth, photosynthesis, and carbon metabolism. Nitzschia clos
content: Low-salinity stress, frequently caused by spring rainfall and estuarine fluctuations, is a major constraint on the large-scale cultivation of marine diatoms and can disrupt their growth, photosynthesis, and carbon metabolism. Nitzschia closterium is a marine diatom with high nutritional value and strong potential for producing PUFAs such as EPA and DHA, and it is also widely used as a live feed in aquaculture. However, effective mitigation strategies for low-salinity stress in this species remain limited, and the effects of multiple exogenous regulators remain poorly understood. In this study, an L 9 (3 4 ) orthogonal design was used to evaluate nine combinations of sesamol (SL), melatonin (MT), and spermidine (SPD) on growth, biochemical composition, and antioxidant responses of N. closterium at salinity 5. Responses varied among the tested combinations and endpoints. Among the nine combinations, 30 mg·L −1 SL + 20 mg·L −1 MT + 150 mg·L −1 SPD (A 2 B 2 C 3 ) produced favorable results for several measured parameters, including higher total lipid (26.8%) and PUFA (55.28%) relative to the low-salinity control, as well as elevated SOD and CAT activities. The lowest MDA content among the additive treatments was observed under a different combination (A 2 B 1 C 2 ). Range analysis indicated that SPD had the strongest influence on growth rate, chlorophyll a, total lipid, EPA, PUFA, soluble sugar, and antioxidant enzyme activities within the tested matrix, whereas SL showed the largest range for MDA reduction and DHA. Because the orthogonal design contained only non-zero levels and did not include additive-free or single-additive treatments, the results are interpreted as an empirical comparison of the nine tested combinations rather than evidence of synergistic or coordinated action. Further dose-range expansion, independent verification, and cultivation-scale assessment are required before practical application can be recommended.

title: Role of defect trapping in the enhanced corrosion resistance of Ni–Mo alloys with yttrium and yttrium oxide additions
summary: Abstract Corrosion of structural alloys remains a critical challenge for advanced molten salt reactors, where aggressive fluoride salts promote continuous dissolution at the salt–metal interface. While most mitigation strategies emphasize t
content: Abstract Corrosion of structural alloys remains a critical challenge for advanced molten salt reactors, where aggressive fluoride salts promote continuous dissolution at the salt–metal interface. While most mitigation strategies emphasize thermodynamic stability, kinetic control of atomic transport has received comparatively less attention. Here, we propose a corrosion mitigation strategy based on diffusion control and vacancy trapping by dilute yttrium (Y) solutes and yttrium oxide (Y 2 O 3 ) dispersions in Ni alloys. A combined computational and experimental approach integrates density functional theory (DFT), self-consistent mean-field (SCMF) diffusion modeling, and an impurity trapping model to quantify the impact of defect trapping on effective vacancy mobility. Strong first-nearest-neighbor vacancy–Y binding, off-lattice vacancy configurations, and elevated rotational and dissociation barriers result in pronounced suppression of vacancy diffusivity, while Y 2 O 3 -associated sites treated as fixed traps in the model further reduce the mobile vacancy population. Ni–Mo (NM), Y-modified (NMY), and Y 2 O 3 -containing (NMYO) alloys were tested in molten fluoride salt at 750 ∘ C. Corrosion penetration decreases systematically from NM to NMY to NMYO, consistent with the predicted reduction in vacancy-mediated transport. The same trend is observed in mass change, with net weight loss decreasing from 0.52% for NM to 0.23% for NMY and 0.09% for NMYO. These results are consistent with an alloy-side transport contribution from defect trapping and reduced atomic transport. This study therefore suggests point defect engineering as a promising alloy design strategy for extreme nuclear environments.

title: Evaluating low-cost NDIR CO 2 sensors for atmospheric observations in rural settings
summary: Most research and monitoring activities involving low-cost atmospheric sensors (LC) have traditionally focused on urban environments, where air quality is a pressing concern. However, an emerging area of research is their application in rur
content: Most research and monitoring activities involving low-cost atmospheric sensors (LC) have traditionally focused on urban environments, where air quality is a pressing concern. However, an emerging area of research is their application in rural landscapes, where land use is a key determinant of climate change and net zero outcomes, directly influencing greenhouse gas emissions, carbon sequestration, and ecosystem functioning. In this study, we examine the use of LC non-dispersive infrared (NDIR) CO 2 sensors to monitor atmospheric mixing ratios in agricultural settings. We present a data analysis framework that addresses errors associated with factory auto-baseline correction and, crucially, accounts for the influence of environmental parameters such as temperature and pressure. This approach leads to improved sensor performance. Results from deployments in both rural and urban environments demonstrate strong agreement with reference-grade instruments, as shown by the root mean square error (RMSE) and coefficient of determination ( R 2 ). Improvements of RMSE from 10 to 4 ppm in winter and 5 to 4 ppm in summer, with corresponding improved R 2 from 0.85 to 0.98 in winter and 0.86 to 0.97 in summer were obtained when compared to a simple scaling correction of the out-of-box data. Our study shows that corrected data not only reproduced the seasonal profile associated with rural emissions, but it also captured the diurnal variability, sometimes characterised by CO 2 change of up to 50 ppm, which is more than three times the typical change in the urban environment (15 ppm). Overall, this study establishes that field calibrated low-cost CO 2 sensors and sensor networks can provide reliable, long-term atmospheric monitoring in rural environments when sensor enclosures are appropriately designed to ensure adequate ventilation and air exchange, thereby preventing moisture accumulation. The observations obtained provide valuable inputs for developing analytical methodologies and offer actionable insights into the influence of rural land-use practices on climate.

title: Effects of Ground Tire Rubber and Trans-Polyoctenamer on the Rheological Properties and Aging Response of Asphalt Binders
summary: Abstract The sustainable management of end-of-life tires represents a persistent environmental challenge, with declining recycling rates leading to increased landfilling and associated ecological risks. This research aligns with the confere
content: Abstract The sustainable management of end-of-life tires represents a persistent environmental challenge, with declining recycling rates leading to increased landfilling and associated ecological risks. This research aligns with the conference theme by presenting a waste-to-resource pathway that transforms ground tire rubber (GTR) into a high-value modifier for asphalt binders, simultaneously addressing waste diversion and infrastructure performance needs. With transportation agencies increasingly specifying higher performance grades such as PG 82 − 22 for demanding applications, this study investigates whether elevated dosages of GTR can serve as a primary, sustainable modifier to meet these specifications. Through a comprehensive experimental program, base binders (PG 64 − 22 and polymer-modified PG 76 − 22) were modified with GTR contents ranging from 10% to 15% and 3% to 8%, respectively, both with and without the compatibility agent trans-polyoctenamer (TOR). Advanced rheological testing using DSR and BBR coupled with chemical characterization via FTIR spectroscopy, evaluated performance and aging characteristics. Results demonstrate that a 15% GTR dosage successfully elevates the high-temperature grade of a base binder from PG 64 to PG 82, achieving the target specification while maintaining critical low-temperature performance. The incorporation of GTR significantly enhanced rutting resistance and elastic response, with the hybrid use of TOR further improving binder compatibility and long-term durability. Critically, this approach can increase the consumption of recycled tire rubber in asphalt by over 50% compared to conventional practice. This study concludes that high-dosage GTR modification presents a technically viable and environmentally strategic method to produce superior asphalt binders. It provides a direct, scalable pathway to enhance the circular economy for scrap tires, reduce reliance on virgin polymer modifiers, and support the development of sustainable, high-performance infrastructure. The findings offer actionable insights for policymakers, material developers, and transportation agencies seeking to integrate waste recycling objectives with advanced engineering performance.

title: Field site-specific proteome remodeling under contrasting environmental conditions in Brassica rapa
summary: BACKGROUND: Plant plasticity enables adaptation to heterogeneous environments, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying long-term climatic acclimation in crops remain insufficiently understood. Here, we investigated the proteome plasticity o
content: BACKGROUND: Plant plasticity enables adaptation to heterogeneous environments, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying long-term climatic acclimation in crops remain insufficiently understood. Here, we investigated the proteome plasticity of Brassica rapa across three contrasting field sites representing subarctic (68°N), temperate (59°N), and subtropical (44°N) climate-associated conditions. Twelve accessions spanning three crop types were cultivated, and subjected to proteome analysis and protein-metabolite correlation analysis. RESULTS: Principal component and clustering analyses revealed a strong imprint of the field sites on proteome patterns. Functional enrichment analysis identified site-specific protein networks: subarctic conditions favored enrichment of proteins involved in photosynthesis, carbohydrate metabolism, and glycolysis, supporting energy capture and cold acclimation; temperate conditions induced proteins related to respiration and redox homeostasis; and subtropical conditions induced proteins involved in clade-specific metabolism, particularly glucosinolate biosynthesis, alongside amino acid and redox pathways. Based on proteome data, key adaptive responses to the three field sites included modulation of cellular respiration proteins, such as NADH dehydrogenase subunits, and shifts in phytohormone regulation, with cytokinins enriched under subarctic, gibberellin-regulated proteins under temperate, and auxin-associated proteins under subtropical conditions. Chinese cabbage accession A247 demonstrated the highest proteome plasticity, whereas root turnip accessions showed lower plasticity. Reaction-norm analyses across the latitudinal climate gradient revealed genotype and crop type dependent trajectories in mean protein Z-scores, which shows contrasting adaptive strategies across cultivars. CONCLUSIONS: B. rapa shows strong proteomic flexibility across different field sites, indicating distinct metabolic adjustments. These findings suggest that proteomic profiling aids in identifying adaptive traits and could guide crop breeding strategies to improve resilience under future climate change.

title: Marine Biological Diversity and the Law of the Sea: A Comprehensive Legal Guide to the BBNJ Agreement
summary: This book provides a comprehensive and practical legal guide to the Agreement under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas Beyond National Jurisdic
content: This book provides a comprehensive and practical legal guide to the Agreement under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ Agreement). Adopted in 2023, this landmark instrument marks a pivotal development in the law of the sea, addressing significant regulatory, governance and institutional gaps in the international law framework for the protection of marine biological diversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction. The book offers an in-depth examination of the BBNJ Agreement’s four key pillars: marine genetic resources, including the fair and equitable sharing of benefits, measures such as area-based management tools, including marine protected areas, environmental impact assessments and finally, capacity-building and marine technology transfer. It critically evaluates the Agreement’s structure, provisions and enforceability while also exploring its relationship with existing international resource and environmental governance regimes. With a strong emphasis on practical implementation, this book considers the legal, administrative and institutional measures required for States Parties to comply with their obligations. It offers guidance on national implementation strategies, including the enactment of implementing legislation, institutional coordination and mechanisms for regional and international cooperation. Additionally, it discusses compliance, monitoring and enforcement challenges and identifies pathways towards effective governance. Providing a comprehensive overview of this important development in international law, this book will be of interest to students and academics of the law of the sea, marine environmental law and biodiversity law. This book will also be of particular assistance to policymakers and their legal advisors within government who will bear the task of implementing the BBNJ Agreement, as well as researchers interested in ocean governance and sustainable development.

title: Deficit Irrigation Combined with Jeevamrutha-Based Nutrient Management Enhances Rhizosphere Microbial Abundance, Agronomic Performance, and Economic Returns of African Marigold Under Semi-Arid Conditions
summary: Abstract Sustainable floriculture in semi-arid regions needs irrigation and nutrient management that conserve water and soil biological function, yet whether deficit irrigation and organic biostimulation act additively or interactively on r
content: Abstract Sustainable floriculture in semi-arid regions needs irrigation and nutrient management that conserve water and soil biological function, yet whether deficit irrigation and organic biostimulation act additively or interactively on rhizosphere microbiology remains untested. This two-season (2023–2025) split-plot trial grew African marigold (Tagetes erecta L.) under three irrigation levels (full, I₁, 1.0 ETc; mild deficit, I₂, 0.8 ETc; moderate deficit, I₃, 0.6 ETc) crossed with four nitrogen regimes: a fully chemical dose (N₁) and Jeevamrutha meeting 100% (N₂), 75% (N₃) or 50% (N₄) of crop nitrogen, with supplementary chemical P and K. Moderate deficit gave the highest rhizosphere bacterial, fungal and actinomycete counts (6.67 × 10⁷, 3.99 × 10⁵ and 2.92 × 10⁶ cfu g⁻¹), 11.5–11.9% above full irrigation; full Jeevamrutha-N substitution raised these counts 26.9–27.8% above chemical fertiliser, with a significant irrigation × nutrient interaction. These responses accompanied improved performance: moderate deficit gave the tallest plants (67.72 cm), longest longevity (22.17 days) and highest yield (14.76 t ha⁻¹), while full Jeevamrutha-N gave the widest canopy (47.74 cm) and highest yield (14.98 t ha⁻¹). Their combination (I₃N₂) ranked highest overall (16,909 kg ha⁻¹ yield, ₹3.38 lakh ha⁻¹ gross and over ₹2.21 lakh ha⁻¹ net returns, and a benefit–cost ratio of 1.90) while cutting seasonal irrigation by 38.6%. Deficit irrigation thus amplified, not merely coexisted with, the response to Jeevamrutha nutrition. By advancing water conservation (SDG 6), reduced synthetic-input use (SDG 12) and soil biological health (SDG 15), the approach offers a scalable pathway to sustainable, water- and input-efficient floriculture.

title: Small Diameter and Decreased Radial Growth Control Pinus palustris Tropical Cyclone Damage in Georgia, USA
summary: Abstract Traditional correlative analyses often struggle to parse the confounding drivers of storm damage in forested systems. To address this limitation, this study utilized a causal inference framework to separate broad observational tren
content: Abstract Traditional correlative analyses often struggle to parse the confounding drivers of storm damage in forested systems. To address this limitation, this study utilized a causal inference framework to separate broad observational trends from underlying biological mechanisms. We applied a non-parametric causal forest algorithm to evaluate how diameter at breast height (DBH) and DBH growth rates influenced tree-level damage probabilities in even-aged longleaf pine ( Pinus palustris Mill.) plantations following Hurricane Helene (2024). The data were from two contrasting sites, an old-field and a cutover plantation, in Berrien County, Georgia, USA, ranging from 5 to 24 cm DBH. Pre-tropical cyclone correlative analysis showed that the old-field site possessed greater aboveground productivity, like increased DBH, height, volume, and basal area. Post-cyclone analysis revealed that while aboveground trends remained, the old-field site suffered a 17% reduction in stand density. While a simple correlative assessment would likely attribute this decline entirely to the vulnerability of larger trees, the causal forest model parsed a more nuanced storm damage response. Specifically, smaller trees (< 12 cm DBH; 1.69 to 8.06 m height) demonstrated high sensitivity to moderate stem damage, while larger, slower-growing individuals (> 12 cm DBH; 10.09 to 12.17 m height) were more susceptible to severe stem failure. These results highlight proactive density management - specifically tailored to maintain increased individual tree growth rates - as a critical tool for building wind resilience in southern pine plantations. Additionally, causal inference applied to site-intensive inventory data provided a precise, data-centered understanding of storm-induced mortality dynamics.

title: A numerical approach of reactive MHD casson ternary hybrid nanofluid flow over an extended surface with activation energy
summary: The increasing demand for innovative heat and mass transfer technologies in thermal management, energy systems, and permeable transport applications has motivated growing interest in Ternary hybrid nanofluid. Although previous studies have
content: The increasing demand for innovative heat and mass transfer technologies in thermal management, energy systems, and permeable transport applications has motivated growing interest in Ternary hybrid nanofluid. Although previous studies have investigated MHD non-Newtonian nanofluids, THNFs, and porous-medium transport, the combined effects of Casson rheology, ternary hybrids nanoparticles, Darcy-Forchheimer resistance, slip conditions, thermal radiation, variable thermal conductivity, heat generation, activation energy, and chemical reaction have received limited attention. This study therefore investigates the steady 2-dimensional MHD flow and coupled heat and mass transfer of a Casson THNF over a permeable stretching surface, providing an integrated framework for examining the collective effect of these physical machines. Similarities transformation is applied to reduce the governing PDEs to a nonlinear system of odes, which is disentangled numerically using the MATLAB bvp4cC scheme. The results show that the magnetic parameter, Darcy resistance, and Forchheimer parameter suppress the velocity field, whereas the Casson and velocity-slip parameters enhance the wall shear response. Thermal radiation, heat generation, and variable thermal conductivity increase the temperature distribution, while thermal slip reduces it. The concentration profile declines with growing Schmidt number, activation-energy parameter, and chemical-reaction parameter. The skin-friction coefficient, Nusselt number, and Sherwood number are also significantly influenced by the governing parameters, particularly by magnetic and permeable-medium effects. The numerical results are validated against established benchmark solutions, demonstrating good agreement. The findings afford new intuition into the coupled hydrodynamic, thermal, and mass-transfer behavior of Casson THNFs in permeable stretching-surface systems, with potential relevance to innovative thermal-management and transport applications.

title: Protease‐Activated Theranostic Nanomedicine for Endometriosis Treatment
summary: ABSTRACT Endometriosis is a chronic gynecological disorder characterized by ectopic growth of endometrial tissue and is associated with pelvic pain and infertility. Here, we identify aberrant matrix metalloproteinase‐9 (MMP‐9) overexpressio
content: ABSTRACT Endometriosis is a chronic gynecological disorder characterized by ectopic growth of endometrial tissue and is associated with pelvic pain and infertility. Here, we identify aberrant matrix metalloproteinase‐9 (MMP‐9) overexpression in endometriotic lesions and develop a novel nanomedicine that integrates MMP‐9‐targeted therapy, ratiometric photoacoustic (PA) imaging, and controlled drug delivery to improve endometriosis diagnosis and treatment. We design MMP‐9‐cleavable peptide‐functionalized nanoparticles that produce turn‐on imaging signals upon enzymatic activation by MMP‐9, enabling sensitive and specific visualization of endometriotic lesions. Comprehensive in vitro and in vivo studies validate the responsiveness of the nanoparticles to MMP‐9 activity, with inhibitor assays confirming MMP‐9‐dependent specificity. In vivo PA imaging demonstrates precise localization and real‐time monitoring of endometriotic lesions, findings further corroborated by ex vivo tissue analyses using near‐infrared fluorescence imaging. Importantly, these peptide‐based nanoparticles serve as carriers for the targeted delivery of letrozole (LTZ), a potent therapeutic agent, allowing selective drug release via MMP‐9‐mediated enzymatic activity within endometriotic lesions. This targeted delivery enhanced the therapeutic efficacy of LTZ while minimizing its systemic side effects and toxicity. Collectively, our integrated theranostic nanoplatform enables simultaneous diagnosis and targeted therapy of endometriosis, highlighting the potential of MMP‐9‐responsive nanotherapeutics combined with advanced imaging for precision medicine in gynecological disorders.

title: Stoichiometric characteristics and environmental drivers of soil in estuarine delta wetlands: a case study of the Yellow River Delta
summary: Estuarine delta wetlands are relatively fragile ecosystems, and soil ecological stoichiometry plays an important role in understanding wetland ecological conditions and developing effective restoration and sustainable management strategies.
content: Estuarine delta wetlands are relatively fragile ecosystems, and soil ecological stoichiometry plays an important role in understanding wetland ecological conditions and developing effective restoration and sustainable management strategies. However, the spatial patterns of soil ecological stoichiometric characteristics and their relationships with environmental factors in estuarine delta wetlands remain insufficiently understood. In this study, we investigated soil physicochemical properties and ecological stoichiometric ratios (ESR) across gradients of soil salinity (Sa), bulk density (BD), and distance to shoreline (DTS) in the Yellow River Delta (YRD) wetland, and explored their associations with environmental factors. The results showed that soil physicochemical properties and ESR exhibited significant spatial heterogeneity. With increasing soil salinity, the contents of total carbon (TC), total nitrogen (TN), and total phosphorus (TP) significantly decreased, whereas the C:N ratio increased and the C:P and N:P ratios decreased ( P < 0.05). With increasing soil bulk density, TC and TN contents significantly declined, accompanied by an increase in C:N and decreases in C:P and N:P ratios ( P < 0.05). Along the DTS gradient, soil nutrient contents increased, C:N decreased, and N:P increased. Nearshore soils exhibited a “low nutrient-high stoichiometric ratio” pattern, whereas offshore soils showed a “high nutrient-low stoichiometric ratio” pattern. C and N contents were identified as important factors associated with variations in soil ecological stoichiometry along the DTS gradient. SEM further revealed significant associations between soil environmental factors and ecological stoichiometric characteristics, indicating that environmental gradients were closely linked to the spatial variation in soil ecological stoichiometry across the YRD wetland. This study elucidates the spatial variability of soil ecological stoichiometric characteristics and their relationships with environmental factors in the YRD wetland, providing scientific support for soil assessment, ecological restoration, and sustainable management of estuarine delta wetlands.

title: AI-assisted synthesis reveals hidden cross-scale degradation in global mangrove ecosystems under human pressure
summary: Abstract Recent satellite evidence shows that global mangrove extent, after a net loss of ~ 2,900 km² between the 1980s and 2010, has since rebounded by ~ 2,000 km², largely through natural seaward expansion and regeneration. Yet this spati
content: Abstract Recent satellite evidence shows that global mangrove extent, after a net loss of ~ 2,900 km² between the 1980s and 2010, has since rebounded by ~ 2,000 km², largely through natural seaward expansion and regeneration. Yet this spatial recovery does not necessarily imply the recovery of biodiversity or ecosystem functioning. Satellites record where mangroves grow and species inventories record which organisms persist, but neither captures how plant physiology or metabolism respond to human and climatic pressures beneath the canopy. These responses are measured in thousands of local field and experimental studies, but they remain scattered and unsynthesized at global scale, and pooling them manually has reached practical limits in scalability and traceability. Here, using a human-in-the-loop Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline, we screened 9,097 articles and built the Quantitative Global Mangrove Biodiversity Risk Database (QGMBRD), compiling 343 independent effect sizes (log response ratios of impacted versus reference conditions) from 6,744 driver-specific studies, spanning landscape to microbial scales under climate change, land-use change, pollution and biological invasion. Despite a nearly fivefold increase in mangrove biodiversity research between 2001 and 2025 (from 1,320 to 6,288 publications). The spatial multilevel meta-analysis further reveals consistent negative responses from macroscopic landscapes to microscopic processes. Crucially, relying solely on traditional taxonomic metrics can yield false-negative conclusions of stability where evidence is scarce and noisy. By contrast, functional metabolic and physiological indicators robustly capture significant degradation and reveal a heavier tail of extreme decline—28.8% of functional observations exceed critical degradation thresholds (|LnRR| > 1), compared with 20.5% for taxonomic metrics. Thus, recent spatial recovery should not be equated with recovery of ecological integrity, global monitoring frameworks must integrate cross-scale functional indicators to diagnose hidden biological impairment. Broadly, our human-centric, AI-augmented framework improves the scalability and traceability of cross-scale ecological evidence synthesis.

title: Effects of mulched drip irrigation on phenological development of spring maize
summary: Based on a field experiment conducted at a fixed site over eight years (2015~2022) in arid northwest China, this study quantified how mulched drip irrigation (DI) and mulched border irrigation (BI) alter spring maize phenology through chang
content: Based on a field experiment conducted at a fixed site over eight years (2015~2022) in arid northwest China, this study quantified how mulched drip irrigation (DI) and mulched border irrigation (BI) alter spring maize phenology through changes in canopy temperature, soil temperature and soil water content. Compared with BI, DI raised the average canopy temperature by 0.72 °C, soil temperature by 1.0 °C and soil water content by 3.4%. The improved microenvironment significantly shortened the seedling and maturity stages. The total growing season declined by 11.44 d on average. The durations of the jointing, heading and filling stages were unaffected. Multiple regression that included the interaction between temperature and water revealed a significant positive interaction between canopy temperature and soil water content. A larger difference in soil water amplified the advance of crop development driven by temperature and partly offset the shortening of the growth period caused by warming. Over the eight years, DI increased average biomass, grain yield and water use efficiency by 4.96%, 11.78% and 27.57%, respectively. Overall, DI optimizes field hydrothermal conditions, advances maize phenology and improves crop productivity. It offers a feasible irrigation strategy for saving water in arid agricultural regions.

title: Gut-derived circulating bacterial vesicles reduce systemic carbapenem exposure and sustain extraintestinal infections
summary: Abstract Infections frequently persist despite appropriate antibiotic therapy against susceptible pathogens. While unexplained treatment failure is typically linked to the pathogen itself or the local infection environment, we show that spa
content: Abstract Infections frequently persist despite appropriate antibiotic therapy against susceptible pathogens. While unexplained treatment failure is typically linked to the pathogen itself or the local infection environment, we show that spatially distinct colonized resistant populations can undermine systemic therapy. In a 1,028-patient cohort, fecal colonization with carbapenem-resistant Escherichia coli (CREC) independently compromised carbapenem efficacy against susceptible extraintestinal Enterobacterales. Mechanistically, CREC secretes the carbapenemase NDM exclusively via outer membrane vesicles (OMVs). Following intestinal barrier injury, NDM-loaded OMVs translocate into the circulation. These circulating vesicles resist plasma inactivation and accelerate systemic carbapenem clearance, dropping effective drug exposure below therapeutic thresholds to rescue distant susceptible pathogens without genetic transfer. This protection requires porin-mediated antibiotic entry into OMVs and is amplified by carbapenem exposure, which increases vesicles release and enriches NDM cargo. NDM-stable aztreonam-avibactam and non-β-lactam amikacin bypass this vesicle sink and retain in vivo efficacy. Thus, gut microbiota resistance acts as a remote pharmacological sink via circulating bacterial vesicles, compromising antibiotic therapy against distant susceptible pathogens.

title: Storying Salicornia: Cuisines, Coastlines and Salty Futures in Europe
summary: This article focuses on the cultural lives of the saline plant salicornia and its entanglement with cuisines, nature conservation and market dynamics across European coastlines. A succulent native to salt marshes, beaches and other brackish
content: This article focuses on the cultural lives of the saline plant salicornia and its entanglement with cuisines, nature conservation and market dynamics across European coastlines. A succulent native to salt marshes, beaches and other brackish ecosystems, salicornia has a long history of being foraged; throughout the 2010s and early 2020s, it has evolved into a gourmet ingredient, resulting in its commercial cultivation. Yet the plant’s growth, harvesting and commercial availability are all threaded through with complex interrelations between coastal communities, their environments and their envisioned futures. Using case studies from culinary nature conservation and climate justice activism in Venice, Italy, and Burgas, Bulgaria, we show how salicornia comes to embody the strategies communities employ to affirm and uphold their stakes in their coastal wetland landscapes. In this way, our own rendition of salicornia offers a fusion of blue humanities, food cultural history and both critical plant and conservation studies.

title: Advances in technologies across the marine plastic value chain in Europe: A critical review
summary: Marine Plastic Pollution (MPP) is widely recognised as a significant global challenge, driven by unsustainable plastic production, ineffective waste management, and the long-term persistence of plastics in marine environments. MPP has becom
content: Marine Plastic Pollution (MPP) is widely recognised as a significant global challenge, driven by unsustainable plastic production, ineffective waste management, and the long-term persistence of plastics in marine environments. MPP has become increasingly widespread across oceans, along coastlines and on the seafloor, resulting in an urgent need for the development of technologies capable of advancing a Circular Economy (CE) for marine-derived products. Advances in cleaner production technologies, including satellite and drone-based remote sensing, autonomous robotic platforms, and machine-vision systems, have improved the efficiency of plastic debris identification, classification, and recovery in complex marine environments. Similarly, innovations in downstream sorting, such as electrostatic separation, selective dissolution, hyperspectral imaging (HSI), and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven classification, are enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of processing MPP. The review evaluates mechanical recycling methods with particular emphasis on recent advances in extrusion, moulding technologies, and additive manufacturing for converting MPP into high-value secondary materials in a CE framework in Europe. These technological developments demonstrate the potential for establishing viable and scalable valorisation routes. Overall, the review outlines key opportunities to strengthen a sustainable CE and guide future research and industrial adoption. In doing so, it provides a comprehensive examination of state-of-the-art technologies across the entire marine plastics value chain in Europe, from detection and recovery to separation, identification, and recycling.

title: AI-driven entropy analysis of Sutterby tetra-hybrid nanofluid energy conversion for electromagnetic peristaltic flow
summary: Predicting nano-blood transport in electromagnetically actuated peristaltic microchannels requires solving coupled nonlinear equations for momentum, energy, mass, and microorganism conservation a computationally expensive task when Hall and
content: Predicting nano-blood transport in electromagnetically actuated peristaltic microchannels requires solving coupled nonlinear equations for momentum, energy, mass, and microorganism conservation a computationally expensive task when Hall and ion-slip effects, thermal radiation, viscous dissipation, entropy generation, and Sutterby non-Newtonian rheology are all included, limiting real-time clinical use. This study addresses that bottleneck by developing a Levenberg-Marquardt optimized artificial neural network (ANN-LM) trained on 2,400 high-fidelity datasets generated from the governing Multiphysics equations, to predict velocity, temperature, concentration, and microorganism distributions for a Sutterby tetra-hybrid nanofluid. The ANN-LM achieves mean absolute errors below 0.3% and correlation coefficients near unity across all fields, while reducing computational cost by more than two orders of magnitude relative to direct numerical solution. By coupling deep learning with electromagnetic-rheological-bioconvective modeling for the first time in this configuration, the framework enables millisecond-scale parametric exploration and inverse design previously infeasible with conventional solvers offering a practical route toward real-time, patient-specific control in magnetically guided drug delivery, cardiovascular interventions, and microfluidic diagnostic platforms.

title: Optimizing sap sampling methodologies for nutrient diagnostics in lettuce and tomato grown under controlled environment agriculture
summary: Effective nutrient management is crucial for maintaining growth and yield in controlled environment agriculture (CEA). However, nutrient interpretation depends on sampling methodology, and standardized sampling protocols for sap analysis re
content: Effective nutrient management is crucial for maintaining growth and yield in controlled environment agriculture (CEA). However, nutrient interpretation depends on sampling methodology, and standardized sampling protocols for sap analysis remain inconsistent. This study evaluated five key sap-sampling methods: leaf number, tissue age, tissue part (only for tomatoes, Solanum lycopersicum L.), collection time, and sampling frequency, to establish sampling protocols for hydroponic lettuce ( Lactuca sativa ) and tomato in CEA. A split-plot design with repeated measures was employed using three cultivars per crop, and nutrient concentrations were analyzed within each cultivar using linear mixed-effects models with treatment, stage, and their interaction (treatment × stage), with rep included as a random effect. Two sap-extraction methods were employed: mechanical tissue crushing (TC) and potassium chloride (KCl) extraction. Nutrient leaf analysis (NLA) was subsequently used as the comparative reference method representing total tissue nutrient status. In lettuce, sampling effects were generally modest and nutrient- and cultivar-specific, and responses were frequently not conserved between TC and KCl. Effects of leaf number were more evident under KCl extraction than under TC. Tissue-age effects were present but expressed differently by extraction method; time-of-collection effects were small and inconsistent, and stage effects over the short cycle, 12 vs. 24 days after transplantation (DAT), were limited and method-dependent. In tomatoes, sampling effects were stronger and more structured. The number of leaves interacted with the developmental stage, and sap inorganic N consistently showed a leaf number × stage interaction across cultivars under both TC and KCl, indicating that leaf number must remain constant across DAT for valid interpretation. Tissue age produced strong separation with cultivar-specific age × stage interaction patterns across methods, and in tissue part, we found part × stage interactions, confirming that blade and petiole sap are not interchangeable. Sampling frequency affected tomato sap nutrient profiles across 63–253 DAT, with TC capturing short-term nutrient pools and KCl more clearly reflecting long-term enrichment patterns.

title: Potential therapeutic strategies targeting ferroptosis in chronic diabetic wounds
summary: Chronic diabetic wounds, most commonly presenting as diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs), represent one of the most devastating complications of diabetes mellitus. They affect a large proportion of diabetic patients worldwide and are associated wit
content: Chronic diabetic wounds, most commonly presenting as diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs), represent one of the most devastating complications of diabetes mellitus. They affect a large proportion of diabetic patients worldwide and are associated with elevated risks of non-traumatic lower limb amputation, high mortality, and substantial socioeconomic burden. Many affected patients fail to achieve complete wound closure following standard-of-care treatment, highlighting a critical unmet need for novel mechanism-driven therapeutic targets. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death (RCD) driven by the lethal accumulation of lipid peroxides, has emerged in recent years as a key pathogenic mechanism underlying impaired diabetic wound repair. Ferroptosis is defined by glutathione depletion, intracellular iron overload, and unrestrained lipid peroxidation. This review synthesizes current evidence regarding the regulatory mechanisms of ferroptosis, with a particular focus on its detrimental effects on the four major wound-repair-associated cell populations involved in cutaneous wound healing. Furthermore, we delineate the pathological alterations in chronic diabetic wounds that sensitize cells to ferroptosis. Ferroptosis-related biomarkers that may have clinical utility for predicting wound healing prognosis and monitoring therapeutic responses were also evaluated. A central emphasis of this review is placed on emerging anti-ferroptotic therapeutic strategies for diabetic wounds, accompanied by a critical appraisal of their preclinical efficacy and translational potential. Finally, we discuss prevailing challenges in the field and propose future research directions to accelerate the clinical translation of ferroptosis-targeted therapies for chronic diabetic wounds.

title: Missed Opportunities Forgo One-Third of Mass Timber’s Carbon Storage Potential
summary: Abstract Building materials are increasingly positioned as a scalable option for carbon dioxide removal (CDR). Carbon-storing engineered wood products, such as structural mass timber, will be instrumental for CDR. However, system-level pers
content: Abstract Building materials are increasingly positioned as a scalable option for carbon dioxide removal (CDR). Carbon-storing engineered wood products, such as structural mass timber, will be instrumental for CDR. However, system-level perspectives can overlook operational choices that forfeit storage potential. Using stage-resolved life-cycle inventories, scenario-aware uncertainty analysis, and dynamic carbon accounting, we trace carbon flows across mass timber supply chains in the United States, from harvest slash and mill residue to wood products through end-of-life. Across modeled deployment scenarios, we show that management decisions, not technical limits, cut 1.4–2.6 gigatons (Gt) of CO2e storage by 2120, corresponding to roughly one-third of mass timber’s storage potential. Globally, storage losses from these choices could reach 3.8–12 Gt CO2e. We outline a storage-first pathway including slash pyrolysis, diversion of mill residue from bioenergy to wood panel markets, and reuse or pyrolysis at end-of-life. Together, these strategies redirect carbon into value-added, long-lived pools rather than short-lived fates, showing that release timing and supply chain routing choices can matter more than production decarbonization in shaping warming outcomes under mass timber deployment. If implemented, these choices recover forgone storage and aid in developing the built environment as a durable carbon reservoir.

title: Influence of injection mode and hydrogen enrichment on in-cylinder phenomena in CNG/HCNG engines: a simulation study
summary: This study compares CNG and HCNG combustion under direct and indirect injection using high-fidelity CFD simulations in a standard spark-ignition engine model. The objective is to understand how injection mode and hydrogen enrichment affect
content: This study compares CNG and HCNG combustion under direct and indirect injection using high-fidelity CFD simulations in a standard spark-ignition engine model. The objective is to understand how injection mode and hydrogen enrichment affect in-cylinder thermodynamics, mixture formation, heat release, and emissions in order to identify configurations that improve efficiency while managing nitrogen oxides (NOx) and other pollutants. Four fuel/injection configurations are examined: CNG-DI, CNG-IDI, HCNG-DI, and HCNG-IDI in a 1.6 MPI engine, a compression ratio of 14:1, and a swept volume of 1598 cc. In this engine, we applied CNG mass of 4.96496 mg and hydrogen mass corresponding to 20% in HCNG, i.e., 0.23504 mg. The governing mass, momentum, energy, and species equations are solved with detailed chemistry to capture ignition delay, flame propagation, and combustion stability. Key performance indicators include cylinder pressure and temperature histories, heat release rate (HRR), mean heat transfer coefficient (HTC) at the piston head, combustion fluctuation, and emissions indices (CO₂, NO) across the crank-angle range. The results show that direct injection (DI) yields faster energy release, higher peak pressures, and higher peak temperatures due to improved local mixing and earlier flame development. Hydrogen enrichment (HCNG) amplifies these effects. HCNG-DI exhibits the most significant pressure increase, the earliest and highest peak temperatures (approximately 1900–2000 K), and the highest HRR. Conversely, IDI produces a smoother energy release with lower peak pressures and broader ignition timing sensitivity. This offers enhanced operability and reduced carbon buildup, though it typically results in lower peak efficiency. HCNG-IDI increases NO formation due to extended high-temperature residence and stronger heat release; however, CO₂ production also increases, indicating improved combustion completeness under HCNG. These findings inform engine design regarding injection strategies and hydrogen enrichment, guiding the timing, duration, and spray characteristics for various operating conditions. The study underscores the importance of simulation-driven evaluations in selecting DI or IDI configurations and HCNG blending levels to balance power output, emissions, and reliability in future clean vehicle applications.

title: Effects of pre-harvest foliar application of plant-regulating substances and their combinations on fruit development and quality formation in blueberry
summary: To explore the effects of different plant-regulating substances (including classical plant growth regulators [PGRs], nutrients, biostimulants, and metabolic precursors) and their combinations on flower-fruit transition, fruit development, r
content: To explore the effects of different plant-regulating substances (including classical plant growth regulators [PGRs], nutrients, biostimulants, and metabolic precursors) and their combinations on flower-fruit transition, fruit development, ripening progression, and quality formation of blueberry, a field experiment was conducted on blueberry cultivar L25 at a planting base located at 23.4771°N, 103.2510°E with an altitude of 1300 m. All field treatments were arranged in a randomized complete block design with three biological replicates. Four functional categories of exogenous treatments, encompassing nutrition and biostimulation, vegetative growth promotion, ripening modulation, and quality regulation, were established with both single-agent and compound combinations. The study consisted of two experimental phases: screening individual substances at varying concentrations, and evaluating formulated combinations. All reagents were applied via foliar spraying during the key flower and young fruit developmental stages with conventional diluted concentrations suitable for blueberry cultivation. Plant growth, floral and fruit developmental traits, fruit morphological parameters, and internal nutritional attributes were comprehensively evaluated, including chlorophyll content, flower quantity, fruit population dynamics, fruit size, single fruit weight, fruit shape index, soluble solids, titratable acid, anthocyanins, and ascorbic acid (vitamin C) content. The results indicated that different plant-regulating treatments exhibited distinct regulatory performances in modulating blueberry flower-fruit transition, fruit enlargement, color maturation, and quality formation. Naphthalene acetic acid (NAA) and chitooligosaccharides produced consistent effects on regulating fruit longitudinal and transverse growth as well as fruit weight. Forchlorfenuron (CPPU), diethyl aminoethyl hexanoate (CSN-DA-6), and paclobutrazol improved single fruit weight and soluble solid accumulation, and CPPU exerted a relatively stronger promoting effect on fruit morphogenesis. Ethephon, sodium nitrophenolate, and cyanamide mainly promoted fruit ripening and anthocyanin accumulation, while most of these treatments failed to maintain stable ascorbic acid (vitamin C) levels in mature fruits. In comparison, thidiazuron, gibberellic acid, and 24-epibrassinolide comprehensively improved fruit appearance and nutritional performance, and 24-epibrassinolide showed favorable performance in balancing soluble solids and titratable acidity. Each treatment or combination displayed trait-specific regulatory advantages without universal superiority across all measured indices. Combination Treatment 2 exhibited preferable performance in optimizing fruit dimensional traits and single fruit weight. Overall, the selection of plant-regulating substances should be tailored to specific growth stages and cultivation objectives to achieve uniform fruit ripening and high-quality berry production.

title: Ecological Health Assessment in a Sub-Tropical Lake: Integrating Water Quality Index with Multivariate Statistical Methods
summary: Abstract This study provides a comprehensive ecological health assessment of Bangladesh's Kaptai Lake through an integrated analysis of physicochemical and biological parameters across pre-monsoon, monsoon, and post-monsoon seasons. Data fr
content: Abstract This study provides a comprehensive ecological health assessment of Bangladesh's Kaptai Lake through an integrated analysis of physicochemical and biological parameters across pre-monsoon, monsoon, and post-monsoon seasons. Data from five monitoring stations revealed significant seasonal variations, with the pre-monsoon period characterized by peaks in NH₃ (0.16 ± 0.04 mg L − 1 ), phytoplankton density (14.28 ± 1.52×10⁵cells L − 1 ), and gross primary production (3.38 ± 0.30 g C m − ² d − 1 ), while post-monsoon exhibited maximum DO (6.56 ± 0.27 mg L − 1 ) and conductivity (112.6 ± 12.57 µS cm − 1 ). Spatial analysis identified distinct gradients, including significantly higher DO at Langadu (7.05 ± 0.46 mg L − 1 , p < 0.01) and WQI values indicated comparatively poorer water quality conditions at Naniarchar, although spatial differences were not statistically significant. Multivariate analysis identified mineralization and productivity gradients as major sources of environmental variability, with the first two principal components explaining 46.8–60.1% of the total variance. Ecosystem health assessment using the Direct Measurement Method (DMM) ranked post-monsoon conditions as the most favorable, with Kaptai Dam station maintaining the healthiest balance (Bz/Bp = 0.48, structural Exergy = 28.32 MJ mg − 1 ). Overall, WQI indicated generally favorable water quality conditions for aquatic life. The successful application of WQI coupled with DMM indicators demonstrates that the lake is seasonally influenced by anthropogenic activities, highlighting the critical need for targeted management strategies to mitigate seasonal water quality deterioration and maintain critical ecosystem services in this economically vital freshwater resource.

title: The Fine-Root Ecology Database: a free and open resource of root traits and auxiliary data
summary: Distal roots of plants are directly responsible for nutrient and water uptake and represent a dominant pathway for plant carbon to enter soil. However, these ‘fine’ roots are a poorly understood component of terrestrial ecosystems, and synt
content: Distal roots of plants are directly responsible for nutrient and water uptake and represent a dominant pathway for plant carbon to enter soil. However, these ‘fine’ roots are a poorly understood component of terrestrial ecosystems, and synthetic analyses to improve our global understanding have historically been hindered by a lack of robust, organized, and freely-available data. The release of the Fine-Root Ecology Database version 4.0 addresses this issue. With this release, users will have access to roughly 40% more coverage across hundreds of root traits which can be accessed through an online portal or as a flat csv file. Importantly, FRED includes metadata allowing users to make informed decisions regarding inclusion or exclusion of data measured on different fine-root pools. Altogether, FRED 4.0 is a freely-available resource enabling analyses of fine-root traits at local to global scales.

title: Long-term trends and spatial contrasts in Soil Organic Carbon (SOC) of Kolkata, India
summary: Abstract Soil Organic Carbon (SOC) is used as a proxy to assess the degree of natural as well as anthropogenic stress factors. In an over populated urban zone, the values of SOC is regulated by several factors such as deposition of dust by
content: Abstract Soil Organic Carbon (SOC) is used as a proxy to assess the degree of natural as well as anthropogenic stress factors. In an over populated urban zone, the values of SOC is regulated by several factors such as deposition of dust by running vehicles, atmospheric fall out, deposition of plant litter, transference of materials from the surrounding urban environment etc. This research analyzed an yearly SOC dataset for four sites in the megacity of Kolkata, namely Moulali, Rajabazar, Manicktala and Shyambazar, covering more than three decades (1990–2025) of timescale. Over the 36-year period, SOC increased from 0.62 to 1.34% at Moulali, from 0.71 to 1.61% at Rajabazar, from 0.49 to 1.03% at Manicktala and from 0.51 to 1.12% at Shyambazar. Linear trends were positive at all four sites, with fitted slopes between 0.0140 and 0.0207 percentage points per year. A noticeable dip occurred in 2020, followed by only a modest recovery in 2021 and a stronger hike thereafter. Both natural phenomenon and anthropogenic stress factors contribute to this spatio-temporal variations. The study therefore treats the present series as a baseline record and aims to explore the SOC patterns across the four selected sites. The spatio-temporal analysis of SOC is essential to understand the carbon sequestration potential of urban soils. This may further help environmentalists to understand carbon dynamics across urban ecosystems and ways to mitigate the carbon-dioxide through sequestration of terrestrial carbon.

title: Beyond stomata: Interspecific heterogeneity and structural controls of urban ozone deposition
summary: Abstract. Urban environments are critical ozone (O3) hotspots where intense precursor emissions and high population densities escalate human exposure risks. Current deposition models typically rely on coarse land-use classifications, failin
content: Abstract. Urban environments are critical ozone (O3) hotspots where intense precursor emissions and high population densities escalate human exposure risks. Current deposition models typically rely on coarse land-use classifications, failing to capture the species-level heterogeneity at the city scale. We quantified O3 dry deposition across 20 common tree species in a subtropical megacity using a modified micrometeorological gradient method to derive species-resolved resistance parameters. Field measurements identified substantial interspecific variation: daytime canopy concentration gradients peaked at 10.02 ± 0.86 ppb (Platanus acerifolia). While standardized stomatal conductance correlates with the inverted minimum stomatal resistance (1/Rs, min, R2 = 0.36, P < 0.001), this relationship provides partial physiological support for the inferred resistance parameters. Sensitivity analysis showed that model-estimated deposition velocity was most sensitive to LAI, followed by wind speed and roughness length. Notably, a 20 % LAI increase reduced estimated deposition velocity by 17.55 % under the prescribed sensitivity experiments. These findings highlight species-level differences in O3 deposition and the coupled roles of canopy structure, aerodynamic transport, and physiological regulation. The resulting resistance estimates provide observational constraints for species-resolved parameterization in atmospheric deposition models, although their transferability requires further validation.
