Its objective focuses on ensuring universal access to affordable, reliable, sustainable, and modern energy by 2030. It aims to increase the share of renewable energy, enhance energy efficiency, and facilitate energy accessibility for all. To achieve these goals, India has undertaken significant initiatives to boost the use of renewable or non-conventional energy sources, particularly in electricity generation. This paper examines the legislative framework governing the renewable energy sector in India, highlighting key legal developments and reforms. The study explores critical legislation, including the Electricity Act, 2003, the National Tariff Policy, and the Draft Renewable Energy Act. Additionally, it analyzes the implementation and impact of the Renewable Purchase Obligation (RPO) imposed on state distribution companies. The broader implications of sectoral reforms and their effects on the renewable energy landscape are also discussed. Furthermore, the paper examines the stance of the Indian judiciary on energy laws, shedding light on its role in shaping the legal and regulatory framework for renewable energy. This comprehensive analysis seeks to provide insights into India's evolving renewable energy laws and their significance in fostering a sustainable energy transition.

title: Pre‐Branching Conversion of Bio‐Diols via Methanol‐Mediated Cascade Coupling for Sustainable Aviation Fuels
summary: ABSTRACT Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) is indispensable for aviation decarbonization. Nevertheless, conventional SAF syntheses from biomass‐derived alcohols suffer from tedious reaction pathways, energy‐intensive post‐isomerization, and i
content: ABSTRACT Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) is indispensable for aviation decarbonization. Nevertheless, conventional SAF syntheses from biomass‐derived alcohols suffer from tedious reaction pathways, energy‐intensive post‐isomerization, and inadequate control of alkane branching. Herein, we propose a novel “pre‐branching” strategy for high‐quality SAF production: C 2 ‐C 4 bio‐based vicinal diols convert into C 4 ‐C 6 branched alcohols over CuMgAlO x in supercritical methanol, integrating dehydrogenation, cross‐aldol condensation, pinacol rearrangement, and in‐situ hydrogenation; subsequent oligomerization and hydrotreating further upgrade C 4 ‐C 6 alcohol intermediates into branched C 8 ‐C 16 alkanes for aviation applications. With ethylene glycol as a model substrate, a maximum 77.9 C% yield of C 4 ‐C 6 alcohols was achieved. In situ spectroscopy and 13 C isotope labeling reveal that Cu + /Cu 0 sites catalyze (de)hydrogenation, MgO promotes C─C coupling via cross‐aldol condensation, acidic AlO x sites induce 1,2‐alkyl migration of vicinal diols for skeletal branching, and methanol serves as an in situ hydrogen donor. Subsequent oligomerization over Amberlyst‐35 and hydrotreating over Ni/Al 2 O 3 deliver an 83.3 C% toward C 8 ‐C 16 iso‐alkanes, affording a 64.9% overall carbon yield from ethylene glycol. Without post‐isomerization, the SAF features a ‐65°C freezing point and robust feedstock compatibility with crude biomass polyols. This work provides a new paradigm for controllable synthesis of high‐performance SAF from renewable bio‐diols.

title: Pengembangan E-Modul Fisika Berbasis Inkuiri Terbimbing Terintegrasi Green Physics Pada Peserta Didik SMA
summary: Physics instruction in senior high schools remains largely teacher-centered, while renewable energy topics are difficult to visualize due to limited laboratory equipment, leaving students' science process skills underdeveloped. This study a
content: Physics instruction in senior high schools remains largely teacher-centered, while renewable energy topics are difficult to visualize due to limited laboratory equipment, leaving students' science process skills underdeveloped. This study aimed to develop a guided inquiry-based physics e-module integrated with green physics principles on renewable energy to enhance the science process skills of tenth-grade students. The study employed a Research and Development approach using the Rowntree model, comprising planning, development, and evaluation stages, combined with Tessmer's formative evaluation involving self evaluation, expert review, one-to-one evaluation, and small group evaluation. A field trial was conducted with 33 tenth-grade students at SMA Negeri 3 Banyuasin 1 using a pretest-posttest design. The results showed that the e-module achieved a validity score of 88.4% (Highly Valid) and a practicality score of 87.9% (Highly Practical). N-Gain analysis revealed an increase in science process skills of 0.65 (moderate category), with average scores rising from 33.9 to 77.0. These findings indicate that the developed e-module is feasible as an alternative physics learning medium that integrates conceptual mastery with environmental awareness, while supporting the implementation of active learning under the Kurikulum Merdeka.

title: Worker employability in the energy transition: a systematic literature review of evidence from declining and growing sectors
summary: Systematic literature review with a descriptive bibliometric component. The review asks what determines the employability of workers affected by the energy transition, which interventions (reskilling, vocational training, micro-credentials,
content: Systematic literature review with a descriptive bibliometric component. The review asks what determines the employability of workers affected by the energy transition, which interventions (reskilling, vocational training, micro-credentials, just transition policies) have been studied, and how evidence differs between declining sectors (coal, oil and gas, thermal power) and growing sectors (renewable energy, transition minerals), and between the Global North and Global South. Records were identified in Scopus and OpenAlex on 14 November 2026. Status at registration: searches and title/abstract screening are complete; full-text eligibility assessment, quality appraisal (MMAT 2018), data extraction and synthesis have not started. The review forms part of a doctoral project on the employability of local workers in a nickel-mining region of Indonesia.

title: A qualitative assessment of perceived resilience in agricultural marketing cooperatives
source: Journal of Co-operative Organization and Management
summary: Agricultural marketing cooperatives are vital to agricultural systems, yet their resilience remains understudied. This research applies and extends the resilience assessment framework for farm systems to these cooperatives, examining robust
content: Agricultural marketing cooperatives are vital to agricultural systems, yet their resilience remains understudied. This research applies and extends the resilience assessment framework for farm systems to these cooperatives, examining robustness, adaptability, transformability, and anticipation. Using a qualitative approach, we conducted in-depth interviews with 18 German cooperative decision-makers from December 2023 to February 2024 to examine their perceptions of resilience. Our study employs thematic analysis and deductive category formation to investigate the framework's applicability, gain insights into perceived resilience capacities and strategies, and examine how cooperative values are perceived to foster resilience through the resilience capacities. Results show the adapted framework effectively captures unique cooperative aspects from the perspective of interviewees. Respondents generally describe their organizations as robust and diversified, and as maintaining resilience through adaptability in business fields and functions. While overall resilience is perceived as high, individual capacities vary, with robustness rated highest and anticipatory capacity lowest. Cooperative values are viewed by respondents as contributing to resilience, especially during crises, but are also described as facing challenges. This study provides one of the first systematic qualitative analyses of perceived resilience in agricultural marketing cooperatives and contributes to understanding factors that may support stability and sustainability in food systems.

title: Mean-field games with rough common noise: the linear-quadratic case
summary: Motivated by mean-field games (MFG) with common noise on the one hand and pathwise stochastic control theory on the other, we formulate here a linear-quadratic (LQ) MFG with rough common noise, along with a satisfactory well-posedness theor
content: Motivated by mean-field games (MFG) with common noise on the one hand and pathwise stochastic control theory on the other, we formulate here a linear-quadratic (LQ) MFG with rough common noise, along with a satisfactory well-posedness theory for the linear-quadratic case. A novel Volterra-type (or mild) formulation allows to keep technical (rough-stochastic) consideration to a minimum. We derive a characterization of the optimal state and optimal control through a rough forward-backward SDE (rough FBSDE), and provide an existence and uniqueness result under the usual assumptions. Our theory is accompanied by stability estimates with respect to initial data and common noise while we also establish continuity of what we call the Itô-Lions-Lyons map for rough mean-field games. Finally, we discuss randomization of the rough common noise under appropriate conditions on the coefficients. When the latter is given by the Stratonovich lift of a Brownian motion independent of the idiosyncratic noise, we show that solutions of the rough LQ MFG coincide with those obtained by conditioning on the common noise.

title: Individual pitch control with two azimuth offsets in the reverse multiblade coordinate transformation for reducing periodic blade loads in wind turbines
summary: Individual pitch control (IPC) is commonly used to mitigate periodic blade loads in wind turbines, relying on the multiblade coordinate (MBC). Although the transformed axes are theoretically decoupled, practical implementations exhibit pers
content: Individual pitch control (IPC) is commonly used to mitigate periodic blade loads in wind turbines, relying on the multiblade coordinate (MBC). Although the transformed axes are theoretically decoupled, practical implementations exhibit persistent interactions. Prior studies have shown that introducing an azimuth offset in the reverse MBC transform or applying static inverted decoupling reduces these interactions. This study proposes an extended IPC formulation that introduces two independent azimuth offsets in the MBC transformation, enabling separate phase compensation of the tilt and yaw components. The approach is analytically shown to be equivalent to static inverted decoupling, providing a unified interpretation of decoupling-based IPC strategies. Design expressions based on the steady-state gain matrix of the 2 × 2 IPC process are provided, along with practical guidelines for upgrading existing IPCs by adjusting controller gains when offsets or decoupling are introduced. The proposed methods are evaluated on the IEA 15-MW reference wind turbine using OpenFAST at a nominal operating point. Multi-objective optimization is employed to tune several IPC schemes and assess the trade-off between blade fatigue reduction and pitch actuator activity. Results show that optimized azimuth offset IPC reduces blade damage equivalent loads by 6–9% with control effort comparable to conventional IPC, while steady-state based designs achieve 4–6% reductions. The two-offset scheme provides the greatest flexibility, although improvements over a single offset remain modest due to similar optimal offset values.

title: Molecular Structure-Dependent External Electric Field Modulation of Interfacial Charge Separation
summary: Abstract Based on density functional theory, this paper systematically investigates the external electric field-regulated charge-transfer behavior of two donor:acceptor interfaces, PBDB-T:CF3-BDP-Cz and PBDB-T:CF3-BDP-TPA. These two BODIPY-
content: Abstract Based on density functional theory, this paper systematically investigates the external electric field-regulated charge-transfer behavior of two donor:acceptor interfaces, PBDB-T:CF3-BDP-Cz and PBDB-T:CF3-BDP-TPA. These two BODIPY-based acceptors share the same BODIPY core but differ in their terminal donor groups, namely carbazole (Cz) and triphenylamine (TPA), providing a well-defined model system for elucidating the relationship between molecular structure and interfacial charge transfer. The results show that the different terminal groups lead to significant differences in the electric-field response mechanisms of the two interfaces. For the PBDB-T:CF3-BDP-Cz interface, the excited-state properties show a relatively weak response to the electric field, while the charge-transfer rate exhibits a nonmonotonic dependence on electric-field intensity, and an optimal electric-field range is identified that favors charge separation. The charge-transfer characteristics of the PBDB-T:CF3-BDP-TPA interface are more sensitive to changes in the electric field. Although the charge-recombination rate is consistently higher than the charge-separation rate throughout the entire electric-field range, the relative efficiency of charge separation continuously increases with increasing electric-field strength because the charge-separation rate increases more rapidly than the charge-recombination rate. This study reveals the intrinsic relationship between terminal-group structure, electric-field modulation, and interfacial charge-transfer mechanism, providing a theoretical basis for understanding the field-controlled charge-separation mechanism of organic photovoltaic interfaces.

title: Reactor operation induced thermal effects on neutron flux measurements using 3He neutron detectors at a TRIGA Mk II research reactor
summary: A variation of the measured neutron flux using 3 He detectors at a TRIGA Mk II nuclear research reactor during steady-state operation is reported in this article. The observed effect shows a statistically significant anti-correlation ( > 7
content: A variation of the measured neutron flux using 3 He detectors at a TRIGA Mk II nuclear research reactor during steady-state operation is reported in this article. The observed effect shows a statistically significant anti-correlation ( > 7 σ ) between the temperature in the reactor pool and recorded neutron count rates. Following reactor start-up under nominal operating conditions, the effect occurs for a specific time period until both thermal equilibrium and a constant neutron count rate are reached. Simultaneous neutron and temperature measurements are performed in different configurations around the reactor in order to gain qualitative insights about the temperature dependent count rate behavior.

title: HelioTR-Atlas couples satellite-retrieved direct irradiance with station-validated topographic thermodynamics for explainable photovoltaic yield mapping in complex terrain
summary: Abstract Terrain-resolved photovoltaic (PV) yield assessment needs an irradiance source whose direct component is retrieved rather than assumed, thermodynamic fields corrected for elevation and validated against ground stations, and an attr
content: Abstract Terrain-resolved photovoltaic (PV) yield assessment needs an irradiance source whose direct component is retrieved rather than assumed, thermodynamic fields corrected for elevation and validated against ground stations, and an attribution layer explaining why yield departs from irradiance. These are rarely met together. We present HelioTR-Atlas, a reproducible framework coupling SARAH-3 satellite irradiance with lapse-rate-corrected ERA5-Land temperature, dew point and wind, propagated through an anisotropic transposition, a cell-temperature model and an efficiency model calibrated to a 325 W module. The retrieved direct component avoids the Erbs diffuse-fraction assumption, which overestimated clear-sky direct irradiance by 25 W m⁻². Lapse-rate correction reduced ERA5-Land air-temperature root-mean-square deviation against 62 stations from 3.25 to 2.52 °C, a 22.5% improvement; dew point and wind were evaluated against 119 stations. For Türkiye over 2000–2025 the framework gives a climatological mean yield of 1805 kWh/kWp across 32,479 land cells, an inter-annual coefficient of variation of 3.3%, and provincial means from 1334 kWh/kWp on the eastern Black Sea coast to 1994 kWh/kWp in the southeast. In-plane irradiation matched PVGIS to within 2.1%. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) attribution separates two regimes: irradiance sets the spatial pattern of yield, whereas air temperature governs the performance ratio, most strongly at elevation extremes.

title: KAZLEATHER 2030: A POLICY FRAMEWORK FOR TRANSFORMING KAZAKHSTAN’S LEATHER INDUSTRY
summary: The article considers the development of the leather industry of Kazakhstan in the context of industry diversification and sustainable production. The goal of the research is to assess the current state of the leather industry and develop p
content: The article considers the development of the leather industry of Kazakhstan in the context of industry diversification and sustainable production. The goal of the research is to assess the current state of the leather industry and develop policyoriented recommendations to transform it into a competitive and environmentally sustainable industry. The methodology uses a mixed-methods approach that includes analysis of official statistical data, policy analysis, and semi-structured interviews with key industry actors. The findings indicate that the industry is characterized by limited deep processing, underutilized capacity, environmental costs, weak institutional coordination, and a shortage of personnel. Based on the comparative analysis of the European Union, Türkiye, China, and Uzbekistan, a framework concept for the KazLeather 2030 transformation is proposed that includes the e-vet&Traceability digital platform, the KazLeather Research Grant and the implementation of the KazLeather environmental standard. The research contributes to discussions on modernizing resource-based industries and offers practical instruments for upgrading value-added chains.

title: Closed-Loop Fabrication of Regenerated Cellulose Battery Separator via Solvent-Guided Structural Regulation
summary: Abstract The development of battery separators derived from renewable feedstocks that can simultaneously achieve high porosity, robust mechanical strength, excellent thermal stability, reliable electrochemical performance, and satisfactory
content: Abstract The development of battery separators derived from renewable feedstocks that can simultaneously achieve high porosity, robust mechanical strength, excellent thermal stability, reliable electrochemical performance, and satisfactory environmental sustainability remains a core challenge in the field of sustainable energy storage material. Herein, we report a regenerated cellulose membrane prepared through a dissolution/regeneration process using lithium bromide Molecular dynamics simulation results show that water is the effective antisolvent for driving the formation of cellulose–cellulose H-bonds, yielding cellulose with a better crystalline structure. Subsequently, tert-butanol was utilized to replace water in the cellulose membrane precursor prior to drying, preventing capillary-induced pore collapse. This membrane exhibits high porosity of 70.1%, excellent electrolyte uptake capacity of 243.7%, ionic conductivity of 0.77 mS/cm, excellent thermal stability (no shrinkage at 150 °C), and roust mechanical strength. The Na/HC half-cells assembled with this membrane displays high cycle capacity retention rate of 87.1% at 0.1 C after 500 cycles, which is comparable to commercial separators. This membrane fabrication process enables closed-loop solvent recycling, and the membrane fully degraded after 4 months of soil burial, and life cycle assessment indicated lower impacts than commercial battery separators. These results establish a practical closed-loop strategy for sustainable, high-performance battery separators.

title: Dual-Stream Downscaling and Flow-Constrained Correction of Meteorological Fields over Complex Terrain
summary: Abstract High-resolution near-surface meteorological fields are essential, yet conventional numerical simulation is computationally expensive and data-driven methods often lack physical consistency. Here, a lightweight framework for meteoro
content: Abstract High-resolution near-surface meteorological fields are essential, yet conventional numerical simulation is computationally expensive and data-driven methods often lack physical consistency. Here, a lightweight framework for meteorological-field downscaling and observation-driven correction is presented as a cost-effective alternative. In the downscaling stage, multivariate synoptic-scale information is fused with high-resolution terrain by a dual-stream generative adversarial network, and the fields are refined in a reconstruction-driven cascade. In the correction stage, a simplified UNet learns additive corrections supervised directly by station observations, and a flow-constrained regularizer enforces physical consistency. In independent tests, the downscaling stage reduces the 0.25° four-variable error by 54.0–73.5% relative to bicubic interpolation, and the full-field correction reduces the station MAE of T2m, V10, and U10 by 17.81%, 27.59%, and 21.06%, respectively. The full training-to-inference workflow can be completed within a few days on an ordinary personal computer, making it practical for operational fine-scale meteorological services.

title: Topology-Dependent Stress Relaxation in Epoxy Vitrimers via Reactive Coarse-Grained Modeling
summary: Abstract Bond-exchange reactions (BERs) enable vitrimers to relax stress through dynamic topology rearrangement, yet their mechanical effectiveness depends strongly on network architecture. Here, experimental stress-relaxation measurements
content: Abstract Bond-exchange reactions (BERs) enable vitrimers to relax stress through dynamic topology rearrangement, yet their mechanical effectiveness depends strongly on network architecture. Here, experimental stress-relaxation measurements are combined with reactive coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations of epoxy–acid networks with systematically varied backbone flexibility and cross-linker length. A dimensionless acceleration factor reveals consistent chemistry-dependent trends between experiment and simulation, with BER producing stronger relative acceleration in the relatively rigid DGEBA-based networks than in the flexible BDDE-based networks. Two-mode Kohlrausch–Williams–Watts (KWW) analysis separates a fast relaxation mode associated with local segmental dynamics from a slow network-level mode strongly accelerated by BER. In DGEBA-based networks, the slow stress-relaxation and topology-relaxation time scales closely correspond, indicating strong coupling between topology reshuffling and long-time stress dissipation. In contrast, BDDE-based networks exhibit substantial stress relaxation before complete topology decorrelation, consistent with their greater intrinsic internal mobility and an additional mobility-assisted relaxation pathway. These results demonstrate that the mechanical effectiveness of BER is governed not by topology-reshuffling speed alone, but by its coupling with backbone mobility and the stress-bearing network architecture.

title: Translating pathogen biology into diagnostic and management strategies for gummy stem blight in cucumber production
summary: Gummy stem blight (GSB) is a major disease of cucurbits caused by Stagonosporopsis spp. and is increasingly problematic in intensive cucumber production systems, particularly where warm, humid environments favour infection, sporulation and
content: Gummy stem blight (GSB) is a major disease of cucurbits caused by Stagonosporopsis spp. and is increasingly problematic in intensive cucumber production systems, particularly where warm, humid environments favour infection, sporulation and rapid disease spread. GSB can infect vegetative and reproductive tissues and remain latent in fruit for several days before visible symptoms develop, creating a distinctive commercial challenge: disease may be difficult to detect before harvest yet cause significant post-harvest losses, reducing grower and retailer confidence. Compounding these problems, current diagnostic tools for detecting pre-symptomatic infection are often insufficiently validated for species specificity, sensitivity, turnaround time, cost, crude-sample compatibility and practical use by production staff. Many of these limitations reflect the relative lack of genomic resources for Stagonosporopsis. Therefore, this review integrates evidence from other pathosystems with current knowledge of Stagonosporopsis taxonomy, infection biology, epidemiology, diagnostics, fungicide resistance, effector biology and host resistance to identify pathways towards grower-ready tools. Specifically, we focus on how recent advances in genomics, paired with previously designed detection systems such as loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) and clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats/CRISPR-associated proteins (CRISPR/Cas), could be adapted for species-specific detection of the causal pathogen and, simultaneously, provide a regional profile of fungicide resistance. In parallel, we explore how a deeper functional genomic understanding of the disease, particularly of effector proteins expressed during the early stages of infection, could provide valuable insights into the dynamics of this host-pathogen interaction and support strategies to disrupt these interactions through novel fungistatic compounds and the development of disease-resistant cultivars. Together, these approaches could support a staged technology-development and adoption roadmap for more precise, rapid and sustainable GSB management in cucumber production.

title: Smallholder livestock farmers' willingness to adopt biogas technology to meet the energy crisis in rural Bangladesh
summary: Despite gains in national electrification, rural Bangladesh continues to experience persistent energy insecurity, while livestock-based livelihoods generate large volumes of organic waste that remain underutilized as locally available renew
content: Despite gains in national electrification, rural Bangladesh continues to experience persistent energy insecurity, while livestock-based livelihoods generate large volumes of organic waste that remain underutilized as locally available renewable energy resources. This study investigates smallholder livestock farmers’ willingness to adopt biogas technology as a decentralized clean-energy solution for reducing rural energy shortages and advancing SDG-oriented outcomes related to clean energy, climate resilience, and sustainable livelihoods. A semi-structured household survey was conducted among 480 livestock-farming households selected from 12 Upazilas in four northern districts of Bangladesh, where livestock dependence, rural poverty, and recurrent electricity interruptions make household-scale biogas particularly relevant. Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, exploratory factor analysis to construct an awareness index, and a maximum-likelihood probit regression model were employed to identify the determinants of adoption willingness. The model demonstrates strong explanatory performance, with an LR chi-square value of 92.67 and a pseudo R² of 0.5457. The findings reveal that daily electricity shortage (coefficient = 0.3361), awareness of biogas benefits (1.0406), surplus homestead space (0.4826), women’s work-related energy burden (0.0835), electricity-related disruption to children’s education (-0.5707), and educational attainment are statistically associated with willingness to install biogas technology at the reported significance levels. These results indicate that biogas adoption is shaped not only by resources but also by information access, education, infrastructure constraints, gendered labor burdens, and the everyday consequences of unreliable electricity. Scaling rural biogas diffusion therefore requires integrated policy support, including targeted awareness campaigns, technical extension, concessional finance, space-sensitive plant designs, and incorporation of biogas into rural energy planning.

title: Seasonal Performance of a Sail-Assisted Parallel Hybrid Marine Vessel with Power-Follower Control
summary: This study evaluates seasonal fuel use and power sharing in a sail-assisted parallel hybrid vessel. A state-of-charge (SOC)-adaptive power-take-off/power-take-in power follower is implemented in MATLAB/Simulink for the Kuala Terengganu–Sing
content: This study evaluates seasonal fuel use and power sharing in a sail-assisted parallel hybrid vessel. A state-of-charge (SOC)-adaptive power-take-off/power-take-in power follower is implemented in MATLAB/Simulink for the Kuala Terengganu–Singapore–Langkawi return route. Case A uses diesel propulsion. Case B adds a shaft motor–generator, a 430.08 kWh battery and 32 m2 of photovoltaic (PV) area (6.72 kWp). Case C combines the same hybrid machinery with 312 m2 of sails and 182.4 m2 of PV (38.304 kWp). Forty-eight 27-day simulations cover January, April, July and October of 2022–2025, with four matched year-periods per month. Fuel consumption follows A > B > C in every period. Overall propulsion fuel decreases by 0.85% in B and 3.89% in C relative to A. The additional C-to-B saving is 4.17 ± 0.64% (mean ± SD) in January. This difference includes both increased PV capacity and sail assistance. Motor and generator modes remain mutually exclusive, with SOC within 30.01–100%. Higher January waves increase propulsion demand, while stronger winds increase sail assistance. January engine energy decreases from 42.40 to 40.24 MWh per cycle despite a decrease in engine efficiency. The results show how seasonal demand and renewable inputs affect the evaluated configurations. They remain conditional on the estimated component maps, wave-resistance extrapolation and irradiance-based PV representation.

title: Thickness and Field-dependent evolution ofmagnetic domains in ferrimagnetic TbFe thin films
summary: Abstract Rare-earth–transition-metal ferrimagnetic thin films have emerged as a versatilematerial platform for spintronic and magnetic memory technologies, owingto their rich magnetic domain behavior and the ability to engineer perpendicula
content: Abstract Rare-earth–transition-metal ferrimagnetic thin films have emerged as a versatilematerial platform for spintronic and magnetic memory technologies, owingto their rich magnetic domain behavior and the ability to engineer perpendicularmagnetic anisotropy (PMA). Although magnetic reversal and domaindynamics can be tailored through multilayer architectures and interface modification,the extent to which film thickness alone can modulate domain evolutionand magnetization-reversal pathways in single-layer ferrimagnets remains insufficientlyexplored. In this work, we examine the combined influence of filmthickness and an externally applied out-of-plane (OOP) magnetic field on thedomain dynamics and magnetization reversal mechanisms of single-layer TbFeferrimagnetic films. TbFe films of 30 and 100 nm thicknesses were depositedby electron-beam evaporation and systematically characterized using vibrational samplemagnetometry (VSM) and magnetic force microscopy (MFM). Magnetometrymeasurements revealed strong PMA in both samples, accompanied bywasp-waisted OOP hysteresis loops, characteristic of exchange-coupled magneticsublattices. MFM revealed labyrinthine domain patterns in both films. Upon theapplication of positive OOP magnetic field, both films undergo complete magnetizationreversal, where switching dynamics differ markedly. The 30 nm filmexhibits an abrupt reversal accompanied by a narrow and symmetric switching fielddistribution, whereas the 100 nm film reverses gradually through viscousdomains and with broader switching-field distribution. Field-dependent domainimaging further shows distinct and asymmetric domain-evolution pathways, consistentwith a Kondorsky-type reversal mechanism. XPS depth profiling of filmrevealed pronounced compositional inhomogeneity and Fe/Tb imbalance, directly linking chemical inhomogeneity, defect-mediated pinning, and sublattice-specificanisotropy that govern the observed reversal asymmetry. These results highlightthe combined effects of film thickness and external magnetic fields on TbFedomain dynamics, guiding the design of single-layer ferrimagnetic thin filmswith precise domain control and reversible switching for memory and spintronicapplications.

title: A Comparative Framework for AI-Enhanced Renewable Energy Auditing in South Asia: A Multi-Country Evidence-Based Study
source: Advances in computational intelligence and robotics book series
summary: The exponential development of renewable energy in South Asia has put a spotlight on the issues of transparency, accountability, and governance in sustainability. Reliance on conventional auditing practices, which mainly involve manual veri
content: The exponential development of renewable energy in South Asia has put a spotlight on the issues of transparency, accountability, and governance in sustainability. Reliance on conventional auditing practices, which mainly involve manual verification through site visits and reporting that is not sufficiently consolidated, as well as compliance checks that take place after implementation, is not enough to only tackle the operational, financial, and environmental aspects of the new renewable energy endeavors. Such weaknesses expose the parties involved to major risks like tampering with data, inadequate checking of compliance with ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) standards, slowing down the process of monitoring compliance, and greenwashing. In this chapter the author has a detailed look at the rising use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-automated auditing techniques in line with governance promotion in the renewable energy industry in India, Bangladesh, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka.

title: BO‘LAJAK MUHANDISLARDA INGLIZ TILIGA OID LINGVISTIK KOMPETENSIYANI SHAKLLANTIRISHNING INTEGRATIV YONDASHUVGA ASOSLANGAN PEDAGOGIK MODELI
summary: Mazkur maqolada bo‘lajak muhandislarda ingliz tiliga oid lingvistik kompetensiyani shakllantirishning integrativ yondashuvga asoslangan pedagogik modeli nazariy-metodik jihatdan asoslanadi. Muhandislik fanlari mazmunini ingliz tili ta’limi
content: Mazkur maqolada bo‘lajak muhandislarda ingliz tiliga oid lingvistik kompetensiyani shakllantirishning integrativ yondashuvga asoslangan pedagogik modeli nazariy-metodik jihatdan asoslanadi. Muhandislik fanlari mazmunini ingliz tili ta’limi bilan uyg‘unlashtirish, kasbiy terminologiyani o‘zlashtirish, grammatik va fonetik vositalarni kasbiy kommunikativ vaziyatlarda qo‘llash hamda texnik matnlarni tushunish masalalari tahlil qilinadi. Maqsadli, mazmuniy, jarayonli va diagnostik-natijaviy komponentlardan tashkil topgan pedagogik model taklif etiladi. Shuningdek, modelni amalga oshirish bosqichlari, integrativ topshiriqlar, baholash mezonlari va amaliy joriy etish shartlari tavsiflanadi. Maqola nazariy-metodik xarakterga ega bo‘lib, model samaradorligini empirik tekshirish uchun keyingi tajriba-sinov ishlariga ehtiyoj mavjudligi qayd etiladi.

title: ენერგომატარებლებზე მაღალი ფასების გავლენა ნავთობის იმპორტიორ ეკონომიკებზე: გერმანიის მაგალითი რუსეთ-უკრაინის ომის პერიოდში - VAR-მოდელი
summary: doi.org/10.52340/eab.2026.18.03.06 რუსეთ-უკრაინის ომმა ენერგომომარაგებაში სერიოზული შეფერხებები გამოიწვია, განსაკუთრებით ევროპულ ქვეყნებში, რომლებიც ძლიერად იყვნენ დამოკიდებული რუსულ ნავთობსა და გაზზე. კონფლიქტის შედეგად ნავთობის ფასმა ბარე
content: doi.org/10.52340/eab.2026.18.03.06 რუსეთ-უკრაინის ომმა ენერგომომარაგებაში სერიოზული შეფერხებები გამოიწვია, განსაკუთრებით ევროპულ ქვეყნებში, რომლებიც ძლიერად იყვნენ დამოკიდებული რუსულ ნავთობსა და გაზზე. კონფლიქტის შედეგად ნავთობის ფასმა ბარელზე 140 დოლარს მიაღწია, რაც მძიმედ აწვება ენერგიაზე დამოკიდებულ სექტორებს, როგორიცაა წარმოება და ტრანსპორტი. ეს ენერგოკრიზისი განსაკუთრებული გამოწვევაა ისეთი ნავთობის იმპორტიორი ეკონომიკებისთვის, როგორიცაა გერმანია, სადაც უკვე შეინიშნება მრავალფეროვანი ეკონომიკური შედეგები და გაჩნდა გადაუდებელი საჭიროება ალტერნატიული ენერგომომარაგების წყაროების მოძიებისა. გერმანია, როგორც ევროპის უდიდესი ენერგომომხმარებელი, განსაკუთრებით დაუცველი აღმოჩნდა. ომამდე მისი ბუნებრივი გაზის 50%-ზე მეტი და ნავთობის მნიშვნელოვანი ნაწილი რუსეთიდან შემოდიოდა. ენერგომომარაგების მოულოდნელმა შეწყვეტამ გერმანია აიძულა სწრაფად გაემრავალფეროვნებინა მომწოდებლები და დაეჩქარებინა განახლებადი ენერგიის სისტემების ინტეგრაცია. თუმცა, ამ პროცესში ქვეყანა ცდილობს ერთდროულად შეინარჩუნოს მოკლევადიანი ენერგოუსაფრთხოება და გრძელვადიანი კლიმატური ვალდებულებები, რაც რთულ ბალანსს ქმნის. ენერგიის ფასების ზრდამ მკვეთრად გააძლიერა ინფლაციური პროცესები. როგორც კვლევა აჩვენებს, ენერგიის გაძვირება იწვევს „cost-push“ დინამიკას, რაც ამცირებს მომხმარებელთა მყიდველუნარიანობას. ინფლაციის გარდა, წარმოების ხარჯების ზრდა, კომპანიებს აიძულებს სამუშაო ძალის შემცირებას, რის შედეგადაც უმუშევრობა იზრდება. ამასთან, გერმანიის ინდუსტრიული სექტორი გარკვეულ გამძლეობას ავლენს, რადგან ნელ-ნელა გადადის ალტერნატიულ ენერგიაზე და აუმჯობესებს ეფექტიანობას. კვლევის მეთოდოლოგია ეფუძნება VAR მოდელს, რომელიც საშუალებას იძლევა შეაკავოს ენერგიის ფასების შოკების გავლენა ეკონომიკურ ზრდაზე, ინფლაციაზე, უმუშევრობასა და ინდუსტრიულ პროდუქტიულობაზე. მონაცემები მიღებულია მსოფლიო განვითარების ინდიკატორებიდან (WDI) და OAPEC–ისგან. შედეგები აჩვენებს, რომ ენერგიის ფასების ცვლილებები მნიშვნელოვან გავლენას ახდენს ყველა მაკროეკონომიკურ ცვლადზე, განსაკუთრებით ინფლაციასა და უმუშევრობაზე. ჩვენი title: Cost Reduction Through Learning Curve Effects at CSP Power Plants in China
summary: A considerable number of combined PV/CSP power plants are currently being installed in China, with a focus on power tower technology. The new “Document No. 136”, published 09.02.25 by China’s National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC
content: A considerable number of combined PV/CSP power plants are currently being installed in China, with a focus on power tower technology. The new “Document No. 136”, published 09.02.25 by China’s National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) introduces market-based pricing by 2025-06-01 and means new opportunities and challenges for CSP technologies and firms. It will increase the need for cost reduction and highly efficient project implementation. This paper first outlines the Chinese policies aimed at gradually integrating CSP technologies into the market, culminating in the recent shift to market-oriented pricing as defined in “Document No. 136”. Furthermore, the paper reports the recent progress achieved in the parabolic trough and heliostat technologies, developed by sbp sonne and implemented together with their Chinese partners Dongfang Boiler Group Co. Ltd. (DEC Boiler) and China Shipbuilding New Power Co. Ltd. (CSNP) in several large-scale projects. Both technologies have benefited from a continuous learning curve over nearly a decade and multiple major projects in China. The paper presents some of the most significant learning milestones achieved through industrialization and localization.

title: Extraction of Water from Atmospheric Air Using Solar Power
source: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
summary: Water is one of the most essential natural resources required for human survival. However, the availability of clean drinking water is decreasing in many regions due to population growth, climate change, and water scarcity. The project “Ext
content: Water is one of the most essential natural resources required for human survival. However, the availability of clean drinking water is decreasing in many regions due to population growth, climate change, and water scarcity. The project “Extraction of Water from Atmospheric Air Using Solar Power” aims to develop an eco-friendly and energy-efficient system to obtain water from the moisture present in the atmosphere by utilizing solar energy. The proposed system works by extracting moisture from atmospheric air through a suitable water-condensation process. Solar energy is used as the primary power source to operate the required components, such as a fan, cooling system, and other electrical devices, depending on the design. When the moist air comes into contact with a sufficiently cold surface, the water vapour condenses into liquid water. The collected water can then be filtered and treated to improve its quality for suitable uses. The main objective of this project is to reduce dependence on conventional water sources and provide an alternative water supply, especially in water-scarce and remote areas. The system also aims to reduce dependence on grid electricity by utilizing renewable solar energy, thereby minimizing environmental impact. It may be useful in rural areas, emergency situations, and disaster-affected regions where access to water is limited. In conclusion, this project explores the possibility of producing water from atmospheric moisture using solar power. Its performance depends on factors such as humidity, air temperature, solar radiation, and system efficiency. With proper design and further development, the system has the potential to support sustainable water management and provide an alternative source of water.

title: Boundary-Layer Regimes and Wind Energy Climate Resilience in North Africa: A Comparative Assessment of Egypt and Morocco
summary: Abstract. Egypt and Morocco have Africa's most ambitious wind energy programs, yet the climate resilience of their wind resources remains poorly constrained by conventional approaches that overlook fundamental atmospheric processes. Here we
content: Abstract. Egypt and Morocco have Africa's most ambitious wind energy programs, yet the climate resilience of their wind resources remains poorly constrained by conventional approaches that overlook fundamental atmospheric processes. Here we introduce a boundary-layer regime framework that classifies wind farm sites according to their dominant wind-generation mechanism—Mechanically Forced (M-BL), Thermally Forced (T-BL), or Complex Forced (C-BL)—and apply it to twelve wind farms across Egypt's Gulf of Suez and Morocco's Atlantic and Mediterranean coasts. Using a consistent CORDEX-Africa CMIP5 ensemble under RCP 8.5 through 2100, combined with validated baseline wind power density from ERA5 reanalysis, we analyze projected changes using the delta change method. We find a hierarchy of climate vulnerability governed by boundary-layer physics. Egyptian M-BL sites and Moroccan southern M-BL sites show the greatest resilience (mean ΔWPD50 = +1.6 %), while Moroccan T-BL sites (Essaouira, Taza) and C-BL sites (Tanger I, II) show larger declines (mean ΔWPD50 = −5.5 % and −10.8 %, respectively). The Mediterranean SST corridor creates a shared threat with divergent outcomes: Tanger remains viable because topographic acceleration at the Strait of Gibraltar partially compensates for the weakened thermal gradient, whereas the Egyptian Mediterranean coast has no wind farms because it lacks such compensation. The Zafarana case shows that urbanization can override M-BL resilience. The regime hierarchy is consistent with a companion CMIP6-based analysis, suggesting that the framework is robust to scenario-generation and ensemble-size differences. Our framework provides a physics-based, universally applicable tool for climate risk assessment in wind energy development.

title: Centralized vehicle-to-grid coordination for behind-the-meter value in commercial fleets: Evidence and deployment lessons from a pilot demonstration
summary: Vehicle-to-grid operation in commercial fleets remains debated due to interoperability limits, user acceptance, warranty concerns, and regulatory uncertainty. This paper reports a five-week multi-site pilot demonstration in mainland Portuga
content: Vehicle-to-grid operation in commercial fleets remains debated due to interoperability limits, user acceptance, warranty concerns, and regulatory uncertainty. This paper reports a five-week multi-site pilot demonstration in mainland Portugal evaluating a centralized coordination architecture that uses V2G and low-complexity rule-based control to capture behind-the-meter value: energy arbitrage under time-of-use tariffs, peak-load shaving, and photovoltaic surplus self-consumption, relying only on site telemetry, charging-session data, and conservative state-of-charge (SoC) limits agreed with fleet users. Across three sites, 374 kWh of charging was shifted from peak to off-peak periods, 150 kWh was discharged during peak periods, and 16.6 kWh of additional charging was enabled from solar surplus. These actions resulted in €20 of EV charging cost savings (a 26% cost-weighted reduction against the rebased baseline), €7.9 of site-level energy savings, and an estimated €39.4 reduction in demand-related charges, modest and highly site-specific values. Average departure SoC decreased from 96% to 79% but remained above the agreed 50% minimum throughout the pilot. Beyond these outcomes, the study draws deployment lessons on measurement uncertainty, control-interval limits, plug-in behavior, battery-condition observability, protocol maturity, deployment cost, and regulatory constraints.

title: Agro-fotovoltaik sistemlerin karşılaştırmalı analizi: Geleneksel PV, yükseltilmiş APV ve dikey APV sistemler üzerine bir inceleme
source: Pamukkale University Journal of Engineering Sciences
summary: Arka Plan—Son yıllarda hızla artan enerji talebi ve çevresel kaygılar, yenilenebilir enerji kaynaklarının önemini daha da ön plana çıkarmıştır. Bu bağlamda, güneş enerjisi; sürdürülebilir, temiz ve kolay erişilebilir yapısıyla enerji üretim
content: Arka Plan—Son yıllarda hızla artan enerji talebi ve çevresel kaygılar, yenilenebilir enerji kaynaklarının önemini daha da ön plana çıkarmıştır. Bu bağlamda, güneş enerjisi; sürdürülebilir, temiz ve kolay erişilebilir yapısıyla enerji üretiminde kritik bir seçenek olarak öne çıkmaktadır. Ancak artan enerji yatırımları, özellikle tarım arazileri üzerindeki alan baskısını artırarak gıda güvenliği açısından riskler yaratabilmektedir. Agro-fotovoltaik (APV) sistemler, bu soruna yenilikçi bir çözüm sunarak aynı arazi üzerinde hem tarımsal faaliyetlerin hem de güneş enerjisi üretiminin eş zamanlı olarak gerçekleştirilmesini mümkün kılmaktadır. Fotovoltaik (PV) panellerin tarım arazilerine bitki gelişimini engellemeyecek şekilde yerleştirilmesi, tarımsal üretime ek olarak enerji üretimi sağlayarak arazi kullanım verimliliğini artırmaktadır. Ayrıca, APV sistemlerin sağladığı gölgeleme etkisi ile bitkilerde su tasarrufu ve sıcaklık kontrolü gibi çevresel faydalar da elde edilir.Amaç—APV sistemler, sınırlı tarım alanlarında hem gıda hem de enerji üretimini birlikte mümkün kılan bütünleşik çözümler olarak giderek daha fazla ilgi görmektedir. Ancak planlama ve yatırım kararlarını yönlendirecek, farklı APV mimarilerini geleneksel PV sistemlerle aynı tüketim koşulları altında enerji performansı bakımından karşılaştıran nicel analizler yeterince yaygın değildir. Bu çalışmada geleneksel PV sistem, yükseltilmiş APV sistem ve dikey APV sistem olmak üzere üç farklı kurulumun enerji üretim performansları ve arazi kullanım etkileri karşılaştırılarak en verimli yöntemin saptanması amaçlanmıştır.Yöntem—Çalışmada ortak bir iklim veri seti ve birleşik sistem parametreleri altında, sabit bir tarımsal yük ile PV üretimini birleştiren saatlik bir simülasyon modeli geliştirilmiştir. Üç yerleşim planı – geleneksel yere monte PV, yükseltilmiş APV ve dikey APV – aynı kurulu kapasiteyle modellenmiş ve bir yıl boyunca çalıştırılarak PV üretimi, yerinde talep ve şebeke değişimi arasındaki zamana bağlı enerji dengesi elde edilmiştir. Bu simülasyonlardan, yük karşılama oranı, öz tüketim oranı ve fazla üretim dahil olmak üzere yıllık performans göstergeleri hesaplanarak üç sistem konfigürasyonunun niceliksel olarak karşılaştırılması sağlanmıştır.Bulgular—Araştırma bulguları; geleneksel PV sistemlerin en yüksek toplam enerji üretimini sağlasa da tarımsal faaliyetleri kısıtladığını ve tesisin tüketim ihtiyacını tam olarak karşılayamadığını göstermektedir. Yükseltilmiş APV sistem, panel altındaki arazinin tarımda kullanılmasına olanak tanırken, dikey APV sistem sabah ve akşam saatlerindeki üretim avantajı sayesinde öz tüketimin %48’ini karşılayarak enerji ihtiyacını en iyi dengeleyen sistem olmuştur. Böylece şebekeye bağımlılığı azaltmıştır. Arazi açısından daha fazla alana ihtiyaç duysa da, panel sıraları arasındaki boşlukların ekim alanı olarak değerlendirilmesi arazi kaybını %10 seviyelerinde tutmuştur.Sonuç—Araştırma sonuçları, tüketim profiline uygun olarak tasarlanan APV sistemleri

title: AI-Enhanced Smart Infrastructure Compliance Systems for Predictive Maintenance in Urban Energy Management Projects
source: WORLD JOURNAL OF INNOVATION AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
summary: As cities transition toward intelligent, sustainable infrastructures, the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into compliance systems becomes essential for managing complex urban energy environments. Traditional infrastructure compl
content: As cities transition toward intelligent, sustainable infrastructures, the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into compliance systems becomes essential for managing complex urban energy environments. Traditional infrastructure compliance models are reactive, data-siloed, and inefficient, leading to unplanned maintenance, safety violations, and energy losses. This review explores how AI-enhanced compliance systems can enable predictive maintenance, ensure regulatory alignment, and optimize operational efficiency in smart infrastructure projects. The paper investigates AI applications in real-time monitoring, anomaly detection, and failure prediction across urban energy assets such as smart grids, HVAC systems, and renewable energy platforms. It also examines the use of machine learning models for compliance verification, risk scoring, and automated reporting in dynamic urban settings. Emphasis is placed on integrating AI with Internet of Things (IoT) networks and Building Information Modeling (BIM) for seamless data ingestion, contextual analysis, and lifecycle asset management. Case studies from global urban energy projects illustrate practical applications, performance benefits, and deployment challenges. Finally, the review outlines key barriers, policy recommendations, and future research directions for scalable, trustworthy, and intelligent infrastructure compliance solutions that support sustainable urban growth and energy resilience.

title: People, places and politics: A systemized review of public opposition to high voltage transmission lines.
summary: As modern society shifts toward clean and renewable energy, expanding and modernizing high-voltage transmission line (HVTL) infrastructure has become essential. However, planning and constructing these large-scale lines frequently encounter
content: As modern society shifts toward clean and renewable energy, expanding and modernizing high-voltage transmission line (HVTL) infrastructure has become essential. However, planning and constructing these large-scale lines frequently encounters significant resistance from local communities and landowners. While historical debates and popular commentary often dismissed this resistance as self-interest or "Not In My Backyard" (NIMBY) sentiment, decades of research demonstrate that public responses are driven by multi-dimensional concerns. The primary purpose of this project is to synthesize what is currently known about why citizens and stakeholders oppose transmission line projects and to trace how these concerns have evolved over time. By bringing together global empirical research conducted between 2012 and 2026, the project seeks to bridge persistent knowledge gaps regarding how community reactions develop, how disagreements emerge between developers and host communities, and why certain infrastructure proposals face intense dispute. Rather than viewing public opposition through a single lens, this research organizes the diverse drivers of public opposition into four related areas: 1. Proximity: Examining how physical distance influences community concern. 2. Individual Perceptions: Capturing aesthetics, perceived property valuations, as well as perceived health and environmental risks. 3. Community Dynamics: Understanding the attributes of host communities, particularly local landscapes, place identity, and collective action. 4. Institutions: Investigating how institutional trust, procedural fairness, meaningful citizen engagement, and broader political contexts shape whether communities accept or reject transmission decisions. The primary deliverable of this work will be a comprehensive theoretical framework that integrates geographic, psychological, social, and political factors into a unified model of public opposition. Additionally, the project will analyze historical trends in public sentiment over the past decade and a half. By pinpointing where the existing evidence remains sparse, contradictory, or methodologically incomplete, the final synthesis will deliver policy recommendations to help policymaker more collaborative and effective infrastructure siting processes.

title: Enhancing solar conversion efficiency of CdTe-based absorber solar cells via SCAPS-1D simulation
summary: Abstract The growing global energy demand and the need for new sources have driven significant advancements in energy storage technologies, which are essential for improving energy sustainability and efficiency. Cadmium telluride (CdTe) is
content: Abstract The growing global energy demand and the need for new sources have driven significant advancements in energy storage technologies, which are essential for improving energy sustainability and efficiency. Cadmium telluride (CdTe) is one of the most efficient and cost-effective thin-film solar cell materials with an ideal band gap between 1.44 eV and 1.5 eV. CdTe is a long-standing material in the fabrication of solar cells for its ideal band gap and high optical absorption coefficient. This is a promising material due to its efficient devices and cost ratio because of its large flexibility in the manufacturing process. Due to its properties, CdTe has been regarded as a material for producing high-efficiency solar cells. In the ideal band gap range, which is suitable for the solar cell spectrum and maximum absorption (more than 90%) of incoming photons at a thickness of 2 µm. CdTe is the absorber; the cadmium sulphide (CdS) film and the back contact are the typical layers that make up the conventional structure of a superstrate CdTe solar cell. An absorber layer with Nickel oxide (NiO) as the window layer was investigated in order to enhance the Photovoltaic (PV) system’s device features as well as parameters. To assess the effectiveness of the thin-film solar cell architectures, can be modelled utilising computer simulations. The efficiency of CdTe Photovoltaic (PV) cells was found to be 27.7% by simulation in SCAPS-1D simulation software.

title: Research on Forecasting International Energy Price Volatility based on Model Combination
source: Transactions on Environment Energy and Earth Sciences
summary: As an important support for the national economy, the volatility of international energy price is of great importance to the stability of the national economy, the maintenance of social stability and the protection of national security. The
content: As an important support for the national economy, the volatility of international energy price is of great importance to the stability of the national economy, the maintenance of social stability and the protection of national security. The modeling and forecasting of international energy market price volatility based on many forecasting factors have attracted more and more attention. The model combination method, which can integrate the strengths of various models, is widely used in the field of financial forecasting. In view of this, based on the monthly volatility data of international energy market, macroeconomic variables, uncertainty index and AR extended model from January 1994 to December 2022, this paper adopts five model combination forecasting methods for the prediction of international energy price volatility, and the adaptability of the model combination to different predictors and its performance in predicting the volatility of different energy markets are discussed. Through empirical study, it is found that the forecasting ability of single macroeconomic variable is not satisfactory when forecasting international energy price volatility, but the model combination forecasting method can significantly improve the forecasting accuracy of international crude oil market volatility, and the model combination forecasting based on the uncertainty index performs well in both the crude oil market and the natural gas market. Therefore, this paper can provide some empirical basis for international energy market investors to carry out risk management and portfolio optimization, and also help policy makers grasp the timing of policy issuance and implementation.

title: Global Risk Transmission and Monetary Stability in Brunei Darussalam: Evidence from a Time-Varying Parameter VAR Approach
summary: This study investigates the impact of global risk factors specifically geopolitical risk (GPR), economic policy uncertainty (GEPU), market volatility (VIX), and commodity price dynamics on the monetary stability of Brunei Darussalam. Given
content: This study investigates the impact of global risk factors specifically geopolitical risk (GPR), economic policy uncertainty (GEPU), market volatility (VIX), and commodity price dynamics on the monetary stability of Brunei Darussalam. Given the vulnerability of small open economies to external shocks, understanding the transmission mechanism of these risks is critical for maintaining the resilience of the Brunei Dollar (BND) peg. Utilizing monthly data from January 2015 to May 2025, the empirical analysis employs a dual-stage econometric framework: the Toda–Yamamoto Granger causality test for static inference and the Time-Varying Parameter Vector Autoregression (TVP-VAR) model for dynamic assessment. The results reveal that geopolitical tensions and gold prices are the predominant long-term predictors of exchange rate fluctuations. Furthermore, the dynamic connectedness analysis indicates that the transmission of global shocks is regime-dependent, intensifying significantly during systemic crises such as the COVID-19 pandemic and the 2022 geopolitical escalation in Ukraine. While digital assets exhibit limited influence, the study confirms that Brunei’s monetary stability remains deeply integrated into global energy and safe-haven markets. These findings underscore the necessity for the Brunei Darussalam Central Bank (BDCB) to adopt adaptive, time-varying macro-prudential monitoring to mitigate cross-border risk spillovers effectively in the future.

title: Iot for Smart Homes and Energy Conservation Technologies, Applications, Challenges, and Future Perspectives
source: International Research Journal on Advanced Engineering and Management (IRJAEM)
summary: The Internet of Things (IoT) is transforming residential environments by connecting electrical appliances, sensors, smart meters, controllers, and communication networks to enable intelligent monitoring and automated control. Smart homes us
content: The Internet of Things (IoT) is transforming residential environments by connecting electrical appliances, sensors, smart meters, controllers, and communication networks to enable intelligent monitoring and automated control. Smart homes use IoT technologies to improve energy efficiency, reduce unnecessary electricity consumption, enhance user convenience, and support sustainable living. This paper presents a review of IoT-based smart-home systems with particular emphasis on sensing technologies, home automation, energy monitoring, communication protocols, and data privacy. It discusses how temperature, occupancy, light, and current sensors can be integrated with microcontrollers and intelligent control systems to optimize lighting, heating, ventilation, air conditioning, and other household loads. The paper also examines technologies such as Wi-Fi, Bluetooth Low Energy, Zigbee, Thread, and Matter, along with cloud-based and edge-computing approaches. Despite their advantages, IoT-enabled homes face challenges related to interoperability, cybersecurity, installation costs, reliability, and user privacy. The review concludes that combining secure communication, local intelligence, interoperable devices, and energy-aware automation can contribute to more efficient, reliable, and sustainable residential energy management.

title: Steady-State and Dynamic Validation of Renewable Transition Pathways: An Automated PLEXOS-PSS/E Simulation Framework
summary: Techno-economic planning identifies renewable generation, storage, and flexibility portfolios but cannot establish their AC-network feasibility or dynamic security. This study develops an automated Python framework coupling PLEXOS planning
content: Techno-economic planning identifies renewable generation, storage, and flexibility portfolios but cannot establish their AC-network feasibility or dynamic security. This study develops an automated Python framework coupling PLEXOS planning with steady-state and RMS dynamic assessment in PSS/E. Critical hourly operating conditions are transferred into network cases, tested against disturbances, and evaluated using voltage, frequency nadir, and rate of change of frequency (RoCoF). The framework is demonstrated across four systems (23–505 nodes) and successive renewable energy sources (RES) penetration stages. Across 144–256 screened PSS/E cases per system, the largest individual violation category affected 12.24–41.67% of cases, establishing a conservative minimum affected-case share and revealing technical limitations not represented in the upstream planning assessment, including AC-feasibility, voltage-recovery, and frequency-security limitations. Both benchmark systems exhibited their highest RoCoF near 75% RES rather than at maximum penetration; the IEEE 39-node case reached 1.87 Hz/s, while its lowest nadir occurred at 50% RES. Halving available fast frequency response increased peak RoCoF by 0.05–0.11 Hz/s and lowered nadir by 0.05–0.50 Hz. These findings show that critical transition stages depend on synchronous inertia, network flows, operating conditions, and flexibility deployment. The framework also identifies actionable requirements, including regional voltage support and transmission reinforcement, for subsequent long-term planning.

title: From Skills Gaps to Energy Resilience: Building a Territorialized Solar Workforce Ecosystem in Indonesia
summary: Indonesia’s electricity plan for 2025–2034 projects 69.5 GW of additional generation capacity, including 17.1 GW of solar power, while government estimates associate the plan with 348,057 solar-related job opportunities. These projections m
content: Indonesia’s electricity plan for 2025–2034 projects 69.5 GW of additional generation capacity, including 17.1 GW of solar power, while government estimates associate the plan with 348,057 solar-related job opportunities. These projections make workforce capability a material implementation issue: renewable infrastructure requires technicians, engineers, safety specialists, project managers and locally available operations-and-maintenance personnel. Yet headline job estimates do not reveal whether workers are available in the required occupations, locations or project phases. This article examines how workforce development can be linked to the resilience of solar infrastructure in an archipelagic state. It uses a focused qualitative documentary analysis, official Indonesian planning and employment documents, and international institutional evidence, interpreted through energy security, capacity development and energy justice perspectives. The analysis identifies four interlocking governance gaps: incomplete skills intelligence; weak alignment between training, certification and project demand; uneven territorial distribution of operational capability; and limited feedback from infrastructure performance into workforce planning. The article proposes a territorialized solar workforce resilience framework in which workforce data, competency standards, work-based learning, local maintenance capacity and critical-infrastructure performance are planned together. The framework is a theory-building contribution, not an estimate of causal effects. Before journal submission, its propositions require validation through comparative project-level fieldwork and verified occupational data.

title: A Physically Consistent AI Framework for Predictive Design of Microfluidic Double Emulsions Toward Precision Liposome Fabrication
summary: Microfluidic double emulsions offer a powerful route for templated liposome fabrication; however, precise and reproducible control over droplet architecture remains challenging due to the highly nonlinear coupling between flow dynamics and
content: Microfluidic double emulsions offer a powerful route for templated liposome fabrication; however, precise and reproducible control over droplet architecture remains challenging due to the highly nonlinear coupling between flow dynamics and interfacial phenomena. Here, we present a physics-consistent, data-driven framework that combines artificial neural networks (ANNs) with genetic algorithms (GAs) to enable predictive inverse design and target-driven optimization of double-emulsion generation. By systematically varying lipid concentration, surfactant concentration, and flow-rate parameters within a flow-focusing microfluidic platform, the ANN model learns the underlying relationships governing droplet formation with near-unity predictive accuracy. Coupling the trained model with a GA enables precise control of droplet morphology, demonstrated here by the generation of droplets with a targeted 30 µm core diameter and 5 µm shell thickness, resulting in liposomes with diameters of approximately 30 µm after solvent extraction. Experimental results closely matched the model predictions for both the selected processing conditions and the resulting droplet properties, confirming the reliability of the proposed framework. The flow-related parameters had the greatest impact on droplet diameter and production frequency. This study demonstrates a practical, interpretable AI-guided optimization approach for complex microfluidic platforms, while offering a scalable route for the fabrication of liposomes and other structured soft-material systems.

title: Optimized Power Flow and Efficient Load Sharing in DC Microgrid Systems
source: The International Journal of Maritime Engineering
summary: Existing power management strategies for interconnected DC microgrids often face limitations such as poor adaptability to nonlinear dynamics, inefficient handling of renewable intermittency, and slow convergence of optimization-based contro
content: Existing power management strategies for interconnected DC microgrids often face limitations such as poor adaptability to nonlinear dynamics, inefficient handling of renewable intermittency, and slow convergence of optimization-based controllers, which hinder stable bidirectional power sharing and voltage regulation. To address these gaps, this work proposes an Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System with Dingo Optimizer (ANFIS-DO) for intelligent power flow management in DC microgrids integrating PV generation, battery energy storage, and a Dual Active Bridge (DAB) converter. The PV subsystem with MPPT and boost converter maximizes energy harvesting under variable irradiance, while the DAB ensures efficient bidirectional transfer and voltage stability. ANFIS models complex nonlinear relationships among inputs such as bus voltage error, power mismatch, PV variation, state of charge, and duty cycle to generate optimized control signals. The Dingo Optimizer fine-tunes ANFIS parameters by mimicking encircling, hunting, and attacking behaviors, thus balancing exploration and exploitation for faster convergence. Simulation results validate that ANFIS-DO achieves minimal tracking errors (RMSE 0.08 kW), balanced grid load sharing (48% vs. 44%), and superior computational efficiency (1.8 s, 65 iterations), consistently outperforming Firefly Algorithm (FFA) and Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA), thereby establishing its effectiveness in adaptive, stable, and reliable DC microgrid power management.

title: Horizontal Soil Reaction of a Pile Segment in Cohesive Soil with Interface Slip
summary: Abstract Under lateral loading, relative slip between a pile and the surrounding soil can occur at displacements as small as 10 − 4 pile diameters. Conventional p – y formulations, widely used in the analysis of slender laterally loaded pil
content: Abstract Under lateral loading, relative slip between a pile and the surrounding soil can occur at displacements as small as 10 − 4 pile diameters. Conventional p – y formulations, widely used in the analysis of slender laterally loaded piles, assume perfect bonding between pile and soil and do not explicitly account for the progressive interface slip, which can yield unconservative overpredictions of the overall pile stiffness. This note presents a novel semianalytical theoretical solution to predict the degradation of the elastic p – y stiffness due to the progressive slip at a cohesive pile-soil interface. The solution is developed in two dimensions by expanding the stress and displacement fields around the pile in Fourier series in the angular direction, and employing discretization at the pile-soil interface and outer boundary to satisfy boundary conditions. The formulation provides a computationally efficient alternative to finite-element and finite-difference analyses, against which it is validated, while preserving physical transparency and simple calibration. The resultant solution allows progressive interface behavior to be incorporated in a p – y analysis, providing a more realistic representation of lateral pile response under serviceability limit states.

title: SmartKrishi-AI: A Survey of AI-Integrated Agriculture Decision Support and Farm Resource Management
source: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
summary: Agricultural choices depend heavily on a complex mix of environmental variables, including soil properties, fluctuating weather patterns, crop compatibility, market dynamics, pest threats, and the availability of vital farming resources. Mo
content: Agricultural choices depend heavily on a complex mix of environmental variables, including soil properties, fluctuating weather patterns, crop compatibility, market dynamics, pest threats, and the availability of vital farming resources. Most contemporary digital services target only one of these factors, forcing growers to manually gather data from multiple disconnected websites and local contacts. This paper reviews recent developments related to SmartKrishi–AI, a conceptual, integrated platform designed for agricultural decision-making and asset coordination. Our analysis evaluates several vital domains, including crop recommendation frameworks, weather forecasting networks, commodity price models, plant disease diagnostics, public welfare discovery, equipment leasing, and labor scheduling. We analyze recent research from 2023 to 2026 indexed across major venues such as IEEE, Elsevier/ScienceDirect, and MDPI, exploring their mathematical approaches, dataset constraints, evaluation methods, and practical challenges. Based on these insights, we introduce a conceptual multilayer architecture that connects data-driven analytical models with verified institutional channels and peer-to-peer resource exchange workflows. Because the proposed ecosystem serves as a structural blueprint rather than an experimentally fieldtested software tool, no project-specific crop yield or predictive precision increases are claimed. Finally, we highlight persistent open challenges in this sector, such as data quality gaps, geographic adaptation limits, model interpretability, forecast volatility, system interoperability, regional language support, and the necessity for rigorous field trials.

title: Membranes or solution? Reassessing open-circuit voltage losses in a natural-water reverse electrodialysis pilot
summary: Abstract The open-circuit voltage (OCV) of a reverse electrodialysis (RED) stack reflects solution activities, membrane selectivity and the salinity gradients established during operation. The differences between measured and ideal OCV can
content: Abstract The open-circuit voltage (OCV) of a reverse electrodialysis (RED) stack reflects solution activities, membrane selectivity and the salinity gradients established during operation. The differences between measured and ideal OCV can arise from solution nonideality, imperfect membrane response and transport-induced changes in the local concentration gradients.. Published pilot data from Okinawa, with seawater or reverse-osmosis brine against river water, were reanalyzed with multicomponent Pitzer activities and independently measured membrane properties. Solution non-ideality and membrane response together account for only 19–33% of the deficit; the remaining 67–81% cannot be allocated with the available data. The split also depends on the ideal reference chosen for the river water, which is not NaCl-like. As a consequence, the OCV deficits obtained with natural waters should be reported together with their reference and interpreted only alongside independent membrane and stack measurements.

title: Μελέτη της ποιότητας ανάφλεξης των φυτικών ελαίων και των μεθυλεστέρων των λιπαρών οξέων ως υποκατάστατων των συμβατικών καυσίμων
source: DSpace - NTUA (National Technical University of Athens)
