title: Nitrogen–nitrogen bond-containing natural products: isolation, bioactivity, synthesis, biosynthesis, and pharmacology
summary: Natural products that contain nitrogen-nitrogen (N-N) bonds are a class of natural products consisting of multiple functional groups with important biological activities. Currently, such molecules have been widely isolated from microorganis
content: Natural products that contain nitrogen-nitrogen (N-N) bonds are a class of natural products consisting of multiple functional groups with important biological activities. Currently, such molecules have been widely isolated from microorganisms, plants, and marine organisms. In recent years, due to the novel skeletal structures and unique biological activities of these compounds, research into their synthetic routes and mechanisms of action continues to be increasingly in-depth. Therefore, this review summarizes the isolation and identification of 131 N-N bond-containing compounds of microbial origin, biosynthesis and synthesis, with special emphasis on the summary of the mechanism of N-N bond formation and pharmacological elaboration during the period of 2014-2024, laying the foundation for future research into the drug development potential of compounds containing N-N bonds.

title: A ribosome-dependent small-ORF switch controls flagellar gene expression and virulence
summary: RNA structures are active regulators of bacterial translation. Here, we identified a naturally occurring translation-enhancing small open reading frame (tesORF) that controls the expression of the flagellar operon fliFGHIJK in Salmonella en
content: RNA structures are active regulators of bacterial translation. Here, we identified a naturally occurring translation-enhancing small open reading frame (tesORF) that controls the expression of the flagellar operon fliFGHIJK in Salmonella enterica and other motile Enterobacterales. Nucleotide-resolution ribosome profiling revealed this previously unannotated 54-nucleotide ORF immediately upstream of fliF. Genetic, transcriptomic, and biochemical analyses support a model in which tesORF translation counteracts an inhibitory RNA structure, exposing the fliF ribosome-binding site and promoting translation initiation independently of the encoded peptide sequence. Disruption of tesORF translation reduced expression of the downstream operon and impaired motility and virulence-associated phenotypes in Escherichia coli, Salmonella, and Yersinia. Together, our findings reveal how translation of a conserved small ORF regulates an entire flagellar operon through RNA structural remodelling, with consequences expending to the wider flagellar regulon, linking RNA structural dynamics to bacterial motility and virulence.

title: Ferrites for the Magnetically Induced CO 2 Reduction
summary: CO 2 mitigation is one of the most urgent issues humanity needs to address, and magnetically induced catalysis could be a powerful tool to contribute to this goal. Developing dual‐functional materials (DFMs) that can act both as catalysts a
content: CO 2 mitigation is one of the most urgent issues humanity needs to address, and magnetically induced catalysis could be a powerful tool to contribute to this goal. Developing dual‐functional materials (DFMs) that can act both as catalysts and as heating agents under an external magnetic field is challenging. Yet, it could unlock the full potential of induction heating for CO 2 valorization. In this work, we present a series of CoFe 2 O 4 and NiFe 2 O 4 ‐based DFMs capable of catalyzing the reduction of this greenhouse gas in the range 220–300 °C, under low alternating magnetic fields (19.6–39.2 mT, 100 kHz frequency). The reduction pretreatment is closely linked to their heating ability, since alloy formation plays a fundamental role in magnetically induced energy dissipation as heat. CoFe 2 O 4 prepared via a sol–gel autocombustion route exhibits the highest catalytic activity ( ≈ 60%, S CO = 95% at 300 °C), along with the best heating ability, where the formation of localized hot spots under magnetic induction may contribute to the observed performance. Accordingly, it emerges as a reference candidate for magnetically induced CO 2 reduction.

title: The Effects of Entrepreneurial Education Frameworks on Students' Perceived Feasibility and Perceived Desirability on Intentions to Start a New Venture: A Casual-Comparative Approach
summary: This purpose of this quantitative casual comparative study was to determine if there is a difference between perceived feasibility, perceived desirability, and intentions to create a new business among university students experiencing diffe
content: This purpose of this quantitative casual comparative study was to determine if there is a difference between perceived feasibility, perceived desirability, and intentions to create a new business among university students experiencing different entrepreneurship education frameworks: about. for, and through. This is important because of the rapid growth of entrepreneurship education, and the current understanding of what and how to teach entrepreneurship remains a research domain that requires coherence in instructional approaches, content, and accurate reporting of student outcomes. This study responds to the calls for research that clarify how these different frameworks influence student outcomes. Data was collected using the Entrepreneurial Event Questionnaire (EEQ) administered through Qualtrics from entrepreneurial college students in a northern state (N=225). A One-way MANOVA demonstrated a statistically significant, Wilks' Lambda, F(4, 444) = 5.373, p = <.001; Wilks' Λ = .909; partial η2 = .046. The researcher rejected the null hypothesis of no significant differences among perceived feasibility, perceived desirability, and entrepreneurial intentions. The data analysis showed that perceived feasibility differed significantly across frameworks, while perceived desirability and intention scores did not. The results indicate that the educational framework may influence student confidence in their capabilities, while motivational desire and intent to start a new venture do not. It is suggested that future research explore alternative instruments, expanded geographical approaches, and mixed-method design capturing nonlinear approaches to entrepreneurship education.

title: Assessing the Risk of Aquatic Nuisance Species Transfer from Ballast Water Discharge: Establishment of Great Lakes Focal Ports to Determine Interlake Transfer
summary: Understanding risks posed by cargo ships that operate exclusively within the Great Lakes (‘Lakers’) to contribute to secondary dispersal of aquatic nuisance species (ANS) is important for the development of policy to protect against future
content: Understanding risks posed by cargo ships that operate exclusively within the Great Lakes (‘Lakers’) to contribute to secondary dispersal of aquatic nuisance species (ANS) is important for the development of policy to protect against future range expansion of harmful biota throughout Great Lakes waters including high-traffic port environments. To evaluate the potential for Lakers to contribute to range expansion of ANS and native biota among port environments and explore recent changes to the inventory of ANS and native biota in port environments, we conducted a set of studies focused on understanding spatial and temporal variation in crustacean zooplankton diversity at four high-risk ports (focal ports) including Duluth-Superior, Two Harbors, and Marquette on Lake Superior, and Toledo on Lake Erie. The results are contained in four studies spanning 2023 to 2026. Our primary objectives were to: (1) design, implement, and evaluate a broad-spectrum monitoring program to characterize crustacean zooplankton diversity at the focal ports; (2) identify changes in crustacean zooplankton diversity in the Duluth-Superior port over a 15-year gap between 2007/2008 and 2024/2025; and (3) implement target-species monitoring to determine if the invasive bloody red shrimp (Hemimysis anomala) is established in the Duluth-Superior port. MAJOR ACCOMPLISHMENTS/FINDINGS A broad-spectrum monitoring program was designed, implemented, and evaluated tocharacterize crustacean zooplankton diversity at four focal ports identified as presenting elevated risks of species dispersal through ballast-water transport including Duluth-Superior, Two Harbors, and Marquette on Lake Superior, and Toledo on Lake Erie. Theprogram offers a blueprint for the design of future monitoring programs and a baseline of information for determination of potential shifts in diversity over time. Findings showed that crustacean zooplankton species richness increased from 2007/2008to 2024/2025 in the Duluth-Superior port and nearby waters, in part due to additional non-native taxa (Diaphanosoma fluviatile, Nitokra hibernica, and Thermocyclopscrassus), but primarily caused by increases to native species inventories. Findings produced the first published evidence of an established population of the invasive bloody red shrimp (Hemimysis anomala) in the Duluth-Superior port, making it the first documentation in Lake Superior. Findings demonstrated that bloody red shrimp occupied no less than seven locations in the Duluth-Superior port in 2026 across Wisconsin and Minnesota waters including waters adjacent to public recreational watercraft landings, a result that could intensify the risk of its dispersal to inland regional waterbodies.

title: MuEdit: An efficient multi-task editing method towards inter-domain knowledge conflicts
summary: Large language models (LLMs) require frequent knowledge updates across heterogeneous domains, but existing editing methods fail when applied sequentially to multi-task settings. We trace this collapse to inter-domain null-space misalignment
content: Large language models (LLMs) require frequent knowledge updates across heterogeneous domains, but existing editing methods fail when applied sequentially to multi-task settings. We trace this collapse to inter-domain null-space misalignment: heterogeneous tasks induce distinct Jacobian geometries, causing their common null space to shrink dramatically and leaving insufficient admissible directions for conflict-free updates. We propose the Conflict Index to quantify this geometric interference, and introduce Mu-Edit, which mitigates multi-task conflicts via (1) conflict-aware ordering to minimize cumulative interference, and (2) dynamic low-rank approximation to expand the null space when ordering alone is insufficient. Experiments across five functional domains and three backbones show that Mu-Edit significantly outperforms existing baselines in multi-task editing performance while preserving general capabilities, and remains effective under incremental task arrival.

title: Weathering the Divide: Social Determinants, Neighborhood Context, and Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Among African American Women
source: Digital Commons - East Tennessee State University (East Tennessee State University)
summary: Background: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) disproportionately affects African American women and contributes to racial health disparities in the United States. Although genetic susceptibility influences disease risk, growing evidence su
content: Background: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) disproportionately affects African American women and contributes to racial health disparities in the United States. Although genetic susceptibility influences disease risk, growing evidence suggests that social determinants of health (SDOH), including neighborhood conditions, structural racism, and socioeconomic disadvantage, contribute to disease development and progression. Epigenetic mechanisms may provide a biological pathway linking adverse social conditions to chronic disease disparities. This dissertation examined the influence of SDOH on SLE disparities through evidence synthesis and empirical investigation to inform public health practice and policy. Methods: This integrated learning experience consisted of three complementary manuscripts. Aim 1 was a PRISMA-ScR scoping review examining associations among SDOH, epigenetic mechanisms, and chronic disease outcomes. Aim 2 was a secondary cross-sectional analysis of baseline data from a case-control study the Social Factors, Epigenomics, and Lupus in African American Women (SELA) Study examining neighborhood racial composition and SLE disease activity using generalized estimating equations (GEE). Aim 3 was a secondary case-control analysis of SELA data examining neighborhood racial composition and confirmed SLE diagnosis using GEE. Results: Aim 1: Twenty-two studies demonstrated associations between adverse SDOH, epigenetic alterations, and chronic disease outcomes. Neighborhood disadvantage, economic instability, food insecurity, adverse childhood experiences, and discrimination were associated with accelerated biological aging and poorer health outcomes, whereas educational attainment, social capital, supportive relationships, and neighborhood resources were protective. Aim 2: Neighborhood racial composition was not associated with SLE disease activity after adjustment for age and educational attainment; however, lower educational attainment was associated with greater disease activity. Aim 3: Neighborhood racial composition was associated with confirmed SLE diagnosis after adjustment for age, educational attainment, and Sea Islander status. Each one-percentage-point increase in neighborhood African American composition was associated with approximately 2.3% higher odds of SLE diagnosis. Conclusions: Adverse SDOH contribute to chronic disease disparities through individual- and neighborhood-level pathways. Neighborhood racial composition was associated with SLE diagnosis but not disease activity, suggesting neighborhood context may influence disease occurrence more than disease severity. These findings support public health policies and community interventions that address structural inequities and neighborhood disadvantage to reduce SLE disparities among African American women.

title: DIALEKTIKA HUKUM WARIS ADAT DAN ISLAM: MENEGOSIASIKAN KEADILAN DALAM PEMBAGIAN HARTA WARISAN
summary: Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis dialektika antara hukum waris adat dan hukum waris Islam dalam membangun pola pembagian harta warisan yang berkeadilan di Indonesia. Penelitian menggunakan metode yuridis-normatif dengan pendekatan peru
content: Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis dialektika antara hukum waris adat dan hukum waris Islam dalam membangun pola pembagian harta warisan yang berkeadilan di Indonesia. Penelitian menggunakan metode yuridis-normatif dengan pendekatan perundang-undangan, konseptual, historis, dan komparatif melalui studi kepustakaan. Sumber data meliputi Al-Qur’an, hadis, Kompilasi Hukum Islam, peraturan perundang-undangan, buku, artikel jurnal, disertasi, dan penelitian terdahulu yang relevan. Data dianalisis secara deskriptif-analitis, komparatif, dan interpretatif untuk mengidentifikasi pola interaksi serta ruang negosiasi antara kedua sistem hukum. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa hukum waris Islam dan hukum waris adat tidak selalu berada dalam posisi yang berlawanan, tetapi dapat berinteraksi melalui proses adaptasi, musyawarah, ?ul?, hibah, wasiat, dan kesepakatan keluarga. Hukum Islam memberikan kerangka normatif mengenai hak kewarisan, sedangkan hukum adat menghadirkan konteks sosial dan kultural yang memengaruhi pola pembagian warisan. Keadilan dalam pembagian warisan tidak semata-mata diukur berdasarkan kesamaan nominal, tetapi juga mempertimbangkan hak, kebutuhan, tanggung jawab, relasi kekerabatan, dan kemaslahatan keluarga. Penelitian ini merekomendasikan penguatan literasi hukum kewarisan serta penelitian empiris pada berbagai komunitas adat untuk menguji model negosiasi keadilan dalam praktik.

title: Financial slack, capital intensity, and firm performance: Evidence from global listed firms
summary: Financial slack may preserve operating continuity and investment capacity, but excess resources can weaken financial discipline. This study examines the within-firm association between financial slack and firm performance and formally tests
content: Financial slack may preserve operating continuity and investment capacity, but excess resources can weaken financial discipline. This study examines the within-firm association between financial slack and firm performance and formally tests whether it varies with capital intensity and growth opportunities. We construct a pooled-standardized, equally weighted Financial Slack Index from cash holdings, liquidity, and unused debt capacity for 4,832 firm-year observations from 524 listed firms in 21 countries during 2016-2025. Firm and year fixed-effects models are complemented by country-year effects, country-exclusion and equal-weighting checks, wild-country bootstrap inference, COVID-period tests, alternative index construction, and omitted-variable sensitivity analysis. Financial slack is positively associated with return on assets (b = 0.0170, p < .001) and market-to-assets. Capital intensity is negatively associated with performance, whereas the continuous financial-slack-by-capital-intensity interaction is insignificant. Formal slope comparisons show weak evidence of a stronger association among high-capital-intensity firms (p = .099), but strong evidence among high-growth firms (p < .001). The financial-slack slope does not differ across pre-COVID, COVID, and post-COVID periods. Results remain positive under country-year effects and after excluding the two dominant countries. The evidence supports financial slack as conditional financial flexibility, especially for growing firms, while remaining associative rather than causal.

title: SMART RETAILING IN INTERNET COMMERCE: AN AI-ENABLED CUSTOMER-CENTRIC SERVICE FRAMEWORK
source: EPH - International Journal of Business & Management Science
summary: This conceptual paper examines AI-enabled smart retailing as a customer-facing service transformation in Internet commerce rather than as a narrow technological or operational innovation. Drawing on a selective, theory-driven synthesis of s
content: This conceptual paper examines AI-enabled smart retailing as a customer-facing service transformation in Internet commerce rather than as a narrow technological or operational innovation. Drawing on a selective, theory-driven synthesis of services marketing, smart retailing, AI-enabled marketing, customer experience, service-dominant logic, human–AI interaction, and responsible-AI research, it develops a three-layer framework linking AI-enabled service capabilities, customer-experience mechanisms, and Internet-commerce outcomes. The framework identifies three capability groups—algorithmic personalisation and decision support, AI-mediated service interaction, and predictive service intelligence—and four evaluative mechanisms: decision value, interaction quality, transaction confidence, and algorithmic legitimacy. These mechanisms shape customer satisfaction, engagement, service-recovery effectiveness, platform trust, relationship quality, continuance intention, value co-creation, and inclusive service value. Human–AI governance, including privacy protection, transparency, fairness, customer control, human review, and digital accessibility, is treated as a boundary condition that determines whether AI-enabled services are perceived as trustworthy and customer-centred or as intrusive, opaque, unfair, and exclusionary. The paper contributes to Internet-commerce research by repositioning AI as a service-enabling capability and by explaining how customer evaluations translate AI applications into commercial and relational outcomes. It also proposes a focused research agenda for empirical testing across e-commerce websites, mobile applications, online marketplaces, social-commerce platforms, and omnichannel systems.

title: The Impact of Actigraphic Data Processing on the Quantification and Pattern Analysis of Human Locomotor Activity
source: SZTE Repository of Dissertations (University of Szeged)
summary: Actigraphy is a multidisciplinary method of measuring human locomotor activity using wrist-worn, accelerometer-based devices. A major limitation of this method is that devices from different manufacturers often compress raw acceleration dat
content: Actigraphy is a multidisciplinary method of measuring human locomotor activity using wrist-worn, accelerometer-based devices. A major limitation of this method is that devices from different manufacturers often compress raw acceleration data into activity values using different and proprietary algorithms, which significantly hinders the reproducibility and comparability of studies. In this work, I comprehensively explored the activity determination methods available in the literature, and we synthesized them into a two-stage, generalized data processing pipeline. Then, I systematically compared these methods by applying them to real-world, wrist-measured acceleration signals, thereby emulating the operation of various commercial actigraphs. The impact of these signal processing steps was quantified through correlation analysis, as well as by comparing circadian rhythm indicators and sleep-wake classifications extracted from the resulting activity signals. I showed that different actigraphs can quantify the exact same motion in vastly different ways, potentially inducing deviations in clinical indicators that exceed those typically associated with pathological conditions. Rather than employing the widely used approach based on probability distribution functions, I investigated the scale-invariant properties of locomotor activity in the spectral domain. Based on an extensive analysis, we showed that both multi-day raw acceleration signals and activity signals derived from them exhibit universal, scale-free spectral characteristics, including 1/f noise, which closely aligns with our observations regarding the spectral patterns of spatial displacement data. To achieve this, I analyzed the power spectral density (PSD) and the fluctuation function of the multiday signals, applying a Daniell method-based variance reduction technique to the PSD estimates. We found that this spectral approach is considerably less methodology-dependent than traditional statistical-distribution-based evaluations. However, my analyses also revealed that when separating actigraphic time series into sleep and wake periods, the fluctuation analyses widely used in clinical research can be heavily biased by device-specific signal processing and the presence of measurement errors.

title: A stabilized abdominal imaging platform for intravital interrogation of preclinical omental metastatic niche models
summary: The omentum is a highly specialized immunological and metabolic tissue that frequently acts as a permissive niche for metastatic dissemination within the peritoneal cavity. Despite its central role in metastatic progression and therapeutic
content: The omentum is a highly specialized immunological and metabolic tissue that frequently acts as a permissive niche for metastatic dissemination within the peritoneal cavity. Despite its central role in metastatic progression and therapeutic response, real-time interrogation of the omental microenvironment in preclinical in vivo models remains technically challenging because of respiratory motion, tissue drift, and the fragility of abdominal tissues. Current methodologies largely rely on endpoint analyses or invasive tissue externalization procedures that disrupt physiological tissue dynamics and limit longitudinal investigation. Here, we present a mechanically stabilized abdominal imaging platform that enables high-resolution longitudinal intravital imaging of the omentum in live mice. The system combines a custom abdominal imaging window with a lift-support stabilization structure that mechanically isolates the omentum from respiratory motion while preserving tissue architecture and physiological immune cell behavior. Using fluorescent reporters, we demonstrate stable, long-term visualization of tumor progression, immune cell recruitment, and adoptive cell transfer targeting within the omental niche. As a proof-of-concept application, the platform was validated using an omentum-tropic model of peritoneal ovarian cancer dissemination, enabling longitudinal monitoring of metastatic engraftment and spatiotemporal immune dynamics during locoregional immunotherapy. Importantly, imaging through the stabilized window preserved lymphocyte motility significantly better than conventional tissue externalization approaches, thereby supporting the physiological relevance of the system. Overall, this platform provides a robust, adaptable framework for studying immune and metastatic processes in the peritoneal cavity and may facilitate preclinical evaluation of intraperitoneal therapies, cell-based immunotherapies, and microenvironment-targeted interventions.

title: Digitalisation, Eco‐Innovation and SME Internationalisation: A Dynamic Capabilities Perspective
summary: ABSTRACT This study integrates the digitalisation and dynamic capabilities literature to examine the relationship between digitalisation, eco‐innovation and internationalisation in small and medium‐sized enterprises (SME). Using data obtain
content: ABSTRACT This study integrates the digitalisation and dynamic capabilities literature to examine the relationship between digitalisation, eco‐innovation and internationalisation in small and medium‐sized enterprises (SME). Using data obtained from 300 SME owner‐managers operating in the United Kingdom, the findings suggest that digitalisation positively impacts eco‐innovation and consequently the nature of internationalisation activities. In addition, there is a moderating effect of internationalisation experience on the relationship between eco‐innovation and internationalisation. These findings highlight the pivotal role of eco‐innovation, digitalisation and international experience in enabling SMEs to thrive in international markets. Furthermore, the study offers empirical evidence of how SMEs dynamically develop digital resources, and internationalisation is an outcome of building such capabilities. The implications for practice and future research avenues are examined.

title: Kepemimpinan Transformasional, Kepuasan Kerja, dan Kinerja Karyawan: Peran Mediasi Komitmen Organisasi pada Suku Dinas Tenaga Kerja, Transmigrasi, dan Energi Kota Jakarta Utara
source: Jurnal Ilmiah Ekonomi dan Manajemen Indonesia
summary: Kinerja Karyawan pada instansi pelayanan publik berkaitan dengan kepemimpinan atasan, kepuasan kerja, dan komitmen pegawai terhadap organisasi. Penelitian ini bertujuan menguji pengaruh kepemimpinan transformasional dan kepuasan kerja terha
content: Kinerja Karyawan pada instansi pelayanan publik berkaitan dengan kepemimpinan atasan, kepuasan kerja, dan komitmen pegawai terhadap organisasi. Penelitian ini bertujuan menguji pengaruh kepemimpinan transformasional dan kepuasan kerja terhadap Kinerja Karyawan serta peran komitmen organisasi sebagai variabel mediasi pada Suku Dinas Tenaga Kerja, Transmigrasi, dan Energi Kota Administrasi Jakarta Utara. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif melalui survei kuesioner dengan skala Likert 1–4 terhadap seluruh pegawai pada lima unit kerja (sensus; N = 100), setelah pretest terhadap 34 pegawai di luar sampel utama. Data dianalisis menggunakan Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) dengan SmartPLS 4. Hasil evaluasi model pengukuran menunjukkan bahwa seluruh konstruk memenuhi kriteria validitas dan reliabilitas, dengan AVE sebesar 0,600–0,783 dan composite reliability sebesar 0,899–0,940. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa kepemimpinan transformasional (β = 0,468) dan kepuasan kerja (β = 0,394) berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap Kinerja Karyawan. Kepuasan kerja juga berpengaruh positif terhadap komitmen organisasi (β = 0,607), sedangkan kepemimpinan transformasional tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap komitmen organisasi (β = −0,059). Komitmen organisasi berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap Kinerja Karyawan (β = 0,487) serta memediasi pengaruh kepuasan kerja terhadap Kinerja Karyawan (β = 0,174), tetapi tidak memediasi pengaruh kepemimpinan transformasional terhadap Kinerja Karyawan. Dengan demikian, lima hipotesis didukung (H1, H2, H4, H5, dan H7), sedangkan H3 dan H6 tidak didukung. Temuan ini menunjukkan pentingnya kepemimpinan transformasional, kepuasan kerja, dan komitmen organisasi dalam mendukung kinerja pegawai pada instansi yang diteliti.

title: Integrating Socio-Political and Economic Strategies for Achieving Sustainable Development Goals in Emerging Economies
source: OIDA International Journal of Sustainable Development
summary: Abstract: The successful realization of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) set forth by the United Nations by the year 2030 needs both huge capital mobilizations as well as efficient governance. However, in emerging markets, financial
content: Abstract: The successful realization of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) set forth by the United Nations by the year 2030 needs both huge capital mobilizations as well as efficient governance. However, in emerging markets, financial tools like the issuance of green bonds and improvements in governance structures tend to be implemented independently of each other. The current study analyses the complementary role played by governance and sustainable financing allocations on SDG realization in developing countries. Using the balanced panel dataset comprising of twenty emerging markets from five different geographical regions (Asia, Latin America, Europe, Africa, and the Middle East) over a time period of twelve years (2015-2026; N × T = 240 panel observations), the two-way fixed effects regression analysis is conducted using the GMM estimation method to address endogeneity and reverse causality issues. The Institutional variables are taken from the World Bank Worldwide Governance Indicators (WGI), financial allocations from the IMF Financial Access Survey and Climate Bonds Initiative, and development indicators from the UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN) SDG Index. Empirical results show that although individual sustainable finance allocations lead to positive but moderate levels of SDGs, the interaction between governance quality and sustainable finance is positive and significant (β₃ = 0.041, p < 0.01). This indicates that institutional quality is a multiplier rather than a control factor in the analysis since at high institutional environments (for instance, GOV score = 70), a 1% rise in sustainable finance allocation leads to 3.017 points improvement in the SDG index, which is much higher than 1.377 points in low institutional settings (GOV score = 30). This result responds directly to the key issues in sustainable development since it demonstrates that policy dissipation occurs due to lack of institutional absorptive capacity in the process of capital allocation. Four policy frameworks—proceeds-linked verification authorities, governance-dependent blended finance, decentralized municipal monitoring system, and inter-ministerial finance council—are suggested for aligning capital flows with institutional reform. The study contributes to the sustainable development literature by providing an integrated framework in which both institutional governance and financial instruments play a role as co-determinants of global sustainability objectives. Keywords: sustainable development goals; governance quality; sustainable finance; emerging economies; institutional integration; panel data analysis

title: Influence of Stakeholder Engagement Dynamics on Project Performance: Evidence from SUNCASA Project in Kigali
source: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
summary: Despite advances in project management frameworks, urban development projects, particularly multistakeholder nature-based initiatives, continue to experience challenges related to coordination, implementation efficiency, and stakeholder res
content: Despite advances in project management frameworks, urban development projects, particularly multistakeholder nature-based initiatives, continue to experience challenges related to coordination, implementation efficiency, and stakeholder responsiveness, resulting in suboptimal project performance.These persistent challenges highlight the need to better understand how stakeholder engagement practices contribute to successful project implementation.This study examined the influence of stakeholder engagement dynamics on project performance in the SUNCASA Project in Kigali City.The study adopted a quantitative, explanatory cross-sectional case study design involving 135 stakeholders.Primary data were collected using a structured questionnaire based on a five-point Likert scale.Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation analysis, and multiple linear regression.The findings revealed that stakeholder engagement practices jointly explained 60.4% of the variation in project performance (R² = 0.604, p < 0.001).Stakeholder feedback integration emerged as the strongest predictor of project performance (β = 0.354, p < 0.001), followed by stakeholder participation and stakeholder communication, all of which exerted statistically significant positive effects.Conversely, stakeholder consultation exhibited a positive but statistically insignificant influence (β = 0.144, p = 0.091), suggesting that consultation alone does not directly enhance project performance unless stakeholder inputs are translated into implementation decisions.The study concludes that effective stakeholder engagement enhances project performance primarily through collaborative decision-making, adaptive management, and systematic integration of stakeholder feedback.It recommends institutionalizing participatory governance and formal stakeholder feedback management systems to strengthen the implementation and sustainability of urban resilience and nature-based projects in Rwanda.

title: Effect of Project Management Practices on the Performance of the Agribusiness and Food Supply Chains Project Financed by Bank of Kigali in Kigali City, Rwanda
source: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
summary: This study examined the effect of project management practices on the performance of the Agribusiness and Food Supply Chains Project financed by Bank of Kigali in Kigali City, Rwanda.The study focused on three project management practices:
content: This study examined the effect of project management practices on the performance of the Agribusiness and Food Supply Chains Project financed by Bank of Kigali in Kigali City, Rwanda.The study focused on three project management practices: project planning and appraisal, risk assessment and mitigation, and monitoring and evaluation.Respondents reported high levels of project planning and appraisal (M = 4.6113, SD = 0.62136), risk assessment and mitigation (M = 4.5052, SD = 0.83047), monitoring and evaluation (M = 4.6546, SD = 0.67753), and project performance (M = 4.6361, SD = 0.65030).Project performance was positively associated with project planning and appraisal (r = .502),risk assessment and mitigation (r = .341),and monitoring and evaluation (r = .479).The regression model was statistically significant, F(3, 190) = 61.294,p < .001,and explained 49.2% of the variation in project performance (R² = .492).Project planning and appraisal had the strongest standardized effect (β = .444),followed by monitoring and evaluation (β = .367)and risk assessment and mitigation (β = .274),all p < .001.The study concludes that systematic project management practices are important determinants of project performance and recommends stronger planning, proactive risk management, regular monitoring, clear milestones and continuous stakeholder engagement.

title: Contemporary screen exposure among children under two: a representative survey, implications and perspectives
summary: Abstract Professional guidelines consistently recommend avoiding screen exposure in children under two years of age; however, international evidence indicates that early media use is widespread. This narrative review synthesizes contemporar
content: Abstract Professional guidelines consistently recommend avoiding screen exposure in children under two years of age; however, international evidence indicates that early media use is widespread. This narrative review synthesizes contemporary data on screen exposure in infancy and toddlerhood, integrates findings from recent longitudinal research on developmental implications, and discusses expectations and intervention strategies across family, clinical, public health, and policy levels. Drawing on international cohorts and previously published representative Hungarian data ( N = 2569), we describe high prevalence, substantial daily exposure, and marked socioeconomic gradients. Nearly half of Hungarian 18-month-olds were exposed to screens daily, and over one third exceeded one hour per day on a typical day. Synthesizing literature from the last ten years, we examine early screen use within a developmental-ecological framework. Evidence links higher exposure in the first two years to poorer language, cognitive, and self-regulatory outcomes, while also indicating bi-directional and transactional processes. Beyond total exposure time, displacement of interaction-rich activities and caregiver-driven “technoference” may alter the microstructure of early social exchange, with potential implications for attachment, co-regulation, and language development. Given that early communication and self-regulation form foundational systems for later academic achievement, socio-emotional functioning, and health behaviours, early screen practices may influence longer-term developmental trajectories. We conclude by outlining developmentally informed expectations, family-level strategies, clinical guidance, and emerging policy approaches, emphasizing the need to move beyond descriptive prevalence estimates and strictly restrictive guidelines toward integrated, evidence-based responses adapted to contemporary digital environments.

title: Energy landscapes and structural plasticity of intrinsically disordered proteins
summary: Intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) populate broad energy landscapes with multiple shallow minima rather than a single dominant structural basin. Their functions and disease-associated dysfunctions arise from shifts in conformational p
content: Intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) populate broad energy landscapes with multiple shallow minima rather than a single dominant structural basin. Their functions and disease-associated dysfunctions arise from shifts in conformational populations driven by sequence variation, post-translational modifications, molecular interactions, and environmental conditions. Characterizing these landscapes remains challenging because experimental observables are often ensemble-averaged and computational models face sampling and accuracy limitations. After outlining energy-landscape concepts and integrative strategies for ensemble generation and refinement, we focus on applications of molecular featurization and dimensionality reduction (DR) to IDP ensembles. We examine how DR maps high-dimensional structural information onto low-dimensional representations that facilitate ensemble visualization and comparison, clustering, representative selection, and identification of preferentially populated regions. We further discuss applications to sequence- and condition-dependent ensemble shifts, molecular recognition, and aggregation-related conformations, highlighting how DR helps relate conformational heterogeneity to biological function.

title: From oil dependence to opportunity dependence: institutional reconfiguration and sustainable entrepreneurship in Gulf economies
summary: Purpose This paper investigates whether sustainability-oriented institutional reforms in Gulf rentier states reshape entrepreneurial ecosystems and opportunity structures for sustainable venture formation by mobilising sustainable finance a
content: Purpose This paper investigates whether sustainability-oriented institutional reforms in Gulf rentier states reshape entrepreneurial ecosystems and opportunity structures for sustainable venture formation by mobilising sustainable finance and stimulating sustainability-oriented entrepreneurship. Design/methodology/approach The study develops a mechanism-based framework linking institutional reform intensity, sustainable finance development and sustainability-oriented entrepreneurial activity. A country-year panel for Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates (2010–2024) is constructed using a novel reform intensity index, indicators of sustainable finance expansion and multiple proxies for sustainable entrepreneurial activity. Fixed effects panel models and mediation analysis are employed to test direct and indirect effects while controlling for macroeconomic conditions. Findings Higher sustainability reform intensity is positively associated with sustainable finance development. Sustainable finance, in turn, is positively related to sustainability-oriented entrepreneurial activity. Mediation analysis indicates that sustainable finance partially transmits the effect of institutional reform on entrepreneurship, alongside a remaining direct effect consistent with regulatory and legitimacy signalling mechanisms. Practical implications For Gulf policymakers, sustainable finance emerges as a core transmission mechanism through which sustainability governance is translated into entrepreneurial reorientation within Arab economies. Regulatory clarity, ESG disclosure mandates and credible green finance frameworks jointly shape viable sustainability-linked opportunity spaces. Originality/value The paper introduces an opportunity architecture lens to sustainability governance and demonstrates how institutional reform reshapes entrepreneurial ecosystems within Arab rentier economies. It advances the concept of policy-induced sustainable entrepreneurship through comparative, mechanism-based evidence from GCC reform contexts.

title: Unpacking Greenwashing in Corporate Social Responsibility : A Systematic Literature Review
summary: The escalation of global regulations and capital market preferences for Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) standards has transformed Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) disclosures from mere administrative obligations into strate
content: The escalation of global regulations and capital market preferences for Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) standards has transformed Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) disclosures from mere administrative obligations into strategic instruments that determine business sustainability. However, the disconnect between the prevalence of green narratives and the reality of environmental degradation has spurred widespread greenwashing practices. This study aims to synthesize the typologies of greenwashing modus operandi, map its internal and external drivers, evaluate its cognitive impacts on stakeholders, and formulate a responsive reconstruction of regulatory and governance frameworks. Employing a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) guided by the PRISMA 2020 protocol, 15 reputable international and national scholarly articles (2016–2026) retrieved from Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, Emerald, Wiley, and Sinta databases were screened and comprehensively analyzed. The findings reveal that greenwashing modi operandi have evolved from simple ambiguous product claims into complex financial and ESG report manipulations (decoupling, SDGwashing, bluewashing, and pinkwashing). These practices are driven internally by agency problems, short-term incentives, and weak ethical cultures, and externally by regulatory loopholes and a lack of public oversight. Such manipulations yield destructive impacts, triggering green skepticism, investor capital divestment, consumer boycotts, and the failure of Creating Shared Value (CSV). Consequently, this research formulates the Anti-Greenwashing Governance Framework, which integrates internal controls and external oversight to generate transparent and accountable sustainability signals.

title: Effect of Supply Chain Risk Management on Operational Performance of Raising the Village in Gasabo District, Rwanda
source: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
summary: The purpose of this study was to examine the effect of Supply Chain Risk Management on Operational Performance of Raising the Village in Gasabo District, Rwanda.The study was guided by four specific objectives, namely, to assess the effect
content: The purpose of this study was to examine the effect of Supply Chain Risk Management on Operational Performance of Raising the Village in Gasabo District, Rwanda.The study was guided by four specific objectives, namely, to assess the effect of Supplier Risk Management, Inventory Risk Management, Transportation & Logistics Risk Management, and Information & Technology Risk Management on Operational Performance.The target population was 219 employees and stakeholders connected to Raising the Village operations in Gasabo District, while a sample size of 142 respondents was calculated using Slovin's formula.Quantitative data were processed through editing, coding, and tabulation, and analysis was performed using SPSS Version 29 through descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and multiple regression analysis.A total of 136 complete questionnaires (95.8%) were analysed.The regression findings indicated that Supplier Risk Management B = 0.163, t = 3.396, p = 0.001, Inventory Risk Management B = 0.142, t = 2.679, p = 0.008, Transportation and Logistics Risk Management B = 0.389, t = 7.073, p = 0.000, Information and Technology Risk Management B = 0.171, t = 3.288, p = 0.001 had positive and statistically significant effects on Operational Performance in Raising the Village in Gasabo District, Rwanda.The study concluded that strengthening Supplier Risk Management, Inventory Risk Management, Transportation and Logistics Risk Management, Information and Technology Risk Management improve Operational Performance.It is recommended that management should strengthen the most influential practices while maintaining continuous monitoring of all significant variables.

title: STRAPSim: A Portfolio Similarity Metric for ETF Alignment and Portfolio Trades
source: ACM International Conference on AI in Finance (ICAIF)
summary: Accurately measuring portfolio similarity is critical for a wide range of financial applications, including Exchange-Traded Fund (ETF) recommendation, portfolio trading, and risk alignment. Existing similarity measures often rely on exact a
content: Accurately measuring portfolio similarity is critical for a wide range of financial applications, including Exchange-Traded Fund (ETF) recommendation, portfolio trading, and risk alignment. Existing similarity measures often rely on exact asset overlap or static distance metrics, which fail to capture similarities among the constituents (e.g., securities within the portfolio) as well as nuanced relationships between partially overlapping portfolios with heterogeneous weights. We introduce STRAPSim (Semantic, Two-level, Residual-Aware Portfolio Similarity), a novel method that computes portfolio similarity by matching constituents based on semantic similarity, weighting them according to their portfolio share, and aggregating results via residual-aware greedy alignment. We benchmark our approach against Jaccard, weighted Jaccard, as well as BERTScore-inspired variants across public classification, regression, and recommendation tasks, as well as on corporate bond ETF datasets. Empirical results show that our method consistently outperforms baselines in predictive accuracy and ranking alignment, achieving the highest Spearman correlation with return-based similarity. By leveraging constituent-aware matching and dynamic reweighting, portfolio similarity offers a scalable, interpretable framework for comparing structured asset baskets, demonstrating its utility in ETF benchmarking, portfolio construction, and systematic execution.

title: Time-Inhomogeneity in Risk Averse Objectives for Financial Applications of Reinforcement Learning
source: ACM International Conference on AI in Finance (ICAIF)
summary: In finance, sequential decision problems are often faced, for which reinforcement learning (RL) emerges as a promising tool for optimisation without the need of analytical tractability. However, the objective of classical RL is the expected
content: In finance, sequential decision problems are often faced, for which reinforcement learning (RL) emerges as a promising tool for optimisation without the need of analytical tractability. However, the objective of classical RL is the expected cumulated reward, while financial applications typically require a trade-off between return and risk. In this work, we focus on settings where one cares about the time split of the total return, ruling out most risk-aware generalisations of RL which optimise a risk measure defined on the latter. We notice that a preference for homogeneous splits, which is satisfactory for hedging, can be unfit for other problems, and therefore propose a new risk metric which still penalises uncertainty of the single rewards, but allows for an arbitrary planning of their target levels. We study the properties of the resulting objective and the generalisation of learning algorithms to optimise it. Finally, we show numerical results on toy examples.

title: Estimates of Rare Storm Surges in Poorly Gauged Coastal Areas
summary: Abstract Estimating low‐probability storm surges is essential for flood risk management, yet conventional asymptotic extreme value methods use only a small subset of observations and therefore produce large uncertainty at poorly gauged and
content: Abstract Estimating low‐probability storm surges is essential for flood risk management, yet conventional asymptotic extreme value methods use only a small subset of observations and therefore produce large uncertainty at poorly gauged and ungauged sites. We present MEVD‐S, a new framework that combines the Metastatistical Extreme Value Distribution with an original regionalization scheme to overcome data scarcity in rare storm surge analysis. MEVD‐S uses all observed events to infer annual maxima and incorporates nearby observations through weights inversely related to site heterogeneity, avoiding rigid homogeneous regions and fixed spatial boundaries. This allows information to be integrated seamlessly across space and time while better representing the continuity of storm‐surge‐generating processes. Evaluation with tide‐gauge records from North America, Europe, and Japan shows that MEVD‐S outperforms at‐site Generalized Extreme Value (GEV) estimates and yields predictions at ungauged locations, with bias and uncertainty comparable to those obtainable from long local records.

title: Ordinal Gates, Cardinal Bets: Matching LLM Confidence to the Financial Decision Operator
source: ACM International Conference on AI in Finance (ICAIF)
summary: LLM confidence scores are not independently deployable objects: their decision value depends on the downstream operator and exposure controller that consume them. Monotone recalibration cannot change a coverage-matched rank-based gate, wher
content: LLM confidence scores are not independently deployable objects: their decision value depends on the downstream operator and exposure controller that consume them. Monotone recalibration cannot change a coverage-matched rank-based gate, whereas position sizing consumes score magnitude, so changing a confidence map can invalidate a scale fitted to the previous score distribution. We test this on FactSet news for Nasdaq-100 equities, fitting maps and scales on 2021 and evaluating nine open-weight LLMs out-of-sample on 2022–2023. Maps and scales are not portable. Transferring a fitted scale to a different confidence map lowers certainty-equivalent return (CER) in 8/9 models, and mismatched systems realize \(3.3\%\) to \(11.8\%\) mean volatility against a \(5\%\) target. Uncalibrated confidence alone runs one model at up to 2.8 × its intended risk. Pairing each map with its own fitted scale improves ensemble CER by 9.2 percentage points per year under frozen-scale control, but this economic gain is conditional: only 3.6pp/yr exceeds a shuffled-label refitting baseline, the gain falls to an insignificant + 1.6pp/yr under an adaptive-volatility controller, and annual walk-forward gains do not survive multiplicity correction. The map–scale coupling is more stable than the gain, with a positive interaction in every walk-forward fold. Confidence transformations should therefore be validated jointly with the controllers that consume them.

title: Effect of plastic deformation on corrosion, biological and technological properties of anodized Ti6Al4V ELI implants
summary: Abstract Electrochemical anodization improves the surface properties of titanium implants, but the resulting oxide layer may be damaged by plastic deformation during insertion or service. This study investigated how four deformation levels,
content: Abstract Electrochemical anodization improves the surface properties of titanium implants, but the resulting oxide layer may be damaged by plastic deformation during insertion or service. This study investigated how four deformation levels, together with an undeformed reference, affect anodized Ti6Al4V ELI. Surface morphology, roughness, wettability, microstructure, cytocompatibility, and electrochemical behavior were evaluated. Deformation progressively increased surface roughness and induced micro- and macrocracking of the anodic layer, while all surfaces remained hydrophilic. Damage to the oxide markedly reduced corrosion protection: the corrosion rate increased from approx. 50 to 650 nm year⁻¹, whereas polarization resistance decreased from 11,920 to 327 kΩ·cm². Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy indicated facilitated ionic transport through deformation-induced defects. Nevertheless, no cytotoxic effect on MC3T3-E1 cells was observed, and differences in cell viability were not statistically significant. Thus, plastic deformation substantially impairs the electrochemical barrier function of anodized Ti6Al4V ELI without adversely affecting its short-term cytocompatibility.

title: O'ZBEKISTONDА YASHIL IQTISODIYOTNI BАNKLАR ORQАLI MOLIYALАSHTIRISH: «YASHIL» KREDITLАR SАMАRАDORLIGI VА YASHIL NIQOBLАSHNING OLDINI OLISH
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Tezisda O'zbekistonda yashil iqtisodiyotni tijorat banklari orqali moliyalashtirishning bugungi holati, «yashil» kreditlarni tasniflash va ularning ekologik natijadorligini baholash bilan bog'liq muammolar tadqiq etilgan. Yashil niqoblashni
content: Tezisda O'zbekistonda yashil iqtisodiyotni tijorat banklari orqali moliyalashtirishning bugungi holati, «yashil» kreditlarni tasniflash va ularning ekologik natijadorligini baholash bilan bog'liq muammolar tadqiq etilgan. Yashil niqoblashning banklar, investorlar va moliya bozori barqarorligiga ta'siri ochib berilgan. Tijorat banklarida yashil kreditlar samaradorligini baholash indeksi, ekologik natijalarni monitoring qilish tizimi va ochiq hisobot standartlarini joriy etish bo'yicha takliflar ishlab chiqilgan.

title: RAQAMLI MOLIYA VA YASHIL MOLIYALASHTIRISH SINERGIYASI: QAYTA TIKLANUVCHI ENERGIYAGA INVESTITSIYALAR SAMARADORLIGI
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Ushbu tadqiqot raqamli moliya va yashil moliyalashtirish o'rtasidagi sinergiyaning qayta tiklanuvchi energiya investitsiyalari samaradorligiga ta'sirini hamda moliyaviy inklyuziyaning ushbu munosabatdagi vositachi rolini o'rganishga qaratil
content: Ushbu tadqiqot raqamli moliya va yashil moliyalashtirish o'rtasidagi sinergiyaning qayta tiklanuvchi energiya investitsiyalari samaradorligiga ta'sirini hamda moliyaviy inklyuziyaning ushbu munosabatdagi vositachi rolini o'rganishga qaratilgan. Tadqiqotning nazariy asosini moliyaviy vositachilik, axborot nomutanosibligi, texnologik innovatsiyalar va barqaror moliya nazariyalari tashkil etadi. Raqamli moliya elektron to'lovlar, mobil banking, raqamli kreditlash, masofaviy identifikatsiya va ma'lumotlarga asoslangan kredit skoringi orqali kapitalga kirish imkoniyatlarini kengaytirishi mumkin. Yashil moliyalashtirish bilan birgalikda ushbu vositalar qayta tiklanuvchi energetika loyihalarini moliyalashtirish xarajatlarini kamaytirish, investorlar uchun axborot shaffofligini oshirish va moliyaviy resurslarni ekologik jihatdan samarali loyihalarga yo'naltirish imkoniyatini yaratadi. Tadqiqot doirasida panel kvantil regressiyasi, mediatsiya tahlili, System-GMM va o'zaro ta'sir modellari yagona empirik strategiya doirasida qo'llanishi taklif etiladi. Xitoy, Singapur, Buyuk Britaniya va Yevropa Ittifoqi tajribasi qiyosiy institutsional tahlil uchun asos sifatida olinadi. Empirik tadqiqot uchun mamlakatlar paneli shakllantirilib, raqamli moliya rivojlanishi, yashil moliyalashtirish, moliyaviy inklyuziya va qayta tiklanuvchi energetika investitsiyalari o'rtasidagi munosabatlar tekshiriladi. Maqolaning ilmiy hissasi raqamli moliyaning bevosita ta'sirini yashil moliyalashtirish bilan o'zaro ta'siri va moliyaviy inklyuziya orqali yuzaga keladigan bilvosita ta'siridan ajratib baholashga qaratilgan. Taklif etilgan yondashuv O'zbekistonda fintech infratuzilmasini yashil kreditlash va qayta tiklanuvchi energiya loyihalari bilan integratsiyalash bo'yicha ilmiy asoslangan siyosiy tavsiyalar ishlab chiqish imkonini beradi.

title: Current Liabilities in Contemporary Corporate Finance and Economic Systems: A Narrative Review of Governance, Liquidity Transmission, and Firm Performance
summary: Current liabilities represent the critical nexus between short-term operational continuity, working capital architecture, and macroeconomic credit transmission. Despite their central role in corporate solvency, scholarly insights into short
content: Current liabilities represent the critical nexus between short-term operational continuity, working capital architecture, and macroeconomic credit transmission. Despite their central role in corporate solvency, scholarly insights into short-term obligations remain fragmented across accounting regulation, supply chain finance, and corporate leverage literature. This study presents a comprehensive narrative review synthesizing peer-reviewed journal articles published over the latest seven-year period (2020–2026) to evaluate the conceptual taxonomy, regulatory governance, and economic performance consequences of current liabilities. Employing a structured narrative synthesis across six thematic domains, the review examines recent International Financial Reporting Standards reforms—specifically the IAS 1 amendments on covenant-linked liability classification and the IAS 7 and IFRS 7 disclosures for supplier finance arrangements—alongside empirical evidence on trade payables, short-term bank debt, maturity mismatch, and crisis-era liquidity management. The findings demonstrate that while spontaneous trade credit and reverse factoring buffer operating cash flows, excessive reliance on short-term financial debt to fund long-term assets induces rollover fragility, elevates idiosyncratic equity volatility, impairs environmental, social, and governance performance, and accelerates transitions toward Minskyan Ponzi financing during macroeconomic shocks.

title: Fixed Assets in Contemporary Economic and Accounting Research: A Narrative Review of Valuation, Capital Structure, Tax Shields, and Firm Performance
summary: Tangible fixed assets, encompassing property, plant, equipment, and productive infrastructure, constitute the physical foundation of macroeconomic capital formation and corporate value creation. However, empirical findings over the past fiv
content: Tangible fixed assets, encompassing property, plant, equipment, and productive infrastructure, constitute the physical foundation of macroeconomic capital formation and corporate value creation. However, empirical findings over the past five years reveal complex tensions regarding how fixed asset valuation, capital allocation, depreciation policies, and tax shields interact across diverse institutional regimes. This study conducts a comprehensive narrative review of peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2022 and 2026 to synthesize contemporary economic and accounting perspectives on fixed assets. Using a structured thematic synthesis across five analytical domains, the review demonstrates that: (1) gross fixed capital formation drives labor productivity up to country-specific macroeconomic thresholds before exhibiting diminishing returns; (2) fair value revaluation under IAS 16 strengthens balance sheet equity and operating returns in transparent markets but introduces opportunistic distortion under high leverage and currency volatility; (3) asset tangibility and redeployability expand debt capacity in accordance with Trade-Off Theory, particularly during post-pandemic credit contractions; (4) life-cycle maintenance, subsidy-adjusted depreciation modeling, and digital XBRL reporting enhance operational profitability and timely impairment recognition; and (5) fixed asset intensity generates non-debt depreciation tax shields that significantly reshape corporate effective tax rates.

title: Pengaruh Diversitas Gender, Keragaman Usia, dan Good Corporate Governance terhadap Kinerja Keuangan:Systematic Literature Review
summary: Pertumbuhan dunia usaha menuntut perusahaan mengoptimalkan pengelolaan aset dengan kinerja keuangan sebagai ukuran utama keberhasilan operasional. Kinerja keuangan turut dipengaruhi oleh dinamika internal dewan, seperti diversitas gender, k
content: Pertumbuhan dunia usaha menuntut perusahaan mengoptimalkan pengelolaan aset dengan kinerja keuangan sebagai ukuran utama keberhasilan operasional. Kinerja keuangan turut dipengaruhi oleh dinamika internal dewan, seperti diversitas gender, keragaman usia, dan Good Corporate Governance (GCG). Penelitian ini bertujuan mengkaji pengaruh diversitas gender, keragaman usia dewan, serta GCG terhadap kinerja keuangan perusahaan. Melalui metodologi Systematic Literature Review (SLR), sebanyak 15 artikel ilmiah terakreditasi periode 2022–2026 yang meneliti perusahaan di Bursa Efek Indonesia maupun konteks global dianalisis secara sistematis. Hasil sintesis menunjukkan bahwa keragaman usia dewan umumnya tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap profitabilitas karena homogenitas rentang usia para eksekutif. Di sisi lain, diversitas gender memberikan pengaruh bervariasi antar-sektor industri dan baru berdampak positif secara optimal apabila keterwakilan perempuan melampaui batas formalitas (tokenism). Sementara itu, konsistensi penerapan GCG terbukti berdampak positif dan signifikan terhadap peningkatan kinerja keuangan melalui pengawasan yang efektif serta efisiensi biaya keagenan. Kesimpulannya, GCG merupakan instrumen paling efektif untuk mendorong kinerja keuangan, sedangkan pengaruh variabel demografi dewan sangat bergantung pada proporsi keterwakilan serta karakteristik spesifik sektor industri.

title: Does Breakthrough Innovation in Key Core Technologies Always Enhance Urban Economic Resilience? Evidence From Diverse Resource‐Based Cities
summary: ABSTRACT This study develops a dynamic framework incorporating heterogeneous innovation to examine how breakthroughs in key core technologies affect urban economic resilience in China. A constant elasticity of substitution (CES) function in
content: ABSTRACT This study develops a dynamic framework incorporating heterogeneous innovation to examine how breakthroughs in key core technologies affect urban economic resilience in China. A constant elasticity of substitution (CES) function integrates breakthrough and incremental innovation while accounting for their dynamic accumulation and resource allocation. Using 416 branches of key digital technologies, the study applies term frequency–inverse document frequency (TF‐IDF) to IPC classification information and combines it with cosine similarity to construct a patent‐level measure of breakthrough innovation in key core technologies (BIKT), which is then aggregated to the city‐year level. Based on panel data for Chinese prefecture‐level cities from 2000 to 2023, two‐way fixed‐effects models show that BIKT significantly enhances urban economic resilience. Mechanism tests indicate that the accumulation of R&D capital stock and improvements in labor allocation efficiency are important channels through which BIKT affects urban economic resilience. Heterogeneity analysis further shows that BIKT improves economic resilience in growth‐stage and mature resource‐based cities, reduces it in declining cities, and has no significant effect in regenerative cities. These findings highlight the need for differentiated innovation policies across resource‐based cities at different development stages.

title: Gestión de Empaques Plásticos Alimentarios en Grecia, Costa Rica: Lineamientos para Trazabilidad, Ecodiseño y Recuperación
summary: La gestión de empaques y envases plásticos utilizados en alimentos en el cantón de Grecia, Costa Rica, presentan brechas de identificación, reciclabilidad potencial y recuperación posconsumo, donde el 62,2 % de los materiales no son recicla
content: La gestión de empaques y envases plásticos utilizados en alimentos en el cantón de Grecia, Costa Rica, presentan brechas de identificación, reciclabilidad potencial y recuperación posconsumo, donde el 62,2 % de los materiales no son reciclables según los criterios aplicados y encontró que solo un 16,3 % de los empaques tienen una codificación visible que coincide con la composición identificada en el laboratorio. El objetivo consiste en establecer lineamientos técnicos y ambientales orientados hacia la gestión responsable de los plásticos de un solo uso; para ello, se desarrolló una investigación aplicada, no experimental y transversal, sustentada en 193 empaques primarios seleccionados de 17 categorías de productos comercializados en supermercados del cantón. La información de rotulado, la identificación mediante espectroscopía infrarroja por transformada de Fourier y la reciclabilidad potencial se integraron con una revisión documental y con el criterio de cuatro personas expertas, para desarrollar una triangulación que permitiera el diseño de la propuesta, con una dimensión estratégica compuesta por cuatro ejes, así como una dimensión táctica desglosada en cinco grupos de lineamientos, cada uno con indicadores de seguimiento, previstos para un plan piloto de doce meses, aún no implementado. Los lineamientos propuestos articulan rotulado verificable, correspondencia entre material declarado y composición real, ecodiseño, separabilidad, retorno y fiscalización, sin reducir el problema hacia un reciclaje final; se concluye que la propuesta ofrece una ruta técnica para distribuir responsabilidades según la capacidad de intervención de cada actor; su aplicabilidad y posible escalamiento deberán evaluarse mediante el plan piloto propuesto.

title: Adapting to Crisis and Strengthening the Capacities of Organisations of Women with Disabilities in Haiti
source: Palgrave Studies in Disability and International Development
summary: Abstract Over the past 15 years, Haitian women with disabilities have created organisations of women with disabilities (OWDs) to support their members and lobby the government. They have used United Nations’ forums to denounce the multiple
content: Abstract Over the past 15 years, Haitian women with disabilities have created organisations of women with disabilities (OWDs) to support their members and lobby the government. They have used United Nations’ forums to denounce the multiple forms of discrimination they face. They have urged feminist and disability movements to take their voices into account. Nevertheless, research suggests that their gains have been overshadowed by the serious multidimensional crisis in Haiti. This chapter updates our understanding of how three institutional actors adapted their support to OWDs in that context: the Bureau du secrétaire d’État à l’intégration des personnes handicapées (BSEIPH); the Disability Rights Fund (DRF); and the Engendering Disability-Inclusive Development-Genre, handicap et développement inclusif (EDID-GHDI) partnership. The authors document the adaptation of financial and technical support, focused on strengthening institutions and leadership, knowledge production, and knowledge sharing. They offer strategic lessons from these experiences for OWDs, their partners in Haiti, and beyond.

title: The Impact of Shariah Governance and Its Consequences on CSR Disclosure: Evidence from Islamic Banks in Bangladesh
source: International Journal of Science and Business
summary: The purpose of current study is to reveal the level of CSRD practices of the Islamic banks operating in Bangladesh as well as to investigate the influence of Shariah Governance (SG) factors on CSR disclosure practices. To collect data for t
content: The purpose of current study is to reveal the level of CSRD practices of the Islamic banks operating in Bangladesh as well as to investigate the influence of Shariah Governance (SG) factors on CSR disclosure practices. To collect data for this study a nine-dimensional testable disclosure index was prepared on the basis of AAOIFI, Governance Standard No. 7, 2010 and from prior studies. Then data were collected from 8 Islamic banks for 10 years span ranging from 2013 to 2022 comprising 80 observations through content analysis of the annual reports available in the sampled banks websites. Each line of the annual report has been examined to identify whether any bank reveals CSR data specified in the CSRD index and if they do then receive a score of (1); if not, receive a score of (0). However, to analyze the panel data set the study employed OLS regression model to test the relationship among the hypothesized variables and generated descriptive statistics by using STATA Software version 16. The data analysis result reveals a relatively high level of CSR disclosure (66.36%) practices in the sampled Islamic banks. Moreover, it has been found that variables of SG included in this study explain about 72% of CSRD practices of sampled Islamic banks. The study also finds that board size, SSB size, and number of independent directors in the board have significant positive influence on CSRD. On the other, AC size, cross membership of board members show significant negative influence on CSRD. But, the result of gender composition and AC meeting indicate insignificant negative influence on CSRD. Thus, findings of this study provide new insights about the role of shariah governance in enhancing CSRD practices among the shariah based banks of Bangladesh and as such help improve their overall performance and sustainability.

title: Cognitive Benefits of Active Breaks in Sport and Exercise: A Systematic Review
summary: Background. Active breaks are brief periods of physical activity during the workday and are increasingly seen as a sustainable, low-cost way to support employee well-being. Objectives. This systematic review aimed to assess the effects of a
content: Background. Active breaks are brief periods of physical activity during the workday and are increasingly seen as a sustainable, low-cost way to support employee well-being. Objectives. This systematic review aimed to assess the effects of active breaks on employees’ physical and psychological health, work performance, cognitive functioning, and stress management. Materials and Methods. Nine studies conducted across different work settings were included, with interventions based on walking, stretching, and relaxation exercises. Results. The results were generally consistent and showed that active breaks can reduce perceived stress, improve mood, and support cognitive functions such as working memory and problem-solving. Several studies also reported physiological benefits, including improved heart rate variability and reduced mental load. Conclusions. Overall, active breaks appear to enhance productivity and decision-making while encouraging healthier and more sustainable work routines. Further research should clarify their long-term effects and identify the most effective types and frequencies of activities.

title: Mastering Money: Empowering Women to Shape a Sustainable Future through Financial Literacy
summary: Background and Aim: In a world of economic uncertainty and environmental concerns, economic inclusion plays a key role in bringing the world into a sustainable future. Financial literacy will provide women with the skills to become confiden
content: Background and Aim: In a world of economic uncertainty and environmental concerns, economic inclusion plays a key role in bringing the world into a sustainable future. Financial literacy will provide women with the skills to become confident in managing their finances, gain independence and invest their money responsibly. This study explores how closing the gender gap in financial capability and digital financial inclusion can enable women to become a driving force in creating a sustainable economy and environment. Methodology: This study uses a mixed methods approach to give a full overview of how financial literacy impacts women in becoming a driving force in creating a sustainable future. Primary Data: A cross-sectional survey and interview was conducted with 450 women from a targeted sample of entrepreneurs, professionals and homemakers in urban and semi urban regions. The primary data looks at how much financial knowledge individuals have, how they budget and if they have access to DFS. Secondary Data: A thorough literature review was conducted using academic journals from 1998 to 2026 and documents from authoritative institutions including the OECD, World Bank and global gender equality frameworks. This gave an insight into the global trends surrounding gender gaps, financial inclusion and green entrepreneurship. Findings: The results show that financial literacy increases women’s economic empowerment and intentions to become a sustainable entrepreneur. Digital finance tools also help decrease the barriers to entering the green financial market. Conclusion and Implications: The results show that increasing financial literacy is an important policy tool to achieve SDGs globally. Recommendations have been made to policymakers, financial institutions and NGOs to create financial systems that are gender sensitive to create a sustainable and fair economy.

title: Blockchain Innovation and Central Bank Digital Currency Readiness Among Financial Technology Firms in Nairobi County, Kenya
summary: The rapid advancement of digital financial technologies has intensified global interest in Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) as a potential instrument for improving payment systems, financial inclusion and transaction security. However,
content: The rapid advancement of digital financial technologies has intensified global interest in Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) as a potential instrument for improving payment systems, financial inclusion and transaction security. However, the extent to which fintech firms are organizationally and technologically prepared to support a potential retail CBDC remains insufficiently established. This study examined the influence of blockchain innovation on CBDC readiness among financial technology firms in Nairobi County, Kenya. Specifically, the study examined the influence of blockchain-enabled process innovation and blockchain-enabled service innovation on CBDC readiness. The study was anchored on Systems Theory, Modern Portfolio Theory, Transaction Cost Theory, and Public Interest Theory of Regulation. An explanatory research design was adopted, targeting 144 licensed fintech firms in Nairobi County, from which 113 responses were obtained. Primary data were collected using structured questionnaires administered to relevant senior management personnel, and the data were analysed using descriptive statistics, correlation analysis and multiple regression analysis. The regression results showed that the four blockchain innovation dimensions jointly accounted for 83.6% of the variation in CBDC readiness (Adjusted R² = .836), and the overall regression model was statistically significant, (F (2,109) =290.039, p<0.001). Individually, blockchain process innovation and service innovation were statistically significant predictors of CBDC readiness based on the reported regression results. The study concludes that blockchain innovation is significantly associated with the readiness of fintech firms to operate within a potential CBDC environment. The study recommends continued development of enabling policies for interoperability, investment in blockchain-enabled process and service innovation, and strengthening of security, transparency and internal controls among fintech firms. Key terms: blockchain innovation, process innovation, service innovation, CBDC readiness, fintech firms in Kenya

title: Could party funding reform restore political trust? Evidence from Aotearoa New Zealand
summary: Allegations of conflicts of interest in government decision-making are often linked to the funding of political parties. Using data from the 2023 New Zealand Election Study (NZES), we test the claim that reforms increasing state funding and
content: Allegations of conflicts of interest in government decision-making are often linked to the funding of political parties. Using data from the 2023 New Zealand Election Study (NZES), we test the claim that reforms increasing state funding and limiting corporate donations might improve citizens’ political trust by reducing perceptions of donors’ ‘undue influence’. We suggest that any gains in political trust following a hypothetical reform of the party funding regime would be marginal at best. Perceptions of government responsiveness to the mass public are likely to matter more. Higher trust in politicians is found among people who feel governments listen to their concerns and protect their interests. The more people see government in those terms, the more likely they are to trust politicians. Overall, our data suggests moderate support for funding reform. While partisanship shapes attitudes to reform, there may be potential for majority support. On this issue, however, political party elites are more polarised than the mass public, making reform difficult. We also highlight another dilemma: unless business contributions to political parties are entirely excluded, increased transparency in party funding sources is more likely to reduce trust than increase it.

title: Faktor Penentu Keputusan Investasi Generasi Z Di Pontianak
summary: This study examines whether financial literacy and media exposure are associated with the investment decisions of Generation Z in Pontianak City. The researchers distributed questionnaires to 154 respondents aged 17–29 who lived in Pontiana
content: This study examines whether financial literacy and media exposure are associated with the investment decisions of Generation Z in Pontianak City.
