summary: Student Government Organisations (SGOs) provide platforms for student representation, participation in institutional governance, and advocacy for welfare services. This study examined how they address student welfare concerns at four higher
content: Student Government Organisations (SGOs) provide platforms for student representation, participation in institutional governance, and advocacy for welfare services. This study examined how they address student welfare concerns at four higher education institutions in Mbeya City, Tanzania. Using an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design, the study collected data from 104 participants: 80 students, 20 SGO leaders, and four faculty deans. Students were randomly selected, whereas SGO leaders and deans were selected purposively. Data were collected through questionnaires and semi-structured interviews. Quantitative data were analysed descriptively, while qualitative data were examined using content analysis. Findings indicate that SGOs addressed welfare concerns through representation, communication with management, student support, and the facilitation of health, accommodation, counselling, sports and security services. Students reported moderate involvement in institutional decision-making. Key welfare concerns included accommodation, food costs, financial support, healthcare, and learning facilities. Limited funding and restricted decision-making authority were the leading challenges facing SGOs, each reported by 28.7% of respondents. The study concludes that SGOs play an important advocacy role, but their effectiveness depends partly on institutional support, adequate resources, and meaningful participation in decision-making. It recommends stronger institutional collaboration, improved funding and communication, and greater student representation in welfare-related decisions.

title: Towards inclusive growth in Ghana: the role of fiscal policy, institutions, and employment: analysis of the moderating effect
summary: The study assessed the direct and indirect impacts of fiscal policy on inclusive growth in Ghana, with institutional quality and employment serving as the transmission channels for fiscal policy. We developed an inclusive growth index compr
content: The study assessed the direct and indirect impacts of fiscal policy on inclusive growth in Ghana, with institutional quality and employment serving as the transmission channels for fiscal policy. We developed an inclusive growth index comprising measures of wealth inequality for the top 1% and 10% shares, the bottom 50% share, income inequality, economic growth, and average national income, using principal component analysis (PCA). The study employed the autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) approach on a time series of data from 1960 to 2023. The findings show that, first, fiscal policy related to general government expenditure significantly enhances inclusive growth independently in the short run. Institutional quality and employment each improve inclusive growth in the long run but dampen it in the short run. Second, institutional quality and employment moderate fiscal policy in promoting inclusive growth in the long run. The marginal effect of fiscal policy, given the observed mean and maximum levels of institutional quality and employment, varies between the long run and short run periods. Recommendations for policymaking and practice are presented and discussed.

title: Fit for the future?
summary: Zijn de Nederlandse politieke partijen fit for the future? Politieke partijen zijn onmisbaar in een vertegenwoordigende democratie, als verbindende schakel tussen de parlementaire politiek en de samenleving. Tegelijkertijd staat die schakel
content: Zijn de Nederlandse politieke partijen fit for the future? Politieke partijen zijn onmisbaar in een vertegenwoordigende democratie, als verbindende schakel tussen de parlementaire politiek en de samenleving. Tegelijkertijd staat die schakelfunctie al geruime tijd onder druk. Partijen zijn losser geraakt van de samenleving, met dalende trends in ledentallen en veel grotere beweeglijkheid van de kiezer als oorzaak én gevolg. In dit proces zijn partijen juist méér georiënteerd geraakt op de overheid, die hen subsidie verstrekt om voort te kunnen bestaan. Politieke partijen, zo leert de geschiedenis, zijn echter flexibel en hebben een groot aanpassingsvermogen: zij passen zich aan de veranderende politieke en sociale omgeving aan, bijvoorbeeld wanneer zij mogelijkheden zien om hun electorale concurrentievermogen te vergroten of als zij onzekerheden of risico’s willen verkleinen. Tegen de achtergrond van de afgenomen maatschappelijke worteling richt deze bundel zich op de impact van maatschappelijke trends, technologische ontwikkelingen en institutionele aanpassingen op de organisatie en het optreden van hedendaagse politieke partijen in Nederland. Experts uit de wetenschap en de politieke praktijk gaan na of ontwikkelingen als personalisering, professionalisering, mediatisering en regulering partijen kansen bieden om hun schakelfunctie te versterken, of daarvoor juist een risico vormen. Uiteindelijk raakt de discussie over de toekomstbestendigheid van politieke partijen ook aan bredere vragen over de staat van de representatieve democratie: over de richting waarin zij zich ontwikkelt, haar kwaliteit en legitimiteit.

title: Overview and Growth Trends of Sukuk and Islamic Capital Markets
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This research examines the global development and growth trends of Sukuk and Islamic Capital Markets. It explores current market performance, international issuance trends, emerging opportunities, green and sustainability Sukuk, digitalisat
content: This research examines the global development and growth trends of Sukuk and Islamic Capital Markets. It explores current market performance, international issuance trends, emerging opportunities, green and sustainability Sukuk, digitalisation, market challenges, and future growth prospects. The study highlights the increasing importance of Sukuk in financing infrastructure, supporting economic development, diversifying investment opportunities, and strengthening Shari'ah-compliant financial markets. It also provides policy recommendations aimed at improving market liquidity, regulatory frameworks, investor participation, transparency, and sustainable growth. Author: Abdirashid Mohamed NageyeAffiliation: Central Bank of Somaliland

title: Partisan Demographics
summary: This paper defines and reviews partisan demographics as an emerging field at the intersection of political demography, political economy, and population economics. Whereas political demography examines how population change affects politics
content: This paper defines and reviews partisan demographics as an emerging field at the intersection of political demography, political economy, and population economics. Whereas political demography examines how population change affects politics, partisan demographics studies how political events, party control, political climates, and policy regimes influence demographic behavior in ways that vary with the partisan alignment of individuals, households, or local populations. The chapter asks under what conditions partisan events become demographic shocks and organizes the evidence around five mechanisms: economic expectations, policy anticipation, affective identity, social matching and sorting, and risk perception and health behavior. The strongest evidence currently concerns fertility and reproductive behavior, including conceptions and abortions, while studies of marriage, partnership formation, residential sorting, health behavior, wellbeing, and mortality extend the field with varying degrees of empirical support. Evidence on migration, integration, and naturalization remains more limited. Particular attention is given to empirical credibility, including the timing of political shocks and demographic responses, the distinction between behavior and attitudes, the measurement of partisan exposure, and the separation of partisan effects from pre-existing demographic differences. The chapter concludes by identifying the conditions under which partisan politics becomes a consequential determinant of demographic behavior and by outlining priorities for future research.

title: Determining Urban Freight Terminal Location Using the Gravity Location Model and Analytical Hierarchy Process
source: Journal of Infrastructure Policy and Management
summary: Urban freight activity in Singkawang City has increased alongside its role as a regional trade and transit hub in West Kalimantan. However, the absence of a dedicated freight terminal requires heavy freight vehicles to conduct parking and l
content: Urban freight activity in Singkawang City has increased alongside its role as a regional trade and transit hub in West Kalimantan. However, the absence of a dedicated freight terminal requires heavy freight vehicles to conduct parking and loading and unloading activities on public roads, reducing effective road capacity and disrupting urban logistics. This study determines an optimal freight terminal location by sequentially integrating the Gravity Location Model (GLM) and Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) within the STEEP framework. GLM was applied to three freight-distribution scenarios involving 19 major freight-generating firms to identify spatially efficient candidates. AHP then evaluated three GLM-derived locations and one alternative designated in the Regional Spatial Plan (RTRW), based on assessments by five multi-institutional experts. GLM identified Sijangkung, Sanggau Kulor, and Pasiran, whereas AHP selected Sedau as the preferred location with a priority weight of 0.456, followed by Sanggau Kulor (0.233), Pasiran (0.168), and Sijangkung (0.143). Political criteria received the highest weight (30.7%), followed by Economic (24.6%) and Technical (23.1%). A preliminary 30,000 m² terminal plan allocates 11,351.20 m² to facilities, 6,810.72 m² to circulation, and 11,838.08 m² to green space and future expansion.

title: Yashil turizmni rivojlantirishda raqamli texnologiyalardan foydalanishning imkoniyatlari
summary: В статье систематически анализируются возможности использования цифровых технологий в развитии экологического туризма. Автор утверждает, что основная часть цифровизации в туристическом секторе в настоящее время сосредоточена на процессах пр
content: В статье систематически анализируются возможности использования цифровых технологий в развитии экологического туризма. Автор утверждает, что основная часть цифровизации в туристическом секторе в настоящее время сосредоточена на процессах продаж и бронирования и мало способствует устойчивому развитию. В исследовании разработана классификация цифровых технологий на шесть групп в соответствии с их функциями в экологическом туризме, определены возможности в областях управления потоками посетителей, экологического мониторинга, цифрового маркетинга, виртуального туризма и инклюзивных услуг. Также рассмотрены ограничения цифровизации, такие как собственный экологический след, эффекты обратной связи и цифровое неравенство, и проанализированы препятствия в условиях Узбекистана. В заключении утверждается, что цифровые технологии являются инструментом экологического туризма, и их воздействие на окружающую среду определяется не самой технологией, а целью её применения.

title: Who Will be Assigned Unreasonable Tasks by Supervisors: A Conjoint Survey Experiment
summary: ABSTRACT Supervisors sometimes assign employees tasks that employees may perceive as unreasonable because they fall outside their formal job duties. Prior research has mostly focused on the negative effects of unreasonable tasks on employee
content: ABSTRACT Supervisors sometimes assign employees tasks that employees may perceive as unreasonable because they fall outside their formal job duties. Prior research has mostly focused on the negative effects of unreasonable tasks on employee outcomes, without examining the fundamental question of who is more likely to be assigned such tasks by their supervisors. To answer this question, we examined three distinct logics underlying the assignment of unreasonable tasks based on employee attributes (i.e., age, gender, task performance, helping behavior, recent workload, and relationship closeness): stereotype‐driven logic, efficiency‐driven logic, and exchange‐driven logic. In a fully randomized conjoint survey experiment, we asked 464 supervisors to allocate an unreasonable task based on evaluations of 4640 hypothetical employee profiles, with profiles varying randomly on six employee attributes. Results show that supervisors are more likely to assign unreasonable tasks to younger employees who perform better on tasks, exhibit more helping behavior, currently have lighter workloads, and maintain closer relationships with their supervisor. The relatively stronger effects of employees' recent workload, task performance, and helping behavior suggest that the efficiency‐driven logic plays the most influential role in shaping supervisors' unreasonable task assignments. We discuss the theoretical, methodological, and practical implications of our findings.

title: Title: Natural Resources and Beyond: How Armed Groups in Conflict Combine Illicit Markets and Criminal Activities
summary: Abstract Armed groups involved in conflict are widely known to rely on illicit activities, particularly natural resource exploitation, yet how these activities are combined and evolve remain underexplored. Drawing on the Rebel Contraband Da
content: Abstract Armed groups involved in conflict are widely known to rely on illicit activities, particularly natural resource exploitation, yet how these activities are combined and evolve remain underexplored. Drawing on the Rebel Contraband Dataset, this study investigates patterns of illicit activity diversification among 121 armed groups involved in conflicts worldwide between 1990 and 2015. Three complementary methods are employed: latent class analysis to identify distinct diversification profiles, social network analysis to examine the co-occurrence of illicit activities, and trajectory analysis to assess changes in diversification over time. The results identify three distinct profiles of armed groups. The first comprises groups extensively involved in the exploitation of various natural resources, particularly through extortion. The second consists of groups with limited involvement in natural resource exploitation, relying primarily on other serious criminal activities. The third includes groups specializing in illicit drug markets, predominantly through smuggling. Network analysis reveals that extortion is recurrent across all three profiles, although the combinations of illicit activities differ substantially. Trajectory analysis further highlights variations in how armed groups expand, reduce, or maintain their involvement in different illicit activities over time. These findings contribute to bridging conflict research and criminology by providing a systematic understanding of how armed groups diversify their illicit activities during conflict.

title: Overcoming home institutional limitations via global platform involvement: A contingency perspective
summary: Do institutional limitations inhibit or encourage entrepreneurship in the digital age? We advance research on this theoretical tension by focusing on global platform involvement, a novel strategic option. Specifically, we analyze how entrep
content: Do institutional limitations inhibit or encourage entrepreneurship in the digital age? We advance research on this theoretical tension by focusing on global platform involvement, a novel strategic option. Specifically, we analyze how entrepreneurs access globally dispersed resources and escape certain limitations in home institutions. We argue that limitations in enabling institutions induce greater global platform involvement at the national level as a form of institutional escape, whereas limitations in constraining institutions persist as barriers to entrepreneurship and therefore deter such involvement. We further examine how formal and informal institutions interact to form configurations that jointly shape global platform involvement across countries. Based on these theoretical ideas, we propose a contingency-based perspective on the theoretical tension, emphasizing the type of focal institutions and their interactions. We test our hypotheses using data from a prominent global crowdfunding platform, where funding goals capture entrepreneurs’ intended engagement with the platform; our empirical analysis largely supports our arguments. We contribute to the international business literature by integrating contrasting viewpoints in the institution-based view and by extending the concept of institutional escapism to incorporate digital and entrepreneurial perspectives.

title: Power-sensitive partnerships for just nature-based solutions in urban informal settlements
summary: Nature-based solutions should better redistribute benefits and reduce climate risks for vulnerable groups in urban informal settlements. To enable this, we argue for power-sensitive partnerships and a deep commitment to pluralism in values,
content: Nature-based solutions should better redistribute benefits and reduce climate risks for vulnerable groups in urban informal settlements. To enable this, we argue for power-sensitive partnerships and a deep commitment to pluralism in values, ways of knowing, and understandings of nature.

title: From Code Completion to Agentic Development: A Survey of AI Coding Agents, Ecosystems, and Evolving Software Engineering Practice
summary: Abstract Large language models have extended software-development assistance from token-level completion to systems that can navigate repositories, edit files, execute tools, and iterate on test feedback. This survey studies the design, use
content: Abstract Large language models have extended software-development assistance from token-level completion to systems that can navigate repositories, edit files, execute tools, and iterate on test feedback. This survey studies the design, use, and evaluation of these AI coding agents, together with their commercial and societal context. Reproducible database queries support literature discovery, but the cited corpus is selected and coded for relevance; we therefore describe the work as a structured scoping survey rather than an exhaustive systematic review. We organize the field using five dimensions: interaction paradigm, computational architecture, deployment form, orchestration mode, and human-oversight mode. Treating oversight separately from architecture resolves a conceptual overlap in earlier classifications and gives each representative system one value per dimension. The technical synthesis covers repository context, planning, tool use, multi-agent coordination, SDLC applications, and benchmark limitations. We keep technical capability evidence separate from business and adoption reports. Vendor and news sources are used as dated context, not as proxies for maturity or user preference. The survey covers material available through 28 February 2026.

title: E-Procurement Technology and Sustainable Procurement: The Moderating role of Regulatory Environment and Supplier Readiness & Collaboration
source: IOASD Journal of Business and Management Studies
summary: Purpose: Despite the growing adoption of e-procurement platforms, the extent to which these technologies contribute to sustainable procurement objectives remains unclear and inconsistent, especially across varying institutional and market c
content: Purpose: Despite the growing adoption of e-procurement platforms, the extent to which these technologies contribute to sustainable procurement objectives remains unclear and inconsistent, especially across varying institutional and market contexts. This situation highlights the urgent need for empirical research that addresses how and under what conditions e-procurement technologies can support sustainable procurement, particularly within regulatory and supplier-related contingencies. Methodology: The study employs a quantitative research approach. The study is also anchored in the positivist research philosophy. This study adopts the purposive sampling technique to obtain a sample size of 385. The study relies on primary data collected directly from the selected respondents. Findings: The study concludes that E-Procurement Technology (EPT) is a significant driver of Sustainable Procurement. It is also concluded that the Regulatory Environment strengthens the positive relationship between E-Procurement Technology and Sustainable Procurement. The study further concludes that Supplier Readiness and Collaboration (SRC) significantly enhances the effect of E-Procurement Technology on Sustainable Procurement. Implications: Organizations should prioritize the implementation of advanced e-procurement systems that integrate procurement, finance, and inventory operations to improve efficiency and transparency. Continuous training programs for procurement staff should be instituted to ensure effective use of digital tools and minimize errors associated with manual processes. Firms should regularly evaluate and upgrade e-procurement platforms to incorporate features that support sustainability, such as tracking environmental and social compliance of suppliers. Organizations should actively monitor and align their procurement processes with relevant national and industry regulations to ensure compliance and reduce legal risks.

title: How Digital Market Infrastructure Generates Interorganizational Trust: An Agent-Based Simulation Study of Networked Business
summary: Abstract Digital networked business is changing the conditions under which interorganizational trust is generated. Prior research emphasizes direct interaction, historical experience, and relational embeddedness. In electronic markets, digi
content: Abstract Digital networked business is changing the conditions under which interorganizational trust is generated. Prior research emphasizes direct interaction, historical experience, and relational embeddedness. In electronic markets, digital platforms, and digital supply chains, however, organizations can form cooperation judgments without sufficient direct cooperation experience by using object visibility, digital signals, public records, third-party evaluations, failure explanations, and remedial mechanisms. This study defines the digital context as digital market infrastructure supported by information systems and uses Agent-based modeling to examine its affects interorganizational trust judgment, conversion, repair, and network sedimentation. The results show that digital market infrastructure improves the conversion efficiency from trust judgment to post-interaction trust ties by changing information visibility, judgment screening, failure handling, and relationship accumulation. Under comprehensive digital infrastructure, it also increases trust network density, cumulative trust ties, and network centralization. This study introduces digital market infrastructure into interorganizational trust research and shows that trust in networked business is generated through a dynamic relational mechanism shaped by information visibility, records and evaluations, failure governance, and network feedback.

title: Hybrid BiLSTM–Graph Neural Networks Learn Efficient Secondary Structure Representations for Protein–Protein Interface Prediction
summary: Protein–protein interfaces (PPIs) are essential for numerous biological processes and represent attractive targets for drug discovery and protein engineering. Although recent protein language models have enabled powerful sequence representa
content: Protein–protein interfaces (PPIs) are essential for numerous biological processes and represent attractive targets for drug discovery and protein engineering. Although recent protein language models have enabled powerful sequence representations for downstream structural prediction tasks, they require substantial computational resources and produce general-purpose embeddings that are not optimized for specific applications. In this work, we investigate whether task-specific representation learning can provide a computationally efficient alternative for PPI prediction. Proteins are represented as graphs of secondary structure elements (SSEs), where each node corresponds to an SSE described by its ordered amino acid sequence and edges encode spatial relationships between neighboring SSEs. We propose an approach based on a hybrid Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory–Graph Neural Network (BiLSTM-GNN) architecture that learns SSE embeddings directly from residue-level physicochemical descriptors and optimizes them jointly with a downstream graph neural network. The proposed approach is compared with an alternative pipeline based on pretrained ESM2 embeddings while keeping the graph representation and GNN architecture unchanged. Experimental results show that the task-specific BiLSTM encoder achieves competitive predictive performance with respect to the pretrained protein language model, in almost all the considered metrics, in the most challenging evaluation setting while requiring a lower computational effort. These findings suggest that end-to-end task-specific representation learning constitutes an effective and efficient alternative to pretrained protein language models for PPI prediction.

title: Topics in Tax Administration, Accounting, and Related Issues
summary: Abstract This chapter is devoted to a discussion of how administrative improvements are facilitated by our tax reform proposal. Tax administration issues discussed in this chapter include the definition and function of advanced payment agen
content: Abstract This chapter is devoted to a discussion of how administrative improvements are facilitated by our tax reform proposal. Tax administration issues discussed in this chapter include the definition and function of advanced payment agents (APAs) and payments to taxpayers that form the basis of advanced taxes on the return to various types of nonhuman and human capital. Advanced taxes include a fringe benefits tax as well as withholding on measures of entity income accruing to equity owners. An alternative approach to transfer pricing is proposed. Examples are used to illustrate how various advanced taxes will work in practice and how the information generated is used to derive taxable income and the net tax payment.

title: Conceptualising the intersection of urban degrowth and shrinking cities
summary: Urban degrowth and shrinking cities are two research fields that have gained increasing attention in recent years. The intersection of the two fields is likewise attracting growing interest due to their potential synergy: shrinking cities r
content: Urban degrowth and shrinking cities are two research fields that have gained increasing attention in recent years. The intersection of the two fields is likewise attracting growing interest due to their potential synergy: shrinking cities research provides empirical evidence of degrowth-oriented planning, while urban degrowth research offers in-depth analysis and critique of growth-oriented planning that may prove useful for shrinking cities research. Despite the growing interest, research into their relation remains scarce. This paper studies the intersection of urban degrowth and urban shrinkage, and establishes a conceptual framework linking the two concepts. After reviewing existing literature to identify the synergetic potential of the two fields, a framework of policy responses to urban shrinkage is used to illustrate the relation between urban degrowth and shrinking city planning. The paper demonstrates that planning for shrinkage, one type of policy response to urban shrinkage, is key to linking the two concepts. It then provides definitions and examples of urban degrowth without shrinkage, planning for shrinkage that is not degrowth-oriented, and degrowth-oriented planning for shrinkage, to clarify their differences and compatibility. By providing a conceptual framework that links the two concepts, the paper paves the way for further research that will feed into both fields.

title: Effects of urban renewal on the mental health of older adults: evidence from China
summary: Objectives This study aims to evaluate the impact of urban renewal on the mental health of older adults in China. Methods Based on the micro-data from the 2016, 2018, and 2020 waves of the China Longitudinal Aging Social Survey (CLASS) and
content: Objectives This study aims to evaluate the impact of urban renewal on the mental health of older adults in China. Methods Based on the micro-data from the 2016, 2018, and 2020 waves of the China Longitudinal Aging Social Survey (CLASS) and the macro-data at the city level, nine indicators at the household, community, and city levels were selected and integrated through principal component analysis to reflect urban renewal. Then the study explored the impact of urban renewal on the mental health of older adults in China using the fixed-effects model. Results The findings revealed that urban renewal has a positive impact on the mental health of older adults at the 1% significance level. The conclusion was still valid after the instrumental variable regression method (IV) and the propensity score matching method (PSM) were used for robustness analysis. The social adaptability and life satisfaction of older adults played a significant mediating role. The heterogeneity analysis showed that older adults aged 60–69 and 80 years or older, as well as rural residents, benefit more from urban renewal. Conclusion This study highlights that urban renewal should be further intensified to increase the renewal of various facilities and services at the household, community, and city levels, thereby expanding the benefits of urban renewal on the mental health of older adults.

title: Influence of biodegradable microplastic alteration during composting and drying/rewetting cycles on soil physicochemical properties
summary: Biodegradable microplastics (MPs) may enter soils either as pristine materials during agricultural plastic use or through organic fertilizers after partial degradation during composting. Their impacts on soil properties may be influenced by
content: Biodegradable microplastics (MPs) may enter soils either as pristine materials during agricultural plastic use or through organic fertilizers after partial degradation during composting. Their impacts on soil properties may be influenced by climatic conditions. The aim of this study was to investigate how (i) MP degradation state (pristine or composted) and (ii) physical stress cycles (alternating freeze–thaw, drying–rewetting) influence soil properties. To this end, one Cambisol was exposed in controlled conditions to three types of MPs at a concentration of 1% (w/w), with four soil incubation replicates: a conventional polyethylene (PE) film, and two biodegradable films, a poly(butylene adipate terephthalate) and starch (PBAT/starch) film, and an ethylcellulose-based (EC-based) film. MPs were introduced either as pristine or after composting, then visible fragments were removed after a 59-day incubation period, to evaluate the effects of incubation on soil physical properties after removal of visible plastic fragments, rather than their physical presence. However, some leachates or small plastic fragments may still be present. Incubation was conducted either under constant conditions or under alternating physical stress cycles. Soil physicochemical and aggregation properties were measured and SOC composition analyzed using Rock-Eval ® pyrolysis. Soil responses varied primarily according to plastic type and degradation state. No significant effects on the measured properties were observed during the 59-day incubation with PE MPs, whether pristine or composted, whereas state-dependent responses were observed for biodegradable MPs. Pristine PBAT/starch and EC-based MPs changed soil pH and electrical conductivity, and increased mean weight diameter (MWD). Composting attenuated several of these effects, particularly for PBAT/starch. For EC-based MPs, composting attenuated responses for mean weight diameter and SOC content, whereas pH and electrical conductivity showed opposite trends between pristine and composted MP treatments. Alternating physical stress cycles selectively modulated specific soil properties in a treatment- and plastic composition-dependent manner, with effects mainly observed for MWD, soil pH, and electrical conductivity.

title: How did production occupations evolve over time in terms of their skill sets and numbers?
summary: Abstract The job profile of industrial employment is changing because of Industry 4.0 worldwide. In this paper, we investigate the most susceptible job sector to automation, which is a production occupation, as stated by many authors in the
content: Abstract The job profile of industrial employment is changing because of Industry 4.0 worldwide. In this paper, we investigate the most susceptible job sector to automation, which is a production occupation, as stated by many authors in the scientific literature. To assess this, we reviewed the production occupations from the DOT (Dictionary of Occupational Titles) from the 1965 and 1991editions and 1998 to 2024 versions, its successor, the O*NET (Occupational Information Network) database. In addition, we examined the Worker Functions variable from the DOT and the Skills variable from the O*NET database for Production Occupations. By considering these variables, we analyzed the real data from each edition to determine the real impact of Industry 4.0. In this study, we developed a hypothesis by investigating the Gone, Remained, and New Jobs of the Production Jobs category; this specific job cluster from 1965 to 2024; and its required worker functions and skills to obtain a better understanding of each job’s nature and how its skill sets are susceptible to automation. Our findings suggests that the relevance of technological bottlenecks to automation varies across production occupations. Furthermore, the results indicate that some skills can be automated, but the whole content of a production occupation cannot be automated.

title: Genesis of Socially Responsible Design
summary: This article presents the genesis and development of the notion of socially responsible design (SRD), following its history from the Arts & Crafts movement (1888) and Bruce Archer’s activity, through the ground-breaking criticism included i
content: This article presents the genesis and development of the notion of socially responsible design (SRD), following its history from the Arts & Crafts movement (1888) and Bruce Archer’s activity, through the ground-breaking criticism included in Victor Papanek’s Design for the Real World (1972), up to the contemporary theoretical and practical models. It discusses the key approaches to SRD: Victor and Sylvia Margolins’ social model of design, human-centred design methodology of Ideo group, Carla Cipolla’s dialogical approach, and the eight-core-features model developed by Caroline L. Davey, Andrew B. Wootton, Rachel Cooper and their collaborators. The author proposes to define SRD as planning changes responsive to the needs of people prone to social exclusion, accounting for local resources and preventing the negative effects of the solution on users and the environment. The article indicates connections between SRD and the tradition of Polish design education – from the Krakow Workshops and Institute of Industrial Design to the programme of the Faculty of Industrial Design of the Academy of Fine Arts in Kraków, inspired by the ideas of Bauhaus and HfG Ulm. In the part dedicated to challenges, the text discusses the role of social innovation incubators of financed from EU funds as spaces of practical implementation of SRD in Poland. Keywords: socially responsible design, social innovations, social exclusion, participatory design, design education

title: The Analysis of Financial Performance of the Mongolian Banking Sector Under Consideration of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)
source: International Journal of Social Science and Human Research
summary: This study investigates the impact of green finance on bank credibility in Mongolia using ten-year panel data from four systemically important commercial banks, covering the periods before and after the adoption of green finance. Green fina
content: This study investigates the impact of green finance on bank credibility in Mongolia using ten-year panel data from four systemically important commercial banks, covering the periods before and after the adoption of green finance. Green finance is measured by the Green Asset Ratio (GAR), while bank performance is assessed using Return on Assets (ROA) and Return on Equity (ROE). Descriptive statistics, independent-samples t-tests, and regression analyses are conducted using SPSS. The results show significant improvements in bank profitability and operating scale following the adoption of green finance. Regression analysis indicates that green finance positively affects asset profitability, whereas its effect on shareholder returns is more indirect through lending activity, capitalization, and institutional development. Overall, green finance appears to strengthen bank credibility by improving profitability and supporting institutional development, thereby contributing to sustainable development and long-term competitiveness in emerging markets.

title: Finding Your Buyer: How Configurational Analysis Reveals Five Purchase Segments
summary: Abstract Purpose — Live streaming commerce (LSC) research predominantly assumes trust, emotional attachment, and psychological ownership independently drive purchase intention through an additive logic. This study challenges that assumption
content: Abstract Purpose — Live streaming commerce (LSC) research predominantly assumes trust, emotional attachment, and psychological ownership independently drive purchase intention through an additive logic. This study challenges that assumption by testing a configurational alternative: whether any single psychological mechanism is necessary for purchase, and whether multiple credibility configurations are jointly sufficient, among small farm food streamers—over 97% of LSC sellers yet largely unexamined. Design/methodology/approach — Survey data from 393 Chinese consumers with farm food LSC experience were analyzed using Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA) for necessity testing, fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA) for sufficiency identification, and Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) for net effect estimation. Findings — NCA establishes no single condition—including trust—is necessary for high purchase intention. fsQCA identifies five distinct configurations sufficient for purchase, each representing a different consumer persona. PLS-SEM confirms significant net effects across all credibility dimensions while revealing that expertise does not operate through psychological ownership. Research limitations/implications — The cross-sectional design limits causal inference; the Chinese farm food context warrants replication in other markets. Practical implications — Small streamers need not excel across every credibility dimension; purchase occurs when their profile aligns with a specific consumer persona. Platforms may leverage the five configurations for matching streamers to target audiences. Originality/value — This study demonstrates that trust, psychological ownership, and emotional attachment—constructs from independent theoretical traditions—operate configurally, substituting for one another across distinct pathways to the same outcome. This equifinality principle repositions consumer–streamer relationship theorizing from 'what works?' to 'what works for whom?' JEL classification: M31

title: Financing Universal Sanitation: Regulation, Investibility and the Political Economy of Water Infrastructure
summary: Sanitation is difficult to finance for reasons that have little to do with the availability of savings. Networks absorb sunk capital, revenues are set politically, assets outlive the governments that authorise them, and universal service ob
content: Sanitation is difficult to finance for reasons that have little to do with the availability of savings. Networks absorb sunk capital, revenues are set politically, assets outlive the governments that authorise them, and universal service obliges providers to reach households whose capacity to pay is weakest exactly where unit costs run highest. Four literatures have grown around these facts and rarely speak to one another: public health and human rights, concerned with access, affordability and accountability; utility regulation, concerned with commitment, tariffs and administrative capacity; infrastructure finance, concerned with risk allocation, bankability and creditor protection; and critical political economy, which follows the financialisation of water through debt, ownership and valuation. This review integrates them around a single object: the claim on future tariff revenue, and the institutional work that manufactures, prices and enforces it. Financeability, on this reading, is produced rather than discovered. Territorial design, revenue rules, project preparation, regulatory credibility and enforceable creditor rights make an asset investible; public development banks shape that outcome through preparation and standardisation at least as much as through lending. Because the same arrangements redistribute risk and authority among users, governments and investors, the volume of capital mobilised tells us almost nothing about universalisation on its own. Brazil supplies the sharpest available test. A statutory deadline of 2033, a drive towards regionalised provision, national reference norms and a fast-growing market in infrastructure debentures now operate in a sector still marked by deep territorial inequality and uneven regulatory capacity. The review sets out what a credible research agenda must measure, and why ownership is the wrong variable to measure it with.

title: Employee share ownership in the contemporary business environment
source: Technological and Economic Development of Economy
summary: In the contemporary business environment, human capital is decisive for the accomplishment of companies’ performance objectives. In the relevant literature, there are studies that present mixed results, regarding the relationship between em
content: In the contemporary business environment, human capital is decisive for the accomplishment of companies’ performance objectives. In the relevant literature, there are studies that present mixed results, regarding the relationship between employee share ownership and company performance. This research investigates the relationship between employee share ownership and company market value, by using a cross-sectional data set of French companies listed on the Euronext Paris Stock Exchange. The results show that the status of employees as shareholders is positively related to the company market value in intermediate-sized enterprises, these results being inconsistent for small and medium enterprises along with large enterprises. These findings extend the literature on shareholder theory by a complementary approach, showing that company size plays an important role in the relationship between companies and their employees through the perspective of shareholder position. First published online 13 November 2026

title: Javanese Plant Metaphors for Ritual Offerings
summary: The production of utterances involves cognitive, physiological, and physical processes. This research focuses on the cognitive aspect, specifically the mental mechanisms underlying the creation of metaphorical terms associated with Javanese
content: The production of utterances involves cognitive, physiological, and physical processes. This research focuses on the cognitive aspect, specifically the mental mechanisms underlying the creation of metaphorical terms associated with Javanese plants used in ritual offerings. The study aims to shed light on how metaphorical expressions in the traditional Javanese language emerge. The data, comprising metaphorical terms related to ritual plants, were purposively selected from Javanese lexical sources. The research employs observation and intuition as primary approaches, with analytical methods including matching, distributional, and reflective-introspective techniques. The findings reveal that the generation of metaphorical expressions relies heavily on cognitive association processes, linking the source domain (e.g. plant characteristics or functions) with the target domain (cultural or spiritual concepts). This association demonstrates how metaphor functions as a cognitive tool to conceptualise abstract ideas through tangible elements within Javanese cultural practices. Ultimately, the study illuminates how cultural cognition is reflected in linguistic expressions, particularly in the symbolic use of plants in ritual contexts.

title: Selectivity of entomopathogenic fungi Metarhizium anisopliae isolate IBCB 425 (Hypocreales: Clavicipitaceae) on the predatory lacewings Ceraeochrysa cincta (Schneider, 1851) and Chrysoperla externa (Hagen, 1861) (Neuroptera: Chrysopidae)
summary: Abstract Metarhizium anisopliae is widely used in biological control programs against insect pests, although information on its compatibility with natural enemies remains limited. This study evaluated the selectivity of M. anisopliae isolat
content: Abstract Metarhizium anisopliae is widely used in biological control programs against insect pests, although information on its compatibility with natural enemies remains limited. This study evaluated the selectivity of M. anisopliae isolate IBCB 425 (Hypocreales: Clavicipitaceae) toward the predatory lacewings Ceraeochrysa cincta (Schneider, 1851) and Chrysoperla externa (Hagen, 1861) (Neuroptera: Chrysopidae). Larvae of both species were fed Diatraea saccharalis (Fabricius, 1794) (Lepidoptera: Crambidae) eggs treated with 4 × 10 7 , 8 × 10 7 , or 4 × 10 8 conidia/mL until the prepupal stage. Larval mortality, pupal, adult, and egg inviability, oviposition, and midgut morphology were evaluated using statistical, histological, and ultrastructural analyses. Under the experimental conditions, exposure to M. anisopliae did not cause detectable adverse effects. Larval mortality ranged from 4 to 8% in C. cincta and from 6 to 8% in C. externa . Pupal inviability ranged from 2 to 6% in both species, whereas adult inviability ranged from 6 to 8% in C. cincta and from 4 to 6% in C. externa . Egg inviability remained low, ranging from 0.92 to 2.53% in C. cincta and from 0.50 to 0.65% in C. externa , with no significant differences among treatments. Oviposition also did not differ from the control, and no histological or ultrastructural alterations were observed in the larval midgut. These findings indicate that M. anisopliae isolate IBCB 425 is selective toward both lacewing species, supporting its compatibility with these predators in integrated pest management programs.

title: C2C rule library v0.1: 21 disclosure rules from the Green Loan Principles, the Sustainability-Linked Loan Principles and IFRS S2
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Twenty-one disclosure requirements from the Green Loan Principles (2023), the Sustainability-Linked Loan Principles (2023) and IFRS S2 (2023), each rewritten as one yes/no question with its search terms. Prototype version, fixed on 29 Octob
content: Twenty-one disclosure requirements from the Green Loan Principles (2023), the Sustainability-Linked Loan Principles (2023) and IFRS S2 (2023), each rewritten as one yes/no question with its search terms. Prototype version, fixed on 29 October 2026. Provided as an Excel file and as JSON with the same content.

title: Transparency matters
summary: This study examines how sponsorship disclosure format and influencer compensation nature shape perceived sponsorship transparency and its effects on source credibility, information credibility, online engagement, and purchase intention amon
content: This study examines how sponsorship disclosure format and influencer compensation nature shape perceived sponsorship transparency and its effects on source credibility, information credibility, online engagement, and purchase intention among Instagram micro-influencers. Drawing on the Persuasion Knowledge Model, Communication Transparency Theory, Parasocial Interaction Theory, and Source Credibility Theory, the study conceptualizes perceived sponsorship transparency as consumers’ holistic judgment of how openly the commercial relationship is communicated. A between-subjects experiment (420 participants) was analyzed using two-way analysis of variance, regression, and serial mediation. Disclosure format, but not compensation nature, influenced perceived transparency, with platform-integrated disclosures outperforming hashtag-based ones, extending the Persuasion Knowledge Model to platform-governed ecosystems. Transparency sequentially mediated behavioral outcomes through source and information credibility, with source credibility the stronger mediator. Limitations include snowball sampling, a fictitious influencer and brand, and no confirmatory factor analysis.

title: Toward a conceptual framework of hard and soft behavior change interventions in sustainable transport
summary: This paper aims to identify effective strategies for promoting behavioral change toward more sustainable travel patterns, drawing on evidence from the literature and practice. Established objectives for behavior change interventions include
content: This paper aims to identify effective strategies for promoting behavioral change toward more sustainable travel patterns, drawing on evidence from the literature and practice. Established objectives for behavior change interventions include reducing emissions, alleviating congestion, and enhancing overall well-being through targeted interventions. Drawing on existing frameworks for behavior change, the paper focuses on the key dimensions which are relevant to the design and evaluation of policy measures. A multi-dimensional conceptual framework of behavior change interventions in transport is proposed to highlight the importance of combining ‘hard’ measures, such as road user charges and infrastructure investments, with ‘soft’ measures, like public awareness campaigns and incentive programmes and working from home. The other three dimensions cover the timeframe for change, the level of change impact and the “push” and “pull” change strategies. Evidence of previous impact is presented, distinguishing between marginal and non-marginal changes and, where appropriate, the longevity of impact. The evidence demonstrates that tailoring these strategies to specific population segments and geographic contexts is crucial for delivering impact, particularly given the diverse travel needs and socio-demographic factors that exist within different jurisdictions. The paper concludes with recommendations for advancing research to better understand the synergetic effects of various behavior change interventions using the proposed framework whilst also recognizing that measures to minimize travel must be seen in context.

title: Robo-advisors, green finance, and greenwashing: effects on financial performance in the banking sector
source: Journal of economic and administrative sciences.
summary: Purpose This study aims to investigate the relationship between robo-advisors, green finance, and banks' financial performance, with greenwashing as a mediating mechanism, in the Indonesian banking sector. Design/methodology/approach Using
content: Purpose This study aims to investigate the relationship between robo-advisors, green finance, and banks' financial performance, with greenwashing as a mediating mechanism, in the Indonesian banking sector. Design/methodology/approach Using a non-experimental, survey-based design, data were collected from financial, environmental, and operations managers in Indonesian banks and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to test the hypothesized relationships. Findings The results indicate that robo-advisors significantly enhance green finance investment, which subsequently improves banks' financial performance. Green finance also has a direct positive effect on financial performance, while greenwashing mediates this relationship, leading to short-term performance gains. Originality/value This study is among the first to empirically examine the interplay between robo-advisors, green finance, and financial performance through greenwashing in the banking sector. The findings advance theoretical understanding and offer actionable insights for managers and policymakers aiming to align technological innovation with sustainable finance.

title: Partnerships for development: collaborative governance in blended finance strategies in Brazil
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine how antecedent and initial conditions of collaborative governance combine to shape the approval of consortium proposals in blended finance. Using the first BNDES Blended Finance Fund in Brazil, it asks whi
content: Purpose This study aims to examine how antecedent and initial conditions of collaborative governance combine to shape the approval of consortium proposals in blended finance. Using the first BNDES Blended Finance Fund in Brazil, it asks which combinations of organizational resources, expertise, prior relationships and sectoral diversity make consortia more credible to a development finance institution. The study addresses a gap in research on the organizational and relational conditions that precede partnership formation and influence access to development finance. Design/methodology/approach The study applies fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA) to 27 consortia competing in the BNDES call, eight of which were approved. Six conditions were analyzed: social entrepreneurship expertise, financial expertise, diversity of capital sources, prior relationship with BNDES, sustainability expertise and sectoral diversity. Organizational data were coded from websites and activity reports, aggregated at consortium level and calibrated into set memberships. Necessity and sufficiency analyses were complemented by robustness tests across alternative calibrations and analytical thresholds. Findings Approval is associated with a stable configurational backbone combining social entrepreneurship expertise, capital diversity, prior ties with BNDES, sustainability expertise and sectoral diversity. Sectoral diversity is the condition closest to necessity and becomes necessary under alternative calibrations. Rejection is more equifinal and follows multiple pathways, but the absence of sectoral diversity recurs across all specifications. Financial expertise is not a stable component of approval: its role changes with analytical thresholds, while financially sophisticated but thematically weak or sectorally closed coalitions are consistently associated with non-approval. Research limitations/implications The analysis concerns the selection stage of a single BNDES call and relies on observable organizational attributes, potentially understating informal capabilities and internal governance practices. With 27 cases and six conditions, the study also has limited generalizability despite covering the analyzed proposal universe and conducting robustness tests. Approval may partly reflect BNDES-specific policy preferences, while factors such as project quality, territorial fit and leadership remain unmodeled. Future research should compare programs and countries and track how initial configurations translate into implementation performance and impact. Practical implications Public development banks can treat sectoral diversity as a design criterion rather than merely a scoring bonus, require governance charters defining decision rules and accountability and monitor whether formal diversity produces effective participation. Matchmaking and capacity-building can reduce advantages enjoyed by organizations with prior funder relationships. Applicants should document v

title: SOFT SKILLS ЯК ІНСТИТУЦІЙНИЙ ЧИННИК РЕАЛІЗАЦІЇ СОЦІАЛЬНОЇ ТА УПРАВЛІНСЬКОЇ СКЛАДОВИХ ESG-КОНЦЕПЦІЇ СТАЛОГО РОЗВИТКУ
summary: У статті досліджено роль soft skills як інституційного чинника реалізації соціальної та управлінської складових ESG-концепції сталого розвитку. Обґрунтовано, що ефективне впровадження ESG-принципів залежить не лише від формальних політик і
content: У статті досліджено роль soft skills як інституційного чинника реалізації соціальної та управлінської складових ESG-концепції сталого розвитку. Обґрунтовано, що ефективне впровадження ESG-принципів залежить не лише від формальних політик і процедур, а й від сформованих моделей поведінки, комунікації та управлінської взаємодії в організації. На основі узагальнення сучасних наукових досліджень, аналітичних матеріалів обґрунтовано, що однією з ключових перешкод ефективної ESG-реалізації є втрата неформалізованих знань, практичного досвіду та управлінських компетентностей. Доведено, що саме soft skills виступають носіями tacit knowledge (неявних знань), які накопичуються в процесі щоденної професійної діяльності та забезпечують ефективну комунікацію, командну взаємодію, лідерство, довіру, етичну поведінку та відповідальне прийняття рішень. Від рівня розвитку таких компетентностей залежить узгодженість дій працівників, стабільність корпоративного управління і результативність практичного впровадження соціальних та управлінських ESG-принципів.

title: Prof. Judgment Before Answers: Generative AI in First-Year Mathematical Analysis
source: Journal of Education and Culture Studies
summary: Generative AI now produces plausible solutions to many standard exercises in first-year Mathematical Analysis, yet the same systems mishandle quantifier scope, omit essential hypotheses, and invite students to substitute fluent text for mat
content: Generative AI now produces plausible solutions to many standard exercises in first-year Mathematical Analysis, yet the same systems mishandle quantifier scope, omit essential hypotheses, and invite students to substitute fluent text for mathematical judgment. This paper argues that the pedagogical question is not whether GenAI should enter the analysis classroom, but how its use can be designed so that the student, rather than the tool, performs the cognitive labor the course exists to cultivate. Drawing on recent evidence concerning AI in proof-based undergraduate courses, the paper develops a three-principle design framework—tiered access, error-centered inquiry, and judgment-oriented assessment—and instantiates it through worked examples from the first-year syllabus. The examples span limit computations ( and arguments, rationalization, boundedness), integral computations (substitution, integration by parts, symmetry, the Riemann integral and its limitations), and the convergence of function sequences. In each case the AI output is treated not as an answer key but as a case to be diagnosed, and the student's task is to supply the judgment that distinguishes a valid argument from a plausible one.

title: Beyond escape: psychological restoration, nostalgia, and meaning-making in domestic rural tourism destination in Indonesia
summary: Understanding domestic tourists’ motivations for rural tourism requires moving beyond conventional Push-Pull Theory, which often treats motivations as static, decontextualized variables. Such approaches may overlook how tourist motivations
content: Understanding domestic tourists’ motivations for rural tourism requires moving beyond conventional Push-Pull Theory, which often treats motivations as static, decontextualized variables. Such approaches may overlook how tourist motivations are shaped by personal memory, identity, social relationships, and cultural contexts. Addressing this limitation, this study investigates how domestic tourists in Indonesia construct and experience their motivations for visiting rural tourism destinations and how internal and destination-based factors interact. Drawing on in-depth semi-structured interviews with 35 domestic tourists and thematic analysis, the findings identify three interrelated experiential processes: psychological restoration through emotional regulation, nostalgia through the reconstruction of personal and cultural memories, and experiential learning through embodied engagement with rural social life. These findings suggest that rural tourism motivations extend beyond escape and leisure, emerging through tourists’ interactions with destination environments, local communities, and personal histories. Accordingly, push and pull factors are better understood as relationally interpreted processes than as independent motivational antecedents. By conceptualizing rural tourism motivation as a relational and restorative practice embedded in Indonesia’s socio-cultural context, this study advances an interpretive understanding of domestic tourist motivation and offers insights for sustainable rural tourism development.

title: Amyloid formation as local environment-dependent process
summary: Treatment for AD/PD should be based on three solutions: (1) preventing the formation of amyloid fibrils; (2) stopping the propagation of an existing fibril and (3) the potential fragmentation of an existing fibril. Proposals (the first two)
content: Treatment for AD/PD should be based on three solutions: (1) preventing the formation of amyloid fibrils; (2) stopping the propagation of an existing fibril and (3) the potential fragmentation of an existing fibril. Proposals (the first two) for solving this problem at the molecular level are based on method using the analysis of the distribution of hydrophobicity in native proteins compared with this distribution in amyloid forms. This analysis is conducted using the fuzzy oil drop model (FOD-M). The approach based on the polarity/hydrophobicity relationship stems from the water-based environments present within a living organism, as water constitutes the fundamental environment in which proteins are active in living organisms. The main finding is in form of proposed solution for point 1 concerns the identification of factors that alter the characteristics of an aqueous environment acting as an external force field for folding proteins. The proposal for point 2 recalls the solution elaborated by evolution in the case of solenoid proteins using the short polypeptide chains preventing the unlimited propagation. The conclusions arising from the presented analysis lead to proposals for a series of experimental studies to confirm or reject the proposed solutions. The key question, however, is: Why does a fibril structure with unlimited potential for propagation form in the first place? An attempt to answer this question is postulated in this paper. The limitation of the presented model is that it operates on the known structures.

title: Perceived priorities, experiences and provision gaps in urban green spaces: evidence from university students in Pécs, Hungary
summary: Urban green spaces play a vital role in enhancing the liveability and sustainability of cities, particularly for university students. This study applies a socially differentiated importance–experience framework to the evaluation of urban gr
content: Urban green spaces play a vital role in enhancing the liveability and sustainability of cities, particularly for university students. This study applies a socially differentiated importance–experience framework to the evaluation of urban green spaces by university students in Pécs, Hungary. The sample was not representative of the target population, primarily because foreign students were overrepresented. Post-stratification weights were therefore applied to align the sample with the composition of the student population at the University of Pécs. Using these weights, Multiple Factor Analysis identified three dimensions for both the importance and experience measures, as well as six dimensions representing the gap between the corresponding importance and experience ratings. Each dimension was subsequently modelled using post-stratification-weighted linear regression. The explanatory variables describing patterns of green-space use were preselected using the Boruta feature-selection algorithm. The findings reveal substantial importance–experience gaps for several basic attributes, including public toilets, accessibility for people with reduced mobility, benches, cleanliness, waste bins and vegetation. Associations with citizenship and patterns of green space use were dimension-specific rather than indicating consistently less experiences among respondents with foreign citizenship. The results suggest that the students’ evaluations of urban green spaces reflect a multidimensional interplay of practical, environmental, and social attributes. Future research should examine comparative settings and incorporate qualitative methods to explore variation among more precisely defined user groups and across urban contexts. Given the non-representative sample and the aggregation of respondents with foreign citizenship into a single group, the results should be interpreted cautiously, particularly regarding gender-specific patterns and heterogeneity within the foreign-citizenship group.

title: The neural basis of regret and disappointment and its influence on pricing decisions: insights from self-agency and other-agency responsibility pricing experiments
summary: Abstract By incorporating neuroscientific methods into the classical pricing framework, we studied participants' neural responses to regret and disappointment, measured by ERP waveforms and scalp potential spatial distributions. We observed
content: Abstract By incorporating neuroscientific methods into the classical pricing framework, we studied participants' neural responses to regret and disappointment, measured by ERP waveforms and scalp potential spatial distributions. We observed significant neural activation for underpricing and overpricing regret, as well as marginally significant neural activation for underpricing disappointment, whereas no notable activation was found for overpricing disappointment. We found heterogeneity in individual ERP responses and used negative differences in FRN amplitudes across cases as representative variables for underpricing and overpricing regret. These measures were then employed to investigate their effects on participants' pricing behaviors. Our findings contradict the common belief in behavioral economics that individuals strategically make decisions to avoid regret-related negative emotions.

title: Ethics of Generative AI in Translation: Literacy, Guidelines, and Implementation
summary: Advancing research on the ethics of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in translation, this book moves the discussion beyond abstract ethical concerns, towards empirical inquiry and evidence-based recommendations that inform future
content: Advancing research on the ethics of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in translation, this book moves the discussion beyond abstract ethical concerns, towards empirical inquiry and evidence-based recommendations that inform future research and practice. Drawing on three empirical studies involving international samples, this book introduces an empirically grounded ethical-capacity framework that integrates tools for assessing GenAI ethical literacy, practical guidelines developed through expert consensus, and strategies for addressing implementation challenges in professional practice. Ethical capacity is a central theme throughout, emphasising the importance of equipping translators with the knowledge and skills needed to engage responsibly with GenAI, as well as with the professional and institutional support required to put ethical principles into action. An essential resource for researchers in translation technology, AI ethics, and professional ethics, the book will also be valuable to educators, professional translators, language-service providers, translator associations, and policymakers seeking to address the ethical challenges surrounding the use of GenAI in translation.

title: Greenness, Air Pollution, and Insulin Resistance in a Latin American Megacity: A Longitudinal Mediation Analysis of the ELSA‑Brasil Cohort
summary: Abstract Studies examining the relationship between greenness and insulin resistance may elucidate the distal association between greenness and type 2 diabetes. The role of air pollution on this association remains unclear. We investigated
content: Abstract Studies examining the relationship between greenness and insulin resistance may elucidate the distal association between greenness and type 2 diabetes. The role of air pollution on this association remains unclear. We investigated whether air pollution mediated the association between greenness and insulin resistance, among non-diabetic participants ( N = 2715) from the Brazilian Longitudinal Study of Adult Health (ELSA-Brasil) in São Paulo megacity, Brazil, followed-up for approximately 8 years (2008–2010, 2012–2014, 2017–2019). Neighborhood greenness (NDVI, in quartiles), air pollution (PM 2.5 and PM 10 ), and insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) were examined using mediation analysis, allowing for exposure-mediator interaction. Total, natural direct, and natural indirect effects were estimated, using mixed-effects models, stratified by the neighborhood socioeconomic status (NSES) and adjusted for individual age, sex, education and income. In PM 10 analysis for participants from low NSES, higher neighborhood greenness was associated with lower insulin resistance, in a dose-response pattern, as indicated by the total ( β = −0.49, 95% CI −0.91, −0.05; β = −0.20, 95% CI −0.54, 0.16; and β = −0.07, 95% CI −0.38, 0.27, for the 4th, 3rd, and 2nd NDVI quartile vs 1st quartile, respectively) and natural direct effects ( β = −0.59, 95% CI −1.06, −0.09; β = −0.32, 95% CI −0.67, 0.03; and β = −0.05, 95% CI −0.37, 0.27, for the 4th, 3rd, and 2nd NDVI quartile vs 1st quartile, respectively). The natural indirect effect indicated no mediation by PM 10 . Similar results were found for the PM 2.5 analysis. Greenness was associated with lower insulin resistance among adults living in low NSES areas. However, no evidence of air pollution mediation was found. These results suggest that greater neighborhood greenness may be associated with better cardiometabolic health in socioeconomically disadvantaged areas.

title: GAZ SANOATI KORXONALARIDA YASHIL IQTISODIY FAOLIYATGA TA’SIR ETUVCHI INSTITUTSIONAL, TEXNOLOGIK VA MOLIYAVIY OMILLAR TAHLILI
summary: This article uses a systems approach to analyse the institutional, technological and financial factors affecting the development of green economic activity in gas industry enterprises. Across gas production, processing, transmission and dis
content: This article uses a systems approach to analyse the institutional, technological and financial factors affecting the development of green economic activity in gas industry enterprises. Across gas production, processing, transmission and distribution, energy consumption, methane losses, equipment condition and compliance with environmental requirements are considered key aspects of green transformation. Institutional factors include legislation and standards, public oversight, corporate governance and environmental disclosure; technological factors include equipment modernisation, methane leak detection, energy efficiency and digital monitoring; financial factors cover investment resources, lending conditions, green finance and project returns. The article proposes an analytical matrix for integrated factor diagnosis. The analysis is conceptual and qualitative; in the absence of company-level statistics, no quantitative empirical findings are claimed. The approach can be tested using data from Transgaz

title: Multivalent mRNA tuberculosis vaccines protect against mycobacterial infection in zebrafish, mice and guinea pigs
summary: Despite a century of BCG use, tuberculosis remains a leading cause of death from infectious diseases and more effective vaccines are urgently needed. Here we combined antigen discovery in zebrafish with mRNA vaccine technology to generate m
content: Despite a century of BCG use, tuberculosis remains a leading cause of death from infectious diseases and more effective vaccines are urgently needed. Here we combined antigen discovery in zebrafish with mRNA vaccine technology to generate multivalent vaccine candidates, TUmRNA 4 , TUmRNA 6 and TUmRNA 9 , encoding four, six, or nine Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigens, respectively. The vaccines were well tolerated, and induced robust antigen-specific cellular immune responses, including IFNγ production and expansion of memory T-cell populations. In mice, TUmRNA 4 and TUmRNA 6 reduced pulmonary M. tuberculosis burden and lung pathology to levels comparable to BCG vaccination and TUmRNA 6 enhanced BCG-mediated protection when used as a booster vaccine. In guinea pigs, TUmRNA 9 reduced bacterial burden in the lungs, spleen, and lymph nodes and decreased pulmonary lesions. These findings demonstrate that protective antigens identified in zebrafish can be translated into effective multivalent mRNA vaccines and establish a framework for tuberculosis vaccine development across multiple preclinical models.

title: Modeling and application of multi-objective optimization algorithm in green asset allocation
summary: Faced with the multi-objective conflict problem of risk minimisation and environmental benefit maximisation in green asset allocation, the traditional single-objective optimisation method has obvious limitations. This study innovatively pro
content: Faced with the multi-objective conflict problem of risk minimisation and environmental benefit maximisation in green asset allocation, the traditional single-objective optimisation method has obvious limitations. This study innovatively proposes a hybrid multi-objective optimisation algorithm (HMOA). The algorithm combines the Pareto optimisation ability of the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm 2 (NSGA-II), the dynamic convergence of particle swarm optimisation, and the subjective viewpoint quantification mechanism of the Black–Litterman model; it introduces a displacement fluctuation strategy to enhance diversity and uses a long short-term memory (LSTM) network to dynamically generate prior information. The test results show that HMOA is significantly better than the baseline model in terms of hypervolume (HV) = 0.85, inversion generation distance = 0.12, and other indicators (such as 8.97% higher than the HV of NSGA-II). In practical verification, its Sharpe ratio reached 1.25, and its carbon dioxide (CO2) emission reduction reached 1.256 million tons of carbon dioxide. In addition, the robustness test shows that the HV change rate of the algorithm is only 5.2% under noise, which proves that the algorithm can effectively balance multi-objective conflicts. Therefore, this study provides a new method with complete theory and strong practicability for green asset allocation, and promotes the innovative application of multi-objective optimisation theory in sustainable finance.

title: The Agrarian Matrix: A Conceptual Agriculture–Energy–Telecommunications Framework for Rural Infrastructure in Nigeria
summary: Nigeria’s rural economy is constrained at the same time by unreliable electricity, high post-harvest losses and uneven telecommunications coverage, yet these problems are planned and financed in separate sectoral programmes. This article is
content: Nigeria’s rural economy is constrained at the same time by unreliable electricity, high post-harvest losses and uneven telecommunications coverage, yet these problems are planned and financed in separate sectoral programmes. This article is a desk-based conceptual study; it is not a deployed or experimentally validated system. It proposes the “Agrarian Matrix”, a framework in which agricultural production, embedded electronic systems and telecommunications infrastructure are designed together around shared solar-powered rural infrastructure. Using a purposive, tiered compilation of secondary evidence from regulatory, multilateral, peer-reviewed, programme and media sources, the study reports that rural electricity access was about 33% in 2023 against about 89% in urban areas (access, not reliability); that the grid has about 13,000 MW of installed capacity but only 5,151 MW was available for dispatch in December 2025, with delivered energy lower still; and that reported post-harvest losses range from 5–20% for grains to 50–60% for tubers, fruits and vegetables, with a media-reported valuation of about ₦3.5 trillion a year that could not be verified against primary data. The framework comprises a five-layer node architecture, illustrative sizing assumptions, three testable hypotheses on the benefits of co-engineering, and a phased roadmap. Components of the framework have been piloted separately in Nigeria, but no integrated field validation exists, so the benefits attributed to co-engineering remain hypotheses. The contribution is an organising framework and research agenda; scenario-based techno-economic analysis and paired pilot comparisons are the priority next steps.

title: Operationalizing green governance and environmental SDGs through local planning and budgeting in federal Nepal: Evidence from Palpa district
summary: Local governments are increasingly responsible for translating environment-related Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into practical actions, yet evidence remains limited on whether national commitments materially shape local plans, budge
content: Local governments are increasingly responsible for translating environment-related Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into practical actions, yet evidence remains limited on whether national commitments materially shape local plans, budgets, and implementation in federal Nepal. This study aims to assess how green governance and environmental SDGs 6, 11, 13, and 15 are operationalized through planning and budgeting in four local governments of Palpa District. A qualitative-dominant mixed-methods case study combines national and local policy and planning documents, five fiscal years of budget and expenditure data, 31 key informant interviews, and six focus group discussions. Results show that all periodic plans reference the SDGs, but measurable environmental targets and indicators remain weak. Environmental SDG-related expenditure accounts for approximately 6.0% to 18.2% of total expenditure across cases and years, with allocations concentrated on SDG 6 and SDG 11, while SDG 13 and especially SDG 15 receive smaller and more fragmented funding. Intergovernmental fiscal rules, limited technical capacity, political incentives for visible projects, and unequal participation help explain the gap between policy commitments and budget choices.
