HESS J1832-085 is a point-like TeV source lacking a confirmed multiwavelength (MWL) counterpart. In this paper, we present evidence supporting a gamma-ray binary interpretation of HESS J1832-085 . We aim to investigate the nature of HESS J1832-085 using the available X-ray and Fermi Large Area Telescope (LAT) data, complemented by a near-infrared (NIR) identification of a possible stellar companion and broadband radiative modeling, to assess its classification as a potential gamma-ray binary. Archival X-ray observations were examined to search for a counterpart and to characterize its spectrum and potential variability. We further analyzed ∼17.3 yrs of Fermi LAT data between 1 and 300 GeV to establish a possible gigaelectronvolt (GeV) counterpart of HESS J1832-085. We also examined archival NIR images from the UKIRT Infrared Deep Sky Survey (UKIDSS) and the Two Micron All Sky Survey (2MASS), together with 2MASS catalog photometry. The broadband emission was interpreted using models commonly applied to gamma-ray binaries. A potential X-ray counterpart was identified in archival X-ray data, exhibiting a hard, absorbed spectrum and moderate variability. We also identified a tentative GeV gamma-ray excess that is spatially consistent with HESS J1832-085 and the proposed X-ray counterpart. We further identified a candidate stellar counterpart in both the UKIDSS and 2MASS images, located in close spatial proximity to the X-ray counterpart. The adopted illustrative binary radiative model broadly reproduces the X-ray and TeV emission, but fails to explain the emission from the tentative GeV excess. Our results support HESS J1832-085 as a promising gamma-ray binary candidate , motivating dedicated MWL follow-up observations to confirm the source nature.

title: Four-wave mixing and secondary radiations generated by nonharmonic two-color filaments in air: Influence of the Kerr and plasma nonlinearities
summary: Four-wave mixing (FWM) is an efficient source of light waves emitted at various frequencies, usually associated with third-order optical nonlinearities. Whereas attention has mostly been paid in the past to the generation of Stokes (e.g., v
content: Four-wave mixing (FWM) is an efficient source of light waves emitted at various frequencies, usually associated with third-order optical nonlinearities. Whereas attention has mostly been paid in the past to the generation of Stokes (e.g., visible) modes by mixing two nonharmonic frequencies in degenerate FWM, the present work aims to analyze the weaker components, i.e., the anti-Stokes (resp. mid-IR) radiation and cascaded satellites, and characterize their conversion efficiency and tunability. Here we report the production of tunable mid-infrared radiation around 3.3 $μ$m delivered by two-color femtosecond filaments in air combining $\sim 800$ nm fundamental and $\sim 1.3$ $μ$m seed waves. Although the Kerr response of air plays a key role in creating both visible and mid-IR radiations, we show that plasma nonlinearities also contribute by broadening and mixing the pump frequencies. Two experimental setups are exploited to focus, separately, on the production of FWM modes and cascaded satellites - called secondary radiations. A first filamentation setup employing different focal lengths for the two colors displays an ionization-induced broadening of the mid-IR radiation during the plasma stage. A second setup focusing the two pump components over equal propagation distances allows us to unveil the secondary radiations emerging at lower intensity levels when plasma occurs. We examine which player, among the plasma- or Kerr-induced FWM, is the most active in the conversion process. Numerical simulations based on a local-current model and a unidirectional solver highlight the role of the Kerr stage in amplifying the FWM radiations prior to the development of the weaker satellites in plasma regime. Their results, agreeing well with the experimental data, demonstrate that a broad visible emission is needed to trigger secondary radiations.

title: Combinatorial Synthesis and Direct-to-Biology Antibacterial Evaluation of Ruthenium(II) and Iridium(III) N^O -Schiff−Base Complexes
summary: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) represents a major global health challenge, compounded by a limited antibiotic discovery pipeline and restricted chemical diversity among clinically used antibiotics. Metal-based complexes offer promi
content: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) represents a major global health challenge, compounded by a limited antibiotic discovery pipeline and restricted chemical diversity among clinically used antibiotics. Metal-based complexes offer promising antimicrobial agents owing to their structural diversity and unique modes of action. Here, we report the synthesis and biological evaluation of two combinatorial libraries comprising 176 novel ruthenium(II) p-cymene (RuCy) and iridium(III) Cp* (IrCp) N^O-Schiff-base complexes. Syntheses used a robust three-step, room-temperature methodology, with automated LC−MS characterization enabling Direct-to-Biology screening. Against Staphylococcus aureus, 50−80% of compounds inhibited growth, whereas no significant activity was observed against Escherichia coli. Three leads exhibited MICs of 1.56−12.5 μM against Gram-positive pathogens, therapeutic indices exceeding 15, and negligible haemolysis. Mechanistic studies suggest that IrCp-B5, incorporating the ligand (E)-2-bromo-4-chloro-6-(((naphthalen-2-ylmethyl)imino)methyl)phenol, disrupts membrane associated processes, while RuCy-J3, incorporating (E)-1-((cyclohexylimino)methyl)naphthalen-2-ol, targets intracellular DNA-related pathways. This work demonstrates the utility of Direct-to-Biology approaches for accelerated antimicrobial lead identification and prioritization.

title: Carbon monoxide utilisation by Thermanaeromonas species and description of Thermobium azorense gen. nov., sp. nov.
summary: Syngas fermentation by carbon monoxide (CO)-utilising acetogens offers a sustainable route for converting gasified waste materials into value-added chemicals. In this study, we isolated a novel thermophilic CO-utilising bacterium, strain AZ
content: Syngas fermentation by carbon monoxide (CO)-utilising acetogens offers a sustainable route for converting gasified waste materials into value-added chemicals. In this study, we isolated a novel thermophilic CO-utilising bacterium, strain AZ2, from marine hydrothermal sediment collected on the island of São Miguel, Azores, Portugal. Strain AZ2 is an obligately anaerobic, spore-forming bacterium. Average nucleotide identity (ANI) and digital DNA-DNA hybridization (dDDH) analyses indicate that strain AZ2 represents a novel species within a previously uncharacterised lineage represented by the GTDB placeholder genus UBA 12545 in Neomoorellaceae. It is also the first cultured representative of this genus. Strain AZ2 was able to consume CO, producing acetate. We further demonstrated that its closest isolated relatives-Thermanaeromonas toyohensis and Thermanaeromonas sp. strain 9S-are capable of utilising CO, producing either acetate or hydrogen gas (H2). Additionally, we unveiled the genomic potential for CO utilisation within other members of the GTDB placeholder class DSM-521 (previously Moorellia) to which our isolate belongs, expanding the list of possible thermophilic CO-utilising acetogens. We propose that strain AZ2T represents the type strain of a novel genus and species, named Thermobium azorense gen. nov., sp. nov. (= DSM 121889T = JCM 39698T).

title: Efficient Fuzzy PSI under One-Sided Assumptions
source: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)
summary: Fuzzy private set intersection (PSI) enables two parties to identify approximately matching elements between their input sets, where two elements are considered a match if their distance is at most a threshold ? under a given metric. Althou
content: Fuzzy private set intersection (PSI) enables two parties to identify approximately matching elements between their input sets, where two elements are considered a match if their distance is at most a threshold ? under a given metric. Although substantial progress has been made, existing constructions for general Minkowski distances either rely on strong two-sided geometric separation assumptions or incur substantial overhead under one-sided assumptions. In this work, we present the first concretely efficient fuzzy PSI protocols for general L p∈[1,∞] distances under one-sided assumptions, relying solely on lightweight symmetric-key primitives. Our constructions support both sender-sided and receiver-sided settings. We further study sparser input distributions and present more efficient protocols tailored to this case. To reduce the overhead scaling with ?, we non-trivially incorporate prefix trie techniques into our protocols, achieving O(log?) complexity for general L p∈[1,∞] distances for the first time, improving upon O((log?) d ) or O(?) complexities of prior works. Extensive experiments, across a wide range of parameter settings, show that our protocols significantly outperform prior works under the same assumptions. Specifically, against van Baarsen and Pu (EUROCRYPT'24), our protocols achieve up to 248× faster computation and up to 20× lower communication. Against Dang et al. (CCS'25), we achieve up to 568× speedup and up to 63× communication reduction. Against Bui et al. (ASIACRYPT'25), we achieve up to 4978× faster computation and up to 282× lower communication.

title: Discovery of an Extremely Luminous Sporadic Radio Pulsar
summary: Abstract We have discovered PSR J2108+5055, an extremely luminous but sporadic mode-changing rotating radio transient (RRAT), with a period of 0.495 s using the Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment (CHIME) Fast Radio Burst (FRB) i
content: Abstract We have discovered PSR J2108+5055, an extremely luminous but sporadic mode-changing rotating radio transient (RRAT), with a period of 0.495 s using the Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment (CHIME) Fast Radio Burst (FRB) instrument. We show that the brightest pulse from PSR J2108+5055 has a flux density of 3.1 ± 1.0 kJy, corresponding to a spectral luminosity of (7.5 ± 2.3) × 10 23 erg s −1 Hz −1 , assuming a dispersion-measure-derived distance of 1.6 ± 0.3 kpc. We place an upper limit on the duty cycle of PSR J2108+5055 at 0.002 and measure a surface magnetic field of 5.8 × 10 11 G, a characteristic age of 1.2 × 10 7 yr, and a spindown luminosity of 2.2 × 10 32 erg s −1 . Using a simple model based on the Green Bank North Celestial Cap (GBNCC) survey, we place an upper limit on the number of PSR J2108+5055–like sources with similar peak flux densities in the GBNCC survey area of ∼80 RRATs. We show that if PSR J2108+5055 were placed at the edge of the Local Group of galaxies, the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST) would detect its brightest pulse. The second brightest pulse has a peak flux density of 1.5 ± 0.7 kJy, and FAST would detect such a pulse out to ∼1 Mpc, covering the inner Local Group, including Andromeda.

title: Meme Coin Factories: Uncovering Large-Scale Manipulations on pump.fun
source: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)
summary: Once complex, creating and deploying a new cryptocurrency has become trivial. Coin launchpads now allow users to generate a new coin with merely a few clicks, at a minimal cost. Launchpad popularity has grown in tandem with the rise of "mem
content: Once complex, creating and deploying a new cryptocurrency has become trivial. Coin launchpads now allow users to generate a new coin with merely a few clicks, at a minimal cost. Launchpad popularity has grown in tandem with the rise of "meme coins," which usually do not offer any novel technological properties and are purely created for fun. The most prominent coin launchpad, pump.fun, has gained significant traction, grossing over 100 million USD in daily trading volume. The mass adoption of coin launchpads, however, also enables strategic actors to easily manipulate trading signals, unbeknownst to inexperienced traders who then buy certain coins, and enable these strategic actors to profit from rapid and unsustainable price increases ("pumps"). To identify such manipulations at scale, we conduct a large-scale study of pump.fun, collecting information on all 15 million coins launched in the last two years, and performing analysis on large, random samples of transaction data. We identify five classes of manipulation strategies: 1) wash trading, 2) creator address obfuscation, 3) coordinated sell, 4) copycat coins, and 5) social media manipulation. We find that strategic actors often bypass the platform interface and implement these strategies in a highly automated and low-latency fashion, by interacting directly with the blockchain. We further uncover the existence of "Market-Manipulation-as-a-service (MMaaS)," third-party tools that enable users to perform these manipulations without any technical expertise. We conclude by devising mitigations and proposing recommendations for traders, pump.fun, wallets or chain scanners, software development platforms, and regulators.

title: When Ad Networks Misbehave: Understanding Risks of Semi-Drive-By Splash Ads
source: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)
summary: We investigate the mobile splash ads ecosystem, i.e., full-screen advertisements shown at app launch, where monetization relies on interaction signals that are difficult to verify end-to-end. This ad format is especially sensitive because i
content: We investigate the mobile splash ads ecosystem, i.e., full-screen advertisements shown at app launch, where monetization relies on interaction signals that are difficult to verify end-to-end. This ad format is especially sensitive because it sits at the boundary between app startup and user navigation, where incidental touches and sensor-driven callbacks are common yet easy to misattribute as engagement. Prior work has largely framed mobile ad fraud as a publisher-side problem, while a small number of studies have attributed fraudulent operations to embedded ad libraries. Yet a distinct risk remains underexplored in splash advertising: ad SDKs control both how interaction signals are interpreted and how the resulting events are measured and reported, creating an opportunity to reinterpret ambiguous user or device signals as valid advertising interactions. We uncover a previously less-known form of fraud at the ad-network layer in which splash ads are triggered not by intentional user actions but by incidental or indirect interactions, a behavior we term semi–drive-by splash ads. By translating non-ad interactions into billable engagement events, ad networks can systematically inflate performance metrics, overcharge advertisers, and erode user trust while providing little or no real user interest. To expose this behavior in the wild, we design AdHive, an automated honeypot-like analysis framework capable of inducing evasive splash-ad delivery and landing behaviors under realistic device conditions. Unlike traditional VM-based approaches, AdHive reproduces human-like activity through LLM-generated usage traces and sensor dynamics, enabling execution paths that remain hidden under conventional analysis environments. Our large-scale measurement across thousands of popular Android applications demonstrates that semi-drive-by splash ads are widespread and are often triggered by subtle environmental signals such as minor sensor variations. We further confirm real-world impact by working with one of China's largest advertisers to identify multiple ad networks engaging in this fraud, which led to enforced repayments of about 4 million Yuan (≈US$600,000).

title: How It's Made: Uncovering Detection Engineering Processes for Network Intrusion Detection Rules
summary: Many Security Operations Centers rely on signature-based Network Intrusion Detection Systems like Suricata, yet detection rule engineering remains understudied. We investigate this process by introducing SuriCap, a platform for rule enginee
content: Many Security Operations Centers rely on signature-based Network Intrusion Detection Systems like Suricata, yet detection rule engineering remains understudied. We investigate this process by introducing SuriCap, a platform for rule engineering exercises, and hosting CTF-style workshops where 60 participants, trained MSc students, and experienced SOC professionals, created rules for four scenarios. Participants produced 3146 valid rules, enabling analysis of their methods, performance, and iteration patterns. Surprisingly, prior experience had limited impact on rule quality, suggesting that less experienced engineers can produce rules comparable to experts. We also observed challenges in generalizing rules beyond available tests, underscoring the need for sufficient labeled data. From our study, we identify three phases and a common pattern in rule engineering, offering SOC managers insights to improve their processes and expectations of engineer expertise.

title: SERS reveals counterion-controlled Au( i )/Au( iii ) speciation in thiocyanate-mediated gold nanowire growth
summary: (CN) positions distinct from both synthesis-derived signatures and induces no anisotropic growth, indicating that the structure-directing species forms prior to reduction in solution. These findings establish SERS as a practical probe of r
content: (CN) positions distinct from both synthesis-derived signatures and induces no anisotropic growth, indicating that the structure-directing species forms prior to reduction in solution. These findings establish SERS as a practical probe of reactive speciation and identify the counterion as a controlling parameter for selecting mechanistic pathways in anisotropic nanoparticle synthesis.

title: SPICY 30021: An embedded bona fide FU Orionis star with a mid-infrared precursor
summary: The unstable mass accretion process in young stellar objects often leads to observable outbursts. These episodic accretion bursts play a key role in the stellar mass assembly during the pre-main-sequence evolution. The outbursts with the hi
content: The unstable mass accretion process in young stellar objects often leads to observable outbursts. These episodic accretion bursts play a key role in the stellar mass assembly during the pre-main-sequence evolution. The outbursts with the highest amplitude and longest duration are commonly identified as FU Orionis stars (FUors). Only ∼50 FUor events were confirmed until recently. Most of these eruptive events occur in embedded protostars, which are difficult to monitor from optical surveys. We present photometric and spectroscopic observations of an eruptive young star (SPICY 30021) originally discovered from the mid-infrared time series. We constructed the spectral energy distribution and physically characterised the eruptive nature of SPICY 30021. NEOWISE We gathered multi-wavelength photometric time series from , VVV, and the recently established VVV-RENEW surveys. We also conducted photometric and spectroscopic observations during the outburst using instruments on the SOAR, Magellan, and VLT telescopes, including data from the ESO public survey VVVX-GalCen. We first identified the location of the outbursting source and disentangled it from nearby companions. We then measured the line-of-sight extinction by comparing spectroscopic features. The stellar parameters were then estimated from radial velocity, proper motions, and stellar evolution models. NEOWISE We found that SPICY 30021 is an optically obscured FUor with a line-of-sight (interstellar and circumstellar) extinction of A_V = 12.5 mag. The spectrum of SPICY 30021 closely resembles the spectra of classical FUors. Using various methods, we measured the distance of SPICY 30021 as 1.7 = 30 ̊m L_⊙, which is moderate for FUors. The quiescent near-infrared photometry is consistent with a young, 0.9 ̊m M_⊙ progenitor, although the mass remains dependent on the model and distance. kpc. The accretion luminosity of the outburst is L_ ̊m acc We confirm that SPICY 30021 is a bona fide FUor event. The mid-infrared precursor suggests an outside-in triggering mechanism.

title: Crafting Ventures Communally:How community and cultural capital shape entrepreneurial pathways
summary: Entrepreneurship is often understood as a process driven by individual intention, strategic planning, and the ability to recognize and pursue opportunities. While these perspectives have contributed significantly to entrepreneurship researc
content: Entrepreneurship is often understood as a process driven by individual intention, strategic planning, and the ability to recognize and pursue opportunities. While these perspectives have contributed significantly to entrepreneurship research, they offer only a partial understanding of how entrepreneurial pathways develop within social and community settings. This dissertation examines how community, cultural capital, and historically rooted institutional conditions shape entrepreneurial emergence and early venture development, particularly in environments where formal resources are limited. Drawing on qualitative interviews, historical analysis, photographs, and observational data from Virginia’s craft brewing industry, this dissertation brings together three interconnected studies. The first examines how historical and institutional constraints shape different pathways into entrepreneurship, distinguishing between deliberate and accidental entrepreneurs. The second explores how individuals who never initially intended to become entrepreneurs develop entrepreneurial intention and identity through participation, shared experiences, and recognition from others. The third examines how customers take on multiple roles beyond traditional market exchange, contributing to the amplification of cultural capital, venture legitimacy, and early-stage development. Together, these studies show that entrepreneurship does not always begin with a deliberate intention to start a business. Instead, entrepreneurial pathways can develop gradually through relationships, community involvement, and experiences that shape how individuals come to see themselves as entrepreneurs. The findings also demonstrate how customers and community members become active participants in venture development, providing forms of support that extend beyond financial resources. By bringing together historical context, identity formation, and customer participation, this dissertation offers a more socially embedded understanding of entrepreneurship and highlights the importance of the communities, cultural meanings, and relationships through which ventures emerge, develop, and endure.

title: Plasmodium species positivity rates across regions with different malaria transmission intensities in Mainland Tanzania: Data from a nationwide survey conducted in 2023
summary: Although Plasmodium falciparum is the most prevalent and highly virulent species in Sub-Saharan Africa, non-falciparum species are increasingly recognized as a hidden burden. Generally, infections caused by non-falciparum species occur with
content: Although Plasmodium falciparum is the most prevalent and highly virulent species in Sub-Saharan Africa, non-falciparum species are increasingly recognized as a hidden burden. Generally, infections caused by non-falciparum species occur with low parasite densities and often present as co-infections with P. falciparum. These parasites may evade detection by routine diagnostics, complicating malaria case management and control efforts. To investigate the distribution of different Plasmodium parasites, we analysed 5,314 randomly selected samples from 18,969 samples collected across all 26 regions of Mainland Tanzania in 2023. Plasmodium parasites were detected using 18S qPCR. Of the analyzed samples, 52.3% (n = 2,780) were positive for any Plasmodium species. P. falciparum was detected in 51.2% (2,719/5,314), P. malariae in 1.4% (76/5,314), and P. ovale spp. in 1.8% (98/5,314) of the samples. Mixed infections were detected in 2.0% (107/5,314), with P. malariae and P. falciparum in 0.8% (40/5,314), and P. ovale mixed with P. falciparum in 1.1% (61/5,314) of the samples analysed. Among the samples with positive results (n = 2,780), mono-infections were detected at 93.9% (2,612/2,780) for P. falciparum, 1.1% (30/2,780) for P. malariae, and 1.1% (31/2,780) for P. ovale spp., respectively. Unlike P. malariae and P. ovale, P. falciparum infections were significantly influenced by transmission intensities, with the highest odds in regions with high transmission intensities compared to those with low (OR=1.61, p < 0.001), and very low transmission (OR=1.48, p < 0.001). School children had higher odds of P. falciparum infections compared to adults (OR=1.56, p < 0.001) and under-fives (OR=1.47, p < 0.001). Adults were also less likely to have P. malariae infections than schoolchildren (OR= 0.45, p = 0.021).The findings of the first-ever nation-wide survey reveal a high prevalence of P. falciparum, low prevalence of non-falciparum species, and complex species landscape. They underpin the need to expand surveillance systems beyond P. falciparum and adapt interventions to target all Plasmodium species.

title: Revisiting the centrifugal breakout scaling relationship for H α emission in light of ρ Oph C, the coolest B-type star with an H α -bright centrifugal magnetosphere
source: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
summary: Abstract The corotating magnetospheres of B-type stars are strongly affected by magnetic field strength and rotational velocity, which determine both the geometry and strength of visible and radio emission; however, Hα emission largely disa
content: Abstract The corotating magnetospheres of B-type stars are strongly affected by magnetic field strength and rotational velocity, which determine both the geometry and strength of visible and radio emission; however, Hα emission largely disappears below a bolometric luminosity of log (L/L⊙) ~ 2.8. The nearby B5 V star ρ Oph C (HD 147932) is the least-luminous rapidly rotating magnetic B-type star to display magnetospheric Hα emission. While ρ Oph C’s radio magnetosphere has been extensively studied, its magnetic field and Hα magnetosphere have been constrained only via snapshot observations. We present a new dataset of high-resolution ESPaDOnS spectropolarimetry covering the star’s rotational period, which is revisited by combining Hipparcos, K2 and TESS photometry. We find that the star’s magnetic field strength and geometry are consistent with the model inferred from radio data. As expected from the magnetic model, there is very little variability in Hα. Comparison of the light curve to both equivalent width measurements from metallic lines and magnetospheric models suggests that the star’s photometric variability is dominated by surface chemical abundance spots; however, there is complex rotationally modulated variability at about the mmag level which probably originates in the magnetosphere. ρ Oph C is the least luminous B-type star in which magnetospheric Hα emission has yet been detected, and its emission is notably weaker than the predictions of the centrifugal breakout model. Its photometric eclipse depth is also much lower than predicted by the CBO model. However, its radio luminosity is consistent with CBO predictions. We speculate on this basis that ρ Oph C may be a transitional object between effective temperature regimes with hydrogen-dominated and decoupled metallic winds.

title: Tác động không đồng nhất của FDI đến ô nhiễm không khí: Bằng chứng từ phương pháp hồi quy phân vị tại Việt Nam
source: Tạp chí Kinh tế và Phát triển
summary: Nghiên cứu phân tích tác động không đồng nhất của đầu tư trực tiếp nước ngoài (FDI) đến ô nhiễm không khí tại Việt Nam dựa trên dữ liệu 14144 dự án trong giai đoạn 2012-2019. Nghiên cứu sử dụng phương pháp hồi quy phân vị khoảnh khắc (Metho
content: Nghiên cứu phân tích tác động không đồng nhất của đầu tư trực tiếp nước ngoài (FDI) đến ô nhiễm không khí tại Việt Nam dựa trên dữ liệu 14144 dự án trong giai đoạn 2012-2019. Nghiên cứu sử dụng phương pháp hồi quy phân vị khoảnh khắc (Method of Moments Quantile Regression - MMQR) để xác định tác động của FDI lên toàn bộ phân bố có điều kiện của ô nhiễm không khí. Kết quả cho thấy FDI làm giảm đáng kể ô nhiễm không khí, với tác động mạnh hơn tại các phân vị ô nhiễm cao. Chủ nghĩa tập thể đóng vai trò điều tiết trong mối quan hệ này, theo đó, FDI có xu hướng làm gia tăng ô nhiễm tại những địa phương có mức độ chủ nghĩa tập thể thấp, nhưng tác động chuyển sang làm giảm ô nhiễm khi chủ nghĩa tập thể đạt mức đủ cao. Phát hiện này cho thấy lợi ích môi trường của FDI phụ thuộc không chỉ vào đặc điểm dự án mà còn vào bối cảnh văn hóa địa phương. Vì vậy, Việt Nam cần ưu tiên thu hút các dự án FDI sạch, chất lượng cao, đồng thời tăng cường cơ chế giám sát và sự tham gia của cộng đồng nhằm hỗ trợ phát triển bền vững.

title: From barriers to breakthroughs: Navigating success drivers of women entrepreneurs in China
summary: Despite the adolescence stage, the past 30 years have evidenced the proliferation of mainstream academic research for the most interesting and emerging phenomenon, ‘Women Entrepreneurship’. To further shed light on the above-stated phenomen
content: Despite the adolescence stage, the past 30 years have evidenced the proliferation of mainstream academic research for the most interesting and emerging phenomenon, ‘Women Entrepreneurship’. To further shed light on the above-stated phenomenon, this study aims to explore the success drivers and challenges of women entrepreneurs in the specific context of China. For this, success drivers and challenges are treated as antecedents (independent variables), entrepreneurial innovative behavior and government support as moderating variables, and the success of women entrepreneurs is taken as the outcome (dependent variable). To address the aforementioned research agenda, data were gathered from the women entrepreneurs of SMEs located in China who are successfully running their business for at least 3 years. A total of 260 survey responses (free from missing values) were obtained from specific the sample of women entrepreneurs (showing 67% response rate). SPSS 23.00 was used to test the hypothesis about the direct and indirect association of success drivers, challenges, entrepreneurial innovative behavior, Government support and the success of women entrepreneurs. Results revealed that the specific constructs of success drivers and challenges significantly affect the success of women entrepreneurs. Furthermore, entrepreneurial innovative behavior and Government support have also been proven as statistically significant moderators to strengthen the direct association of specific aforementioned constructs. This study is purely unique in theoretical and practical aspects as it addressed the empirically petite-researched phenomenon ‘women entrepreneurship’ specifically in the context of China. The study expanded the normal inquiry mode by looking into the moderated framework of entrepreneurial innovative behavior and Government support to escalate the success of women entrepreneurs.

title: Negotiating Faith and Tradition: Islamic Acculturation and Local Cultural Practices in Indonesian Muslim Communities
source: Dirasah International Journal of Islamic Studies
summary: This study examines how Indonesian Muslim communities negotiate Islamic teachings within local cultural practices using a Systematic Literature Network Analysis (SLNA) approach. Drawing on 86 Scopus-indexed publications from 2015 to 2025, t
content: This study examines how Indonesian Muslim communities negotiate Islamic teachings within local cultural practices using a Systematic Literature Network Analysis (SLNA) approach. Drawing on 86 Scopus-indexed publications from 2015 to 2025, the study integrates a systematic literature review and bibliometric network analysis to map research trends, intellectual structures, and thematic clusters in the field. The findings show that Islamic acculturation in Indonesia is best understood as a dynamic and historically layered process in which religious doctrine, ritual practice, cultural memory, and social cohesion continuously interact. The reviewed literature demonstrates that local rituals, customary institutions, and community-based traditions function as adaptive social spaces through which Islamic values are localized and reproduced. At the same time, the field increasingly highlights tensions generated by reformist discourses, transnational networks, and digital religious communication, which reshape the legitimacy of local traditions. The bibliometric mapping indicates that studies are strongly concentrated in Southeast Asia, with thematic clusters focusing on cultural adaptation, identity negotiation, social harmony, and the contestation of religious authority. However, the study finds that much of the existing literature remains descriptive, case-based, and unevenly theorized, with a notable disconnect between localized ethnography and emerging scholarship on digital religion. This article contributes by proposing future directions for more comparative, theoretically grounded, and digitally engaged interdisciplinary scholarship.

title: Chinese Global Migration
summary: This Element argues that Chinese global migration is best understood as a barometer of global power transitions: each major wave of emigration registers both a reconfiguration of the international order and China's shifting position within
content: This Element argues that Chinese global migration is best understood as a barometer of global power transitions: each major wave of emigration registers both a reconfiguration of the international order and China's shifting position within it. It shows how migration patterns reflect transformations in the East Asian international system alongside China's domestic political upheavals. It offers an analysis of three major waves of Chinese global migration, each aligned with a transformation in the international order and a domestic rupture: China's forced integration into the European imperial system, the political ruptures of the mid-twentieth century, and the post-reform opening of the People's Republic of China. It examines the varying roles successive Chinese states have played in regulating and responding to population mobility, the lived experiences of migrants, and how the meaning of 'return' has changed over the past two centuries. This title is also available as Open Access on Cambridge Core.

title: From Resource Allocation to Mobility Outcomes: Examining the Role of Strategic Financial Configuration in Nairobi’s Urban Transport System
source: Research Journal of Business and Finance
summary: Effective urban mobility requires more than the availability of financial resources; it also depends on how funds, grants and debt are planned, allocated, monitored and aligned with transport priorities. Anchored in the Resource-Based View
content: Effective urban mobility requires more than the availability of financial resources; it also depends on how funds, grants and debt are planned, allocated, monitored and aligned with transport priorities. Anchored in the Resource-Based View and complemented by Resource Orchestration Theory, this study examined the association between strategic financial resource configuration, defined as the deliberate structuring of fund, grant and debt resources, and perceived urban mobility outcomes (safety, reliability and efficiency) in Nairobi City, Kenya. A positivist, cross-sectional descriptive correlational survey design was used. The target population comprised 765 organisational actors in 25 public, private and international development institutions. A sample of 263, computed with Yamane’s formula, was allocated proportionally across the three stakeholder strata, and respondents within strata were selected purposively. Of 220 returned questionnaires (83.7%), 214 usable responses were analysed in SPSS version 30 using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and simple linear regression. Financial resource configuration showed a moderate-to-strong positive association with urban mobility outcomes (r = .635, p < .001) and accounted for 40.4% of their variance, F(1, 212) = 143.42, p < .001; B = 0.352, 95% CI [0.295, 0.409]. Planning, allocation, accountability and monitoring practices are therefore important correlates of perceived mobility performance.

title: Does AI empower corporate green technological innovation? The role of operational performance, resource allocation, and financing constraints
summary: Amidst escalating global climate concerns and rapid artificial intelligence (AI) advancement, this study examines how AI empowers corporate green technological innovation (GTI) to facilitate low-carbon transitions. Using data from Chinese A
content: Amidst escalating global climate concerns and rapid artificial intelligence (AI) advancement, this study examines how AI empowers corporate green technological innovation (GTI) to facilitate low-carbon transitions. Using data from Chinese A-share listed companies (2007–2025), we demonstrate that AI significantly enhances GTI, with effects more pronounced in manufacturing, high-tech sectors, and firms located in eastern China. Mechanistically, AI fosters GTI through operational-performance improvements and optimised resource-allocation efficiency. However, financing constraints exert a critical negative moderating role, curtailing AI’s potential. Policy implications highlight the need for tailored interventions – including sector-specific AI integration, cross-regional innovation alliances, and dual-track governance – to unlock AI’s dual pathways of operational optimisation and strategic reallocation while addressing capital accessibility and equitable development.

title: State Management of the Urban Environment in the Pursuit of Sustainable Economic Development: A Case Study of Phu Dien Ward, Hanoi, Vietnam
source: International Journal of Advanced Multidisciplinary Research and Studies
summary: Rapid urbanisation has made environmental quality a condition for, rather than a by-product of, sustainable economic development in Vietnam's large cities. Since 1 July 2025, wards in Hanoi have become the lowest level of a two-tier local g
content: Rapid urbanisation has made environmental quality a condition for, rather than a by-product of, sustainable economic development in Vietnam's large cities. Since 1 July 2025, wards in Hanoi have become the lowest level of a two-tier local government system and carry direct responsibility for many tasks of urban environmental management. This paper analyses state management of the urban environment in Phu Dien ward, a fast-urbanising ward in the west of Hanoi formed by merging Phu Dien with most of Phuc Dien and parts of Mai Dich and Co Nhue 1. Using a qualitative case design with document analysis and descriptive statistics, and a pressure-state-response framework, the study examines the city context and the ward's management practices for waste, air, water and green space. Hanoi's annual mean PM2.5 concentration rose for the third consecutive year to 45.4 µg/m³ in 2024, nearly double the national limit of 25 µg/m³; domestic solid waste increased from about 6,400 tonnes per day in 2014 to about 7,500 tonnes per day in 2025 and is forecast to approach 10,000 tonnes per day by 2030; and the Nhue river, which flows through the ward, remains seriously polluted. At ward level, management relies on contracted waste collection, inspection with ward police and community campaigns, but incidents such as unauthorised waste and broken-glass storage sites show gaps in monitoring and enforcement. The paper proposes six groups of solutions that link environmental management with the ward's economic development, including clearer ward mandates, performance-based waste contracts, construction dust control, protection of the Nhue corridor and Mai Dich retention lake, digital monitoring and co-management with residents and businesses.

title: Modulation of the TGF-β1-related response of human dental pulp stem cells by PRF membranes with and without bone allograft
summary: Introduction To our knowledge, no previous study has directly compared the TGF-β1-related responses of human dental pulp stem cells (hDPSCs) to conditioned media derived from A-PRF+, H-PRF, Gel A-PRF+, and e-PRF, with and without bone allog
content: Introduction To our knowledge, no previous study has directly compared the TGF-β1-related responses of human dental pulp stem cells (hDPSCs) to conditioned media derived from A-PRF+, H-PRF, Gel A-PRF+, and e-PRF, with and without bone allograft. Aim To evaluate the TGF-β1-related cellular response of hDPSCs following exposure to conditioned media derived from different PRF preparations, used alone or combined with bone allograft. Materials and methods Four PRF preparations (A-PRF+, H-PRF, Gel A-PRF+, and e-PRF) were investigated with and without bone allograft. Each experimental group included 10 independent biological samples (n = 10). Conditioned media were collected after 24 h and on day 14. hDPSCs cultured in unconditioned medium served as controls. After 48 h of treatment, TGF-β1-related cellular immunoreactivity was assessed using Cell ELISA and normalized to glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH). Statistical analysis included the Kruskal–Wallis test with Dunn’s post hoc test and Bonferroni correction. Direct paired comparisons were performed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test with Bonferroni correction. Results PRF preparations without allograft showed no significant increases in the normalized TGF-β1/GAPDH signal compared with controls. After 24 h of conditioning, significant increases were observed for H-PRF, Gel A-PRF+, and e-PRF combined with allograft compared with controls. After 14 days, significant increases were observed for Gel A-PRF+ and e-PRF with allograft. Direct paired comparisons demonstrated significantly higher signals for Gel A-PRF+ and e-PRF with allograft after 14 days compared with the corresponding preparations without allograft, whereas no significant differences were detected after 24 h. Conclusion The TGF-β1-related response of hDPSCs varied according to PRF preparation, allograft supplementation, and conditioning period. The significant effects observed for Gel A-PRF+ and e-PRF combined with allograft support further investigation of these constructs as potential bioactive materials for vital pulp therapy.

title: Can Coastal Ecological Restoration Promote Corporate ESG Performance? Evidence from China’s Blue Bay Remediation Action
summary: Coastal ecological degradation poses wide-ranging challenges to marine ecosystems and the sustainable development of coastal economies. However, evidence on whether public ecological restoration policies influence corporate environmental, s
content: Coastal ecological degradation poses wide-ranging challenges to marine ecosystems and the sustainable development of coastal economies. However, evidence on whether public ecological restoration policies influence corporate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance remains limited. This study examines China’s Blue Bay Remediation Action (BBRA), launched in 2016, as a quasi-natural experiment to assess its effects on the ESG performance of Chinese listed maritime firms. Using panel data on China’s A-share listed maritime companies from 2008 to 2021 and a PSM-IPW-DID design, we find a statistically significant positive effect of the BBRA on overall ESG scores. Positive effects are also statistically significant for the environmental and governance scores. Additional analyses indicate that BBRA implementation is associated with increased environmental subsidies, reduced financing constraints, stronger environmental regulation, and greater institutional investor attention. The positive effects are more pronounced among non-state-owned firms, firms in southern coastal regions, and firms located in cities with higher public environmental concern. The findings provide empirical evidence on the relationship between ecological restoration policies and corporate sustainable development, along with policy insights for improving coastal ecological governance and supporting firms’ green transition in China.

title: Designing LLM-Based Conversational Agents for Prosocial Decisions: The Roles of Warmth and Competence
summary: As Conversational agents increasingly support morally consequential decisions, it remains unclear whether anthropomorphic design promotes prosocial behavior. Integrating self-humanization theory with the stereotype content model, we examine
content: As Conversational agents increasingly support morally consequential decisions, it remains unclear whether anthropomorphic design promotes prosocial behavior. Integrating self-humanization theory with the stereotype content model, we examine how anthropomorphic cues shape perceived warmth, perceived competence and, in turn, algorithm aversion and prosocial behavior. In a preregistered, incentivized between-subjects experiment, 521 participants interacted with either a human-like conversational agent, a computer-like conversational agent, or a static text-based control before allocating money to an animal-related charity. Anthropomorphic cues increased both perceived warmth and perceived competence. However, only perceived competence was significantly associated with lower algorithm aversion and higher donation amounts, though the two paths did not differ significantly. Exploratory mediation analyses indicated an indirect association of anthropomorphic design with donations through competence. These findings qualify the presumed primacy of warmth in prosocial contexts and identify perceived competence as a pathway through which anthropomorphic conversational agents may support prosocial behavior.

title: Preparing Organizations for the AI Era: Organizational Readiness, Capability Building, Digital Transformation, and Business Performance
source: MANTRA Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Management
summary: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) has encouraged organizations to move beyond technology adoption toward broader organizational preparation and transformation. This study aims to examine how organizational readiness and
content: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) has encouraged organizations to move beyond technology adoption toward broader organizational preparation and transformation. This study aims to examine how organizational readiness and capability building support AI-driven digital transformation and how these processes contribute to business performance. A Systematic Literature Review (SLR) was conducted using the PRISMA 2020 framework. Relevant studies published between 2021 and 2026 were identified through SpringerLink and ScienceDirect. The selection criteria included English-language, open-access research articles related to organizational and business contexts. Following the screening and eligibility process, 20 studies were included in the final synthesis. The selected studies were analyzed thematically and grouped into four major themes: organizational readiness, capability building, digital transformation, and business performance. The findings show that successful AI adoption depends not only on technological infrastructure but also on leadership, data readiness, employee capabilities, organizational culture, governance, and strategic alignment. Capability building plays a critical role in strengthening AI capability, digital capability, absorptive capacity, intellectual capital, organizational agility, and AI literacy. Digital transformation subsequently acts as an organizational process that embeds these capabilities into business processes, innovation, learning, and value creation. The reviewed studies further indicate that AI-related performance is multidimensional, including productivity, innovation, resilience, ESG performance, environmental performance, and sustainable business outcomes. This review concludes that business value from AI is generated through the interaction of organizational readiness, capability development, and digital transformation rather than through technology adoption alone.

title: Application of vibrational spectroscopy in the discrimination of soil samples
summary: Purpose: The primary aim of this study was to ascertain whether IR spectroscopy integrated with chemometric data analysis can effectively distinguish the impact of land use on the intensity of humus transformation. Additional focus was put
content: Purpose: The primary aim of this study was to ascertain whether IR spectroscopy integrated with chemometric data analysis can effectively distinguish the impact of land use on the intensity of humus transformation. Additional focus was put on humic acids (HAs) and fulvic acids (FAs) as representatives of soil organic matter. Methods: Humic and Fulvic acids were extracted from 12 soils of different land-use: woodland (W), arable land (A) and fallow (F). The FTIR-ATR technique was applied to collect spectra of HA, FA and soil. The spectral data were then used to construct discriminant models applying the Partial least squares - discriminant analysis (PLS-DA) algorithm. Results: The averaged ATR spectra exhibited differences between FA and HA from the three different environments. The distribution of samples in the LV1/LV3 coordinate system of PLS-DA models revealed a clustering of samples based on their origin; a clear separation between the forest-derived samples and the field- and fallow-originating samples was observed. Similarly to the PLS-DA modeling of the spectral data for the extracts, the forest soil samples are distinguishable from the other two groups. Conclusions: FTIR-ATR spectroscopy combined with chemometric analysis is a valuable tool for distinguishing the origin of the soils from which humic substances were extracted. Moreover, the results obtained are consistent with analyses performed on the soils themselves, proving that humic and fulvic acids accurately reflect the properties of soil organic matter. Supplementary Information: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s11368-026-04621-1.

title: Strategic Green Entrepreneurship, Digital Transformation and Sustainable Business Performance: An Integrative Review and Future Research Agenda for Emerging Economies
source: WORLD JOURNAL OF ENTREPRENEURIAL DEVELOPMENT STUDIES
summary: The increasing challenges of climate change, environmental degradation, and resource scarcity have compelled organizations to integrate sustainability into their strategic operations. Green entrepreneurship has emerged as an effective appro
content: The increasing challenges of climate change, environmental degradation, and resource scarcity have compelled organizations to integrate sustainability into their strategic operations. Green entrepreneurship has emerged as an effective approach for creating economic value while promoting environmental protection and social well-being. Similarly, digital transformation has become a critical organizational capability that enhances innovation, operational efficiency, and sustainable business development. However, existing studies have largely examined green entrepreneurship, digital transformation, and sustainable business performance independently, resulting in limited understanding of their interconnected roles in achieving long-term sustainability. This paper presents a systematic integrative review of literature published between 2020 and 2026 to examine the relationships among green entrepreneurship, digital transformation, business innovation, and sustainable business performance. The review synthesizes contemporary theoretical and empirical evidence to develop an integrated conceptual framework grounded in the Triple Bottom Line Theory, Dynamic Capability Theory, and Ecological Modernization Theory. The findings indicate that green entrepreneurship and digital transformation complement one another, while business innovation serves as the key mechanism through which these capabilities improve economic, environmental, and social performance. The review further highlights the importance of institutional support, green finance, technological infrastructure, and effective governance in promoting sustainable entrepreneurial ecosystems. The study contributes to sustainability and entrepreneurship literature by integrating fragmented knowledge into a unified framework and offering practical implications for entrepreneurs, managers, policymakers, and researchers seeking to advance sustainable business development.

title: The New Geopolitics of Global Power: Exploring the Transformation of International Order in an Era of Strategic Competition
summary: Since the end of the Cold War, the liberal international order has faced increasing challenges. Major powers, particularly the United States and China, are engaged in strategic competition that is reshaping trade, technology, security, alli
content: Since the end of the Cold War, the liberal international order has faced increasing challenges. Major powers, particularly the United States and China, are engaged in strategic competition that is reshaping trade, technology, security, alliances, and the institutions of global governance. The prevailing discussion, however, tends to center narrowly on military rivalry or great-power competition. This limited perspective overlooks the broader transformation of the international order through economic statecraft, technological rivalry, institutional contestation, regional alignments, sanctions, supply-chain restructuring, and diplomatic competition. Hence, this study investigates how strategic competition is transforming the distribution of power, patterns of alignment, and the functioning of the international order. It uses a qualitative, interpretive, and comparative documentary research design. Data sources include peer-reviewed academic publications, official policy documents, strategic doctrines, communiqués, reports of international institutions, and credible think-tank publications. Sources were selected through purposive sampling based on their credibility, diversity of perspectives, and direct relevance to the research questions. The data were analyzed using Braun and Clarke's six-phase thematic analysis. The analysis identified five themes: power transition, strategic competition, and the erosion of uncontested unipolarity; economic statecraft, technological rivalry, and the securitization of interdependence; institutional contestation, selective multilateralism, and parallel institutions; regional realignment, security dilemmas, and the hedging strategies of middle powers; and normative competition and the formation of a fragmented and negotiated order. Together, these themes indicate that the international order is becoming more plural, fragmented, negotiated, and competitive, and that it cannot be adequately described as simply unipolar, bipolar, or multipolar. The study contributes to debates on global governance, international order, strategic autonomy, and the future of multilateral cooperation. It also provides a broader framework for understanding how major-power competition is changing the structures and practices of international politics.

title: Intellectual structure and research trends in consumer behaviour and retail investment through bibliometric review analysis
summary: The study explores the intellectual structure, thematic evolution, and collaborative patterns in mutual fund investment behaviour research using a bibliometric and scientometric approach applied to 653 records retrieved from Scopus and Web
content: The study explores the intellectual structure, thematic evolution, and collaborative patterns in mutual fund investment behaviour research using a bibliometric and scientometric approach applied to 653 records retrieved from Scopus and Web of Science in 1983–2025. Performance and science mapping analyses were carried out with Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny and VOSviewer to identify publication trends, citation patterns, source and author productivity, co-authorship, keyword co-occurrence, thematic evolution, and cooperation. The number of documents increased significantly after 2010 and peaked in 2024; however, caution is advised in comparing citations of recent publications because citation impact depends on the age of a document and the year 2025 was not complete at the time of analysis on 9 August 2025. The USA dominated the literature in terms of quantity and impact, followed by India and China, with the UK, Spain, Germany, and the Netherlands producing a considerable number of articles and citations. The analysis also revealed that keywords and themes were concentrated in performance, risk, returns, flows, and fund-related subjects, as well as behavioural and consumer-related areas, such as risk perception, overconfidence, heuristics, Prospect Theory, financial literacy, information search, preferences, and consumer behaviour, with sustainability- and digital-finance related topics also playing an important role in the literature, albeit as emerging and specialised fields. The study discusses the findings in relation to key theories and approaches, including behavioural finance, consumer behaviour, financial services marketing, and technology adoption, but does not attempt to establish causal relationships or theoretical influences due to the limitations of bibliometric analysis. The study also highlights research opportunities, including digital trust, consumer behaviour in FinTech, ESG and ethical investing, consumer segmentation, and regulatory protection, as well as methodological innovation, for future empirical and theoretical studies. In conclusion, the study provides an evidence-based overview of the intellectual and thematic evolution of mutual fund investment research and identifies potential areas of investigation for future studies.

title: Biodiversity and wilderness sustainability in environmental ethics: What can Yoruba eco-philosophy offer?
source: Journal of Asian and African Studies
summary: This work interrogates some theories of environmental ethics. It identifies biodiversity loss and wilderness degradation as pivotal environmental problems facing our world today. This is because the local and global environment is presently
content: This work interrogates some theories of environmental ethics. It identifies biodiversity loss and wilderness degradation as pivotal environmental problems facing our world today. This is because the local and global environment is presently experiencing biodiversity loss and wilderness degradation, traceable to destructive anthropogenic activities such as deforestation, pollution, hunting, urbanisation and uncontrolled capitalist-inspired agricultural practices. Using relationalism as a theoretical framework, the work examines the practice of Igbo oro in Yoruba eco-philosophy and untangles the inherent similarity and the point of divergence between Yoruba eco-philosophy and deep ecology of the western philosophical tradition. It argues that the practice of Igbo oro among the Yoruba people embodies and goes beyond what deep ecology stands for. The work goes further to demonstrate how the practice of Igbo oro pragmatically shows respect for nature, thereby constituting an indigenous African paradigm for environmental sustainability. This argument is significant since it debunks the position held in certain quarters that the practice of Igbo oro in Yorubaland is only for the fulfilment of religious aspirations of the Yoruba people.

content:
总体平稳 向新向优——透视10月国民经济运行态势
2026-11-16 20:39
字号：默认
新华社北京11月16日电 题：总体平稳 向新向优——透视10月国民经济运行态势
新华社记者王雨萧、张晓洁
10月份我国主要经济指标运行情况如何？国民经济呈现哪些特点？如何研判全年经济走势？在国新办16日举行的新闻发布会上，国家统计局新闻发言人就相关情况进行介绍。
经济运行“稳”的特质明显
国家统计局新闻发言人付凌晖表示，10月份国际环境动荡不安，地缘政治冲突延宕发酵，全球能源、航运市场持续波动，我国经济顶住压力，继续保持总体平稳、向新向优发展态势，展现出强大韧性和活力，“稳”的特质明显、“稳”的底气增强。
生产供给增加稳。10月份，规模以上工业增加值同比增长4.8%，保持平稳较快增长；服务业生产指数同比增长4.6%。
消费市场运行稳。1至10月，社会消费商品和服务零售总额同比增长2.5%，其中服务零售额增长4.9%，成为消费市场扩容的重要推动力。
外贸增长势头稳。10月份，我国进出口总额同比增长31.2%，今年以来持续保持较快增长。
“稳”还反映在就业和物价的稳定。
“随着季节性因素影响消退，全国城镇调查失业率从9月份开始连续两个月下降，10月份全国城镇调查失业率为5.1%。从物价情况看，尽管受国际能源市场波动带来的输入性冲击影响，我国加大保供稳价力度，价格形势总体稳定。”付凌晖说。
针对10月部分指标增速出现回落，国家统计局新闻发言人王冠华表示，月度指标出现波动是经济运行中比较常见的现象，比如10月部分指标回落一定程度上受到中秋错月因素影响，部分需求在9月提前释放，客观上会对10月服务业消费等指标形成一定下拉影响。判断经济走势，既要看当月也要看累计，既要看总量更要看结构，既要跟自己比，也要放在全球经济坐标中来看。
“今年前三季度中国经济增长4.6%，在全球范围内也是一个非常亮眼的表现。进入四季度，经济平稳运行的态势没有改变。”王冠华说，中国经济在复杂环境中保持总体稳定的发展势头，这种“稳”本身就是全球的稀缺资源和宝贵资产。
向新向优发展态势延续
超过五成——这是今年前10个月以高端制造、智能制造为代表的新动能对规模以上工业增加值增长的贡献。
“新动能快速成长，对经济增长的贡献稳步提升，有力助推了经济高质量发展，成为今年以来经济运行的突出亮点。”付凌晖说。
市场需求加快向“新”拓展。
从消费看，文体旅游服务消费和智能绿色商品消费持续扩大。10月份，高能效等级家电和可穿戴智能设备零售额保持较快增长，旅游咨询租赁服务类零售额保持两位数增长。
从外贸看，高技术产品和绿色产品增势较好。10月份，我国高技术产品和“新三样”产品出口额同比增长均超过50%。
从投资看，资金和建设项目向创新驱动和产业升级等重点领域集聚。1至10月份，知识产权产品投资、设备工器具购置投资分别增长9.2%和8.9%。
“前10个月固定资产投资降幅有所扩大，主要是经济发展阶段变化、产业结构调整等多方面因素导致的。我们要客观理性全面看待，既要看到投资总量变化情况，更要看投资结构、质量、效益的改善。”付凌晖说。
产业向“新”发展同步加快。10月份，数字产品制造业增加值同比增长18.4%，工业机器人、集成电路产量增速均在20%以上；不少传统行业含“新”量提升，铁路、船舶、航空航天和其他运输设备制造业增加值同比增长9.2%。
绿色生产力加快打造，日益成为拉动经济的新增长点。
“清洁能源利用占比稳步提升，绿色产品增长势头良好，10月汽车用锂离子电池产量同比增长33.9%，碳纤维及其复合材料产量增长52.2%。”付凌晖说。
实现全年预期目标有支撑有条件
展望全年，经济发展预期目标能否顺利实现？
“当前经济发展确实面临着一些困难和挑战，需要采取有针对性的措施解决。但在应对挑战、攻坚克难的过程中，支撑高质量发展的有利条件和独特优势也在不断巩固拓展。”王冠华说。
从运行基础看，前10个月供需两端指标比较平稳，城镇调查失业率稳定，物价温和上涨，能源供给充足，为全年目标顺利实现奠定良好基础。
从支撑因素看，新动能的驱动力越来越强。前10个月，规模以上高技术制造业、专精特新“小巨人”工业企业增加值分别增长14.6%和11.1%。
“在新旧动能转换过程中，一些传统行业面临转型调整的压力，同时也有一大批新产业、新业态、新模式冒出来、跑起来，这种新旧动能的彼长此消、接力转换，正是当前中国经济最为鲜明的特征。”王冠华说，新兴领域发展潜能大、成长势头好，无疑将有利于全年经济的平稳运行。
此外，外贸韧性和优势将持续彰显。
王冠华表示，面对全球经贸环境起伏不定，我国出口额和进口额连续多个月保持两位数快速增长，靠的是我国完备的产业体系和超大规模市场优势。依托完备产业链、多元化市场布局以及持续扩大的制度型开放，外贸对经济增长的支撑作用还将有效发挥。
“随着各项宏观政策协同发力不断显效，中国经济有望延续向新向优向好的发展态势，实现全年预期目标有支撑、有条件。”王冠华说。
